nodes.name: Morrigan
nodes.domain: war, death, prophecy, fate, sovereignty
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: shapeshifting, cloaked, red hair, red eyebrows, sometimes huge / standing-astride
nodes.significantEvent: Encountered standing astride the river Unius at Glenn Eitenn, where she couples with the Dagda at Samhain before the Second Battle of Mag Tuired and promises to deprive the Fomoirean king Indech of the blood of his heart. Pronounces both the prophecy of peace ('peace up to heaven, heaven down to earth') and the corresponding prophecy of doom at the close of the same battle. Approaches Cú Chulainn at the ford in three transformations — eel, she-wolf, hornless red heifer — when he refuses her offer of love. Performs the Washer-at-the-Ford role before the deaths of doomed warriors.
nodes.symbolism: Celtic Terrible Mother/war goddess
nodes.neumannArchetype: Celtic war/death goddess representing the Terrible Mother.
nodes.birthCircumstances: Daughter of Ernmas of the Tuatha Dé Danann; sister of Badb and Macha (and in some recensions Banba, Fódla, and Ériu).
nodes.object_source: Táin Bó Regamna (the red one-legged horse and red chariot of the prophesying Morrigan)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Cath Maige Tuired §84-85 (Gray ed. 1982 — Samhain union with Dagda); Cath Maige Tuired §166-167 (the two prophecies); Táin Bó Cúailnge recension I, lines 1845-1880 (Lebor na hUidre — three transformations against Cú Chulainn); Táin Bó Regamna; Aided Con Culainn (Washer-at-the-Ford); Reicne Fothaid Canainne
nodes.eventTypes_source: Cath Maige Tuired §84-85 (sovereignty rite — hieros gamos with the Dagda); Cath Maige Tuired §166-167 (prophecies); Táin Bó Cúailnge (battle-incitement). 'Seduction' replaced with 'sovereignty rite' for the Dagda episode (it is a hieros gamos / sovereignty-rite, not seduction); the Cú Chulainn approach is more accurately 'rejected-suit' than 'seduction'.
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Lebor Gabála Érenn §60-62 (Macalister ed.); Banshenchas
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Táin Bó Regamna (red brows, red horse, red chariot, cloaked); Táin Bó Cúailnge recension I ('her two eyebrows were red as crimson'); Cath Maige Tuired §84 (standing astride the river Unius)
nodes.domain_source: Cath Maige Tuired §137, §166-167 (war, prophecy); Táin Bó Cúailnge (war, death); Cath Maige Tuired §84-85 (sovereignty); Banshenchas (sovereignty/fate complex)
nodes.animals_source: All five animals are attested as transformation-forms: crow/raven (Táin Bó Cúailnge battlefield form); wolf, eel, cow/heifer (Táin Bó Cúailnge recension I, ll. 1845-1880 — three transformations against Cú Chulainn). Correctly placed in 'animals' per the protocol's symbolic-embodiment rule.
nodes.characterTrait_source: Cath Maige Tuired (the Second Battle of Mag Tuired); Táin Bó Cúailnge; Tochmarc Emire
nodes.birthTypes_source: Lebor Gabála Érenn (the Morrígan as daughter of Ernmas, sister of Badb and Macha)

nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine guardian of the boundary between the known and unknown

nodes.domain: divine beings, the kami collectively, sacred spirits, the concept of divinity
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a general term for the kami as divine beings, the sacred spirits of the Shinto tradition
nodes.significantEvent: the collective concept of divine beings in Shinto, encompassing all kami from the highest creation deities to the spirits in trees, rocks, and natural phenomena
nodes.symbolism: the divine as pervading all existence, the kami as the universal sacred presence, divinity as immanent in all natural phenomena rather than transcendent above them
nodes.neumannArchetype: the numinous that pervades all of nature and consciousness, the collective divine presence in the world

nodes.name: Pun Tao Kong
nodes.domain: peaches, immortality, longevity, feasting
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: deity associated with the peaches of immortality
nodes.significantEvent: associated with the celestial peach garden where the immortality-granting peaches grow, connected to the Peach Banquet hosted by the Queen Mother of the West
nodes.symbolism: the peach as the fruit of immortality, the celestial garden where longevity is cultivated, the feast of immortals as the supreme celebration
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine guardian of the Great Mothers immortality garden, the keeper of the fruit of eternal life

nodes.name: Hathor
nodes.domain: sky, music, motherhood, animals
nodes.object: sistrum; menat-necklace; the solar disk between cow-horns on her head; the mirror; the Seven Hathors (seven aspects who pronounce fate at birth)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Anthropomorphic woman with the solar disk between cow-horns on her head; sometimes fully bovine (a cow); sometimes fully leonine (in her Sekhmet-Eye-of-Ra aspect). The Seven Hathors who attend childbirth are her plural-aspects.
nodes.significantEvent: Goddess of love, beauty, music, joy, motherhood, foreign lands, the dead (she welcomes them into the necropolis with milk). In the Destruction of Mankind narrative, sent as the Eye of Ra to destroy rebellious humanity — she becomes Sekhmet (the wrathful lioness) and slaughters until she becomes drunk on beer dyed red to look like blood (Ra's ruse) and is pacified, returning to her Hathoric form. As the Lady of the West, receives the dead into the necropolis.
nodes.symbolism: Nurturing cow of heaven; horns as maternal symbols; fused with Isis as Isis-Hathor; cow-heaven mother
nodes.neumannArchetype: The nurturing cow of heaven. Associated with both terrible and positive aspects. Fused with Isis.
nodes.birthCircumstances: Daughter of Ra in most traditions; in the Edfu tradition, paired with Horus of Edfu.
nodes.domain_source: Pyramid Texts; Coffin Texts; Book of the Dead; the Dendera temple inscriptions (her main cult-center); the Destruction of Mankind narrative (preserved in the tomb of Seti I); the Tale of the Doomed Prince; the Festival of Drunkenness liturgy

nodes.name: Harpocrates
nodes.domain: silence, secrets, confidentiality
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: young child with finger raised to his lips in a gesture of silence
nodes.significantEvent: became widely worshipped in the Greco-Roman world as the god of silence and secrecy, associated with mystery cults
nodes.symbolism: the sacred silence of mystery traditions, secrecy as a divine quality, the child-god who knows but does not speak
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child in his silent aspect, consciousness that contains truth but does not articulate it
nodes.birthCircumstances: Greek adaptation of the Egyptian child-god Horus (Har-pa-khered, Horus the Child), reinterpreted as a god of silence

nodes.name: Bellerophon
nodes.domain: heroism, monster-slaying, hubris, horsemanship
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: handsome hero riding the winged horse Pegasus
nodes.significantEvent: tamed Pegasus with a golden bridle given by Athena, slew the Chimera from the air on Pegasuss back, attempted to fly to Olympus but was thrown down by Zeus and wandered crippled and alone
nodes.symbolism: the hero who rises too high, the danger of mortal hubris in seeking divine status, the winged horse as the vehicle of transcendence that can also destroy
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hero who achieves the heights of consciousness but is destroyed by his attempt to transcend human limits
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Poseidon and Eurynome, raised as foster son of Glaucus king of Corinth

nodes.domain: sea monsters, the dangers of the deep, primordial sea
nodes.characterTrait: monstrous, ancient, beautiful yet terrible, generative of horrors
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: primordial sea goddess, sometimes described as beautiful with golden scales, mother of monsters
nodes.significantEvent: with her brother-husband Phorcys she bore Medusa, the Graeae, Echidna, Ladon the serpent, and Scylla, populating the sea with terrors
nodes.symbolism: the sea as source of horror and wonder, the beautiful mother who generates monsters, the primordial depths from which terrors emerge
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Terrible Mother of the sea whose beautiful surface conceals monstrous depths
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Pontus (Sea) and Gaia (Earth)

nodes.domain: alchemy, immortality, Daoism
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Daoist immortal associated with alchemical practices
nodes.significantEvent: achieved immortality through Daoist alchemical cultivation, worshipped as a perfected being (Zhenren)
nodes.symbolism: the alchemical transformation of the mortal body into the immortal, Daoist cultivation as the path to transcendence
nodes.neumannArchetype: the transformed sage who has undergone the alchemical opus of self-transmutation
nodes.birthCircumstances: The document had been copied by the grandson of the keeper of Ho Tong Bio Temple in Banyuwangi on June 2, 1880, at Buleleng, Bali.

nodes.name: Ajax the Lesser
nodes.domain: war, speed, impiety, punishment
nodes.object: spear, thunderbolt, trident, helmet, shield, sword
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: smaller than his namesake but swift and fierce, skilled with the spear
nodes.significantEvent: raped Cassandra in the temple of Athena during the sack of Troy, punished by Athena who wrecked his fleet with storms on the voyage home, drowned clinging to a rock after boasting that he survived against the gods will
nodes.symbolism: impiety and its consequences, the warrior whose skill cannot save him from divine retribution, the violation of sanctuary as the worst sin
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow hero who violates the sacred feminine (Athenas temple) and is destroyed by the offended goddess
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Oileus king of Locris

nodes.name: Puti Zushi
nodes.domain: Buddhism, martial arts, Zen, the Shaolin tradition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Buddhist patriarch associated with the founding of Zen/Chan Buddhism and martial arts
nodes.significantEvent: sat facing a wall for nine years in meditation at the Shaolin Temple, associated with the founding of Shaolin Kung Fu, tore off his eyelids to prevent falling asleep during meditation
nodes.symbolism: the paradox of the meditation master who also founds a martial art, stillness as the source of the most powerful movement, the foreign sage who transforms Chinese spirituality
nodes.neumannArchetype: the transcendent masculine who through absolute stillness generates the greatest power, the sage whose ego-death (wall-gazing) opens a new form of consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: identified with Bodhidharma who brought Chan Buddhism from India to China

nodes.name: San Yisheng
nodes.domain: medicine, healing, the Three Sage Doctors
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: one of the Three Sage Doctors of Chinese medical tradition
nodes.significantEvent: one of three legendary physicians worshipped as divine healers in Chinese folk medicine
nodes.symbolism: the threefold healing tradition of Chinese medicine, the sage physician as a divine figure
nodes.neumannArchetype: the healing masculine as one of a sacred triad of physicians

nodes.name: Cronus
nodes.domain: time, harvest, sovereignty, the Golden Age
nodes.characterTrait: cunning, tyrannical, devouring, fearful of prophecy
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: bearded elder, wielding the sickle with which he castrated his father
nodes.significantEvent: castrated his father Uranus with a sickle at his mothers urging, swallowed each of his children at birth to prevent a prophecy of his overthrow, defeated by Zeus in the Titanomachy and imprisoned in Tartarus
nodes.symbolism: the devouring father who consumes his own progeny, the Golden Age ruler overthrown by the new order, time that consumes all things
nodes.neumannArchetype: the devouring father archetype, the Terrible Father who must be overthrown by the hero-son for consciousness to emerge
familyRoles: youngest son of Ouranos and Gaia
father of the first six Olympians
nodes.birthCircumstances: youngest of the twelve Titans, son of Uranus and Gaia
nodes.deathCircumstances: Hesiod, Theogony — imprisoned in Tartarus after Titanomachy; in some traditions (the Orphic and Hellenistic), released to rule the Isles of the Blessed in the Western Ocean
nodes.domain_source: Hesiod, Theogony 154-210 (castration of Ouranos), 459-506 (devouring of children); Apollodorus 1.1.4; Orphic theogony fragments; Plato, Cratylus
nodes.object_source: Cronus iconography — sickle (ἅρπη, with which he castrated Ouranos); the stone he was given to swallow in place of Zeus
nodes.characterTrait_source: Hesiod, Theogony — son-devouring tyrant; in the Orphic-Hellenistic tradition, ruler of the Golden Age
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Hesiod; classical iconography
nodes.significantEvent_source: Hesiod, Theogony 154-210 — youngest son of Ouranos and Gaia; at Gaia's urging castrated his father Ouranos with a sickle while the latter copulated with her, casting the genitals into the sea (from the sea-foam Aphrodite was born). Became king of the Titans. Married his sister Rhea, by whom he had Hestia, Demeter, Hera, Hades, Poseidon, Zeus. Warned by a prophecy that one of his children would overthrow him, he swallowed each at birth. Rhea hid Zeus on Crete and gave Cronus a stone wrapped in swaddling. Zeus eventually forced him to vomit up his siblings, and led them in the Titanomachy. Cronus was imprisoned in Tartarus.
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Hesiod, Theogony 137-138 — son of Ouranos and Gaia
nodes.birthTypes_source: Hesiod, Theogony

nodes.name: Tiamat
nodes.domain: primordial saltwater, the sea, monstrous progeny, primordial motherhood, war, chaos
nodes.object: Tablets of Destiny (given to her champion Kingu); the eleven monsters (mušḫuššu, bashmu, ušumgallu, lahmu-warriors, ugallu, uridimmu, girtablullu, kulullu, kusarikku, etc.)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: dragon, serpentine, open gullet
nodes.significantEvent: Mother and grandmother of the gods (Apsu's spouse). After Apsu is murdered by Ea, she raises an army of eleven monsters under Kingu's command, to whom she gives the Tablets of Destiny. Confronts the gods; defeats Anu and frightens Ea; is finally challenged and slain by Marduk, who pierces her with the four winds and shoots her with his bow. Her body is split: her upper half forms the heavens, her lower half the earth; her tears form the Tigris and Euphrates.
nodes.symbolism: Male-female uroboric unity with Apsu; primordial chaos of water; mother of all gods; split body becomes heaven and earth
nodes.neumannArchetype: Key example of the uroboric Great Mother. Constitutes primordial male-female unity with Apsu.
nodes.birthCircumstances: Primordial; existed before the heavens or earth were named.
nodes.deathCircumstances: Slain by Marduk in single combat. He distends her with the four winds, shoots her with his bow, splits her body, and forms the cosmos from her remains.
nodes.domain_source: Enuma Elish I 1-10 (waters mingling); II-IV (her army and battle); IV 137-146 (her body becomes the cosmos)
nodes.object_source: Enuma Elish I 132-146 (creation of monsters); I 147-162 (Tablets of Destiny given to Kingu)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Enuma Elish I 1-10, 132-162; II-III (challenge); IV 93-104 (battle and slaying); IV 137-146 (body→sky); V 53-60 (tears→Tigris/Euphrates)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Enuma Elish I 1-4 — primordial, existed before the heavens were named
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Enuma Elish I 1-4
nodes.animals_source: Enuma Elish I 132-146 (her army of monsters); standard iconography of the primordial dragon
nodes.characterTrait_source: Enuma Elish I-IV — initially mothering and patient with the noisy younger gods, only roused to wrath by Apsu's murder; then implacable, raging, dragon-form
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Enuma Elish IV 95-104 (her open gullet, her body that splits)

nodes.name: Valkyrie
nodes.domain: war, death, prophecy, fate
nodes.object: spear, shield, helm, mail; the cup of mead they bear to the einherjar; the loom of war (Darraðarljóð, where the warp is intestines and the weights are heads)
nodes.characterTrait: war-choosing, slain-selecting, mead-bearing in Valhǫll, sometimes loving (the swan-maiden / mortal-husband tradition)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Armed warrior-maidens; named valkyries include Hildr, Þrúðr, Hlǫkk, Herfjǫtur, Gǫll, Geirahǫð, Randgríð, Ráðgríð, Reginleif (Grímnismál 36). Often depicted with swan-cloaks in the swan-maiden variant (Vǫlundarkviða).
nodes.significantEvent: Choose the slain on battlefields; bear them to Valhǫll where they pour mead for Odin's einherjar; in some traditions, swan-maidens who can be entrapped by men (Vǫlundarkviða — Vǫlundr and his brothers).
nodes.symbolism: Death-bringing feminine warrior; waelcyrge (chooser of the slain); associated with ravens and fate
nodes.neumannArchetype: Death-bringing feminine warrior. Waelcyrge (chooser of slain) connects to fate.
nodes.birthCircumstances: In some traditions, daughters of mortal kings whom Odin elevates (Sigrún, Sváva, Sigrdrífa); in others, divine from the beginning.
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 36; Grímnismál 36 (the thirteen named valkyries); Vǫluspá 30; Darraðarljóð (the valkyrie-weaving song); Helgakviða Hundingsbana I-II; Vǫlsunga saga (Sigrdrífa/Brynhildr)
nodes.object_source: Darraðarljóð; standard valkyrie iconography
nodes.characterTrait_source: Vǫluspá 30; Grímnismál 36; Darraðarljóð; Helgakviða
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Grímnismál 36; Vǫlundarkviða
nodes.significantEvent_source: Gylfaginning 36; Grímnismál 36; Darraðarljóð; Vǫlundarkviða
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Helgakviða Hundingsbana II; Sigrdrífumál
nodes.birthTypes_source: Helgakviða II

nodes.name: Castor and Pollux
nodes.domain: horsemanship, boxing, sailing, rescue, brotherhood
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: twin young men, often helmeted and mounted, associated with twin stars
nodes.significantEvent: Pollux shared his immortality with his dead twin Castor so they alternate between Olympus and Hades, they became the constellation Gemini, patrons of sailors who appear as St Elmos fire
nodes.symbolism: the bond of brotherhood that transcends death, the Indo-European Divine Twins archetype, mortality and immortality as twin aspects of human nature
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Divine Twins representing the duality of mortal and immortal, the dual hero who bridges the worlds
nodes.birthCircumstances: sons of Leda, Castor was mortal son of Tyndareus while Pollux was divine son of Zeus who came to Leda as a swan, born from an egg

nodes.domain: protection, driving away enemies, repelling evil
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess who drove away enemies and evil influences
nodes.significantEvent: invoked to repel and drive away enemies, evil spirits, and negative influences from the home and community
nodes.symbolism: the divine feminine power of repulsion, the protective force that drives evil away, the defensive aspect of the household goddess
nodes.neumannArchetype: the protective Great Mother who drives the shadow away from consciousness

nodes.name: Eve
nodes.domain: creation, motherhood, first pair of humans
nodes.object: the rib from which she was formed; the forbidden fruit; the serpent; fig leaves and animal-skin garments
nodes.characterTrait: created-from-Adam, helper-companion, deceived (in 1 Timothy 2:14 framing), ashamed, sorrow-bearing in childbirth, mother of Cain, Abel, and Seth
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Formed from Adam's rib (Genesis 2:21-22); named ʾiššāh ('woman') because taken from ʾīš ('man'); later named Ḥawwāh (Eve, 'living') by Adam after the curse, 'because she was the mother of all living' (Genesis 3:20).
nodes.significantEvent: Formed from Adam's rib (Genesis 2:21-22). Tempted by the serpent and eats from the tree of knowledge, gives to Adam (Genesis 3:1-7). Cursed with painful childbirth and subordination to husband (3:16). Bears Cain and Abel (4:1-2); after Abel's murder, bears Seth (4:25), saying 'God has appointed me another seed in place of Abel'.
nodes.symbolism: Unnatural origin from Adam reverses natural birth; 'the naked Eve. Her belly is life'; resembles Astarte and Gaea
nodes.neumannArchetype: Her origin from Adam is an 'unnatural symbol.' In Jewish aspect, life-affirming.
nodes.birthCircumstances: Formed by YHWH from Adam's rib while Adam was in deep sleep (taʾrdēmāh).
nodes.deathCircumstances: Mortal per the curse of Genesis 3:19 ('to dust you shall return'); her death is not narrated in the biblical text.
nodes.domain_source: Genesis 2:18-25, 3:1-24, 4:1-2, 4:25; 1 Timothy 2:13-14; Quran 7:19-25, 20:117-123 (the Quran does not name Eve, calling her zawjuhu 'his spouse', though later Islamic tradition gives the name Ḥawwāʾ); rabbinic and Christian tradition extensively
nodes.birthTypes_source: Genesis 2:21-22
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Genesis 2:21-22
nodes.deathTypes_source: implied in Genesis 3:19 (curse of mortality); explicit death not narrated

nodes.domain: hunting, herding, pastoral life, prophecy
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: son of Hermes, combining hunter and herdsman
nodes.significantEvent: Agreus inherited the gift of prophecy from his mother Sose and was a skilled hunter, Nomios was a shepherd god
nodes.symbolism: the dual mastery of hunting and herding as complementary aspects of pastoral civilization
nodes.neumannArchetype: the dual pastoral hero combining the active (hunter) and contemplative (herder) masculine

nodes.name: Muzha
nodes.domain: war, Buddhism, protection, the Investiture of the Gods
nodes.object: staff, ring of wind and fire
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: second son of Li Jing, warrior wielding ring weapons
nodes.significantEvent: originally named Mu Zha, fought alongside his father in the Investiture of the Gods, became a Buddhist guardian, in Journey to the West serves as an attendant to Guanyin
nodes.symbolism: the second son who finds his path through Buddhist service, the warrior transformed into the bodhisttvas attendant, the middle child who bridges family duty and spiritual vocation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine in service to the compassionate feminine (Guanyin), the warrior redirected from destruction to protection through spiritual transformation
nodes.birthCircumstances: second son of Li Jing and Lady Yin, brother of Jinzha and Nezha, disciple of Guanyin Bodhisattva

nodes.name: Tu'er Shen
nodes.domain: love between men, matchmaking, rabbits, the moon
nodes.characterTrait: compassionate, matchmaking, rabbit-formed, protector of same-sex love
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: rabbit deity associated with the moon, patron of male homosexual love
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped in some temples as the patron of male same-sex love, ties red threads of fate between men destined to be partners, his cult represents a rare positive divine endorsement of same-sex love in traditional religion
nodes.symbolism: divine sanction of same-sex love, the red thread of fate binding male lovers, the rabbit as a symbol of the moon and of same-sex desire in Chinese culture
nodes.neumannArchetype: the anima in its role of connecting masculine consciousnesses through the bond of love, the divine matchmaker who transcends the normative heterosexual pairing
nodes.birthCircumstances: a rabbit spirit who became a patron deity of homosexual men in Chinese folk religion

nodes.name: Adam
nodes.domain: creation, first man, knowledge, mortality, first pair of humans
nodes.object: the dust/ʿadamah from which he was formed; the breath of life; Eden's garden; the tree of knowledge of good and evil; the rib (Genesis 2:21-22); fig leaves and animal-skin garments (Genesis 3:7, 21)
nodes.characterTrait: formed from earth, image-of-God-bearing, naming the animals, originally innocent, then disobedient, ashamed, exiled, mortal, mournful (over Cain-Abel), prolific (930 years, many sons and daughters per Gen 5)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Formed from the dust/ʿadamah of the ground (Genesis 2:7); breathed into by YHWH; created in the divine image (Genesis 1:27). In rabbinic tradition (b. Hagigah 12a, Genesis Rabbah 8:1), originally a giant whose body extended from one end of the world to the other before being diminished. Lived 930 years (Genesis 5:5).
nodes.significantEvent: Formed from dust by YHWH (Genesis 2:7); placed in Eden; names the animals (Genesis 2:19-20); receives Eve from his rib (2:21-22); transgresses the prohibition by eating from the tree of knowledge (Genesis 3); exiled from Eden; toils on the cursed ground; fathers Cain, Abel, and Seth (and other sons and daughters); dies at 930 years. In Quran, Allah commands the angels and Iblis to bow to Adam; Iblis refuses; Adam is taught the names; tempted by Iblis; repents and is forgiven (Quran 2:30-39, 7:19-25, 20:115-123).
nodes.symbolism: First human; fall from grace; origin of sin and mortality; dust to dust
deathTypes: mortal — natural death after long life
nodes.birthCircumstances: Formed from the dust of the ground (Hebrew ʿadamah, the source of his name) by YHWH, who breathed the breath of life into his nostrils. In Quran, formed from clay (ṣalṣāl) and shaped by Allah's two hands (Surah 38:75).
nodes.deathCircumstances: Lived 930 years and died (Genesis 5:5). The first human death narrated in Genesis is Abel's (Genesis 4:8); Adam's own death is recorded only in the genealogy.
nodes.domain_source: Genesis 1:26-28, 2:7-25, 3:1-24, 5:1-5; Quran 2:30-39, 7:11-25, 15:26-44, 20:115-123; Talmudic and Midrashic literature passim
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Genesis 1:26-28, 2:7, 5:5; b. Hagigah 12a; Genesis Rabbah 8:1; Quran 15:26-29

nodes.name: Polemos
nodes.domain: war, battle, conflict, strife
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: daemon of war and battle
nodes.significantEvent: personification of warfare itself, the cosmic principle of armed conflict
nodes.symbolism: war as a divine force beyond human control, the spirit of battle that drives nations to conflict
nodes.neumannArchetype: the destructive masculine as the spirit of war itself, the archetype of conflict
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Eris in some traditions, or a separate deity

nodes.name: Eurynome
nodes.domain: universal rule, ocean, the primeval queen, joy, meadows
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful Oceanid goddess who danced upon the waters of chaos before creation
nodes.significantEvent: in Pelasgian myth she danced on the primeval waters and created all things, in Olympian myth she was mother of the Charites (Graces) by Zeus, rescued Hephaestus when he was cast from Olympus
nodes.symbolism: the dancing feminine that creates through movement, the oceanic mother who nurtures the rejected, the joy that undergirds creation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial Great Mother who creates the world through her dance upon the waters of chaos
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Oceanus and Tethys, or the primordial goddess who danced on the sea before creation

nodes.name: Ishtar
nodes.domain: war, love, sex, fertility, the morning and evening star (Venus), kingship, divine sovereignty, justice
nodes.object: lion-driven chariot, eight-pointed star, bow and quiver
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Young armed woman, crowned with the šugurra (horned crown), holding bow and quiver; sometimes depicted with breasts bared; standing on her lion or in her lion-driven chariot. The eight-pointed star is her cosmic emblem.
nodes.significantEvent: The Akkadian Ishtar's Descent to the Underworld (parallel to Sumerian Inanna's Descent, but shorter and lacking the Dumuzi substitution detail). Refusal of Gilgamesh's hand and unleashing the Bull of Heaven against him. Granting kingship to Sargon of Akkad and to Hammurabi.
nodes.symbolism: Great Goddess combining terrible and positive; creatress as potter (Mama/Aruru); with branches/ears of grain
nodes.neumannArchetype: Both terrible and positive. At negative pole as terrible Ishtar, but also Great Goddess encompassing multiple aspects.
nodes.birthCircumstances: In Akkadian theology, daughter of Anu (the sky-god). This differs from Sumerian Inanna, who is daughter of Nanna and Ningal. Both genealogies are preserved on cognate nodes.
nodes.domain_source: Standard Babylonian Ishtar's Descent to the Underworld (Lambert/Foster); Epic of Gilgamesh tablets VI-VII; Erra Epic I; Codex Hammurabi prologue (col. III); Ishtar Hymn of Iddin-Dagan (Sumerian-Akkadian bilingual); Enheduanna's nin-me-shara (= ETCSL 4.07.2)
nodes.object_source: Old Babylonian Ishtar iconography; Ishtar Gate reliefs; Ishtar Hymn of Iddin-Dagan

nodes.name: Emperor Yi of Chu
nodes.domain: kingship, defeat, the Mandate of Heaven lost
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: last ruler of the Chu kingdom during the Chu-Han contention
nodes.significantEvent: initially the most powerful warlord after the fall of Qin, defeated by Liu Bang at the Battle of Gaixia, refused to cross the Wu River and committed suicide rather than face dishonor
nodes.symbolism: noble defeat and the choice of death over dishonor, the loss of the Mandate of Heaven, the tragic hero whose pride prevents survival
nodes.neumannArchetype: the tragic warrior king whose refusal to retreat embodies the masculine preference for death over the shame of defeat

nodes.name: The Primordial Waters
nodes.domain: chaos, creation, the unconscious, potential
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: boundless dark waters existing before creation, sometimes personified as a serpent or dragon
nodes.significantEvent: from the primordial waters creation emerges across Nun (Egyptian), Apsu-Tiamat (Mesopotamian), the Deep (Biblical), cosmic ocean (Hindu)
nodes.symbolism: the state before differentiation, the unconscious from which consciousness emerges, creative potential preceding form
nodes.neumannArchetype: the uroboric state of undifferentiated wholeness, the Great Round as primordial ocean

nodes.name: Uroboros
nodes.domain: creation, eternity, cyclical renewal, primordial chaos
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: serpent or dragon devouring its own tail, forming a circle
nodes.significantEvent: appears in ancient Egyptian funerary texts as symbol of the sun cycle, adopted across Greek alchemy and Norse cosmology as Jormungandr
nodes.symbolism: eternal cyclic renewal, unity of creation and destruction, the Great Round preceding all differentiation, wholeness containing all opposites
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Round preceding all differentiation, contains both masculine and feminine, precedes the separation of the World Parents
nodes.birthCircumstances: primordial symbol predating individual mythological traditions

nodes.name: Kuebiko
nodes.domain: agriculture, wisdom, knowledge, scarecrows, immobility
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a scarecrow god who cannot walk but knows everything that happens in the world, sits in the fields and observes all
nodes.significantEvent: despite being unable to move, Kuebiko knows everything in the world because he stands in the fields and observes ceaselessly, identified with the scarecrow (kakashi) that watches over the rice paddies
nodes.symbolism: the scarecrow as the all-seeing observer, wisdom through immobility and constant observation, the agricultural guardian who cannot move but knows all, the paralyzed wise one
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wise old man trapped in immobility, consciousness that knows everything but cannot act, the observer-wisdom of the agricultural world

nodes.domain: earth, soil, mountains, the underworld, Tibetan Buddhism
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: earth deity or earth demon in Chinese-Tibetan tradition
nodes.significantEvent: associated with the earth and underworld in Chinese Buddhist and folk traditions influenced by Tibetan religion
nodes.symbolism: the raw earth power beneath the civilized surface, the chthonic force that must be placated
nodes.neumannArchetype: the chthonic masculine of the deep earth, the raw telluric power beneath consciousness

nodes.name: Hermes
nodes.domain: travel, commerce, trickery, communication, boundaries, souls, thieves, language
nodes.object: caduceus, winged sandals, winged helmet, lyre, shepherds crook
nodes.characterTrait: clever, cunning, liminal, guiding, inventive, eloquent, mischievous
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: youthful, athletic, beardless in later art, winged sandals and hat, carrying caduceus
nodes.significantEvent: stole Apollos cattle on the day he was born, invented the lyre from a tortoise shell, guided souls to the underworld as psychopomp, slew the hundred-eyed giant Argus
nodes.symbolism: the crossing of all boundaries, communication between divine and human realms, the psychopomp who guides between life and death, trickery as creative intelligence
nodes.neumannArchetype: the soul-guide (Seelenfuhrer) who mediates between consciousness and the unconscious, the snake-entwined healing staff connecting the worlds
familyRoles: son of Zeus and Maia (the eldest Pleiad)
god of trade, thieves, travelers, heralds
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Zeus and the Pleiad Maia, born in a cave on Mount Cyllene in Arcadia
nodes.domain_source: Homer, Iliad and Odyssey passim (the psychopomp role, the messenger-role); Homeric Hymn to Hermes (the central comic-trickster source); Hesiod, Theogony 938-939; Apollodorus 3.10.2; the Athenian Hermai pillar-cult
nodes.object_source: Hermes iconography — caduceus (κηρύκειον — the herald's staff with intertwined serpents); winged sandals (πέδιλα); winged petasos-hat; the Hermai (boundary-marker pillars topped with his bust)
nodes.animals_source: Hermes's sacred animals: ram (his prime sacrificial animal); cock (Hermes Trismegistos's herald); tortoise (from whose shell he made the first lyre as a newborn); hare; messengers-of-various-kinds
nodes.characterTrait_source: Homeric Hymn to Hermes; Homer; the Apolline contrast
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard Hermes iconography — youthful athletic male, wearing winged petasos and winged sandals, bearing the caduceus; sometimes bearded in archaic depictions
nodes.significantEvent_source: Homeric Hymn to Hermes — born of Zeus and Maia in a cave on Mount Cyllene at dawn; by midday he had stolen Apollo's cattle and made the first lyre from a tortoise-shell; argued his case before Zeus; gave the lyre to Apollo (who became master of music); received the caduceus and the office of messenger and psychopomp in exchange; the slayer of Argus (sent by Hera to guard Io); the conductor of Persephone's annual ascent; the night-time messenger of dreams
nodes.eventTypes_source: Homeric Hymn to Hermes; Homer; Apollodorus
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Homeric Hymn to Hermes — born in a cave on Mount Cyllene at dawn
nodes.birthTypes_source: Homeric Hymn to Hermes

nodes.name: Lady of the Beasts
nodes.domain: hunt, wild animals, wilderness, fertility, sovereignty over nature
nodes.characterTrait: wild, primordial, sovereign, untamed, protective of animals
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: female figure flanked by animals, often winged, grasping beasts in each hand
nodes.significantEvent: depicted on Minoan seals and Greek pottery as Potnia Theron, identified with Artemis and Circe in Homer
nodes.symbolism: primordial feminine sovereignty over the animal world, the Great Goddess in her aspect as mistress of nature, predating Olympian religion
nodes.neumannArchetype: ancient form of the Great Goddess predating differentiated pantheons, the feminine as sovereign over all living things
nodes.birthCircumstances: Neolithic and Bronze Age archetype surviving into classical mythology

nodes.name: Ra
nodes.domain: sun, sky, creation, order
nodes.object: solar barque (the Mandjet by day, the Mesektet by night); the Aten (the visible sun-disk); the ankh; the was-scepter
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Originally depicted as a falcon-headed man wearing the sun-disk; in his Re-Horakhty composite form, a falcon-headed king; in the Amduat night-journey, ram-headed; the Aten as the visible disk itself with rays ending in hands.
nodes.significantEvent: Daily traverses the sky in his solar barque, descending into the Duat at sunset to be regenerated through the twelve hours of night, fighting the serpent Apep (Apophis) who attempts to swallow the sun. At dawn re-emerges renewed. The Litany of Re names his 74 forms; the Amduat narrates his nightly journey hour by hour. In Heliopolitan theology, identified with or as the supreme creator (Atum-Ra). Sent his Eye (Hathor-Sekhmet) to destroy rebellious humanity, then relented and saved them by tricking her with beer dyed red.
nodes.symbolism: Sun god born from self-generating mother Neith; endangered son protected by cow goddess recitations
nodes.neumannArchetype: Born from self-generating mother. The heavenly cow goddess composed recitations for her endangered son Ra.
nodes.birthCircumstances: In Heliopolitan theology, self-engendered as Atum-Ra rising from the primordial Nun on the benben-stone, masturbating or spitting forth Shu and Tefnut.
nodes.domain_source: Pyramid Texts (the oldest religious corpus, c. 2400-2300 BCE); Coffin Texts; Book of the Dead; the Litany of Re; the Amduat ("Book of the Hidden Chamber"); the Book of Gates; the Book of Caverns; the New Kingdom royal-tomb sun-hymns

nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Egyptian iconography from Old Kingdom onward; Amduat

nodes.name: Aeolus
nodes.domain: wind, storms, seafaring
nodes.characterTrait: hospitable, obedient to the gods, sovereign over winds
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: king dwelling on the floating island of Aeolia
nodes.significantEvent: gave Odysseus a bag containing all adverse winds to ensure safe passage home, but his crew opened it and they were blown back
nodes.symbolism: divine control over natural forces, the fragility of human discipline before temptation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the keeper of elemental forces, the threshold guardian on the heros journey
nodes.birthCircumstances: In Greek mythology, Aeolus (; , ), the son of Hippotes, was the ruler of the winds encountered by Odysseus in Homer's Odyssey.

nodes.name: Securitas
nodes.domain: security, safety, stability, freedom from anxiety
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: relaxed woman leaning against a column or seated at ease, personification of security and safety
nodes.significantEvent: appeared on coins of emperors who wished to emphasize the security and stability of their reign, represented the absence of threat and the calm of assured safety
nodes.symbolism: the relaxed posture as the state of total security, the column as the support of stability, safety as a divine feminine gift to the state
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of security, the feminine ground of being that provides the stability from which consciousness can safely operate

nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Erebus (Darkness) and Nyx (Night), brother of Hemera (Day)

nodes.name: Nut
nodes.domain: sky, cosmos, death-and-rebirth (swallows the sun each evening, gives birth to it each morning); mother of stars; consort of Geb
nodes.object: ankh; the sun and stars on her star-studded body
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Anthropomorphic woman arching over the earth (Geb) with her hands and feet touching the four horizons, her body star-studded; in the Book of Nut, swallows the sun each evening and gives birth to it each morning (which technically makes her endlessly pregnant/parturient).
nodes.significantEvent: Daughter of Shu and Tefnut; sister-wife of Geb. Geb impregnated her, and Shu separated them. The five epagomenal days of the Egyptian calendar were created by Thoth specifically so Nut could give birth on them (Ra having cursed her not to give birth on any day of the existing 360-day year). On these five days she bore: Osiris, Horus the Elder (Haroeris), Set, Isis, and Nephthys. Daily swallows the sun at the western horizon and births it at the eastern. The deceased pharaoh climbs up Nut's body to rejoin the stars.
nodes.symbolism: Celestial goddess; symbol of femininity; Lady of Heaven; goddess of rebirth but also death as Nuit
nodes.neumannArchetype: Celestial vessel-goddess. 'Goddess of rebirth, but she also has the character of death as Nuit.'
eventTypes: daily swallowing and birthing of the sun
nodes.birthCircumstances: Daughter of Shu and Tefnut.

nodes.name: Demeter
nodes.domain: agriculture, grain, fertility, motherhood, the Eleusinian Mysteries, seasons, law
nodes.characterTrait: grieving, nourishing, life-giving, wrathful when wronged, lawgiving
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: mature, beautiful woman, often veiled or crowned with grain, carrying a torch
nodes.significantEvent: searches desperately for her abducted daughter Persephone, causes universal famine until Persephone is returned, establishes the Eleusinian Mysteries, pig sacrificed in Thesmophoria festival
nodes.symbolism: the grieving mother, death and rebirth of vegetation, the Eleusinian mystery of grain that dies in earth and is reborn, the mother-daughter bond as the deepest human relationship
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive pole of the Great Mother (M+), the nourishing earth goddess whose loss of the daughter represents the mysteries of death and regeneration
familyRoles: sister of Zeus, Hera, Poseidon, Hades, Hestia
mother of Despoina and the horse Areion (by Poseidon)
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the Titans Cronus and Rhea, swallowed by Cronus at birth and later disgorged
nodes.object_source: Demeter iconography — torch (with which she searched for Persephone); sheaf of grain; cornucopia; poppy; mystic basket (κίστη)
nodes.animals_source: Demeter's sacred animals: snakes (especially in her chariot); pigs (sacrificial); horses (in her Demeter-Erinys form at Telpusa where she was raped by Poseidon-as-stallion)
nodes.domain_source: Homeric Hymn to Demeter (the central source for the Persephone abduction); Hesiod, Theogony 912-914; Pausanias 1.14.1 (the Eleusinian Mysteries); Apollodorus 1.5; the Eleusinian and Thesmophoria cult traditions
nodes.significantEvent_source: Homeric Hymn to Demeter — daughter Persephone abducted by Hades; Demeter wandered the earth in mourning, refusing to allow the grain to grow, threatening universal famine; Zeus intervened; Persephone returned but had eaten pomegranate seeds in the underworld and must spend part of each year there (the seasonal-myth origin); during her stay at Eleusis as a mortal nurse, Demeter taught the Eleusinian Mysteries to Triptolemus and Eumolpus
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Hesiod, Theogony — swallowed by Cronus, regurgitated
nodes.characterTrait_source: Homeric Hymn to Demeter; Hesiod
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Demeter iconography — mature matronly goddess, veiled, with grain-sheaf and torch; the Eleusinian tradition's veiled-mourning aspect
nodes.birthTypes_source: Hesiod, Theogony

nodes.domain: war, twin warriors, the Molionides
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: conjoined or twin warriors of supernatural strength, joined at the hip in some versions
nodes.significantEvent: defeated Heracles in battle at Cleonae, later killed treacherously by Heracles at a truce, their joint strength made them nearly invincible

nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine twins as the doubled masculine, the hero pattern reflected and doubled into invincibility
nodes.birthCircumstances: sons of Poseidon (or Actor) and Molione
nodes.deathCircumstances: However after the latter made peace, the brothers attacked Heracles and were subsequently killed by him outside Cleonae.

nodes.name: Tudigong
nodes.domain: earth, local protection, agriculture, land, prosperity
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: kindly elderly man in simple robes, the most commonly worshipped local deity in China
nodes.significantEvent: every village, neighborhood, and even individual tree can have its own Tudigong shrine, he reports to the City God who reports to the Jade Emperor, guards the local land and its prosperity
nodes.symbolism: the divine in the most local and immediate form, the earth as the foundation of all prosperity, the lowest-ranking official who is nonetheless the most important for daily life, the accessible face of the divine bureaucracy
nodes.neumannArchetype: the earth father in his most localized and benevolent form, the grounding masculine consciousness closest to everyday life
nodes.birthCircumstances: the Earth God, the lowest-ranking deity in the celestial bureaucracy but the most immediately present in everyday life

nodes.name: Tefnut
nodes.domain: moisture, rain, dew, fertility, order, cosmic justice
nodes.object: solar disk and uraeus (in her lion-headed depictions); ankh
nodes.characterTrait: moist, fierce, life-giving, wrathful when provoked, nurturing
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Anthropomorphic woman often lion-headed (occasionally fully leonine); wearing the solar disk and uraeus; sister-consort of Shu.
nodes.significantEvent: Twin-sister and consort of Shu; mother of Geb and Nut. In one mythological cycle (preserved in the Demotic Tefnut-Anhour narrative), Tefnut once fled Egypt to Nubia in anger and had to be brought back by Shu and Thoth, restoring fertility.
nodes.symbolism: moisture as the feminine complement to air, the distant goddess whose return brings life, the lioness rage that must be appeased and transformed into nurturing fertility
nodes.neumannArchetype: the fierce feminine that departs from the patriarchal order and must be wooed back, the Great Mother in her dual aspect of destroyer (lioness) and nurturer (moisture)
nodes.birthCircumstances: Emerged from Atum with her twin-brother Shu in the first generation of the Heliopolitan cosmogony.

nodes.domain: war, demon-slaying, motherhood, supreme goddess (Śākta), protection, lion/tiger-rider, the unapproachable one (durgā), slayer of Mahiṣa
nodes.object: ten-armed: trident (from Śiva), discus (Viṣṇu), conch (Varuṇa), bow-arrows (Vāyu), thunderbolt (Indra), spear (Agni), staff (Yama), goad (Kāla), sword, shield

nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Many-armed (typically ten in Devī Māhātmya, eighteen in some Tantric forms); golden-complexioned; mounted on lion or tiger; bearing weapons of all male gods.
nodes.significantEvent: Emanated from the combined tejas of all male gods when Mahiṣāsura defeated them. Slays Mahiṣa (Devī Māhātmya 2-3), then Śumbha and Niśumbha (5-10), generating Kālī from her brow.
nodes.symbolism: The 'Unapproachable' and 'Perilous'; Indian Terrible Mother; blood sacrifice
nodes.neumannArchetype: The 'Unapproachable' and 'Perilous.' Indian Terrible Mother requiring blood sacrifice.
familyRoles: mother of Gaṇeśa and Skanda (when identified with Pārvatī)
nodes.birthCircumstances: Emanated from combined wrath-radiance of male gods at the Himalayas.

nodes.name: Michael
nodes.domain: war, justice, protection, judgment, strength
nodes.object: sword and scales (in Christian iconography — the weighing of souls at the Last Judgment); the dragon-slaying spear
nodes.characterTrait: warring, princely, protective, the great prince who stands for Israel (Daniel 12:1); contending with Satan over Moses's body (Jude 1:9, citing Assumption of Moses); leader of the heavenly armies
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: In Christian iconography, armed warrior in armor, often with sword raised, sometimes with scales, frequently shown standing on the dragon. His name means 'Who is like God?' (mî kāʾēl) — itself a battle-cry/slogan against the prideful claim 'I will be like the Most High'.
nodes.significantEvent: Disputes with the prince of Persia for 21 days, aided by Gabriel (Daniel 10:13); contends with Satan over the body of Moses (Jude 1:9); leads the heavenly armies against the dragon and casts him out of heaven (Revelation 12:7-9); the great prince who stands at the time of the end (Daniel 12:1). In Islamic angelology, the angel of mercy and provision (Mīkāl, alongside Gabriel/Jibrāʾīl).
nodes.symbolism: Divine warrior; heavenly champion against evil; protector of the faithful; cosmic battle between good and evil
nodes.birthCircumstances: Created angelic being. Archangel.

nodes.name: Marduk
nodes.domain: kingship of the gods, Babylon, justice, magic and incantation, the planet Jupiter, agriculture (in his Asalluhi aspect), creation and cosmogony
nodes.object: bow and quiver, Tablets of Destiny (taken from Kingu), four winds (gift of Anu), thunderbolt and lightning, the great net, the mušḫuššu-dragon as mount-companion
nodes.characterTrait: champion, kingly, four-eared and four-eyed, wise, oracular, magical (master of incantation)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: four-eyed, four-eared, of grand stature, surrounded by aura
nodes.significantEvent: Born to Ea and Damkina in pure Apsû (EE I 78-83). Receives the four winds from his great-grandfather Anu (IV 41-46). When Anu and Ea fail to confront the avenging Tiamat, the gods elect Marduk as their champion (II-III). Slays Tiamat in single combat (IV 93-104) and splits her body to form the cosmos (IV-V). Establishes the constellations and the calendar (V). Creates humanity from the blood of the slain Kingu (VI 33-37). Is established as king of the gods and given his fifty names (VI-VII). Founds Babylon as the gods' shrine.
nodes.symbolism: Patriarchal sun god who defeats uroboric mother; creates ordered world from chaos
nodes.neumannArchetype: Patriarchal sun god who defeats Tiamat, splitting her body to create heaven and earth.
nodes.birthCircumstances: Born in pure Apsû (the freshwater abyss) to Ea and Damkina. Endowed at birth with quadrupled senses and prodigious strength.

nodes.object_source: Enuma Elish tablet IV 35-36 (bow), 41-46 (winds), 39-40 (thunderbolt), 95-104 (net); IV 121 (Tablets of Destiny)

nodes.domain: loyalty, sacrifice, remonstrance, the Shang Dynasty

nodes.significantEvent: remonstrated against King Zhous cruelty and was executed by being roasted alive on a bronze pillar (cannon burning), one of the first martyrs of righteous remonstrance

nodes.birthCircumstances: minister to the tyrannical King Zhou of Shang
nodes.deathCircumstances: King Di Yi's Supreme Minister]] Mei Bo () was an official of the Shang dynasty who was killed by Di Xin, King Zhou of Shang.

nodes.name: Inanna
nodes.domain: war, love, fertility, sky/heaven, kingship, divine sovereignty, the storehouse, transformation, the Venus star, the underworld passage
nodes.object: seven me (the cosmic offices/garments worn during her descent), the šugurra-crown, lapis-lazuli necklace, the pala-garment, mascara, breastplate
nodes.characterTrait: passionate, powerful, contradictory, paradoxical, desirous, acquisitive, descending, quarrelsome with kin, protective of her favourites
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Young woman, often armed and crowned with the šugurra (horned crown), wearing the divine measuring-line and pe (lapis-lazuli rod). In her sex/love aspect: voluptuous, breasts bared. In her warrior aspect: beard sometimes attributed by Enheduanna ('She wears manliness in her hand'). Standing on her lion or with the lion-driven chariot.
nodes.significantEvent: Acquired the me (divine offices) from Enki by getting him drunk in Eridu and absconding with them by boat to Uruk. Defeated the mountain Ebih. Descended to the netherworld through seven gates, was killed by Ereshkigal and hung from a hook, was rescued by Enki's emissaries, and returned by substituting Dumuzi for herself. Her courtship with Dumuzi is celebrated in the Sumerian sacred-marriage hymns.
nodes.symbolism: Sumerian Great Goddess; precursor to Ishtar
nodes.neumannArchetype: Sumerian precursor to Babylonian Ishtar.
nodes.birthCircumstances: Daughter of the moon-god Nanna/Suen and Ningal; sister of the sun-god Utu/Shamash and of the netherworld queen Ereshkigal.
nodes.deathCircumstances: Hung on a hook in the netherworld by Ereshkigal; revived by emissaries (kurgarra and galatura) sent by Enki; required to send Dumuzi as her substitute.
nodes.domain_source: Inanna and Ebih lines 1-25 (ETCSL 1.3.2 — war); the Dumuzi courtship cycle ETCSL 4.08.01-33 (love, fertility); her name nin-an-ak 'Lady of Heaven' (sky); Inanna and Enki ETCSL 1.3.1 (acquisition of the me — sovereignty); the Iddin-Dagan hymn (sacred marriage, kingship); Enheduanna's nin-me-šara ETCSL 4.07.2 (transformation/paradox). 'Death' replaced with 'underworld passage' — she visits the underworld in Inanna's Descent (ETCSL 1.4.1) but Ereshkigal is the death-goddess.

nodes.name: Aruru
nodes.domain: creation of humanity, motherhood, midwifery, the womb, kingship-conferring
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Mother-goddess; standard mother-deity iconography (matronly, sometimes nursing).
nodes.significantEvent: In Atrahasis: creates humanity from clay mixed with the blood of slain god We-ila/Geshtu-e, on Enki's instruction. In Gilgamesh: at Anu's command, pinches off clay and creates Enkidu as a foil for Gilgamesh.
nodes.symbolism: Creatress as potter; creates humanity from clay
nodes.neumannArchetype: Creatress/potter figure. Variant of Mama/Nintu.
nodes.domain_source: Atrahasis I 192-260 (Aruru/Mami creates humans from clay mixed with the blood of slain god We-ila); Epic of Gilgamesh I 101-112 (Aruru pinches off clay and creates Enkidu); Enuma Elish VI 33-37 (parallel humanity-from-blood tradition)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Atrahasis I 192-260; Epic of Gilgamesh I 101-112
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard Sumerian-Akkadian mother-goddess iconography; Atrahasis I
nodes.characterTrait_source: Atrahasis I 192-260; Gilgamesh I 101-112 (her clay-pinching for Enkidu)
nodes.object_source: Atrahasis I; Gilgamesh I 101-112 (the clay she pinches off)

nodes.name: Wudao Jiangjun
nodes.domain: the underworld, road spirits, guidance of the dead
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: generals of the five roads in the underworld
nodes.significantEvent: guide the dead along the five paths of the underworld, ensuring souls reach their proper courts for judgment
nodes.symbolism: the five directions of the afterlife, the roads of death as requiring divine guidance
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine guides through the underworld labyrinth of the unconscious

nodes.name: Gabriel
nodes.domain: revelation, communication, annunciation, prophecy, mercy
nodes.object: trumpet (later Christian and Islamic eschatological tradition — the trumpet at the Last Day, though the biblical text never explicitly names the trumpeter); scroll (in Islamic tradition, the medium of revelation)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: In Daniel 8-9, of human appearance; in Luke 1, terrifies Zechariah and reassures Mary. His name means 'Strength of God' (gəbar ʾēl). In Islamic tradition (per the hadith), Muhammad sees Gabriel in his true form filling the horizon (Bukhari, Sahih).
nodes.significantEvent: Interprets Daniel's visions of the ram and goat (Daniel 8:16-26) and the seventy weeks (Daniel 9:21-27). Announces John's conception to Zechariah (Luke 1:11-20). Announces Jesus's conception to Mary (Luke 1:26-38). In Islamic tradition, the angel of revelation: brings the Quran piecemeal to Muhammad over 23 years; first encounter at Mt. Hira ('Iqraʾ' = 'Recite!'); also said to have visited earlier prophets including Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses.
nodes.symbolism: Divine messenger; herald of God; bridge between divine and human; revelation and truth
nodes.birthCircumstances: Created angelic being.
nodes.domain_source: Daniel 8:16-26, 9:21-27 (interpreting Daniel's visions); Luke 1:11-20 (annunciation to Zechariah), 1:26-38 (annunciation to Mary); Quran 2:97-98, 16:102, 26:193 (named as Jibrāʾīl, the angel of revelation, who brings the Quran to Muhammad); 1 Enoch 9, 20:7, 40:6; rabbinic and patristic tradition; b. Yoma 77a (Gabriel and the angel-name etymologies)
nodes.object_source: Christian and Islamic eschatological tradition; standard Annunciation iconography
nodes.characterTrait_source: Daniel 8-9; Luke 1; Quran 2:97-98
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Daniel 8-9; Luke 1; Sahih al-Bukhari (the hadith of Gabriel)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Daniel 8-9; Luke 1; Quran 2:97; Sahih al-Bukhari (the iqraʾ hadith)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Standard angelology
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Standard angelology

nodes.name: Dionysus
nodes.domain: wine, ecstasy, theater, fertility, ritual madness, death and rebirth, vegetation
nodes.object: thyrsus, kantharos (wine cup), ivy crown, grapevine, mask
nodes.animals: bull, panther, leopard, serpent, dolphin, donkey
nodes.characterTrait: ecstatic, transformative, dangerous, liberating, maddening, joyful
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: effeminate, beautiful, sometimes bearded and robed, sometimes youthful and androgynous, crowned with ivy
nodes.significantEvent: establishes his cult across Greece against opposition, drives resisters mad, descends to the underworld to rescue his mother Semele, reconciled with Apollo at Delphi
nodes.symbolism: the dissolution of individual identity in ecstasy, the dying and rising god of vegetation, the union of civilization and wildness, wine as divine madness
nodes.neumannArchetype: the ecstatic-matriarchal realm, the son-lover of the Great Mother who dies and is reborn, his opposition to Apollo is superficial as both are reconciled at Delphi
familyRoles: twice-born (from Semele's incineration, then from Zeus's thigh)
husband of Ariadne (after Theseus abandoned her on Naxos)
sometimes counted as the 12th Olympian (replacing Hestia)
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Zeus and the mortal Semele, born from Zeus thigh after Semele was destroyed by Zeus thunderbolt, in Orphic tradition torn apart as Zagreus and reborn
nodes.deathCircumstances: In the Orphic Zagreus tradition, the infant Dionysus is lured by the Titans with toys, dismembered, and devoured (except for his heart, saved by Athena). Zeus consumes the heart and conceives Dionysus anew with Semele; the second-born Dionysus is then re-born from Zeus's thigh after Semele is consumed by Zeus's manifest glory. Hence his epithet διμήτωρ (twice-born) / dimētōr.
nodes.object_source: Dionysus iconography — thyrsus (fennel-staff topped with pinecone, wreathed in ivy); wine-cup (kantharos); ivy and grape-vine wreath; the panther- or leopard-pelt (nebris)
nodes.animals_source: Dionysus's sacred animals: bull (his prime epiphany-form, frequent in Euripides's Bacchae); goat (the τράγος from whose sacrifice tragedy is etymologized); leopard/panther (his chariot-team); snake (his cradle-companion as the divine child); donkey
nodes.domain_source: Euripides, Bacchae (the central tragic source); Homeric Hymn 1, 7, 26 (to Dionysus); Hesiod, Theogony 940-942; Apollodorus 3.4.3 (the Semele narrative); Nonnus, Dionysiaca (5th c. CE — the most extensive narrative); the Athenian Dionysia (the dramatic-festival origin)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Apollodorus 3.4.3
nodes.significantEvent_source: Apollodorus 3.4.3 — son of Zeus and Semele; Hera persuaded Semele to ask Zeus to reveal his full glory; she was incinerated; Zeus rescued the fetal Dionysus and sewed him into his thigh until birth (the 'twice-born' god, διμήτωρ or Διθύραμβος); raised by Hermes and the nymphs of Mount Nysa; wandered the world teaching wine-cultivation; the Bacchic frenzy of his maenads; the Pentheus-tearing in Thebes; rescued his mother Semele from Hades; descended to bring Ariadne back from Naxos
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Apollodorus 3.4.3 — fetal Dionysus rescued from incinerated Semele, sewn into Zeus's thigh
nodes.deathTypes_source: Orphic theology (Olympiodorus, In Phaed. 1.3); Nonnus, Dionysiaca 6
nodes.deathCircumstances_source: Orphic fragments (OF 35, 220 Bernabé); Nonnus, Dionysiaca 6.169-205; Olympiodorus, In Phaedonem 1.3-6; Diodorus Siculus 3.62.6, 3.64.1-2, 5.75.4
nodes.characterTrait_source: Euripides, Bacchae; the Dionysiac mystery-cult tradition; the Plutarchan Isiac comparison; Nonnus
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard Dionysus iconography — variable: youthful effeminate beardless (the late-classical type) or mature bearded (the archaic type); ivy-crowned; carrying thyrsus; sometimes riding panther

nodes.name: Pandora
nodes.domain: creation, womankind, curiosity, all gifts, deception
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful woman fashioned from clay by Hephaestus, adorned by all the gods
nodes.significantEvent: opened the jar releasing all evils into the world, only Hope remained inside, sent by Zeus as a punishment disguised as a gift to Epimetheus
nodes.symbolism: the all-giver whose gifts include suffering, the feminine as both blessing and curse in patriarchal mythology, curiosity as the price of knowledge
nodes.neumannArchetype: the all-giver aspect of the feminine, associated with Aphrodite as the vessel containing both beauty and destruction
nodes.birthCircumstances: molded from earth by Hephaestus on Zeus orders as punishment for Prometheus theft of fire, each god gave her a gift

nodes.name: Evander of Pallantium
nodes.domain: civilization, colonization, writing, diplomacy, Arcadia
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Arcadian hero who founded the settlement on the Palatine Hill in Rome
nodes.significantEvent: led a group of Arcadian colonists to Italy, founded a settlement on the Palatine Hill sixty years before the Trojan War, introduced writing and music to the Italian natives
nodes.symbolism: the Greek civilizing mission to the west, the Arcadian origins of Roman culture, the bearer of writing and law to the barbarian world
nodes.neumannArchetype: the culture hero who carries consciousness (writing, music, law) from the Greek center to the western frontier
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Hermes and an Arcadian nymph Themis (or Nicostrate/Carmenta)

nodes.symbolism: desire for what is not present, the ache of absence, longing as the deepest form of love, the pain of separation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine principle of longing, desire as the pull of consciousness toward the absent feminine
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Aphrodite, or brother of Eros and Himeros

nodes.domain: fire, warfare, the Investiture of the Gods
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: warrior deity associated with fire and warfare
nodes.significantEvent: figure from the Fengshen Yanyi (Investiture of the Gods), participated in the war between the Shang and Zhou dynasties
nodes.symbolism: fire as a weapon of divine warfare, the loyal warrior in the cosmic conflict
nodes.neumannArchetype: the fiery warrior masculine in the service of cosmic transformation

nodes.name: Heh
nodes.domain: eternity, infinity, endlessness, millions of years
nodes.object: palm ribs (symbolizing years), shen ring of eternity
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: man kneeling on one knee with arms raised supporting the sky, holding palm ribs in each hand, sometimes frog-headed
nodes.significantEvent: represents the concept of millions of years and spatial infinity, part of the Ogdoad who together created the conditions for the emergence of the sun from the primordial waters
nodes.symbolism: eternity as a personified force, the millions of years as the unfathomable depth of time, the kneeling figure supporting infinity, the Ogdoad as the eight forces of pre-creation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial masculine principle of infinite duration, the uroboric eternity that precedes and encompasses all temporal consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the eight primordial deities of the Ogdoad of Hermopolis, personification of infinity

nodes.name: Ganymede
nodes.domain: youth, beauty, cupbearer of the gods, divine desire
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the most beautiful of mortal youths, young Trojan prince
nodes.significantEvent: abducted by Zeus in the form of an eagle (or by the eagle) to serve as cupbearer on Olympus, replacing Hebe, his father received divine horses as compensation
nodes.symbolism: divine desire for mortal beauty, the boy snatched up to heaven, immortality granted through beauty rather than heroic deeds, the origin of the constellation Aquarius
nodes.neumannArchetype: the beautiful youth seized by the sky father, the passive masculine absorbed into the divine through beauty rather than action
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of King Tros of Troy (or Laomedon), descended from Dardanus and Zeus

nodes.name: Antevorta
nodes.domain: foresight, seeing the future, childbirth, prophecy
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: aspect of the goddess Carmenta who sees the future, one of the two Carmentae
nodes.significantEvent: together with Postverta she represents the two aspects of prophetic sight: Antevorta sees the future, Postverta sees the past, invoked during childbirth to see the childs future
nodes.symbolism: prophetic foresight as a feminine divine faculty, the ability to see what is coming as a gift at birth
nodes.neumannArchetype: the forward-looking aspect of the prophetic feminine, the anima that perceives the future

nodes.name: Raphael
nodes.domain: healing, protection, guidance, pilgrimage
nodes.object: staff (as a traveler accompanying Tobias); the fish — heart, liver, gall (which he instructs Tobias to use medicinally and apotropaically); the bonds with which he ties Asmodeus in the Egyptian wilderness (Tobit 8:3)
nodes.characterTrait: healing, accompanying, protective, instructing, hidden (he travels in disguise as Azarias for the duration of the journey, revealing his identity only at the end)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Travels in human form as 'Azarias' (a young Israelite kinsman) for the duration of the Tobit narrative; reveals his angelic identity at the end (Tobit 12:15). His name means 'God heals' (rāphāʾ ʾēl).
nodes.significantEvent: Sent in answer to the simultaneous prayers of Tobit (afflicted by blindness from sparrow droppings) and Sarah (afflicted by Asmodeus, who has killed her seven husbands). Disguised as Azarias, accompanies Tobit's son Tobias on his journey to Media. Instructs Tobias to keep the heart, liver, and gall of a great fish; with these, drives out Asmodeus from Sarah's bridal chamber and heals Tobit's blindness. Reveals himself as 'one of the seven angels who stand and enter before the glory of the Lord' (Tobit 12:15).
nodes.symbolism: Divine healer; guardian of travelers and pilgrims; restoration of sight both physical and spiritual
familyRoles: one of the seven who stand before God
nodes.birthCircumstances: Created angelic being; one of the seven archangels (Tobit 12:15).
nodes.domain_source: Tobit 3:17, 5:4-22, 6:1-12:22 (the central source — Raphael as Azarias accompanying Tobias); 1 Enoch 10:7, 20:3, 22:6, 40:9; Talmudic tradition; rabbinic and Christian angelology
nodes.characterTrait_source: Tobit 5-12
nodes.significantEvent_source: Tobit 3-12 (the entire frame narrative)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Standard angelology
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Tobit 12:15; 1 Enoch 20

nodes.name: Re-Hor-achti
nodes.domain: the sun, the horizon, the rising and setting sun, kingship
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: falcon-headed man with a sun disk, combining Ra and Horus into a single solar deity, representing the sun at the horizon
nodes.significantEvent: represented the sun at the horizon, both at dawn and sunset, the supreme solar deity worshipped at Heliopolis during the New Kingdom, the pharaoh was his earthly representative
nodes.symbolism: the sun at the horizon as the meeting of heaven and earth, the falcon of kingship combined with the sun of creation, the horizon as the threshold between the visible and invisible worlds
nodes.neumannArchetype: the solar Great Father at the threshold of consciousness, the sun of awareness at the horizon between the conscious and unconscious
nodes.birthCircumstances: syncretistic solar deity combining Ra (the sun) and Horus (the falcon king)

nodes.name: Heracles
nodes.domain: strength, heroism, endurance, civilization, protection
nodes.object: club, lion skin, bow, golden apples
nodes.animals: eagle, serpent, snake, bull, horse, lion, ram, boar, dog, dragon, centaur, minotaur, hydra, cerberus
nodes.characterTrait: strong, enduring, wrathful, gluttonous, courageous, suffering
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: massively muscular, bearded, wearing lion skin, carrying club
nodes.significantEvent: completed the Twelve Labors imposed by King Eurystheus, killed his own children in a fit of madness sent by Hera, freed Prometheus, died on a funeral pyre and was apotheosized to Olympus
nodes.symbolism: the mortal who achieves divinity through suffering and labor, civilization triumphing over the monstrous, the hero who must endure the Great Mothers persecution to achieve immortality
nodes.neumannArchetype: the supreme hero who overcomes the Terrible Mother in all her forms through the twelve labors, achieving transformation from mortal to divine
familyRoles: deified at death — ascended to Olympus
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Zeus and the mortal Alcmene, conceived when Zeus took the form of her husband Amphitryon
nodes.domain_source: Homer, Iliad and Odyssey (especially Od. 11.601-628 — the encounter in Hades); Hesiod, Theogony 950-955, Shield of Heracles; Apollodorus 2.4-7 (the central comprehensive narrative); Euripides, Heracles and Alcestis; Sophocles, Trachiniae; Diodorus Siculus 4.8-39
nodes.object_source: Heracles iconography — Nemean lion-skin (after his first labor); great club (κορύνη); bow and arrows (poisoned with Hydra blood); the Cup of Helios (in which he sailed to Erytheia for Geryon's cattle)
nodes.animals_source: Heracles's sacred animals: lion (the Nemean lion he strangled and wore thereafter as his hide-cloak); various labors-creatures (Erymanthian boar, Ceryneian hind, Stymphalian birds, Cretan bull, etc.)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Apollodorus; Euripides; Sophocles
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard Heracles iconography — muscular bearded hero in lion-skin, bearing great club; one of the most-depicted figures in all Greek art
nodes.significantEvent_source: Apollodorus 2.4-7 — son of Zeus and Alcmene (Zeus impersonating her husband Amphitryon); persecuted by Hera from birth (the cradle-snakes which he strangled); married Megara, killed her and their children in Hera-induced madness; performed the Twelve Labors as penance (Nemean lion, Lernaean Hydra, Ceryneian hind, Erymanthian boar, Augean stables, Stymphalian birds, Cretan bull, mares of Diomedes, girdle of Hippolyta, cattle of Geryon, apples of the Hesperides, Cerberus); killed by the poisoned shirt of Nessus given by his jealous wife Deianeira; immolated himself on Mount Oeta; ascended to Olympus, married Hebe, was deified
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Apollodorus 2.4.8 — Zeus impersonating Amphitryon engendered Heracles on Alcmene; Hera delayed his birth so that Eurystheus (a Perseid) was born first and ruled Mycenae over him
nodes.birthTypes_source: Apollodorus 2.4.8
nodes.deathTypes_source: Sophocles, Trachiniae — death by the poisoned-shirt of Nessus (centaur-blood)
nodes.deathCircumstances_source: Sophocles, Trachiniae; Apollodorus 2.7.7 — Deianeira gave him the shirt soaked in Nessus's poisoned blood (thinking it a love-charm); Heracles in agony built a pyre on Mount Oeta and immolated himself; ascended to Olympus and was deified

nodes.name: Raijū
nodes.domain: lightning, thunder beasts, storms, supernatural animals
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a lightning beast, depicted as a cat-like, weasel-like, or wolf-like creature wreathed in lightning
nodes.significantEvent: the companion beast of Raijin that falls to earth with lightning bolts, causing damage where it lands, people would hide under mosquito nets during storms to avoid the raiju
nodes.symbolism: lightning as a living beast that falls from the sky, the storm animal as the embodiment of electrical power, the feral nature of the lightning bolt
nodes.neumannArchetype: the instinctual animal form of lightning, the beast-consciousness of the storm that falls from the sky into the earth

nodes.name: Quetzalcoatl
nodes.domain: wind, rebirth, creation of humanity, civilization, priesthood, the morning star (Venus), maize, light
nodes.object: conch shell pectoral (ehēca-cōzcatl, 'wind jewel'), stepped wind-mask, hooked staff, atlatl (spear-thrower)
nodes.characterTrait: spiritual, transformative, priestly, chaste, civilizing, self-sacrificing, tricked-and-fallen
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: appears as a feathered serpent, or as a bearded human figure with priestly turquoise diadem (xiuhuitzolli), or as Ehecatl-Quetzalcoatl with a round wind-mask featuring a protruding bird-beak
nodes.significantEvent: Descended to Mictlan (the underworld) and retrieved the bones of past humanity, grinding them and mixing them with his own blood to create the present human race. Discovered maize for humans by transforming into a black ant and following a red ant to its hidden grain-mountain. Reigned as priest-king of Tollan (Tula). Was tricked by Tezcatlipoca, who showed him his own aged face in a mirror, intoxicated him with pulque, and made him break his celibacy with his sister Quetzalpetlatl. In shame, he departed Tula eastward to Tlillan-Tlapallan, where he immolated himself; his heart rose to become Venus, the morning star.
nodes.symbolism: Name combines quetzalli 'tail feather' and coatl 'serpent'; highest form of spiritual hero myth; inner transformation
nodes.neumannArchetype: Highest form of the hero myth achieving spiritual self-transformation.
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of the dual creator Ometeotl (Ometecuhtli/Omecihuatl) in some traditions; one of the four sons of Ometeotl alongside Tezcatlipoca, Huitzilopochtli, and Xipe Totec.
nodes.deathCircumstances: Self-immolated at Tlillan-Tlapallan after his fall from Tula; his heart rose into the sky and became Venus, the morning star.
nodes.tradition_source: Aztec strata: Florentine Codex (Sahagún, Anderson-Dibble); Annals of Cuauhtitlan / Codex Chimalpopoca (Bierhorst); Histoyre du Mechique. Toltec stratum: Annals of Cuauhtitlan §29ff. (the priest-king of Tula). Maya cognate Kukulkan / Q'uq'umatz: Popol Vuh, lines 16-32 (Christenson tr.). The single tag 'Aztec' privileged the latest stratum.
nodes.domain_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — Quetzalcoatl ('Plumed Serpent') as creator-deity and cultural-hero; Sahagún Books 1.5, 3 (the Topiltzin Quetzalcoatl narrative); Codex Chimalpopoca; the Toltec Tula tradition
nodes.object_source: Codex Borgia and Magliabechiano — conch-shell pectoral (the ehecailacacozcatl or 'wind-jewel'); conical wind-mask (his Ehecatl-aspect); the duck-billed mask of his wind-god form
nodes.animals_source: Quetzalcoatl's sacred animals: feathered serpent (his name and primary form); quetzal-bird (whose feathers gave him his name)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Florentine Codex 3.3 — sage, civilizing, peace-loving, opposed to human sacrifice (in his Topiltzin-aspect)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Codex Borgia — feathered serpent, or anthropomorphic with conch-pectoral and conical wind-mask; in his cultural-hero Topiltzin form, bearded white-skinned king (the famous prophecy that the Spaniards exploited)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — Five Suns narrative: Quetzalcoatl was the second sun. Recovered the bones of past humanity from Mictlan, sprinkling them with his own blood to create the present (fifth) humanity. With Tezcatlipoca, raised the sky from the earth using a feathered-serpent and an ocelot. Created the maguey-pulque tradition. As Topiltzin (legendary Toltec king of Tula), exiled by Tezcatlipoca's trickery (incest-revelation), sailed east on a raft of serpents promising to return.
nodes.eventTypes_source: Leyenda de los Soles; Topiltzin narrative
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Codex Chimalpopoca — primordial; in cultural-hero aspect, son of Mixcoatl and Chimalman
nodes.familyRoles_source: brother: Tezcatlipoca, Huitzilopochtli, Xipe Totec (Histoyre du Mechique ch. 1); twin: Xolotl (Florentine Codex 7.2 — Xolotl as evening-star twin); son: Ometeotl
nodes.birthTypes_source: Codex Chimalpopoca
nodes.deathTypes_source: Codex Chimalpopoca, Anales de Cuauhtitlan; Florentine Codex Book 3 (Quetzalcoatl-Topiltzin's self-immolation at Tlapallan and ascension as Venus)

nodes.name: Venus
nodes.domain: love, fertility, motherhood
nodes.significantEvent: Venus of Willendorf; Lespugne Venus; earliest Great Mother representations
nodes.symbolism: Paleolithic fertility figurines; exaggerated hips, breasts, belly; earliest known Great Mother representations
nodes.neumannArchetype: Earliest prehistoric representations of the Great Mother archetype (Venus figurines).
familyRoles: divine ancestress of the Julian gens (Caesar, Augustus)
nodes.domain_source: Lucretius, De Rerum Natura 1.1-49 (the great opening hymn); Ovid, Metamorphoses and Fasti; Virgil, Aeneid (the mother of Aeneas, ancestress of Augustus); the cult of Venus Genetrix established by Julius Caesar; Apuleius, Metamorphoses 4-6 (Cupid and Psyche)
nodes.object_source: Venus iconography — myrtle; rose; apple; mirror; doves; sea-shell (the famous Venus rising from the foam, e.g., Botticelli's later derivation)
nodes.animals_source: Venus's sacred animals: dove (her primary bird); sparrow; hare; sometimes the dolphin (the sea-foam-birth iconography)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Lucretius; Ovid; Virgil
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard Venus iconography — supreme feminine beauty, often nude; Aphrodite's iconography fully adopted; especially significant as the Genetrix (ancestress) of the Julian gens through Aeneas
nodes.significantEvent_source: Roman tradition — though identified with Greek Aphrodite, Venus had her own Italic origin as a vegetation/garden-goddess before the interpretatio. Mother of Aeneas (by Anchises) and thus ancestress of the Julian gens (Caesar built the Temple of Venus Genetrix in 46 BCE in his forum); the Cupid-and-Psyche narrative (Apuleius); Lucretius's opening invocation makes her cosmic generative-principle of nature itself
nodes.eventTypes_source: Virgil, Aeneid; Lucretius; cult of Venus Genetrix
nodes.birthTypes_source: Standard interpretatio

nodes.name: Phanes
nodes.domain: creation, light, the firstborn, the Orphic cosmogony
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: golden-winged, four-eyed, bisexual deity of dazzling light
nodes.significantEvent: emerged from the Cosmic Egg at the beginning of creation and set the cosmos in order, later swallowed by Zeus who thereby absorbed all creation into himself
nodes.symbolism: the first light of creation, the cosmic egg as the origin of all being, the bisexual origin before the differentiation of the sexes, light emerging from the darkness of the egg
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child as the first light of consciousness emerging from the uroboric egg, the luminous hermaphrodite before the separation of opposites
nodes.birthCircumstances: hatched from the Cosmic Egg laid by Nyx or Chronos in Orphic cosmogony
