nodes.name: Maori Xingguan
nodes.domain: astronomy, the constellations, warfare
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: one of the Twenty-Eight Mansions, a stellar warrior spirit
nodes.significantEvent: one of the twenty-eight stellar spirits in Chinese astronomical mythology, plays a role in the Investiture of the Gods narrative
nodes.symbolism: the constellation as a divine warrior, the organized cosmos as a military formation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the stellar masculine warrior in the cosmic army of heaven
nodes.birthCircumstances: He is the son of the bodhisattva Pilanpo.
nodes.deathCircumstances: These constellations are the same as those studied in Western astrology.

nodes.name: Uriel
nodes.domain: wisdom, light, truth, repentance, salvation
nodes.characterTrait: illuminating, instructing, apocalyptic-interpreting, fiery (his name means 'God is my light' or 'fire of God', ʾūr ʾēl)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: In 2 Esdras, appears to interpret Ezra's apocalyptic visions; otherwise not visually described in detail. In Christian iconography, often holds a scroll or a flame.
nodes.significantEvent: Sent to interpret the apocalyptic visions of 4 Ezra (2 Esdras 4-10). In 1 Enoch 19:1, set over the world and Tartarus; in 1 Enoch 20:2, 'set over the world and Tartarus' (the leader of the four/seven archangels in some recensions). In some patristic and apocryphal traditions, the angel who instructs Adam after the expulsion, the angel who guards the gates of Eden with the flaming sword, or the angel who appeared to the Magdalene at the empty tomb.
nodes.symbolism: Fire of God; divine illumination; wisdom that burns away ignorance; light in darkness
nodes.birthCircumstances: Created angelic being; one of the four (or seven) archangels.
nodes.domain_source: Not in the Hebrew Bible. 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 4-10 (Uriel as Ezra's interlocutor and apocalyptic interpreter); 1 Enoch 9, 19, 20:2, 21:5, 27:2, 33:3-4; 3 Enoch; Christian patristic angelology; the Council of Rome 745 (which prohibited cult of unsanctioned angel-names — Uriel survived this); Eastern Orthodox calendar (feast 8 November alongside the synaxis of the archangels)
nodes.object_source: Eastern Orthodox iconography of the archangel synaxis
nodes.characterTrait_source: 2 Esdras 4-10; 1 Enoch 19, 20
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: 2 Esdras 4-10; Christian iconographic tradition
nodes.significantEvent_source: 2 Esdras 4-10; 1 Enoch 19-20; later patristic and apocryphal accretions
nodes.birthTypes_source: Standard angelology
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: 1 Enoch 20; Christian-Jewish angelology

nodes.name: Persephone (Kore)
nodes.domain: underworld, spring, vegetation, death and rebirth, the Eleusinian Mysteries
nodes.object: pomegranate, torch, sheaf of grain, narcissus flower
nodes.characterTrait: innocent, transformative, dual-natured, regal, maiden and queen
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: youthful and beautiful as Kore, regal and fearsome as Queen of the Underworld
nodes.significantEvent: abducted by Hades while gathering flowers, ate pomegranate seeds in the underworld binding her to spend part of each year below, her annual return brings spring
nodes.symbolism: the seed that must descend into the earth to be reborn, the maiden who becomes queen of death, the mother-daughter unity of Demeter-Kore as the deepest mystery of Eleusis
nodes.neumannArchetype: daughter and partial figure of Demeter, the Kore who descends to become queen of the underworld, representing the corn mothers seed returning to earth
familyRoles: Queen of the Underworld for half the year
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Zeus and Demeter
nodes.domain_source: Homeric Hymn to Demeter (the central source); Hesiod, Theogony 912-914; Apollodorus 1.5.1-3; Ovid, Metamorphoses 5.341-571; the Eleusinian Mysteries tradition
nodes.object_source: Persephone iconography — pomegranate (the seeds she ate in the underworld); torch (sometimes); sheaf of grain; the κίστη (mystic basket)
nodes.animals_source: Persephone's sacred animals: dove; the snakes of the Eleusinian Mysteries
nodes.characterTrait_source: Homeric Hymn to Demeter; Apollodorus
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Persephone iconography — youthful Kore (Maiden), in flowing garments; sometimes enthroned with Hades as Queen of the Underworld; cf. the Persephone fresco from the Royal Tomb at Vergina (c. 340 BCE)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Homeric Hymn to Demeter — abducted by Hades while picking flowers in Sicily (the narcissus or asphodel meadow); Demeter wandered the earth in mourning; Zeus eventually intervened; but Persephone had eaten 6 (or 4, or 3) pomegranate seeds, binding her to the underworld for half (or third) of each year — origin of seasons; ruled the underworld as Hades's queen for half the year, returning to her mother for the other half
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Hesiod, Theogony 912-914 — daughter of Zeus and Demeter
nodes.birthTypes_source: Hesiod, Theogony

nodes.name: Ate
nodes.domain: delusion, ruin, folly, blind recklessness
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: swift-footed, walks over the heads of men without touching the ground
nodes.significantEvent: deceived Zeus into swearing an oath that allowed Eurystheus to be born before Heracles, Zeus cast her out of Olympus and she now walks among mortals causing ruin
nodes.symbolism: the blindness that precedes catastrophe, the divine delusion that even the gods are subject to, reckless folly as a cosmic force
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow feminine that clouds consciousness and leads to destruction through blindness
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Zeus according to Homer, or daughter of Eris according to Hesiod

nodes.name: Baalat Gebal
nodes.domain: the sea, love, Byblos, the Near East
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Near Eastern goddess worshipped at Byblos, identified with Hathor and Isis by the Egyptians
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped at Byblos as the Lady of Byblos, connected to the Isis myth through the Byblos episode where Isis recovered the body of Osiris which had been enclosed in a cedar tree at Byblos
nodes.symbolism: the sea trade between Egypt and Byblos as a sacred connection, the foreign goddess who guards the body of Osiris, the cedar of Byblos as the tree of life containing the dead god
nodes.neumannArchetype: the foreign Great Mother who guards the dismembered Great Father (Osiris) in the cedar tree, the feminine across the sea who preserves the masculine principle
nodes.birthCircumstances: Semitic goddess of Byblos adopted into the Egyptian pantheon through the ancient trade relationship between Egypt and Byblos

nodes.symbolism: the sea as the domain of specific clans granted divine maritime authority, the fisherman-ancestor as the founder of coastal civilization, the purification in the sea as the origin of maritime divinity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the sea-father who founds the maritime lineage, the masculine of the ocean whose descendants master the waters
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from Izanagis purification in the sea, associated with the sea realm

nodes.domain: quest, seafaring, kingship, adventure
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: handsome hero wearing one sandal, leader of the Argonauts
nodes.significantEvent: led the Argonauts to Colchis to retrieve the Golden Fleece, won it with Medeas help, betrayed Medea for Glauce of Corinth leading to the murder of his children, died alone beneath the rotting Argo
nodes.symbolism: the quest hero who succeeds through others power rather than his own, the betrayal of the feminine helper, ambition that leads to ruin
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hero who relies on the anima (Medea) for his quest but betrays the feminine, leading to catastrophic reversal
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Aeson, the rightful king of Iolcos, raised by the centaur Chiron

nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Aeacus king of Aegina and the nymph Endeis

nodes.birthCircumstances: grandson of King Minos of Crete, son of Deucalion

nodes.name: Memnon
nodes.domain: war, Ethiopia, the dawn, heroism
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: most beautiful of warriors, with dark skin and golden armor
nodes.significantEvent: came to Troy as an ally with a great Ethiopian army, killed Antilochus but was then killed by Achilles, Zeus granted him immortality at his mothers tears, his men were turned into birds (Memnonides) that visit his tomb annually
nodes.symbolism: the dawn-born hero who falls to the greatest warrior, beauty and nobility in death, the mothers grief that wins immortality for her son
nodes.neumannArchetype: the son of the dawn goddess whose beauty and death embody the tragic hero at the threshold of light and dark
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Eos (Dawn) and the mortal Tithonus, king of Ethiopia

nodes.neumannArchetype: the peripheral hero drawn into the central conflict
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of the Thracian lord Imbrasus
nodes.deathCircumstances: Peirous was killed by Thoas, leader of the Aetolians.

nodes.name: Aurora
nodes.domain: the dawn, morning light, renewal, hope
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful woman in saffron robes with rosy fingers, riding a chariot through the sky at dawn, scattering dew and light
nodes.significantEvent: opened the gates of heaven each morning for the sun god Sol to begin his journey, her tears were the morning dew, associated with the daily renewal of hope and light
nodes.symbolism: the dawn as the daily renewal of consciousness, the rosy fingers as the first light touching the world, the morning dew as the tears of the awakening goddess, the daily hope of a new beginning
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of the dawn, the feminine that opens the gates for the masculine sun-consciousness to emerge from the darkness
nodes.birthCircumstances: identified with the Greek Eos, the dawn goddess

nodes.name: Namazu
nodes.domain: earthquakes, catfish, disaster, containment
nodes.characterTrait: earthquake-causing, catfish-like, restrained, destructive when free
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a gigantic catfish that lives underground and causes earthquakes when it thrashes
nodes.significantEvent: the giant catfish restrained by the god Kashima who pins it down with a great stone (kaname-ishi), when Kashima relaxes his guard the catfish thrashes and causes earthquakes
nodes.symbolism: the catfish as the subterranean cause of earthquakes, the necessity of divine restraint over chaotic natural forces, the kaname-ishi as the pinning stone of cosmic order
nodes.neumannArchetype: the chthonic chaos-beast restrained beneath the earth, the unconscious instinctual force (the catfish) that must be kept pinned by patriarchal consciousness to prevent earthquakes of the psyche

nodes.name: Xipe-Totec
nodes.domain: spring, renewal, agriculture, flayed skin, goldsmiths, the east, regeneration
nodes.object: flayed human skin, golden attire, shield, rattle staff
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Our Lord the Flayed One, depicted wearing a suit of flayed human skin, golden body paint
nodes.significantEvent: duplicate entry for Xipe Totec, the god of spring renewal whose worship involved the wearing of flayed human skin as a metaphor for the earth shedding its dead surface for new growth in spring
nodes.symbolism: the flayed skin as the dead surface of winter earth replaced by new spring growth, the sacrifice of the old for the emergence of the new, the golden body beneath the dead skin as the treasure of renewal
nodes.neumannArchetype: the vegetation god whose flaying is the ritual of the earths renewal, the masculine of the spring transformation
nodes.birthCircumstances: parents: Ometecuhtli and Omecihuatl (Codex Zumarraga)

nodes.name: Zeus
nodes.domain: sky, thunder, lightning, weather, kingship, justice, cosmic order, hospitality, oaths, marriage
nodes.characterTrait: sovereign, powerful, patriarchal, just, amorous, wrathful, protective of order
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: tall, bearded, majestic, enthroned, wielding thunderbolt
nodes.significantEvent: overthrew his father Cronus and the Titans in the Titanomachy, divided the cosmos with his brothers Poseidon and Hades, established divine and human law from Olympus
nodes.symbolism: divine sovereignty and cosmic order, the sky father who maintains justice, the tension between absolute power and moral law, honey as purest product of nature nourishing the infant god
nodes.neumannArchetype: the patriarchal sky god who inherits and divides the Great Mothers realms with his brothers, fed with honey as newborn representing natures purest essence
familyRoles: youngest son of Cronus and Rhea
one of the three brothers (Zeus-Poseidon-Hades) who divided the cosmos
father of countless Olympians and heroes
nodes.birthCircumstances: youngest son of Cronus and Rhea, hidden in Crete by his mother to escape being swallowed, raised on honey and goats milk in a cave
nodes.domain_source: Homer, Iliad and Odyssey passim; Hesiod, Theogony 453-506 (birth narrative), 617-885 (Titanomachy and Typhonomachy); Homeric Hymns 23 and 1; Pindar; Aeschylus; the Eleian-Olympic cult; Hesychius; the Iliadic 'father of gods and men' formula (πατὴρ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε)
nodes.object_source: Standard Zeus iconography — thunderbolt (κεραυνός) crafted by the Cyclopes; aegis (γαὶγίς, the goatskin shield); scepter; eagle as messenger; oak as sacred tree
nodes.animals_source: Zeus's sacred animals: eagle (his messenger); bull (the form he took to abduct Europa, Apollodorus 3.1.1); swan (the form he took for Leda); cuckoo (the form for first approaching Hera)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Hesiod, Theogony — Zeus was hidden on Crete by Rhea (against Cronus who swallowed his other children); led the Titanomachy; defeated Typhon; established the Olympian order; married Hera (after Metis, Themis, Eurynome, Demeter, Mnemosyne, Leto). Countless extramarital affairs producing Heracles (by Alcmene), Perseus (by Danae), Helen (by Leda), Apollo and Artemis (by Leto), Hermes (by Maia), Dionysus (by Semele), and others.
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Hesiod, Theogony 468-491 — hidden by Rhea on Crete in the Idaean cave; Cronus given a stone wrapped in swaddling-cloth which he swallowed
nodes.characterTrait_source: Homeric corpus; Hesiod's Theogony; the Pindaric and tragic-stage corpus
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard archaic-to-classical iconography — bearded mature king, often enthroned, holding thunderbolt and scepter; cf. Pheidias's chryselephantine Zeus at Olympia (5th c. BCE)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Hesiod, Theogony 468-491

nodes.name: Metis
nodes.domain: wisdom, cunning, counsel, prudence
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Titaness of wisdom, sometimes depicted as a thoughtful woman
nodes.significantEvent: Zeus swallowed her while she was pregnant with Athena because of a prophecy that her children would be wiser than him, Athena was later born fully armed from Zeus head
nodes.symbolism: wisdom devoured and incorporated by patriarchal power, the feminine intelligence that becomes the source of the greatest goddess from within the male god
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine wisdom swallowed by the patriarchal consciousness, the Great Mother incorporated into the Father who then gives birth to the wisdom-goddess Athena
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Oceanus and Tethys, first wife of Zeus

nodes.name: Harmonia
nodes.domain: harmony, concord, cosmic order, music
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful goddess who brings together opposites
nodes.significantEvent: married Cadmus in a wedding attended by all the gods, received a cursed necklace that brought misfortune to all who wore it, transformed into a serpent alongside Cadmus in old age
nodes.symbolism: harmony born from the union of opposites (war and love), the cursed gifts that follow divine marriages, the serpent transformation as return to the primordial
nodes.neumannArchetype: the reconciling feminine born from the union of masculine aggression and feminine desire, the daughter who embodies the resolution of opposites
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Ares (War) and Aphrodite (Love), embodying the union of strife and desire

nodes.name: Lampetia
nodes.domain: light, the sun, herding, brilliance
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: radiant nymph who tends the cattle of the sun
nodes.significantEvent: together with her sister Phaethusa she guarded the sacred cattle of Helios on the island of Thrinacia, warned her father when Odysseus crew slaughtered his cattle
nodes.symbolism: the faithful guardian of the sacred, the daughter of light who protects the solar patrimony
nodes.neumannArchetype: the luminous feminine as the faithful guardian of the solar masculines treasure
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Helios (Sun) and the nymph Neaera

nodes.name: Troilus
nodes.domain: youth, tragedy, the Trojan War, Apollo
nodes.animals: bull, horse, lion, dove, raven, wolf, dog, bear, cock
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: youngest and most beautiful son of King Priam of Troy
nodes.significantEvent: killed by Achilles despite his youth, an oracle said Troy could not fall while Troilus lived to age twenty, Achilles killed him in the sanctuary of Apollo, further angering the god
nodes.symbolism: the beautiful youth whose death seals Troys doom, the violation of sanctuary, the child sacrifice that dooms the killer (Achilles) to divine retribution
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child whose survival could have preserved the old order (Troy), killed in the sanctuary of the sun god who will avenge him
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Priam and Hecuba, prince of Troy
nodes.deathCircumstances: Prophecies link Troilus' fate to that of Troy and so he is ambushed and murdered by Achilles.

nodes.name: Ferentina
nodes.domain: springs, the Latin League, political assembly
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess of a sacred spring near the Alban Hills where the Latin League assembled
nodes.significantEvent: her sacred grove and spring at Aricia was the meeting place of the Latin League, where the Latin peoples assembled for political and religious purposes
nodes.symbolism: the sacred spring as the gathering place of political community, the feminine waters as the foundation of political assembly, the grove-spring as the birthplace of Latin political culture
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of political assembly, the feminine waters around which masculine political order organizes

nodes.name: Nyx
nodes.domain: night, darkness, the primordial void
nodes.characterTrait: primordial, powerful, feared even by Zeus, mysterious
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: dark-robed, winged, driving a chariot of darkness across the sky
nodes.significantEvent: mother of a vast brood of cosmic forces including Death, Sleep, Dreams, Fate, and Strife, even Zeus feared to displease her
nodes.symbolism: the primordial darkness from which all things emerge, the power of the unconscious that even the ruling consciousness fears
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial uroboric darkness preceding consciousness, the Great Mother in her most ancient nocturnal aspect
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from Chaos, one of the first beings to emerge at creation

nodes.name: Aegipan
nodes.domain: nature, the wild, divine panic
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: sea-goat with the upper body of a goat and lower body of a fish
nodes.significantEvent: helped Zeus in the battle against the Titans by blowing a conch shell to create panic, or helped recover Zeus sinews stolen by Typhon, honored as the constellation Capricornus
nodes.symbolism: divine aid from the wild places, panic as a weapon of the gods, the goat-fish hybrid representing the boundary between land and sea
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wild nature spirit who assists the sky father in his battle against the primordial chaos
nodes.birthCircumstances: According to Hyginus, Aegipan was the son of Zeus (some sources say his son Apollo) and Aega (also named Boetis or Aix), and was transferred to the stars.

nodes.name: Themis
nodes.domain: divine law, justice, natural order, prophecy, custom, assemblies
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: stately Titaness, sometimes blindfolded, holding scales of justice
nodes.significantEvent: second wife of Zeus before Hera, bore the Horae (Seasons) and the Moirai (Fates), held the oracle at Delphi before Apollo, summoned the gods to assembly
nodes.symbolism: divine law as distinct from human legislation, the natural order that precedes and transcends mortal institutions, prophecy as the voice of cosmic justice
nodes.neumannArchetype: the ancient feminine wisdom that establishes cosmic law, the Titaness whose authority precedes and undergirds the Olympian order
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Uranus and Gaia, one of the twelve Titans
nodes.deathCircumstances: Dike executed the law of judgments and sentencing and, together with her mother Themis, she carried out the final decisions of Moirai.

nodes.name: Coeus
nodes.domain: intellect, the axis of heaven, inquiry
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Titan associated with the celestial axis, the pole of heaven around which the stars revolve
nodes.significantEvent: married his sister Phoebe and fathered Leto and Asteria, imprisoned in Tartarus after the Titanomachy
nodes.symbolism: the cosmic intellect, the axis around which celestial knowledge revolves, the questioning mind
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine intellectual principle among the Titans, the axis of heavenly consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Uranus and Gaia, one of the twelve Titans

nodes.name: Plutus
nodes.domain: wealth, agricultural abundance, prosperity
nodes.characterTrait: generous, blind, indiscriminate in distributing wealth
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: youthful winged boy, sometimes depicted blind, carrying a cornucopia
nodes.significantEvent: blinded by Zeus so he would distribute wealth indiscriminately to both good and bad people, in Aristophanes comedy he is cured of his blindness
nodes.symbolism: wealth as blind fortune, agricultural abundance as divine gift, the tension between deserved and undeserved prosperity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the child of the earth mother (Demeter) and the mortal sower, wealth as the fruit of the sacred agricultural union
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Demeter and the mortal Iasion, conceived in a thrice-ploughed field in Crete

nodes.name: Aoös
nodes.domain: rivers, Thessaly
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: river god of Thessaly
nodes.significantEvent: personification of the river Aoos in Thessaly
nodes.symbolism: the living waters of northern Greece, the river as divine being
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine water principle of the specific regional landscape
nodes.birthCircumstances: Aoös (Greek Αώος, pronounced aO-os) was another name for god Adonis and also the mythic son of Eos and Cephalus who became the first king of Cyprus.

nodes.name: Kakia
nodes.domain: vice, moral baseness, wickedness
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful woman in alluring dress who promises an easy path, the embodiment of vice
nodes.significantEvent: in Prodicus fable of the Choice of Heracles she appeared alongside Arete (Virtue) and offered Heracles an easy life of pleasure, which he rejected in favor of Aretes hard path of virtue
nodes.symbolism: the seductive ease of vice contrasted with the difficult path of virtue, beauty as a mask for moral corruption
nodes.neumannArchetype: the seductive shadow feminine who offers regression to the unconscious pleasures rather than the difficult ascent of consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: In the Gnostic tradition, Kakia is personified as the child of the first angel and Authadia with siblings Zelos (emulation), Phthonus (envy), Erinnys (fury), and Epithymia (lust).

nodes.symbolism: intoxication as a divine state, the altered consciousness that wine produces, the dangerous gift of the vine
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine of intoxication, the loosening of consciousness through the Dionysiac
nodes.birthCircumstances: Methe was the daughter of Dionysus in some accounts.

nodes.domain: the full moon, all-brightness, dew

nodes.symbolism: the full moon as the peak of lunar power, the daughter of the moon as the embodiment of complete lunar radiance
nodes.neumannArchetype: the full moon feminine in her complete radiance, the lunar consciousness at its brightest
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Zeus and Selene (Moon)

nodes.neumannArchetype: the nurturing feminine in her healing aspect, the gentle restoration of wholeness

nodes.name: Kuni-no-Tokotachi
nodes.domain: the eternal land, the first standing, primordial earth, foundations
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the kami who represents the eternal standing of the land, one of the primordial hitorigami
nodes.significantEvent: appeared as the seventh generation of kami in the creation sequence, representing the eternal foundation of the land upon which all creation would stand
nodes.symbolism: the eternal standing of the earth as a divine principle, the land-foundation that endures beneath all change, the primordial act of standing as the establishment of the solid ground of existence
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial masculine foundation of the earth, the standing consciousness that establishes the solid ground from which all else grows
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the earliest kami to appear during creation, a hitorigami who immediately concealed himself

nodes.domain: labor, toil, hardship, pain
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: spirit of hard labor and toilsome suffering
nodes.significantEvent: the personification of the hard labor that wears down mortal life, one of the hardships born of Strife
nodes.symbolism: the divine weight of toil, labor as a cosmic burden placed upon humanity, the pain of work that sustains life
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow of the culture heros gift, labor as the price consciousness pays for its existence
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Eris (Strife)

nodes.name: Bia
nodes.domain: force, raw power, compulsion, violence
nodes.characterTrait: forceful, relentless, unyielding, obedient to Zeus
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: powerful divine figure, companion of Kratos at Zeus command
nodes.significantEvent: together with Kratos she bound Prometheus to the rock in the Caucasus on Zeus orders, as depicted in Aeschylus Prometheus Bound
nodes.symbolism: raw force in service of cosmic order, power without mercy, the enforcement of divine will
nodes.neumannArchetype: the instrumental force of the patriarchal order, power serving the sky fathers authority
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the Titan Pallas and the Oceanid Styx, sister of Nike, Kratos, and Zelus

nodes.name: Epimetheus
nodes.domain: hindsight, foolishness, afterthought
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: brother of Prometheus, the after-thinker
nodes.significantEvent: despite Prometheus warning he accepted Pandora as a gift from Zeus, opening the way for all evils to enter the world, distributed all animal traits but left nothing for humanity
nodes.symbolism: the folly of acting without foresight, hindsight as the complement to forethought, the acceptance of dangerous gifts
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow of the culture hero, the brother who lacks consciousness and thereby brings catastrophe
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of the Titan Iapetus and the Oceanid Clymene, brother of Prometheus, Atlas, and Menoetius

nodes.name: Uranus
nodes.domain: sky, creation, heavens, the starry vault
nodes.characterTrait: tyrannical, suppressive, fearful of offspring, generative
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the vast sky itself, arching over the earth, sometimes depicted as a giant
nodes.significantEvent: mated with Gaia to produce the Titans, Cyclopes, and Hecatoncheires, imprisoned his monstrous children in Tartarus, castrated by his son Cronus with a sickle provided by Gaia
nodes.symbolism: the primal sky father, the tyrannical suppression of creativity that must be overthrown for creation to proceed, the separation of heaven and earth
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial sky father who must be castrated for the world to emerge from the undifferentiated uroboric state
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from Gaia alone, or self-generated as the primordial sky

nodes.name: Calliste
nodes.domain: beauty, the sea, islands
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: sea nymph of great beauty, daughter of Triton
nodes.significantEvent: given to the Argonauts as a clod of earth by her father Triton, the clod later transformed into the island Calliste (Thera/Santorini)
nodes.symbolism: the gift that transforms into a new land, beauty as the genesis of place
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine as generative of new land, the clod of earth as the Great Mothers creative potential
nodes.birthCircumstances: In Greek mythology, Calliste or Callistis () is the daughter of the sea-god Triton and the Libya of Egypt, who was given to the Argonauts as a clod of earth that transformed into the island Calliste.

nodes.name: Asia
nodes.domain: geography, continents, the eastern lands
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Oceanid nymph who gave her name to the continent of Asia
nodes.significantEvent: mother of the Titans who shaped human destiny: Prometheus (forethought), Epimetheus (afterthought), Atlas (endurance), and Menoetius (recklessness)
nodes.symbolism: the eastern lands as the source of the Titan lineage, the maternal ocean from which the shapers of humanity spring
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Oceanic Mother whose children define the human condition
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Oceanus and Tethys, wife of Iapetus, mother of Prometheus, Atlas, Epimetheus

nodes.name: Aura
nodes.domain: breeze, dawn air, the morning wind, virginity
nodes.characterTrait: wild, virginal, swift, cruel when maddened
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: swift, wild maiden of the breezes, daughter of a Titan
nodes.significantEvent: mocked Artemis virginity saying Artemis must secretly be unchaste, Artemis had Dionysus drive her mad, in her madness she killed her twin sons and was transformed into a spring
nodes.symbolism: the danger of mocking the divine, the wind as both gentle and destructive, virginity as a serious sacred state not to be questioned
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wild feminine punished for challenging the Great Goddess, madness as the price of transgression against the sacred feminine
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the Titan Lelantos and the nymph Periboea (or Cybele)

nodes.name: Telete
nodes.domain: initiation, mystery rites, consecration
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: personification of the mystery initiation itself

nodes.symbolism: the mystery of initiation as a divine being, the transformation that occurs through sacred ritual, the unspeakable experience at the heart of the Mysteries
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine mystery of transformation itself, initiation as the Great Mothers transformative encounter with consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Dionysus and Nicaea in some traditions

nodes.domain: fire, the hearth, the kitchen, cooking, purification by fire
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: god of fire and the hearth, associated with the cooking fire and domestic flames
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped as the guardian of the kitchen hearth fire, associated with purification and the sacred fire of cooking, also connected to the wild fire of the mountains and forests
nodes.symbolism: the hearth fire as the sacred domestic flame, the kitchen as the temple of fire, cooking as a sacred transformation by fire, the dual nature of fire as both domestic servant and wild destroyer
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine fire-spirit of the hearth, the domesticated flame that serves consciousness in the kitchen while retaining its wild destructive potential

nodes.name: Wei Zheng
nodes.domain: justice, dream guardianship, the Tang Dynasty, door gods
nodes.object: sword, fish basket (to catch demons in dreams)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: stern-faced Tang Dynasty official and advisor
nodes.significantEvent: in folklore he beheaded the Dragon King in a dream after promising him safety, earning the enmity of dragons, in some door god traditions he is one of the two door gods, famous for his stern and incorruptible governance
nodes.symbolism: the incorruptible official whose justice extends even into the dream world, the stern advisor who tells the emperor uncomfortable truths, governance that penetrates even the realm of sleep
nodes.neumannArchetype: the stern patriarch whose authority extends into the unconscious (dream world), the incorruptible masculine consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: historical Tang Dynasty chancellor (580-643 CE), advisor to Emperor Taizong

nodes.name: Thoth
nodes.domain: wisdom, writing, magic, the moon, measurement, judgment, knowledge
nodes.object: reed-pen and palette (his scribal kit); the moon-disk on his head; the ibis; the Eye of Horus (which he restored)
nodes.characterTrait: wise, inventive, measuring, just, eloquent, magical
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Ibis-headed man, or sometimes a baboon (his other sacred form); wearing the moon-disk; holding reed-pen and palette.
nodes.significantEvent: The scribe of the gods; inventor of writing, mathematics, astronomy. Healer of the wounded Eye of Horus. Mediator in the Contendings of Horus and Set. Recorder at the weighing of the heart (he writes down Ma'at's verdict in the judgment-hall of Osiris). In the Hermopolitan cosmogony, the original cosmic egg from which Ra emerged was laid by Thoth-as-ibis on the primordial mound. Brought Tefnut back from Nubia (Demotic Tefnut-cycle). In the Greco-Roman period, identified with Hermes/Mercury; Hermes Trismegistus (the supposed author of the Hermetic corpus) is Thoth.
nodes.symbolism: writing as the most sacred technology, the moon as the measurer of time, the ibis as wisdom wading through the waters of knowledge, the baboon greeting the dawn as the celebration of renewed consciousness
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father as the divine intellect, the masculine principle of logos expressed through writing, measurement, and the ordering of knowledge
nodes.birthCircumstances: In Hermopolitan cosmogony, primordial and self-engendered (emerges from the cosmic egg before creation, or is the cosmic egg's laying agent).
nodes.domain_source: Pyramid Texts; Coffin Texts; Book of the Dead; the Hermopolitan cosmogony; the Tefnut-cycle (Demotic); Plutarch (where Thoth is identified with Hermes); the Book of Thoth (Demotic philosophical text)

nodes.name: Xuanwu
nodes.domain: the north, water, martial arts, exorcism, turtles and snakes
nodes.object: sword, dark banner, serpent and tortoise
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: dark-armored warrior deity standing on or accompanied by a turtle entwined with a serpent, one of the most important Chinese deities
nodes.significantEvent: the most important deity of the Ming Dynasty, his cult was promoted by the Yongle Emperor who claimed Xuanwu helped him seize the throne, temples dedicated to him on Wudang Mountain became centers of martial arts training
nodes.symbolism: the union of the tortoise (earth/endurance) and serpent (water/transformation) as the northern guardian, the martial arts as spiritual cultivation, the dark warrior who commands the underworld forces
nodes.neumannArchetype: the dark masculine who integrates the shadow (serpent) and endurance (tortoise) into a powerful unity, the warrior of the unconscious depths (north/water) who protects through mastery of the chthonic
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the Four Symbols (Black Tortoise/Turtle of the North), elevated to a supreme deity during the Ming Dynasty

nodes.name: Hatmehit
nodes.domain: fish, fertility, the Nile, Mendes, the Delta
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman wearing a fish (Nile tilapia) on her head, or depicted as a fish, the fish goddess of Mendes
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped at Mendes alongside Banebdjedet, the tilapia fish was sacred to her because it carried its young in its mouth, symbolizing protection and rebirth
nodes.symbolism: the tilapia as the fish of rebirth (because it carries young in its mouth), the Nile fish as the sustenance of Egypt, the fish as a symbol of sexual fertility and renewal
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother in her aquatic fish form, the feminine that carries the young within herself
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient fish goddess of Mendes in the Nile Delta

nodes.name: Parthenopaeus
nodes.domain: archery, the Seven against Thebes, heroism, motherhood
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: handsome young warrior with a striking face
nodes.significantEvent: one of the Seven against Thebes, killed at the gates of Thebes fulfilling the doom of the expedition, suckled by a partridge or bear after exposure
nodes.symbolism: the child of the huntress raised by wild nature, the doomed hero who inherits his mothers wildness and his fathers fate
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hero born of the masculine-feminine (Atalanta the hunter-maiden), raised by the animal mother (bear), fated to die in the assault on the patriarchal city
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Atalanta and either Meleager or Hippomenes, exposed at birth and suckled by a she-bear
nodes.deathCircumstances: Parthenopaeus was killed by either Periclymenus or Amphidicus (Asphodicus), a son of Astacus.

nodes.name: Metatron
nodes.domain: heavenly scribe, divine presence, knowledge, cosmic order, children
nodes.object: scroll (he is the heavenly scribe); fiery throne; the seventy names; pen of fire
nodes.characterTrait: exalted, scribal, knowledge-bearing, the 'lesser YHWH' (in 3 Enoch), prince of the divine presence (sar ha-panim), heavenly intermediary
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: In 3 Enoch, transformed from the patriarch Enoch into a being of fire and light, his stature filling the cosmos, with 36 wings and 365,000 eyes. His body becomes flame, his veins fire, his eyelashes lightning-flashes. He is given the seventy names of God and seated on a throne.
nodes.significantEvent: In 3 Enoch, Enoch (Genesis 5:24, who 'walked with God, and was not, for God took him') is taken up to heaven and transformed into Metatron, the prince of the divine presence. He is given the seventy names, the pen and book of fire, and is set over the divine throne-chariot. In b. Hagigah 15a, Acher (the apostate Elisha ben Abuyah) sees Metatron seated and concludes 'there are two powers in heaven' — for which heresy Metatron is given sixty lashes by God to demonstrate his subordination. In Kabbalistic tradition, Metatron is identified with the divine glory (kavod) and sometimes with the angel who led Israel through the wilderness (Exodus 23:20-23, 'my name is in him').
nodes.symbolism: Highest angel; bridge between human and divine; the sacred geometry of Metatrons Cube; cosmic record-keeper; transformation from mortal to celestial
nodes.birthCircumstances: In 3 Enoch tradition, originally the patriarch Enoch (great-grandfather of Noah), who walked with God and was taken up (Genesis 5:24); then transformed into the angelic Metatron in the heavenly court.
nodes.domain_source: b. Hagigah 15a (the famous 'two powers in heaven' passage — Metatron as a 'second' power); b. Sanhedrin 38b; b. Avodah Zarah 3b (Metatron as the angel-prince who teaches Torah to the schoolchildren of departed souls); 3 Enoch (Sefer Hekhalot, Hekhalot literature, c. 5th-9th c. CE) — the principal source, in which the patriarch Enoch is transformed into Metatron; Zohar; Heikhalot Rabbati; Talmudic and Kabbalistic tradition

nodes.characterTrait_source: 3 Enoch (Hekhalot Rabbati); b. Hagigah 15a
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: 3 Enoch (Sefer Hekhalot) chapters 9, 15, 16; Hekhalot Rabbati
nodes.significantEvent_source: b. Hagigah 15a; 3 Enoch (Sefer Hekhalot); Zohar; Hekhalot Rabbati
nodes.birthTypes_source: 3 Enoch (the Enoch-Metatron transformation)
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Genesis 5:24; 3 Enoch chapters 3-15

nodes.name: Heka
nodes.domain: magic, the spoken word, creative power, healing, medicine
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: man with arms raised in the ka gesture, sometimes depicted as a man carrying a staff entwined with serpents
nodes.significantEvent: the divine force through which all creation was accomplished, without Heka no spell, prayer, or ritual could function, he was the power behind all magical acts in both the divine and human realms, physicians invoked him for healing
nodes.symbolism: magic as the fundamental creative force of the universe, the spoken word as power, the ka gesture as the activation of creative energy, magic as the technology of creation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine logos-power through which consciousness creates reality, the word as the creative force of the Great Father
nodes.birthCircumstances: personification of the creative power of magic itself, coexistent with the creator gods

nodes.domain: war, the Eastern Desert, foreign lands, punishment, stars
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: falcon wearing two tall feathers and a uraeus, or a man with falcon features carrying weapons
nodes.significantEvent: protected Egypts eastern border against Asian invaders, punished the enemies of Egypt, associated with the star Orion in some traditions
nodes.symbolism: the falcon warrior of the eastern frontier, the divine defender against Asian invasion, the feathered warrior of the border
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine warrior-guardian of the eastern boundary, the patriarchal defender of civilization against the foreign unknown
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient war god of the 20th nome of Lower Egypt, guardian of the eastern frontier

nodes.name: Elasioi
nodes.domain: drivers away of disease, propitiation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: spirits who drive away disease and evil
nodes.significantEvent: invoked in ritual to ward off plague and pestilence, associated with Apollo in his healing aspect
nodes.symbolism: the divine forces that drive away affliction, propitiation as a communal healing act
nodes.neumannArchetype: the protective spirits that guard the boundary between health and disease
nodes.birthCircumstances: Either way, the Elasioi were said to be children or descendants of the heroine Alexida, daughter of the deified Amphiaraus.

nodes.name: Abraham
nodes.domain: covenant, faith, fatherhood, obedience, nations
nodes.object: the altars he builds (Shechem, Bethel, Hebron, Moriah); the knife at the binding of Isaac; the tent at the oaks of Mamre; the cave of Machpelah (his burial site, Genesis 23)
nodes.characterTrait: faithful, hospitable (to the three visitors at Mamre), obedient (the Akedah), bargaining (interceding for Sodom, Genesis 18:22-33), wandering, covenant-receiving
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Patriarchal figure; lived 175 years (Genesis 25:7); circumcised at age 99 (Genesis 17:24); described as 'old' and 'well stricken in age' at the time of his and Sarah's miraculous parenthood (Genesis 18:11-12).
nodes.significantEvent: Called by YHWH to leave Ur of the Chaldeans (Genesis 12:1); receives the threefold covenant promise of land, descendants, and blessing-to-the-nations; circumcision-covenant in Genesis 17; hospitality to the three visitors at Mamre (Genesis 18); intercession for Sodom; binding of Isaac (Akedah, Genesis 22) — central event in Jewish, Christian, and Islamic memory; purchases the cave of Machpelah from Ephron the Hittite as Sarah's burial place (Genesis 23). In Quran, breaks his father's idols (Surah 21:57-67), is cast into a fire by Nimrod which Allah cools (21:68-71), builds the Kaʿbah with Ishmael (2:127), institutes the ḥajj rites.
nodes.symbolism: Father of Nations; model of faith and obedience; the binding of Isaac as ultimate test of devotion; ancestor of all Abrahamic peoples
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Terah, born in Ur of the Chaldeans (Genesis 11:26-28). Originally named Abram; renamed by YHWH at the covenant of circumcision (Genesis 17:5).
nodes.deathCircumstances: Died at 175 years, 'in a good old age, an old man and full of years' (Genesis 25:8); buried by Isaac and Ishmael in the cave of Machpelah with Sarah.
nodes.domain_source: Genesis 11:26 - 25:10; Romans 4; Galatians 3-4; Hebrews 11; Quran 2:124-141, 6:74-83, 14:35-41, 19:41-50, 21:51-71, 37:83-113 (Ibrāhīm); Josephus, Antiquities 1.7-13
nodes.object_source: Genesis 12-25 passim; Genesis 22:6, 22:10 (the knife); Genesis 23 (Machpelah)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Genesis 11:26-32

nodes.name: Selene
nodes.domain: moon, night, time, illumination
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: radiant, pale, crowned with crescent moon, driving a chariot across the night sky
nodes.significantEvent: fell in love with the mortal shepherd Endymion and asked Zeus to grant him eternal sleep so she could visit him every night, bore him fifty daughters
nodes.symbolism: the eternal feminine cycle, the moon as reflection of the sun, the desire for the beautiful mortal who must sleep to be preserved
nodes.neumannArchetype: the moon goddess as aspect of the Great Goddess, listed alongside Persephone and Medusa as manifestations of the archetypal feminine
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the Titans Hyperion and Theia, sister of Helios the sun and Eos the dawn

nodes.name: Geras
nodes.domain: old age, decay, the final stage of life
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: tiny shriveled old figure, depicted on Greek vases as a small wrinkled man confronted by Heracles
nodes.significantEvent: depicted in vase paintings being confronted or defeated by Heracles, symbolizing the heros desire to overcome aging
nodes.symbolism: the inevitability of decay, old age as a cosmic force, the enemy that not even heroes can truly defeat
nodes.neumannArchetype: the devouring aspect of time, the withering of the masculine hero-consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Nyx alone, or of Nyx and Erebus
nodes.deathCircumstances: Geras as embodied in humans represented a virtue: the more gēras a man acquired, the more kleos (fame) and arete (excellence and courage) he was considered to have.

nodes.name: Hephaestus
nodes.domain: fire, metalworking, craftsmanship, forging, volcanoes, sculpture
nodes.characterTrait: creative, industrious, patient, bitter, cunning, skilled
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: lame, bearded, muscular arms and chest, deformed feet, sooty from the forge
nodes.significantEvent: forged the weapons and armor of the gods, created Pandora from clay, trapped Ares and Aphrodite in an unbreakable net, built automatons and mechanical servants
nodes.symbolism: the creative power born from rejection, the transformative fire that shapes civilization, the artisan god whose physical imperfection produces perfect works
nodes.neumannArchetype: the rejected son of the Great Mother who transforms his suffering into creative mastery over fire and metal
familyRoles: son of Hera (and Zeus in some accounts, parthenogenetic in others)
husband of Aphrodite (in Homer) or Aglaia (in Hesiod)
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Hera alone without a father, or son of Zeus and Hera, cast from Olympus as an infant because of his lameness
nodes.domain_source: Homer, Iliad 18 and Odyssey 8; Hesiod, Theogony 927-929; Homeric Hymn 20; Apollodorus 1.3.5; the Lemnian cult; the Athenian Hephaisteion
nodes.object_source: Hephaestus iconography — hammer; tongs; bellows; the great forge under Mount Etna (or on Lemnos); the golden net that caught Ares and Aphrodite; the automata of his workshop (the golden tripods, the bronze giant Talos, the first woman Pandora)
nodes.animals_source: Hephaestus's sacred animals: donkey (his mount, due to his lameness); the bronze automata of his forge (Talos, the golden serving-maidens)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Homer (especially Iliad 1's tale of his lameness and his comic role); Hesiod; the Lemnian tradition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard Hephaestus iconography — bearded and lame; sometimes hunched; wearing the workman's pilos-cap; carrying hammer and tongs
nodes.significantEvent_source: Homer, Iliad 1.586-594, 18.395-409 — son of Hera (parthenogenetically in some accounts, by Zeus in others); thrown from Olympus by Zeus (Iliad 1) or by Hera (Iliad 18); landed on Lemnos and was raised by Thetis; built the great forge; trapped Ares and Aphrodite in the golden net (Odyssey 8); created Achilles' divine armor (Iliad 18); created Pandora (Hesiod's Theogony and Works and Days)
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Hesiod, Theogony 927-929 — parthenogenetic conception by Hera (in jealousy at Zeus's birthing of Athena)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Hesiod, Theogony 927-929

nodes.name: Gaia
nodes.domain: earth, creation, prophecy, motherhood, oaths
nodes.animals: serpent, bull, bear, scorpion, cow, centaur
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: giant earth goddess, rises from the ground, sometimes depicted nursing infants
nodes.significantEvent: bore Uranus the sky, the mountains, and the sea without union, held the original oracle at Delphi before Apollo, sent Typhon and the Giants against Zeus
nodes.symbolism: the living earth as divine maternal body, prophecy arising from the earth itself, the primordial feminine that precedes and encompasses all later deities
nodes.neumannArchetype: the archetypal Great Mother in her most primordial undifferentiated form, containing both creation and destruction
familyRoles: mother (with Ouranos) of the Titans, Cyclopes, Hekatonkheires
nodes.birthCircumstances: emerged from Chaos at the beginning of creation, self-generated
nodes.domain_source: Hesiod, Theogony 116-138 (the central source — the primordial trinity of Chaos, Gaia, Eros); Homer; Pausanias 1.22.3 (the Athenian Gaia cult); the Delphic oracle's pre-Apolline ownership
nodes.object_source: Gaia iconography — emerging from the earth (in childbearing scenes); cornucopia; serpent (her Pythian aspect)
nodes.animals_source: Gaia's sacred animals: snake/serpent (especially Python, the great serpent of Delphi originally guarding her oracle before Apollo's arrival)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Hesiod, Theogony; Aeschylus, Eumenides (the original Delphic oracle as Gaia's)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Gaia iconography — half-emerging-from-earth maternal figure; cf. the Pergamon Altar friezes where she pleads for her Giant sons
nodes.significantEvent_source: Hesiod, Theogony 116-153 — primordial earth-goddess emerging from Chaos (with Tartarus and Eros); produced Ouranos (sky), Pontos (sea), Ourea (mountains) from herself; mated with Ouranos to produce the Titans, Cyclopes, Hekatonkheires; encouraged Cronus to castrate Ouranos to free her children; later produced the Gigantes from Ouranos's spilt blood; produced Typhon from union with Tartarus to oppose Zeus after the Titanomachy
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Hesiod, Theogony 116-118 — emerged from Chaos with Tartarus and Eros
nodes.birthTypes_source: Hesiod, Theogony

nodes.name: Atalanta
nodes.domain: hunt, racing, virginity, the wild
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful, athletic huntress, the swiftest of all mortals
nodes.significantEvent: drew first blood against the Calydonian Boar, defeated all suitors in foot races until Hippomenes used golden apples from Aphrodite to distract her, both transformed into lions for profaning a temple
nodes.symbolism: the autonomous feminine warrior, the race that no man can win without divine trickery, the punishment for violating sacred space
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Artemis-like feminine who resists integration with the masculine, the wild huntress who must be tricked rather than conquered
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Iasus or Schoeneus and Clymene, exposed at birth because her father wanted a son, nursed by a she-bear sent by Artemis

nodes.name: Iapetus
nodes.domain: mortality, the mortal lifespan, craftsmanship
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Titan ancestor of the human race through his sons
nodes.significantEvent: fathered Atlas, Prometheus, Epimetheus, and Menoetius, whose actions shaped the relationship between gods and humanity, imprisoned in Tartarus after the Titanomachy
nodes.symbolism: the Titan whose lineage defines the human condition: foresight (Prometheus), hindsight (Epimetheus), endurance (Atlas), and recklessness (Menoetius)
nodes.neumannArchetype: the ancestral Titan whose sons embody the cardinal qualities of human consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Uranus and Gaia, one of the twelve Titans

nodes.neumannArchetype: the son who carries the fathers healing legacy into mortal communities
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of the god Asclepius and the mortal Aristodeme of Sicyon

nodes.neumannArchetype: the protective masculine that cleanses the community of dangerous spiritual forces

nodes.domain: war, fatherhood, the Trojan defense
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Trojan warrior and elder son of Antenor
nodes.significantEvent: attacked Agamemnon with a spear to avenge his brother Iphidamas, wounded Agamemnon but was killed by him
nodes.symbolism: the elder brother who dies avenging the younger, the futility of revenge in the face of superior arms
nodes.neumannArchetype: the protective eldest son whose vengeance against the patriarchal enemy leads to his own destruction
nodes.birthCircumstances: eldest son of the Trojan elder Antenor

nodes.domain: air, the unseen, invisibility, Titans
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Titan of air and concealment, moving unseen

nodes.symbolism: the unseen dimension of the world, the power of concealment and subtlety, the Titan of that which is present but imperceptible
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow Titan of concealment, the masculine principle of stealth and the invisible
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of the Titans Coeus and Phoebe in some accounts

nodes.name: Kushinadahime
nodes.domain: rice paddies, salvation, marriage, Susanoo, Yamata-no-Orochi
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful maiden associated with rice paddies, wife of Susanoo
nodes.significantEvent: was about to be sacrificed to the eight-headed serpent Yamata-no-Orochi when Susanoo arrived and saved her by devising a trap using eight vats of sake, married Susanoo after the serpent was slain
nodes.symbolism: the rice paddy maiden as the feminine saved from the monstrous serpent, the maiden-sacrifice averted by the hero, the marriage of the storm god to the rice maiden as the union of wild power with agricultural fertility
nodes.neumannArchetype: the anima rescued from the devouring dragon (Orochi) by the hero (Susanoo), the feminine of agricultural fertility saved from the destructive unconscious
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the earthly kami Ashinazuchi and Tenazuchi

nodes.name: Wu Zixu
nodes.domain: revenge, strategy, the Wu state, filial vengeance
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: powerful minister and military strategist of the Wu state
nodes.significantEvent: fled Chu and served the Wu state, helped Wu defeat Chu and had the Chu kings corpse whipped in revenge, later forced to commit suicide by the king of Wu after warning of the threat from Yue, his body was thrown in the river and he became the spirit of the tidal bore
nodes.symbolism: the loyal advisor whose warnings go unheeded, vengeance that spans kingdoms, the spirit of the tidal bore as the returning wrath of the betrayed
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine spirit of vengeance who transcends death to become a force of nature (the tidal bore), the betrayed advisor whose rage becomes elemental
nodes.birthCircumstances: originally from the Chu state, fled after his family was executed by the Chu king

nodes.name: Psyche
nodes.domain: the soul, love, beauty, transformation, immortality
nodes.animals: eagle, ram, ant, butterfly, donkey, cerberus
nodes.characterTrait: curious, beautiful, suffering, transformed, loving, immortal
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful mortal woman with butterfly wings, carrying a lamp and a golden box, the beloved of Cupid
nodes.significantEvent: loved by Cupid but forbidden to see his face, she lit a lamp to look at him and he fled, undertook impossible tasks set by Venus including a descent to the underworld, was ultimately made immortal and reunited with Cupid
nodes.symbolism: the butterfly as the symbol of the souls transformation, the lamp of curiosity that reveals the divine lover, the descent to the underworld as the souls initiation, the mortal who achieves immortality through suffering and love
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine soul (psyche) that must undergo trials and descend to the unconscious before achieving union with the divine masculine (Eros) and the transformation into immortality
nodes.birthCircumstances: mortal princess of extraordinary beauty who aroused the jealousy of Venus

nodes.name: Iphigenia
nodes.domain: sacrifice, purity, the transition from human to divine
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful young princess, maiden of noble bearing
nodes.significantEvent: sacrificed by her father Agamemnon at Aulis so the Greek fleet could sail to Troy, in some versions Artemis substituted a deer at the last moment and transported Iphigenia to Tauris as her priestess
nodes.symbolism: the innocent sacrifice demanded by divine power, the father who kills his daughter for political ambition, the maiden transformed through sacrifice into priestess
nodes.neumannArchetype: the sacrificed maiden archetype, the daughter offered to appease the Terrible Mother (Artemis) so the patriarchal quest (Troy) may proceed
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of King Agamemnon and Queen Clytemnestra of Mycenae
nodes.deathCircumstances: In some versions, such as Hyginus's Fabulae, Iphigenia is not sacrificed.

nodes.name: Amphiaraus
nodes.domain: prophecy, war, the underworld, divine favor
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: seer and warrior who foresaw his own death
nodes.significantEvent: foresaw his own death if he joined the Seven against Thebes but was forced to go by his wife Eriphyle who was bribed with Harmonias necklace, swallowed alive by the earth during battle through Zeus intervention
nodes.symbolism: the prophet who knows his fate but cannot escape it, the seer whose wife betrays him for gold, divine intervention as both destruction and salvation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the prophetic hero swallowed by the earth (Great Mother) rather than killed in battle, suggesting a return to the maternal ground
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Oicles, a prophet descended from the seer Melampus

nodes.name: Eunostus
nodes.domain: grain mills, justice for women
nodes.characterTrait: just, protective of women, vengeful when wronged
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Boeotian hero of unusual righteousness
nodes.significantEvent: murdered by his kinswomen for his virtue toward women, avenged by a plague until his cult was established
nodes.symbolism: the virtuous man destroyed by the very group he protects, the hero cult born from unjust murder
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive masculine destroyed by the shadow feminine, whose death establishes a new sacred order
nodes.birthCircumstances: His parents were Elieus, son of Cephissus, and Scias.

nodes.name: Bai Qi
nodes.domain: war, death, strategy, the Qin state
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: feared Qin general, known as the Human Butcher
nodes.significantEvent: buried alive 400,000 surrendered Zhao soldiers after the Battle of Changping in 260 BCE, the most devastating military action in ancient Chinese history, later forced to commit suicide by the Qin king
nodes.symbolism: the terrible cost of total war, military genius without mercy, the butcher as the shadow of the strategist
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow warrior whose absolute masculine efficiency produces total destruction
nodes.birthCircumstances: general of the state of Qin during the Warring States period

nodes.name: Dongyue Dadi
nodes.domain: death, the afterlife, mountains, judgment of the dead
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: imposing deity in imperial robes, the Great Emperor of the Eastern Peak
nodes.significantEvent: supreme judge of the dead in Chinese folk religion, rules over the ten courts of the underworld (Diyu), determines the fate of souls and their reincarnation, his bureaucracy mirrors the imperial government
nodes.symbolism: death as a bureaucratic process mirroring earthly government, Mount Tai as the gateway between the living and the dead, cosmic justice administered through divine bureaucracy
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father as judge of the dead, the patriarchal ordering of the afterlife through bureaucratic procedure
nodes.birthCircumstances: deity of Mount Tai (Taishan), the most sacred of Chinas Five Great Mountains

nodes.name: Taizi Changqin
nodes.domain: filial piety, music, the guqin, the Zhou Dynasty
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Zhou Dynasty prince known for his filial devotion and musical skill
nodes.significantEvent: legendary prince who exemplified filial piety through his devotion to the guqin and his parents
nodes.symbolism: filial devotion expressed through the art of music, the princes love channeled into cultural achievement
nodes.neumannArchetype: the obedient son who expresses his devotion through the creative arts
nodes.birthCircumstances: He is the only son of the fire god Zhurong and was the first musician in the Three Realms.

nodes.name: Praxidice
nodes.domain: justice, oaths, vengeance, execution of justice
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess or triple goddesses of vengeance and just retribution
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped at Haliartos in Boeotia as the enforcer of oaths and just punishment, associated with Persephone in some traditions
nodes.symbolism: the triple feminine principle of justice enforcement, the goddess who ensures oaths are kept through the threat of retribution
nodes.neumannArchetype: the triple Great Mother as the enforcer of cosmic law, the feminine principle that holds the patriarchal order to its own oaths

nodes.name: Kvasir
nodes.domain: poetry, the mead of poetry, wisdom, inspiration, fermentation
nodes.object: his blood (transformed into the mead of poetry); the vats Boðn, Són, and the cauldron Óðrerir into which his blood is collected
nodes.characterTrait: wise (formed from the spittle-pact of Aesir and Vanir), all-knowing, gentle
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Formed from the spittle of the Aesir and Vanir when they made peace after their war by all spitting into a common vat (Skáldskaparmál 5; Ynglinga saga 4); a being of total wisdom who could answer any question.
nodes.significantEvent: Born of the spittle-truce. Travels widely teaching wisdom. Killed by the dwarves Fjalar and Galar, who drain his blood into Óðrerir, Boðn, and Són; mix it with honey to create the mead of poetry. The mead passes through Suttungr (a giant) before Odin steals it in eagle-form (Skáldskaparmál 5-6; Hávamál 104-110).
nodes.symbolism: the peace treaty made flesh that is murdered for its wisdom, blood mixed with honey as the sacred drink of inspiration, poetry as the product of sacrifice and fermentation, the theft of inspiration as the shamanic quest
nodes.neumannArchetype: the sacrificed divine child whose blood becomes the mead of poetic consciousness, wisdom as the product of death and transformation
birthTypes: miraculous — from spittle of two pantheons
nodes.birthCircumstances: Formed from the spittle of all the Aesir and Vanir when they made peace after their war.
nodes.deathCircumstances: Killed by the dwarves Fjalar and Galar; his blood drained into the vats Óðrerir, Boðn, and Són; mixed with honey to make the mead of poetry.
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Skáldskaparmál 5-6 (the central source — the mead of poetry narrative); Heimskringla, Ynglinga saga 4 (the alternative version); Hávamál 104-110 (Odin's theft of the mead, with Kvasir's role implicit)

nodes.name: Mut
nodes.domain: motherhood, the sky, protection, royalty, vultures
nodes.object: double-crown of Egypt; vulture-headdress (her hieroglyph and emblem); ankh; was-scepter
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Anthropomorphic woman wearing the double-crown of Egypt with a vulture-headdress beneath; her name Mwt means 'mother' (hieroglyph: vulture). Sometimes lion-headed (in her Sekhmet-fused aspect).
nodes.significantEvent: Consort of Amun and mother of Khonsu in the Theban triad. Her cult-center was the Mut-precinct at Karnak. Often syncretically merged with Sekhmet, Hathor, and Wadjet (in her Eye of Ra aspect).
nodes.symbolism: the divine mother whose wings of protection spread over Egypt, the vulture as the supreme maternal symbol (feeding young with her own blood), the queen of heaven as consort of the king of gods
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the supreme maternal protectress, the sky-mother whose wings shelter all creation
nodes.birthCircumstances: Primordial; Theban tradition treats her as eternal consort of Amun.

nodes.domain: the moon, time, healing, travel, youth
nodes.object: moon-disk and crescent on his head; the crook and flail; sidelock of youth; sometimes the falcon-headed depiction

nodes.significantEvent: Moon-god, son of Amun and Mut in the Theban triad; god of time, healing, and travel. The Bentresh Stela records his being sent to heal a foreign princess. In the Khonsu Cosmogony (a late Theban tradition), takes on the supreme creator role.
nodes.symbolism: the divine youth as the moon, the sidelock as perpetual childhood, the moon as the nocturnal form of divine light, the travelers protector who illuminates the night
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child of the Great Father (Amun) and Great Mother (Mut), the lunar consciousness that illuminates the darkness of the unconscious
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Amun and Mut in the Theban triad.

nodes.name: Moses
nodes.domain: law, liberation, prophecy, covenant, leadership
nodes.object: the rod (which becomes a serpent, Exodus 4; turns the Nile to blood; parts the Red Sea; strikes the rock for water); the two tablets of the law; the Bronze Serpent (Numbers 21:9); his veil (after the Sinai descent, Exodus 34:33-35); the priestly garments and tabernacle furnishings (which he oversees)
nodes.characterTrait: initially reluctant ('I am slow of speech', Exodus 4:10), eventually authoritative; meek (Numbers 12:3 — 'the meekest man on earth'); faithful (Hebrews 3:5); intercessory (Exodus 32:11-13, 32:31-32); legislator; theophanically singular (the only one who 'spoke face-to-face with YHWH', Exodus 33:11, Numbers 12:8, Deuteronomy 34:10)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: In Exodus 34:29-35, his face shines (Hebrew qāran, 'rayed' or 'horned' — the Vulgate's translation cornuta gave rise to Michelangelo's horned Moses) after descending from Sinai with the second tablets; he wears a veil thereafter except when speaking with YHWH or to the people. Lived 120 years; 'his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated' at death (Deuteronomy 34:7).
nodes.significantEvent: Born in Egypt to Hebrew slaves; hidden in the bulrushes; raised in Pharaoh's household (Exodus 2). Flees to Midian after killing an Egyptian; marries Zipporah; encounters YHWH at the burning bush (Exodus 3-4). Returns to Egypt; brings the ten plagues (Exodus 7-12); leads the Exodus through the Red Sea (Exodus 14); receives the law at Sinai (Exodus 19-24); intercedes after the Golden Calf (Exodus 32). Leads Israel through 40 years in the wilderness; dies on Mount Nebo, prevented from entering the Promised Land because of the waters-of-Meribah incident (Numbers 20:7-13, Deuteronomy 34). In Quran, leads Bani Isrāʾīl out of Egypt, receives the Tawrat (Torah), and is the model prophet.
nodes.symbolism: Lawgiver; liberator; mediator between God and humanity; the Exodus as paradigm of liberation; the covenant of law
nodes.birthCircumstances: Born to Amram and Jochebed of the tribe of Levi during the Egyptian persecution. Hidden in a basket of bulrushes in the Nile to escape Pharaoh's decree; rescued by Pharaoh's daughter; raised in the Egyptian court but nursed by his own mother (Exodus 2:1-10). His name is given an Egyptian etymology by tradition but a Hebrew folk-etymology in Exodus 2:10 ('drawn out of the water').
nodes.deathCircumstances: Climbs Mount Nebo, views the Promised Land from afar, and dies there at 120 years (Deuteronomy 34:1-7). YHWH himself buries him 'in the valley in the land of Moab, opposite Beth-peor; but no one knows the place of his burial to this day' (Deuteronomy 34:6). The post-canonical Assumption of Moses (Testament of Moses) describes a dispute between Michael and Satan over Moses's body (cf. Jude 1:9).
nodes.domain_source: Exodus through Deuteronomy (the Pentateuch's central figure); Quran (Mūsā, the most-mentioned prophet — Surah 7, 20, 26, 28 in particular, plus many other passages); Talmudic and Midrashic literature; Philo, Vita Mosis; Josephus, Antiquities 2-4

nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Exodus 34:29-35; Deuteronomy 34:7
nodes.birthTypes_source: Exodus 2:1-10
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Exodus 2:1-10
nodes.deathCircumstances_source: Deuteronomy 34:1-8; Jude 1:9 (with Assumption of Moses tradition)

nodes.name: Hera
nodes.domain: marriage, women, childbirth, family, sovereignty, sky
nodes.object: pomegranate, scepter, crown, chariot, arrow, spear
nodes.animals: cow, cuckoo, peacock, eagle, serpent, snake, bull, bear, tortoise, crane, minotaur, hydra
nodes.characterTrait: jealous, vengeful, regal, protective of marriage, powerful, vindictive
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: tall, majestic, cow-eyed, beautiful, crowned with a polos or diadem, veiled
nodes.significantEvent: persecutes Heracles throughout his life, punishes Zeus many lovers and their children, tricks Zeus with the golden apple, sides against Troy in the Trojan War
nodes.symbolism: the sacred institution of marriage, feminine sovereignty and jealous power, the tension between patriarchal rule and the older feminine divine order
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Goddess diminished to jealous consort under patriarchal Olympian order, retaining traces of her former sovereignty
familyRoles: youngest daughter of Cronus and Rhea
mother of Ares, Hebe, Eileithyia, Hephaestus
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Cronus and Rhea, swallowed by Cronus at birth and later disgorged, sister and wife of Zeus
nodes.domain_source: Homer, Iliad passim (especially Books 14-15); Hesiod, Theogony 921-923; Homeric Hymn 12; the Heraion at Argos (the major cult-center); the Heraion at Samos; Pausanias
nodes.object_source: Hera iconography — diadem and high-cylindrical polos; peacock-feathered scepter; pomegranate (fertility); cuckoo (Zeus's first approach to her)
nodes.animals_source: Hera's sacred animals: peacock (whose tail-feathers received Argus's hundred eyes); cuckoo (Zeus's first approach); cow (her epithet βοῶπις 'cow-eyed'); lion
nodes.characterTrait_source: Homeric corpus — especially her wrath against Zeus's mistresses and their offspring (Heracles, Dionysus, Io)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard Hera iconography — mature regal queen, diademed, often with peacock-feathered scepter; the Argive Heraion sculptural tradition
nodes.significantEvent_source: Hesiod, Theogony 921-923; Homer; Apollodorus 1.3.1 — youngest daughter of Cronus and Rhea, swallowed and regurgitated; married Zeus (Iliad 14.295-296 narrates their first union on Mount Ida); persecuted Zeus's mistresses (Io, Leto, Alcmene, Semele) and offspring (Heracles, Dionysus); mother of Ares, Hebe, Eileithyia, Hephaestus
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Hesiod, Theogony — swallowed by Cronus, regurgitated when Zeus tricked him
nodes.birthTypes_source: Hesiod, Theogony

nodes.name: Proioxis
nodes.domain: battle charge, the onset of battle, forward rush
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: spirit of the forward charge in battle
nodes.significantEvent: the counter-force to Palioxis (Retreat), personification of the forward charge that drives an army against the enemy
nodes.symbolism: the momentum of the attack, the forward drive that overcomes fear and drives warriors into combat
nodes.neumannArchetype: the aggressive masculine drive toward engagement, the forward surge of martial consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: associated with Ares and the battle daimons

nodes.name: Omoikane
nodes.domain: wisdom, thought, deliberation, the counsel of the gods
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the kami of wisdom and thought, the divine counselor and thinker
nodes.significantEvent: devised the plan to lure Amaterasu out of the cave, including the mirror, the comic dance, and the assembly of the gods, his wisdom saved the world from eternal darkness
nodes.symbolism: wisdom as the divine quality that saves the world, the plan that restores the light as the supreme intellectual achievement, the counselor-god as the essential thinker behind the heroic act
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wise old man archetype among the kami, the masculine intellect that devises the plan to restore solar consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: parents: Takamimusubi

nodes.domain: the eight islands, marriage, the dwelling of the earthly kami, creation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: one of the kami born from the creative acts of Izanagi and Izanami during the generation of the land
nodes.significantEvent: born during the generation of the land and kami by the primordial couple, one of the many deities produced during the creation of the Japanese islands and the natural world
nodes.symbolism: the generation of specific kami for each aspect of the created world, the divine attention to every detail of creation
nodes.neumannArchetype: one of the generated consciousnesses of the created world, a specific differentiation of the creative act of the primordial parents
nodes.birthCircumstances: He is the son of Susanoo-no-Mikoto and Kushinadahime.

nodes.name: Mixcoatl
nodes.domain: hunting, the Milky Way, stars, war, the Chichimec ancestors, fire-making
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Cloud Serpent, god of hunting and the Milky Way, associated with the Chichimec warrior ancestors
nodes.significantEvent: father of Quetzalcoatl and the four hundred Mimixcoa (stars), associated with the Milky Way as a celestial hunter, ancestor of the Chichimec peoples, patron of hunting and fire-making through friction
nodes.symbolism: the Cloud Serpent as the Milky Way stretching across the sky, the celestial hunter whose arrows are the stars, fire-making by friction as the hunters gift, the Chichimec ancestor as the wild hunter who precedes civilization
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father of the hunt and the stars, the wild masculine of the Milky Way who precedes and generates the civilized order
nodes.birthCircumstances: an ancient hunting deity predating Aztec civilization
nodes.domain_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — Mixcoatl ('Cloud Serpent') as god of hunting and the Milky Way; Sahagún Book 1.18; Codex Telleriano-Remensis; Chimalman narrative (the conception of Quetzalcoatl-Topiltzin)
nodes.object_source: Florentine Codex — bow and arrows; the netted hunting cape; black-and-white face stripes
nodes.animals_source: Mixcoatl's sacred animals: deer (the central hunted animal); two-headed-deer prodigy (his form in some narratives)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Florentine Codex 1.18; Chimalpopoca
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Codex Telleriano-Remensis — hunter-warrior with black-and-white striped face, bearing bow and arrows
nodes.significantEvent_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — Chichimec hunting-god incorporated into Aztec pantheon. Identified with the Milky Way ('Cloud Serpent'). Father of Quetzalcoatl-Topiltzin (the legendary Toltec king) by Chimalman whom he shot with an arrow that bounced off her shield. Sometimes identified with Camaxtli (the Tlaxcaltec form).
