nodes.name: Fortuna
nodes.domain: prophecy, luck, fate
nodes.significantEvent: Parallels Indian/Tibetan Tara
nodes.symbolism: Fate goddess in lion chariot; parallel to Tara; Great Mother as fate
nodes.neumannArchetype: Sat in chariot drawn by lions, paralleling Tara on lion.
familyRoles: in Praeneste tradition, mother of Jupiter and Juno (uniquely Italic)
many cult-aspects (Primigenia, Virilis, Muliebris, Redux, Augusta)
nodes.domain_source: Ovid, Fasti; Plutarch, On the Fortune of the Romans; the cult of Fortuna at Praeneste (the most famous Italian oracular sanctuary); the cult of Fortuna Primigenia; the Servian temple of Fortuna in Rome; Livy 1.46
nodes.object_source: Fortuna iconography — cornucopia; rudder (guiding fortune's unstable course); ball (her instability); wings (in some traditions); the wheel (in late-classical depictions, though the rota Fortunae is largely medieval)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Plutarch; Roman cult tradition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Fortuna iconography — woman with cornucopia and rudder, sometimes wings, often blindfolded; the Praenestine Fortuna shown nursing twin infants (Jupiter and Juno, in a uniquely-Italic tradition)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Roman tradition — identified with Greek Tyche but with rich indigenous Italic origins; the Praeneste sanctuary was a major oracular center with sortes (lots); Fortuna Primigenia uniquely Italic (the mother-Fortuna nursing Jupiter and Juno); Fortuna Virilis (women's cult); Fortuna Muliebris; Fortuna Redux (safe-return); the cult exploded under Augustus with Fortuna Augusta
nodes.birthTypes_source: Roman cult tradition

nodes.name: Wen Zhong
nodes.domain: war, loyalty, thunder, the Shang Dynasty, the Investiture of the Gods
nodes.characterTrait: fierce, loyal, thunderous, devoted to the Shang
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: fearsome warrior with a third eye on his forehead that emits a destructive beam of light
nodes.significantEvent: remained loyal to the Shang Dynasty against the Zhou rebellion despite knowing the Shang was doomed, his third eye could see through illusions, after death he was deified as the God of Thunder
nodes.symbolism: absolute loyalty even to a doomed cause, the third eye of truth that cannot save one from the wrong side of fate, the thunder as the voice of the loyalist even after death
nodes.neumannArchetype: the loyal patriarchal servant whose third eye (heightened consciousness) cannot overcome his devotion to the dying order, transformed into thunder (the voice of the old law)
nodes.birthCircumstances: Grand Tutor of the Shang Dynasty in the Fengshen Yanyi
nodes.deathCircumstances: His mount is named Mo Qilin (the Qilin has wind and cloud horns on its head, can fly in the sky with a single flap, and can travel a thousand miles in an instant; later it was killed by Leizhenzi).

nodes.name: Satan
nodes.domain: evil, temptation, pride, chaos, deception, rebellion
nodes.object: serpent-form (Eden in Christian and rabbinic interpretation, though Genesis 3 itself does not name him); the chains with which he is bound for a thousand years (Revelation 20:1-3); the lake of fire (Revelation 20:10)
nodes.characterTrait: accusing (the original sense of śāṭān), tempting, deceiving, prideful, fallen, prince-of-this-world, ultimately defeated
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: In Job, appears among the bnê hāʾĕlōhīm without distinct description. As the serpent in Eden (Christian-rabbinic interpretation). In Revelation 12, the great red dragon with seven heads and ten horns. Medieval iconography: horned, hooved, bat-winged, often red — but these are post-biblical accretions.
nodes.significantEvent: In the Hebrew Bible, the śāṭān (accuser) of Job (Job 1-2) and Joshua the high priest (Zechariah 3); incites David to number Israel (1 Chronicles 21:1). In the NT: tempts Jesus in the wilderness (Matthew 4 / Luke 4); enters Judas (John 13:27); falls 'like lightning from heaven' (Luke 10:18); cast out at the cross/resurrection (John 12:31); identified with the dragon and ancient serpent (Revelation 12:9); bound for a thousand years and ultimately cast into the lake of fire (Revelation 20). In Christian tradition, fell from heaven through pride (Augustine, Aquinas); Milton's Paradise Lost is the major literary elaboration.
nodes.symbolism: The Adversary; the Fall from grace through pride; the tempter; embodiment of evil and moral corruption; the shadow archetype; cosmic opposition to the divine
birthTypes: angelic — created good, fell through pride (Christian theology)
deathTypes: eschatological — cast into lake of fire
nodes.birthCircumstances: In Christian theological tradition, an angel originally created good who fell through pride (Augustine, Aquinas). The biblical text does not narrate his origin directly; the Genesis-3 serpent and the bnê hāʾĕlōhīm of Job 1-2 are the principal direct attestations.
nodes.deathCircumstances: Eschatological: bound for a thousand years (Revelation 20:1-3), released, finally 'cast into the lake of fire and brimstone... and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever' (Revelation 20:10).
nodes.domain_source: Hebrew Bible: 1 Chronicles 21:1; Job 1-2; Zechariah 3:1-2 (śāṭān as 'the accuser'). NT: Matthew 4:1-11; Mark 1:13; Luke 4:1-13, 10:18, 22:3; John 8:44, 13:27; 2 Corinthians 4:4 (god of this age), 11:14 (angel of light); Ephesians 6:11-12; 1 Peter 5:8; Revelation 12:7-12, 20:1-3, 20:7-10. Pseudepigrapha: 1 Enoch (Watchers tradition); Life of Adam and Eve (the fall of Satan in pride); 2 Enoch. Patristic and medieval demonology
nodes.object_source: Genesis 3 (the serpent, Christian-rabbinic identification); Revelation 12 (the great red dragon); Revelation 20
nodes.animals_source: Symbolic embodiment from Genesis 3 (the serpent, identified with Satan in Christian and rabbinic interpretation); Revelation 12:9 ('that ancient serpent, who is called the devil and Satan'); Revelation 20:2 (the dragon)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Job 1-2 (the accuser); Matthew 4 (the tempter); John 8:44 ('a liar from the beginning'); Isaiah 14:12-15 (read in Christian tradition as the fall of Satan, though originally about the king of Babylon); Revelation 12, 20
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Job 1-2; Genesis 3 (serpent identification per Christian/rabbinic tradition); Revelation 12:3
nodes.significantEvent_source: Job 1-2; Zechariah 3; 1 Chronicles 21; Matthew 4; Luke 10:18; John 12-13; Revelation 12, 20; patristic and Miltonic tradition
nodes.birthTypes_source: Christian theological tradition (Augustine, Civ. Dei 11; Aquinas, ST I.63); Isaiah 14:12-15 (read typologically); Ezekiel 28:12-19 (the king of Tyre, read typologically)
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Augustine, City of God 11; Aquinas, Summa Theologica I.63; Isaiah 14 and Ezekiel 28 typologies

nodes.name: Glaucus
nodes.domain: the sea, prophecy, transformation, fishing, herbs
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: sea god with fish tail and seaweed hair, green-skinned
nodes.significantEvent: ate a magical herb that made fish come alive, threw himself into the sea and was transformed into a sea god by Oceanus and Tethys, became a prophetic deity consulted by sailors
nodes.symbolism: transformation from mortal to divine through contact with the magical herb, the fisherman who becomes a fish-god, the sea as the realm of prophetic wisdom
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine transformed through consuming the Great Mothers magical vegetation, the mortal absorbed into the oceanic unconscious and emerging as a prophet
nodes.birthCircumstances: originally a mortal fisherman or son of the sea deities Nereus and Thetis
nodes.deathCircumstances: Later in the war, when the fighting over Achilles' corpse took place, Glaucus was killed by Ajax.

nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow of consciousness that avoids responsibility through rationalization
nodes.birthCircumstances: According to Pindar, she was the daughter of Epimetheus.

nodes.name: Hongjun Laozu
nodes.domain: creation, the Dao, primordial unity, origin of all
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the most ancient and primordial Daoist deity, depicted as an ancient sage sitting on a cloud
nodes.significantEvent: emerged from primordial chaos and taught the Three Pure Ones who in turn created the cosmos, represents the undifferentiated Dao before any separation or creation, teacher of Laozi, Yuanshi Tianzun, and Tongtian Jiaozhu
nodes.symbolism: the Dao before creation, the unity before all differentiation, the ancestor of the ancestors, the primordial teacher from whom all subsequent wisdom flows
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial father beyond all form, the original consciousness from which all subsequent differentiation of the psyche emerges
nodes.birthCircumstances: the first being to emerge from the primordial chaos, teacher of the Three Pure Ones (Sanqing)

nodes.name: Randeng Daoren
nodes.domain: Buddhism, Daoism, enlightenment, the Investiture of the Gods
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: ancient sage who bridges Daoist and Buddhist traditions, often depicted carrying an eternal lamp
nodes.significantEvent: in the Fengshen Yanyi he is a Daoist master who foresees the coming of Buddhism and arranges the transition, his ever-burning lamp symbolizes the transmission of wisdom across traditions
nodes.symbolism: the transmission of spiritual wisdom across religious traditions, the ever-burning lamp of enlightenment that precedes and anticipates the future, the bridge between Daoism and Buddhism
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wise old man who transmits consciousness from one tradition to the next, the lamp-bearer who illuminates the path between the old and new spiritual orders
nodes.birthCircumstances: Daoist immortal who becomes the Dipankara Buddha (Lamp-Lighter Buddha) in Buddhist tradition

nodes.name: Medusa
nodes.domain: terror, protection, death, petrification
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: snake-haired
nodes.significantEvent: transformed from a beautiful maiden into a monster by Athena for being violated by Poseidon in Athenas temple, beheaded by Perseus, from her blood sprang Pegasus and Chrysaor
nodes.symbolism: the petrifying terror of the feminine, the apotropaic face that wards off evil, beauty destroyed and made monstrous, the gaze that freezes consciousness
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Terrible Mother whose petrifying gaze belongs to the province of the negative pole (M-), representing the terrifying aspect of the unconscious feminine
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the sea deities Phorcys and Ceto, the only mortal among the three Gorgon sisters

nodes.name: Graeae
nodes.domain: the gray sea, old age, guardianship, hidden knowledge
nodes.characterTrait: gray, ancient, sharing one eye and one tooth, withholding
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: three old women sharing a single eye and a single tooth between them, gray-haired from birth
nodes.significantEvent: Perseus tricked them into revealing the location of the Gorgon Medusa by stealing their shared eye and tooth, refusing to return them until they told him
nodes.symbolism: shared consciousness (one eye) and shared power (one tooth) among ancient beings, the guardians of terrible secrets who can be tricked, old age as the gateway to hidden knowledge
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Triple Goddess in her Terrible Old Woman aspect, the ancient guardians whose diminished powers still hold the key to the monstrous
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughters of Phorcys and Ceto, sisters of the Gorgons: Deino, Enyo, and Pemphredo

nodes.name: Isis
nodes.domain: magic, kingship, motherhood, rebirth, mourning, healing, protection
nodes.object: throne hieroglyph, sistrum, knot of Isis (tjet/tyet), wings
nodes.characterTrait: nurturing, powerful, cunning, grieving, protective, resourceful
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: crowned, cow horns, solar disk
nodes.significantEvent: Cunning of Isis to learn Ra's secret name (Papyrus Turin 1993). Search for and reassembly of Osiris's body. Mourning ritual with Nephthys. Hiding of the infant Horus in the marshes of Khemmis. Healing the scorpion-stung child. Aid to Horus in his contest with Set. Isis-Sothis as the rising of the Nile.
nodes.symbolism: Throne as 'seat' - the mother is the throne that makes the king; combines features of Terrible and Good Mother; Stella Maris (Star of the Sea)
nodes.neumannArchetype: Central archetype combining Terrible and Good Mother. Corresponds to the full Great Mother archetype.
nodes.birthCircumstances: Daughter of Geb (earth) and Nut (sky), born in the early period of the gods. One of the children of Geb and Nut: Osiris, Isis, Set, Nephthys (and in some genealogies, Horus the Elder).
nodes.domain_source: Pyramid Texts §1466-67; Coffin Texts; Book of the Dead; the Lamentations of Isis and Nephthys; Plutarch, Isis and Osiris (Roman period); Apuleius, Metamorphoses 11 (the Roman Isis-cult); the Aretalogy of Isis (Kyme inscription)
nodes.object_source: Standard Isiac iconography; Plutarch; throne-headdress (the hieroglyph for her name); the tyet-knot (Isis-knot); sistrum; the wings she spreads to fan life back into Osiris
nodes.significantEvent_source: Plutarch 13-20; Pyramid Texts §1466-67 (the resurrection-from-Isis hymn); the Lamentations
nodes.characterTrait_source: Plutarch; the Aretalogy of Isis; Coffin Texts
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard Isiac iconography; throne-headdress
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Plutarch 12 — born on epagomenal day; daughter of Geb and Nut
nodes.birthTypes_source: Plutarch 12

nodes.name: Protesilaus
nodes.domain: war, sacrifice, the first death at Troy, the threshold
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: young warrior who leaped first from the Greek ships onto Trojan soil
nodes.significantEvent: first Greek to set foot on Trojan soil knowing an oracle predicted the first to land would be the first to die, killed immediately by Hector, his wife Laodamia was so devoted she had a statue of him made and embraced it until the gods returned him from the dead for three hours
nodes.symbolism: the willing sacrifice of being first, the threshold hero who pays the price of initiation, love that transcends death, the first step onto hostile ground
nodes.neumannArchetype: the sacrificial hero who crosses the threshold first, paying with his life to open the way for the collective
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Iphicles king of Phylace in Thessaly
nodes.deathCircumstances: An oracle by Thetis had prophesied that the first Greek to walk on the land after stepping off a ship in the Trojan War would be the first to die, he was himself slain by Hector.

nodes.name: Jesus
nodes.domain: salvation, resurrection, redemption, sacrifice, love, forgiveness, eternal life, prophecy, messianic kingship
nodes.object: cross (the central Christian symbol of his death); crown of thorns; spear (Longinus); sponge of vinegar; robe (cast lots for); five loaves and two fish (feeding miracle); the chalice/grail (Last Supper, John 13)
nodes.characterTrait: compassionate (Matthew 9:36, 14:14), authoritative ('he taught them as one having authority, not as the scribes', Mark 1:22), miracle-working, parable-teaching, prophetically critical, paradoxical (the kingdom of God in parable), suffering, forgiving ('Father, forgive them', Luke 23:34), risen, exalted
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Galilean Jew of the early 1st century CE; the NT provides no physical description. Identified in early Christian art under various symbolic forms (the Good Shepherd, the lamb, the fish, the chi-rho); the bearded long-haired iconographic type stabilizes from the 4th-6th centuries onward (Christ Pantocrator).
nodes.significantEvent: Conceived of the Holy Spirit and born to Mary in Bethlehem (Luke 2, Matthew 1-2). Baptized by John in the Jordan; the Spirit descends as a dove and the Father's voice declares him beloved (Mark 1:9-11). Tempted in the wilderness (Matthew 4 / Luke 4). Public ministry of teaching, healing, exorcising. Transfiguration (Mark 9). Triumphal entry into Jerusalem; Last Supper instituting the Eucharist (Mark 14, 1 Corinthians 11). Arrested in Gethsemane; tried before the Sanhedrin and Pilate; crucified at Golgotha; dies and is buried; rises on the third day; appears to disciples; ascends into heaven (Acts 1). In Quran: born of virgin Mary by Allah's command (3:47); a prophet and the Messiah (al-masīḥ); performed miracles by Allah's leave; was not crucified — Allah raised him alive (4:157-158); will return at the end of days.
nodes.symbolism: The Logos (Word of God); the Lamb of God; the Good Shepherd; the Light of the World; sacrificial love and redemption; dying-and-rising god archetype
familyRoles: only-begotten of the Father (in Christian theology)
nodes.birthCircumstances: Conceived by the Holy Spirit in the Virgin Mary in Nazareth (the Annunciation); born in Bethlehem during the reign of Augustus (Luke 2). In Quran, conceived by Allah's word 'be' (kun fa-yakūn, 3:47); Mary births him alone under a palm tree (19:23-26).
nodes.deathCircumstances: Crucified at Golgotha during the procuratorship of Pontius Pilate (c. 30-33 CE) at the instigation of the Jerusalem temple authorities. Buried in the tomb of Joseph of Arimathea. Risen on the third day per the four Gospels and 1 Corinthians 15:3-8. In Islamic theology (Quran 4:157-158), he was not crucified, but Allah raised him to himself; another was made to appear in his likeness; he will return at the end of days.
nodes.domain_source: The four canonical Gospels (Matthew, Mark, Luke, John); the Pauline corpus and Acts; the rest of the NT; Quran 3:45-59, 4:157-159, 4:171-172, 5:46-47, 5:110-118, 19:16-36, 43:57-65, 61:6, 61:14 (ʿĪsā son of Maryam); Josephus, Antiquities 18.3.3 (Testimonium Flavianum, contested); Talmud Sanhedrin 43a (brief polemical references); Tacitus, Annals 15.44; the Nicene Creed (325/381) and the Definition of Chalcedon (451)
nodes.object_source: The Passion narratives in all four Gospels; John 6:9 (loaves); Mark 14:23 / Matthew 26:27 / Luke 22:20 / 1 Corinthians 11:25 (the cup of the Last Supper)
nodes.characterTrait_source: The four Gospels passim; Pauline christology (Philippians 2:5-11)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: The NT is silent on his physical appearance; Christian iconographic tradition develops from late antiquity onward
nodes.significantEvent_source: The four Gospels; Acts 1; 1 Corinthians 11; Quran 3:45-59, 4:157-159, 19:16-36
nodes.eventTypes_source: The Gospels; Acts; Pauline corpus; Quran
nodes.birthTypes_source: Matthew 1:18-25; Luke 1:26-38; Quran 3:45-47, 19:16-22; Christian creedal tradition
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Matthew 1-2; Luke 1-2; Quran 3:45-47, 19:16-26
nodes.deathTypes_source: The four Gospels (crucifixion and resurrection); Quran 4:157-158 (denying the crucifixion, affirming Allah's raising him)

nodes.name: Sanxing
nodes.domain: happiness, prosperity, longevity, the Three Stars, blessings
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: three star gods usually depicted together: Fu (Happiness) holds a child, Lu (Prosperity) wears official robes, Shou (Longevity) has an elongated head and carries a peach
nodes.significantEvent: displayed together in homes and businesses to attract the three supreme blessings of Chinese culture: happiness, prosperity, and long life, especially prominent during Chinese New Year
nodes.symbolism: the threefold blessing of the complete good life, the unity of happiness, wealth, and longevity as the fullest expression of heavenly favor, the three stars as the celestial guarantors of human flourishing
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive triple patriarch, the three faces of the benevolent father archetype bestowing the three essential gifts of consciousness: joy, abundance, and endurance
nodes.birthCircumstances: personifications of the three most important blessings in Chinese culture, associated with specific stars

nodes.name: Ha
nodes.domain: the Western Desert, fertility, oases, boundaries
nodes.characterTrait: western, boundary-guarding, desert-dwelling, fertile in the desert
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: man wearing the crown of the Western Desert (Libya), sometimes with a curved knife
nodes.significantEvent: protected Egypts western border against Libyan invasion, presided over the oases that provided essential resources, his domain was the vast desert to the west of the Nile Valley
nodes.symbolism: the desert boundary as a sacred frontier, the guardian of the west where the living world meets the realm of the dead, the oasis as the gift of fertility within the barren desert
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine guardian of the western threshold between life and death, the patriarchal protector of the boundary between the known and unknown
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient god of the Western Desert

nodes.name: Huehuecoyotl
nodes.domain: trickery, dance, music, old age, storytelling, the old coyote
nodes.characterTrait: tricky, old, dancing, storytelling, coyote-like, mischievous, humorous
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Very Old Coyote, a trickster deity depicted as an old coyote or a man in coyote attire, associated with music and dance
nodes.significantEvent: the trickster deity who brings disorder through pranks and humor, a patron of music, dance, and storytelling, his tricks often backfire, associated with sexuality and indulgence
nodes.symbolism: the old coyote as the trickster who disrupts order through laughter, music and dance as the arts of the trickster, the coyote as the cunning animal who embodies the disorderly wisdom of chaos
nodes.neumannArchetype: the trickster-father, the old masculine of chaos whose pranks disrupt the ordered consciousness but also bring laughter and creative disorder
nodes.birthCircumstances: parents: Omecihuatl (Emerged by Tecpatl)

nodes.name: Itztapaltotec
nodes.domain: obsidian, flint, Xipe Totec, sacrifice, the obsidian lord
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Obsidian Knife of Xipe Totec, or an aspect of the flaying god associated with the obsidian sacrificial blade
nodes.significantEvent: associated with the obsidian blade used in the flaying sacrifices of the Xipe Totec cult, represents the divine aspect of the sacrificial instrument itself
nodes.symbolism: the obsidian blade as the divine instrument of sacrificial flaying, the knife as having its own divine identity, the tool of sacrifice as a god in its own right
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow-instrument of sacrifice, the obsidian consciousness of the blade that separates the skin from the body

nodes.name: Dea Viriplaca
nodes.domain: marriage, reconciliation, domestic peace, marital harmony
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the goddess who reconciles husbands and wives, her shrine was on the Palatine Hill
nodes.significantEvent: quarreling wives went to her shrine on the Palatine to seek reconciliation with their husbands, her temple was a place of marital counseling and domestic peace-making
nodes.symbolism: the divine feminine as the reconciler of the marriage bond, the shrine as the space where marital discord is healed, domestic peace as a sacred concern
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine principle of marital harmony, the anima that reconciles the masculine and feminine within the marriage bond

nodes.name: Azrael
nodes.domain: death, transition, souls, afterlife
nodes.object: scroll on which the names and lifespans of all souls are written (per Islamic tradition); his hand (with which he extracts the soul)
nodes.characterTrait: awe-inspiring, inevitable, gentle to believers/harsh to disbelievers per Islamic tradition, faithful to his task
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: In Islamic tradition, an angel of immense size with four faces or many eyes (number varies by source); his appearance varies according to whom he comes for. In one famous hadith, Moses strikes the angel of death and puts out his eye — Allah heals him and sends him back.
nodes.significantEvent: Charged with extracting souls at the appointed time of death (Quran 32:11, 6:61). In one hadith, Moses strikes him and puts out his eye when he comes; Allah heals him and gives him the option to return to Moses with the choice of death. In some traditions, he travels at the speed of light; in others, he can be in many places at once.
nodes.symbolism: Psychopomp; transition between life and death; benevolent guide of souls; inevitability of death
nodes.birthCircumstances: Created angelic being; the angel of death.
nodes.domain_source: Quran 32:11 ('the angel of death' — malak al-mawt — though the name Azrael is post-Quranic); Sahih al-Bukhari (hadith of the angel of death visiting Moses); Islamic eschatological tradition; later rabbinic literature names the angel of death variously (Samael, the Angel of Death) — Azrael (ʿAzrāʾīl) is more strongly Islamic than Jewish
nodes.object_source: Islamic eschatological tradition (the lawḥ maḥfūẓ — the preserved tablet — bears the names and lifespans)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Quran 32:11; Islamic ḥadīth and eschatological tradition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Sahih al-Bukhari (the Moses hadith); Islamic eschatological tradition
nodes.significantEvent_source: Quran 32:11, 6:61; Sahih al-Bukhari (the Moses hadith)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Standard angelology
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Standard angelology

nodes.name: Domiduca
nodes.domain: guidance, leading the bride, marriage, domestic transition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess who led the bride to her new home, associated with the marriage ceremony
nodes.significantEvent: invoked during Roman weddings to guide the bride from her fathers house to her husbands home, one of the many specialized deities of the Roman marriage ceremony
nodes.symbolism: the divine guidance of the bride through the threshold from maidenhood to marriage, the transition between households as a sacred journey requiring divine escort
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine guide through the transition from one domestic world to another, the anima of marital transition

nodes.domain: the south wind, Huitzilopochtli, the southern direction
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the South Wind, associated with Huitzilopochtli and the southern direction
nodes.significantEvent: one of the four directional wind deities, associated with the south and the war god Huitzilopochtli
nodes.symbolism: the south wind as the breath of the war god, the directional wind as a manifestation of the deity who rules that quarter, the warm southern wind as the martial breath
nodes.neumannArchetype: the directional consciousness of the south wind, the atmospheric extension of the solar war-god

nodes.name: Europa
nodes.domain: sovereignty, abduction, the continent
nodes.characterTrait: beautiful, innocent, chosen by the gods
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Phoenician princess of extraordinary beauty
nodes.significantEvent: abducted by Zeus in the form of a white bull who carried her across the sea to Crete, where she bore him Minos, Rhadamanthys, and Sarpedon
nodes.symbolism: the maiden seized by divine power in bull form, the transfer of civilization from East to West, the bull as symbol of the Great Goddess appropriated by the sky god
nodes.neumannArchetype: the maiden figure connected to bull symbolism of the Great Goddess, the feminine carried away by the masculine divine
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the Phoenician king Agenor and queen Telephassa

nodes.name: Hou Yi
nodes.domain: archery, the sun, heroism, drought, marital tragedy
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the greatest archer in Chinese mythology, strong and handsome
nodes.significantEvent: shot down nine of the ten suns that were scorching the earth, killed multiple monsters terrorizing the land, his wife Chang E stole and drank the elixir of immortality and flew to the moon, leaving him mortal and alone
nodes.symbolism: the hero who saves the world but loses everything personal, the archer who reduces the excessive suns to the proper single sun, the tragic separation of the heroic masculine from the feminine (Chang E on the moon)
nodes.neumannArchetype: the solar hero who limits the excessive masculine (nine extra suns) to restore balance, then loses the anima (Chang E) who ascends to the lunar realm, the eternal separation of sun and moon consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: sent by the heavenly emperor (or descended voluntarily) to save humanity from cosmic catastrophe

nodes.name: Oedipus
nodes.domain: fate, knowledge, kingship, blindness, prophecy
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: pierced and swollen feet from infancy, later blind and ragged as an exile
nodes.significantEvent: solved the riddle of the Sphinx saving Thebes, unknowingly killed his father and married his mother fulfilling the prophecy, blinded himself upon discovering the truth, died at Colonus
nodes.symbolism: the inescapability of fate, the tragic cost of self-knowledge, the riddle of human identity, blindness as the price of seeing the truth
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hero whose quest for truth leads to the destruction of the ego, the solver of the Sphinxs riddle who cannot solve the riddle of himself
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of King Laius and Queen Jocasta of Thebes, exposed on Mount Cithaeron as an infant due to a prophecy that he would kill his father

nodes.symbolism: the fusion of dance and warfare, martial training as a sacred art, the war dance as preparation for battle
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine ritual that transforms the body into a weapon through rhythmic movement

nodes.name: Huang Feihu
nodes.domain: war, loyalty, the supernatural, Mount Tai
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: mighty warrior riding a five-colored sacred ox
nodes.significantEvent: initially served King Zhou of Shang but rebelled against his tyranny and joined King Wu of Zhou, killed in battle and deified as the God of Mount Tai (Dongyue Dadi) who judges the dead
nodes.symbolism: the loyal warrior who transfers allegiance from the corrupt to the righteous, death in righteous battle leading to apotheosis as judge of the dead
nodes.neumannArchetype: the warrior transformed through righteous death into the judge of souls, the martial masculine elevated to the throne of underworld judgment
nodes.birthCircumstances: Shang Dynasty general and prince in the Fengshen Yanyi

nodes.name: Shangdi
nodes.domain: supreme deity, heaven, sovereignty, creation, sacrifice, agriculture
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the supreme deity of ancient Chinese religion, later identified with Tian (Heaven) and with the Jade Emperor
nodes.significantEvent: received sacrifices from the Shang kings who communicated with him through oracle bones, controlled the weather, granted victory in battle, and determined the fate of the harvest, later merged with the concept of Tian (Heaven)
nodes.symbolism: the original Chinese supreme deity, the lord above all who controls the cosmos, the ancestor of all later Chinese supreme deity concepts, the divine source of the Mandate of Heaven
nodes.neumannArchetype: the supreme Great Father archetype of Chinese civilization, the original patriarchal deity from whom all subsequent divine authority descends
nodes.birthCircumstances: the original supreme deity of Chinese religion predating both Daoism and Buddhism, worshipped since the Shang Dynasty

nodes.name: Wenchang Wang
nodes.domain: literature, examinations, scholarship, education, the stars
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: handsome scholarly deity in official robes, sitting among the stars
nodes.significantEvent: the supreme patron of scholarship and the civil service examinations, scholars pray to him before taking their exams, his temples were essential to the examination culture of imperial China
nodes.symbolism: the divine origin of scholarly achievement, the star that guides scholars to success, literature and examination as sacred endeavors, the celestial endorsement of learning
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive father archetype as the patron of cultural consciousness, the stellar father who endorses and rewards scholarly achievement
nodes.birthCircumstances: the star god of literature, associated with a constellation near the Big Dipper

nodes.name: Bastet
nodes.domain: protection, cats, joy, music, dance, fertility, home
nodes.characterTrait: protective, joyful, fierce when provoked, domestic, sensual, musical
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman with the head of a cat, or as a cat, holding a sistrum and aegis, graceful and elegant
nodes.significantEvent: her transformation from the fierce Sekhmet to the gentle Bastet represents the taming of divine wrath, her cult center at Bubastis held the most popular festival in Egypt with music, dance, and celebration, cats were sacred to her and killing one was punishable by death
nodes.symbolism: the tamed divine feminine, the domestic cat as the protector of the home, music and dance as expressions of divine joy, the transformation of rage into grace
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother in her gentle protective aspect, the fierce feminine transformed into the nurturing domestic guardian, the joy of the tamed instinct
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Ra, originally a fierce lioness goddess (Sekhmet) who was transformed into a gentle cat

nodes.name: Hermanubis
nodes.domain: the afterlife, Greco-Egyptian syncretism, mummification, guidance
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Greco-Egyptian hybrid deity combining features of Anubis and Hermes, depicted with Anubis jackal features and Hermes attributes
nodes.significantEvent: guided souls of the dead through the underworld in the Greco-Egyptian religious tradition, combining Anubis role as embalmer and guide with Hermes role as psychopomp (soul-guide)
nodes.symbolism: the meeting of Egyptian and Greek conceptions of the death guide, cultural syncretism as a creative force in religion, the guide of the dead who speaks both religious languages
nodes.neumannArchetype: the psychopomp who bridges two cultural unconsciousnesses, the guide of consciousness through death who speaks the language of both civilizations
nodes.birthCircumstances: syncretistic deity created during the Ptolemaic and Roman periods in Egypt

nodes.name: Libitina
nodes.domain: funerals, death, burial, the transition from life to death
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess of funerals and burial, associated with the cypress tree and the rites of the dead
nodes.significantEvent: her sacred grove on the Esquiline Hill was a place of burial and funeral rites, all funeral arrangements were made through her temple, a register of all deaths was kept in her precinct
nodes.symbolism: the cypress as the tree of death and mourning, the funeral as a sacred transition mediated by the feminine, the registration of death as a divine record, the grove of burial as the sacred feminine space of death
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of death, the feminine that receives consciousness back into the earth at the end of life

nodes.domain: war, destruction, sack of cities, bloodshed
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess of war covered in blood, companion and sister (or mother) of Ares
nodes.significantEvent: accompanies Ares on the battlefield, delights in bloodshed and the destruction of cities, depicted at the sack of Troy
nodes.symbolism: the feminine face of war as pure destruction, the goddess who embodies the chaos and horror of battle without strategy or glory
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Terrible Mother in her most destructive warrior aspect, the feminine that delights in annihilation
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Zeus and Hera, or daughter of Phorcys and Ceto

nodes.symbolism: the divine protection at liminal spaces, the crossroads as the place of choice and danger, the guardian of transitions
nodes.neumannArchetype: the liminal feminine who guards the thresholds between worlds, the goddess of roads as the paths of the soul
nodes.deathCircumstances: Timarete of Corinth, who died in Pella, Macedonia, in the late 5th century BC and Chrysame.

nodes.domain: civilization, kingship, heroism, democracy, labyrinth
nodes.characterTrait: brave, civilizing, sometimes faithless, democratic, strong
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: strong, handsome young hero of Athens

nodes.neumannArchetype: the hero who enters the labyrinth of the unconscious (the Great Mothers domain) and slays the monster at its center, emerging to found civilization
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Aegeus king of Athens or the god Poseidon, and Aethra princess of Troezen

nodes.name: Hygieia
nodes.domain: health, hygiene, cleanliness, prevention of disease
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: radiant young woman feeding a serpent from a patera
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped alongside her father Asclepius at his healing temples, her cult emphasized prevention of illness over cure, the Hippocratic oath invokes her name
nodes.symbolism: health as a positive state rather than merely absence of disease, prevention as wisdom, the serpent of renewal fed by conscious care
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive nurturing feminine in her aspect as preserver of health and wholeness
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Asclepius the god of medicine, granddaughter of Apollo

nodes.name: Erinyes
nodes.domain: vengeance, blood guilt, torment, the underworld
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: giant, winged, snake-haired, with bloodshot eyes, carrying torches and whips
nodes.significantEvent: pursue and torment those guilty of kin-murder and oath-breaking, hounded Orestes across Greece after he killed his mother
nodes.symbolism: the primordial law of blood vengeance, guilt as an inescapable cosmic force, the ancient chthonic order older than the Olympians
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible feminine as agents of the ancient maternal law, the chthonic forces of guilt and retribution
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from the blood of Uranus when Cronus castrated him, or daughters of Nyx

nodes.domain: seasons, natural order, justice, peace, good order
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful maidens dancing in a circle, sometimes winged, crowned with flowers
nodes.significantEvent: guard the gates of Olympus, opening and closing the cloud barrier for the gods, preside over the natural sequence of seasons
nodes.symbolism: the ordered cycle of seasons as divine law, the connection between natural order and moral order, time as regular rhythm
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine as the ordering principle of natural time, the daughters of law who maintain cosmic rhythm
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughters of Zeus and Themis

nodes.name: Muses
nodes.domain: arts, sciences, inspiration, memory, poetry, music, dance
nodes.object: lyre, scroll, stylus, mask, globe, compass
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: nine beautiful women, sometimes winged, each carrying her specific attribute
nodes.significantEvent: defeated the Pierides in a singing contest and transformed them into magpies, inspired Homer and Hesiod, dwell on Mount Helicon and Pieria
nodes.symbolism: divine inspiration as the source of all art and knowledge, the nine domains of human creativity, memory as the mother of culture
nodes.neumannArchetype: the ninefold differentiation of the Great Mothers creative aspect, the feminine as the wellspring of all cultural consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: nine daughters of Zeus and the Titaness Mnemosyne, conceived over nine consecutive nights
nodes.deathCircumstances: They were considered the source of the knowledge embodied in the poetry, lyric songs, and myths that were related orally for centuries in ancient Greek culture.

nodes.name: Perseus
nodes.domain: heroism, monster-slaying, divine favor, kingship
nodes.object: harpe sword, mirrored shield, winged sandals, cap of invisibility, kibisis bag
nodes.characterTrait: brave, pious, resourceful, favored by the gods
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: handsome young hero with winged sandals, carrying Medusas head
nodes.significantEvent: beheaded the Gorgon Medusa using a mirrored shield to avoid her petrifying gaze, rescued Andromeda from a sea monster, turned Atlas and Polydectes to stone with Medusas head
nodes.symbolism: the hero who conquers terror through reflection rather than direct confrontation, divine favor enabling the impossible quest, the mirror as consciousness facing the unconscious
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hero who defeats the Terrible Mother (Medusa) by using the mirror of consciousness, the archetypal dragon-slayer
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Zeus and Danae, conceived when Zeus visited Danae as a shower of gold in her bronze prison
nodes.deathCircumstances: Disappointed by not having a male heir, Acrisius consulted the Oracle at Delphi, who warned him that he would one day be killed by his own grandson.

nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine threshold of evening, consciousness transitioning toward the night of the unconscious

nodes.name: Serapis
nodes.domain: death, rebirth, the underworld, fertility, healing
nodes.object: staff with serpent, grain measure, scepter
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: composite deity combining Osiris and Apis, depicted with a Greek figure bearing an Egyptian crown with a grain basket (modius) on his head
nodes.significantEvent: Ptolemy I established his cult to unite Greek and Egyptian worship in Alexandria, his cult spread throughout the Roman Empire, his temple the Serapeum at Alexandria was a wonder of the ancient world
nodes.symbolism: the syncretic union of Greek and Egyptian religion, divine kingship over death and rebirth, healing and fertility united in one universal god
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father combining the Egyptian dying-and-rising god with the Greek lord of the underworld, the syncretic resolution of two great religious traditions
nodes.birthCircumstances: syncretic god created in Ptolemaic Egypt combining Egyptian Osiris-Apis with Greek Hades and Asclepius

nodes.name: Huang Shigong
nodes.domain: strategy, wisdom, Daoism, hermit sages
nodes.object: scroll, Three Strategies of Huang Shigong
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: elderly hermit sage who tests the worthy with humbling tasks
nodes.significantEvent: tested the young Zhang Liang by dropping his shoe off a bridge three times and making him retrieve it, then rewarded him with the Three Strategies military classic that helped Zhang Liang advise Liu Bang to found the Han Dynasty
nodes.symbolism: the sage who tests humility before bestowing wisdom, the shoe test as the gateway to strategic knowledge, the hermit whose gift changes the course of history
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wise old man who tests the hero through humiliation before granting the transformative knowledge

nodes.name: Shao Siming
nodes.domain: childbirth, destiny of children, protection of the young
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: youthful deity associated with the protection and destiny of children
nodes.significantEvent: determines the destiny and wellbeing of children, worshipped by parents seeking protection for their young
nodes.symbolism: the divine protection of childhood, the weaving of childrens destinies, the sacred guardianship of the most vulnerable
nodes.neumannArchetype: the protective animus of childhood, the divine guardian of the young consciousness before it reaches maturity

nodes.name: Wenshu Guangfa Tianzun
nodes.domain: wisdom, Buddhism, Daoism, the Investiture of the Gods
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Daoist immortal who is the Daoist form of Manjusri Bodhisattva
nodes.significantEvent: in the Fengshen Yanyi he is a powerful Daoist master who later becomes the Buddhist Bodhisattva Manjusri (Wenshu), representing the transition from Daoism to Buddhism in Chinese religious history
nodes.symbolism: the wisdom that transcends sectarian boundaries, the Daoist sage who becomes the Buddhist Bodhisattva of wisdom, the sword of wisdom that cuts through illusion
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine wisdom principle that transforms from one spiritual tradition (Daoism) to another (Buddhism), consciousness evolving through different forms
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the Twelve Golden Immortals of Kunlun Mountain

nodes.name: Sekhmet
nodes.domain: war, plague, healing, fire, the sun, destruction
nodes.object: solar disk and uraeus on her head; ankh; the arrows of plague (the 'Seven Arrows of Sekhmet')
nodes.characterTrait: fierce, destructive, healing, solar, wrathful, powerful
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Lioness-headed woman wearing the solar disk and uraeus; muscular and fierce; clad in red garments (the color of blood and the desert).
nodes.significantEvent: The fierce-warrior form of the Eye of Ra. In the Destruction of Mankind narrative, sent by Ra to slaughter rebellious humanity — she became so bloodthirsty that even Ra feared total annihilation; he poured 7,000 jugs of beer dyed red (with red ochre or pomegranate) into the field, and she drank it thinking it was blood, became drunk, and was thereby pacified — transforming back to her Hathoric form. Her priests were the physicians of pharaonic Egypt — paradoxically, since she is the plague-sender, she is also the plague-healer. In Memphis, consort of Ptah and mother of Nefertem.
nodes.symbolism: the destructive sun unleashed, divine wrath that must be tricked into stopping, the lioness as the most terrifying form of the divine feminine, healing and destruction from the same source
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Terrible Mother as the destroying solar feminine, the Great Mothers wrathful aspect that threatens to consume all creation, the rage of the feminine that can only be stopped through intoxication
nodes.birthCircumstances: Emanation from Ra's eye (the Eye of Ra in wrathful aspect); also paired primordially with Ptah in the Memphite cosmogony.
nodes.domain_source: Pyramid Texts; the Destruction of Mankind narrative; the Memphite tradition; medical papyri (Edwin Smith, Ebers — where Sekhmet's priests are physicians); the Litany of Sekhmet (with 4,000+ statues commissioned by Amenhotep III)
nodes.object_source: Standard Sekhmet iconography; medical papyri
nodes.characterTrait_source: Destruction of Mankind; medical papyri; Pyramid Texts
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard iconography; Amenhotep III's Sekhmet-statues at Karnak
nodes.significantEvent_source: Destruction of Mankind (tomb of Seti I); Memphite tradition; medical-papyri Sekhmet-prayers
nodes.birthTypes_source: Destruction of Mankind
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Destruction of Mankind; Memphite Theology

nodes.name: Hermes Trismegistus
nodes.domain: magic, alchemy, wisdom, astrology, Greco-Egyptian syncretism
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Greco-Egyptian syncretic deity combining Thoth and Hermes, the legendary author of the Hermetic writings
nodes.significantEvent: legendary author of the Hermetic Corpus and the Emerald Tablet, the foundation texts of Western alchemy, astrology, and occultism, his teachings influenced Renaissance philosophy, Rosicrucianism, and Freemasonry
nodes.symbolism: the three-fold greatness of priest-philosopher-king, the emerald tablet as the key to all alchemical wisdom, the as above so below principle, the synthesis of Egyptian and Greek wisdom
nodes.neumannArchetype: the supreme culture hero of syncretic wisdom, the thrice-great masculine consciousness that integrates priestly, philosophical, and royal knowledge into a single transformative tradition
nodes.birthCircumstances: syncretistic deity created from the merger of Egyptian Thoth and Greek Hermes, the Thrice-Great (Trismegistus)

nodes.name: Hesperus
nodes.domain: the evening star, Venus at dusk, twilight
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: handsome youth carrying a torch, the evening star personified
nodes.significantEvent: identified with the planet Venus as it appears at dusk, in later tradition reunited with his brother Eosphorus when they were recognized as the same planet
nodes.symbolism: the star that heralds the night, beauty at the threshold of darkness, the luminous guide into evening
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine light-bearer who guides consciousness toward the night, the twilight animus
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Eos (Dawn) and Cephalus, or of Atlas, brother of Eosphorus (the morning star)

nodes.name: Seven against Thebes
nodes.domain: war, siege, fratricidal conflict, prophecy, Thebes
nodes.object: thunderbolt, spear, chariot, shield, torch, sword
nodes.animals: serpent, snake, horse, lion, boar, dragon, sphinx
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: seven warrior-kings united against the city of Thebes
nodes.significantEvent: seven champions marched against Thebes to restore Polynices to the throne against his brother Eteocles, all but one (Adrastus) were killed, the brothers killed each other in single combat
nodes.symbolism: the fratricidal war that destroys both sides, the doom of hereditary curse (the House of Oedipus), seven heroes against seven gates as a cosmic number of completeness
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine collective doomed by the curse of the patriarch (Oedipus), the patriarchal order destroying itself through its own contradictions
nodes.deathCircumstances: They tried and failed to take Thebes, and all but Adrastus died in the attempt.

nodes.name: Hundun
nodes.domain: primordial chaos, the undifferentiated, creation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a shapeless sack-like being without eyes, ears, nose, or mouth, the embodiment of primordial chaos
nodes.significantEvent: in the Zhuangzi his two friends Shu and Hu drilled seven holes in him (for eyes, ears, nostrils, mouth) to give him the senses of an ordinary being, and on the seventh day Hundun died, metaphor for how differentiation kills primordial unity
nodes.symbolism: the undifferentiated chaos before creation, the death of primordial unity through the imposition of order and distinction, the loss of innocence through consciousness
nodes.neumannArchetype: the uroboric state of primordial unity before consciousness differentiates it, the chaos-egg that dies when the seven openings of perception are created
nodes.birthCircumstances: the primordial state of chaos before creation in Chinese cosmology

nodes.name: Shen Gongbao
nodes.domain: betrayal, sorcery, rivalry, the Investiture of the Gods
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: dark-complexioned Daoist immortal riding a black unicorn-like creature
nodes.significantEvent: served the Shang Dynasty against the righteous Zhou in the Investiture of the Gods, repeatedly sent monsters and sorcerers to oppose Jiang Ziya, the archetypal betrayer and troublemaker of the narrative
nodes.symbolism: the dark disciple who uses spiritual power for selfish ends, jealousy that corrupts spiritual cultivation, the enemy within the tradition
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow brother of the culture hero, the dark twin who opposes the mission of consciousness with the same tools of spiritual power
nodes.birthCircumstances: fellow disciple of Jiang Ziya (Taigong Wang) under the master Yuanshi Tianzun, expelled from the sect for his wickedness

nodes.name: White Emperor
nodes.domain: the west, metal, autumn, warfare, punishment
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the White Emperor, ruler of the western sky and the autumn season
nodes.significantEvent: presides over autumn and the western direction, associated with the metal element, warfare, and the harvesting season when nature dies back, the punishing season that follows the abundance of summer
nodes.symbolism: the west as the direction of death and punishment, metal as the element of cutting and warfare, autumn as the dying season, the stern face of the cosmic order
nodes.neumannArchetype: the western father of death and punishment, the autumn consciousness where the yang principle begins its descent
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the Wufang Shangdi (Five Forms of the Highest Deity), rules the west and autumn
nodes.deathCircumstances: In the legend, a gigantic white serpent killed some of the outlaws with its poisonous breath; the serpent was killed by a drunk Liu during the night.

nodes.name: Khnum
nodes.domain: creation, the Nile, pottery, the flood, birth
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: ram-headed man seated at a potters wheel, fashioning human beings from clay
nodes.significantEvent: fashioned all human beings and their ka (spirits) on his potters wheel from Nile clay, controlled the annual inundation of the Nile from his cavern beneath the First Cataract at Elephantine, created the gods as well
nodes.symbolism: the divine potter who shapes all beings from earth and water, the ram as creative virility, the Nile source as the origin of all Egyptian life, the potters wheel as the mechanism of continuous creation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father as the divine shaper who forms consciousness from the raw material of the earth (Great Mother), the masculine principle that gives form to the formless
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient ram-headed god of the First Cataract and the source of the Nile

nodes.name: Arsinoe II Philadelphos
nodes.domain: queenship, divine femininity, Ptolemaic cult, the sea
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: deified Ptolemaic queen, wife of Ptolemy II Philadelphos
nodes.significantEvent: deified after death and worshipped as a goddess alongside Isis and Aphrodite, the first of the Ptolemaic queens to be fully deified, her cult established the pattern for later Ptolemaic queen worship
nodes.symbolism: the mortal queen who becomes a goddess, the Greek-Egyptian synthesis in royal divine cult, the feminine power of the Ptolemaic dynasty made divine
nodes.neumannArchetype: the human feminine elevated to the status of the Great Mother through the power of the Ptolemaic state
nodes.birthCircumstances: historical queen (c. 316-270 BCE), deified after death as a divine consort
nodes.deathCircumstances: ===Queen of Ptolemy Keraunos=== In 281 BC, Lysimachus died in battle and Arsinoë fled to Cassandreia ().

nodes.name: Homonoia
nodes.domain: concord, unanimity, unity
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: personification of concord and unanimity, depicted holding a cornucopia
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped as the spirit of civic unity, had altars in several Greek cities, invoked in political assemblies to ensure unanimity
nodes.symbolism: the divine gift of social harmony, the unity that makes the polis function, concord as a sacred civic virtue
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive feminine principle of social unity, the binding force that holds the community together
nodes.birthCircumstances: Homonoia was believed to be the daughter of Soter, the saviour daimon, and Praxidike, the goddess of judicial punishment and vengeance.

nodes.name: Sirius
nodes.domain: the dog star, drought, fever, summer heat
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the brightest star in the sky, depicted as a brilliant fiery figure
nodes.significantEvent: his rising with the sun in midsummer brings the dog days of heat, drought, and fever, the Athenians sacrificed to him to avert the worst of the summer heat
nodes.symbolism: the scorching celestial fire that brings summer fever, the boundary between the beneficent and destructive aspects of stellar light
nodes.neumannArchetype: the burning masculine of the sky at its most intense, the solar principle pushed to destructive excess
nodes.birthCircumstances: sometimes described as the hound of Orion placed among the stars

nodes.name: Hung Shing
nodes.domain: the sea, weather, fishing, southern China
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: deified Song Dynasty official who protects fishermen and sailors
nodes.significantEvent: deified as a protector of fishing and seafaring communities along the southern Chinese coast, temples dedicated to him throughout Guangdong and Hong Kong
nodes.symbolism: the righteous official who becomes the divine protector of the sea, the bureaucratic virtue extended to the maritime realm
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive father as the protector of those who venture onto the oceanic unconscious
nodes.birthCircumstances: Hong Sheng, a Song Dynasty official associated with southern Chinese sea communities

nodes.name: Shenlong
nodes.domain: rain, dragons, imperial authority, spiritual power
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: great spiritual dragon, often blue or silver, sinuous and elongated, can be enormous or invisible
nodes.significantEvent: the imperial dragon who brings rain to nourish the earth, his appearances signal divine favor, mishandling or offending him causes drought or flood
nodes.symbolism: the dragon as the mediator between heaven and earth through rain, the imperial symbol of Chinese sovereignty, the benevolent serpent power of the waters
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive dragon of consciousness that mediates between the sky father (heaven) and the earth mother, bringing the fertilizing rain of awareness
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the four types of dragon in Chinese mythology, the spiritual dragon that controls rain and wind

nodes.name: Wisdom King
nodes.domain: Buddhism, protection, wrath, demon-subduing
nodes.characterTrait: wrathful, protective, demon-subduing, compassionate beneath wrath
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: fierce multi-armed Buddhist deity with flaming halo, surrounded by fire
nodes.significantEvent: wrathful manifestation of Buddhist compassion that subdues demons and protects the dharma through terrifying appearance and overwhelming power
nodes.symbolism: compassion expressed through wrathful force, the Buddhist paradox of fierce love, the flame of wisdom that burns away ignorance
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wrathful masculine protector whose terrifying appearance serves the highest compassion, force in service of consciousness

nodes.name: Khepri
nodes.domain: the rising sun, dawn, transformation, rebirth, creation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: man with a scarab beetle in place of his head, or as a scarab beetle pushing the sun disk
nodes.significantEvent: pushes the sun across the sky each morning just as the scarab beetle rolls its ball of dung, represents the daily rebirth of the sun and the continuous renewal of creation
nodes.symbolism: the scarab beetle rolling the sun as the image of cosmic renewal, transformation through the cycle of day, the morning sun as daily rebirth, creation through self-transformation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the self-renewing masculine consciousness that pushes the sun of awareness into being each dawn, the ego reborn each morning from the darkness of the unconscious
nodes.birthCircumstances: aspect of the sun god Ra representing the morning sun as it rises

nodes.name: Wadj-wer
nodes.domain: the sea, the ocean, greatness, the Mediterranean
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: man with a large belly representing the sea, green-skinned or blue-skinned, personification of the Mediterranean Sea or the Great Green
nodes.significantEvent: represented the vast Mediterranean Sea and the oceanic forces, contrasted with Hapi who represented the Nile, the sea was both feared and revered as the boundary of the known Egyptian world
nodes.symbolism: the Great Green as the oceanic boundary of the Egyptian world, the sea as the vast other to the Nile, the pregnant belly of the waters
nodes.neumannArchetype: the oceanic masculine, the great paternal waters that surround and bound the world of consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: personification of the sea (the Great Green) in Egyptian cosmology

nodes.name: Iusaaset
nodes.domain: creation, the hand of Atum, sexuality, Heliopolis
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess representing the hand of Atum with which he created the first gods, or depicted as a woman with a scarab beetle on her head
nodes.significantEvent: represented the feminine creative principle within the self-creation of Atum, the hand that enabled the creator to generate Shu and Tefnut, the grandmother of all subsequent deities
nodes.symbolism: the hand as the instrument of solitary creation, the feminine within the masculine creator, the paradox of the self-created who requires a feminine aspect to create
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hidden feminine within the primordial masculine creator, the anima of the self-creating Great Father
nodes.birthCircumstances: personification of the hand of Atum used in the act of creation, considered one of the most ancient goddesses

nodes.name: Nemesis
nodes.domain: retribution, divine justice, balance, vengeance against hubris
nodes.object: scales, wheel, sword, measuring rod, bridle
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: winged goddess, stern and beautiful, sometimes veiled, carrying a wheel or scales
nodes.significantEvent: pursued by Zeus in many forms until she became a goose and laid the egg from which Helen of Troy was born, worshipped at Rhamnus with an important cult statue
nodes.symbolism: the cosmic force that restores balance, divine punishment of human arrogance, the inescapability of justice, the wheel of fortune
nodes.neumannArchetype: the retributive aspect of the Great Goddess who maintains cosmic balance, ensuring that excessive pride is punished
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Nyx in most traditions, or of Oceanus, or of Zeus and Necessity

nodes.name: Caryatis
nodes.domain: walnut trees, Laconian cult
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: nymph associated with the walnut tree
nodes.significantEvent: Artemis Caryatis was worshipped at Caryae in Laconia where maidens danced in her honor, the Caryatids (pillar-maidens) are named after these dancers
nodes.symbolism: the maiden who becomes a pillar, the dance of worship transformed into architecture, the walnut tree as sacred feminine
nodes.neumannArchetype: the dancing maiden who becomes the architectural support, the feminine as the pillar of the temple

nodes.name: Sophrosyne
nodes.domain: temperance, moderation, self-control, prudence
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: personification of moderation and self-restraint
nodes.significantEvent: one of the cardinal virtues of Greek philosophy, central to the ethics of Plato and Aristotle, the quality that allows humans to resist excess
nodes.symbolism: the golden mean between excess and deficiency, the self-knowledge that knows ones proper limits, the virtue that preserves the soul from the inflation of hybris
nodes.neumannArchetype: the conscious feminine restraint that prevents the ego from overreaching, the virtue of knowing the limits of consciousness

nodes.name: Jade Emperor
nodes.domain: heaven, cosmic governance, supreme authority, virtue, justice
nodes.object: imperial regalia, jade tablet, twelve-tiered crown
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: seated on an imperial throne wearing the twelve-tiered crown of pearls and imperial robes, long beard, dignified and serene
nodes.significantEvent: rules the celestial bureaucracy of heaven mirroring the Chinese imperial court, governs all gods, humans, and spirits, his birthday is celebrated on the ninth day of the first lunar month, central figure in Journey to the West commissioning the pilgrimage
nodes.symbolism: the supreme heavenly authority modeled on the Chinese imperial system, cosmic governance as divine bureaucracy, patience and cultivation over eons as the path to supreme power, the emperor above all emperors
nodes.neumannArchetype: the supreme patriarchal archetype, the Great Father as the cosmic emperor who governs all through bureaucratic order and heavenly mandate
nodes.birthCircumstances: in legend he was originally a prince who renounced his throne to cultivate the Dao for millions of kalpas before attaining supreme authority over heaven

nodes.name: Shennong
nodes.domain: agriculture, medicine, herbal knowledge, the market, civilization
nodes.object: whip of a hundred herbs, plow, herbs
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Divine Farmer depicted with an ox head and human body, or with a transparent abdomen through which one could see the effects of herbs
nodes.significantEvent: tasted hundreds of plants to discover their medicinal and poisonous properties, using his transparent stomach to observe their effects, invented the plow and taught humanity agriculture, established the first markets, died from tasting a poisonous herb
nodes.symbolism: the divine experimenter who risks his own body to discover medicines for humanity, agriculture as the second great gift of civilization (after Fuxis trigrams), the transparent body as the perfect instrument of knowledge
nodes.neumannArchetype: the sacrificial culture hero who takes the Great Mothers substances (herbs) into his own body to transform them into healing knowledge for humanity, the masculine that processes the feminine (nature) through self-experimentation
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the Three Sovereigns (San Huang), successor to Fuxi

nodes.name: Wufang Guidi
nodes.domain: the underworld, the five directions, judgment of the dead
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: five emperors of the dead who rule the five directions of the underworld
nodes.significantEvent: govern the five regions of the Chinese underworld, each presiding over specific courts and punishments for the dead
nodes.symbolism: the five-directional structure of the underworld mirroring the five-element cosmic order, death organized according to the same principles as life
nodes.neumannArchetype: the fivefold patriarch of the underworld, the patriarchal ordering of death according to the cosmic five-element system

nodes.name: Min
nodes.domain: fertility, sexuality, virility, the harvest, the desert, generation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: ithyphallic man (with erect phallus) wearing a double-plumed crown, one arm raised holding a flail, skin painted black
nodes.significantEvent: the supreme god of male sexual power and generation, worshipped at Coptos and Akhmim, his festivals involved ritual sexuality and the presentation of lettuce (believed to be an aphrodisiac due to its milky sap), protector of the desert routes to the Eastern Desert mines
nodes.symbolism: male sexual power as a cosmic creative force, the raised flail as the generative gesture, the lettuce as the aphrodisiac plant sacred to virility, the black skin as the fertile earth
nodes.neumannArchetype: the phallic Great Father in his most direct expression, the masculine generative principle displayed without mediation
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the most ancient Egyptian gods, predating the dynastic period

nodes.name: Yam
nodes.domain: the sea, chaos, storms, the Near East, primordial waters
nodes.characterTrait: chaotic, stormy, primordial, Near Eastern, watery
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Semitic sea god or sea monster adopted into the Egyptian pantheon
nodes.significantEvent: fought against the gods and was defeated, associated with the chaotic forces of the sea, connected to the Semitic sea-chaos traditions (Yam in Ugaritic mythology)
nodes.symbolism: the chaotic sea as the enemy of cosmic order, the Near Eastern sea monster integrated into Egyptian cosmology, the storm-tossed waters as the adversary of the sun
nodes.neumannArchetype: the chaos dragon of the sea, the primordial aquatic unconscious that threatens the solar order of consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: Near Eastern sea deity adopted into Egyptian mythology during the New Kingdom

nodes.domain: music, singing, rejoicing, the harvest, festivals

nodes.symbolism: music as a cosmic force that maintains harmony, the singing feminine as the voice of divine joy, the harvest celebration as a sacred musical event
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the voice of cosmic joy, the feminine whose singing maintains the harmony of creation

nodes.symbolism: the heroic embodiment of physical power
nodes.neumannArchetype: the purely physical hero expressing undifferentiated masculine strength

nodes.name: Sosipolis
nodes.domain: protection of children, the city, serpent cults, Elis
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: divine child who appeared as a serpent
nodes.significantEvent: during a battle between the Eleans and Arcadians his mother placed her infant before the Elean army, the child transformed into a serpent and routed the Arcadians, worshipped at Elis with a serpent cult
nodes.symbolism: the divine child whose transformation saves the city, the serpent as the protective chthonic power, the infant as weapon of divine defense
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child who manifests the chthonic serpent power of the Great Mother to protect the community
nodes.birthCircumstances: His mother was the childbirth-goddess Eileithyia, daughter of Zeus and Hera.

nodes.name: Jinqianbo
nodes.domain: wealth, money, luck, gambling
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: wealth deity associated with the flow of money
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped by merchants and gamblers seeking financial luck, associated with the circulation of wealth rather than its hoarding
nodes.symbolism: money as a flowing divine gift rather than a static possession, luck in financial matters as a divine dispensation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the trickster aspect of the wealth god, fortune as a flowing and unpredictable gift

nodes.name: Shenshu and Yulü
nodes.domain: protection, exorcism, door guardianship, New Year
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: two fierce warrior figures made of peach wood, placed on doors to ward off evil spirits
nodes.significantEvent: guarded the Ghost Gate on Dushuo Mountain through which demons passed, caught evil spirits and fed them to tigers, their images placed on doors became the first door god tradition in China
nodes.symbolism: the peach wood as the most potent apotropaic material, the door as the threshold between the safe domestic space and the dangerous outside, the guardian pair who feeds evil to the tiger
nodes.neumannArchetype: the archetypal threshold guardians, the paired masculine forces that protect the domestic (conscious) space from the intrusion of the demonic (unconscious)
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient door gods predating Qin Qiong and Yuchi Gong, the oldest Chinese door guardians

nodes.name: Wutong Shen
nodes.domain: wealth, sensuality, plague, the supernatural, ambiguity
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: five powerful spirits who can grant wealth but also bring plague and disaster
nodes.significantEvent: five spirits worshipped throughout southern China who can either bestow wealth or inflict plague, their cult was both feared and sought, reflecting the ambiguity of supernatural power
nodes.symbolism: the ambiguity of supernatural power that can bless or curse, wealth and plague from the same divine source, the five as a cosmic number of totality
nodes.neumannArchetype: the ambiguous numinous that grants and destroys, the shadow powers whose blessing and curse are inseparable

nodes.name: Bes
nodes.domain: protection, childbirth, music, dance, merriment, the household
nodes.characterTrait: grotesque, protective, joyful, fierce, domestic, apotropaic
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: dwarf god with a lion mane, bow legs, and a protruding tongue, often shown dancing or playing instruments, grotesque appearance meant to frighten away evil
nodes.significantEvent: protected mothers during childbirth, guarded the household against evil spirits, his image was placed on beds, mirrors, and cosmetic vessels, one of the few Egyptian gods depicted full-face rather than in profile
nodes.symbolism: the grotesque as the protective form, the dwarf who frightens away evil through ugliness, merriment and dance as apotropaic acts, the protector of the most vulnerable moments (birth and sleep)
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow figure whose grotesque appearance protects against the dark unconscious forces, the trickster-guardian of the domestic threshold
nodes.birthCircumstances: origins uncertain, possibly of African or Near Eastern origin

nodes.name: Resheph
nodes.domain: war, plague, thunder, the Near East
nodes.animals: gazelle, horse, serpent, bull, lion, stag, vulture, ram, goat, sphinx
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Semitic war god with a tall conical crown, wielding a mace and shield, adopted into the Egyptian pantheon
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped by Egyptian warriors and pharaohs as a god of military prowess, associated with devastating plague and the terrifying power of the storm, Ramesses II was compared to Resheph in battle
nodes.symbolism: the foreign war god adopted for his terrifying power, plague and war as instruments of the same divine force, the thunderbolt as the weapon of divine wrath
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible foreign Great Father of war and plague, the destructive masculine power imported from the Near East
nodes.birthCircumstances: Semitic war and plague god adopted into Egypt during the New Kingdom

nodes.symbolism: the lioness of Upper Egypt, the fierce feline feminine of the southern kingdom
nodes.neumannArchetype: the fierce feminine hunter of Upper Egypt, the lioness Great Mother of the south

nodes.name: Genius loci
nodes.domain: local protection, place spirits, guardianship of specific locations
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: depicted as a serpent or a young man with a cornucopia at specific locations
nodes.significantEvent: the divine spirit of a specific place, every location had its own Genius loci that protected and defined that place, Roman generals sacrificed to the Genius loci before battle
nodes.symbolism: every place as having its own divine spirit, the genius of place as the unique character of a location, the serpent at the boundary as the guardian of sacred space
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine consciousness of place, the individuated spirit that defines the unique character of each location

nodes.name: Ariadne
nodes.domain: labyrinths, thread, wine, divine marriage
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful Cretan princess, later divine consort crowned with stars
nodes.significantEvent: gave Theseus a ball of thread to navigate the Labyrinth and slay the Minotaur, abandoned by Theseus on Naxos, rescued and married by Dionysus who placed her crown among the stars as Corona Borealis
nodes.symbolism: the feminine wisdom that provides the thread of consciousness through the labyrinth, abandonment transformed into divine union, the mortal bride of the god
nodes.neumannArchetype: the anima figure who enables the heros journey through the labyrinth, later elevated to divine status through union with Dionysus
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of King Minos of Crete and Pasiphae, granddaughter of Helios

nodes.domain: epic poetry, bardic tradition, memory, the Muses
nodes.characterTrait: blind, inspired, all-seeing through inner vision, master poet

nodes.significantEvent: composed the Iliad and Odyssey, the foundational texts of Western literature, said to have competed with Hesiod in a poetry contest
nodes.symbolism: blindness as inner sight, the poet as the vessel of divine memory, the oral tradition as the foundation of civilization, the Muses speaking through a mortal voice
nodes.neumannArchetype: the blind seer-poet who channels the Great Mothers memory (Mnemosyne) through masculine creative voice, the archetypal vessel of cultural consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: traditionally born in Ionia, son of various fathers in different traditions, divinely inspired by the Muses

nodes.name: Soter
nodes.domain: salvation, safety, deliverance, preservation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: savior deity, an epithet of Zeus and other gods in their protective aspect
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped as Zeus Soter (Zeus the Savior) and Athena Soteira throughout Greece, libations poured to Zeus Soter at the third cup of the symposium
nodes.symbolism: divine salvation and protection, the gods in their capacity as saviors and preservers of mortals, the third libation as the perfect number of salvation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive masculine as the protective and saving principle, the sky father in his benevolent guardian aspect

nodes.name: Jintong
nodes.domain: service, heavenly attendance, purity, celestial court
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: golden boy attendant in celestial court robes, paired with Yunü (Jade Maiden)
nodes.significantEvent: together with Yunü (Jade Maiden) he attends the great deities as servant, sometimes sent to earth on missions and punished for falling in love with Yunü, a common theme in Chinese folklore
nodes.symbolism: the divine servant of heaven, the golden purity of celestial youth, the forbidden love between paired celestial attendants as a metaphor for the longing of the divine for the earthly
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child as celestial attendant, the youthful masculine paired with the feminine (Yunü) in service to the Great Father
nodes.birthCircumstances: celestial attendant in the court of the Jade Emperor or Guanyin

nodes.name: Shi Gandang
nodes.domain: protection, stone talismans, evil suppression, mountains
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a protective stone or stone tablet inscribed with the characters Mount Tai dares to resist, placed at T-intersections and corners of buildings
nodes.significantEvent: stone tablets inscribed Shi Gandang (literally Stone dares to resist) are placed at road intersections, building corners, and other vulnerable spots to ward off evil spirits, a practice dating back over a thousand years
nodes.symbolism: the immovable protective power of sacred stone, the mountain as the ultimate defense against evil, the written word on stone as a talisman of cosmic protection
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine as the immovable stone of consciousness, the mountain father whose written name alone wards off the shadow
nodes.birthCircumstances: associated with the power of Mount Tai (Taishan), the most sacred mountain

nodes.name: Xianhe Tongzi
nodes.domain: service, immortality, cranes, celestial attendance
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: celestial boy attendant who rides a crane
nodes.significantEvent: attendant spirit associated with immortals and celestial beings, often depicted riding a crane as a symbol of approaching immortality
nodes.symbolism: the crane as the vehicle of immortality, the youthful attendant who accompanies the sage to heaven, purity of service
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child as the attendant of the wise old man, the youthful consciousness that accompanies wisdom

nodes.name: Imhotep
nodes.domain: medicine, architecture, wisdom, deification, healing
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: seated man holding an open papyrus scroll on his lap, wearing a skullcap
nodes.significantEvent: designed the Step Pyramid at Saqqara (the first monumental stone building in history), was deified approximately 2,000 years after his death and became the Egyptian god of medicine identified with Asclepius by the Greeks, one of very few commoners elevated to divine status
nodes.symbolism: the human who achieves divinity through wisdom, the architect as the most divine of human professions, medicine and architecture as twin expressions of ordering knowledge, the mortal who becomes a god
nodes.neumannArchetype: the human hero elevated to the status of the Great Father through the supreme achievements of consciousness (architecture and healing)
nodes.birthCircumstances: historical person (c. 2650 BCE), chancellor of Pharaoh Djoser, later deified as a god of medicine and wisdom

nodes.name: Hauron
nodes.domain: protection, the Near East, gardens, fertility
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Near Eastern deity depicted as a warrior or falcon-headed figure, adopted into the Egyptian pantheon
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped as a protector of gardens and children, associated with the Levantine agricultural traditions, venerated by workers and common people
nodes.symbolism: the foreign protector of gardens and youth, the Near Eastern masculine guardian adopted into domestic Egyptian worship
nodes.neumannArchetype: the protective foreign masculine who guards the garden (the cultivated feminine space)
nodes.birthCircumstances: Semitic deity from the Levant adopted into Egypt during the New Kingdom
