nodes.name: Renpet
nodes.domain: the year, time, renewal, eternity, vegetation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess wearing a notched palm rib on her head, personification of the year and its cycle
nodes.significantEvent: personified the concept of the year (renpet) and the annual renewal of time, her appearance marked the beginning of each new year and its promise of renewal
nodes.symbolism: the year as a living cycle, time as a feminine principle of renewal, the notched palm rib as the count of years, the new year as rebirth
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of time and renewal, the feminine that cycles through death and rebirth each year

nodes.name: Deus
nodes.domain: the supreme divine principle, the god, divine unity
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the concept of the supreme god or divine principle in Roman philosophical theology
nodes.significantEvent: the philosophical concept of a supreme divine principle underlying all Roman religion, discussed by Varro, Cicero, and other Roman philosophers, anticipating later monotheistic trends
nodes.symbolism: the divine unity behind the multiplicity of gods, the philosophical god as the supreme consciousness behind all divine manifestations
nodes.neumannArchetype: the supreme patriarchal principle, the Great Father abstracted into the philosophical concept of the divine unity

nodes.name: Leto
nodes.domain: motherhood, childhood, protection of the young
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful Titaness, modest and veiled, devoted mother
nodes.significantEvent: wandered the earth pregnant with Apollo and Artemis while persecuted by Hera, no land would receive her until the floating island of Delos agreed, punished Niobe for boasting by having her children killed
nodes.symbolism: the persecuted mother who endures suffering to bring forth the divine, the wandering that precedes the birth of light (Apollo), maternal devotion against cosmic hostility
nodes.neumannArchetype: the maternal figure who must endure the Terrible Mothers persecution (Hera) to birth the solar hero (Apollo)
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the Titans Coeus and Phoebe, sister of Asteria

nodes.name: Horkos
nodes.domain: oaths, perjury, punishment of oath-breakers
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: spirit of the oath who punishes those who break their sworn word
nodes.significantEvent: pursues and punishes all who break oaths, the most feared of the children of Strife because his punishment is inescapable
nodes.symbolism: the sacred binding power of the oath, the terrible consequences of breaking ones word, the divine enforcement of verbal contracts
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow of consciousness that binds through language, the word made punishing law
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Eris (Strife) according to Hesiod

nodes.domain: salvation, safety, deliverance
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: personification of safety and deliverance from danger
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped after successful escapes from danger or victory in battle, festivals of Soteria held at Delphi after the Gauls were repelled
nodes.symbolism: the divine gift of salvation from danger, deliverance as a cosmic grace, the gratitude owed for rescue from peril
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive feminine of preservation and rescue, safety as a gift of the divine

nodes.name: Jinzha
nodes.domain: war, Buddhism, transformation, obedience
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: eldest son of Li Jing (Pagoda-Bearing Heavenly King), warrior wielding paired dragon staffs
nodes.significantEvent: fought alongside his father in the Investiture of the Gods narrative, initially served the Shang Dynasty but converted to the Zhou cause, became a Buddhist guardian deity
nodes.symbolism: the obedient eldest son who follows duty, the eldest brothers role as the stabilizing force in the family, the transition from Daoist warrior to Buddhist guardian
nodes.neumannArchetype: the dutiful son who follows the fathers path, the eldest masculine principle that maintains patriarchal order
nodes.birthCircumstances: eldest son of Li Jing and Lady Yin, elder brother of Muzha and Nezha, disciple of Manjusri Bodhisattva

nodes.name: Shunfeng'er
nodes.domain: clairaudience, supernatural hearing, protection, sea
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: deity with supernatural hearing who can hear sounds from a thousand miles away, companion to Qianliyan
nodes.significantEvent: together with Qianliyan (Thousand-Mile Eye) serves as the ears and eyes of the sea goddess Mazu, listening for the cries of sailors in distress
nodes.symbolism: supernatural hearing as a divine gift of protection, the complementary senses guarding the vulnerable, the redeemed demon transformed into a divine guardian
nodes.neumannArchetype: the transformed shadow (demon) who becomes the all-hearing ear of the protective Great Mother (Mazu)
nodes.birthCircumstances: originally a demon subdued by the goddess Mazu and converted into her servant

nodes.name: Xingtian
nodes.domain: rebellion, headless combat, defiance, will
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: headless giant who continues to fight using his nipples as eyes and his navel as a mouth, wielding a shield and axe
nodes.significantEvent: challenged the Yellow Emperor for supremacy and was beheaded, but his headless body continued to fight, eternally swinging his weapons in defiance
nodes.symbolism: the indomitable will that fights on even after decapitation, defiance that transcends death, the body that continues without the directing head, the refusal to submit
nodes.neumannArchetype: the headless warrior as the body-consciousness that persists without the ego (head), the undying drive of the masculine will disconnected from rational direction
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the servants or allies of the Flame Emperor (Yandi)

nodes.name: Sobek
nodes.domain: water, crocodiles, military power, the Nile, the Fayum
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: man with the head of a crocodile, or as a full crocodile, often wearing the atef crown with uraeus
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped extensively at Crocodilopolis in the Fayum where sacred crocodiles were kept, adorned with jewelry, and mummified at death, feared and venerated simultaneously as the lord of the waterways, associated with pharaonic military might
nodes.symbolism: the crocodile as the terrifying power of the Nile, the ambiguity of a deity both feared and venerated, water power as military might, the predator lurking beneath the surface
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father in his terrible aquatic aspect, the masculine predator-consciousness lurking beneath the waters of the unconscious
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Neith in some traditions, or emerged from the primordial waters

nodes.physicalCharacteristics: lion-headed man wearing a triple-plumed crown, sometimes with multiple arms and elephant tusks

nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father as the African lion-king, the indigenous masculine sovereignty of Nubia
nodes.birthCircumstances: supreme war god of Nubia and the Meroitic Kingdom

nodes.name: Mnemosyne
nodes.domain: memory, remembrance, oral tradition
nodes.characterTrait: contemplative, preserving, foundational to all art
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Titaness, sometimes depicted as a mature pensive woman
nodes.significantEvent: lay with Zeus for nine consecutive nights and bore the nine Muses who preside over all arts and sciences, her pool in Hades allows the dead to remember their past lives
nodes.symbolism: memory as the foundation of all culture, the Titaness whose union with the sky god produces all the arts, remembrance as the antidote to the oblivion of death
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of the arts, memory as the feminine ground from which consciousness and culture spring
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Uranus and Gaia, one of the twelve Titans

nodes.name: Hyacinth
nodes.domain: vegetation, beauty, rebirth, male beauty, spring
nodes.characterTrait: beautiful, beloved, tragic, reborn as a flower
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: most beautiful of mortal youths, Spartan prince

nodes.symbolism: beauty destroyed by accident or jealousy, the dying god who returns as a flower, the blood that generates new life, the pre-Hellenic vegetation deity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the beautiful youth killed by the masculine god, the dying and rising vegetation deity who transforms death into perennial flowering
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of King Amyclas of Sparta and Diomede

nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mothers chthonic son hidden in the form of the nourishing tree, the rebellious masculine absorbed back into the vegetative mother
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the Giants who warred against the gods

nodes.name: Kang Jinlong
nodes.domain: astronomy, protection, the constellations
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: one of the Twenty-Eight Mansions (Xiu), celestial guardians
nodes.significantEvent: one of the twenty-eight stellar spirits guarding the four directions of the sky in Chinese astronomical mythology
nodes.symbolism: the constellation as a divine guardian, the heavens organized into protective celestial beings
nodes.neumannArchetype: the stellar masculine as guardian of the cosmic order

nodes.name: Six Sages of Meishan
nodes.domain: war, mountain spirits, transformation, the Investiture of the Gods
nodes.animals: snake, goat, pig, dog, rooster, ox, monkey, tiger, dragon
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: six powerful mountain sages or demons who serve Erlang Shen
nodes.significantEvent: allied with Erlang Shen in the Investiture of the Gods and Journey to the West, help him subdue Sun Wukong and other powerful enemies, each possesses unique supernatural abilities
nodes.symbolism: the wild mountain spirits who serve the civilizing hero, untamed nature allied with cosmic order, the six as a cosmic number of service
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wild nature spirits (shadow) tamed and enlisted by the hero of consciousness (Erlang Shen)

nodes.name: Xiyue Dadi
nodes.domain: the west, mountains, judgment, protection
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Great Emperor of the Western Peak, ruler of Mount Hua
nodes.significantEvent: one of the five sacred mountain deities, rules the western sacred mountain Mount Hua and judges souls in the western region
nodes.symbolism: the western mountain as the seat of divine judgment, the mountain peak as the throne of cosmic authority
nodes.neumannArchetype: the mountain father of the west, the patriarchal consciousness seated on the peak of the western direction

nodes.name: Nefertem
nodes.domain: the lotus, perfume, beauty, healing, the sun, sunrise
nodes.object: blue lotus (his iconic emblem — the primeval lotus from which Ra emerged at creation); sistrum
nodes.characterTrait: beautiful, fragrant, healing, youthful, solar, lotus-born
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Anthropomorphic young man wearing a lotus-flower headdress (often with feathers and menat-necklaces hanging from it); sometimes lion-headed (inheriting Sekhmet's leonine aspect).
nodes.significantEvent: The young god of the blue lotus — the flower from which Ra was born at the dawn of creation (in one cosmogonic tradition). In Memphis, son of Ptah and Sekhmet; completing the Memphite triad. Patron of perfume and the lotus-cult.
nodes.symbolism: the lotus as the flower of creation that opens at dawn, perfume and beauty as sacred offerings, the young god born from the flower of the first morning, healing through fragrance
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child born from the lotus of creation, the youthful masculine beauty that emerges from the Great Mothers flower at the dawn of consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Ptah and Sekhmet in the Memphite triad; identified with the primordial lotus-emergence.

nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father of Nubian creation, the indigenous African patriarchal creator

nodes.name: Bona Dea
nodes.domain: fertility, healing, women, mystery rites, chastity
nodes.object: serpent, herbs, wine jar (forbidden to men)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess depicted with serpents and healing herbs, her rites were exclusively for women
nodes.significantEvent: her annual festival in December was held in the home of the highest magistrate, exclusively for women with no men allowed, the scandal of Publius Clodius sneaking into the rites in 62 BCE became one of the most famous scandals in Roman history
nodes.symbolism: the exclusively feminine sacred space from which men are barred, the serpent as the healing feminine power, the forbidden name as the mystery of the unspeakable feminine, wine disguised as milk in her rites
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother in her exclusively feminine mystery aspect, the sacred feminine that excludes the masculine entirely from its most intimate rites
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient Roman goddess of women and fertility, her true name was forbidden to be spoken

nodes.name: Hybris
nodes.domain: hubris, excessive pride, arrogance, reckless disregard
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: spirit of insolence and violence born from excess
nodes.significantEvent: the great sin of Greek tragedy, the overreaching pride that leads to divine punishment and destruction, embodied by figures like Niobe and Ajax
nodes.symbolism: the fatal flaw of overstepping human limits, the arrogance that brings divine retribution, the inflation that precedes the fall
nodes.neumannArchetype: the inflation of consciousness that refuses to acknowledge its limitations, the psychic crime of identifying the ego with the Self
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Koros (Surfeit) or born from Dysnomia (Lawlessness)

nodes.name: Telephus
nodes.domain: kingship, Mysia, the wound that only the wounder can heal
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: mighty warrior-king of Mysia
nodes.significantEvent: wounded by Achilles spear when the Greeks mistakenly attacked Mysia, the wound would not heal until Achilles agreed to apply rust from the same spear that caused it, then guided the Greeks to Troy
nodes.symbolism: the wound that only the wounder can heal, the enemy who becomes the guide, the exposed divine child raised by wild nature
nodes.neumannArchetype: the abandoned divine child (son of Heracles) nurtured by the animal mother (deer), whose wound becomes the bridge between enemy camps
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Heracles and Auge, abandoned at birth and suckled by a deer, raised in Mysia

nodes.name: King Father of the East
nodes.domain: immortality, the east, yang energy, longevity
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: ancient male deity counterpart to the Queen Mother of the West, ruler of the eastern paradise
nodes.significantEvent: rules the eastern paradise as the male complement to Xiwangmu (Queen Mother of the West), together they represent the cosmic yin-yang balance of immortality, hosts the male immortals
nodes.symbolism: the yang principle of immortality, the eastern counterpart to the western Queen Mother, the balance of masculine and feminine divine authority
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive father archetype as the lord of eastern immortality, complementing the Great Mother (Xiwangmu) in the cosmic balance
nodes.birthCircumstances: Many Taoist mythological works describe him as born of the Pure and the Holy Mother of Origins, ruling the animated beings and the yin and yang that breathes from the eastern sky.

nodes.name: Sun Bin
nodes.domain: strategy, war, military science, revenge, disability
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: crippled military strategist who had to be carried in a chariot due to his mutilated legs
nodes.significantEvent: his fellow student Pang Juan had his kneecaps removed and face tattooed out of jealousy, later Sun Bin served the state of Qi and destroyed Pang Juans army at the Battle of Maling using brilliant tactical deception, author of Sun Bins Art of War
nodes.symbolism: the crippled sage whose mind overcomes his bodys destruction, strategic genius born from suffering and betrayal, revenge achieved through intellectual superiority rather than physical force
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wounded hero whose disability forces the development of pure mental consciousness, the masculine intelligence that triumphs over the physical through the power of strategic thought
nodes.birthCircumstances: descendant of the legendary strategist Sun Tzu, student of the hermit sage Guiguzi

nodes.name: Xu Shilin
nodes.domain: filial piety, the White Snake legend, love, law
nodes.characterTrait: filial, caught between love and law, human
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: son of the White Snake Lady (Bai Suzhen) and the mortal Xu Xian
nodes.significantEvent: studied hard and became a scholar, upon learning of his mothers imprisonment under Leifeng Pagoda he knelt before it in filial devotion until it collapsed and freed her
nodes.symbolism: filial devotion that breaks the prison of cosmic law, the human child of a divine mother who earns her freedom through scholarly merit and love, the bridge between the human and the supernatural
nodes.neumannArchetype: the human son who rescues the imprisoned Great Mother (snake goddess) through the power of filial devotion and cultural achievement
nodes.birthCircumstances: son born to the snake-spirit Bai Suzhen while she was imprisoned under Leifeng Pagoda

nodes.name: Amesemi
nodes.domain: queenship, Nubia, fertility, Meroe
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Nubian queen-goddess, consort of Apedemek or Sebiumeker
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped as a divine queen in the Meroitic Kingdom, associated with the powerful Candaces (queen mothers) of Nubia
nodes.symbolism: the divine Nubian queen as the embodiment of African feminine royal power, the Candace tradition of powerful African queens
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the African queen, the indigenous feminine sovereignty of Nubia
nodes.birthCircumstances: Meroitic goddess associated with Nubian royal feminine power

nodes.name: Nike
nodes.domain: victory, triumph, athletic and military success
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: winged woman, often depicted in flight, carrying a wreath or palm of victory
nodes.significantEvent: sided with Zeus in the Titanomachy along with her siblings, became Athenas constant companion, the famous Nike of Samothrace statue commemorates a naval victory
nodes.symbolism: the divine moment of triumph, victory as a divine gift rather than human achievement, the winged descent of success
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive transformative feminine as the gift of victory, the divine endorsement of the heros success
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the Titan Pallas and the Oceanid Styx, sister of Kratos, Bia, and Zelus

nodes.name: Hysminai
nodes.domain: battles, combat, fighting
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: spirits of battle and combat, feminine personifications of fighting
nodes.significantEvent: the battles personified, they swarm across the fields of war bringing death and destruction
nodes.symbolism: warfare as a swarming demonic force rather than a heroic endeavor, the dehumanizing chaos of mass combat
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible feminine of war, battle as the devouring swarm of death
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughters of Eris (Strife)

nodes.name: Telesphorus
nodes.domain: healing, convalescence, recovery, the divine child
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: small hooded boy, often depicted as a child wrapped in a cloak
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped at healing temples (Asklepieia) as the spirit of recovery, small statues of him were dedicated by those who had been healed
nodes.symbolism: recovery as a mystery wrapped in a cloak, the healing that happens during sleep, the divine child who brings convalescence
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child of the Great Healer, the small hidden one whose mystery is the restoration of health
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Asclepius in some traditions, or an aspect of the healing power of sleep

nodes.name: Kitchen God
nodes.domain: hearth, home, family, annual report to heaven
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: deity residing in the kitchen hearth, depicted as a kindly old man or couple, his paper image placed above the stove
nodes.significantEvent: ascends to heaven on the 23rd of the 12th lunar month to report each familys behavior to the Jade Emperor, families smear honey or sticky candy on his lips to sweeten his report or prevent him from speaking ill
nodes.symbolism: the divine surveillance of domestic life, the hearth as the sacred center of the home, the annual accounting of moral behavior, the bribable deity as a humorous folk adaptation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the domestic masculine as the watchful guardian of the hearth, the father-figure who reports to the supreme patriarch (Jade Emperor)
nodes.birthCircumstances: a deified mortal in various legends, sometimes Zhang Dan who was unfaithful to his wife

nodes.name: Sun Wukong
nodes.domain: rebellion, transformation, immortality, journey, mischief, protection
nodes.object: Ruyi Jingu Bang (golden-hooped staff), golden chain mail, phoenix-feather cap, cloud-stepping boots
nodes.characterTrait: rebellious, clever, loyal, impatient, powerful, irreverent, devoted
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: stone monkey king with golden fur, fiery eyes with golden pupils (huoyan jinjing), can transform into 72 different forms, rides clouds at incredible speed
nodes.significantEvent: proclaimed himself the Great Sage Equal to Heaven, wreaked havoc in the Celestial Palace, imprisoned under Five Elements Mountain by Buddha for 500 years, freed to protect the monk Xuanzang on the journey to India to retrieve Buddhist scriptures, achieved Buddhahood upon completion
nodes.symbolism: the irrepressible spirit of rebellion and freedom, the journey from chaos to enlightenment, the monkey mind tamed through devotion and discipline, the stone-born being who achieves the highest consciousness through service
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine trickster-child born from the Great Mother (stone/earth) who challenges the patriarchal order (Heaven), is imprisoned, and achieves the highest consciousness through the discipline of the journey and service to the teaching
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from a magical stone egg on the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit, nourished by the five elements

nodes.name: Yanluo Wang
nodes.domain: the underworld, judgment of the dead, punishment, the ten courts
nodes.object: judge tablet, mirror of karma, brush of judgment
nodes.animals: bull, horse, bear, ox, monkey, dragon
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: stern judge in official robes and hat, seated in judgment in the underworld courts
nodes.significantEvent: supreme judge of the dead who reviews each souls life in the Mirror of Karma, determines punishment and the conditions of reincarnation, administers the ten courts of the Chinese underworld where specific sins receive specific punishments
nodes.symbolism: death as a judicial process, the karmic mirror that shows the truth of a life lived, the underworld bureaucracy that processes souls with the same rigor as earthly government, the ten courts as the comprehensive accounting of all sin
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father as the terrible judge of the dead, the patriarchal consciousness that evaluates and punishes the shadow in the underworld
nodes.birthCircumstances: Chinese adaptation of the Indian Buddhist Yama (King of the Dead), ruler of the ten courts of Diyu (hell)

nodes.name: Ma’at
nodes.domain: truth, justice, cosmic order, balance, judgment, morality
nodes.characterTrait: truthful, just, ordered, balanced, cosmic, unwavering
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman wearing a single ostrich feather on her head, or depicted as the feather alone, sometimes with wings
nodes.significantEvent: her feather was weighed against the heart of the dead in the Hall of Judgment, if the heart was heavier than the feather (laden with sin) it was devoured by Ammit, the pharaoh was obligated to uphold Maat as the foundation of good governance
nodes.symbolism: truth as the cosmic ordering principle, the feather as the lightest measure against which a life is weighed, justice as the foundation of creation, the balance of the scales as the moment of ultimate judgment
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine principle of cosmic order, the Great Mothers law that governs all creation and against which every consciousness is measured
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Ra, established at the moment of creation as the ordering principle of the cosmos

nodes.symbolism: the sun at the horizon as the ferryman between the living and the dead, the solar journey as the archetypal passage
nodes.neumannArchetype: the solar psychopomp, the masculine sun-consciousness that guides between the worlds

nodes.domain: the underworld, devouring, lakes of fire, punishment
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: ferocious dog-like or lion-like creature of the underworld associated with lakes of fire
nodes.significantEvent: dwelt in a lake of fire in the underworld and devoured the condemned souls, one of the most fearsome beings in the Egyptian afterlife
nodes.symbolism: the lake of fire as the ultimate punishment, the devouring creature of the deep underworld, fiery destruction of the wicked
nodes.neumannArchetype: the devouring shadow of the underworld, the terrible masculine that consumes the consciousness that has failed the judgment

nodes.domain: lightning, storms, protection from lightning, electricity
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess of lightning and electrical storms
nodes.significantEvent: invoked for protection against lightning strikes, which were considered divine messages, places struck by lightning were considered sacred (bidental) and fenced off
nodes.symbolism: lightning as a divine feminine force, the thunderbolt as the sacred mark of divine attention, the place struck by lightning as consecrated ground
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine of the thunderbolt, the divine feminine as the electrical energy of consciousness

nodes.name: Concordia
nodes.domain: harmony, agreement, peace between citizens, the state
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman holding an olive branch and cornucopia, sometimes with joined hands, personification of civic harmony
nodes.significantEvent: her temple in the Roman Forum was one of the most important civic temples, rebuilt multiple times including by Tiberius, represented the ideal of harmony between the social orders (patricians and plebeians, Senate and people)
nodes.symbolism: civic harmony as a divine feminine principle, the olive branch as the sign of peace between citizens, the joined hands as the agreement of opposing factions
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine principle of social harmony, the anima that unifies opposing masculine forces within the state
nodes.birthCircumstances: personification of the concept of concordia (harmony and agreement)

nodes.name: Cloacina
nodes.domain: sewers, purification, the Cloaca Maxima, cleansing, Venus
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: aspect of Venus associated with the purification of sewers and flowing water, specifically the Cloaca Maxima of Rome
nodes.significantEvent: her shrine was in the Cloaca Maxima, Romes great sewer system, she represented the purifying power of flowing water that cleansed the city, a statue of Venus Cloacina stood above the sewer entrance in the Forum
nodes.symbolism: purification through flowing water even in the sewers, the divine feminine present even in the most humble and unclean places, the sacred cleansing of civilizations waste, the sewer as a temple of purification
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of purification, the feminine that cleanses even the waste of civilization through the flow of sacred water

nodes.name: Gorgon
nodes.domain: terror, protection, death, the apotropaic
nodes.characterTrait: terrifying, petrifying, protective when controlled, primal
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: female face with serpent hair, tusks, lolling tongue, wide staring eyes, sometimes winged
nodes.significantEvent: Medusa the mortal Gorgon was beheaded by Perseus, her head was placed on Athenas aegis as an apotropaic device, the Gorgoneion was used throughout Greek art as a protective emblem
nodes.symbolism: the terrifying face of the unconscious feminine, the Gorgoneion as ward against evil by confronting viewers with primal terror, the mask as the boundary between human and monstrous
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Terrible Mother projection, the terrifying aspect of the unconscious feminine at the negative pole (M-), the face that petrifies consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughters of the sea gods Phorcys and Ceto, the three sisters Stheno, Euryale, and Medusa

nodes.name: Iacchus
nodes.domain: the Eleusinian Mysteries, procession, ecstasy, wine
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful youth carrying a torch, leading the mystai in procession
nodes.significantEvent: led the sacred procession from Athens to Eleusis on the sixth day of the Mysteries, his name was shouted in the ritual cry Iacche
nodes.symbolism: the ecstatic leader of the mystery procession, the torchlight that guides initiates through the darkness toward revelation, the Dionysiac element within the Eleusinian Mysteries
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child as the guide through the mystery, the youthful masculine light that leads consciousness through the transformative darkness of the Great Mothers rites
nodes.birthCircumstances: variously identified as the son of Demeter, son of Persephone, or an aspect of Dionysus

nodes.name: Tenes
nodes.domain: kingship, Apollo, martyrdom, justice, Tenedos
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: handsome young king of the island of Tenedos
nodes.significantEvent: falsely accused by his stepmother and thrown into the sea in a chest by his father, established himself as king of Tenedos, killed by Achilles when the Greeks landed on the island
nodes.symbolism: the falsely accused divine son who establishes his own kingdom, killed by the greatest hero at the threshold of the Trojan War, Apollo avenging his son by later guiding Paris arrow to kill Achilles
nodes.neumannArchetype: the abandoned divine child who becomes king, then is destroyed by the hero, his divine father later exacting revenge
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Apollo (or Cycnus), abandoned at birth and raised on Tenedos

nodes.name: Clementia
nodes.domain: mercy, clemency, forgiveness, restraint
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: serene woman holding an olive branch and leaning on a column, personification of clemency and mercy
nodes.significantEvent: the Temple of Clementia was built in honor of Julius Caesars famous clemency toward his enemies, became an important imperial virtue on Roman coins
nodes.symbolism: mercy as a divine feminine quality, clemency toward enemies as the highest Roman virtue, the olive branch as the sign of sparing the defeated
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine principle of mercy within the patriarchal order, the anima that restrains the masculine impulse to destroy

nodes.domain: good fortune, favorable outcomes, success, fever protection

nodes.symbolism: divine favor in the small matters of daily life, the practical religious concern with favorable outcomes and the avoidance of illness
nodes.neumannArchetype: the protective feminine of favorable daily outcomes, the Great Mother of the practical everyday

nodes.name: Iaso
nodes.domain: healing, recovery, cure
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: gentle goddess of healing and recovery from illness
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped alongside her father and sisters at healing sanctuaries, invoked in the Hippocratic Oath
nodes.symbolism: the process of recovery and cure, healing as a gradual restoration rather than an instant miracle
nodes.neumannArchetype: the nurturing feminine as the restorer of health, the gentle process of cure
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Asclepius and Epione

nodes.name: The Litae
nodes.domain: prayers, supplication, atonement, Ruin repair
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: old wrinkled women who limp along after Ate (Ruin), daughters of Zeus
nodes.significantEvent: in Homers Iliad they follow Ate trying to undo the damage she causes, those who receive them well are blessed, those who reject them are cursed with Ates ruin
nodes.symbolism: the prayers that limp after ruin trying to heal its damage, the slow healing that follows swift destruction, humility and supplication as the only remedies for the damage of pride
nodes.neumannArchetype: the crippled but persistent feminine of repair, the old women of consciousness who hobble after the destruction of inflation trying to restore wholeness
nodes.birthCircumstances: parents: Zeus

nodes.name: Kui Xing
nodes.domain: examinations, literature, scholarship, the stars
nodes.object: writing brush, ink stone, dipper constellation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: fierce-looking deity standing on the head of a giant turtle or fish, kicking the Big Dipper constellation with one foot, brandishing a writing brush
nodes.significantEvent: presides over civil service examinations and literary achievement, scholars pray to him before imperial exams, his image is common in study halls throughout China
nodes.symbolism: scholarly achievement despite physical disadvantage, the stars of the Big Dipper as the celestial judges of literary merit, the brush as the weapon mightier than the sword
nodes.neumannArchetype: the compensatory masculine, the shadow (ugly face) transformed into the patron of the highest cultural achievement (scholarship)
nodes.birthCircumstances: originally a brilliant scholar who was denied success due to his ugly face, attempted suicide but was saved and deified

nodes.name: Taibai Jinxing
nodes.domain: diplomacy, the stars, Venus, heavenly bureaucracy
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: kindly old man with white beard, often depicted descending from the sky on a cloud, identified with the planet Venus
nodes.significantEvent: serves as the diplomatic envoy of the Jade Emperor, sent to negotiate with powerful adversaries including Sun Wukong, advocates for mercy and negotiation over force in heavenly councils
nodes.symbolism: celestial diplomacy, the morning star as the voice of reason in heavens councils, the gentle elder who represents the possibility of peaceful resolution
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wise old man as the diplomatic aspect of the Great Father, the senex who advocates reconciliation over the warriors direct confrontation
nodes.birthCircumstances: the star spirit of the planet Venus, a senior minister of the celestial court

nodes.name: Yidi
nodes.domain: wine, brewing, invention, celebration
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: legendary inventor of wine or alcoholic beverages
nodes.significantEvent: invented wine and presented it to Yu the Great, who tasted it and prophesied that wine would one day cause the downfall of kingdoms, afterward Yu banned wine from the court
nodes.symbolism: the invention of wine as both a gift and a curse, the prophetic warning about intoxications danger, the ambiguity of the intoxicating discovery
nodes.neumannArchetype: the culture hero of intoxication, the inventor whose gift is immediately recognized as dangerous by the wise ruler
nodes.birthCircumstances: servant or official of Yu the Great, the legendary sage-king

nodes.name: Amunet
nodes.domain: hiddenness, air, the primordial void, the Ogdoad
nodes.characterTrait: hidden, invisible, primordial, mysterious, feminine complement
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: serpent-headed woman, the feminine counterpart of Amun in the Ogdoad of Hermopolis
nodes.significantEvent: together with Amun she represents the hidden and invisible aspect of creation, part of the Ogdoad that generated the conditions for the suns emergence
nodes.symbolism: the feminine aspect of the hidden, the invisible generative force complementing the masculine hidden god, the serpent as the chthonic form of the hidden feminine
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hidden feminine counterpart of the hidden masculine (Amun), the Great Mother in her invisible pre-creation aspect
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the eight primordial deities of the Ogdoad, the feminine aspect of the hidden primordial force

nodes.domain: strength, the underworld, terror, darkness

nodes.symbolism: raw strength in the service of underworld guardianship, terror as a defensive force in the realm of the dead
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow guardian of the unconscious depths, the raw masculine power of the underworld

nodes.name: Perit
nodes.domain: seeds, germination, agriculture, the afterlife, vegetation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess associated with seeds and the germination of grain
nodes.significantEvent: associated with the germination of grain seeds and the parallel process of resurrection in the afterlife, the seed as the promise of new life from death
nodes.symbolism: the seed as the container of future life, germination as the model of resurrection, the agricultural cycle as the template of eternal life
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of germination, the feminine earth that brings forth new life from the seed of the dead masculine (grain)

nodes.name: Dies
nodes.domain: daylight, the day, the diurnal cycle
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: personification of daylight and the day itself
nodes.significantEvent: personification of the day in Roman cosmology, the bright counterpart to Nox (Night), represented the daylight hours as a divine presence
nodes.symbolism: daylight as a divine personification, the day as a living cosmic presence
nodes.neumannArchetype: the bright masculine consciousness of day, the solar awareness in its diurnal aspect
nodes.birthCircumstances: She was the daughter of Chaos and Caligo (mist), and the counterpart of the Greek goddess Hemera.

nodes.name: Aeneas
nodes.domain: duty, piety, founding of Rome, exile, destiny
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: tall, handsome Trojan warrior, carrying his father on his back from burning Troy
nodes.significantEvent: escaped the fall of Troy carrying his aged father Anchises and leading his son Ascanius, wandered the Mediterranean, loved and abandoned Dido queen of Carthage, descended to the underworld, founded the line that would establish Rome
nodes.symbolism: duty and destiny over personal desire, the exile who founds a greater civilization, piety as the supreme virtue, the bridge between the Greek and Roman worlds
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hero of destiny who sacrifices personal happiness (Dido) for the collective fate of founding a new civilization
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of the Trojan prince Anchises and the goddess Aphrodite, born on Mount Ida

nodes.domain: knowledge, sight, the seeing one
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Oceanid nymph whose name means She Who Knows

nodes.symbolism: the oceanic wisdom that produces the sorceress, the mother of magical knowledge, the deep knowing of the sea
nodes.neumannArchetype: the oceanic Great Mother as the source of feminine magical knowledge, the wise water from which the sorceress-daughter springs
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Oceanus and Tethys

nodes.name: Trophonius
nodes.domain: oracles, the underworld, earth mysteries, healing through incubation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: underground oracle figure, associated with a cave sanctuary
nodes.significantEvent: built a temple and was swallowed by the earth, became an oracle god whose consultation required an elaborate terrifying descent into his underground cave at Lebadeia, those who consulted him emerged changed forever
nodes.symbolism: the terrifying oracle of the earth, the descent into the underworld for knowledge, the transformative terror of encountering the chthonic divine
nodes.neumannArchetype: the swallowed hero who becomes the chthonic oracle, consciousness that descends into the Great Mothers body to gain terrible knowledge
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Apollo or of Erginus king of Orchomenus, brother of Agamedes

nodes.name: Kuimulang
nodes.domain: astronomy, the constellations, protection
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: one of the Twenty-Eight Mansions, the Wood Wolf of the Legs constellation
nodes.significantEvent: one of the twenty-eight stellar spirits, plays a significant role in Journey to the West where he helps the pilgrims
nodes.symbolism: the stellar guardian as a benevolent divine being, the constellation made personal
nodes.neumannArchetype: the stellar masculine as the guardian of the cosmic order
nodes.deathCircumstances: These constellations are the same as those studied in Western astrology.

nodes.name: Taiyi Zhenren
nodes.domain: immortality, protection, healing, Daoism, lotus rebirth
nodes.object: nine-dragon divine fire cover, wind fire wheels, fire-tipped spear
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Daoist immortal of great power, one of the Twelve Golden Immortals of Kunlun
nodes.significantEvent: master and spiritual father of Nezha, rebuilt Nezhas body from lotus roots after his death, gave him his divine weapons, one of the most powerful immortals in the Fengshen Yanyi narrative
nodes.symbolism: the spiritual father who remakes the divine child from sacred material (lotus), creative power that can restore life in a new form, the lotus as the vehicle of rebirth
nodes.neumannArchetype: the spiritual father who resurrects the divine child through the Great Mothers symbol (lotus), the alchemical master who transforms death into rebirth
nodes.birthCircumstances: Another interpretation suggests that this deity is the same as the King Father of the East (), born from the essence of the sun.

nodes.name: Yin Cha
nodes.domain: the underworld, arrest of souls, enforcement
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: underworld officers who arrest and escort souls to the courts of hell
nodes.significantEvent: the shadowy figures who come for the dying and escort their souls to the underworld for judgment, working under the authority of Yanluo Wang
nodes.symbolism: the inescapable arrest of the soul at death, the underworld as a judicial system with its own enforcement, death as a summons
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow enforcement of the patriarchal underworld order, the binding masculine that brings consciousness to account

nodes.name: Onuris
nodes.domain: war, hunting, the sky, slaying
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: man wearing four tall plumes and holding a lance, sometimes depicted catching enemies with a rope
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped as a war god who hunts and captures enemies, associated with the pharaohs hunting exploits, sometimes shown as the personification of the warriors prowess in capturing enemies on the battlefield
nodes.symbolism: the warrior who hunts both animals and enemies, the lance as the sky-piercing weapon, the capture of chaos through the warriors skill
nodes.neumannArchetype: the aggressive masculine hunter-warrior, the active solar consciousness that pursues and captures the forces of the unconscious
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient war and hunting god of the Thinite region

nodes.domain: pain, mourning, the underworld, dread
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: fearsome underworld deity whose name literally means that soul, associated with pain and mourning
nodes.significantEvent: one of the dangerous beings in the underworld whom the dead sought to avoid during their journey to the afterlife
nodes.symbolism: the pain and dread of the underworld passage, the soul of suffering that haunts the afterlife journey
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow of pain in the unconscious, the dreadful masculine that consciousness must pass through on its underworld journey

nodes.name: Petbe
nodes.domain: revenge, violence, the underworld, chaos
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: violent underworld deity associated with revenge and retribution
nodes.significantEvent: one of the dangerous underworld spirits, associated with violent revenge and the chaotic forces of the afterlife
nodes.symbolism: the divine vengeance of the underworld, violence as a cosmic force, the dangerous spirits that haunt the guilty dead
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow of vengeance in the unconscious, the retributive masculine of the underworld

nodes.name: Epona
nodes.domain: horses, cavalry, mules, donkeys, fertility, travel
nodes.characterTrait: equine, fertile, protective of horses, nurturing, traveling
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman seated between two horses or on a horse, often holding grain or fruit, the only Celtic goddess officially adopted into the Roman pantheon
nodes.significantEvent: the only Celtic deity officially worshipped in Rome, adopted by the Roman cavalry and widely venerated across the empire, her festival was December 18, stables were decorated with roses in her honor
nodes.symbolism: the horse goddess as the link between Celtic and Roman religion, the mare as the symbol of sovereignty and fertility, the stable as the sacred space of the horse-goddess
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of horses, the theriomorphic feminine of the mare who represents sovereignty and the journey
nodes.birthCircumstances: originally a Celtic goddess adopted into the Roman pantheon, protectress of horses and cavalry

nodes.name: Dione
nodes.domain: fertility, prophecy, the oracle at Dodona, the sky
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: ancient Titaness or Oceanid, consort of Zeus at Dodona
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped alongside Zeus at the oracle of Dodona as his original consort before Hera, in Homers Iliad she comforts Aphrodite who is her daughter
nodes.symbolism: the ancient feminine counterpart of Zeus predating the Olympian order, the oracle as feminine wisdom, the sky goddess whose name is the feminine form of Zeus
nodes.neumannArchetype: the ancient Great Mother who was the original consort of the sky father before being displaced by the Olympian order
nodes.birthCircumstances: either a Titaness daughter of Uranus and Gaia, or an Oceanid daughter of Oceanus and Tethys

nodes.name: Inachus
nodes.domain: rivers, Argos, kingship, the first river
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: river god and first king of Argos
nodes.significantEvent: judged the contest between Hera and Poseidon for patronage of Argos, chose Hera, Poseidon punished him by drying up his river, father of Io
nodes.symbolism: the river-king who chooses the Great Goddess over the sea god and is punished with drought, the first sovereign as a flowing presence
nodes.neumannArchetype: the river father who chooses the Great Mother (Hera) and suffers the masculine gods retribution, the primordial flowing king
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Oceanus and Tethys, the oldest river god of the Argolid
nodes.deathCircumstances: The historian Pausanias describes him as the eldest king of Argos who named the river after himself and sacrificed to Hera.

nodes.name: Zagreus
nodes.domain: death and rebirth, the Orphic Mysteries, wine, hunting, dismemberment
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the first Dionysus, often depicted as a horned child or bull-formed god
nodes.significantEvent: as an infant he was lured away by the Titans with toys and a mirror, dismembered and devoured by them, his heart was saved by Athena and from it Zeus created the second Dionysus (son of Semele), the Titans were destroyed by Zeus thunderbolt and from their ashes humanity was created
nodes.symbolism: the god dismembered and reborn, the divine spark within humanity (from the Titans who ate him), the mirror of self-knowledge, death as the prerequisite for cosmic rebirth
nodes.neumannArchetype: the archetypal dying-and-rising god, the divine child dismembered by the Titans (the devouring old order) whose heart (consciousness) survives to be reborn, and whose substance generates a new humanity
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Zeus in serpent form and Persephone, born in the underworld

nodes.name: Leigong
nodes.domain: thunder, lightning, punishment, justice
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: fearsome blue-skinned deity with wings, clawed feet and a beak-like face, surrounded by drums that he beats to create thunder
nodes.significantEvent: punishes the wicked by striking them with lightning, works alongside Dianmu (Lightning Goddess) who uses mirrors to direct his bolts, in folk tales he can be tricked but always delivers cosmic justice
nodes.symbolism: thunder as divine judgment, the storm as the voice of cosmic justice, punishment from the sky that cannot be evaded, the complementary pair of thunder and lightning as masculine and feminine forces of justice
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wrathful sky father who punishes through thunder and lightning, the masculine justice principle delivered from the heavens
nodes.birthCircumstances: the Thunder God, one of the most ancient Chinese deities

nodes.name: Three Great Emperor-Officials
nodes.domain: heaven, earth, water, forgiveness, blessing, cosmic governance
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: three emperor-officials who govern heaven, earth, and water respectively
nodes.significantEvent: the Heavenly Official grants blessings (Shangyuan Festival), the Earth Official grants forgiveness (Zhongyuan Festival/Ghost Festival), the Water Official wards off misfortune (Xiayuan Festival), together they govern the three realms
nodes.symbolism: the triple governance of the cosmos through heaven, earth, and water, the three festivals as the annual rhythm of blessing, forgiveness, and protection, bureaucratic governance of the spiritual realms
nodes.neumannArchetype: the triple masculine governance of the three cosmic levels, the patriarchal ordering of heaven, earth, and water
nodes.birthCircumstances: in Daoist tradition they are the three sons of a primordial sage, or aspects of the cosmic order

nodes.name: Ying Bu英布
nodes.domain: war, rebellion, loyalty, betrayal, the Chu-Han contention
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: fearsome warrior covered in battle scars
nodes.significantEvent: one of the most ferocious generals of the Chu-Han contention, initially served Xiang Yu then defected to Liu Bang, was later betrayed and executed by Liu Bang and Empress Lu
nodes.symbolism: the scarred warrior whose every wound tells a story of battle, the general who changes sides and is destroyed by the suspicion this creates
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow warrior whose fierce loyalty is undermined by his own history of shifting allegiances
nodes.birthCircumstances: originally a convict who escaped and joined the rebellion against the Qin Dynasty

nodes.name: Maahes
nodes.domain: war, protection, the sun, devouring, punishment
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: lion-headed man or full lion, son of the fierce goddesses Sekhmet or Bastet
nodes.significantEvent: a fierce lion god who devoured captives and guarded sacred places, served as an executioner of the gods, associated with the heat of summer and the destructive power of the sun
nodes.symbolism: the lion as the supreme predator-protector, the devouring sun at its most ferocious, divine punishment enacted through the jaws of the lion
nodes.neumannArchetype: the fierce son of the terrible mother (Sekhmet), the devouring masculine that enacts divine punishment through the predatory instinct
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Sekhmet (or Bastet) and Ptah, the lion god of war and protection

nodes.name: Babi
nodes.domain: virility, aggression, the underworld, baboons
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: baboon deity with an erect phallus, dangerous and aggressive
nodes.significantEvent: a dangerous underworld being who threatened the dead, his uncontrolled aggression and sexuality represented the base masculine instincts that the dead had to overcome, the baboon as the ithyphallic beast of chaos
nodes.symbolism: uncontrolled male sexuality and aggression as dangers of the underworld, the baboon as the primal beast of base instinct, the phallus as uncontrolled power
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow masculine of uncontrolled instinct, the phallic aggression of the uroboric unconscious that the dead must overcome
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient baboon god of the underworld, associated with uncontrolled male sexuality and aggression

nodes.name: Raet-Tawy
nodes.domain: the sun, femininity, Heliopolis, solar worship
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the feminine form of Ra, the sun goddess of Heliopolis
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped at Heliopolis as the feminine counterpart of Ra, representing the female solar principle
nodes.symbolism: the sun as having both a masculine and feminine aspect, the feminine sun as the complement to the masculine Ra
nodes.neumannArchetype: the solar feminine, the Great Mothers solar aspect as the complement to the Great Fathers sun
nodes.birthCircumstances: the feminine aspect of the sun god Ra

nodes.name: Phaethon
nodes.domain: sun, youthful ambition, cosmic catastrophe
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: radiant, beautiful youth, son of the sun
nodes.significantEvent: demanded to drive his fathers sun chariot to prove his divine parentage, lost control of the horses and scorched the earth, struck down by Zeus thunderbolt to save the world
nodes.symbolism: youthful hubris attempting to wield divine power, the catastrophe of exceeding mortal limits, the son who must prove his fathers identity at the cost of his life
nodes.neumannArchetype: the failed solar hero who cannot bear the burden of full consciousness, destroyed by the very light he sought to command
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Helios the sun god and the Oceanid Clymene

nodes.name: Ino
nodes.domain: the sea, Dionysiac cult, nursing, transformation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: mortal queen who became a sea goddess, sometimes depicted with a flowing veil
nodes.significantEvent: raised the infant Dionysus after Semeles death, maddened by Hera she threw herself and her son Melicertes into the sea, transformed into the sea goddess Leucothea, later saved Odysseus from drowning by lending him her veil
nodes.symbolism: the mortal nurse of the god who is transformed through madness and death into a divine protector of sailors, motherly love surviving even death and madness
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as nurse who passes through madness and death to become the protective sea goddess, the transformative power of maternal devotion
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Cadmus and Harmonia, sister of Semele, wife of King Athamas

nodes.name: Šanta
nodes.domain: pestilence, illness, divine punishment, Hittite-Greek syncretism
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: plague deity of Anatolian origin adopted into Greek tradition
nodes.significantEvent: associated with the transmission of plague and its divine cure, reflecting the Anatolian layer of Apollos plague and healing functions
nodes.symbolism: the foreign origin of Apollos plague function, the god who both sends and cures disease, the Anatolian roots of Greek religion
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible masculine as the sender of plague, the destructive aspect of the solar god rooted in pre-Greek Anatolian religion
nodes.birthCircumstances: Luwian/Hittite deity later syncretized with Apollo in his plague-sending aspect

nodes.name: Li Jing
nodes.domain: war, Buddhism, pagoda-bearing, heavenly authority
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: imposing celestial general carrying a miniature golden pagoda on his palm that can capture and imprison demons
nodes.significantEvent: his son Nezhas violent birth and rebellious nature brought him into constant conflict until Buddha reconciled them, the golden pagoda was given to him to control Nezha, became one of the Four Heavenly Kings
nodes.symbolism: the conflict between patriarchal authority and the divine child, the pagoda as the instrument of control over rebellious power, the stern father who must learn to accommodate the new generation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the authoritarian father who must be reconciled with the rebellious divine child, the patriarch whose instrument of control (pagoda) is also his burden
nodes.birthCircumstances: based on the Indian Buddhist figure Vaisravana (Kubera), in Chinese mythology father of Nezha, Jinzha, and Muzha

nodes.name: Ying Ziying
nodes.domain: the fall of Qin, last ruler, surrender
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the last ruler of the Qin Dynasty
nodes.significantEvent: surrendered to Liu Bang and the rebel armies after only 46 days on the throne, effectively ending the Qin Dynasty, was later killed by Xiang Yu
nodes.symbolism: the last ruler of a doomed dynasty, the noble surrender that cannot prevent the destruction to follow, the innocent heir who inherits catastrophe
nodes.neumannArchetype: the final patriarch of a collapsing order, the last king who inherits only the destruction of his predecessors
nodes.birthCircumstances: grandson of Qin Shi Huang, placed on the throne after the murder of the Second Emperor

nodes.name: Nehebkau
nodes.domain: serpents, protection, magic, the afterlife, binding
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: serpent deity, sometimes depicted as a winged serpent or a human with a serpent body
nodes.significantEvent: guardian of the underworld who swallowed seven cobras to gain their power, protected the pharaoh in the afterlife, coiled around the mound of creation
nodes.symbolism: the serpent power that protects through binding, the snake that swallows other snakes to gain their power, the coiled serpent around the primordial mound
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive serpent of the unconscious that protects rather than threatens, the uroboric power harnessed for protection
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient serpent god who existed from the beginning of creation

nodes.name: Bata
nodes.domain: agriculture, cattle herding, the bull, the afterlife, twins
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: bull deity or man associated with sacred bulls and agriculture
nodes.significantEvent: protagonist of the Tale of Two Brothers, one of the most famous Egyptian stories, where he is betrayed by his brothers wife, transformed into a bull, and eventually reborn as a pharaoh through multiple transformations
nodes.symbolism: the bull as the sacred agricultural animal, transformation through multiple animal and plant forms as the cycle of death and rebirth, the tale of betrayal and resurrection
nodes.neumannArchetype: the transforming masculine that passes through multiple forms (bull, tree, pharaoh) in its journey from betrayal to sovereignty
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient bull god associated with the Bata and Anubis tale (Tale of Two Brothers)

nodes.domain: fate, protection, ka-spirits, the soul, personal guardians

nodes.significantEvent: the hemsut were feminine guardian spirits associated with the ka of each individual, protecting the life force of the person they guarded
nodes.symbolism: the feminine guardian of the individual soul, the ka-spirit as a personal divine protector, the feminine aspect of ones own life force
nodes.neumannArchetype: the personal anima as the guardian of the individual ka (life force), the feminine protector of individual consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: parents: Ptah

nodes.name: Hypnos
nodes.domain: sleep, rest, dreams, twilight
nodes.object: poppy, horn of sleep-inducing opium, branch dripping Lethe water
nodes.characterTrait: gentle, irresistible, all-subduing, twin of death
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: winged youth, or winged old man, gentle and soft, dwelling in a cave of eternal twilight
nodes.significantEvent: put Zeus to sleep at Heras request so she could work against the Trojans, fled to Nyx when Zeus woke and raged, Zeus dared not pursue because even he feared Nyx
nodes.symbolism: sleep as the gentle twin of death, the dissolution of consciousness each night, the cave of twilight between waking and the underworld
nodes.neumannArchetype: the dissolution of ego-consciousness, the nightly return to the uroboric state of undifferentiation
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Nyx, twin brother of Thanatos (Death)

nodes.name: Kydoimos
nodes.domain: battle confusion, chaos in war, din
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: spirit of the confusion and din of battle
nodes.significantEvent: personification of the madness and confusion that sweeps through combatants in the chaos of melee
nodes.symbolism: the psychological disorientation of close combat, the dissolution of order in the violence of war
nodes.neumannArchetype: the dissolution of masculine consciousness in the chaos of battle, the shadow that devours rational thought in combat
nodes.birthCircumstances: son or companion of Ares

nodes.name: Ao Guang
nodes.domain: sea, dragons, weather, the East Sea
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: enormous dragon king in royal robes, can assume human form, blue-green scales in dragon form
nodes.significantEvent: ruler of the East Sea, his son was killed by Nezha who stripped the dragons tendons, Ao Guang appealed to the Jade Emperor for justice, features prominently in Journey to the West when Sun Wukong stole his magical iron pillar weapon
nodes.symbolism: the power and majesty of the ocean, the dragon as the lord of rain and water, the temperamental authority of the sea
nodes.neumannArchetype: the water father archetype, the patriarchal ruler of the oceanic unconscious whose treasures are seized by the young hero
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the four Dragon Kings ruling the four seas
nodes.deathCircumstances: After Ao Guang's favorite investigator Li Gen and third son Ao Bing were both killed by Nezha, Ao Guang set out to talk to Nezha's father, Li Jing.

nodes.name: Li Tieguai
nodes.domain: medicine, healing, iron crutch, immortality, the poor
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: disheveled old beggar with a lame leg leaning on an iron crutch, carrying a medicine gourd, the most visually striking of the Eight Immortals
nodes.significantEvent: first and eldest of the Eight Immortals, his medicine gourd can cure any illness, teaches the lesson that divine power can inhabit the most wretched of forms, patron of the sick and disabled
nodes.symbolism: the divine hidden in the wretched, healing power in the most broken vessel, the beggar-sage whose ugliness conceals supreme wisdom, compassion for the outcast
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wounded healer archetype, the masculine whose broken body conceals the highest consciousness, the divine disguised in the shadow
nodes.birthCircumstances: originally a handsome man, his soul left his body for too long while visiting Laozi in heaven, his disciple cremated his body, forcing his soul to inhabit the body of a dead beggar

nodes.name: Thunder Ancestor
nodes.domain: thunder, punishment, justice, storms
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: ancestor or supreme form of the thunder gods, wielding drums that create thunder
nodes.significantEvent: the progenitor or supreme form of the thunder deities in Chinese mythology, commands all the thunder spirits
nodes.symbolism: thunder as the voice of cosmic justice, the ancestor of all storm punishment, the drumbeat of divine wrath
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wrathful sky father as the origin of all storm-punishment, the archetypal thunder voice of cosmic law

nodes.name: Yinyanggong
nodes.domain: yin and yang, fortune telling, cosmic balance, Daoism
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: deity of yin-yang harmony and cosmic balance
nodes.significantEvent: associated with the cosmic balance of yin and yang forces and the art of geomantic divination (feng shui)
nodes.symbolism: the divine balance of all opposing forces, the cosmic complementarity that underlies all existence, divination as the art of reading the yin-yang balance
nodes.neumannArchetype: the reconciling consciousness that perceives and maintains the balance of all opposites

nodes.name: Gengen-Wer
nodes.domain: creation, the primordial goose, the cosmic egg, sound
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Great Cackler, a primordial goose who laid the cosmic egg at the beginning of creation
nodes.significantEvent: broke the silence of the primordial darkness with his great cackle, laid the cosmic egg from which the sun was born, his cry was the first sound in the universe
nodes.symbolism: the cosmic egg as the container of all creation, the first sound breaking the primordial silence, the goose as the bird of creation whose voice initiates the universe
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial creative masculine whose cry breaks the uroboric silence and whose egg contains the sun of consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: primordial goose who existed before creation, also known as the Great Cackler (Gengen Wer)

nodes.name: Ta-Bitjet
nodes.domain: scorpions, venom, healing, protection
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: scorpion goddess associated with healing from scorpion stings
nodes.significantEvent: protected against scorpion stings and healed those who were stung, associated with Serket and the broader scorpion-healing tradition
nodes.symbolism: the scorpion as both the source of and cure for venom, the healing power that comes from the same creature that wounds
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine healer whose power comes from the same venom that causes the wound, the Great Mother who poisons and cures

nodes.name: Libertas
nodes.domain: freedom, liberty, the republic, the rights of citizens
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman holding the pileus (liberty cap) and a rod of liberation (vindicta), sometimes with a cat at her feet
nodes.significantEvent: her temple on the Aventine Hill was founded in 238 BCE, her image appeared on Roman coins throughout the Republic and Empire, later became the model for modern Liberty symbols including the Statue of Liberty
nodes.symbolism: the liberty cap as the symbol of freed slaves, freedom as a divine feminine gift, the broken chains as liberation from bondage, the cat as the independent animal of liberty
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine as the principle of liberation from bondage, the anima that frees consciousness from its chains
nodes.birthCircumstances: personification of the concept of liberty in the Roman Republic and Empire

nodes.name: Hebe
nodes.domain: youth, rejuvenation, the prime of life, divine service
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: eternally youthful and beautiful, cupbearer of the gods
nodes.significantEvent: served as cupbearer to the gods until replaced by Ganymede, married Heracles after his apotheosis as his divine reward, able to rejuvenate the old
nodes.symbolism: eternal youth as divine gift, the reward awaiting the hero who achieves immortality, youth as divine service
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive anima as the reward for the completed hero, the maiden aspect of the Great Mother bestowed upon the victorious son
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Zeus and Hera, the youngest of the Olympian family

nodes.name: Lampsace
nodes.domain: local cult, city founding, sexual virtue
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: maiden heroine of the city of Lampsacus
nodes.significantEvent: saved the Greek hostages held by the Bebryces and was honored as the eponymous heroine of Lampsacus, or was honored for her virtue
nodes.symbolism: the maiden whose virtue or bravery founds a city, the heroine as the moral foundation of the community
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive maiden whose self-sacrifice establishes the sacred foundation of the city
nodes.birthCircumstances: Lampsace was the daughter of Mandron, king of the Bebryces in Pityussa (the older name for Lampsacus).

nodes.name: Azure Dragon
nodes.domain: spring, the east, wood, benevolence, rain
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: coiling azure or blue-green dragon stretching across the eastern sky, composed of seven star constellations
nodes.significantEvent: appears in spring bringing rain and renewal, one of the four directional guardians protecting the world, represents the Wood element and spring growth
nodes.symbolism: the rising yang energy of spring, benevolent power, the dragon as rain-bringer and life-giver, the east as the direction of new beginnings
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive masculine as the dragon of renewal, the rising consciousness of spring emerging from the waters of winter
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the Four Symbols of Chinese constellations, associated with the East

nodes.name: Lingbao Tianzun
nodes.domain: creation, treasure, Daoism, transformation
nodes.characterTrait: transformative, treasured, second of the Three Pure Ones
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the second of the Three Pure Ones (Sanqing), depicted holding a ruyi scepter and jade book
nodes.significantEvent: rules the second of the three heavens, holds the jade book of life and death, represents the Dao in its creative and treasuring aspect, associated with the yin-yang and the five elements
nodes.symbolism: the treasure of the cosmos preserved in the second emanation of the Dao, the jade book as the cosmic record of all being, creation preserved through wisdom
nodes.neumannArchetype: the second level of cosmic consciousness, the father archetype as the preserver of the cosmic treasure
nodes.birthCircumstances: second emanation of the primordial Dao, the Celestial Worthy of Numinous Treasure

nodes.name: Tian
nodes.domain: heaven, cosmic order, the Mandate of Heaven, supreme moral authority, fate
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: not depicted as a person but as the overarching cosmic principle of Heaven itself, the sky as divine being
nodes.significantEvent: grants the Mandate of Heaven (Tianming) to righteous rulers and withdraws it from the corrupt, the philosophical foundation of Chinese political legitimacy, dynastic cycles are determined by Tians judgment
nodes.symbolism: heaven as the ultimate moral authority, the impersonal cosmic principle that judges rulers and determines dynastic fate, the sky as the visible expression of the highest moral order
nodes.neumannArchetype: the depersonalized Great Father, the patriarchal principle abstracted into the cosmic moral order itself, the sky as impersonal consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: the supreme cosmic principle of Chinese philosophy and religion, successor concept to Shangdi

nodes.name: Yu Shi
nodes.domain: rain, weather, agriculture, storms
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Rain Master who controls rainfall and precipitation
nodes.significantEvent: controls rainfall and is invoked during droughts, works in concert with Fengbo (Wind Master) and Leigong (Thunder God) to produce weather, often depicted sprinkling water from a pot with a willow branch
nodes.symbolism: rain as a divine gift that must be requested and maintained through proper worship, the willow branch as the instrument of gentle rainfall, the rain deity who responds to human need
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine water-giver who responds to the earth mothers need for rain, the fertilizing water consciousness

nodes.name: Eye of Ra
nodes.domain: the sun, destruction, protection, cosmic wrath, divine agency
nodes.characterTrait: wrathful, protective, destroying, fiery, loyal to Ra
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the personified burning eye of the sun god Ra, taking the form of a cobra (uraeus), lioness, or other fierce goddess
nodes.significantEvent: sent to punish Ras enemies and those who violated cosmic order, the burning eye that became the uraeus on the pharaohs crown, when it departed from Ra (the Distant Goddess myth) Egypt fell into chaos until it was lured back
nodes.symbolism: the destructive aspect of solar power personified as the feminine, the uraeus as concentrated divine wrath, the sun that sees all and punishes all transgressions, the inescapable eye of cosmic justice
nodes.neumannArchetype: the fierce feminine emanation of the Great Father (Ra), the destroying anima through which the masculine consciousness punishes and protects
nodes.birthCircumstances: emanation of Ras own solar power, identified with many goddesses including Sekhmet, Hathor, Tefnut, Wadjet, and Bastet

nodes.name: Heryshaf
nodes.domain: fertility, the sun, creation, rams, Herakleopolis
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: ram-headed man wearing the atef crown and solar disk, the great god of Herakleopolis
nodes.significantEvent: supreme deity of Herakleopolis during the First Intermediate Period when that city was the capital of Egypt, combined solar and fertility aspects
nodes.symbolism: the ram as solar fertility, the lake as the primordial waters from which the creator god rules, Herakleopolis as the rival creation center to Thebes and Memphis
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father as the solar ram who rules from the primordial waters, the fertile masculine sovereignty emerging from the lake of creation
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient ram god of Herakleopolis Magna, the ruler on his lake

nodes.name: Nehmetawy
nodes.domain: protection, justice, sistrum, Hermopolis
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess of Hermopolis depicted holding a sistrum and menat collar
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped at Hermopolis alongside Thoth as his consort, played the sistrum to drive away evil and maintain cosmic harmony
nodes.symbolism: the sistrum as the instrument of cosmic harmony, the feminine complement to the wisdom god, music as justice
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine complement to the Great Fathers wisdom (Thoth), the musical feminine that maintains harmony
nodes.birthCircumstances: A local form of the god Horus called Horus-nefer ("Horus, the good one)" might have been viewed as the son of Thoth and Nehmetawy.

nodes.name: Priapus
nodes.domain: fertility, gardens, livestock, male sexuality, abundance
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: permanently erect oversized phallus, often depicted as a rustic garden statue
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped as a garden guardian whose image warded off thieves and evil spirits, associated with Lampsacus on the Hellespont where his cult was centered
nodes.symbolism: the comic and apotropaic phallus, male fertility as both generative and ridiculous, the boundary guardian whose grotesqueness wards off evil
nodes.neumannArchetype: the phallic fertility god as both creative and absurd, the masculine generative principle in its most literal and comic form
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Dionysus and Aphrodite, cursed by Hera with ugliness and impotence before birth, or born with his condition

nodes.name: Lycurgus
nodes.domain: kingship, Dionysiac rejection, punishment, Thrace
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: fierce Thracian king who opposed Dionysus
nodes.significantEvent: drove Dionysus and his nurses into the sea with an ox-goad, punished with madness by Zeus, in his frenzy he killed his own son mistaking him for a vine, the land became barren until the Edoni killed him
nodes.symbolism: the fatal consequences of rejecting the Dionysiac, the king who opposes ecstasy and is destroyed, the dry land that needs the wine god
nodes.neumannArchetype: the rigid patriarchal consciousness that refuses the transformative feminine (Dionysiac ecstasy) and is destroyed by its own violence
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Dryas, king of the Edoni in Thrace

nodes.name: Bi Gan
nodes.domain: loyalty, sacrifice, the heart, righteous governance
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: noble minister with the legendary seven-aperture heart (a heart with seven openings indicating supreme wisdom)
nodes.significantEvent: remonstrated against King Zhous cruelty and was ordered to cut out his own heart to prove whether sages truly have seven-aperture hearts, deified as the God of Wealth (Caishen) because having no heart made him impartial
nodes.symbolism: loyalty unto death, the wise heart sacrificed for truth, impartiality born from the absence of selfish desire, the incorruptible minister
nodes.neumannArchetype: the sacrificial sage whose heartlessness (ego-death) transforms him into the impartial dispenser of fortune
nodes.birthCircumstances: uncle and minister of King Zhou of Shang, the last Shang king
nodes.deathCircumstances: }} When Hu Yuan, who served King Min of Qi, was about to be executed, he referenced both Prince Bigan and Wu Zixu: "Yin had its Bigan, Wu had its Zixu, and Qi has its Hu Yuan.

nodes.name: Liu Chenxiang
nodes.domain: filial piety, heroism, rescuing the divine mother, mountains
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: young half-divine hero wielding a divine axe
nodes.significantEvent: his mother was imprisoned under Mount Hua by his uncle Erlang Shen for marrying a mortal, he grew up, obtained a divine axe, split Mount Hua open, and rescued his mother
nodes.symbolism: filial piety as the force that splits mountains, the half-divine child who defies celestial law to rescue the imprisoned feminine, the axe as the instrument of liberation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hero who splits the mountain (consciousness breaking through the barrier) to rescue the imprisoned Great Mother, the filial son who defies the patriarchal uncle
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of the goddess Sanshengmu (Third Holy Mother) and a mortal scholar

nodes.name: Tianhuang Emperor
nodes.domain: primordial kingship, the earliest age, cosmic rulership
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: one of the primordial emperors of the earliest age of creation
nodes.significantEvent: ruled during the earliest period of creation, established the first cosmic order before the Five Emperors
nodes.symbolism: the primordial sovereignty that established the cosmic template for all subsequent rule
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial patriarch of the earliest age, the first expression of sovereign consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the legendary Three August Ones (Sanhuang) who ruled in the primordial age

nodes.name: Yuanshi Tianzun
nodes.domain: creation, supreme Daoism, the primordial beginning
nodes.object: ruyi scepter, three-jeweled jade scepter, pangu banner
nodes.characterTrait: supreme, primordial, originating, first of the Three Pure Ones
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the most exalted of the Three Pure Ones, depicted as a serene sage holding a jade scepter and emanating primordial light
nodes.significantEvent: rules the highest heaven (Jade Clarity Realm), in the Fengshen Yanyi he is the master of the Chan sect (Sect of Elucidation), teacher of the Twelve Golden Immortals including Nezhas master Taiyi Zhenren
nodes.symbolism: the primordial beginning of all existence, the first emanation of the Dao, the supreme Daoist consciousness before any differentiation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the supreme primordial father, the first differentiation of consciousness from the undifferentiated Dao
nodes.birthCircumstances: first of the Three Pure Ones (Sanqing), the Celestial Worthy of Primordial Beginning, the highest deity in Daoism

nodes.name: Banebdjedet
nodes.domain: fertility, virility, rams, Mendes, the ba-soul
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: ram god or ram-headed man wearing the atef crown, the sacred ram of Mendes
nodes.significantEvent: the sacred ram of Mendes was worshipped as an incarnation of the ba (soul) of Osiris, later associated with all four major gods (Ra, Osiris, Shu, and Geb), Herodotus described his cult
nodes.symbolism: the ram as the supreme symbol of male fertility, the living ram as the incarnation of the divine soul, the ba-soul made visible in animal form
nodes.neumannArchetype: the phallic Great Father in his theriomorphic ram form, the masculine generative principle incarnated in the sacred animal
nodes.birthCircumstances: the Great Ram of Mendes, lord of Djedet (Mendes) in the Nile Delta

nodes.name: Kolanthes
nodes.domain: healing, Greco-Egyptian religion, medicine
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Greco-Egyptian healing deity
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped during the Ptolemaic and Roman periods as a healing deity combining Egyptian and Greek medical traditions
nodes.symbolism: the meeting of Egyptian and Greek healing traditions in a single divine figure
nodes.neumannArchetype: the syncretic healing masculine, the physician consciousness that bridges cultures
nodes.birthCircumstances: Kolanthes was identified with Horus, the divine child and the Pharaoh, and he was called "the child of Osiris and Isis".
