nodes.name: Unut
nodes.domain: hares, speed, protection, Hermopolis
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: hare goddess or woman with a hare head, associated with swiftness and fertility
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped at Hermopolis as a hare goddess, later merged with other goddesses, the hare was associated with fertility and the moon
nodes.symbolism: the hare as the swift and fertile animal of the moon, speed as a divine quality, the hare-goddess as the swift protectress
nodes.neumannArchetype: the swift Great Mother in her hare form, the lunar feminine of fertility and speed

nodes.name: Semele
nodes.domain: earth, motherhood, divine epiphany, death through divine encounter
nodes.characterTrait: beautiful, mortal, trusting, doomed by divine love
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful Theban princess, mortal beloved of Zeus
nodes.significantEvent: tricked by Hera into asking Zeus to reveal himself in his true divine form, consumed by his thunderbolt, the unborn Dionysus was rescued from her womb and sewn into Zeus thigh, later rescued from the underworld by Dionysus and made immortal as Thyone
nodes.symbolism: the mortal who is destroyed by encountering the divine directly, the mother of the god who dies to give birth, later redeemed by her own divine son
nodes.neumannArchetype: the mortal vessel of the divine child who is destroyed by the full power of the sky father, later rescued from death by the son she bore
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Cadmus and Harmonia, princess of Thebes

nodes.name: Machai
nodes.domain: battles, combat
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: spirits of battle, personifications of individual combats within a larger battle
nodes.significantEvent: the individual fights that make up a battle personified as swarming spirits
nodes.symbolism: the atomization of warfare into individual combats, battle as composed of countless smaller struggles
nodes.neumannArchetype: the fragmenting aspect of the war daimons, consciousness dissolved into multiple violent encounters
nodes.birthCircumstances: offspring of Eris (Strife)

nodes.name: Budai
nodes.domain: contentment, abundance, happiness, the future Buddha
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: fat laughing monk with an exposed belly carrying a cloth sack, bald with large earlobes
nodes.significantEvent: wandered as an eccentric monk giving candy and small gifts to children from his cloth sack, before dying he recited a verse revealing himself as Maitreya, became the Laughing Buddha of Chinese temples
nodes.symbolism: contentment and abundance found in simplicity, the sacred fool whose laughter reveals enlightenment, the fat belly as a symbol of spiritual fullness rather than physical greed
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child as the laughing sage, enlightenment expressed through joy and generosity rather than austerity
nodes.birthCircumstances: based on a 10th-century Chinese Chan Buddhist monk named Qici, identified as an incarnation of Maitreya the future Buddha

nodes.name: Lu Ban
nodes.domain: carpentry, engineering, craftsmanship, architecture, invention
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: patron saint of carpenters and craftsmen, depicted holding woodworking tools
nodes.significantEvent: invented the saw, the plane, the grindstone, the ink marking line, and numerous other tools, created mechanical birds that could fly and a wooden horse-carriage that moved by itself, became the patron deity of all craftsmen and builders
nodes.symbolism: human ingenuity as a divine quality, the craftsman elevated to godhood through mastery of his art, tools as the extensions of human creative intelligence
nodes.neumannArchetype: the supreme culture hero of craft, the masculine creative intelligence that transforms raw material into civilization through tools
nodes.birthCircumstances: historical figure, master craftsman of the State of Lu during the Spring and Autumn Period (507-444 BCE)

nodes.name: Tongtian Jiaozhu
nodes.domain: Daoism, primordial creation, opposition, the Investiture of the Gods
nodes.object: sword of immortal-killing, four swords of Zhu Xian
nodes.characterTrait: powerful, opposing, master of formation, proud
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: powerful Daoist master who controls the deadly Zhu Xian sword formation, one of the three disciples of Hongjun Laozu
nodes.significantEvent: led his disciples of the Jie sect against Jiang Ziya and the Zhou in the Investiture of the Gods, his Zhu Xian sword formation was one of the most powerful weapons in Daoist mythology, ultimately defeated and converted to Buddhism
nodes.symbolism: the opposition within the spiritual tradition, the master whose power serves the wrong cause, the conversion from Daoism to Buddhism as cosmic destiny
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow master whose spiritual power opposes the hero, the dark brother of the patriarchal tradition who must be overcome and transformed
nodes.birthCircumstances: master of the Jie sect (Sect of Interception), the third disciple of the primordial sage Hongjun Laozu
nodes.deathCircumstances: As a result, many of Tongtian Jiaozhu's disciples were killed by Chan’s disciples.

nodes.name: Yue Fei
nodes.domain: patriotism, loyalty, war, martial arts, righteous defeat
nodes.animals: eagle, horse, swan, bear, rooster, crane, monkey, elephant, tiger
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Song Dynasty general known for his brilliant martial ability and fierce patriotism, had the characters serve the country with utmost loyalty tattooed on his back by his mother
nodes.significantEvent: successfully fought back the Jurchen Jin invasion of southern China, was recalled on false charges by the traitorous chancellor Qin Hui, imprisoned and executed on fabricated evidence despite his victories, later exonerated and elevated to the highest military honors
nodes.symbolism: the supreme patriotic hero destroyed by corruption within his own government, loyalty tattooed on the body by the mother, the righteous general betrayed by the treacherous civilian, the eternal model of selfless patriotism
nodes.neumannArchetype: the supreme positive warrior destroyed by the shadow within his own patriarchal order, the hero whose mothers inscription (the anima) defines his destiny
nodes.birthCircumstances: Song Dynasty general (1103-1142 CE), one of the most celebrated military heroes in Chinese history
nodes.deathCircumstances: Because of his warlike stance, he was put to death by the Southern Song government in 1142 under a frameup, after a negotiated peace was achieved with the Jin dynasty.

nodes.name: Harsomtus
nodes.domain: divine union, the sun, the falcon, Edfu
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: falcon or falcon-headed youth representing the union of Horus and other deities
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped at the temple of Edfu as the son of the divine marriage of Horus and Hathor, represented the daily renewal of the sun and the unity of Upper and Lower Egypt
nodes.symbolism: the divine child born from the sacred marriage, the solar unity of the two lands, the falcon as the renewed sun
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child born from the hieros gamos (sacred marriage), the renewed consciousness emerging from the union of the divine parents
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Hathor and Horus at Edfu, the divine child of their sacred marriage

nodes.name: Oizys
nodes.domain: misery, woe, distress, suffering
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: spirit of misery and suffering
nodes.significantEvent: the personification of woe and suffering that afflicts humanity, one of the evils from Pandoras jar
nodes.symbolism: misery as a cosmic force, suffering as a divine affliction rather than mere accident, the weight of existence
nodes.neumannArchetype: the dark feminine of suffering, the Great Mothers withholding aspect experienced as existential pain
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Nyx alone, or twin sister of Momus

nodes.name: Pheme
nodes.domain: fame, rumor, report, reputation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: winged goddess covered with eyes, ears, and tongues, growing larger as she travels
nodes.significantEvent: spreads news and rumor throughout the world growing larger with each retelling, neither truth nor falsehood but an indiscriminate mix, announced Didos affair with Aeneas throughout Africa
nodes.symbolism: the uncontrollable nature of rumor, fame as a monster that grows with each telling, the indistinguishability of truth and falsehood in public discourse
nodes.neumannArchetype: the archetypal spread of consciousness through collective communication, the positive and negative aspects of shared knowledge
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Gaia (Earth) according to Virgil

nodes.name: Potnia Theron
nodes.domain: wild animals, hunting, nature, the wilderness
nodes.characterTrait: wild, sovereign over beasts, nurturing of animals, ancient
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess flanked by wild animals, often lions or deer, sometimes winged, grasping animals in both hands
nodes.significantEvent: depicted on Minoan seals and pottery from the earliest periods, Homer uses the title for Artemis, represents the most ancient layer of the hunting goddess
nodes.symbolism: the divine mistress of the animal world, the feminine as sovereign over wild nature, the goddess who both nurtures and hunts the beasts
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother in her most ancient theriomorphic aspect, the Lady of the Beasts who rules all animal nature

nodes.domain: the north wind, Mictlantecuhtli, the northern direction, cold, death
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the North Wind, associated with Mictlantecuhtli and the northern direction of death
nodes.significantEvent: one of the four directional wind deities, associated with the north and the death god Mictlantecuhtli
nodes.symbolism: the north wind as the cold breath of death, the icy wind from the direction of the underworld, the atmospheric breath of the death lord
nodes.neumannArchetype: the cold wind-consciousness of death, the atmospheric extension of the death-father from the north

nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine of repair and restoration, the Great Mothers mending of the torn

nodes.domain: sight, light, precious metals, brilliance, the shining sky
nodes.characterTrait: luminous, precious, ancient, generative of light

nodes.significantEvent: married her brother Hyperion and bore Helios (Sun), Selene (Moon), and Eos (Dawn), the three sources of earthly light
nodes.symbolism: the divine light that makes precious things shine, the origin of all celestial luminosity, the Titaness whose children illuminate the world
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother in her luminous aspect, the feminine origin of all light and sight in the cosmos
nodes.birthCircumstances: eldest daughter of Uranus (Sky) and Gaia (Earth), one of the twelve Titans

nodes.domain: child-rearing, nursing, protection of children
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess or epithet for deities who protect children

nodes.neumannArchetype: the nurturing feminine collective that raises the divine child on the sacred mountain, the Great Mothers multiple aspects as nurses

nodes.domain: wine, olive, grain, agriculture, miraculous transformation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: three sisters with the divine gift of transforming earth into food and drink

nodes.neumannArchetype: the triple feminine as the transformative power that turns raw nature into the three pillars of Mediterranean civilization
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughters of King Anius of Delos, granted their powers by Dionysus

nodes.domain: kingship, bee cult, healing, oracles
nodes.animals: serpent, bull, vulture, scarab, cow, cerberus
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: mythological king, sometimes associated with the sacred bull
nodes.significantEvent: legendary king of Argos, taught his people the art of government, killed by Aetolus in a chariot race
nodes.symbolism: the sacred king connected to both Greek and Egyptian royal traditions, the bull as symbol of sovereignty
nodes.neumannArchetype: the sacred king archetype, the ruler whose sovereignty is connected to the divine bull
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Phoroneus in Greek tradition, or associated with the Egyptian Apis bull
nodes.deathCircumstances: Initially, he was assigned a significant role in her worship, being sacrificed and reborn.

nodes.name: Aristaeus
nodes.domain: beekeeping, cheese-making, herding, olive cultivation, hunting
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: rustic god sometimes depicted as a winged young man
nodes.significantEvent: taught humanity beekeeping, cheese-making, and olive cultivation, pursued Eurydice leading to her death by snakebite, lost his bees as divine punishment and learned the Bugonia (ox-born bees) ritual to restore them
nodes.symbolism: the civilizing arts of pastoral life, the unintended consequences of desire, the death and regeneration of the bee colony as a mystery of nature
nodes.neumannArchetype: the culture hero who brings the pastoral arts to humanity, the positive masculine principle in harmony with nature
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Apollo and the huntress nymph Cyrene, raised by the Muses who taught him healing and prophecy

nodes.name: Asclepius
nodes.domain: healing, medicine, resurrection, snakes
nodes.characterTrait: wise, healing, compassionate, transgressive in resurrecting the dead
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: bearded, dignified, carrying the serpent-entwined staff of healing
nodes.significantEvent: became so skilled in healing he could raise the dead, struck down by Zeus thunderbolt for upsetting the natural order, after death honored as a god with major temples at Epidaurus and Cos
nodes.symbolism: healing as divine art, the serpent as symbol of renewal and regeneration, the boundary between life and death that medicine transgresses
nodes.neumannArchetype: the healing son of the solar god, wielding the snake-entwined staff that connects the worlds of life and death
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Apollo and the mortal Coronis, cut from his dying mothers womb by Apollo, raised by the centaur Chiron who taught him the art of medicine
nodes.deathCircumstances: Coronis was killed by Artemis for being unfaithful to Apollo and was laid out on a funeral pyre to be consumed, but Apollo rescued the child by cutting him from Coronis's womb.

nodes.name: Anytos
nodes.domain: vegetation, the underworld, Arcadian mysteries
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Titan or giant in Arcadian tradition, depicted in armor at Lycosura
nodes.significantEvent: raised the goddess Despoina on behalf of Demeter, his statue stood alongside Despoinas at the temple of Lycosura wearing armor
nodes.symbolism: the chthonic guardian who raises the divine child, the protective masculine within the Great Mothers mysteries
nodes.neumannArchetype: the nurturing Titan who serves the Great Mother by protecting her hidden daughter
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the Titans in Arcadian tradition

nodes.name: Mama
nodes.domain: creation of humanity, motherhood, midwifery (Akkadian)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Mother-goddess; standard mother-deity iconography.
nodes.significantEvent: The Akkadian counterpart of Sumerian Aruru/Ninhursag in the creation-of-humanity tradition. Upon completing the creation she takes the title Belet-ili 'Mistress of the gods'.
nodes.symbolism: Wise creatress; recites incantations of creation; variant of Aruru/Nintu
nodes.neumannArchetype: Wise creatress. 'Mama recited the incantation; when she completed...'
nodes.domain_source: Atrahasis I 189-end (Mami / Belet-ili summoned to create humans on Enki's instruction); Enuma Elish VI (parallel)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Atrahasis I 192-260
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard Akkadian mother-goddess iconography; Atrahasis I
nodes.characterTrait_source: Atrahasis I 192-260
nodes.object_source: Atrahasis I

nodes.name: Orbona
nodes.domain: orphans, bereaved parents, childlessness, loss
nodes.characterTrait: mourning, protective of orphans, loss-associated, compassionate
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess of bereaved parents and orphaned children, protectress of the parentless
nodes.significantEvent: invoked by parents who had lost their children and by orphans who had lost their parents, representing the divine compassion for the most vulnerable losses
nodes.symbolism: the divine feminine response to the loss of children, the goddess who accompanies the bereaved parent and the orphaned child, loss as a condition requiring divine feminine attention
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of loss, the feminine that accompanies consciousness through the most painful separation

nodes.name: Chronos
nodes.domain: time, eternity, the ages
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: old figure with grey beard, sometimes serpentine, distinct from Cronus the Titan
nodes.significantEvent: in Orphic cosmogony, entwines with Ananke around the cosmic egg, from which Phanes the first god is born
nodes.symbolism: time as the all-consuming force, the eternal cycle that creates and destroys, distinct from Cronus though often confused with him
nodes.neumannArchetype: the uroboric serpent of time encircling creation, the masculine counterpart to Necessity
nodes.birthCircumstances: self-generated primordial being in Orphic tradition, or equated with Cronus

nodes.symbolism: the torpor of inaction, sloth as a cosmic force opposing effort
nodes.neumannArchetype: the regressive pull back toward the uroboric state of unconsciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Aether and Gaia

nodes.domain: good fortune, vineyards, grain, household protection
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: serpent form or young man with cornucopia, associated with household shrines
nodes.significantEvent: received a libation of unmixed wine at the end of every meal in Athenian households, closely associated with the Agathe Tyche (Good Fortune)
nodes.symbolism: the beneficent spirit protecting the household and harvest, the serpent as guardian of prosperity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive masculine spirit of fortune and protection at the domestic level

nodes.name: Rangda
nodes.domain: death, black magic, chaos, witchcraft
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: long hair, fanged, bulging eyes, long tongue, pendulous breasts, clawed
nodes.significantEvent: Balinese witch representing the Terrible Mother
nodes.symbolism: Balinese Terrible Mother/witch archetype
nodes.neumannArchetype: Balinese witch representing the Terrible Mother archetype.

nodes.name: Feilian
nodes.domain: wind, storms, chaos, rebellion
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: wind god depicted as a winged deer with a serpents tail, or as a bird with a deers head
nodes.significantEvent: served Chiyou in the war against the Yellow Emperor, creating great winds and storms to confuse the Yellow Emperors army, defeated and subjugated by the Yellow Emperor
nodes.symbolism: the wild wind as chaos and rebellion, the storm that serves the rebel cause, untamed nature allied with the forces challenging cosmic order
nodes.neumannArchetype: the chaotic wind spirit aligned with the shadow warrior (Chiyou) against the established patriarchal consciousness

nodes.name: Bu Luotuo
nodes.domain: sky, water, storms, kingship, creation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: creator deity associated with storms and celestial authority
nodes.significantEvent: a creation deity in some Chinese traditions associated with ordering the sky and waters
nodes.symbolism: the storm as creative power, the ordering of sky and water as the foundation of the cosmos
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine sky father who orders the primordial waters through storm power

nodes.name: Kikurihime-no-Kami
nodes.domain: mediation, the boundary between life and death, Izanagi and Izanami, reconciliation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess who mediated between Izanagi and Izanami at the boundary between the worlds of the living and dead
nodes.significantEvent: at the moment when Izanagi and Izanami confronted each other at the border between the land of the living and Yomi (the land of the dead), Kikurihime mediated between them, her words are lost but she resolved the cosmic divorce
nodes.symbolism: the mediator at the boundary of life and death, the feminine voice that negotiates between the separated cosmic parents, the words spoken at the border that resolve the primal divorce
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine mediator between the Great Mother (Izanami in death) and the Great Father (Izanagi in life), the anima that bridges the gap between consciousness and the unconscious

nodes.physicalCharacteristics: martial deity in military attire

nodes.symbolism: righteous martial power in service of the community
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive protective masculine, the warrior in service of justice

nodes.neumannArchetype: the localized patriarch of the Daoist tradition in diaspora

nodes.name: Aletheia
nodes.domain: truth, sincerity, honesty
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: depicted as a naked woman representing truth unadorned
nodes.significantEvent: Plutarch describes her as the nurturer of Apollo, according to philosophical tradition she hides at the bottom of a well
nodes.symbolism: truth as naked and unadorned, the divine quality of sincerity, truth concealed from most mortals
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine as the ground of truth, the light of consciousness as honesty
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Zeus according to Pindar

nodes.name: Maron
nodes.domain: wine, Dionysiac companionship, Thrace
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: old priest or companion of Dionysus
nodes.significantEvent: companion of Dionysus who taught viticulture to the people of Thrace, associated with the finest wines, possibly the first to mix wine with water
nodes.symbolism: the priestly tradition of winemaking, the old companion who carries the gods wisdom of the vine
nodes.neumannArchetype: the silenic wise man of the Dionysiac circle, the priestly masculine who mediates between the wine god and humanity
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Silenus, or son of Dionysus himself

nodes.name: Caishen
nodes.domain: wealth, prosperity, fortune, commerce
nodes.object: gold ingot, ruyi scepter, treasure bowl
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: richly dressed deity in official robes, sometimes riding a black tiger, carrying a golden rod
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped especially during Chinese New Year when merchants and families pray for prosperity in the coming year, offerings of incense and food are made to attract his favor
nodes.symbolism: divine wealth as reward for virtue, prosperity as a gift of heaven, the impartial distribution of fortune, the New Year renewal of economic hope
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive father archetype as the generous dispenser of material abundance, the benevolent patriarch of prosperity
nodes.birthCircumstances: multiple figures identified as Caishen including Bi Gan and Zhao Gongming
nodes.deathCircumstances: After Bi Gan was put to death by his nephew King Zhou of Shang, Bi Gan's wife and son escaped into the woods.

nodes.name: Cihang Zhenren
nodes.domain: compassion, mercy, salvation, Buddhism, water
nodes.object: willow branch, vase of pure water
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Daoist immortal who is a manifestation of Guanyin (Avalokitesvara)
nodes.significantEvent: left Daoism to become a Buddhist, identified with Guanyin Bodhisattva, saved many during the Investiture of the Gods narrative
nodes.symbolism: the transition from Daoist to Buddhist practice, compassion as the highest spiritual attainment, the saving power of mercy
nodes.neumannArchetype: the anima figure as the merciful savior, the feminine principle of compassion that transcends sectarian boundaries
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the Twelve Golden Immortals of the Kunlun Mountains in Fengshen Yanyi

nodes.name: Angelos
nodes.domain: underworld, the moon, Hecate
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: became an underworld goddess after her transgression
nodes.significantEvent: stole her mother Heras anointments and gave them to Europa, fled to a childbed woman then a corpse procession, purified by the Cabiri and taken to the underworld
nodes.symbolism: the divine daughter who transgresses and is cast down, theft of divine beauty leading to underworld exile
nodes.neumannArchetype: the fallen daughter of the Great Mother who descends to the underworld through transgression
nodes.birthCircumstances: In Greek mythology, Angelos () or Angelia (Ἀγγελία) was a daughter of Zeus and Hera.

nodes.name: Meilichios
nodes.domain: propitiation, appeasement, the gentle side of Zeus, honey
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Zeus in his gentle and propitious aspect, often depicted as a kindly bearded figure
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped throughout Greece as Zeus Meilichios (the Kindly), received offerings of honey cakes rather than blood sacrifice, often depicted as a great serpent
nodes.symbolism: the terrifying god made gentle through propitiation, divine wrath transformed into kindness, the serpent form of the sky god connecting him to the chthonic
nodes.neumannArchetype: the sky father in his chthonic-benevolent form, the terrible masculine made gentle through the sweetness of the Great Mothers offering (honey)

nodes.name: Cangdi
nodes.domain: water, the north, winter, the Azure Emperor, the Green Emperor
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: one of the five directional deities of Chinese cosmology
nodes.significantEvent: rules over the eastern direction or associated with water and the north in some cosmological schemes, one of the Wufang Shangdi (Five Forms of the Highest Deity)
nodes.symbolism: the elemental order of Chinese cosmology, the directional deities as aspects of the supreme cosmic order
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine ordering of the cosmos through directional and elemental principles
nodes.birthCircumstances: In Daoism, it is often said that he is the grandson of the Jade Emperor.

nodes.name: Ma Chao
nodes.domain: war, horsemanship, the Qiang people, loyalty
nodes.characterTrait: fierce, independent, proud, terrifying in battle
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: one of the Five Tiger Generals of Shu Han, known for his extraordinary horsemanship and ferocity
nodes.significantEvent: known as Ma the Splendid, terrified Cao Cao so much that Cao cut his beard and threw away his robe to flee, later surrendered to Liu Bei and became one of the Five Tiger Generals
nodes.symbolism: the western warrior whose ferocity terrifies even the most powerful warlord, the Qiang horseman as the embodiment of frontier martial spirit
nodes.neumannArchetype: the fierce shadow warrior whose terrifying appearance embodies the untamed martial masculine
nodes.birthCircumstances: general of Shu Han during the Three Kingdoms period, of Qiang descent

nodes.name: Yŏn Kaesomun
nodes.domain: war, resistance, Korean-Chinese relations, Goguryeo
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: powerful military dictator of Goguryeo
nodes.significantEvent: effectively controlled Goguryeo as its military dictator, successfully resisted multiple invasions by Tang Dynasty China, his resistance preserved Korean independence for decades
nodes.symbolism: the military strongman who preserves independence through force, resistance to the great empires advance, the general who becomes the de facto ruler
nodes.neumannArchetype: the martial masculine who preserves the autonomy of consciousness against overwhelming external force
nodes.birthCircumstances: military dictator of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo (603-666 CE)

nodes.name: Taweret
nodes.domain: pregnancy, childbirth, fertility, protection of women and children
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: standing female hippopotamus with pendulous human breasts, the paws of a lion, and the back of a crocodile, leaning on a sa sign of protection
nodes.significantEvent: one of the most commonly depicted household deities, her image was placed on beds and headrests to protect during sleep and childbirth, together with Bes she guarded the most vulnerable moments of human life
nodes.symbolism: the hippopotamus as the fierce protector of her young, the hybrid form combining the most powerful animal qualities in defense of mother and child, the sa sign as the mark of protective magic
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible-good Great Mother in her most direct expression, the fierce animal-mother who protects the birth process with overwhelming physical power
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient goddess of pregnant women and childbirth

nodes.name: Kothar-wa-Khasis
nodes.domain: craftsmanship, metalworking, building, the Near East
nodes.characterTrait: crafting, skilled, divine artisan, Near Eastern
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Near Eastern craftsman god, the divine smith and builder from Ugaritic mythology adopted into Egyptian tradition
nodes.significantEvent: the divine craftsman who built the palace of Baal in Ugaritic mythology, his skills were recognized in the broader Near Eastern world including Egypt
nodes.symbolism: the divine artisan whose craft creates the dwelling places of the gods, the smith as the supreme creative profession, Near Eastern craftsmanship as a divine attribute
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father as the divine artisan, the masculine consciousness that shapes the material world through craft
nodes.birthCircumstances: Ugaritic craftsman god (Kothar-wa-Khasis, the Skillful and Wise One)

nodes.name: Two Ladies
nodes.domain: protection, Upper and Lower Egypt, royalty, duality, the pharaohs crown
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the paired cobra (Wadjet of Lower Egypt) and vulture (Nekhbet of Upper Egypt) on the pharaohs crown, the two divine protectresses of unified Egypt
nodes.significantEvent: the Two Ladies (Nebty) were part of the pharaohs royal titulary, their presence on the crown symbolized the protection of both Upper and Lower Egypt and the unity of the two lands under one ruler
nodes.symbolism: the duality of Upper and Lower Egypt unified under one crown, the cobra and vulture as the two modes of feminine protection (striking and sheltering), the Two Ladies as the divine guarantee of national unity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the dual Great Mother protecting the patriarchal ruler from both directions, the feminine duality that guards the unity of the kingdom
nodes.birthCircumstances: [to the] King of Upper and Lower Egypt, Nebmaatra, heir of Ra, Son of Ra, [Amenhotep, ruler of Thebes].

nodes.name: Pax
nodes.domain: peace, prosperity, the absence of war, civilization
nodes.object: olive branch, cornucopia, caduceus, torch (burning weapons)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: serene woman holding an olive branch and cornucopia, sometimes shown burning weapons
nodes.significantEvent: the Ara Pacis (Altar of Peace) built by Augustus in 9 BCE is one of the greatest monuments of Roman art, her temple was built by Vespasian after the civil wars to celebrate the return of peace to Rome
nodes.symbolism: peace as the burning of weapons, the olive branch as the universal sign of peace, the cornucopia as the abundance that peace brings, the Pax Romana as the golden age of civilization
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of civilization, the feminine peace that allows the fruits of consciousness to ripen
nodes.birthCircumstances: personification of peace, identified with the Greek Eirene

nodes.name: Astraeus
nodes.domain: stars, planets, astrology, dusk
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Titan of the dusk, father of the stars and winds
nodes.significantEvent: married the dawn goddess Eos and fathered the four Winds (Boreas, Notus, Euros, Zephyrus) and the five Wandering Stars (planets)
nodes.symbolism: the dusk that gives birth to the stars, the union of twilight and dawn producing all celestial phenomena
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine twilight principle whose union with the feminine dawn generates the visible cosmos
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of the Titans Crius and Eurybia

nodes.name: Melicertes
nodes.domain: the sea, harbors, protection of sailors, transformation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: young sea god, often depicted riding a dolphin
nodes.significantEvent: when his mother Ino went mad and jumped into the sea with him, he was transformed into the sea god Palaemon, worshipped as protector of harbors and sailors, the Isthmian Games were said to be founded in his honor
nodes.symbolism: the child transformed by drowning into a marine protector, death by water as divine transformation, the harbor god born from a mothers madness
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child reborn through the waters of the Great Mother, death-and-rebirth through immersion in the oceanic unconscious
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Ino (Leucothea) and Athamas, originally named Melicertes

nodes.name: Che Kung
nodes.domain: protection, healing, fortune, martial arts
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: armored warrior deity carrying a halberd
nodes.significantEvent: famous for suppressing a plague in southern China, temples dedicated to him are visited during Chinese New Year for fortune divination using a fan-wheel
nodes.symbolism: martial power directed toward healing and protection, the general who defeats plague as he would defeat an army, the New Year oracle of fortune
nodes.neumannArchetype: the protective warrior-healer, the masculine that combats disease as an enemy to be vanquished
nodes.birthCircumstances: deified Song Dynasty general Che Kung (also known as Che Daliangshou)

nodes.name: Ma Wu
nodes.domain: war, loyalty, the Eastern Han restoration
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: powerful Eastern Han general known for his fierce loyalty and combat prowess
nodes.significantEvent: one of the Cloud Terrace Twenty-Eight Generals who helped Emperor Guangwu restore the Han Dynasty, known for his personal bravery in battle
nodes.symbolism: the loyal warrior whose personal combat prowess helps restore the rightful dynasty
nodes.neumannArchetype: the loyal warrior masculine in service to the restoration of the patriarchal order
nodes.birthCircumstances: general who served Emperor Guangwu in restoring the Han Dynasty

nodes.name: Zhang Fei
nodes.domain: war, brotherhood, righteousness, ferocity, butchery
nodes.object: serpent spear (zhang ba she mao), wine
nodes.characterTrait: fierce, loyal, impetuous, hot-tempered, brave, loud
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: giant warrior with a thunderous voice and bristling beard, known for his terrifying battle roar that could freeze armies in their tracks
nodes.significantEvent: his roar at Changban Bridge made an entire army retreat, fought countless battles for Shu Han, murdered in his sleep by two subordinates he had punished, one of the Five Tiger Generals
nodes.symbolism: ferocity and loyalty as inseparable qualities, the thunderous voice as a weapon, the butcher who becomes a warrior-god, the hot temper that is both his greatest strength and his downfall
nodes.neumannArchetype: the impetuous shadow-brother of the hero, the uncontrolled masculine whose ferocity serves the righteous cause but whose temper ultimately destroys him
nodes.birthCircumstances: a butcher from Zhuo Commandery, sworn brother of Liu Bei and Guan Yu in the Peach Garden Oath

nodes.name: Seshat
nodes.domain: writing, measurement, architecture, mathematics, records, the stars
nodes.object: writing palette, notched palm rib, star on head
nodes.characterTrait: measuring, recording, precise, stellar, intellectual, feminine wisdom
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman wearing a leopard skin and a seven-pointed star or flower on her head, holding a notched palm rib (for counting years) and writing implements
nodes.significantEvent: recorded the years of the pharaohs reign on the sacred persea tree, calculated the foundations of temples through the stretching of the cord ceremony, the divine librarian who recorded all knowledge in the House of Life
nodes.symbolism: the feminine principle of measurement and record, the star on the head as the celestial origin of knowledge, the notched palm rib as the count of time, the stretching of the cord as sacred geometry
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the keeper of knowledge and the measurer of time, the feminine intellectual counterpart to the masculine Thoth
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the oldest Egyptian deities, the feminine counterpart of Thoth

nodes.name: Mehen
nodes.domain: protection, the sun, serpents, the solar barque, coiling
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: enormous coiled serpent who encircled the sun god Ra in the solar barque, forming a protective barrier
nodes.significantEvent: protected Ra during his nightly journey through the underworld by coiling around him in the solar barque, his coils formed an impenetrable shield against the forces of chaos, especially the serpent Apophis
nodes.symbolism: the protective serpent encircling the sun, coiling as a defensive act, the serpent that protects against other serpents, the solar barque as the vessel of consciousness protected by the coiled instinct
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive serpent of the unconscious that protects the solar consciousness (Ra) from the destructive serpent (Apophis), the tamed uroboric power in service of awareness

nodes.name: Wepset
nodes.domain: fire, protection, the uraeus, the pharaoh, burning
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: fire-spitting cobra goddess who burns the enemies of the pharaoh
nodes.significantEvent: the flame-spitting uraeus on the pharaohs brow, she destroyed the pharaohs enemies with her fiery breath
nodes.symbolism: the concentrated fire of divine protection, the cobra whose flame guards the crown, burning as the ultimate defense of sovereignty
nodes.neumannArchetype: the fiery feminine on the brow of the Great Father, the concentrated defensive fire of the anima

nodes.name: Salus
nodes.domain: health, safety, welfare, the state, salvation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman feeding a serpent from a patera (offering bowl), wearing a crown, personification of health and safety
nodes.significantEvent: her temple on the Quirinal Hill was one of the most important in Rome, she represented not just physical health but the welfare of the entire state (Salus Publica Populi Romani), her image appeared on coins as a guarantee of public welfare
nodes.symbolism: the serpent fed from the patera as health maintained through careful attention, public health as a divine feminine concern, the welfare of the state as the mothers care for her children
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the healer and nurturer of the collective, the feminine principle of public welfare
nodes.birthCircumstances: personification of health, safety, and welfare, identified with the Greek Hygieia

nodes.name: Crius
nodes.domain: constellations, the heavenly order, rams
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: one of the elder Titans, sometimes associated with the constellation Aries
nodes.significantEvent: married Eurybia and fathered Astraeus, Pallas, and Perses, imprisoned in Tartarus after the Titanomachy
nodes.symbolism: the ordering of the heavens into constellations, the ram as celestial symbol
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Titan principle of celestial structure, the masculine ordering of the night sky
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Uranus and Gaia, one of the twelve Titans

nodes.name: Chitou Furen
nodes.domain: fertility, childbirth, women, silk
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess of fertility and childbirth
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped by women seeking children and safe childbirth, associated with the protection of women and silk production
nodes.symbolism: feminine fertility and creativity, the divine protection of childbirth, silk as the feminine transformative art
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother in her nurturing and creative aspect, the feminine that both generates life and transforms raw material (silk)
nodes.deathCircumstances: Therefore, the surviving family members of women who died in childbirth would also worship Lady of the Pool, praying that their deceased relatives would be spared suffering in the Blood Pool.

nodes.name: Ma Yuan
nodes.domain: war, pacification, the southern frontier, Vietnam
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: famous Eastern Han general and conqueror
nodes.significantEvent: pacified the southern frontier including Vietnam, erected a bronze pillar marking the boundary of Han territory, became a controversial figure representing both Chinese military achievement and Vietnamese resistance
nodes.symbolism: the conqueror who marks the boundary of civilization with a bronze pillar, the frontier general whose legacy is viewed differently by conqueror and conquered
nodes.neumannArchetype: the patriarchal masculine extending the boundaries of the cosmic order, the ambiguous hero of the frontier
nodes.birthCircumstances: Eastern Han Dynasty general (14 BCE-49 CE)

nodes.name: Zhang Guolao
nodes.domain: immortality, Daoism, the Eight Immortals, reversal, old age
nodes.object: paper donkey, bamboo tube drum, wine gourd, peach of longevity
nodes.animals: donkey (paper donkey that comes to life)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: old man who rides his donkey backwards, one of the Eight Immortals, carries a bamboo tube drum
nodes.significantEvent: rides a magical paper donkey that he folds up and puts in his pocket, always depicted riding backwards symbolizing his rejection of conventional wisdom, performs miraculous healings and transformations
nodes.symbolism: riding backwards as seeing the past clearly while moving into the future, the reversal of ordinary perspective as the key to wisdom, the paper donkey as the illusory nature of the material world, eccentricity as the sign of true understanding
nodes.neumannArchetype: the trickster-sage who reverses all conventions, the old man whose backward riding represents the reversal of ego-consciousness into transpersonal awareness
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the Eight Immortals, historically based on a Tang Dynasty Daoist hermit

nodes.name: Serket
nodes.domain: scorpions, healing, protection, magic, venom
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman with a scorpion on her head, or as a scorpion with a womans head, arms sometimes outstretched in protection
nodes.significantEvent: protected the canopic jars containing the organs of the dead, guarded the pharaoh from poisonous creatures, her priests were healers who specialized in treating scorpion stings and snake bites, protected Isis and baby Horus during their hiding from Set
nodes.symbolism: the scorpion as the guardian whose sting both kills and heals, venom as medicine, the dangerous creature transformed into the supreme protector, guarding the dead through the transition to eternal life
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother whose dangerous power (venom) is the source of both death and healing, the protective feminine whose sting defends the most sacred contents
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient scorpion goddess of healing and protection

nodes.name: Nemty
nodes.domain: ferrying, the river, protection, punishment, Upper Egypt
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: falcon deity or man associated with the ferrying of the dead and the protection of river crossings
nodes.significantEvent: the divine ferryman who transported souls across the river to the afterlife, also associated with the punishment of those who violated sacred law
nodes.symbolism: the ferry crossing as the transition between life and death, the river as the threshold between the worlds, the ferryman who can also punish
nodes.neumannArchetype: the psychopomp who ferries consciousness across the river from life to death, the masculine guide at the water-threshold
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient ferryman god of the 12th Upper Egyptian nome

nodes.domain: magic, protection, power, the uraeus, royalty
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: cobra goddess whose name means Great of Magic, depicted wearing a cobra or as a cobra herself
nodes.significantEvent: placed her divine power in the crowns of Egypt, her magic protected the pharaoh and gave the crowns their supernatural authority, she suckled the royal children
nodes.symbolism: the magic of the royal crowns as a feminine divine power, the cobra as the embodiment of magical authority, the crown itself as alive with divine feminine power
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of magic whose power inhabits the instruments of patriarchal authority (the crowns)

nodes.name: Roma
nodes.domain: the city of Rome, empire, civilization, sovereignty
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: helmeted woman seated on a throne or on a pile of weapons, holding a small statue of Victory and a spear, sometimes with a globe representing world dominion
nodes.significantEvent: the divine personification of Rome worshipped as Dea Roma (Goddess Roma), her temple in the Forum was built by Hadrian, she appeared on countless coins and monuments as the embodiment of Roman power and eternal civilization
nodes.symbolism: the eternal city as a goddess, the empire as a divine feminine body, the she-wolf as the nurturing mother of Romans, the globe as universal dominion, the seated Roma as the permanent foundation of civilization
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the city-state itself, the feminine body of civilization that contains and defines all Roman consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: personification of the city and empire of Rome itself

nodes.name: Morpheus
nodes.domain: dreams, sleep, prophecy through dreams, human form in dreams
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: winged being who takes any human form in dreams
nodes.significantEvent: in Ovids Metamorphoses he takes the form of the dead King Ceyx to appear to his wife Alcyone in a dream, conveying the truth of his shipwreck and death
nodes.symbolism: the power of dreams to reveal truth through illusion, the human form as the medium of divine communication in sleep
nodes.neumannArchetype: the animus of the dream world, the masculine form-giver within the feminine realm of sleep and the unconscious
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Hypnos (Sleep), or of Nyx

nodes.name: Mesembria
nodes.domain: noon, midday, the suns zenith
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Hora of noon and midday
nodes.significantEvent: presides over the hour of noon when the sun is at its peak
nodes.symbolism: the moment of maximum light, the zenith of consciousness and energy in the daily cycle
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine of maximum solar consciousness, noon as the peak of awareness

nodes.name: Mahamayuri
nodes.domain: protection, Buddhism, peacocks, purification
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Buddhist deity seated on a peacock, with multiple arms holding various implements of purification
nodes.significantEvent: the Peacock Wisdom Queen who protects against poison, disease, and demonic influence through the power of mantra and purification, widely venerated in Chinese esoteric Buddhism
nodes.symbolism: the peacock as the transformer of poison into beauty, purification through wisdom rather than force, the beauty that emerges from transmuting evil
nodes.neumannArchetype: the transformative feminine who transmutes poison (the shadow) into beauty through wisdom
nodes.birthCircumstances: Buddhist deity derived from Indian Mahamayuri Vidyaraja

nodes.name: Zhang Xian
nodes.domain: archery, protection of children, fertility
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: divine archer who protects children
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped as a protector of children, his arrow wards off the Heavenly Dog star that threatens children, his image is displayed to protect newborns
nodes.symbolism: the divine archer whose arrow protects the most vulnerable, archery skill directed toward the defense of the young
nodes.neumannArchetype: the protective masculine archer whose weapon defends the divine child from celestial threats

nodes.name: Renenutet
nodes.domain: harvest, fertility, serpents, nursing, nourishment
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: cobra goddess or woman with a cobras head, often depicted in the fields at harvest time
nodes.significantEvent: protected the grain harvest and the threshing floor, nursed the young pharaoh at her breast, her image was placed in granaries to protect the stored grain, associated with the fate and fortune of individuals
nodes.symbolism: the cobra in the grain field as the protector of the harvest, the serpent as the guardian of earths fertility, nursing as the divine act of nourishing the future king
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the serpent of the earth who nurtures both the grain and the divine child, the chthonic feminine whose body is the source of all nourishment
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient serpent goddess of the harvest and fertility

nodes.name: Neper
nodes.domain: grain, agriculture, the harvest, nourishment, vegetation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: man made of grain or with grain stalks growing from his body, the personification of grain
nodes.significantEvent: represented the growth of grain from the earth, his body was the grain itself, offering grain to the gods was an offering of Nepers body, grain mummies (Osiris beds) were planted to show his resurrection
nodes.symbolism: the grain as the body of the god, eating bread as a divine sacrament, the death and resurrection of the grain as the model for human resurrection, agriculture as a sacred mystery
nodes.neumannArchetype: the dying and resurrecting vegetation god, the masculine principle that dies with the harvest and is reborn with the planting, the Great Father as the grain of consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: personification of the grain harvest, associated with Osiris as the dying and rising vegetation

nodes.name: Wosret
nodes.domain: war, Thebes, protection, the pharaoh
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: war goddess of Thebes, depicted as a woman holding a bow and arrows
nodes.significantEvent: one of the early war goddesses of Thebes who protected the pharaoh and the Theban state, her cult was absorbed by other goddesses over time
nodes.symbolism: the Theban war goddess whose bow defends the throne, the feminine warrior of the capital
nodes.neumannArchetype: the fierce feminine warrior who defends the patriarchal seat of power (Thebes)

nodes.name: Victoria
nodes.domain: victory, triumph, success, military glory
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful winged woman carrying a laurel wreath and palm branch, alighting on the prows of ships or on globes
nodes.significantEvent: her golden statue stood in the Curia (Senate house) and was the subject of the last great pagan-Christian controversy when the altar of Victory was removed, her image crowned triumphant generals, the most prominent symbol of Roman military success
nodes.symbolism: wings as the swiftness of divine favor, the laurel wreath as the crown of the victor, the palm branch as the eternal symbol of triumph, victory as a feminine gift bestowed upon the worthy masculine
nodes.neumannArchetype: the anima of triumph, the feminine that crowns the successful masculine enterprise with the wreath of achievement
nodes.birthCircumstances: identified with the Greek Nike, personification of victory

nodes.name: Empanda
nodes.domain: hospitality, open doors, feeding the hungry, generosity
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess of open doors and hospitality, her temple doors were always open to feed the hungry
nodes.significantEvent: her temple was always open and provided food to anyone who was hungry, representing the most basic form of Roman hospitality and generosity toward strangers
nodes.symbolism: the always-open door as the sign of unconditional hospitality, feeding the hungry as a divine act, generosity as the feminine virtue of the open threshold
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of hospitality, the feminine that opens the door and feeds all who come

nodes.name: Britomartis
nodes.domain: hunt, nature, fishing, mountains
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Cretan goddess of wild nature, sweet maiden
nodes.significantEvent: pursued by King Minos for nine months, leaped into the sea to escape and was caught in fishermens nets, became an immortal goddess honored by Artemis
nodes.symbolism: the sweet wildness of untamed nature, the maiden who chooses death over submission, the ancient Cretan face of the Great Goddess
nodes.neumannArchetype: paired with Dictynna as an aspect of the Great Goddess, the Cretan maiden-huntress predating classical Artemis
nodes.birthCircumstances: Cretan goddess, daughter of Zeus and Carme

nodes.name: Messene
nodes.domain: city founding, regional identity, the Peloponnese
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: heroine who gave her name to the region of Messenia
nodes.significantEvent: left Argos with her husband Polycaon and established the kingdom of Messenia in the southwestern Peloponnese, bringing the Eleusinian Mysteries to the region
nodes.symbolism: the princess who founds a new kingdom, the transmission of sacred mysteries to new lands, the feminine as the carrier of civilization
nodes.neumannArchetype: the founding heroine who carries the mysteries of the Great Mother to a new region
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of King Triopas of Argos, wife of Polycaon

nodes.name: City God
nodes.domain: urban protection, civic order, the afterlife, local governance
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: deity in the robes of a government official, specific to each city
nodes.significantEvent: each major Chinese city has its own City God (Chenghuang) who protects the city and judges the souls of the dead within his jurisdiction, temples serve as spiritual courts
nodes.symbolism: the extension of bureaucratic governance into the spiritual realm, divine justice mirroring earthly administration, the locally specific face of cosmic order
nodes.neumannArchetype: the localized father archetype as judge and protector, the divine official who maintains order in both the living and dead communities
nodes.birthCircumstances: usually a deified local hero or righteous official appointed by the Jade Emperor to protect a specific city

nodes.name: Marshal Tianpeng
nodes.domain: war, the heavenly army, the north, waters, command
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: commanding marshal of the heavenly armies, a fearsome warrior
nodes.significantEvent: in Journey to the West he is the celestial identity of Zhu Bajie (Pigsy) before his exile to earth for drunkenly harassing the moon goddess Chang E, banished to be reborn as a pig-man
nodes.symbolism: the fall from celestial grace through lust, the heavenly warrior brought low by desire, the long path of redemption through the journey west
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine shadow (lust, appetite) that causes the fall from consciousness, the celestial warrior exiled to the animal realm who must redeem himself through service
nodes.birthCircumstances: celestial marshal of the Northern Dipper, one of the highest-ranking celestial generals

nodes.name: Zhang Xun
nodes.domain: loyalty, martyrdom, siege defense, the Tang Dynasty
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Tang Dynasty general and defender
nodes.significantEvent: defended Suiyang against the An Lushan Rebellion with extreme determination, when food ran out he killed his own concubine to feed the troops, held the city long enough to save the south of China, worshipped as a god of loyalty
nodes.symbolism: the extreme sacrifice of siege warfare, loyalty that reaches its most terrible extreme, the defender who preserves the empire through unthinkable personal sacrifice
nodes.neumannArchetype: the patriarchal hero whose loyalty reaches the most extreme expression of sacrifice, the masculine that consumes the feminine (concubine) to preserve the larger order
nodes.birthCircumstances: Tang Dynasty military officer (709-757 CE)
nodes.deathCircumstances: " After Zhang arrived at Zhenyuan, he executed Hua for his abuse of power but pardoned Hua's associates, who were able to correct their ways.

nodes.name: Meskhenet
nodes.domain: childbirth, destiny, fate, the birth-brick
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman wearing a birth-brick headdress or depicted as the birth-brick itself personified
nodes.significantEvent: present at every birth in Egypt, she determined the destiny and fortune of the newborn child the moment it was born, the birth-brick upon which Egyptian women squatted during delivery was her sacred symbol
nodes.symbolism: the birth-brick as the threshold between non-existence and life, the moment of birth as the moment of fate, the goddess who speaks the destiny of each child at its first breath
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the determiner of fate at the threshold of birth, the feminine that assigns destiny at the moment consciousness enters the world
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient goddess present at every birth, determining the fate of the newborn

nodes.name: Medjed
nodes.domain: the underworld, the Book of the Dead, obscurity, strange beings
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: mysterious deity mentioned in the Book of the Dead, depicted as a strange being with a round body and protruding legs
nodes.significantEvent: mentioned in the Book of the Dead as an underworld being who could fire rays from his eyes to destroy the enemies of the dead, despite his obscurity he gained modern popularity in Japan after the Book of the Dead was exhibited
nodes.symbolism: the obscure underworld power whose rays destroy evil, the strange and mysterious beings that populate the Egyptian afterlife
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hidden shadow-being of the unconscious whose obscure power serves the dead

nodes.name: Tjenenyet
nodes.domain: brewing, beer, nourishment, Montu, Armant
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess associated with beer and brewing at Armant, consort of Montu
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped at Armant alongside the war god Montu as his consort, associated with the nurturing aspects of beer which was a staple food in ancient Egypt
nodes.symbolism: beer as divine nourishment, the feminine provider of sustenance to the war god, brewing as a sacred feminine art
nodes.neumannArchetype: the nourishing Great Mother who provides sustenance (beer) to the masculine warrior (Montu)
nodes.birthCircumstances: The goddess Tjenenyet is referred to as the daughter of Amun and Mut in a text from Armant.

nodes.name: Abundantia
nodes.domain: abundance, prosperity, generosity, distribution of food and money
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman with cornucopia overflowing with grain and coins, personification of abundance
nodes.significantEvent: personification of abundance in Roman religion, frequently depicted on coins of emperors who wished to emphasize their generosity in grain distributions to the Roman people
nodes.symbolism: the divine abundance that overflows into the world, the cornucopia as the inexhaustible horn of plenty, generosity as a divine feminine attribute
nodes.neumannArchetype: the overflowing Great Mother whose abundance sustains the collective

nodes.name: Charites
nodes.domain: grace, beauty, charm, creativity, festivity, dance
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: three beautiful maidens dancing together, often naked or lightly draped
nodes.significantEvent: attend Aphrodite and adorn her, inspire artists and poets, preside over banquets and social gatherings
nodes.symbolism: the grace that makes life beautiful, the interconnection of beauty, joy, and creativity, the social bonds that make civilization pleasant
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive transformative feminine as the inspiration of all art and social harmony
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughters of Zeus and the Oceanid Eurynome: Aglaea (Splendor), Euphrosyne (Joy), and Thalia (Good Cheer)

nodes.name: Nannacus
nodes.domain: the flood, kingship, lamentation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: ancient king who wept for the destruction he foresaw
nodes.significantEvent: wept for twenty years foreseeing the coming flood, the proverb the lament of Nannacus referred to excessive grieving, his people perished in the flood of Deucalion
nodes.symbolism: the prophet-king who can only weep at the approaching catastrophe he cannot prevent, excessive foreknowledge as torment
nodes.neumannArchetype: the prophetic consciousness overwhelmed by knowledge of the approaching destruction, the king whose tears cannot avert the flood
nodes.birthCircumstances: king of Iconium in Phrygia

nodes.name: Daode Tianzun
nodes.domain: creation, the Dao, ethics, origin, the primordial
nodes.object: ruyi scepter, fan of the five fires
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the eldest and most venerable of the Three Pure Ones, depicted as an ancient sage
nodes.significantEvent: transmitted the Dao De Jing through his manifestation as Laozi, represents the first emanation of the Dao and the origin of all ethics and cosmic law
nodes.symbolism: the Dao in its original undifferentiated purity, ethical perfection as the origin of the cosmos, the primordial sage from whom all teaching flows
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial father archetype, the original consciousness before differentiation, the great ancestor of all wisdom
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the Three Pure Ones (Sanqing), the highest deities in Daoism, represents the Dao itself in its earliest and most undifferentiated form

nodes.name: Miaozhuang Wang
nodes.domain: kingship, fatherhood, Buddhist devotion
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: legendary king and father of the goddess Miaoshan (Guanyin)
nodes.significantEvent: opposed his daughters religious vocation and persecuted her, eventually fell ill and was cured by his own daughters flesh offered as medicine, converted to Buddhism in gratitude and devotion
nodes.symbolism: the tyrant father transformed by the daughters compassionate sacrifice, the patriarchal opposition to feminine spirituality overcome by love, the body offered as medicine
nodes.neumannArchetype: the negative father transformed by the sacrificial feminine (daughter), the patriarchal resistance to the Great Mothers compassion overcome through the daughters bodily offering
nodes.birthCircumstances: Miaozhuang grew angry because he wanted Miao Shan to marry a person of power and wealth, not a healer.
nodes.deathCircumstances: Now struck with fear, her father ordered her to be put to death.

nodes.name: Zhao Gongming
nodes.domain: wealth, war, tiger-riding, the Investiture of the Gods
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: dark-faced warrior riding a black tiger, one of the most important wealth gods in Chinese religion
nodes.significantEvent: fought against the Zhou in the Investiture of the Gods, after death was deified as Marshal Zhao and became the most powerful of the Five Gods of Wealth (Wulu Caishen), rides a black tiger and commands the wealth of the world
nodes.symbolism: the fierce warrior transformed into the god of wealth, the black tiger as the fearsome vehicle of prosperity, wealth as requiring a warriors ferocity to acquire and defend
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow warrior (originally an adversary) transformed into the primary wealth deity, the fierce masculine whose destructive power is redirected into the generation of abundance
nodes.birthCircumstances: originally a Shang Dynasty general and Daoist immortal in the Fengshen Yanyi

nodes.name: Satis
nodes.domain: the Nile cataract, water, hunting, war, Elephantine
nodes.object: white crown of Upper Egypt, bow and arrows
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman wearing the white crown of Upper Egypt with antelope or gazelle horns, holding a bow and arrows
nodes.significantEvent: guarded the southern border of Egypt at the First Cataract, protected the sources of the Nile flood, the pharaohs offered to her to ensure the annual inundation would arrive
nodes.symbolism: the guardian of the Niles source, the southern border as the threshold of Egyptian civilization, the bow as the weapon of the border defender, the water of the cataract as the origin of Egyptian life
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the guardian of the waters source, the feminine who controls the flow of the life-giving waters from the southern threshold
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient goddess of the First Cataract at Elephantine, consort of Khnum

nodes.neumannArchetype: the ambiguous serpent of the unconscious that is both protective and dangerous

nodes.name: Diana
nodes.domain: the hunt, the moon, virginity, wilderness, childbirth
nodes.characterTrait: virginal, independent, huntress, protector of women, wild
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful young woman in a short hunting tunic with bow and quiver, often accompanied by hunting dogs and a deer, crescent moon on her brow
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped at the famous temple at Nemi (Diana Nemorensis) where the Rex Nemorensis (King of the Wood) held office by slaying his predecessor, a crucial site in Frazers The Golden Bough
nodes.symbolism: the virgin goddess of the wild as the feminine that cannot be domesticated, the moon as the light of the night hunt, the woodland sanctuary as the sacred feminine space beyond civilization
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother in her virginal-huntress aspect, the fierce independent feminine that refuses the patriarchal marriage bond
nodes.domain_source: Ovid, Metamorphoses (Actaeon narrative); Virgil, Aeneid; the cult of Diana Nemorensis at Lake Nemi (Aricia); the cult of Diana on the Aventine (founded by Servius Tullius); Catullus, Hymn to Diana (Carmina 34)
nodes.object_source: Diana iconography — bow and arrows; quiver; lunar crescent; hunting-dogs; deer (all inherited from Artemis)
nodes.animals_source: Diana's sacred animals: deer; hunting-dog; she-bear
nodes.characterTrait_source: Ovid; Catullus; the Aventine cult tradition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard iconography — young huntress identical to Artemis; sometimes triple-form (Diana Trivia — at crossroads, as Hecate-like)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Roman tradition — identified with Greek Artemis; the Diana Nemorensis cult at Lake Nemi (the famous Rex Nemorensis priesthood requiring the priest to kill his predecessor in single combat — central to Frazer's Golden Bough); the Aventine cult founded by Servius Tullius as a Latin-League-shared sanctuary; protector of women and slaves
nodes.birthTypes_source: Standard interpretatio

nodes.name: Acca Larentia
nodes.domain: motherhood, foster care, wolves, the founding of Rome, the Lares
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: divine she-wolf or woman who nursed Romulus and Remus, the foster mother of Romes founders
nodes.significantEvent: nursed the infant Romulus and Remus after they were abandoned on the banks of the Tiber, her festival Larentalia was celebrated on December 23, later identified as the mother of the Lares (household spirits)
nodes.symbolism: the she-wolf as the wild maternal principle that nurtures civilization, the foster mother as the nurse of empire, the wolf-nurse as the primordial feminine from which Rome was born
nodes.neumannArchetype: the theriomorphic Great Mother (she-wolf) who nurtures the divine twins (Romulus and Remus) who will found civilization
nodes.birthCircumstances: legendary nurse of Romulus and Remus, either as a literal she-wolf or as a woman called Lupa

nodes.name: Panacea
nodes.domain: universal cure, healing, medicine
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: divine healer, one of the healing sisterhood
nodes.significantEvent: invoked in the Hippocratic Oath alongside her father and sisters, represents the complete cure of all disease
nodes.symbolism: the universal remedy, the dream of complete healing, medicine as a divine aspiration
nodes.neumannArchetype: the nurturing feminine in her aspect as total restoration, the ideal of perfect healing
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Asclepius and Epione, sister of Iaso, Hygieia, Aceso, and Aegle

nodes.name: Neaera
nodes.domain: the sun, herding, radiance
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: luminous nymph, daughter of Helios
nodes.significantEvent: bore Helios two daughters who guarded his sacred cattle on the island of Thrinacia
nodes.symbolism: the radiant mother of the solar guardians, the sun gods beloved who produces the next generation of light-bearers
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine radiance of the solar tradition, the mother who generates the guardians of the masculine solar patrimony
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Helios, mother of Lampetia and Phaethusa

nodes.name: Dapeng Jinchi Mingwang
nodes.domain: justice, Buddhism, transformation, power
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: wrathful Buddhist deity manifesting as a great golden-winged bird (garuda-like figure)
nodes.significantEvent: a powerful demon-subduing deity in Chinese Buddhism, associated with the golden-winged Dapeng bird that can devour dragons, in Journey to the West he is a formidable adversary of Sun Wukong
nodes.symbolism: the wrathful protector who subdues evil through overwhelming power, the great bird that devours the dragon of chaos, justice through terrifying force
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wrathful masculine protector, the solar bird of consciousness that devours the dragon of the unconscious

nodes.name: Na Tuk Kong
nodes.domain: earth, prosperity, local protection, Southeast Asian Chinese religion
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: elderly earth god figure, the Chinese earth deity as worshipped in Southeast Asia
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped throughout Malaysia, Singapore, and Indonesia by Chinese communities as the local earth spirit who protects homes and businesses and brings prosperity
nodes.symbolism: the earth as the foundation of local prosperity, the Chinese religious tradition transplanted and localized abroad, the universal earth god adapted to tropical Southeast Asian contexts
nodes.neumannArchetype: the benevolent earth father who grounds the community in local prosperity, the localized patriarch of place
nodes.birthCircumstances: localized form of the Chinese Earth God (Tu Di Gong) in Southeast Asian Chinese communities

nodes.name: Zhenyuan Daxian
nodes.domain: immortality, Daoism, hospitality, the ginseng fruit
nodes.characterTrait: ancient, powerful, proud, hospitable yet wrathful
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: ancient Daoist immortal who has lived since the creation of the world, guardian of the ginseng fruit tree
nodes.significantEvent: in Journey to the West he hosts the travelers at his Wuzhuang Abbey, Sun Wukong steals and destroys his ginseng fruit tree (which produces human-shaped fruits of immortality that ripen once every 9,000 years), Guanyin Bodhisattva intervenes to restore the tree and reconcile them
nodes.symbolism: the ancient guardian of the rarest immortality fruit, the ginseng fruit tree as the cosmic tree of life bearing human-shaped fruit, the destruction and restoration of the tree as the cycle of loss and renewal
nodes.neumannArchetype: the ancient father-guardian of the cosmic tree, the senex whose treasure (immortality fruit) is stolen by the trickster-child and restored by the Great Mother (Guanyin)

nodes.name: Anuket
nodes.domain: the Nile cataract, water, hunting, nourishment, Elephantine
nodes.object: feathered crown, bow and arrows, ankh
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman wearing a tall feathered crown, holding a papyrus scepter, sometimes depicted embracing the pharaoh
nodes.significantEvent: personified the Nile waters as they rushed through the cataracts, her embrace of the pharaoh symbolized the life-giving waters of the Nile nourishing Egypt, worshipped at Elephantine
nodes.symbolism: the rush of the cataract waters as the divine embrace, the nourishing flow of the Nile as the mothers milk of Egypt, the feathered crown as the spray of the cataract waters
nodes.neumannArchetype: the nourishing Great Mother whose embrace is the flow of the life-giving waters, the feminine that sustains through the gift of the river
nodes.birthCircumstances: goddess of the First Cataract of the Nile, part of the Elephantine triad with Khnum and Satis

nodes.name: Shai
nodes.domain: fate, destiny, fortune, the afterlife, judgment
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: personification of fate and destiny, depicted as a man
nodes.significantEvent: stood at the judgment of the dead alongside Meskhenet, determining the fate of each soul, personified the concept of destined fortune that was assigned to each person at birth and confirmed at death
nodes.symbolism: fate as a divine personification, the inevitability of ones destined fortune, the judgment of the afterlife as the confirmation of earthly destiny
nodes.neumannArchetype: the patriarchal fate-principle, the masculine that determines and confirms the destiny of consciousness

nodes.name: Juno
nodes.domain: marriage, childbirth, women, queenship, the state
nodes.characterTrait: regal, protective of women, jealous, majestic, commanding
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: matronly woman in flowing robes wearing a diadem and veil, holding a scepter and patera, accompanied by a peacock
nodes.significantEvent: protectress of the Roman state and of women throughout their lives, her three great festivals (Matronalia, Caprotinia, and Nonae Caprotinae) honored married women, her temple on the Capitoline was one of the oldest in Rome
nodes.symbolism: the peacock as the display of divine majesty, the veil as the sanctity of marriage, the queen of heaven as the protector of all women, the cow as the maternal feminine of abundance
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the divine queen and protector of the marriage bond, the supreme feminine of the patriarchal order
birthTypes: child of Saturn and Ops; swallowed and regurgitated
familyRoles: sister of Neptune, Pluto, Ceres, Vesta
nodes.domain_source: Ovid, Fasti and Metamorphoses; Virgil, Aeneid (her hostility to the Trojans); Livy 5.50-52 (the geese of Juno Moneta saving the Capitol); the Capitoline cult; the Aventine cult of Juno Regina; Ennius, Annales
nodes.object_source: Juno iconography — diadem; peacock; pomegranate; the geese sacred to her (especially Juno Moneta on the Arx)
nodes.animals_source: Juno's sacred animals: peacock (from her identification with Hera); goose (especially the geese of Juno Moneta whose alarm saved the Capitol from the Gauls in 390 BCE)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Virgil, Aeneid (her wrath against Aeneas); the Junonian cult tradition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard iconography — regal matronly goddess with diadem; often paired iconographically with Jupiter and Minerva (the Capitoline Triad)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Roman tradition — queen of the gods; Juno Moneta whose geese alarmed the Capitol-defenders in 390 BCE during the Gallic sack (Livy 5.47, the famous Marcus Manlius episode); patron of marriage, women, and Rome itself (Juno Regina). In the Aeneid, the relentless adversary of Aeneas and the Trojans (an importation of Hera's hostility from the Iliad)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Roman interpretation of Hesiodic Theogony tradition

nodes.name: Aequitas
nodes.domain: fairness, equality, justice, economic equity
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman holding balanced scales and a measuring rod, personification of fairness and equity
nodes.significantEvent: appeared on Roman coins especially during the Empire to represent the emperors commitment to fair dealing and equitable governance
nodes.symbolism: the balanced scales as the divine standard of fairness, the measuring rod as the instrument of equity, justice as a feminine attribute of governance
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine principle of balance and equity in the patriarchal order

nodes.domain: the underworld, the dead, chthonic powers, the depths
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the gods of the underworld collectively, the divine powers beneath the earth
nodes.significantEvent: the collective divine powers of the Roman underworld, including Dis Pater, Proserpina, and various chthonic spirits, propitiated through offerings at graves and in underground chambers
nodes.symbolism: the divine powers beneath the earth as the collective underworld, the chthonic realm as the mirror of the celestial, death as a realm with its own divine governance
nodes.neumannArchetype: the collective shadow-deities of the unconscious depths, the patriarchal underworld order mirroring the celestial

nodes.name: Moros
nodes.domain: doom, fate, death, the allotted end
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: dark, shadowy personification of impending doom
nodes.significantEvent: drives mortals toward their fated death, not even Zeus can alter what Moros has decreed, represents the doom that awaits all
nodes.symbolism: the inescapable doom allotted to every mortal, fate as an ending rather than a process, the finality that even the gods cannot evade
nodes.neumannArchetype: the dark masculine aspect of fate, the death principle as an inescapable cosmic law
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Nyx alone, or of Nyx and Erebus

nodes.name: Momus
nodes.domain: mockery, satire, criticism, blame, poets
nodes.characterTrait: critical, mocking, sharp-tongued, truthful through ridicule
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: sometimes depicted lifting a mask from his face revealing his true nature
nodes.significantEvent: criticized Athenas house for not being portable, Poseidons bull for not having horns before its eyes, and Aphrodites sandal for creaking, expelled from Olympus for his constant criticism
nodes.symbolism: the critic who finds fault with even divine perfection, satire as a divine function, the necessary voice of dissent
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow trickster who exposes the imperfections of even the highest consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Nyx alone according to Hesiod, twin of the misery goddess Oizys

nodes.name: Aeternitas
nodes.domain: eternity, permanence, the eternal nature of Rome, immortality
nodes.object: phoenix, sun and moon, globe, torch
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman holding a phoenix, sun and moon, or a globe, personification of eternity and permanence
nodes.significantEvent: appeared on Roman coins to assert the eternal nature of the Roman Empire, often associated with the deification of emperors and the promise of eternal Rome
nodes.symbolism: the phoenix as the bird of eternal renewal, the sun and moon as the cosmic guarantors of permanence, Romes claim to eternity expressed as a divine feminine principle
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as eternity, the feminine principle that transcends all temporal limitation

nodes.domain: fertility, the phallus, procreation

nodes.neumannArchetype: the undifferentiated phallic masculine, the raw generative force before cultural elaboration
nodes.birthCircumstances: Patriarch Photius I of Constantinople writes that Orthanes was the son of Hermes and a nymph.

nodes.name: Hyperion
nodes.domain: light, watchfulness, the sun above
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Titan who goes above, embodiment of heavenly light
nodes.significantEvent: married his sister Theia and fathered Helios (Sun), Selene (Moon), and Eos (Dawn), the three luminaries of the sky
nodes.symbolism: the primordial light that precedes and generates the visible celestial bodies, the watcher from above
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial solar masculine, the light-consciousness that precedes the differentiated sun
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Uranus and Gaia, one of the twelve Titans

nodes.name: Ophion
nodes.domain: primordial rule, the cosmic egg, creation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: great serpent who was the first ruler of the cosmos
nodes.significantEvent: ruled Olympus with Eurynome before being overthrown by Cronus and Rhea, cast into the ocean stream
nodes.symbolism: the primordial serpent king of creation, the first cosmic order that must be overthrown for the current world to exist
nodes.neumannArchetype: the uroboric serpent as primordial ruler, the earliest stage of cosmic consciousness that must be surpassed
nodes.birthCircumstances: primordial serpent deity of Pelasgian creation myth
