nodes.name: Alexanor
nodes.domain: healing, hero cult, temple founding
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: grandson of Asclepius worshipped as a healing hero
nodes.significantEvent: established a temple and healing shrine to his grandfather Asclepius at Titane in Sicyon
nodes.symbolism: the transmission of healing knowledge through generations, the hero cult as the foundation of medicine
nodes.neumannArchetype: the grandson who perpetuates the healing tradition of the Great Physician
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Machaon, grandson of Asclepius

nodes.name: Nisus and Euryalus
nodes.domain: friendship, loyalty in war, heroic companionship
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: two young Trojan warriors, close friends
nodes.significantEvent: made a night raid on the sleeping Rutulian camp but Euryalus was captured and killed when the moonlight glinted on his stolen helmet, Nisus died trying to save him
nodes.symbolism: the bond of warrior friendship stronger than the fear of death, the beautiful youth whose love of spoils causes both their deaths, devotion unto death
nodes.neumannArchetype: the doubled hero who fights and dies as one, the masculine bond that transcends individual survival
nodes.birthCircumstances: Nisus elder and more experienced, Euryalus younger and beautiful

nodes.name: Di Jun
nodes.domain: music, the sun, agriculture, ancestor of the Shang
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: supreme deity of pre-Shang mythology, lord of the sun and music
nodes.significantEvent: father of Xihe (mother of the ten suns) or husband to her, his ten sun-children all rose at once scorching the earth until Hou Yi shot down nine of them
nodes.symbolism: the celestial father whose children (the suns) must be limited to preserve the world, creative overabundance that threatens destruction, music as cosmic harmony
nodes.neumannArchetype: the solar father whose excessive progeny (ten suns) threatens the world, requiring the hero (Hou Yi) to limit the masculine solar excess
nodes.birthCircumstances: primordial deity, father of the ten suns (sun-birds) and the twelve moons

nodes.name: Nezha
nodes.domain: war, protection, the sea, childhood, rebellion, lotus rebirth
nodes.object: wind fire wheels, fire-tipped spear, Universe Ring, Red Armillary Sash
nodes.characterTrait: rebellious, fearless, filial yet defiant, protective, childlike, powerful
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: eternally young boy warrior standing on flaming wind-fire wheels, wearing a red sash and golden armillary bracelet, wielding a fire-tipped spear
nodes.significantEvent: killed the Dragon Kings son and stripped his tendons, committed suicide to save his parents from heavenly punishment, his master Taiyi Zhenren rebuilt his body from lotus roots, battled his own father until reconciled by Buddha
nodes.symbolism: the divine child who must destroy and remake himself, rebellion against patriarchal authority as a necessary stage of spiritual growth, the lotus body as rebirth beyond flesh, the wind-fire wheels as mastery of the elements
nodes.neumannArchetype: the archetypal divine child who rebels against the father, dies, and is reborn from the lotus (the Great Mothers flower), the young masculine who must break the old order to establish the new
nodes.birthCircumstances: born as a flesh ball after 3 years and 6 months of pregnancy to Lady Yin and Li Jing, reincarnation of Lingzhu Zi, a spirit pearl attendant
nodes.deathCircumstances: Nezha insulted him, causing him to attack Nezha and be killed by his set of rings called the Qiankun Quan ().

nodes.name: Zhong Kui
nodes.domain: exorcism, demon-slaying, the supernatural, examinations, justice
nodes.object: sword of demon-slaying, official hat, fan
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: large fierce-looking man with a full black beard, bulging eyes, and disheveled appearance, wearing the robes and hat of a scholar-official
nodes.significantEvent: killed himself on the palace steps after being denied his rightful examination title, the Emperor of Heaven appointed him King of Ghosts and Supreme Demon Queller, his image painted on doors during the Chinese New Year wards off evil spirits and demons
nodes.symbolism: ugliness as the mask of supreme justice, the scholar denied his worldly due who becomes the supreme supernatural enforcer, suicide transformed into divine appointment, the demon-queller whose fierce appearance is itself a weapon against evil
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow hero whose rejected appearance becomes the source of his supreme power over evil, the ugly masculine whose denied ego-recognition is transformed into transpersonal authority over the demonic
nodes.birthCircumstances: a scholar who topped the imperial examination but was denied his title due to his ugly appearance

nodes.name: Sopdet
nodes.domain: the star Sirius, the Nile flood, the new year, agriculture
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman with a five-pointed star on her head, or depicted as a celestial cow
nodes.significantEvent: the heliacal rising of Sirius (its first appearance after a period of invisibility) heralded the annual Nile flood and marked the beginning of the Egyptian new year, this astronomical event was the foundation of the Egyptian calendar
nodes.symbolism: the brightest star as the herald of the flood and new year, the star as the celestial timekeeper of Egypts agricultural cycle, the Dog Star as the luminous guardian of the cosmic calendar
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the stellar light that announces the return of the fertilizing waters, the feminine star-consciousness that marks the renewal of the cosmic cycle
nodes.birthCircumstances: personification of the star Sirius (Sothis), the brightest star in the night sky

nodes.name: Shed
nodes.domain: protection, childhood, salvation, desert dangers, hunting
nodes.animals: serpent, scorpion, lion (the animals he vanquishes)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: youthful god or boy depicted vanquishing dangerous animals (serpents, scorpions, lions) while standing in a chariot or on a horse
nodes.significantEvent: protected the vulnerable against dangerous animals and demons, often depicted on stelae designed to protect against scorpion stings and snake bites, associated with Horus as a youthful savior figure
nodes.symbolism: the divine youth as savior, the boy who conquers the dangers of the desert, salvation as the defeat of dangerous beasts, the protective magic of the young hero
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child-hero who conquers the chthonic dangers (serpents, scorpions), the youthful masculine consciousness that overcomes the threats of the unconscious
nodes.birthCircumstances: a salvation deity associated with the protection of the vulnerable

nodes.name: Minerva
nodes.domain: wisdom, war, crafts, strategy, civilization
nodes.object: owl, shield, spear, aegis with Gorgons head, olive branch
nodes.characterTrait: wise, strategic, virginal, crafting, civilizing, just
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: armored woman wearing a crested helmet and aegis breastplate with Medusas head, carrying a spear and shield, accompanied by an owl
nodes.significantEvent: one of the Capitoline Triad (Jupiter, Juno, Minerva), her festival Quinquatria was the major celebration of artisans and craftsmen, patroness of arts, trade, and strategy
nodes.symbolism: wisdom born from the head of the father god, the owl as nocturnal wisdom, the aegis as the terrifying power of the feminine mind, craft and strategy as feminine virtues
nodes.neumannArchetype: the anima as wisdom born from the Great Father, the feminine consciousness that emerges from the masculine head as pure intellect and strategic power
birthTypes: born from Jupiter's head (importing the Athena-Metis narrative)
familyRoles: daughter of Jupiter (in Roman tradition, often without the Metis swallowing narrative)
nodes.domain_source: Ovid, Metamorphoses (especially Book 6 — Arachne); Virgil, Aeneid; Livy; the Capitoline Triad cult; the Etruscan Menrva-cult origin (pre-Greek)
nodes.object_source: Minerva iconography — helmet; spear; aegis with gorgoneion; owl; olive (all inherited from Athena)
nodes.animals_source: Minerva's sacred animals: owl; snake (in some depictions)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Ovid; Virgil; Roman cult tradition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard iconography — armored maiden virtually identical to Athena; the Etruscan pre-Greek Menrva tradition had distinct Etruscan-cult elements eventually absorbed by interpretatio
nodes.significantEvent_source: Roman tradition — though identified with Greek Athena, Minerva had a pre-Greek Etruscan origin (Menrva, evidenced in Etruscan inscriptions from c. 600 BCE onward) before becoming syncretized; one of the Capitoline Triad; patroness of crafts, wisdom, and warfare; the Quinquatria festival (her March 19-23 festival) was central to scholars and artisans
nodes.birthTypes_source: Ovid, Metamorphoses (importing Hesiodic narrative)

nodes.name: Týr
nodes.domain: war, justice, law, oaths, courage, self-sacrifice, the sky
nodes.characterTrait: brave, just, oath-keeping, self-sacrificing — willing to lose his right hand for the binding of Fenrir
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: One-handed: he placed his hand in Fenrir's mouth as a pledge during the binding-test; when Fenrir realized he could not break Gleipnir, he bit off Tyr's hand at the wrist (now called the wolf's-joint, ulfliðr).
nodes.significantEvent: Places his right hand in the mouth of the wolf Fenrir as a pledge during the binding-test of Gleipnir; when Fenrir realizes he is bound and cannot break free, he bites off Tyr's hand (Gylfaginning 25, 34). At Ragnarok, kills the hellhound Garm at the gates of Hel; they are mutual slayers (Vǫluspá 44-49 implicit; Gylfaginning 51).
nodes.symbolism: the hand in the wolfs mouth as the pledge of justice that requires self-sacrifice, the one-handed god as justice that has paid the price, the binding of the wolf as the containment of chaos through personal sacrifice
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father of justice who sacrifices part of himself (the hand) to contain the chaos-beast (Fenrir), the masculine consciousness that binds the destructive through self-mutilation
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Hymir in Hymiskviða; son of Odin in some Eddic genealogies. Genealogically ambiguous in the corpus.
nodes.deathCircumstances: Falls in mutual slaughter with Garmr (the hound of Hel, often identified with Fenrir) at Ragnarök (Vǫluspá 51-52; Gylfaginning 51).
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 25, 34; Skáldskaparmál 9; Vǫluspá 51-56; Hymiskviða 4-39 (the cauldron-quest); Lokasenna 38-40
nodes.characterTrait_source: Gylfaginning 25, 34; Hymiskviða; Lokasenna
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Gylfaginning 25, 34 ('the most daring and stout-hearted...he has no hand'); standard one-handed iconography

nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Hymiskviða 5; Skáldskaparmál 9

nodes.name: Zhou Cang
nodes.domain: loyalty, war, the Three Kingdoms, carrying the halberd
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: massive dark-skinned warrior of immense strength who carries Guan Yus Green Dragon Crescent Blade
nodes.significantEvent: carried Guan Yus famous halberd and followed him faithfully through every battle, when Guan Yu was captured and executed Zhou Cang killed himself in grief and loyalty, remained Guan Yus attendant even in divine form
nodes.symbolism: the ultimate loyal follower whose identity is defined entirely by devotion to his lord, the blade-bearer who serves with absolute self-abnegation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow-servant whose identity is entirely merged with the hero, the devoted masculine whose selfhood is dissolved in service
nodes.birthCircumstances: a fugitive bandit who became Guan Yus most devoted follower
nodes.deathCircumstances: He commits suicide after learning that Guan Yu and Guan Ping have been captured and executed by Sun Quan's forces.

nodes.name: Ahuiateteo
nodes.domain: excess, pleasure
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Pleasure Gods, deities associated with excess, indulgence, and drunkenness
nodes.significantEvent: a group of deities associated with excess and pleasure, often connected to the Centzon Totochtin (Four Hundred Rabbits) who are the gods of drunkenness
nodes.symbolism: the pleasure gods as the divine patrons of excess, indulgence as a divine domain, the thin line between sacred ecstasy and destructive excess
nodes.neumannArchetype: the collective unconscious of pleasure and excess, the archetypal indulgence that dissolves ego boundaries

nodes.name: Alpheus
nodes.domain: rivers, pursuit, unrequited love
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: river god, beautiful and swift-flowing
nodes.significantEvent: pursued the nymph Arethusa who fled across the sea to Sicily where she became a spring, Alpheus followed her as an underground river emerging beside her
nodes.symbolism: the relentless flow of desire, the river as metaphor for pursuit across the world, unrequited love that transcends geography
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine principle pursuing the elusive feminine across the boundaries of land and sea
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of the Titans Oceanus and Tethys, or of Helios
nodes.deathCircumstances: Through him, Alpheus was the grandfather of Diocles, and great-grandfather of a pair of soldiers, Crethon and Orsilochus, who were slain by Aeneas during the Trojan War.

nodes.name: Triptolemus
nodes.domain: agriculture, grain, the Eleusinian Mysteries, civilization
nodes.object: wheat sheaf, winged chariot, serpent-drawn chariot
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: young prince depicted riding a serpent-drawn chariot scattering grain seeds
nodes.significantEvent: taught the art of agriculture by Demeter and sent on her winged serpent-chariot to teach grain cultivation to all humanity, initiated the Eleusinian Mysteries alongside Demeter
nodes.symbolism: the human who receives the divine gift of agriculture and spreads it across the world, the serpent chariot as the chthonic vehicle of civilizing knowledge, the boy who becomes the missionary of the grain goddess
nodes.neumannArchetype: the culture hero chosen by the Great Mother to carry the gift of agriculture (consciousness of cultivation) to all humanity
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of King Celeus and Queen Metanira of Eleusis, or son of Oceanus and Gaia

nodes.name: Adrasteia
nodes.domain: divine justice, distribution, inescapability
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: nymph or goddess associated with inevitability

nodes.symbolism: the inescapable nature of divine justice, the nurturing hand that also distributes fate
nodes.neumannArchetype: the nurturing-terrible dual aspect of the Great Mother, she who nurses the divine child and enforces cosmic law
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Zeus and Ananke, or a Cretan nymph daughter of Melisseus who nursed the infant Zeus

nodes.name: Silenus
nodes.domain: wine, wisdom, prophecy, nature, drunkenness
nodes.characterTrait: wise, drunken, prophetic, jovial, cowardly, truthful when captured
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: fat, bald, snub-nosed old man with horse ears and tail, usually drunk and riding a donkey
nodes.significantEvent: captured by King Midas and revealed that the best thing for mortals is never to be born and the second best is to die soon, tutored the young Dionysus
nodes.symbolism: wisdom hidden in apparent foolishness, the truth that emerges from drunkenness, the comic exterior concealing profound knowledge
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wise old man archetype in his comic and intoxicated aspect, the tutor who imparts forbidden knowledge through apparent foolishness
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Pan or Hermes, raised as tutor and foster father of Dionysus

nodes.domain: agriculture, ploughing, the plough, the constellation Bootes

nodes.symbolism: the divine origin of agriculture, the plough as the tool that transforms wild nature into cultivated civilization, the farmer elevated to the stars
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine culture hero who develops the tool (plough) that transforms the body of the Great Mother (earth) into productive fields
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Demeter and the mortal Iasion

nodes.name: Angerona
nodes.domain: secrecy, silence, winter solstice, the relief of anxiety
nodes.object: sealed lips, finger to mouth, wreath
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: bandaged mouth, finger on lips
nodes.significantEvent: her festival was celebrated on December 21 (the winter solstice) when she relieved the anxieties of the old year, her statue stood in the temple with a sealed mouth, priests made offerings to her requesting the relief of secret fears
nodes.symbolism: the sealed mouth as the power of sacred silence, the winter solstice as the turning point of anxiety, the relief that comes from acknowledging ones secret fears to the divine, silence as a healing act
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of silence who absorbs the anxieties of consciousness at the darkest point of the year (solstice), the feminine that heals through the acceptance of the unspoken

nodes.name: Arke
nodes.domain: messages, betrayal, the rainbow, speed
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: winged goddess, rainbow-like, twin sister of Iris
nodes.significantEvent: sided with the Titans against the Olympians during the Titanomachy, while her sister Iris sided with Zeus. Punished by having her wings torn off
nodes.symbolism: the cost of choosing the wrong side in cosmic conflict, loyalty and betrayal as twin choices, the fallen messenger
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow twin of the divine messenger, the fallen feminine who chose the old order over the new
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the sea god Thaumas and the Oceanid Electra, twin sister of Iris

nodes.name: Oneiros
nodes.domain: dreams, prophecy through sleep, illusion
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: dark-winged spirits who appear in dreams
nodes.significantEvent: the collective spirits of dreams who appear at the gates of ivory (false dreams) and horn (true dreams) in Homers Odyssey
nodes.symbolism: the gateway between waking and sleeping consciousness, the ambiguity of dreams as both truth and illusion, the dual gates of horn and ivory
nodes.neumannArchetype: the spirits of the unconscious that communicate through symbols, the dream as the bridge between the ego and the depths
nodes.birthCircumstances: son or sons of Hypnos (Sleep), or children of Nyx

nodes.name: Dragon King
nodes.domain: rain, water, floods, the sea, weather
nodes.characterTrait: regal, powerful, temperamental, generous when honored
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: great dragon in royal robes, can shift between dragon and human form, ruler of an underwater crystal palace
nodes.significantEvent: controls rainfall and water, can cause floods or droughts, features prominently in Journey to the West and Investiture of the Gods, petitioned by mortals through offerings and dragon boat festivals
nodes.symbolism: the dragon as lord of water and rain, the underwater palace as the treasure-house of the deep, the king whose mood determines whether the land flourishes or drowns
nodes.neumannArchetype: the water father whose depths contain treasure and danger, the dragon king of the unconscious whose moods shape the world above
nodes.birthCircumstances: the four Dragon Kings (Ao Guang, Ao Qin, Ao Run, Ao Shun) rule the four seas

nodes.name: Nio
nodes.domain: protection, Buddhism, temple guardianship
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: fierce muscle-bound guardian figures flanking temple gates, often in open and closed mouth positions
nodes.significantEvent: guard the entrances to Buddhist temples, their fierce appearance wards off evil spirits and protects the sacred space within
nodes.symbolism: the fierce guardians of sacred space, the threshold protectors whose terrifying form shields the sacred from profanation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the threshold guardians of consciousness, the fierce masculine that protects the entry to the sacred center
nodes.birthCircumstances: derived from Indian Buddhist temple guardian traditions (Dvarapala)

nodes.name: Zhuge Liang
nodes.domain: strategy, wisdom, loyalty, Daoism, the Three Kingdoms, invention
nodes.object: feather fan, seven-star lamp, wooden ox and gliding horse (inventions)
nodes.animals: horse, fish, ram, crane, ox, dragon, phoenix
nodes.characterTrait: brilliant, loyal, strategic, foresighted, exhausted by duty, humble
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: slender scholar in a Daoist robe waving a white feather fan, often depicted in a four-wheeled wooden cart
nodes.significantEvent: served as chancellor and supreme strategist of Shu Han, devised the strategy of the three kingdoms, invented military technologies, exhausted himself through devotion to his cause and died during his final northern expedition, the embodiment of wisdom in Chinese culture
nodes.symbolism: the supreme strategist whose wisdom cannot overcome fate, the feather fan as the instrument of gentle but absolute command, the three visits of the ruler to the hermit as the proper way to seek wisdom, the exhaustion of the sage who gives everything and still falls short
nodes.neumannArchetype: the supreme wise old man whose consciousness transcends all opponents but cannot transcend mortality, the sage who exhausts himself in service to the patriarchal order
nodes.birthCircumstances: born in Yangdu (181 CE), emerged from reclusion at the urging of Liu Bei who visited his cottage three times
nodes.deathCircumstances: Zhuge Liang died in 234 at the Wuzhang Plains while on campaign and was posthumously honored as Marquis Zhongwu.

nodes.name: Heqet
nodes.domain: childbirth, fertility, frogs, resurrection, renewal
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman with the head of a frog, or depicted as a frog, associated with the primordial creation and the final stage of childbirth
nodes.significantEvent: assisted at the final moment of birth, breathing life into the newborn, later associated with resurrection and the promise of eternal life, the frog as a symbol of renewal because frogs appeared in great numbers after the Nile flood
nodes.symbolism: the frog as the symbol of teeming life that emerges after the flood, the final breath of life given at birth, resurrection as a second birth, the millions of frogs as the abundance of renewed life
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of birth and rebirth, the feminine that gives the breath of life at both birth and resurrection
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient frog goddess associated with the final stages of birth, one of the oldest Egyptian deities

nodes.name: Charis
nodes.domain: grace, charm, beauty, craftsmanship
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: divine embodiment of grace and charm
nodes.significantEvent: married to Hephaestus the smith god, welcoming Thetis when she came to request armor for Achilles
nodes.symbolism: grace united with craft, beauty as the companion of creative labor, charm as a divine quality
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive anima as the grace that accompanies and completes the creative masculine
nodes.birthCircumstances: in some traditions the wife of Hephaestus, in others identical with Aglaea the youngest of the Charites

nodes.name: Bendis
nodes.domain: moon, hunt, wild nature, Thracian mysteries
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Thracian goddess of the hunt, depicted with two spears and a torch, sometimes on horseback
nodes.significantEvent: introduced to Athens after the Battle of Marathon, worshipped with nocturnal rites, associated with Artemis and Hecate in the Greek world
nodes.symbolism: the foreign huntress goddess assimilated into Greek religion, the nocturnal hunt as sacred ritual, Thracian wildness
nodes.neumannArchetype: the foreign face of the Great Goddess (Artemis/Hecate) imported from the northern wild
nodes.birthCircumstances: Thracian goddess adopted into Greek worship

nodes.name: Ananke
nodes.domain: necessity, fate, compulsion, inevitability

nodes.symbolism: the absolute compulsion of fate against which even the gods are powerless, necessity as the fundamental law of the cosmos
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial feminine as inescapable fate, the uroboric serpent of necessity encircling the cosmos
nodes.birthCircumstances: self-generated primordial being, predating the Titans

nodes.domain: stars, falling stars, the island of Delos, prophetic dreams
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Titaness who transformed into a quail and then a floating island

nodes.neumannArchetype: the protective sister who becomes the ground (island) upon which the new consciousness (Apollo) can be born
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the Titans Coeus and Phoebe, sister of Leto

nodes.name: Emperor Taizu of Song
nodes.domain: war, statecraft, dynastic founding, martial arts
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: founder of the Song Dynasty, skilled martial artist and strategist
nodes.significantEvent: seized the throne through the Chenqiao Mutiny in 960 CE, established the Song Dynasty, unified much of China, created the Taizu Long Fist martial arts style
nodes.symbolism: the general who becomes emperor through decisive action, the founding of dynasties through martial virtue, the warrior turned sage-ruler
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hero who seizes the patriarchal throne through martial excellence and transforms into the wise ruler
nodes.birthCircumstances: Zhao Kuangyin, a military general of the Later Zhou dynasty

nodes.name: Niulang
nodes.domain: love, separation, reunion, the stars, weaving, herding
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: humble cowherd who married a heavenly weaving maiden
nodes.significantEvent: married the heavenly Weaving Maid but they were separated by the Queen Mother of Heaven who created the Milky Way between them, reunited only once a year on the seventh day of the seventh month when magpies form a bridge across the stars
nodes.symbolism: the eternal longing of separated lovers, the Milky Way as the barrier between heaven and earth, the annual reunion as the triumph of love over cosmic law, the magpie bridge of hope
nodes.neumannArchetype: the mortal masculine separated from the divine anima (Weaving Maid) by the Great Mother (Queen Mother), reunited only at the one moment when heaven and earth can meet
nodes.birthCircumstances: mortal cowherd who fell in love with Zhinü (the Weaving Maid), a celestial goddess

nodes.name: Zhunti Daoren
nodes.domain: Buddhism, Daoism, mercy, the Investiture of the Gods
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: western Daoist sage who is the Daoist form of a Buddha
nodes.significantEvent: in the Fengshen Yanyi he is a powerful western sage who helps defeat the Jie sect, representing the coming of Buddhism to China in mythological form, his seven-treasure tree is one of the most powerful weapons
nodes.symbolism: Buddhism arriving in China personified as a Daoist sage, the meeting of eastern and western spiritual traditions, mercy as the supreme spiritual weapon
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wisdom of the west arriving to transform the east, the foreign sage whose compassion overcomes all resistance
nodes.birthCircumstances: master of the Western Sect in the Fengshen Yanyi, identified with a Buddha figure
nodes.deathCircumstances: In this chapter, Zhunti Daoren arrives as a guest from the West to intervene on behalf of Ma Yuan, a man-eating demon who was about to be executed by the Chan sect.

nodes.name: Pakhet
nodes.domain: hunting, the night, lioness, protection, the desert
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: lioness-headed woman or full lioness, goddess of the Eastern Desert near Beni Hasan
nodes.significantEvent: hunted in the wadis of the Eastern Desert, the Greeks identified her with Artemis, her cave temple at Beni Hasan (Speos Artemidos) was an important pilgrimage site
nodes.symbolism: the lioness as the nocturnal hunter of the desert, the wild feminine power of the desert margins, the cave temple as the womb of the hunting goddess
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wild Great Mother as the desert lioness-huntress, the fierce feminine of the liminal desert spaces

nodes.name: Rem
nodes.domain: sleep, the night, fish, the underworld
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: fish deity associated with the underworld and the night
nodes.significantEvent: associated with the hours of the night and the underworld waters, a fish deity of the nocturnal realm
nodes.symbolism: the fish of the underworld waters, the night as the realm of the deep unconscious, the aquatic life beneath the surface of awareness
nodes.neumannArchetype: the aquatic shadow of the unconscious depths, the fish-consciousness of the deep night

nodes.name: Angitia
nodes.domain: healing, serpents, witchcraft, the Marsi, Lake Fucinus
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess associated with serpents and healing herbs, worshipped by the Marsi people of central Italy
nodes.significantEvent: the Marsi were famed throughout Italy as serpent charmers and healers, Angitia was their patron goddess, her grove at Lake Fucinus was a center of herbal medicine and serpent-charming magic
nodes.symbolism: the serpent as the instrument of healing, the Marsian serpent charmers as priests of the chthonic feminine, herbal medicine as divine feminine knowledge, the lake grove as the sacred feminine healing space
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the serpent-healer, the chthonic feminine whose mastery of the serpent (unconscious) produces healing

nodes.domain: agriculture
nodes.significantEvent: Mexican corn goddess; 'Seven Serpent'
nodes.symbolism: Mexican corn/vegetation goddess; nourishing aspect of the Great Mother
nodes.neumannArchetype: Mexican corn goddess representing the nourishing vegetation aspect.

nodes.name: Brimo
nodes.domain: death, the underworld, Hecate, nighttime rites
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: dark underworld goddess, an epithet or aspect of Hecate or Persephone
nodes.significantEvent: identified with Hecate in the Thessalian tradition, invoked in necromantic and chthonic rites
nodes.symbolism: the terrible goddess of the underworld, the wrathful face of the feminine in the realm of death
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Terrible Mother in her underworld aspect, the dark face of the lunar goddess

nodes.domain: war, marriage, broken promises
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Trojan ally from Cabesus
nodes.significantEvent: came to Troy offering to drive away the Greeks in exchange for the hand of Cassandra, killed by Idomeneus without fulfilling his promise
nodes.symbolism: the warrior whose ambition exceeds his ability, the unfulfilled promise and the bride never won
nodes.neumannArchetype: the overreaching masculine who seeks the prophetic feminine (Cassandra) but is destroyed before reaching her

nodes.name: Erlang Shen
nodes.domain: war, truth-seeing, engineering, protection, hunting
nodes.object: three-pointed double-edged lance, Howling Celestial Dog
nodes.characterTrait: dutiful, powerful, conflicted between loyalty and family, just
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: handsome warrior with a third truth-seeing eye on his forehead, armed with a three-pointed lance
nodes.significantEvent: split a mountain to rescue his mother who was imprisoned under it by her divine brother, later becomes a great celestial warrior, in Journey to the West he battles Sun Wukong to a draw
nodes.symbolism: the third eye of truth that sees through deception, the conflict between celestial duty and family loyalty, the half-divine hero who bridges heaven and earth
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hero who defies the divine father (Jade Emperor) to rescue the imprisoned feminine (his mother), the third eye as the higher consciousness that perceives truth
nodes.birthCircumstances: nephew of the Jade Emperor, son of a mortal father and the goddess Yaoji (or Yun Hua), half-divine

nodes.name: Old Man of the South Pole
nodes.domain: longevity, the stars, wisdom, the south, the Southern Cross
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: ancient sage with an enormously elongated bald head, long white beard, carrying a peach of immortality and a staff
nodes.significantEvent: bestows longevity upon those he favors, appears as a kindly but eccentric old sage with his distinctive elongated cranium, a staple figure in Chinese New Year celebrations and birthday celebrations for the elderly
nodes.symbolism: longevity as a celestial blessing from the southern star, the elongated head as a sign of accumulated wisdom, the peach of immortality as the fruit of a long-cultivated life
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive wise old man archetype, the stellar father whose elongated head shows the expansion of consciousness that comes with great age
nodes.birthCircumstances: personification of the star Canopus (the South Pole Star), one of the Sanxing (Three Stars) as Shouxing (Longevity Star)

nodes.name: Zhurong
nodes.domain: fire, the south, punishment, craftsmanship, volcano
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: god of fire, sometimes depicted with a red face and riding on a large tiger, or as a human with fire emanating from his body
nodes.significantEvent: fought against Gonggong (water god) in a cosmic battle, the fire god who punishes evildoers and controls volcanic forces, also credited with teaching humanity the use of fire for metalwork and cooking
nodes.symbolism: fire as both the creative and destructive cosmic force, the southern direction as the realm of maximum fire, the battle of fire and water as a cosmic archetype
nodes.neumannArchetype: the fire-masculine of the south, the burning consciousness that creates through transformation and destroys through purification
nodes.birthCircumstances: descended from Yandi (Flame Emperor), one of the most ancient deities

nodes.name: Meretseger
nodes.domain: the dead, snakes, the Valley of the Kings, silence, mercy
nodes.characterTrait: merciful, silent, cobra-formed, valley-dwelling, protective of the dead
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: cobra goddess or woman with a cobra head, guardian of the Valley of the Kings
nodes.significantEvent: the workers of Deir el-Medina worshipped her as their local protectress, she was both feared (sending cobra bites to sinners) and loved (showing mercy to the repentant), her cult was deeply personal and devotional
nodes.symbolism: the cobra guardian of the valley of the dead kings, the silence of the desert peak as divine mercy, the personal devotion of the workers to their local cobra goddess, punishment and mercy from the same divine source
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of the necropolis, the chthonic feminine who both guards and threatens in the valley of death
nodes.birthCircumstances: the goddess of the peak (Theban Peak) overlooking the Valley of the Kings

nodes.name: Sah
nodes.domain: the stars, Orion, the afterlife, the sky
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: man carrying a scepter and ankh, associated with the constellation Orion
nodes.significantEvent: the constellation Orion was identified with Osiris in the night sky, Sah represented the pharaohs astral afterlife as a star among the imperishable stars, consort of Sopdet (Sirius)
nodes.symbolism: Orion as the celestial Osiris, the pharaohs destiny among the stars, the imperishable stars as eternal consciousness, the constellation as the sky-body of the resurrected god
nodes.neumannArchetype: the stellar Great Father, the masculine consciousness transfigured into the eternal stars after death
nodes.birthCircumstances: personification of the constellation Orion, associated with Osiris in the afterlife

nodes.name: Ziwei Emperor
nodes.domain: the north, stars, sovereignty, imperial authority, Daoism
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Purple Tenuity Emperor, ruler of the North Star and the Purple Forbidden Enclosure of stars
nodes.significantEvent: the celestial emperor whose palace is the Purple Forbidden Enclosure (Ziwei Yuan) around the North Star, the heavenly model for the earthly Forbidden City, rules fate and imperial destiny from the cosmic center
nodes.symbolism: the North Star as the cosmic center around which all other stars revolve, the purple palace of heaven as the model for the earthly imperial palace, the stellar emperor as the cosmic archetype of earthly sovereignty
nodes.neumannArchetype: the stellar patriarch at the cosmic center, the supreme consciousness around which all other lights revolve
nodes.birthCircumstances: the stellar emperor who rules the Pole Star and the purple palace of stars surrounding it

nodes.name: Caerus
nodes.domain: opportunity, the fleeting moment, luck, kairos
nodes.characterTrait: fleeting, beautiful, elusive, bald at the back
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful youth with long forelock but bald at the back of the head, standing on a razor or winged ball
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped at Olympia where a famous statue by Lysippos depicted him, the forelock must be seized as he passes or the opportunity is lost forever
nodes.symbolism: the critical moment that can only be seized from the front, opportunity that once passed cannot be recalled, time as quality not quantity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine moment of decisive consciousness, the instant of transformation that must be grasped
nodes.birthCircumstances: youngest son of Zeus

nodes.name: Ourea
nodes.domain: mountains, the earth, primordial landforms
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the mountains personified as gods, ancient and towering
nodes.significantEvent: the mountains as the first children of the earth, providing the dwelling places of the nymphs
nodes.symbolism: the earth raised toward heaven, the primordial landscape as the body of the Great Mother, mountains as the dwelling of the sacred
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine expression of the Great Mother rising toward the sky, the chthonic reaching upward
nodes.birthCircumstances: children of Gaia without consort, born from the primordial earth

nodes.name: Fengbo
nodes.domain: wind, storms, weather
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: wind deity who controls winds and storms from a great sack or gourd
nodes.significantEvent: controls the winds by releasing them from his wind-sack, worshipped to prevent destructive storms, sometimes identified with Feilian
nodes.symbolism: the wind contained and released at divine will, the power of the atmosphere as a divine gift or punishment
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine elemental force of wind, the container (sack) as the means of controlling the chaotic breath of nature

nodes.name: Pang Juan
nodes.domain: war, strategy, jealousy, tragedy, the Warring States
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: brilliant but jealous military strategist of the Wei state
nodes.significantEvent: jealous of his classmate Sun Bins superior talent, Pang Juan had Sun Bins kneecaps removed and face tattooed, later Sun Bin took revenge by luring Pang Juan into an ambush at the Battle of Maling where Pang Juan died
nodes.symbolism: jealousy that destroys the jealous, the classmate rivalry that becomes a death struggle, the karmic return of cruelty upon the cruel
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow brother whose jealousy of the superior twin leads to his own destruction, the dark double of the culture hero
nodes.birthCircumstances: fellow student of Sun Bin under the same master Ghost Valley
nodes.deathCircumstances: The king believed Pang and was furious, that he ordered Sun Bin to be executed.

nodes.name: Mehet-Weret
nodes.domain: the primordial cow, the sky, the flood, creation, milk
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: enormous celestial cow from whose body the world emerged, the Great Flood cow
nodes.significantEvent: in the Book of the Heavenly Cow she carried the aged Ra up to the sky on her back when he withdrew from earth, her body became the sky, she suckled the sun and the pharaoh
nodes.symbolism: the celestial cow as the sky itself, the milk of the cosmic cow as rain and the Milky Way, the cow who carries the weary sun god upward, the Great Flood as the tears of Ra falling from her body
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial Great Mother in her most cosmic form, the celestial cow whose body is the sky and whose milk nourishes all creation
nodes.birthCircumstances: the primordial celestial cow who existed before the organization of the world

nodes.name: Shezmu
nodes.domain: wine, oil, perfume, execution, the underworld
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: deity associated with wine and oil pressing, and with the execution of the damned in the afterlife
nodes.significantEvent: produced wine and sacred oils for the gods but also pressed the heads of the wicked in his underworld wine press, his dual nature made him both a provider of pleasure (wine) and a punisher of evil
nodes.symbolism: the wine press as both the creation of pleasure and the crushing of the wicked, extraction as a sacred and terrible process, the ambiguity of the pressing god
nodes.neumannArchetype: the ambiguous masculine who both creates (wine/oil) and destroys (crushing the wicked), the pressing consciousness that extracts essence through force

nodes.name: Tellus
nodes.domain: earth, agriculture, fertility, motherhood, the land
nodes.characterTrait: maternal, fertile, earthy, generous, stable, nourishing
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: matronly goddess reclining on the earth, surrounded by fruits and grain, sometimes with infants at her breast
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped at the festival of Fordicidia where pregnant cows were sacrificed to ensure the fertility of the land, the foundation goddess of Roman agriculture, invoked in solemn oaths as the earth beneath ones feet
nodes.symbolism: the earth herself as a living divine body, agriculture as the relationship between humanity and the divine earth, the reclining mother as the landscape itself, the pregnant cow as the earths fertility
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the earth itself, the feminine body that is the ground of all physical existence and nourishment
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient Roman earth goddess, identified with the Greek Gaia

nodes.name: Anna Perenna
nodes.domain: the new year, renewal, spring, the march equinox, perpetual return
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess of the perpetually returning year, worshipped on the first day of the new year (March 15 in the old Roman calendar)
nodes.significantEvent: her festival on March 15 (the Ides of March in the old calendar when the year began) was a raucous public celebration at her sacred grove, marked by feasting, drinking, and obscene songs, the celebration of the years renewal
nodes.symbolism: the eternal return of the year as a divine feminine act, the spring equinox as the moment of cosmic renewal, the raucous celebration as the release of the old years accumulated tension
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of the eternal return, the feminine cycle that brings the year back to its beginning

nodes.name: Caeneus
nodes.domain: transformation, invulnerability, gender, warrior pride
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: born female (Caenis) but transformed into an invulnerable man by Poseidon
nodes.significantEvent: born as the maiden Caenis, raped by Poseidon who granted any wish, asked to become a man and be made invulnerable, killed by Centaurs who buried him under tree trunks since he could not be pierced
nodes.symbolism: gender transformation as divine gift, invulnerability as compensation for violation, the buried hero who cannot be conventionally killed
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine transformed to masculine by the sea god, the invulnerable hero whose strength was born from the violation of the feminine
nodes.birthCircumstances: Caeneus was born a girl, Caenis (), the daughter of Elatus, but after Poseidon had sex with Caenis, she was transformed by him into an invulnerable man.
nodes.deathCircumstances: Caeneus' son was the Argonaut Coronus, who was killed by Heracles while leading a war against the Dorians and their king Aegimius.

nodes.name: Hemera
nodes.domain: day, daylight, the sky by day
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: radiant goddess of the day, embodiment of daylight itself
nodes.significantEvent: born from darkness and night, she displaces her mother Nyx each dawn, sweeping away the mists of night and flooding the world with light
nodes.symbolism: light born from darkness, the daily miracle of dawn as the emergence of consciousness from the unconscious, the daughter who overcomes the mother
nodes.neumannArchetype: the light-consciousness born from the darkness of the primordial mother, the daily emergence of awareness from sleep
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Erebus (Darkness) and Nyx (Night)

nodes.domain: healing, praise, thanksgiving, hymns of healing

nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine healer whose cure is inseparable from the hymn of praise, healing through the word

nodes.name: Four Heavenly Kings
nodes.domain: protection, Buddhism, the four directions, martial power
nodes.object: sword, pipa, umbrella, serpent or mongoose
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: four imposing warrior figures in armor, each guarding one cardinal direction at the gates of Buddhist temples
nodes.significantEvent: guard the entrances to Buddhist temples and the four directions of the world, in Fengshen Yanyi they are the Mo family brothers who become the four heavenly guardians after death
nodes.symbolism: the four-directional protection of the dharma, martial power in service of spiritual truth, the guardian warriors at the gates of enlightenment
nodes.neumannArchetype: the fourfold masculine guardian of the sacred space, the warrior-protectors of the threshold of consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: adapted from Indian Buddhist lokapalas (world protectors), localized in Chinese Buddhism

nodes.name: Pangu
nodes.domain: creation, the cosmic egg, sacrifice, separation of heaven and earth
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a cosmic giant who grew larger every day for 18,000 years, his body filled the space between heaven and earth
nodes.significantEvent: hatched from the cosmic egg and separated heaven (yang) and earth (yin) by growing between them, when he died his body became the world: his breath became the wind, his voice thunder, his eyes the sun and moon, his limbs the four directions, his blood the rivers, his muscles the fertile land, his hair the stars
nodes.symbolism: the cosmic sacrifice that creates the world from the body of the first being, the separation of heaven and earth as the first act of creation, the giant whose death is the worlds birth
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial divine sacrifice, the uroboric unity that must die and be dismembered for the differentiated world to come into being, the cosmic body whose parts become the features of consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: The first being. Born inside the primordial-chaos cosmic egg (the egg described as hundun 混沌, 'chaotic like a chicken egg').
nodes.deathCircumstances: After 18,000 years, when heaven and earth were fully separated, Pangu died, and his body parts became the constituent features of the world: his breath became wind and clouds, his voice thunder, his eyes the sun and moon, his limbs the four cardinal directions, his trunk the mountains, his blood the rivers, his hair the stars, his body-hair the plants, his teeth and bones metals and stones, his sweat the rain.
nodes.domain_source: Sanwu Liji (三五歷紀, Xu Zheng, c. 220-265 CE), preserved in Yiwen Leiju (藝文類聚) ch. 1 and Taiping Yulan (太平御覽) ch. 2; Wuyun Linian Ji (五運歷年紀, Xu Zheng), preserved in Yiwen Leiju ch. 1. NOTE: Pangu is a late entrant — does not appear in pre-Han texts (Shijing, Shujing, Yijing, Zhuangzi, Liezi, Huainanzi).
nodes.object_source: The axe-and-chisel are later iconographic elements (Ming/Qing woodblock prints, Shenxian Tongjian) — NOT in Sanwu Liji or Wuyun Linian Ji. The earliest texts describe him as growing taller and physically pushing apart heaven and earth.
nodes.animals_source: The four sì líng (dragon, phoenix, tortoise, qilin) are cosmologically fundamental (Liji 'Liyun' 禮記·禮運) but NOT specifically attested in Wuyun Linian Ji as constituents of Pangu's body. The body-decomposition list in the primary fragment lists: breath → wind/clouds; voice → thunder; eyes → sun and moon; limbs → four directions; trunk → mountains; blood → rivers; hair → stars; etc. — but no sì líng. The animal attribution is a secondary embellishment.
nodes.significantEvent_source: Sanwu Liji fr. (in Yiwen Leiju 1): 天地混沌如雞子，盤古生其中 'Heaven and earth were chaotic like a chicken egg, and Pangu was born within it.' 天日高一丈，地日厚一丈，盤古日長一丈 'Heaven daily rose one zhang higher, earth daily grew one zhang thicker, and Pangu daily grew one zhang taller.' Wuyun Linian Ji fr. (in Yiwen Leiju 1) for the body-becomes-world.
nodes.eventTypes_source: Sanwu Liji and Wuyun Linian Ji as above
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Sanwu Liji fr. (in Yiwen Leiju 1)
nodes.deathCircumstances_source: Wuyun Linian Ji fr. (in Yiwen Leiju 1)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Sanwu Liji (三五歷紀, c. 3rd c. CE, Xu Zheng) — the primary surviving Pangu source; Wuyun Linian Ji (五運曆年記)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Sanwu Liji; Wuyun Linian Ji — described as a hairy giant emerging from the cosmic egg; later iconography shows him with axe, separating sky from earth
nodes.birthTypes_source: Sanwu Liji (3rd c. CE)
nodes.deathTypes_source: Wuyun Linian Ji (Pangu's body parts becoming the world at death)

nodes.name: Mnevis
nodes.domain: the sun, cattle, fertility, Heliopolis, sacred bulls
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: sacred black bull with a sun disk between its horns, the living incarnation of the sun god at Heliopolis
nodes.significantEvent: the living Mnevis bull at Heliopolis was worshipped as the earthly incarnation of the sun god, similar to the Apis bull at Memphis, it received cult worship and was mummified at death
nodes.symbolism: the bull as the earthly vessel of solar power, the black bull with the sun disk as the union of earth and sky, the living animal as the incarnation of the supreme god
nodes.neumannArchetype: the theriomorphic Great Father, the solar masculine incarnated in the body of the sacred bull
nodes.birthCircumstances: the sacred bull of Ra at Heliopolis, later associated with Atum and Osiris

nodes.name: Ops
nodes.domain: abundance, harvest, wealth, the earth, the Saturnalia
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess of abundance holding a cornucopia and grain, consort of Saturn
nodes.significantEvent: her festival Opiconsivia was celebrated on August 25 when the harvest was completed, her shrine in the Regia could only be entered by the Pontifex Maximus and the Vestal Virgins, the Roman treasury (aerarium) was kept in her temple
nodes.symbolism: the harvest as divine abundance stored for the future, the treasury in the goddess temple as the sacredness of collective wealth, the cornucopia as the overflowing feminine bounty
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of abundance whose harvest is the stored bounty of consciousness
familyRoles: mother of Jupiter, Juno, Neptune, Pluto, Ceres, Vesta
nodes.domain_source: Macrobius, Saturnalia 1.10; Varro, De Lingua Latina; the cult of Ops Consiva (within the regia of the pontifex maximus); Festus s.v.
nodes.object_source: Ops iconography — sheaf of grain; cornucopia (the etymology of opes = wealth)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Macrobius; Varro
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Ops iconography — matronly earth-and-wealth goddess; identified with Rhea in interpretatio
nodes.significantEvent_source: Roman tradition — wife-sister of Saturn (the Italic counterpart of Rhea); patroness of agricultural fertility and accumulated wealth; her cult restricted to the most sacred precincts (Ops Consiva worshipped only by Vestal Virgins and the pontifex maximus); festivals Opiconsivia (August 25) and Opalia (December 19)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Roman cult tradition

nodes.name: Atum
nodes.domain: creation, the setting sun, completion, self-creation, the primordial mound
nodes.object: benben-stone (the primordial mound on which he first arose); ankh; was-scepter
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Anthropomorphic king wearing the double-crown of Upper and Lower Egypt; in some forms a man-headed lion; sometimes depicted as the setting sun (he is 'the completed one' — Atum means 'all' and 'not-yet-existing').
nodes.significantEvent: The self-engendered creator in Heliopolitan cosmogony. Rose from the primordial waters of Nun on the benben-stone. Through autoerotic emission (or by spitting), produced Shu (air) and Tefnut (moisture) — the first pair. Their union produced Geb (earth) and Nut (sky). Geb and Nut's union produced Osiris, Isis, Set, and Nephthys — completing the Ennead. In late theology, identified with the setting sun and contrasted with Khepri (rising) and Ra (midday) — Khepri-Ra-Atum as three solar aspects.
nodes.symbolism: the self-created creator, the setting sun as completion, the primordial mound as the first land, creation through the solitary masculine act, the serpent as the pre-creation form of divine power
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial self-creating father, the uroboric masculine that generates creation from itself without the feminine, the first consciousness emerging from the undifferentiated waters
nodes.birthCircumstances: Self-engendered from the primordial waters of Nun, arising on the benben-stone.
nodes.deathCircumstances: In the eschatological vision of Coffin Texts spell 1130, Atum prophesies that at the end of time he will dissolve all created beings back into himself and the cosmos will return to primordial Nun, with only himself and Osiris remaining as serpents in the waters.
nodes.domain_source: Pyramid Texts §1248-49, §1652, §2057 (the primary Heliopolitan source); Coffin Texts; Book of the Dead; the Theology of Heliopolis (preserved across Old Kingdom royal pyramids)
nodes.object_source: Pyramid Texts; Heliopolitan tradition

nodes.name: Chloris
nodes.domain: spring, flowers, new growth, the color green
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess of flowers and spring, identified with Roman Flora
nodes.significantEvent: transformed from the nymph Chloris into the goddess Flora by Zephyrus who married her, given dominion over all flowers
nodes.symbolism: the greening of the world in spring, the nymphs transformation through the touch of the west wind, flowers as the adornment of the earth
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive transformative feminine, the maiden transformed by the masculine wind into the goddess of flowering
nodes.birthCircumstances: nymph who was abducted by Zephyrus the west wind

nodes.name: Palamedes
nodes.domain: invention, writing, strategy, cunning, martyrdom
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the cleverest of the Greeks at Troy
nodes.significantEvent: invented the lighthouse, board games, the alphabet, weights and measures, and military formations, but was framed by Odysseus and Diomedes for treason and stoned to death by the Greek army
nodes.symbolism: the inventor destroyed by the very civilization he serves, intelligence as a threat to political power, the martyr of cunning betrayed by greater cunning
nodes.neumannArchetype: the culture hero whose gifts of consciousness threaten the established order, the Promethean figure destroyed by those he elevates
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Nauplius and Clymene, prince of Euboea

nodes.name: Fusu
nodes.domain: filial piety, righteous succession, tragedy
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: eldest son of Qin Shi Huang, known for his benevolence
nodes.significantEvent: exiled by his father for criticizing the burning of books, after Qin Shi Huangs death the eunuch Zhao Gao forged a decree ordering Fusus suicide to place the younger prince Huhai on the throne, Fusu obeyed and killed himself
nodes.symbolism: the righteous heir destroyed by court intrigue, filial obedience carried to tragic extreme, the good prince who dies because he trusts a false decree
nodes.neumannArchetype: the obedient son destroyed by the corrupt shadow of the dead father, filial piety weaponized by the trickster (Zhao Gao)
nodes.birthCircumstances: eldest son of the First Emperor of China, Qin Shi Huang

nodes.name: Panhu
nodes.domain: ancestor worship, the Yao people, dogs, loyalty, totemism
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: divine dog who became a man, ancestor of the Yao and She peoples
nodes.significantEvent: killed the enemy general during a war by biting off his head, was rewarded with the emperors daughter as his wife, became the ancestor of the Yao and She ethnic groups
nodes.symbolism: the animal ancestor who earns humanity through heroic deed, the totemic origin of ethnic identity, the dog as the loyal servant who becomes the founding father
nodes.neumannArchetype: the theriomorphic ancestor, the animal masculine who earns the feminine (princess) through heroic service and founds a human lineage
nodes.birthCircumstances: originally a five-colored dog owned by Emperor Ku

nodes.name: Tatenen
nodes.domain: earth, creation, the primordial mound, Memphis, vegetation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: man wearing a crown with two tall plumes and ram horns, sometimes with green skin representing vegetation
nodes.significantEvent: the earth that first appeared from the primordial waters, the foundation upon which Atum stood to begin creation, later merged with Ptah as Ptah-Tatenen, the creative earth principle of Memphis
nodes.symbolism: the first land rising from the waters as the beginning of the physical world, the primordial mound as the navel of creation, the earth that precedes and supports all subsequent creation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father as the first solid ground of consciousness, the masculine earth principle that emerges from the uroboric waters as the foundation of ordered reality
nodes.birthCircumstances: personification of the primordial mound (ta-tenen, the risen land) that emerged from Nun at creation

nodes.domain: protection, the afterlife, divine judgment, guidance
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: protective deity associated with the judgment hall and the afterlife journey
nodes.significantEvent: one of the divine beings who assisted the dead in their passage through the afterlife, offering protection and guidance during the journey to the halls of judgment
nodes.symbolism: divine guidance through the afterlife as a sacred escort, the dignified passage through death
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine guide of consciousness through the afterlife journey
nodes.birthCircumstances: He is believed to be either the son of or husband of Nehmetawy and was often depicted near Thoth.

nodes.name: Luna
nodes.domain: the moon, night, cycles, light in darkness, femininity
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful woman with a crescent moon on her head, driving a two-horse chariot across the night sky
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped on the Aventine Hill, her temple was illuminated on the Ides of March, the lunar calendar was sacred to her, farmers planted and harvested according to her phases
nodes.symbolism: the moon as the feminine light that governs the night, the lunar cycles as the rhythm of feminine power, the chariot across the night sky as the journey through darkness
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the luminous nocturnal feminine, the moon-consciousness that illuminates the darkness of the unconscious
nodes.birthCircumstances: identified with the Greek Selene, the Roman goddess of the moon
nodes.deathCircumstances: In 84 BC, it was struck by lightning, the same day the popularis leader Cinna was murdered by his troops.

nodes.name: Fauna
nodes.domain: wildlife, fertility, forests, prophecy, rural life
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess of wildlife and fertility, the feminine aspect of Faunus, associated with forests and wild places
nodes.significantEvent: associated with prophecy and the voices heard in the wild, sometimes identified with the Bona Dea, her rites involved ecstatic trance and communion with wild nature
nodes.symbolism: the wild feminine of the forest who speaks through the voices of nature, prophecy as the language of the wild, the untamed fertile feminine of the Italian woodland
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of the wild, the untamed feminine of the forest whose prophetic voice is the sound of the unconscious wilderness
nodes.birthCircumstances: wife or daughter or sister of Faunus, associated with the Bona Dea

nodes.name: Elpis
nodes.domain: hope, expectation, anticipation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: young woman, sometimes winged, depicted holding flowers or carrying a cornucopia
nodes.significantEvent: remained inside Pandoras jar after all other spirits escaped, debated whether she is a blessing (sustaining mortals) or a curse (deluding them with false expectations)
nodes.symbolism: the ambiguity of hope as both sustaining and deceiving, the one spirit that remains with humanity, the question of whether hope is a gift or the cruelest torment
nodes.neumannArchetype: the ambiguous feminine gift that sustains consciousness even when all other comforts have fled

nodes.name: Palici
nodes.domain: geysers, oaths, agriculture, twin gods, Sicily
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: twin deities born from the earth, associated with geysers and sulphurous pools
nodes.significantEvent: sacred oaths were sworn at their volcanic lake in Sicily, perjurers were struck blind, their sulphurous pools served as natural lie detectors
nodes.symbolism: the volcanic truth that burns liars, oaths sworn on the earths fiery depths, the chthonic twins as agents of truth
nodes.neumannArchetype: the chthonic divine twins born from the Great Mothers volcanic body, truth emerging from the depths of the earth
nodes.birthCircumstances: sons of Zeus (or Hephaestus) and the nymph Aetna (or Thalia), born from the earth itself

nodes.name: Fuxi
nodes.domain: culture-hero, civilization, divination, eight trigrams (bagua), fishing, animal husbandry, marriage
nodes.object: eight trigrams (bagua), knotted cords, fishing net
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: human head and torso with a serpent or dragon tail, sometimes depicted holding the bagua symbol, often paired with his sister-wife Nuwa with their tails intertwined
nodes.significantEvent: invented the eight trigrams (bagua) by studying the patterns on a dragon-horses back and a turtles shell, taught humanity fishing with nets, animal husbandry, cooking with fire, and the institution of marriage
nodes.symbolism: the origin of civilization through observation of natural patterns, the eight trigrams as the key to understanding cosmic order, the serpent-bodied sage as the bridge between the primordial and the civilized
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial culture hero who decodes the Great Mothers patterns (nature) into the system of human knowledge (the trigrams), the first consciousness to read the signs of the cosmos
nodes.birthCircumstances: first of the Three Sovereigns (San Huang), born from his mother Huaxu who became pregnant after stepping in the footprint of the thunder god Leigong
nodes.domain_source: Yijing, Xici II.2 (the canonical bagua/fishing/knotted-cord passage); Lushi (Luo Bi, 12th c.) and Du Yi Zhi (Tang) for marriage with Nüwa. 'Creation' replaced with 'culture-hero' — Fuxi is a civilization-bringer, not a cosmogonic creator (that is Pangu and Nüwa). 'Cooking' demoted: cooking-with-fire is canonically Suiren's gift (Han Feizi 'Wudu'; Huainanzi 'Zhushuxun'). 'Writing' demoted: writing is canonically Cangjie's invention (Lüshi Chunqiu 'Junshou'; Huainanzi 'Benjing'); Fuxi devised knotted cords and the eight trigrams.
nodes.object_source: Yijing, Xici II.2: 古者包犧氏之王天下也...始作八卦 'Anciently, when Bao Xi (Fuxi) ruled the world... he first made the eight trigrams' — also the knotted cords and fishing net in the same passage
nodes.animals_source: Fuxi's lower body is a serpent/dragon tail. Earliest pictorial: Han-dynasty Wu Liang Shrine reliefs (151 CE), with Fuxi and Nüwa human-torsoed and serpent-tailed, tails intertwined. Textual: Wang Yan, Shuyi Ji; Du Yi Zhi. Symbolic embodiment / physical form, correctly in 'animals'. NOTE: tortoise relocated to 'object' below — it is the messenger of the Luo shu, not Fuxi's embodied form.
nodes.object_added_messengers: dragon-horse (lóngmǎ — bearer of the He tu), divine tortoise (bearer of the Luo shu)
nodes.object_messenger_source: Yijing, Xici I.11; Hanshu, Lülizhi; Shangshu, Gu ming commentary
nodes.deathCircumstances_correction_note: CRITICAL CORRECTION: previous deathCircumstances field contained text describing PANGU's body-decomposition narrative ('Pangu then died after standing up, and his body turned into rivers...'), with a stripped Chinese-character expression visible as empty parentheses '()' (likely 華胥 Huáxū). The text was misattributed to Fuxi. Cleared. Fuxi's actual death is sparsely attested: Lushi and the Diwang Shiji tradition give him a long peaceful reign (~115 years) and a tomb at Huaiyang, Henan; no transformation-narrative.
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Sima Zhen, Sanhuang Benji (8th c. supplement to the Shiji); Lushi; Diwang Shiji (3rd c., now lost but cited): 'His mother, Huaxu, trod on the footprint of a giant in the marsh of Leize, and Bao Xi (Fuxi) was conceived.'
nodes.significantEvent_source: Yijing, Xici II.2 (bagua, fishing, animal husbandry); Lushi and Du Yi Zhi (institution of marriage with Nüwa)
nodes.familyRoles_source: husband and brother: Nüwa (Du Yi Zhi); son: Huaxu (Sanhuang Benji)
nodes.eventTypes_source: Yi Jing 'Great Treatise' (Xici 繫辭) II.2; Sima Qian, Shiji ch. 1 (the Five Emperors); Han apocrypha
nodes.birthTypes_source: Wei Shu (Book of Wei); various Han accounts of Huaxu stepping in a giant footprint at Lei-ze
nodes.characterTrait_source: Yi Jing Xici II.2; Sima Qian, Shiji ch. 1; Han chronological literature
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Mawangdui silk paintings (2nd c. BCE); Han stone reliefs (the entwined-tail Fuxi-Nüwa pairs); Six Dynasties iconography

nodes.name: Peng Yue
nodes.domain: war, strategy, the Han founding, tragedy
nodes.characterTrait: strategic, loyal then betrayed, amphibious warfare pioneer
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Han Dynasty general and prince
nodes.significantEvent: played a crucial role in defeating Xiang Yu through guerrilla warfare and river tactics, was later executed by Liu Bangs wife Empress Lu despite promises of safety
nodes.symbolism: the general who is essential to victory but expendable in peace, the founding warriors betrayal by the dynasty he created
nodes.neumannArchetype: the warrior masculine essential for the revolutionary overthrow but destroyed by the new order he helped establish
nodes.birthCircumstances: rebel leader who helped Liu Bang establish the Han Dynasty
nodes.deathCircumstances: Later that year, Peng Yue was accused of treason and executed along with his family.

nodes.name: Aten
nodes.domain: the sun, monotheism, light, truth, the Amarna revolution
nodes.object: sun disk with radiating arms ending in hands holding ankh signs
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: depicted only as the sun disk with rays ending in human hands offering the ankh of life, never anthropomorphized
nodes.significantEvent: Akhenaten declared Aten the sole god of Egypt, closed all other temples, moved the capital to Akhetaten (Amarna), suppressed the cult of Amun, after Akhenatens death the old religion was restored and Atens cult was destroyed
nodes.symbolism: the sun as the sole divine reality, the hands of light offering life, the revolutionary rejection of all other gods, the most radical monotheistic experiment of the ancient world
nodes.neumannArchetype: the absolute solar masculine principle taken to its extreme, the sun-consciousness that attempts to eliminate all other forms of the numinous
nodes.birthCircumstances: elevated to sole god by Pharaoh Akhenaten during the Amarna Period (c. 1353-1336 BCE)

nodes.name: Imentet
nodes.domain: the west, the dead, the afterlife, welcome, the sunset
nodes.object: hieroglyph of the west on her head
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman wearing the hieroglyph for west on her head, arms outstretched to welcome the dead
nodes.significantEvent: welcomed the souls of the dead as they entered the western realm of the afterlife, depicted on tomb walls with outstretched arms receiving the deceased, offered water and food to sustain the newly dead
nodes.symbolism: the west as the realm of the dead where the sun sets, the welcoming arms as the embrace of death, the sunset direction as the gateway to eternal life
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of death who welcomes consciousness into the western realm of the unconscious, the maternal embrace at the threshold of death
nodes.birthCircumstances: personification of the western realm where the dead entered the afterlife

nodes.name: Tutu
nodes.domain: protection, demons, the underworld, apotropaic magic, sphinxes
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: sphinx-like deity with a human head, lions body, wings, and serpent tail, trampling evil spirits
nodes.significantEvent: depicted on apotropaic stelae and amulets trampling dangerous animals and demons, invoked for protection against nightmares and demonic possession, especially popular in the Greco-Roman period
nodes.symbolism: the sphinx as the supreme protector against demons, the composite creature that combines human intelligence with animal power to overcome evil, the trampling of evil as the supreme protective act
nodes.neumannArchetype: the composite masculine hero who combines multiple powers (human, lion, bird, serpent) to overcome the shadow-demons of the unconscious
nodes.birthCircumstances: protective deity who subdued demons and dangerous spirits

nodes.name: Flora
nodes.domain: flowers, spring, fertility, gardens, youth, pleasure
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful young woman crowned with flowers and wearing garlands, scattering blossoms
nodes.significantEvent: her festival Floralia (April 28-May 3) was one of the most exuberant Roman celebrations with theatrical performances, games, and the distribution of flowers, known for its licentiousness and joy
nodes.symbolism: the flower as the promise of fruit, spring as the season of sexual joy, the Floralia as the sanctioned release of restraint, the garland as the crown of natural beauty
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother in her most youthful blooming aspect, the feminine of spring whose flowers are the promise of fertility and fruitfulness
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient Italian goddess of flowering plants and spring

nodes.name: Gonggong
nodes.domain: water, destruction, chaos, the flood, cosmological catastrophe
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: red hair serpentine figure with a human face, lord of floods and chaos
nodes.significantEvent: battled Zhurong (fire god) for supremacy and lost, in his rage he smashed his head against Mount Buzhou (the pillar supporting the northwest sky) breaking the cosmic pillar and tilting the heavens, causing the great flood that Nuwa had to repair
nodes.symbolism: the destructive power of water unchained, chaos as the result of cosmic rage, the broken pillar as the fracturing of the world order, the flood as the consequence of primordial conflict
nodes.neumannArchetype: the destructive water dragon whose rage shatters the cosmic structure, the shadow of the sky father who breaks the world pillar in his fury
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the oldest Chinese deities, a water god and adversary of cosmic order

nodes.name: Doris
nodes.domain: sea bounty, the mixing of fresh and salt water, fish
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Oceanid goddess of the rich fishing grounds where rivers meet the sea
nodes.significantEvent: married the sea god Nereus and bore the fifty Nereids, the gentle sea nymphs
nodes.symbolism: the bounty of the sea where fresh water meets salt, the fertile mixing zone, the oceanic mother of gentle sea spirits
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive oceanic mother whose union with the Old Man of the Sea produces the benign feminine spirits of the ocean
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Oceanus and Tethys

nodes.name: Pasikrata
nodes.domain: death, the underworld, absolute power
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: epithet of Persephone as the absolute ruler of the dead
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped as Pasikrata (All-Powerful) in her aspect as the dread queen of the underworld who rules all the dead without exception
nodes.symbolism: Persephone at her most terrible, the maiden who became the absolute queen of death, the totality of underworld power
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as absolute ruler of the realm of death, the kore transformed into the terrible queen

nodes.name: Qianliyan
nodes.domain: clairvoyance, the supernatural, long-distance seeing, protection
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: deity with the ability to see a thousand li (miles), one of a pair with Shunfeng Er (Wind-Following Ear)
nodes.significantEvent: together with his companion Shunfeng Er (Thousand-Mile Ear) he serves as the eyes and ears of the sea goddess Mazu, watching over sailors and fishermen, seen in pairs flanking Mazu in her temples
nodes.symbolism: supernatural perception as a divine gift, the complementary senses of sight and hearing protecting the vulnerable, the subdued demon transformed into a guardian
nodes.neumannArchetype: the transformed shadow (former demon) who becomes the all-seeing eye of the protective Great Mother (Mazu)
nodes.birthCircumstances: originally a demon subdued by the goddess Mazu and converted into her servant

nodes.name: Anat
nodes.domain: war, love, sexuality, hunting, the Near East
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman wearing the atef crown or a tall conical crown, carrying weapons, a Near Eastern goddess adopted into the Egyptian pantheon
nodes.significantEvent: given to Set as a wife by Ra to placate him after his defeat by Horus, worshipped in the New Kingdom as a war goddess by Ramesses II and other warrior pharaohs
nodes.symbolism: the foreign war goddess as the consort of chaos (Set), the union of love and war in a single deity, the Near Eastern feminine power adopted into Egyptian religion
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible feminine of war and sexuality, the anima in her dual aspect of attraction and destruction, the foreign Great Mother integrated into the native pantheon
nodes.birthCircumstances: Semitic goddess of war and love adopted into the Egyptian pantheon during the New Kingdom

nodes.name: Hededet
nodes.domain: scorpions, protection, magic, the underworld
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: scorpion goddess of protection, often depicted as a scorpion
nodes.significantEvent: protected against scorpion stings and other venomous creatures, associated with the protection of the dead in the underworld
nodes.symbolism: the scorpion as the guardian whose sting both threatens and protects, the apotropaic power of the dangerous creature turned protector
nodes.neumannArchetype: the dangerous feminine turned protectress, the venomous Great Mother whose sting defends

nodes.name: Bellona
nodes.domain: war, destruction, bloodshed, foreign war
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: fierce woman in armor and helmet wielding a bloody sword and torch, hair wild, sometimes driving a war chariot
nodes.significantEvent: her temple on the Campus Martius was where the Senate met foreign ambassadors and declared war, the ritual of throwing a spear over the columna bellica in front of her temple officially declared war on foreign nations
nodes.symbolism: the feminine face of war as bloodshed and destruction, the war declaration ritual as the sacred initiation of violence, the torch of war as the burning of civilization
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible Great Mother of war, the destructive feminine whose bloodlust fuels the masculine military enterprise
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient Roman war goddess, sometimes identified with the Greek Enyo, sister or wife of Mars

nodes.name: Carmenta
nodes.domain: prophecy, childbirth, writing, invention, the future
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: prophetic goddess and divine midwife, associated with the invention of the Latin alphabet
nodes.significantEvent: her festival Carmentalia was celebrated on January 11 and 15, she had two aspects: Antevorta (who saw the future) and Postverta (who saw the past), credited with inventing the Latin alphabet, her shrine was at the Porta Carmentalis in Rome
nodes.symbolism: the prophetic feminine who sees both forward and backward in time, the midwife as the prophetess of each new life, the invention of writing as a feminine gift, the gate named for the prophetess
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the seer who encompasses past and future, the feminine oracle at the gate of consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient Roman goddess of prophecy and childbirth, mother of Evander
