nodes.name: Goumang
nodes.domain: spring, wood, the east, agriculture, growth
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: deity with a birds body and human face, carries a compass, presides over the spring and the east
nodes.significantEvent: presides over the season of spring and the sprouting of all plant life, carries a compass symbolizing the creative order of spring growth
nodes.symbolism: the organized growth of spring, the wood element as the energy of new life, the eastern direction as the source of renewal
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive masculine as the orderer of spring growth, the assistant to the Great Father who ensures the renewal of vegetation
nodes.birthCircumstances: assistant to the god Taihao (Fuxi), minister of the east and spring

nodes.name: Qin Qiong秦瓊
nodes.domain: war, door protection, martial virtue, the Tang Dynasty
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: armored warrior carrying twin maces, one of the two door gods (Men Shen)
nodes.significantEvent: together with Yuchi Gong stood guard outside Emperor Taizongs bedroom to ward off nightmares and demons, the emperor had their images painted on his doors and they became the archetypal Chinese door gods (Men Shen)
nodes.symbolism: the warrior who becomes the divine protector of the threshold, the image of the loyal general that wards off evil from every Chinese doorway, martial virtue as domestic protection
nodes.neumannArchetype: the threshold guardian whose image (persona) protects the domestic space from the intrusion of evil (the shadow)
nodes.birthCircumstances: historical Tang Dynasty general (571-638 CE) who served Emperor Taizong

nodes.name: Set
nodes.domain: chaos, storms, the desert, foreigners, violence, disorder, strength
nodes.characterTrait: chaotic, violent, powerful, jealous, necessary, protective
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: man with the head of an unidentified animal (the Set animal) with a long curved snout, tall rectangular ears, and forked tail
nodes.significantEvent: murdered his brother Osiris out of jealousy, dismembered his body, fought his nephew Horus for the throne of Egypt in an epic series of contests, despite being the villain of the Osiris myth he protected Ra on the solar barque by slaying the serpent Apophis each night
nodes.symbolism: necessary chaos within order, the desert as the sterile counterpart to the fertile Nile, the outsider who is also the defender, the storm that destroys and purifies, cosmic disorder as an essential force
nodes.neumannArchetype: the archetypal shadow brother, the dark masculine whose violence is both destructive (murdering Osiris) and necessary (protecting Ra from Apophis), the chaos that tests and strengthens cosmic order
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Geb and Nut, born by tearing himself violently from his mothers side
nodes.object_source: Standard Sethian iconography; was-scepter (the Set-animal-headed scepter)
nodes.animals_source: The Set-animal (a distinctive creature with curved snout and squared ears, not identifiable with any real-world animal); also associated with the donkey (negatively); the pig (negatively, in Plutarch); the hippopotamus (negatively, the form in which Horus pursued him)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Plutarch 13-20; Contendings of Horus and Set
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Plutarch 12; Pyramid Texts

nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard Sethian iconography
nodes.birthTypes_source: Plutarch 12

nodes.name: Chalchiuhtecolotl
nodes.domain: owls, darkness, sorcery, chalchihuites (jade), nocturnal spirits
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Jade Owl or Precious Night Bird, a supernatural owl deity associated with darkness and sorcery
nodes.significantEvent: associated with darkness, sorcery, and nocturnal supernatural activity, the owl as a bird of ill omen in Aztec religion
nodes.symbolism: the jade owl as the precious bird of darkness, the owl as the voice of the night, sorcery as the art of the nocturnal jade-spirit
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow-owl of the unconscious night, the nocturnal numinous that sees in the darkness where consciousness cannot

nodes.name: Atlas
nodes.domain: endurance, astronomy, the heavens, cartography
nodes.characterTrait: enduring, knowledgeable, burdened, wise in astronomy
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: enormous Titan bearing the heavens on his shoulders, straining under the cosmic weight
nodes.significantEvent: condemned by Zeus to hold up the sky after the Titans defeat in the Titanomachy, tricked by Heracles during the quest for the golden apples of the Hesperides, turned to stone by Perseus using Medusas head
nodes.symbolism: the burden of cosmic knowledge, the weight of holding the world together, endurance under impossible obligation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Titan who bears the weight of the separation between heaven and earth, embodying the burden of cosmic consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of the Titan Iapetus and the Oceanid Asia or Clymene, brother of Prometheus, Epimetheus, and Menoetius

nodes.domain: childbirth, labor pains, midwifery
nodes.characterTrait: birth-bringing, sometimes obstructing, powerful over labor
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman in labor position, or standing with arms raised, sometimes veiled
nodes.significantEvent: Hera sent her to delay the birth of Heracles and hasten the birth of Eurystheus, her Cretan cave cult predates Olympian religion
nodes.symbolism: the divine power over the moment of birth, the feminine mystery of bringing life into the world, the threshold between nonexistence and existence
nodes.neumannArchetype: the birth goddess representing the generative power of the Great Mother, the feminine as the gate through which all life must pass
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Zeus and Hera, or an ancient pre-Olympian Cretan goddess

nodes.name: Dyssebeia
nodes.domain: impiety, ungodliness, irreverence
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: spirit of impiety, the opposite of Eusebeia
nodes.significantEvent: personification of the refusal to honor the gods, associated with moral decay
nodes.symbolism: the rejection of sacred obligations, the root of civilizational decay in Greek thought
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow of the sacred, the refusal of consciousness to acknowledge the numinous
nodes.birthCircumstances: "I have a timely word of advice: arrogance (hybris) is truly the child of impiety (dyssebia), but from health of soul comes happiness, dear to all, much prayed for.

nodes.name: Comus
nodes.domain: revelry, festivity, merry-making, comedy
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: winged youth carrying a torch and wearing a wreath of flowers, sometimes depicted drowsy with wine
nodes.significantEvent: presides over nighttime festivals and revels, the patron of merry-making that follows banquets
nodes.symbolism: the joy of nocturnal celebration, festivity as a sacred release, the divine permission to revel
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Dionysiac masculine in its lightest and most playful aspect, revelry as a path to joy
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Dionysus and Circe in some traditions

nodes.name: Patroclus
nodes.domain: friendship, war, sacrifice, devotion
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: strong and compassionate warrior, wearing borrowed armor
nodes.significantEvent: when the Greeks were losing at Troy he begged Achilles for his armor and led the Myrmidons into battle, drove the Trojans back to their walls but was killed by Hector, his death motivated Achilles to return to battle
nodes.symbolism: the devoted friend whose death is the catalyst for the greatest warriors return, borrowed identity (Achilles armor) as both strength and doom, friendship as the deepest bond of the heroic world
nodes.neumannArchetype: the alter ego or shadow of the supreme hero, the gentle masculine whose death reactivates the terrible masculine (Achilles)
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Menoetius, raised alongside Achilles in the house of Peleus after accidentally killing a playmate

nodes.name: Eiresione
nodes.domain: olive harvest, peace, supplication, fertility
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: olive or laurel branch wreathed in wool and hung with fruits and small vessels
nodes.significantEvent: carried in procession during the Pyanopsia and Thargelia festivals, hung on doors as a charm for abundance
nodes.symbolism: the olive branch as prayer for abundance, the decorated branch as a bridge between human need and divine generosity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the sacred branch as the connection between the earth mother and human sustenance

nodes.name: Cybele
nodes.domain: earth, nature, motherhood, fertility, wild animals, mountains
nodes.object: tympanum, mural crown, libation bowl, chariot
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: seated, crowned with city walls, robed
nodes.significantEvent: Stone of Pessinus moved to Rome; strangled victims as Gorgon
nodes.symbolism: Mother Goddess who 'strangled them as Gorgon, as Cybele'; stone cult; from Pessinus to Rome
nodes.neumannArchetype: Mother Goddess who 'strangled them as Gorgon, as Cybele.'

nodes.name: Odysseus
nodes.domain: cunning, seafaring, homecoming, strategy, survival
nodes.characterTrait: cunning, resourceful, eloquent, enduring, deceptive, loyal to home
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: short but broad-shouldered, auburn-haired, scarred on the thigh by a boar
nodes.significantEvent: devised the Trojan Horse to end the Trojan War, wandered ten years facing Cyclops Polyphemus and Circe and Scylla and the Sirens, returned home to slay the suitors of Penelope
nodes.symbolism: the triumph of intelligence over brute force, the longing for home as the deepest human drive, the hero who survives through cunning rather than strength
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hero of consciousness who navigates the perils of the unconscious (sea monsters, enchantresses, the underworld) through intelligence and endurance
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Laertes and Anticlea, king of Ithaca, though some traditions name Sisyphus as his true father

nodes.name: Cadmus
nodes.domain: civilization, writing, founding of cities, the alphabet
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Phoenician prince, founder hero of Thebes
nodes.significantEvent: slew the dragon sacred to Ares at the future site of Thebes, sowed its teeth which grew into armed warriors (the Spartoi), founded Thebes, brought the Phoenician alphabet to Greece, transformed into a serpent in old age
nodes.symbolism: the transmission of writing and civilization from East to West, the founding of cities from violence (the sown teeth), the curse that follows the slaying of the sacred
nodes.neumannArchetype: the culture hero who brings the tools of consciousness (writing) from the older civilization to the new
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of King Agenor and Queen Telephassa of Tyre, brother of Europa

nodes.name: Iris
nodes.domain: rainbow, divine messages, communication between gods and mortals, the sea
nodes.object: pitcher of Styx water, caduceus, rainbow
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: golden-winged goddess trailing a rainbow across the sky, carrying a pitcher
nodes.significantEvent: serves as messenger of the gods particularly Hera, carries water from the River Styx for divine oaths, in the Iliad she acts as messenger between gods and mortals
nodes.symbolism: the rainbow as bridge between heaven and earth, divine communication, the faithful servant of the cosmic order
nodes.neumannArchetype: the mediating feminine that connects the divine and human realms, the rainbow bridge between consciousness and the unconscious
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the sea god Thaumas and the Oceanid Electra, sister of the Harpies

nodes.name: Anagyros
nodes.domain: heroism, Attic cult
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: local Attic hero with a sacred grove
nodes.significantEvent: an old man who cut down trees in his sacred grove was cursed, giving rise to the proverb do not move Anagyros meaning do not provoke a sleeping evil
nodes.symbolism: the sanctity of sacred groves, the slumbering hero whose anger must not be provoked
nodes.neumannArchetype: the chthonic hero whose wrath guards the sacred trees of the Great Mother
nodes.birthCircumstances: Angered, the concubine reported back to the old man and falsely accused the son of sexually assaulting her.

nodes.neumannArchetype: the loyal son who mirrors and continues the fathers warrior path, dying together as the ultimate expression of patriarchal loyalty

nodes.birthCircumstances: son of the river god Inachus and the nymph Melia

nodes.neumannArchetype: the river father whose daughter generates the dying-and-rising god (Attis) of the Great Mother
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Oceanus and Tethys

nodes.name: Zhao Yun
nodes.domain: war, loyalty, bravery, the Three Kingdoms, single combat, filial duty
nodes.object: spear, white horse, Azure Dragon sword (later)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: young warrior of extraordinary bravery on a white horse, known as the Little Dragon
nodes.significantEvent: single-handedly rescued Liu Beis infant son Liu Shan from the Battle of Changban, riding through Cao Caos entire army with the baby tucked inside his armor, one of the Five Tiger Generals of Shu Han
nodes.symbolism: the lone warrior who rescues the future through an act of supreme bravery, the white horse knight who saves the infant heir, individual valor that changes the course of history
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hero who rescues the divine child from the enemy, the white-horse knight whose individual courage preserves the future of the kingdom
nodes.birthCircumstances: warrior from Changshan who served Liu Bei through the Three Kingdoms period

nodes.name: Wadjet
nodes.domain: protection, Lower Egypt, the cobra, the throne, royalty
nodes.characterTrait: protective, royal, fiery, cobra-formed, Lower Egyptian
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: rearing cobra (uraeus) or woman with a cobra head, often depicted on the pharaohs crown as the protective uraeus
nodes.significantEvent: her image as the uraeus cobra on the pharaohs brow spat fire at enemies, paired with Nekhbet (vulture of Upper Egypt) as the Two Ladies who together protected unified Egypt
nodes.symbolism: the cobra as the concentrated flame of royal protection, the uraeus as the visible sign of divine authority, Lower Egypt personified as the striking serpent
nodes.neumannArchetype: the protective feminine as the fiery serpent, the Great Mothers concentrated defensive power worn on the brow of the patriarchal ruler
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient cobra goddess of Buto (Pe and Dep) in Lower Egypt, one of the Two Ladies protecting Egypt

nodes.symbolism: need as the mother of desire, poverty as the driving force behind ingenuity and love, want as the creative principle that seeks fulfillment
nodes.neumannArchetype: the deprived feminine that generates Eros through union with the unconscious masculine (sleeping Plenty), need as the origin of longing

nodes.domain: hope, expectation, the future, youth, new beginnings
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: young woman holding a flower bud (not yet bloomed) and lifting her skirts to walk forward, personification of hope

nodes.symbolism: the unopened flower bud as hope not yet realized, the forward-walking posture as the movement toward the future, hope as a youthful feminine quality that persists through adversity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of the future, the feminine that carries the unborn possibility forward

nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow Great Mother, the dark feminine who patronizes the transgressive and the criminal

nodes.domain: truce, armistice, the Olympic truce
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: personification of the sacred truce, depicted in statuary at Olympia

nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible aspect of the Great Mother of fate, the feminine death that cuts the thread of consciousness

nodes.significantEvent: the ancient sea god, less attested than his son Manannan but represents the primordial sea itself, father of the famous sea-and-otherworld god
nodes.symbolism: the sea as the primordial father, the deep ocean as the ancient masculine, the paternal sea whose son becomes the more famous sea god
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial Great Father of the sea, the masculine of the oceanic depths from whom the more active sea-consciousness (Manannan) descends

nodes.symbolism: political freedom as a divine gift, liberty as a sacred feminine quality earned through struggle
nodes.neumannArchetype: the liberating feminine that frees consciousness from bondage
nodes.birthCircumstances: Hyginus describes Eleutheria as a daughter of Zeus and Hera.

nodes.name: Guan Yu
nodes.domain: war, righteousness, loyalty, brotherhood, protection, commerce
nodes.object: Green Dragon Crescent Blade (guandao), Red Hare horse
nodes.characterTrait: loyal, righteous, fierce, honorable, red-faced, incorruptible
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: imposing warrior with a distinctive red face, long black beard, and piercing eyes, usually depicted in green robes holding his great guandao
nodes.significantEvent: took an oath of brotherhood in the Peach Garden, refused enormous bribes from Cao Cao out of loyalty to Liu Bei, read the Spring and Autumn Annals by candlelight, became the most widely worshipped deity in Chinese folk religion as Guan Di (Emperor Guan)
nodes.symbolism: the supreme embodiment of loyalty and righteousness (yi), the red face as the visible sign of loyalty and courage, the warrior-scholar who reads classics and wields a great blade, the brotherhood oath as the highest form of human bond
nodes.neumannArchetype: the supreme positive masculine as the warrior of righteousness, the archetypal hero whose loyalty transcends death and elevates him to godhood
nodes.birthCircumstances: historical general of the late Eastern Han Dynasty (died 220 CE), sworn brother of Liu Bei and Zhang Fei
nodes.deathCircumstances: He was subsequently captured in an ambush by Sun Quan's forces and executed at Linju, Xiangyang Commandery (, present-day Nanzhang County, Xiangyang City, Hubei).

nodes.symbolism: the universal Great Goddess as the supreme feminine divine principle, the Magna Dea as the acknowledgment that behind all specific goddesses stands a single great feminine power
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother archetype itself, the supreme feminine principle that underlies all specific goddess manifestations

nodes.significantEvent: imprisoned by her father Balor in a crystal tower to prevent her from bearing the grandson prophesied to kill him, but Cian reached her and she bore the god Lugh, who fulfilled the prophecy
nodes.symbolism: the imprisoned princess as the feminine locked away by the tyrant-father, the crystal tower as the beautiful prison, the birth of the hero despite all attempts to prevent it, the bridge between enemy races through the maternal
nodes.neumannArchetype: the captive anima imprisoned by the terrible father, the feminine that gives birth to the hero despite the patriarchal attempt to prevent the prophecy
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Balor of the Evil Eye

nodes.name: Arensnuphis
nodes.domain: Nubia, the hunt, the wind, Philae, Greco-Nubian syncretism
nodes.object: crown with double feathers, bow, spear
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Nubian deity depicted wearing a feathered crown, carrying a spear and bow
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped at Philae alongside Isis, his temple at Philae shows the integration of Nubian and Egyptian religious traditions
nodes.symbolism: the Nubian masculine warrior integrated into Egyptian temple worship, the wind as the hunters companion, the syncretic meeting of African and Mediterranean religions
nodes.neumannArchetype: the foreign masculine hunter integrated into the worship of the Great Mother (Isis) at Philae
nodes.birthCircumstances: Meroitic Nubian deity adopted into the Egyptian pantheon during the Ptolemaic period

nodes.domain: destruction, sacking of cities, the Titan of devastation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Titan of destruction and devastation
nodes.significantEvent: father of Hecate by the Titaness Asteria, fought against the Olympians in the Titanomachy and was imprisoned in Tartarus
nodes.symbolism: the destructive Titan whose daughter (Hecate) is honored even by the new gods, destruction as a cosmic principle that generates the goddess of magic
nodes.neumannArchetype: the destroying Titan whose offspring mediates between the old and new orders
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of the Titans Crius and Eurybia, brother of Astraeus and Pallas

nodes.domain: dawn, the awakening, the morning

nodes.symbolism: the maiden of dawn, the light that awakens the world each morning, virginal radiance
nodes.neumannArchetype: the luminous maiden archetype, the daughter of the sun as the dawn of consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Helios (Sun) and Rhode, or another nymph

nodes.name: Guang Chengzi
nodes.domain: Daoism, immortality, cultivation, wisdom
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: ancient Daoist immortal master, one of the Twelve Golden Immortals
nodes.significantEvent: one of the great Daoist masters of Kunlun Mountain in the Fengshen Yanyi, taught the Yellow Emperor the arts of Daoist cultivation
nodes.symbolism: the ancient master who transmits the Way to the sage-king, Daoist cultivation as the highest form of wisdom
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wise old man archetype, the master who transmits consciousness-transforming knowledge to the hero-king
nodes.deathCircumstances: He had sacrificed many years of solitude and had emerged as an immortal.

nodes.name: Pudicitia
nodes.domain: modesty, chastity, sexual virtue, shame
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: veiled woman in modest attire, personification of sexual modesty and chastity
nodes.significantEvent: had two shrines in Rome: one on the Vicus Longus for patrician women and one on the Vicus Longus for plebeian women, representing the importance of sexual virtue across all social classes, scandals violated her sanctity
nodes.symbolism: the veil as the concealment of the feminine from the public gaze, modesty as a social and divine virtue, chastity as a civic contribution, the separation of patrician and plebeian modesty
nodes.neumannArchetype: the veiled feminine, the anima concealed behind the social requirements of patriarchal sexual virtue

nodes.name: Huehueteotl
nodes.domain: fire, the old god, volcanoes, the hearth, the center, age and wisdom
nodes.characterTrait: ancient, fiery, wise, hearth-dwelling, volcano-associated, central
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Old Old God, depicted as an ancient hunched figure with a brazier or incense burner on his head
nodes.significantEvent: the oldest fire deity, depicted as an ancient man bearing the fire on his head, associated with volcanoes and the center of the home, closely identified with Xiuhtecuhtli (the Turquoise Lord)
nodes.symbolism: the old god bearing fire on his head as the burden of ancient wisdom, the volcano as the old fires home, the hearth as the center of domestic and cosmic order, age as the quality of the most primal element
nodes.neumannArchetype: the senex of fire, the oldest patriarchal consciousness whose fire is both the center of the home and the volcanic fury of the earth
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the oldest Mesoamerican deities, worshipped since before the Aztec period

nodes.name: Cian
nodes.domain: the Tuatha De Danann, fatherhood, Lugh, the quest against Balor
nodes.characterTrait: heroic, questing, fatherly, Lugh-siring, Tuatha De Danann
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a warrior of the Tuatha De Danann, father of the great god Lugh
nodes.significantEvent: reached the imprisoned Ethniu in Balors tower and fathered Lugh, who would grow up to kill Balor and lead the Tuatha De Danann to victory, Cian was later murdered by the sons of Tuireann
nodes.symbolism: the father who reaches the imprisoned princess to sire the hero, the murder of the father as the sacrifice that precedes the heros triumph
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine that penetrates the tyrants defenses to reach the captive feminine and sire the solar hero
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Dian Cecht (the physician god) of the Tuatha De Danann

nodes.name: Iat
nodes.domain: milk, nourishment, the afterlife, sustenance
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess associated with milk and nourishment in the afterlife
nodes.significantEvent: provided the dead with milk and sustenance in the afterlife, ensuring the continued nourishment of the soul after death
nodes.symbolism: milk as the sustenance of both the living and the dead, nourishment that transcends death, the divine milk of eternal life
nodes.neumannArchetype: the nourishing Great Mother whose milk sustains consciousness even after death

nodes.symbolism: divine foresight as a feminine quality that protects the state, the globe as the world in the hands of providence, planning as a sacred act
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine of divine foresight, the anima that sees and plans for the future of consciousness

nodes.name: Prometheus
nodes.domain: fire, civilization, forethought, craftsmanship, humanity
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Titan bound to a rock in the Caucasus, an eagle eating his regenerating liver
nodes.significantEvent: stole fire from the gods and gave it to humanity, tricked Zeus with the division of sacrificial meat, punished by being chained to a rock where an eagle ate his liver daily, eventually freed by Heracles
nodes.symbolism: the defiant gift of consciousness to humanity, knowledge gained through divine transgression and eternal suffering, forethought as the defining human capacity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the culture hero who separates from the Great Mother and brings the fire of consciousness to humanity, suffering eternally for this act of liberation
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of the Titan Iapetus and the Oceanid Clymene or Asia

nodes.name: Pasiphaë
nodes.domain: magic, sorcery, oracles, the bestial
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful queen and sorceress, daughter of the sun
nodes.significantEvent: cursed by Poseidon to fall in love with the Cretan Bull as punishment for Minos breaking his vow, commissioned Daedalus to build a wooden cow so she could mate with the bull, gave birth to the Minotaur
nodes.symbolism: the monstrous consequence of broken vows to the gods, the feminine punished through bestial desire, the solar lineage (Helios) twisted into darkness
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother in her terrible and transgressive aspect, bearing the monster that dwells at the center of the labyrinth
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Helios the sun god and the Oceanid Perse, sister of Circe and Aeetes, aunt of Medea
nodes.deathCircumstances: Minos refused to sacrifice the animal, and sacrificed another, inferior bull instead.

nodes.name: Dactyls
nodes.domain: metalworking, magic, music, the forge
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: small finger-sized beings associated with the forge and mountains
nodes.significantEvent: discovered iron-working and metallurgy on Mount Ida, invented rhythm and musical measures, associated with the Mysteries of Samothrace
nodes.symbolism: the magical origin of metalworking, the creative fingers of the earth mother, craft as a divine mystery
nodes.neumannArchetype: the creative dwarfs born from the Great Mothers labor, the miniature masculine as the agent of transformative craft
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from the earth of Mount Ida when Rhea (or Cybele) pressed her fingers into the soil during the birth pangs of Zeus

nodes.name: Sophia
nodes.tradition: Abrahamic / Gnostic (Wisdom literature continuum, from Proverbs through Gnostic systems)
nodes.domain: feminine personification of divine wisdom; God's first-created or eternally-present companion at creation; the calling-out wisdom of the city gates; in Christian theology identified with Christ as "the wisdom of God" (1 Corinthians 1:24); in Gnostic systems an emanation, sometimes fallen, sometimes restored; Hebrew ḥokmâ, Greek sophia
nodes.object: house with seven pillars (Proverbs 9:1); banquet (Proverbs 9:2-6); the lifegiving tree (Proverbs 3:18); the law/Torah (Sirach 24:23 explicitly identifies Wisdom with Torah)
nodes.characterTrait: discerning, calling-out, just, ordering, present-at-creation, life-giving (Proverbs 8:35), justice-loving, in Gnostic systems sometimes errant-then-restored
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Feminine personification — calls aloud at the city gates (Proverbs 1:20-21, 8:1-3); has a house, sets a banquet, sends out maidservants (Proverbs 9:1-3); is "a breath of the power of God, a pure emanation of the glory of the Almighty" (Wisdom 7:25). In Gnostic systems she is variously the lower Sophia (Achamoth) who falls and produces the demiurge (Yaldabaoth), the higher Sophia who remains in the Pleroma, or both.
nodes.significantEvent: Present at creation as God's craftsman ('āmôn) or beloved (Proverbs 8:22-31). Calls out at the city gates inviting people to her banquet (Proverbs 9:1-6). In Sirach 24, sets up her tent in Israel and is identified with the Torah. In Wisdom of Solomon 7, "a reflection of eternal light, a spotless mirror of the working of God". In the New Testament, identified with Christ as "the wisdom of God" (1 Cor 1:24, 30). In Gnostic systems (Apocryphon of John), the lower Sophia (Achamoth) seeks to know the Father independently of her consort, brings forth the demiurge Yaldabaoth, and falls; her restoration is part of cosmic redemption.
nodes.symbolism: Good Mother projection; positive anima figure; represents wisdom and spiritual transformation; counterpart to Gorgon
nodes.neumannArchetype: Represents the Good Mother projection, the positive pole of the Archetypal Feminine.
familyRoles: consort or feminine emanation in Gnostic systems
nodes.birthCircumstances: Begotten/possessed/created by YHWH at the beginning, before the world (Proverbs 8:22-25). In Gnostic systems, an emanation from the Pleroma.
nodes.domain_source: Proverbs 1:20-33, 8:1-36, 9:1-12 (the major Wisdom-as-feminine personification); Job 28; Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 24; Wisdom of Solomon 6-9; Baruch 3:9-4:4; 1 Corinthians 1:18-31; Gnostic sources — Apocryphon of John (NHC II,1), Pistis Sophia, Sophia of Jesus Christ
nodes.object_source: Proverbs 9:1-6, 3:18; Sirach 24:23
nodes.characterTrait_source: Proverbs 8; Wisdom of Solomon 6-9; Apocryphon of John
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Proverbs 1, 8, 9; Wisdom of Solomon 7-8; Gnostic literature
nodes.significantEvent_source: Proverbs 8:22-31, 9:1-6; Sirach 24; Wisdom 7-8; 1 Corinthians 1:24-30; Apocryphon of John passim
nodes.birthTypes_source: Proverbs 8:22-25 — qānānî is contested in translation (LXX ektisen "created" vs. Hebrew "possessed/begotten"), with major implications for Arian-Nicene controversies
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Proverbs 8:22-31

nodes.name: Yaksha
nodes.domain: nature spirits, treasure, forests, earth, guardianship, wealth
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: nature spirits depicted as dwarfish but powerful beings, guardians of treasures and forests
nodes.significantEvent: yakshas are among the most ancient and widespread of Hindu supernatural beings, they guard treasures, forests, and sacred sites, their king Kubera is the god of wealth, they can be benevolent or dangerous
nodes.symbolism: the nature spirit as the guardian of the earths wealth, the yaksha as the bridge between the wild and the civilized, the dwarfish guardian as the chthonic keeper of hidden treasure
nodes.neumannArchetype: the chthonic guardians of the earths treasure, the nature-consciousness that protects the wealth of the unconscious depths

nodes.name: Corus
nodes.domain: surfeit, satiety, excess, arrogance born of plenty
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: spirit of insolent excess born from too much prosperity
nodes.significantEvent: associated with the moral sequence: prosperity leads to koros (surfeit), surfeit leads to hybris (arrogance), hybris leads to ate (ruin)
nodes.symbolism: the dangerous excess of prosperity that breeds arrogance, the fatal sequence from wealth to downfall
nodes.neumannArchetype: the inflation of consciousness from too much abundance, the psychic excess that precedes the fall
nodes.birthCircumstances: child of Hybris (Hubris) in some accounts

nodes.name: Kali
nodes.domain: war, death, time (kāla), demon-slaying, blood-drinking, cremation grounds, sacrifice (Tantric)
nodes.object: sword (khaḍga), severed head, skull-bowl (kapāla), girdle of severed hands, garland of skulls (muṇḍamālā)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: dark-skinned (kṛṣṇa-vārṇa, the 'black one'), many-armed (typically four-armed in Devī Māhātmya, ten or eighteen in Tantric forms), gaping mouth with lolling red tongue, gaunt/emaciated, sunken eyes, three-eyed, often naked (digambarā) in Tantric forms, sometimes shown standing on the supine Śiva
nodes.significantEvent: Emerges from Durgā's furrowed brow in the form of fanged Kālī to slay the demon-generals Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, earning the name Cāmuṇḍā. Slays the demon Raktabīja by drinking his blood from the kapāla before drops can hit the ground and spawn duplicates. Joins Durgā in the destruction of Śumbha and Niśumbha. (Tantric:) standing on the supine Śiva to halt her dance of destruction.
nodes.symbolism: Terrible Mother archetype; 'dark, all-devouring time'; stands on Shiva's corpse; devouring feminine
nodes.neumannArchetype: Primary example of the Terrible Mother. 'Dark, all-devouring time.' Stands on Shiva's corpse.
nodes.birthCircumstances: Emanates from the furrowed brow of the goddess Durgā as her wrathful form when Durgā is enraged by the demons Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa.
nodes.domain_source: Devī Māhātmya (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa 81-93), chapters 7-8; Kālikā Purāṇa; Tantric texts (Mahānirvāṇa Tantra)
nodes.object_source: Devī Māhātmya 7-8; Tantric iconography
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Devī Māhātmya 7-8; Tantric iconography
nodes.significantEvent_source: Devī Māhātmya 7-8 (Cāmuṇḍā; Raktabīja); Liṅga Purāṇa (Dāruka)
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Devī Māhātmya 7
nodes.familyRoles_source: 'Mother' role is Tantric / Bengali Śākta (post-Devī Māhātmya). In the Devī Māhātmya itself she is an aspect of the Devī, not a discrete maternal figure.
nodes.characterTrait_source: Devī Māhātmya 7-8; Tantric tradition
nodes.birthTypes_source: Devī Māhātmya 7

nodes.name: Tara
nodes.domain: compassion, liberation, protection, guidance
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: green or white, seated in lotus, crowned, youthful
nodes.significantEvent: 'Mistress of boats, capable of pacifying the watery flood'; savioress; 'the wise worship me as Tara'
nodes.symbolism: Great Good Goddess; Stella Maris parallel to Madonna and Isis; 'redeeming one' (Tarini)
nodes.neumannArchetype: Great Good Goddess paralleling Madonna and Isis as Stella Maris.

nodes.name: Amano-Iwato
nodes.domain: the cave of heaven, darkness, divine withdrawal, the crisis of the sun
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Heavenly Rock Cave into which Amaterasu withdrew, plunging the world into darkness
nodes.significantEvent: when Amaterasu withdrew into Ama-no-Iwato after Susanoos outrages, the world was plunged into eternal darkness and evil spirits ran rampant, the assembled gods had to devise a plan to lure her out, which succeeded through Ame-no-Uzumes dance and the mirror
nodes.symbolism: the cave as the withdrawal of divine light into the unconscious, the darkness as the world without the solar feminine, the boulder as the barrier between consciousness and the divine, the luring-out as the recovery of light through art and laughter
nodes.neumannArchetype: the cave of the unconscious into which the solar Great Mother withdraws, the darkness of ego-death from which consciousness must be recovered through creative and ecstatic means

nodes.name: Aphrodite
nodes.domain: love, beauty, desire, sexuality, war, seafaring
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: golden, irresistibly beautiful, naked or lightly robed, born from sea foam
nodes.significantEvent: Also goddess of war in Sparta and Cyprus; enchants and ruins men
nodes.symbolism: irresistible desire, beauty as both creative and destructive force, the power of sexuality over gods and mortals alike
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Transformative Feminine as enchantress, the anima figure who enchants and ruins through desire
familyRoles: born from sea-foam; pre-Olympian generation in Hesiodic genealogy (an alternative tradition makes her daughter of Zeus and Dione)
mother of Eros, Anteros, Phobos, Deimos, Harmonia (by Ares); Aeneas (by Anchises); Hermaphroditus (by Hermes)
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from the sea foam that gathered around the severed genitals of Uranus cast into the sea by Cronus
nodes.domain_source: Hesiod, Theogony 188-206 (the foam-birth from Ouranos's severed genitals — the central Hesiodic origin); Homer, Iliad 5 and Odyssey 8 (Hephaestus-Ares-Aphrodite); Homeric Hymn 5 (to Aphrodite); Sappho; Apollodorus 1.3-4; the Paphian, Cyprian, and Cytherean cult-centers
nodes.object_source: Aphrodite iconography — myrtle; rose; apple (the kallisteion in the Judgment of Paris); golden girdle (κεστὸς ἱμάς — the irresistible love-charm); mirror; doves
nodes.animals_source: Aphrodite's sacred animals: dove (her primary bird); sparrow (her chariot-team in Sappho fr. 1); swan; hare; sometimes the dolphin (in her sea-foam-birth iconography)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Hesiod; Homer; Sappho; Homeric Hymn 5; the Pygmalion narrative
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard Aphrodite iconography — supreme feminine beauty, frequently nude (Aphrodite of Knidos by Praxiteles, mid-4th c. BCE, was the first major Greek female nude); cf. the Aphrodite of Melos (Venus de Milo)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Hesiod, Theogony 188-206 — born from the sea-foam created where Ouranos's severed genitals (cut off by Cronus) fell into the sea; came ashore at Cythera then Paphos in Cyprus; the love-affair with Ares (caught by Hephaestus's golden net in Odyssey 8); the love-affair with Anchises producing Aeneas (Homeric Hymn 5); the apple in the Judgment of Paris which precipitated the Trojan War; the Adonis cycle (transformed-into-anemone narrative)
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Hesiod, Theogony 188-206 — sea-foam birth from Ouranos's severed genitals
nodes.birthTypes_source: Hesiod, Theogony 188-206

nodes.symbolism: the divine power of increase in agriculture and animal husbandry, bounty as a gift of the gods
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive masculine as the giver of increase, the bountiful aspect of the vegetation god

nodes.name: Osiris
nodes.domain: agriculture, justice, death-rebirth
nodes.object: crook (heqa) and flail (nekhakha); the Atef-crown (the white crown flanked by ostrich-feathers); ankh; was-scepter; the djed-pillar (his spine, the symbol of stability and resurrection)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Mummified king with green or black skin (green = vegetation/regeneration, black = the fertile silt of the Nile flood); wearing the Atef-crown; holding crook and flail crossed over his chest; bandaged from the chest down (signifying mummification and the resurrected body).
nodes.significantEvent: Son of Geb and Nut, brother and husband of Isis. Once king of Egypt who taught humanity agriculture and civilization. Murdered by his jealous brother Set, who tricked him into a coffin and either threw it in the Nile or chopped his body into fourteen pieces (versions differ; Plutarch 18 has the dismemberment). Isis (and Nephthys) collected the pieces, reassembled them — except his penis, which had been eaten by a fish — and Isis fashioned a phallus, impregnated herself with him posthumously, conceiving Horus. Osiris became lord of the Duat (the underworld), the judge of the dead with Ma'at's feather. The justified dead become 'Osiris N.' (e.g., Osiris-Ramses) — every dead person assimilates to him.
nodes.symbolism: Djed pillar is both phallic-masculine and containing-feminine; cedar tree embraces corpse as earth-womb; promises universal rebirth
nodes.neumannArchetype: His djed pillar is both masculine and feminine-containing. The cedar tree embracing his corpse represents the earth-womb.
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Geb and Nut; one of the five children born on the epagomenal days.
nodes.deathCircumstances: Murdered by his brother Set, who tricked him into a coffin shaped to his measurements, sealed it, and either threw it in the Nile (which carried it to Byblos) or dismembered his body. Isis recovered him; Osiris became lord of the dead in the Duat.
nodes.domain_source: Pyramid Texts (the earliest substantial Osiris-narratives — §1466-67, the resurrection-from-Isis hymn); Coffin Texts; Book of the Dead; the Lamentations of Isis and Nephthys; Plutarch, Isis and Osiris (Roman period, the most extensive narrative source); Hymn to Osiris (Berlin Papyrus 3050)
nodes.object_source: Standard Osirian iconography; the djed-pillar's identification with Osiris's spine is canonical
nodes.characterTrait_source: Plutarch, Isis and Osiris; Hymn to Osiris; the Coffin Texts "transformation-into-Osiris" spells
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard Osirian iconography from Middle Kingdom onward
nodes.significantEvent_source: Plutarch, Isis and Osiris 12-20; Pyramid Texts §1466-67; Coffin Texts spells passim
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Plutarch, Isis and Osiris 12; Pyramid Texts
nodes.birthTypes_source: Plutarch 12

nodes.name: Phaethusa
nodes.domain: the sun, herding, light, guardianship
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: luminous nymph who guards the cattle of the Sun
nodes.significantEvent: together with her sister Lampetia she guarded the sacred cattle of Helios on Thrinacia, reported to her father when Odysseus crew slaughtered the cattle
nodes.symbolism: the faithful daughter of the sun who guards the sacred herd, the solar feminine as protector of the masculine patrimony
nodes.neumannArchetype: the luminous feminine guardian of the solar patrimony, the daughters of light who protect the sacred
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Helios (Sun) and the nymph Neaera
nodes.deathCircumstances: She would have also had a brother, Phaethon, who was killed by Zeus after attempting and failing to drive Helios' chariot.

nodes.name: Norns
nodes.domain: prophecy, time, fate
nodes.object: the well of Urðr (Urðarbrunnr); the threads of fate; the runes; clay/water with which they tend Yggdrasil
nodes.characterTrait: fate-weaving, sovereign-over-destinies, three-fold (Urðr-Verðandi-Skuld), some among them benevolent, others harsh
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Three principal Norns named in Vǫluspá 20: Urðr (past/fate), Verðandi (present), Skuld (future/debt). Snorri describes additional Norns descended from the Æsir, elves, and dwarves. Often depicted as veiled or as weavers at the Well of Urðr.
nodes.significantEvent: At the foot of Yggdrasil at the Well of Urðr; daily water the tree with clay from the well; assign destinies to all newborns (Fáfnismál 12-13).
nodes.symbolism: Triple fate goddesses; spinning and breaking thread of destiny; past-present-future; birth-life-death
nodes.neumannArchetype: Two spin and twist thread, third breaks it off. Represent beginning-middle-end, past-present-future.
nodes.birthCircumstances: The three principal Norns are Jǫtunn-women, daughters of Þursar (giants) per Vǫluspá 8 reconstructions; their origin is one of the major demarcations between cosmic ages.
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 15; Vǫluspá 20; Vafþrúðnismál 49; Fáfnismál 12-13; the Edda passim
nodes.object_source: Vǫluspá 20; Gylfaginning 15 (they water Yggdrasil daily from Urðarbrunnr with white clay from the well)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Vǫluspá 20; Gylfaginning 15; Fáfnismál 12-13 (multiple Norns from gods, elves, dwarves)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Vǫluspá 20; Gylfaginning 15; Fáfnismál 12-13

nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Vǫluspá; reconstructions
nodes.birthTypes_source: Vǫluspá

nodes.name: Maya
nodes.domain: cosmic illusion, the veil over reality, creative power of Brahman; in Advaita Vedānta the principle making Brahman appear as world; in Vaiṣṇavism Yogamāyā / Mahāmāyā
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: When personified, depicted as goddess (Mahāmāyā); often identified with Durgā/Pārvatī/Lakṣmī in cosmic-creative aspects. In Advaita, abstract cosmic principle.
nodes.significantEvent: Bhagavad Gītā 7.14: Kṛṣṇa's māyā is divine and hard to overcome but devotees cross beyond it. In Advaita (Śaṅkara), cosmic veil making One appear as Many. In Vaiṣṇavism, Yogamāyā is Kṛṣṇa's internal energy for divine play (līlā), including the birth-night infant-exchange (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.3).
nodes.symbolism: Cosmic illusion; world as hell or Maya; fate as Heimarmene; goddess as the Maya, 'the great...'
nodes.neumannArchetype: The goddess as Maya, cosmic illusion and fate.
nodes.domain_source: Rig Veda 6.47.18; Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad 4.10; Bhagavad Gītā 7.14-15; Śaṅkara's Advaita; Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa
nodes.characterTrait_source: Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad 4.10; Advaita Vedānta; Bhagavad Gītā 7.14-15
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa
nodes.significantEvent_source: Bhagavad Gītā 7.14-15; Śaṅkara's Brahma Sūtra Bhāṣya; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.3
nodes.birthTypes_source: Vedānta tradition

nodes.name: Gaea
nodes.domain: earth, creation, motherhood, prophecy, fertility
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: emerges from the earth itself, sometimes depicted as a matronly woman rising from the ground
nodes.significantEvent: bore Uranus and mated with him to produce the Titans, urged Cronus to castrate Uranus, later sent the Giants and Typhon against Zeus
nodes.symbolism: the primordial earth from which all life springs, the Great Mother who both creates and threatens the patriarchal order, the earth as living maternal body
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial Great Mother preceding all differentiation, the earth goddess linked to Eve and Astarte
nodes.birthCircumstances: self-born from Chaos at the beginning of creation according to Hesiod

nodes.name: Hecate
nodes.domain: magic, witchcraft, crossroads, ghosts, the moon, necromancy, entrance ways, child-rearing, victory in contests, herdsmen and fishermen
nodes.characterTrait: terrible, dark, liminal, powerful, mysterious, generous to her devotees
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: triple-formed, carrying torches, accompanied by howling dogs, appears at crossroads at night
nodes.significantEvent: assisted Demeter in searching for Persephone with her torches, retains cosmic power even under Zeus rule according to Hesiod, worshipped at crossroads with offerings of food
nodes.symbolism: the liminal spaces between worlds, the terrible aspect of the feminine that rules night and death, crossroads as places of choice and danger, magic as feminine knowledge
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Terrible Mother at the negative pole (M-), the dark moon goddess fused with Artemis representing the full range of the Great Goddess from nurturing to terrifying
familyRoles: daughter of Perses and Asteria (Titanic generation)
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the Titans Perses and Asteria, honored by Zeus above all other gods according to Hesiod
nodes.domain_source: Hesiod, Theogony 411-452 (the central Hesiodic hymn-passage); Homeric Hymn to Demeter 24-25, 51-89 (her role as Persephone-witness); Apollonius, Argonautica 3 (the Medea-Hecate connection); the Chaldean Oracles; Lucian; the magical papyri (PGM)
nodes.object_source: Hecate iconography — twin torches; key (κλείς — the key to the underworld); whip; snake; sometimes three-faced (Hecate Trimorphos) at the crossroads
nodes.animals_source: Hecate's sacred animals: dog (her constant companion; black dogs were sacrificed to her at the crossroads); polecat (Galanthis); snake; horse
nodes.eventTypes_source: Hesiod, Theogony 411-452; Apollonius, Argonautica 3; magical papyri
nodes.significantEvent_source: Hesiod, Theogony 411-452 — Zeus uniquely honored her among the Titans, granting her share in heaven, earth, and sea; assisted Demeter in searching for Persephone (Homeric Hymn to Demeter); patron of witchcraft, crossroads, ghosts, and the dead; mistress of Medea's sorcery (Apollonius, Argonautica 3); invoked in the magical papyri as the great cosmic-chthonic-mediator
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Hesiod, Theogony 411 — daughter of Perses (a Titan) and Asteria
nodes.birthTypes_source: Hesiod, Theogony
nodes.characterTrait_source: Hesiod; the magical-papyri tradition; the Medea-Argonautica tradition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Hecate iconography — variable: in archaic tradition single-faced; in late-classical and Hellenistic tradition three-faced (Hecate Trimorphos) at the crossroads, sometimes with three bodies or three heads facing different directions

nodes.significantEvent: Part of quaternary with Hathor, Neith
nodes.symbolism: Part of Egyptian goddess quaternary; paired with Neith
nodes.neumannArchetype: Part of the quaternary with Hathor and Neith in the Archetypal Feminine.

nodes.name: Odin
nodes.domain: war, death, wisdom, prophecy, poetry, magic (seiðr), kingship, the gallows, fate
nodes.object: spear (Gungnir), runes, ravens (Huginn and Muninn), wolves (Geri and Freki), eight-legged horse (Sleipnir), gold ring (Draupnir), wide-brimmed hat and cloak, throne (Hliðskjálf), mead of poetry (Óðrørir)
nodes.characterTrait: wisdom-seeking, self-sacrificing, cunning, treacherous, wandering, disguised, one-eyed, terror-inspiring, poetic
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: one-eyed; old, long-bearded; wide-brimmed hat; dark cloak
nodes.significantEvent: Cosmogony with brothers Vili and Vé: kills the primal giant Ymir and forms the world from his body. Wins the runes by hanging himself nine nights on Yggdrasil. Sacrifices his eye at Mímir's well for wisdom. Steals the mead of poetry from the giant Suttungr. Binds the children of Loki (Fenrir, Jǫrmungandr, Hel). Dies at Ragnarǫk, devoured by the wolf Fenrir.
nodes.symbolism: Bond with spring of fate; judgment seat at world ash tree; takes wisdom from feminine seeresses
nodes.neumannArchetype: Takes wisdom from feminine seeresses. His hanging from Yggdrasil reflects relation to tree of fate.
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Borr (or Burr) and the giantess Bestla; brother of Vili and Vé.
nodes.deathCircumstances: Devoured by the wolf Fenrir during Ragnarǫk.
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 9-21, 49-51; Vǫluspá; Hávamál; Vafþrúðnismál; Grímnismál; Heimskringla, Ynglinga saga; Saxo Grammaticus, Gesta Danorum; Adam of Bremen, Descriptio Insularum Aquilonis (the Uppsala temple description)
nodes.object_source: Skáldskaparmál (Faulkes ch. 35) and Vǫluspá 24 (Gungnir); Hávamál 138-145 (runes); Grímnismál 19-20 (Geri/Freki, Huginn/Muninn — companions); Gylfaginning 16, 42, Grímnismál 44 (Sleipnir); Skáldskaparmál ch. 35 (Draupnir); Grímnismál prologue (Hliðskjálf, Síðhǫttr/Grímnir disguises); Hávamál 104-110 (mead of poetry). NOTE: Ravens, wolves, and Sleipnir relocated from 'animals' per the protocol's companion-attribute rule.
nodes.animals_source: No animal symbolically embodies Odin in the Athena-owl sense. Ravens, wolves, and Sleipnir are companions/attributes (now in 'object'). Odin shapeshifts into many forms (Ynglinga saga 7) but no single form characterizes him.
nodes.characterTrait_source: Hávamál passim (his wandering ascetic-aspect); Lokasenna 21-24 (Loki's accusation of ergi-magic); Vǫluspá (his Ragnarök fate); Ynglinga saga 6-7
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 17, 20; Grímnismál 46-50 (the long list of Odin's names); standard iconography of one-eyed wanderer
nodes.significantEvent_source: Vǫluspá; Hávamál 138-141 (the self-hanging on Yggdrasil); Gylfaginning passim; Vǫluspá 53 (his death at Ragnarök)
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 6
nodes.deathCircumstances_source: Snorri Sturluson, Gylfaginning 51 (Odin swallowed by Fenrir at Ragnarök); Vǫluspá 53-56; Vafþrúðnismál 53
nodes.birthTypes_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 6 (Odin son of Borr and Bestla)

nodes.name: Horus
nodes.domain: sun, sky, kingship, animals
nodes.object: was-scepter; the double-crown (pschent) of Upper and Lower Egypt; the Eye of Horus (wadjet — the symbol of healing, restored after Set tore it out)
nodes.characterTrait: vengeful (against Set), royal, healing, sky-flying, victorious, justified-heir
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Falcon, or falcon-headed man, wearing the double-crown; the sun and moon as his eyes (the right eye is the sun, the left moon — the moon-eye is the wadjet, torn out by Set and healed by Thoth). Many forms: Horus the Elder (Haroeris, brother of Osiris), Horus son of Isis (Harsiese, the central avenger-figure), Horus of Edfu (Behdety, the winged-disk), Horus the Child (Harpokrates, depicted as a finger-sucking child).
nodes.significantEvent: The central avenger-figure of the Osirian cycle. Conceived posthumously by Isis from the reassembled Osiris (Plutarch 19). Hidden by Isis in the Delta marshes during childhood, surviving Set's attempts to kill him. Comes to manhood and challenges Set for the throne of Egypt. The Contendings of Horus and Set narrates the 80-year legal battle in the divine court — physical contests (the underwater hippo-form race; the semen-deception with Isis's hand), tribunal sessions, mediation by Ma'at. In the end, Horus wins, Set is banished to the desert (or assimilated to thunder). Every pharaoh is the living Horus.
nodes.symbolism: Divine child of the Great Mother; 'through whom alone he is king'; divine child archetype
nodes.neumannArchetype: Son of Isis. The king is Horus through the mother. Represents the divine child archetype.
nodes.birthCircumstances: Conceived posthumously by Isis from the reassembled Osiris (whom Isis had impregnated by fashioning a phallus, his original having been eaten by a fish).
nodes.domain_source: Pyramid Texts (foundational — every pharaoh is 'Horus' in life); Coffin Texts; Book of the Dead; the Edfu temple inscriptions (the Triumph of Horus narrative); the Contendings of Horus and Set (Papyrus Chester Beatty I); the Metternich Stela (Horus-and-the-cures texts); Plutarch, Isis and Osiris
nodes.object_source: Standard Horus iconography; Contendings of Horus and Set
nodes.characterTrait_source: Pyramid Texts; Contendings of Horus and Set; Edfu inscriptions
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard iconography; multiple Horus-forms in Pyramid Texts
nodes.significantEvent_source: Contendings of Horus and Set; Plutarch 19-20; Pyramid Texts §1466-67; Edfu temple narrative
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Plutarch 18-19
nodes.birthTypes_source: Plutarch 19

nodes.name: Hel
nodes.domain: death
nodes.object: her hall Éljúðnir; her plate Hungr; her knife Sultr; her threshold Fallandaforað; her bed Kǫr; her bed-curtains Blíkjandaböl (per Gylfaginning 34)
nodes.characterTrait: grim, half-living half-dead in appearance, harsh-of-disposition, sovereign over the dishonored dead
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Half-blue/black (the side of death) and half flesh-colored (the side of life). Cast down into Niflheim by Odin to rule over the nine worlds and over those who die of sickness or old age (i.e., not battle-deaths, who go to Valhalla or Fólkvangr).
nodes.significantEvent: Cast down by Odin to Niflheim to rule the dead. When Baldr dies, his soul goes to her. Hermóðr rides Sleipnir nine nights down the Helvegr (Hel-way) to her hall and asks her to release Baldr; she will agree only if all things in the world weep for him. All do, except Loki disguised as the giantess Þǫkk — and so Baldr remains with her. At Ragnarok, the dead from Hel sail under Loki on the ship Naglfar to assail the gods (Vǫluspá 51).
nodes.symbolism: Terrible Mother as ruler of the dead; Norse underworld goddess
nodes.neumannArchetype: Norse death goddess representing the Terrible Mother as ruler of the underworld.
nodes.birthCircumstances: Daughter of Loki and the giantess Angrboða; sister of Fenrir and Jörmungandr (Gylfaginning 34). Odin cast her into Niflheim to rule the dead.
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 34 (her creation and assignment), 49 (the realm and Baldr-recovery negotiation); Vǫluspá 43 (her cock at Ragnarök); Baldrs Draumar 2-3; Lokasenna
nodes.object_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 34
nodes.characterTrait_source: Gylfaginning 34 (half black-blue, half flesh-colored; gloomy and harsh); Gylfaginning 49 (the bargaining for Baldr's return)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Gylfaginning 34 ('she is half-blue and half-flesh-colored — hence she is easily recognized — and rather gloomy and grim in appearance')
nodes.significantEvent_source: Gylfaginning 34 (Odin throws her into Niflheim and gives her power over the nine worlds, to govern those who die of sickness or old age); Gylfaginning 49 (the Baldr negotiation — she will return Baldr only if all things weep, which fails through Loki-Þǫkk)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Gylfaginning 34
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Gylfaginning 34

nodes.name: Shiva
nodes.domain: destruction, asceticism, yoga, dance, cremation grounds, death, the liṅga, auspiciousness, cosmic time (Mahākāla), boon-granting, healing of poisons
nodes.object: trident (triśūla), drum (ḍamaru), bow (Pināka), battle-axe (paraśu), skull-staff (khaṭvāṅga), skull-bowl (kapāla), garland of skulls (muṇḍamālā), rudrākṣa beads, the crescent moon, the river Gaṅgā in his hair, ash (vibhūti), tiger and elephant skin
nodes.characterTrait: imperturbable, transcendent, destructive, ascetic, ash-smeared, boon-giving, easily pleased and easily angered, paradoxical (auspicious-and-terrible)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: third eye, ash-coloured (cremation-ash-smeared), blue-throated (Nīlakaṇṭha), matted hair (jaṭā) with the moon and Gaṅgā in it, sometimes five-faced (Sadāśiva)
nodes.significantEvent: Drinks the halāhala poison at the churning of the ocean, turning his throat blue (Nīlakaṇṭha). Destroys the three demon cities of Tripura with a single arrow as Tripurāntaka. Burns the love-god Kāma to ashes with his third eye when Kāma tries to make him desire Pārvatī. Marries Pārvatī after long ascetic courtship. Destroys his father-in-law Daksha's sacrifice via Vīrabhadra after Satī's death. Receives the descending Gaṅgā in his matted hair to break her fall to earth (Bhagīratha episode). Manifests as the infinite pillar of fire (the original liṅga) before Brahmā and Viṣṇu.
nodes.symbolism: Kali stands on his corpse; 'double symbol in which Shiva or Shakti is contained'; 'the imperturbable'
nodes.neumannArchetype: Kali stands on his corpse. 'The imperturbable' contained within Shakti.
nodes.birthCircumstances: Self-existent / without beginning (anādi). Manifests in time as the infinite pillar of fire (liṅga) whose top and bottom Brahmā and Viṣṇu cannot find. In some Mahābhārata accounts emerges as Rudra from Brahmā's anger.
nodes.domain_source: Rig Veda 2.33, 1.114 (Rudra hymns); Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad; Liṅga Purāṇa; Śiva Purāṇa; Mahābhārata, Anuśāsana Parvan; Skanda Purāṇa; Tamil Śaiva canon (Periya Purāṇam)
nodes.object_source: Standard Śaiva iconography across the Purāṇas; trident, drum, axe, skull-staff from Liṅga and Śiva Purāṇas
nodes.characterTrait_source: Mahābhārata; Liṅga Purāṇa; Śiva Purāṇa; Tamil bhakti tradition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard Purāṇic iconography; Śiva Purāṇa Rudra-saṃhitā
nodes.significantEvent_source: Mahābhārata, Anuśāsana 14 (Tripura-dahana); Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.7 (halāhala); Kumārasambhava (Satī, Pārvatī); Liṅga Purāṇa 17 (liṅgodbhava)
nodes.eventTypes_source: Mahābhārata; Liṅga Purāṇa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Kumārasambhava
nodes.birthTypes_source: Liṅga Purāṇa; Vedānta tradition
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Liṅga Purāṇa 17; Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad

nodes.name: Astarte
nodes.domain: love, war, royalty, the morning and evening star (Venus), kingship-conferring (in Phoenician usage), fertility — closely paralleled with Mesopotamian Ishtar and Sumerian Inanna
nodes.object: bow and quiver (parallel to Ishtar); horse and chariot (Phoenician — she is 'Astarte of the chariot' in some inscriptions); the eight-pointed star (Venus emblem)
nodes.characterTrait: royal, warlike, amorous, regal, paralleling Ishtar in dual love-and-war function
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Royal goddess; armed in war-aspect, voluptuous in love-aspect; sometimes depicted standing on a lion (like Ishtar); in Phoenician contexts, wearing a horned crown.
nodes.significantEvent: In Ugaritic narrative, paired with Anat in restraining Baal (KTU 1.2 I 38-40 — they grasp Baal's hand to prevent him from striking Yam's messengers). In Phoenician religion, the chief goddess of Sidon (and Tyre, paired with Melqart). In Punic religion, eclipsed by Tanit.
nodes.symbolism: Fatal enchantment; 'Astarte type' with hands on breasts; linked to Eve and Gaea
nodes.neumannArchetype: Figure of fatal enchantment. The widely distributed 'Astarte type.'
nodes.birthCircumstances: In Ugaritic theology, daughter of El.
nodes.domain_source: KTU 1.2 I 8, 1.14 IV 38-39, 1.16 VI 56 (Athtart in Ugaritic, often paired with Anat); the Eshmunazar sarcophagus inscription (KAI 14, 5th c. BCE — Astarte as 'Astarte who is in Sidon'); the Mesha Stele line 17 ('I have placed there the vessels of YHWH... and dragged them before Chemosh'); 1 Kings 11:5, 33; 2 Kings 23:13 (biblical references to Sidonian Ashtoreth)
nodes.object_source: Late Bronze and Iron Age Phoenician iconography; the Pyrgi Tablets (5th c. BCE Phoenician-Etruscan bilingual — Astarte at Pyrgi)
nodes.animals_source: Phoenician and Punic iconography; the lion-emblem of Astarte appears on coinage of Phoenician cities. Symbolic embodiment paralleling Ishtar.
nodes.characterTrait_source: Ugaritic and Phoenician sources passim; the Eshmunazar sarcophagus (KAI 14)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Late Bronze Age and Iron Age Phoenician iconography; coinage of Tyre, Sidon, Carthage
nodes.significantEvent_source: KTU 1.2 I 38-40; 1.14 IV 38-39; Eshmunazar sarcophagus (KAI 14); the Pyrgi Tablets
nodes.birthTypes_source: Standard Ugaritic theology — daughter of El
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Pantheon list KTU 1.47 / 1.118

nodes.name: Eumenides
nodes.domain: vengeance, blood guilt, justice, oaths, the underworld
nodes.characterTrait: relentless, implacable, just, terrifying, ancient, earth-connected
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: snake-haired, black-robed, weeping tears of blood, carrying torches and whips
nodes.significantEvent: pursued Orestes for the murder of his mother Clytemnestra, transformed into the Eumenides (Kindly Ones) by Athena at the trial on the Areopagus in Aeschylus Oresteia
nodes.symbolism: the ancient chthonic law of blood vengeance, the transition from vendetta to civic justice, the earth-connected feminine powers older than the Olympians
nodes.neumannArchetype: the chthonic sisters of the Great Mother representing the inescapable law of the earth, receiving offerings characteristic of earth goddesses
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from the blood of Uranus that fell on Gaia when Cronus castrated him, or daughters of Nyx

nodes.name: Baubo
nodes.domain: fertility, obscenity, humor, the body, ritual laughter
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: belly as face, legs as chin, vulva as mouth, or simply a woman lifting her skirt
nodes.significantEvent: lifted her skirts to expose herself before the grieving Demeter, making the goddess laugh and breaking her fast during the search for Persephone, Priene terracotta figurines depict her
nodes.symbolism: the sacred obscenity that defeats grief, the belly and genitals as the creative center of the feminine, ritual laughter as restoration of life force
nodes.neumannArchetype: the belly character of the woman, ritual baring and obscenity as life-affirming, the feminine body as source of laughter and renewed vitality against death
nodes.birthCircumstances: Eleusinian figure, wife of Dysaules, or old servant woman

nodes.domain: deep sea waves, underwater currents
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: sea goddess of the deep waves
nodes.significantEvent: raised the young Eumolpus after his father Poseidon saved him from drowning, she adopted and raised him in Ethiopia
nodes.symbolism: the nurturing depths of the sea, the deep waves that carry and sustain rather than destroy
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive oceanic mother who nurtures the abandoned child in the depths
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Poseidon and Amphitrite

nodes.name: Maat
nodes.domain: sky, justice, order
nodes.object: ostrich-feather (the iconic Ma'at-feather, weighed against the heart in judgment); ankh; the balance-scales (in the weighing-of-the-heart scene)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Anthropomorphic woman wearing the ostrich-feather on her head (often the feather is shown alone as her symbol); sometimes winged; small in size as suits her dual function as principle and goddess.
nodes.significantEvent: The cosmic principle of order, justice, truth, righteousness, and balance — the foundational concept of Egyptian thought (paralleling Vedic ṛta and Persian aša). In the judgment hall of Osiris (Book of the Dead 125), the deceased's heart is weighed against Ma'at's feather; if it balances (i.e., the heart is not heavier than truth), the deceased is justified and proceeds to the afterlife; if it is heavier, Ammit devours the heart and the deceased is annihilated. The 42 Negative Confessions are addressed to Ma'at. Every pharaoh's duty is to maintain ma'at and prevent isfet (chaos/wrongdoing).
nodes.symbolism: Justice and cosmic order; correlated with Sophia-Wisdom and Kore
nodes.neumannArchetype: Egyptian goddess of justice correlated with Sophia-Wisdom at the positive pole.
nodes.birthCircumstances: Daughter of Ra; cosmic principle present at creation as the right order Ra established.
nodes.domain_source: Pyramid Texts; Coffin Texts; Book of the Dead (especially the 42 Negative Confessions, ch. 125); the Instructions of Ptahhotep; the Instructions of Amenemope

nodes.name: Lilith
nodes.domain: seduction, child-killing, night, demonic, wind/storm (etymological), succubus / nocturnal sexual predation
nodes.object: screech-owl (lilit) iconography; she steals from babies in incantation-bowl imagery; flowing hair (sign of demonic disorder)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: winged, long-haired (untied/disheveled)
nodes.significantEvent: In the Alphabet of Ben Sira: created by God simultaneously with Adam from the same earth; refused to lie beneath him during intercourse claiming equality; pronounced the Ineffable Name and flew to the Red Sea; God sent three angels (Senoy, Sansenoy, Semangelof) to retrieve her; she refused to return; in punishment 100 of her demon-children (the lilim/lilin) die daily; she became the killer of human newborns (within 8 days for boys, 20 for girls), bound only by amulets bearing the angels' names. In the Zohar: queen of the qelippot (husks of evil), partner of Samael in the demonic realm.
nodes.symbolism: Specter figure; 'Mesopotamian goddess Lilith of night, evil, and death, winged'
nodes.neumannArchetype: Specter figure. Mesopotamian goddess of night, evil, and death.
birthTypes: created from earth simultaneously with Adam
nodes.birthCircumstances: In the Alphabet of Ben Sira: created from the earth simultaneously with Adam, by God. In the Zohar: emerges as the female counterpart of Samael in the qelippot.
nodes.tradition_source: The named figure Lilith (לִילִית) is rabbinic-Jewish: Isaiah 34:14 (one possible biblical mention, contested); Babylonian Talmud (b. Eruvin 100b, b. Niddah 24b, b. Shabbat 151b, b. Bava Batra 73a); Alphabet of Ben Sira (8th-10th c. CE — canonical 'first wife of Adam' narrative); Zohar (13th c.). The Mesopotamian background — Akkadian līlītu / līlû / (w)ardat lilî; Sumerian (k)i-sikil-líl in Gilgamesh, Enkidu, and the Netherworld (ETCSL 1.8.1.4) — is etymologically and typologically ancestral but does not feature the named figure 'Lilith'. Aramaic incantation bowls (5th-7th c. CE) are 'Mesopotamian-Jewish', not Mesopotamian in the Sumero-Akkadian polytheistic sense.
nodes.domain_source: Babylonian Talmud b. Shabbat 151b (danger of sleeping alone — seduction/succubus); b. Niddah 24b and Aramaic incantation bowls (child-killing/miscarriage); b. Eruvin 100b (long hair, wings, nocturnal); Isaiah 34:14 (night/desolation); Akkadian incantations (etymological wind/storm-demon background); Zohar I:148b (succubus). 'Love' replaced with 'seduction' — Lilith is associated with erotic danger, not love as positive domain.
nodes.significantEvent_source: Alphabet of Ben Sira (Stern-Mirsky ed.; the 23a-b passage for the Adam narrative); Zohar I:148a-b, II:267b-268a; Tikkunei Zohar 70; Aramaic incantation bowls (Naveh-Shaked corpora). The Sumerian 'huluppu-tree' demoness (k)i-sikil-líl in Gilgamesh, Enkidu, and the Netherworld (ETCSL 1.8.1.4) lines 27-55 is etymologically related but is an episode of Inanna's tree, not of the named Lilith.
nodes.eventTypes_source: Alphabet of Ben Sira (Adam-rejection, flight to Red Sea, angel-binding)
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Alphabet of Ben Sira 23a-b (Stern-Mirsky); Zohar I:148b. The two traditions conflict; both preserved.
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: b. Eruvin 100b (long hair and wings); b. Niddah 24b; Aramaic incantation bowls (often shown winged and bound)
nodes.animals_source: 'Owl': from Isaiah 34:14, where lilit is variously translated. Modern critical translations (JPS, NRSV) treat lilit as a proper name; KJV's 'screech owl' reflects one interpretive tradition. The Burney Relief (c. 1800 BCE), formerly identified with Lilith, is now usually identified with Ereshkigal or Ishtar. Owl-association is iconographic-traditional more than primary-textual; retained with caveat.
nodes.familyRoles_source: mother: of demonic offspring (lilim/lilin) — Talmud and Zohar. First wife: of Adam in the Alphabet of Ben Sira tradition (a 'former spouse' relation).
nodes.characterTrait_source: b. Eruvin 100b (nocturnal); b. Shabbat 151b (seductive/dangerous); Zohar I:148b (death-dealing). 'Evil' is a classification rather than a primary-text descriptor.
nodes.object_source: Babylonian Talmud b. Erubin 100b (long-haired); Aramaic incantation bowls (Naveh-Shaked); Alphabet of Ben Sira (Lilith's flight); Isaiah 34:14 (lilit at the desolate place)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Alphabet of Ben Sira (a medieval text, c. 700-1000 CE) gives the 'created from earth at the same time as Adam' narrative; in earlier sources (Talmud, Aramaic bowls) she has no birth-account

nodes.name: Huitzilopochtli
nodes.domain: war, sun, sacrifice, creation
nodes.significantEvent: Son of Coatlicue; Aztec war/sun god requiring human sacrifice
nodes.symbolism: Hero god of the Aztecs; son of earth mother Coatlicue; sun warrior deity
nodes.neumannArchetype: Aztec hero/war god, son of Coatlicue the earth mother.
nodes.domain_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — Huitzilopochtli ('Hummingbird of the South' / 'Left-Handed Hummingbird') as the supreme Mexica tribal-god; Sahagún Books 1.1, 3.1; the Templo Mayor inscriptions
nodes.object_source: Florentine Codex; Codex Borbonicus — xiuhcoatl ('turquoise serpent', his fire-serpent weapon); shield with eagle-down (tezcacuitlapilli); the great pyramid Templo Mayor at Tenochtitlan
nodes.animals_source: Huitzilopochtli's sacred animals: hummingbird (his name and form-of-rebirth — slain warriors became hummingbirds in his paradise); eagle (his cosmic-bird)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Florentine Codex 3.1; the Crónica Mexicáyotl
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Codex Borbonicus — blue-painted warrior with hummingbird headdress; bearing xiuhcoatl
nodes.significantEvent_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — born fully-armored from Coatlicue on Mount Coatepec when she conceived him from a ball of feathers that fell from the sky. His siblings the Centzon Huitznahua and his sister Coyolxauhqui (the moon) tried to kill their mother for her dishonor; Huitzilopochtli emerged armed, slew Coyolxauhqui (dismembering her — the cosmic etiology for the moon's lunation), scattered the Centzon Huitznahua (becoming the stars). Led the Mexica from Aztlan to the site of Tenochtitlan (the eagle-cactus-serpent vision foundation, 1325 CE). The principal recipient of the Aztec heart-sacrifice (necessary to fuel his daily sun-victory).
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Florentine Codex 3.1 — born fully-armed on Coatepec ('Serpent Hill') after Coatlicue's miraculous conception
nodes.birthTypes_source: Florentine Codex 3.1

nodes.animals_source: Xochiquetzal's sacred animals: butterflies; hummingbirds (her companions)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Florentine Codex 1.18
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Codex Borgia — beautiful young woman in elaborate quetzal-flower headdress; richly-attired in flowered garments
nodes.significantEvent_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — first wife of Tlaloc, stolen from him by Tezcatlipoca; later wife of Xochipilli or Centeotl. Mother (with Mixcoatl in one tradition) of Quetzalcoatl-Topiltzin. The Aztec Aphrodite, patroness of erotic love.

nodes.object_source: Codex Borgia — spinning-spindle (her weaving-fertility aspect); cotton headdress; black mouth-paint (signifying eaten sins)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Florentine Codex 1.12; Codex Borgia 16
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Codex Borgia — woman with black mouth-paint (signifying the consumed sins), spindle in hair, cotton headdress
nodes.significantEvent_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — Tlazolteotl received the once-in-a-lifetime confession of carnal sins from each Aztec adult, eating the sins and purifying the confessor; principally a women's-deity and childbirth-patron; one of the central Teotleco (gods' descent festival) figures.

nodes.name: Ceres
nodes.domain: fertility, storm, agriculture
nodes.significantEvent: Ceres-Spes (Hope) association; bee symbolism; Cretan Great Goddess connection
nodes.symbolism: Ceres-Spes (Hope); bee association with moon; Cretan Great Goddess; Demeter parallel
nodes.neumannArchetype: Roman Demeter. Associated with Spes (Hope) and the Cretan Great Goddess.
familyRoles: plebeian patron-goddess of the Aventine Triad (with Liber and Libera)
nodes.domain_source: Ovid, Metamorphoses 5 (Proserpina narrative); Fasti 4.393-620 (Cerealia April 19); Cicero, In Verrem 4.106-109 (the Sicilian Demeter-Ceres cult); the plebeian Aventine cult of Ceres-Liber-Libera (founded 493 BCE)
nodes.object_source: Ceres iconography — sheaf of grain; torch; cornucopia; mystic basket (kiste)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Ovid; Roman cult tradition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Ceres iconography — matronly grain-goddess identical to Demeter; the plebeian-Aventine cult emphasized her champion-of-the-people aspect
nodes.significantEvent_source: Roman tradition — identified with Greek Demeter; the Sicilian and Eleusinian connection runs through her cult (Sicily was Roman granary, the Proserpina-abduction was located at Enna); plebeian patron-goddess (the Aventine cult of Ceres-Liber-Libera was the plebeian counterpart to the patrician Capitoline Triad); Cerealia April 12-19; the ludi Cereri festival
nodes.birthTypes_source: Roman interpretation

nodes.name: Holda
nodes.domain: winter, spinning, domestic arts, the Wild Hunt, fertility, death

nodes.symbolism: duality of nurturing and terrifying aspects of nature, winter and renewal, domestic industry as sacred feminine work
nodes.neumannArchetype: Great Mother in her dual benevolent-terrible aspect, combining nourishment with death
nodes.birthCircumstances: pre-Christian Germanic deity surviving in folklore

nodes.name: Shakti
nodes.domain: divine feminine power, creative-dynamic energy of universe, supreme goddess principle (Śākta); every god has his śakti as the female personification of his power (Brahma-Sarasvati, Viṣṇu-Lakṣmī, Śiva-Pārvatī)
nodes.object: varies by manifestation — trident, sword, lotus, weapons of the goddess-forms; the yoni in tantric iconography
nodes.characterTrait: dynamic, creative, powerful, active, transformative — without her the male god is a śava (corpse)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: When personified, manifests as Pārvatī/Durgā/Kālī/Lakṣmī/Sarasvatī depending on context; in tantric iconography, active feminine principle in union with passive masculine.
nodes.significantEvent: The cosmic principle of feminine power. In Śākta tradition, the supreme reality of which all goddesses are manifestations. Devī Māhātmya 1.78 declares the Devī supreme power creating-maintaining-destroying the universe. In Tantric tradition (Kashmir Śaivism, Śrī Vidyā), Śakti is the spanda — cosmic vibration whose pulsation is the universe.
nodes.symbolism: Divine feminine power; 'double symbol in which Shiva or Shakti is contained'
nodes.neumannArchetype: 'Double symbol in which Shiva or Shakti is contained.' Cosmic feminine principle.
familyRoles: consort of every male god (in his śakti-aspect)
nodes.domain_source: Devī Māhātmya; Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Tantric tradition (Mahānirvāṇa Tantra, Kulārṇava Tantra); Soundarya Laharī; Tirumantiram
nodes.object_source: Tantric tradition; Devī Māhātmya 2
nodes.characterTrait_source: Tantric tradition; Soundarya Laharī verse 1
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Tantric and Śākta iconography
nodes.significantEvent_source: Devī Māhātmya 1.78; Tantric Śaiva and Śākta traditions
nodes.birthTypes_source: Śākta-Tantric tradition

nodes.neumannArchetype: Listed alongside Isis, Demeter, Artemis as forms of the positive Great Mother.

nodes.name: Cihuacoatl
nodes.domain: war, fertility, earth, animals
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: serpent woman
nodes.significantEvent: Aztec serpent woman/earth goddess
nodes.symbolism: Mexican serpent woman; earth goddess; Terrible Mother
nodes.neumannArchetype: Mexican serpent woman representing the earth goddess.
nodes.domain_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — Cihuacoatl ('Woman Serpent') as goddess of motherhood, midwives, and women who died in childbirth (mociuaquetzque); Sahagún Books 1.6, 6.27; the title 'cihuacoatl' was also the highest political office below the tlatoani (e.g., Tlacaelel)
