nodes.characterTrait_source: Florentine Codex 1.6, 6.27 — fierce, wailing in the night (one of the omens of the Conquest was Cihuacoatl's wailing through Tenochtitlan)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Codex Borgia — woman with skull-face or warrior-helmet; wailing; spectral
nodes.significantEvent_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — patron of women dying in childbirth (mociuaquetzque), who were honored as warriors and went to Cincalco (the western paradise of dead warriors). One of the eight cosmic-omens of the Conquest: Cihuacoatl wailed at night through Tenochtitlan ('My children, where shall I take you?').

nodes.name: Groa
nodes.domain: seeress, healer, spell-singer — the volva who chants healing charms over Thor (the Grógaldr)
nodes.object: her chants/galdrar (the nine healing charms); the whetstone-shard in Thor's head (which she tries to remove)
nodes.characterTrait: healing, magical, motherly (to Svipdagr in Grógaldr), distractible (Skáldskaparmál 17 — Thor distracts her with news of her husband Aurvandill, causing her to forget her chant and leave the whetstone-shard permanently in his head)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Volva-seeress; wife of Aurvandill the Bold.
nodes.significantEvent: In Skáldskaparmál 17, after Thor's fight with Hrungnir, Thor has a whetstone-shard lodged in his head. Gróa is summoned to chant it out. As her spells begin to loosen it, Thor (wanting to thank her) tells her that her long-lost husband Aurvandill is on his way home — Thor having carried him from the north in a basket. Hearing the good news, Gróa is so distracted that she forgets her spell, and the shard remains forever in Thor's head. Also the volva of Grógaldr (a late Eddic poem), where she chants nine charms over her son Svipdagr before his quest.
nodes.symbolism: Seeress who heals with magic songs; feminine wisdom figure
nodes.neumannArchetype: Sings magic songs over Thor. Feminine wisdom/seeress tradition.
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Skáldskaparmál 17 (the Hrungnir-aftermath narrative); Grógaldr (the late Eddic poem)
nodes.object_source: Skáldskaparmál 17; Grógaldr
nodes.characterTrait_source: Skáldskaparmál 17; Grógaldr
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Skáldskaparmál 17
nodes.significantEvent_source: Skáldskaparmál 17; Grógaldr

nodes.name: Coatlicue
nodes.domain: death, earth, creation, motherhood
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: snake skirt
nodes.significantEvent: Mother of Huitzilopochtli; Mexican Terrible Mother
nodes.symbolism: Mexican snake goddess; Terrible Mother; earth combining creation and death
nodes.neumannArchetype: Mexican snake goddess representing the Terrible Mother.
nodes.domain_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — Coatlicue ('Serpent Skirt') as earth-mother and mother of Huitzilopochtli; Sahagún Book 3.1; the famous monumental Coatlicue statue (Templo Mayor, 1487, now in the Museo Nacional de Antropología, Mexico City)
nodes.object_source: Codex Borgia and Magliabechiano — skirt of intertwined serpents; necklace of human hearts, hands, and a skull; her own decapitated head replaced by two facing serpents (representing two streams of blood)
nodes.animals_source: Coatlicue's sacred animals: serpents (composing her skirt)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Florentine Codex 3.1; Coatlicue-iconography
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: The monumental Coatlicue statue (Templo Mayor, 1487) — beheaded, with two serpents facing each other emerging from her neck representing two streams of blood; serpent-skirt; necklace of severed hands, hearts, and a central skull; clawed feet
nodes.significantEvent_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — while sweeping at Coatepec, conceived Huitzilopochtli from a ball of feathers that fell from the sky into her bosom; her daughter Coyolxauhqui and her 400 sons the Centzon Huitznahua, ashamed of the apparent dishonor, tried to kill her; Huitzilopochtli emerged fully-armed and slew Coyolxauhqui (dismembering her). Mother of Tezcatlipoca's victims and Coyolxauhqui's body (the dismembered moon-goddess at the foot of the Templo Mayor pyramid).

nodes.name: Rhea
nodes.domain: fertility, motherhood, generation, mountains, the flow of time
nodes.object: stone wrapped in swaddling clothes, tambourine, crown
nodes.characterTrait: protective, maternal, cunning, defiant of patriarchal tyranny
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: majestic, enthroned between lions, crowned
nodes.significantEvent: saved her youngest son Zeus from being swallowed by Cronus by substituting a stone wrapped in swaddling clothes, hid Zeus in a cave in Crete
nodes.symbolism: the mother who defies the devouring father to preserve the next generation, the Greek parallel to the Anatolian Cybele, the mother of the gods
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Mother of the Gods, the Great Mother who rescues the divine child from the devouring father, Greek parallel to Cybele
familyRoles: mother of Hestia, Demeter, Hera, Hades, Poseidon, Zeus
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Uranus and Gaia, one of the twelve Titans
nodes.domain_source: Hesiod, Theogony 453-491 (the Zeus-saving narrative); Apollodorus 1.1.3; the Cretan Idaean cave-cult tradition
nodes.object_source: Rhea iconography — sometimes a tympanon (drum, in her later identification with Cybele); the stone she gave to Cronus
nodes.animals_source: Rhea's sacred animals: lion (in her later Cybele-identification — chariot-lions); bee (the Idaean bees that nourished Zeus)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Hesiod, Theogony
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Rhea iconography — matronly Titaness; in later tradition merged with Phrygian Cybele as the Magna Mater
nodes.significantEvent_source: Hesiod, Theogony 453-491 — daughter of Ouranos and Gaia; sister-wife of Cronus; bore the six first Olympians; when Cronus swallowed each at birth, she hid Zeus on Crete in the Idaean cave (the Curetes clashing their shields to mask the infant's cries), giving Cronus a stone wrapped in swaddling. Zeus's eventual victory restored her swallowed children.
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Hesiod, Theogony 137 — daughter of Ouranos and Gaia
nodes.birthTypes_source: Hesiod, Theogony

nodes.name: Attis
nodes.domain: vegetation, death-rebirth, fertility
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: youthful, long hair, Phrygian cap
nodes.significantEvent: Vegetation god associated with Cybele
nodes.symbolism: Dying-and-rising vegetation god; paired with Cybele
nodes.neumannArchetype: Dying-and-rising vegetation god associated with Cybele.
nodes.deathCircumstances: Castrated himself in madness; died; resurrected as a pine tree

nodes.name: Dictynna
nodes.domain: hunt, fishing, nets, the wild
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: wild huntress associated with nets and the Cretan mountains
nodes.significantEvent: leaped from a cliff into the sea to escape King Minos pursuit, caught in fishermens nets, adopted into Artemis cult
nodes.symbolism: the untamed feminine who would rather die than submit, the net as both capture and salvation, the Cretan origins of the Greek huntress-goddess
nodes.neumannArchetype: aspect of the virginal Great Goddess, the Cretan predecessor of the classical Artemis
nodes.birthCircumstances: Cretan goddess or nymph, sometimes identified with Britomartis

nodes.name: Asherah
nodes.domain: motherhood of the seventy gods, creation by intercession, fertility, the sea (per her epithet `rbt ʾaṯrt ym` 'Lady Athirat of the Sea')
nodes.object: spindle and distaff (in KTU 1.4 II 3-11, she is at her spindle when Baal and Anat approach); the donkey she rides to El's tent (KTU 1.4 IV 1-15)
nodes.characterTrait: dignified, intercessory, queenly, occasionally indignant (mistakes Baal and Anat for hostile messengers); ultimately pivotal in the Baal Cycle's resolution
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Dignified mother-goddess; iconographically associated with the Asherah-tree / sacred pole in Iron Age Israelite religion (the `ʾăšērâ` of the Hebrew Bible). In Ugaritic iconography, less individuated; Iron-Age figurines from Judah (the 'pillar figurines') are sometimes attributed to her cult.
nodes.significantEvent: As 'creatress of the gods' (`qnyt ʾilm`), she negotiates with El for Baal's palace (KTU 1.4 IV-V). When Baal is killed by Mot, she nominates her son Athtar to take Baal's throne; Athtar fails to fill it (KTU 1.6 I 39-65). Mother of the seventy sons of Athirat (`šbʿm bn ʾaṯrt`).
nodes.symbolism: Sacred pillar/pole as symbol of Great Mother; tree/pillar feminine symbolism
nodes.neumannArchetype: The asherah pillar is a symbol of the Great Mother.
nodes.domain_source: KTU 1.4 II-V (her central role in securing El's consent for Baal's palace); KTU 1.6 I 39-46 (Athirat's choice of successor when Baal dies); KTU 1.4 IV 31-40 (her epithet 'Mistress Athirat of the Sea'); pantheon list KTU 1.47 / 1.118
nodes.object_source: KTU 1.4 II 3-11 (spindle); IV 1-15 (her donkey-ride to El's mountain)
nodes.characterTrait_source: KTU 1.4 II 3-26 (her startled response); IV (her intercession with El); 1.6 I 39-65 (choosing the unsuccessful Athtar)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Hebrew Bible polemic against the asherah-pole (e.g., Deuteronomy 16:21, 2 Kings 23:6-7); Judean pillar figurines (Kletter 1996 *The Judean Pillar-Figurines*); Ugaritic narrative does not provide detailed physical description
nodes.significantEvent_source: KTU 1.4 II-V; 1.6 I 39-65; KTU 1.6 V 1 (the seventy sons formula)

nodes.name: Tammuz
nodes.domain: shepherding, fertility, vegetation, the dying-and-returning consort, midsummer mourning rites
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Young shepherd-figure; standard pastoral iconography (similar to Sumerian Dumuzi).
nodes.significantEvent: Husband of Ishtar; substituted for her in the underworld in the Sumerian Inanna's Descent tradition (where Inanna chooses him as her replacement when she finds him enthroned in finery instead of mourning). Annual mourning rite in the month of Tammuz (Du'uzu, midsummer); his cult extended into the Iron-Age western Levant (Ezekiel 8:14).
nodes.symbolism: Dying-and-rising vegetation god; paired with Ishtar/Inanna
nodes.neumannArchetype: Dying-and-rising god paired with Ishtar.
nodes.birthCircumstances: Akkadian sources describe him as son of the goddess Sirtur (Sumerian Duttur).
nodes.deathCircumstances: Seized by demons as Ishtar's substitute in the underworld; lamented annually in the month of Tammuz (Du'uzu, midsummer). His descent and partial return frame the seasonal-vegetation cult.
nodes.domain_source: Standard Babylonian Ishtar's Descent (the substitution); Epic of Gilgamesh VI 46-49 (Tammuz as Ishtar's first lover, 'for whom you decreed yearly weeping'); Ezekiel 8:14 (women weeping for Tammuz at the Jerusalem temple gate)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Sumerian Inanna's Descent (ETCSL 1.4.1) lines 340-380; Akkadian Ishtar's Descent end; Gilgamesh VI 46-49; Ezekiel 8:14
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard Akkadian shepherd-god iconography; Ezekiel 8:14 (Tammuz mourned by women at the Jerusalem temple)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Akkadian sources — son of Sirtur/Duttur
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Sumerian-Akkadian Dumuzi-Inanna corpus; ETCSL 1.4.1.1 (Dumuzid and Geshtin-ana, where his mother Sirtur appears)
nodes.deathCircumstances_source: Ishtar's Descent end; Gilgamesh VI 46-49 ('for whom you decreed yearly weeping'); Ezekiel 8:14
nodes.characterTrait_source: Inanna-Dumuzi courtship cycle; Ishtar's Descent; Ezekiel 8:14
nodes.object_source: Akkadian shepherd-god corpus; Sumerian Dumuzi-Inanna cycle (cognate iconography)

nodes.domain: healing hymns, Apollo as healer
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: epithet of Apollo as healer, or a separate healing deity
nodes.significantEvent: the healing song addressed to Apollo, used as a title for Apollo in his capacity as divine physician
nodes.symbolism: the identity between the healing god and the song of praise addressed to him, Apollo as the god whose music heals
nodes.neumannArchetype: the solar masculine as healer through song, the Apolline principle of healing through harmony

nodes.name: Nerthus
nodes.domain: earth, fertility, peace, prosperity
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: veiled goddess concealed within a sacred cart, never seen directly by mortals
nodes.significantEvent: periodically carried in a veiled cart through the land bringing peace, afterward her slaves who bathed her image were drowned in a sacred lake
nodes.symbolism: earth mother whose presence brings peace, ritual secrecy and the terrible cost of encountering the divine directly
nodes.neumannArchetype: Great Mother in her dual nurturing and devouring aspect, earth goddess demanding sacrifice
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient earth goddess worshipped by Germanic coastal tribes

nodes.name: Aion
nodes.domain: eternity, cyclical time, the ages, the zodiac
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: lion-headed figure entwined by a serpent, standing within a zodiac wheel, or youthful naked figure
nodes.significantEvent: depicted in Mithraic mysteries as the leontocephaline figure, representing the eternal cycle of ages
nodes.symbolism: eternity as distinct from chronological time, the cycles of cosmic ages, the zodiac as the wheel of eternal return
nodes.neumannArchetype: the uroboric eternal return, time transcending the linear into the cyclical and eternal
nodes.birthCircumstances: primordial or orphic deity representing unbounded time

nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial sky conceived as the workspace of cosmic creation
nodes.birthCircumstances: In another genealogy, incorrectly attributed to Hesiod, Acmon is the son of Gaia, and in some sources he is identified with Uranus himself.

nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive feminine as compassion, the mercy that tempers the severity of justice

nodes.name: Hector
nodes.domain: war, honor, duty, family, defense
nodes.object: chariot, shield, spear, sword, arrow, helmet
nodes.characterTrait: brave, noble, devoted to family, dutiful, honorable
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: tall, bearded warrior, the greatest champion of Troy
nodes.significantEvent: the greatest Trojan warrior who defended his city against the Greeks, killed Patroclus in battle, slain by Achilles who dragged his body behind his chariot, his body ransomed by Priam
nodes.symbolism: duty to family and city above personal safety, the noble defender doomed to fall, the tragedy of war that destroys the best on both sides
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hero bound to the collective rather than the individual quest, the defender archetype who fights not for glory but for home
nodes.birthCircumstances: eldest son of King Priam and Queen Hecuba of Troy, brother of Paris

nodes.object: spear, shield, chariot, armor of gold

nodes.neumannArchetype: the hero empowered by the positive anima (Athena) to confront the dark powers directly, one of the few who wounds gods and returns whole
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Tydeus and Deipyle, grandson of Adrastus, king of Argos

nodes.birthCircumstances: autochthonous (earth-born), the first king of Attica

nodes.domain: Eleusinian kingship, Attic hero cult
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Attic hero and king, ancestor of the Hippothontid tribe
nodes.significantEvent: his mother was killed by her father Cercyon for her pregnancy, Hippothoon was exposed but nursed by a mare and eventually became king and the eponymous hero of the Attic tribe Hippothontis
nodes.symbolism: the exposed child who survives through divine intervention (the nurturing mare), the hero who rises from abandonment to kingship
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child abandoned by the human father, nurtured by the animal aspect of the Great Mother (the mare), and rising to sovereign power
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Poseidon and Alope daughter of Cercyon

nodes.name: Menestratus
nodes.domain: self-sacrifice, heroism, love between warriors
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: young hero who sacrificed himself for his city or beloved
nodes.significantEvent: offered himself as a sacrifice to save his community, an act of supreme devotion
nodes.symbolism: the voluntary sacrifice of the hero for the community, love expressed through self-destruction
nodes.neumannArchetype: the sacrificial hero who gives himself for the collective, the highest expression of masculine devotion
nodes.deathCircumstances: The dragon devoured him, and like Menestratus had predicted, it died indeed, though at the cost of Menestratus' own life.

nodes.name: Venus Verticordia
nodes.domain: love, chastity, turning hearts, sexual virtue
nodes.animals: horse, dove, swan, peacock, dolphin, elephant
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: aspect of Venus specifically concerned with turning hearts from lust to virtue, depicted veiled and modest
nodes.significantEvent: her temple was dedicated in 215 BCE after a series of scandals involving married women, specifically to turn womens hearts from lust toward chastity and marital faithfulness
nodes.symbolism: the love goddess in her chaste aspect, Venus turned inward toward virtue rather than outward toward desire, the divine power of love redirected toward fidelity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the anima in her domesticated aspect, the feminine desire-principle turned inward toward virtue and marital loyalty

nodes.name: Phalanthus
nodes.domain: colonization, Sparta, founding of Tarentum
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Spartan exile who founded the colony of Tarentum in southern Italy
nodes.significantEvent: led the Partheniai (outcasts born during wartime) to found the colony of Tarentum (modern Taranto) in Italy around 706 BCE, guided by the Delphic Oracle
nodes.symbolism: the outcast who founds a great city, exile as the seed of new civilization, the marginalized who create
nodes.neumannArchetype: the rejected son who establishes a new patriarchal order in a foreign land, the exile as culture-founder
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of a Spartan mother, one of the Partheniai (sons born to unwed mothers during the Messenian War)

nodes.neumannArchetype: the son of the divine messenger who establishes the human tradition of sacred communication
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Hermes and one of the daughters of Cecrops, or son of Eumolpus

nodes.name: Orpheus
nodes.domain: music, poetry, prophecy, mystery religion, the underworld
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful musician carrying a lyre, his music tames wild beasts and moves stones
nodes.significantEvent: descended to the underworld to retrieve his dead wife Eurydice and nearly succeeded but looked back at the threshold losing her forever, torn apart by Maenads, his severed head continued to prophesy
nodes.symbolism: the power of art to overcome death, the irresistible backward glance of desire, music as the bridge between worlds, the dismembered poet whose voice persists beyond death
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hero who descends to the underworld to rescue the anima but fails at the threshold, the dismembered god whose prophecy continues after death like Osiris
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of the Muse Calliope and either Oeagrus king of Thrace or the god Apollo

nodes.name: Orestes
nodes.domain: matricide, justice, purification, the transition from blood vengeance to law
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: young prince haunted by the Furies
nodes.significantEvent: killed his mother Clytemnestra to avenge his fathers murder, pursued by the Erinyes for matricide, tried and acquitted at Athens by the court of the Areopagus with Athenas casting vote
nodes.symbolism: the transition from the archaic law of blood vengeance to civic justice, the impossible conflict between duty to father and duty to mother, purification through institutional law
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hero caught between the matriarchal (Erinyes) and patriarchal (Apollo) orders, resolved by the emergence of civic consciousness (Athena)
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Agamemnon and Clytemnestra, brother of Electra and Iphigenia

nodes.name: Pelops
nodes.domain: kingship, chariot racing, divine favor, the curse
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: extraordinarily handsome youth with an ivory shoulder replacing the one eaten by Demeter
nodes.significantEvent: resurrected by the gods after Tantalus cooked him, won the hand of Hippodamia by defeating her father Oenomaus in a chariot race through treachery, the curse from this betrayal haunted his descendants through the House of Atreus
nodes.symbolism: the generational curse that follows betrayal, resurrection and divine favor, the original sin that dooms an entire royal line
nodes.neumannArchetype: the dismembered and resurrected son, the founding figure whose transgression initiates the tragic cycle of the patriarchal house
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Tantalus, cut up and served to the gods as a test by his father, restored to life by the gods

nodes.name: Pandion
nodes.domain: kingship, law, Athenian autochthony
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: mythical king of Athens
nodes.significantEvent: expelled from Athens and sought refuge in Megara, his daughters were sacrificed for the city
nodes.symbolism: the righteous king driven from his throne, the father whose daughters are consumed by the citys needs
nodes.neumannArchetype: the displaced patriarch whose feminine (daughters) is sacrificed for the collective
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Erichthonius or Cecrops, king of Athens

nodes.name: Khenti-kheti
nodes.domain: crocodiles, protection, Athribis, the 10th Lower Egyptian nome
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: crocodile deity or falcon-crocodile hybrid worshipped at Athribis
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped at Athribis as the local protective deity, his crocodile form represented the fierce protection of the local waters
nodes.symbolism: the crocodile as the local guardian of the waterways, the territorial predator as divine protector
nodes.neumannArchetype: the territorial masculine predator who guards the local waters of consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient crocodile god of the 10th nome of Lower Egypt

nodes.name: Kunitama
nodes.domain: the soul of the land, the spirit of the nation, the land itself as divine
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the kami that is the soul or spirit of the land itself, the divine essence of the national territory
nodes.significantEvent: the concept that the land of Japan itself possesses a divine soul (tama), the national territory as a living spiritual entity
nodes.symbolism: the land as possessing a divine soul, the nation as a living spiritual being, the earth itself as conscious and divine, the territory as a sacred body
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the soul of the national territory, the feminine earth-consciousness that is the land itself

nodes.name: Fangfeng
nodes.domain: giants, rebellion, floods, punishment
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: enormous giant of ancient Chinese mythology
nodes.significantEvent: killed by Yu the Great for arriving late to an assembly of spirits, or for rebellion against the cosmic order
nodes.symbolism: the giant as the untamed chthonic force that must be subdued by the culture hero (Yu), disobedience to cosmic authority punished by death
nodes.neumannArchetype: the chthonic giant subdued by the ordering hero, the raw natural force brought under the control of civilization
nodes.deathCircumstances: As a mythological figure, Fangfeng is mostly known for arriving late for an assembly called by Yu the Great after the end of the Great Flood and then being executed at the orders of Yu.

nodes.name: Jinjia Yinsuo
nodes.domain: protection, enforcement, Buddhist law
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: celestial enforcers in golden armor carrying chains and locks
nodes.significantEvent: divine guards and enforcers of heavenly law, they bind and restrain demons and wrongdoers at the command of celestial authorities
nodes.symbolism: divine law enforced through binding and restraint, the golden armor as the incorruptible power of heaven, chains as the bonds of cosmic justice
nodes.neumannArchetype: the enforcing masculine of the cosmic order, the binding power that restricts the chaotic and demonic

nodes.name: Hu Ye
nodes.domain: the sea, tigers, protection, Taiwan folk religion
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: tiger god worshipped in Taiwanese and Southeast Asian Chinese communities
nodes.significantEvent: controls tigers and protects against wild animal attacks, worshipped in temples alongside other deities, associated with the suppression of evil spirits through tiger power
nodes.symbolism: the tiger as both danger and divine protector, the wild animal controlled by the sacred, the ferocity of nature channeled into protection
nodes.neumannArchetype: the theriomorphic guardian, the masculine that commands the tiger power of the unconscious and directs it toward protection

nodes.name: Li Shiji}}
nodes.domain: war, strategy, loyalty, the Tang Dynasty
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: one of the greatest Tang Dynasty generals
nodes.significantEvent: played crucial roles in establishing and defending the Tang Dynasty, brilliant strategist who helped unify China
nodes.symbolism: the loyal general whose strategic genius serves the righteous dynasty
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive warrior masculine in service to the patriarchal order
nodes.birthCircumstances: Tang Dynasty general (594-669 CE) who served Emperor Taizong

nodes.name: Hok Tek Cheng Sin
nodes.domain: luck, earth, agriculture, prosperity
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: earth deity associated with luck and prosperity
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped in Southeast Asian Chinese communities as a deity of earth and good fortune, a localized form of the earth god (Tu Di Gong)
nodes.symbolism: the earth as the source of agricultural prosperity, local earth gods as the foundation of community fortune
nodes.neumannArchetype: the earth father as the benevolent local patriarch, the grounding masculine of agricultural fortune
nodes.deathCircumstances: He died when he was 102 years old at 1042 BC on the reign of King Cheng of Zhou.

nodes.name: General Baokeng
nodes.domain: war, storms, latrines, protection
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: military spirit associated with latrines and storms
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped as a protective martial deity with power over storms and unclean spaces
nodes.symbolism: protection that extends even to the most impure spaces, the sacred in the profane
nodes.neumannArchetype: the protective masculine in the realm of the shadow, the guardian of the rejected and impure

nodes.name: Ma Dai
nodes.domain: war, loyalty, the Three Kingdoms
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: cousin and follower of Ma Chao
nodes.significantEvent: remained loyal to Shu Han throughout the Three Kingdoms conflicts, continued his family military tradition
nodes.symbolism: the loyal cousin who sustains the family martial tradition, steadfast duty
nodes.neumannArchetype: the supportive masculine who sustains the warriors legacy through steady loyalty
nodes.birthCircumstances: cousin of Ma Chao, served Shu Han during the Three Kingdoms period
nodes.deathCircumstances: Ma Chao wrote: "Over 200 members of my family were killed by Cao Cao.

nodes.name: Nehalennia
nodes.domain: seafaring, trade, prosperity, the afterlife
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: seated woman with basket of fruit and a dog at her feet, sometimes with a ships prow
nodes.significantEvent: over 160 votive altars found at her temple sites in Domburg and Colijnsplaat in the Netherlands, submerged by the sea
nodes.symbolism: safe passage across the sea, prosperity through trade, guidance of the dead, abundance
nodes.neumannArchetype: Good Mother as protector and provider, guide across the waters of death

nodes.name: Guan Sheng
nodes.domain: war, righteousness, literature
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: warrior deity associated with both martial and literary virtues
nodes.significantEvent: one of the manifestations or attendants of Guan Yu in the broader Guan Di cult
nodes.symbolism: the unity of martial and literary virtue, the warrior who is also a scholar
nodes.neumannArchetype: the integrated masculine combining the warrior and the sage

nodes.name: Epiales
nodes.domain: nightmares, sleep terrors, incubi
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: nightmare spirit that sits on the sleepers chest
nodes.significantEvent: causes nightmares by pressing on sleepers chests, the experience of sleep paralysis personified
nodes.symbolism: the terror that comes in sleep, the nightmare as a visitation by a malevolent spirit, the weight of unconscious fear
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow incubus of the unconscious, the terrifying visitor from the depths of sleep
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from Nyx in some traditions

nodes.name: Baimei Shen
nodes.domain: war, protection, martial arts
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: fierce warrior deity with distinctive white eyebrows
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped as a martial protective deity in Chinese folk religion
nodes.symbolism: martial protection through fierce appearance, the warrior whose distinctive mark signals divine power
nodes.neumannArchetype: the fierce protective masculine, the guardian whose terrifying appearance wards off evil

nodes.name: Mingong
nodes.domain: labor, construction, canals, water management
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: deity or spirit of construction and engineering projects
nodes.significantEvent: associated with the great engineering works of Chinese civilization including canal construction and water management
nodes.symbolism: the divine dimension of engineering labor, human construction as a sacred act
nodes.neumannArchetype: the culture hero of infrastructure, the masculine ordering of the landscape through engineering

nodes.name: White Tiger
nodes.domain: the west, metal, autumn, war, death
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: great white tiger, guardian of the western sky, composed of seven star constellations
nodes.significantEvent: represents autumn, war, and death in Chinese cosmology, one of the four directional guardians alongside Azure Dragon, Vermilion Bird, and Black Tortoise
nodes.symbolism: the killing power of autumn when nature dies, the metal element as the sword of harvest, the tiger as the western death power, war as the autumnal cosmic function
nodes.neumannArchetype: the destructive masculine of the western death direction, the tiger power of the descending consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the Four Symbols of Chinese constellations, associated with the West

nodes.name: Li Mu李牧
nodes.domain: war, strategy, defense, the Zhao state
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: one of Chinas legendary Four Great Generals of the Warring States
nodes.significantEvent: defended Zhao against multiple Qin invasions through brilliant defensive strategy, eventually executed on false charges due to court intrigue, his removal allowed Qin to conquer Zhao
nodes.symbolism: the brilliant general destroyed by his own courts jealousy, defensive genius that can hold off an empire, the tragic pattern of political intrigue destroying military capability
nodes.neumannArchetype: the protective masculine destroyed by the shadow within his own patriarchal system
nodes.birthCircumstances: general of the state of Zhao during the Warring States period

nodes.name: Lu Xiong
nodes.domain: war, revenge, the Han Dynasty
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Han Dynasty warrior and general
nodes.significantEvent: served in the conflicts of the late Qin and early Han periods
nodes.symbolism: the warrior whose personal vengeance serves the larger historical transformation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the martial masculine whose personal drive aligns with the great historical transition

nodes.name: Pa-cha
nodes.domain: plague, locusts, agriculture, protection
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: plague-averting deity who protects against locusts and pestilence
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped by farming communities to protect crops against locust swarms and agricultural plagues
nodes.symbolism: divine protection against the natural disasters that threaten the harvest, the sacred defense of agriculture
nodes.neumannArchetype: the protective masculine that guards the Great Mothers bounty (crops) against destruction
nodes.birthCircumstances: His body beneath the waist resembles a bell (some legends state he was born from a bell) with big crawled bird paws underneath.

nodes.name: Poh Seng Tai Tay
nodes.domain: prosperity, protection, Southeast Asian Chinese religion
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: local protective deity worshipped in Southeast Asian Chinese temples
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped in Malaysian and Singaporean Chinese communities as a patron of prosperity and protection
nodes.symbolism: the Chinese protective tradition adapted to Southeast Asian contexts
nodes.neumannArchetype: the localized protective father of diaspora communities

nodes.name: Qingxu Daode Zhenjun
nodes.domain: Daoism, moral purity, heavenly administration
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Daoist heavenly official of clear virtue
nodes.significantEvent: one of the Daoist heavenly administrators associated with moral purity and the governance of spiritual realms
nodes.symbolism: the administration of heaven through moral purity, virtue as the qualification for celestial governance
nodes.neumannArchetype: the ordered masculine consciousness expressed through moral-administrative authority

nodes.name: Shang Rong
nodes.domain: music, education, loyalty, the Shang Dynasty
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Shang Dynasty sage and musician, teacher of ethics and music
nodes.significantEvent: served as teacher to the Shang Dynasty princes, one of the loyal ministers who opposed King Zhous tyranny
nodes.symbolism: the sage musician whose art carries moral education, music as the vehicle of ethical teaching
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive old sage who transmits culture through music and moral teaching

nodes.name: Epione
nodes.domain: healing, soothing of pain, medicine
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: gentle goddess who soothes pain
nodes.significantEvent: mother of the entire healing divine family, her name means she who soothes, worshipped alongside Asclepius at Epidaurus
nodes.symbolism: the feminine principle of soothing pain, the mother of the healing arts, gentleness as the foundation of medicine
nodes.neumannArchetype: the nurturing feminine as the source of all healing, the mother whose gentleness generates the entire tradition of medicine
nodes.birthCircumstances: wife of Asclepius, mother of Hygieia, Panacea, Iaso, Aceso, and Aegle

nodes.name: Philyra
nodes.domain: healing, herbs, beauty, nature, wisdom
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful Oceanid nymph or Titaness, sometimes depicted as half-horse
nodes.significantEvent: loved by Cronus who transformed himself into a horse to mate with her, bore the centaur Chiron, later transformed into a linden tree
nodes.symbolism: the feminine wisdom that generates the wisest of all beings (Chiron), the nymph transformed into a tree, nature as the source of healing knowledge
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wise oceanic feminine who bears the great healer-teacher (Chiron), the Great Mother as the source of all herbal and medical wisdom
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Oceanus, or a Thessalian nymph

nodes.name: He-He Er Xian
nodes.domain: harmony, joy, unity, marriage, friendship
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: two laughing boys or men, one holding a lotus and the other a box (he-he sounds like harmony-unity), always depicted together and smiling
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped as the immortals of harmony and unity, brought together during weddings and celebrations, sometimes identified with the monks Hanshan and Shide
nodes.symbolism: the union of opposites in harmony, joyful concord, the twin laughing spirits who embody the principle that harmony comes from the meeting of different elements
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine twins as the embodiment of harmonious consciousness, the doubled joy of unified opposites

nodes.name: Wen Shen
nodes.domain: literature, culture, scholarship, writing
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: deity of literature and culture
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped by scholars and writers seeking inspiration and literary success
nodes.symbolism: the divine origin of literary achievement, writing as a sacred act
nodes.neumannArchetype: the culture-father as patron of the written word

nodes.name: Wenquxing
nodes.domain: literature, the stars, examinations, education
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: star spirit associated with literary talent and examination success
nodes.significantEvent: the literary star whose blessing grants success in civil examinations, one of the stellar patrons of scholarship
nodes.symbolism: the star of literary achievement, celestial endorsement of human learning
nodes.neumannArchetype: the stellar masculine as patron of literary consciousness

nodes.name: Xiaoziye
nodes.domain: protection, local cult, children, fertility
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: local protective deity associated with children and fertility
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped in local communities for the protection of children and fertility blessings
nodes.symbolism: the local divine protection of the most vulnerable, fertility as a locally mediated divine gift
nodes.neumannArchetype: the localized protective masculine guarding childhood and new life

nodes.name: Phra Kalachai Si
nodes.domain: Southeast Asian Hinduism, the deity of time, Kala, Thai Hindu worship
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a deity worshipped in Thai Hindu tradition, associated with Kala (time) and the power of time
nodes.significantEvent: represents the Hindu concept of Kala (time) as worshipped in Southeast Asian (particularly Thai) Hindu traditions, the divine power of time that governs all things
nodes.symbolism: time as a divine power worshipped in Southeast Asian Hindu traditions, the Thai adaptation of the Hindu temporal deity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine of cosmic time, the patriarchal consciousness of temporal order
nodes.domain_source: Thai Hindu syncretic tradition; Devasthan in Bangkok
nodes.object_source: Thai iconographic tradition
nodes.characterTrait_source: Thai Hindu tradition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Thai iconographic tradition
nodes.significantEvent_source: Thai Hindu syncretic tradition

nodes.name: Yang Ren
nodes.domain: the supernatural, loyalty, the Investiture of the Gods, eyes of heaven
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: warrior whose eyes were replaced with divine eyes on his palms, giving him supernatural sight
nodes.significantEvent: had his original eyes gouged out but was given divine hands-eyes by his Daoist master, allowing him to see in all directions through his palms, served the Zhou cause in the Investiture of the Gods
nodes.symbolism: the loss of ordinary sight replaced by supernatural vision, eyes in the palms as the union of seeing and doing, the wounded hero whose disability becomes his greatest power
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wounded hero whose lost sight is replaced by the supernatural eyes of consciousness, ordinary perception transformed into divine awareness

nodes.name: Zhao Yu
nodes.domain: war, loyalty, the Three Kingdoms, Zhao Yun
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: warrior figure associated with the Three Kingdoms period
nodes.significantEvent: fought during the Three Kingdoms period as a loyal warrior
nodes.symbolism: the loyal warrior of the Three Kingdoms, service in a divided age
nodes.neumannArchetype: the loyal masculine warrior of the divided kingdom
nodes.deathCircumstances: Zhao Yu died during the Daye (大業) era (605–618 CE).

nodes.name: Siming
nodes.domain: fate, lifespan, the hearth, records of life and death
nodes.object: ledger of life and death, pen
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: celestial official who records the lifespan and fate of every mortal
nodes.significantEvent: keeps the divine register of every persons birth, death, and allotted lifespan, can extend or shorten life based on ones moral conduct, associated with the Kitchen God and the celestial bureaucracy
nodes.symbolism: fate as a bureaucratic record, the divine ledger of life as the ultimate accounting, the lifespan as something that can be earned or lost through moral behavior
nodes.neumannArchetype: the patriarchal consciousness of cosmic accounting, the father archetype as the keeper of lifes records

nodes.name: Tam Kung
nodes.domain: sea, weather, fishing, protection, Hong Kong
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: young deity associated with the sea and weather prediction, worshipped in southern China
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped as a sea deity in Hong Kong and southern China, his temples serve as weather prediction centers, his festival on the fourth day of the fourth lunar month is an important local celebration
nodes.symbolism: the youthful sea protector of fishing communities, divine weather prediction as the protection of livelihoods
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child as protector of the fishing community, the youthful masculine who guards those who venture onto the oceanic unconscious

nodes.name: The Trickster
nodes.domain: deception, transformation, boundary-crossing, culture creation
nodes.characterTrait: cunning, amoral, creative, disruptive, humorous, shape-shifting
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: shape-shifter, often animal form, boundary-crosser between human and divine
nodes.significantEvent: steals fire or sacred knowledge for humanity across multiple traditions, creates through accident or mischief
nodes.symbolism: the creative power of chaos, breaking taboos to advance culture, the shadow side of the culture hero
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow archetype, creative destruction preceding cultural advancement

nodes.name: Epiphron
nodes.domain: prudence, thoughtfulness, carefulness
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: spirit of prudence and careful thought
nodes.significantEvent: embodies the virtue of thinking before acting, the opposite of recklessness
nodes.symbolism: the virtue of careful consideration, prudence as a divine quality, the thoughtfulness that prevents disaster
nodes.neumannArchetype: the cautious aspect of consciousness, the reflective principle before action
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Erebus and Nyx in some traditions

nodes.domain: nightmares, frightening dreams, prophetic terrors
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: takes the form of animals and monsters in nightmares
nodes.significantEvent: appears in dreams as terrifying beasts, serpents, and monsters, creating the nightmares that torment sleepers
nodes.symbolism: the bestial content of the unconscious that erupts in sleep, the animal terrors hidden beneath consciousness
nodes.neumannArchetype: the theriomorphic unconscious, the beast-forms of the deep psyche that surface in nightmares
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Hypnos (Sleep), brother of Morpheus and Phantasos

nodes.name: Ri Ye Youshen
nodes.domain: day and night, patrol, protection, the cycle of time
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: spirits who patrol the world during day and night
nodes.significantEvent: divine patrollers who roam the world during day and night reporting back to the Jade Emperor on the affairs of humans, ensuring no wrongdoing goes unnoticed
nodes.symbolism: the divine surveillance of human behavior across the entire cycle of day and night, the all-seeing bureaucracy of heaven
nodes.neumannArchetype: the watchful masculine consciousness that never sleeps, the divine eyes that maintain awareness through the entire cycle of light and dark

nodes.name: Tianlong
nodes.domain: Buddhism, dragons, celestial beings, protection
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: celestial dragon beings in the Buddhist cosmology, one of the eight classes of supernatural beings
nodes.significantEvent: celestial dragons who protect the Buddhist dharma, attend the Buddhas teachings, and guard temples and sacred sites
nodes.symbolism: the dragon as protector of the dharma, the celestial serpent power dedicated to spiritual truth, the dragon transformed from nature spirit to guardian of enlightenment
nodes.neumannArchetype: the dragon of the unconscious transformed into the protector of the highest consciousness (dharma)

nodes.name: Yuqiang
nodes.domain: sea, wind, the north, the abyss
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: sea god and wind god of the north, sometimes depicted as a fish-bird hybrid
nodes.significantEvent: rules the northern abyss and controls the arctic winds, associated with the vast dark ocean beyond the known world
nodes.symbolism: the abyss of the northern sea as the ultimate unknown, wind from the darkest direction, the ocean beyond all maps
nodes.neumannArchetype: the abyssal masculine of the deep north, the unconscious depths of the most remote and unknown waters
nodes.birthCircumstances: primordial deity of the northern sea and wind

nodes.name: The World Tree
nodes.domain: cosmic axis, connection between worlds, life, knowledge
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: immense tree connecting heaven, earth, and underworld, roots reaching into primordial waters
nodes.significantEvent: serves as cosmic axis in Norse (Yggdrasil), Mesoamerican, Siberian, and Hindu cosmologies
nodes.symbolism: axis mundi connecting all planes of existence, the living structure of the cosmos, knowledge through vertical ascent
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as world-sustaining tree, the axis of transformation between conscious and unconscious

nodes.name: Erechtheus
nodes.domain: kingship, earth-born rule, Athenian autochthony
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: early king of Athens, sometimes confused with or identified as Erichthonius
nodes.significantEvent: sacrificed his daughter to save Athens during war with Eleusis, receiving an oracle that demanded such sacrifice, swallowed by the earth after his victory
nodes.symbolism: the earth-born king who returns to the earth, the ruler who sacrifices his own family for the city, Athenian autochthony
nodes.neumannArchetype: the earth-born hero-king who is reclaimed by the Great Mother, the patriarch who sacrifices the feminine (daughter) for the collective
nodes.birthCircumstances: autochthonous (earth-born) king of Athens, or son of Pandion I
nodes.deathCircumstances: In the following battle between the forces of Athens and Eleusis, Erechtheus won the battle and slew Eumolpus, but then himself fell, struck down by Poseidon's trident.

nodes.significantEvent: Socrates famously described his daimon as an inner voice that warned him against wrong action, each person was believed to receive a daimon at birth
nodes.symbolism: the personal divine spark within each mortal, the inner guide between human and divine, individual fate as a spiritual companion
nodes.neumannArchetype: the inner voice of consciousness, the guiding animus or anima that connects the individual psyche to the transpersonal

nodes.symbolism: the local transmission of the Apolline gifts of music and healing
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine son who carries the solar fathers gifts to the local community
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Apollo and the nymph Rheio in some traditions

nodes.name: Yuding Zhenren
nodes.domain: Daoism, immortality, cultivation, the Investiture of the Gods
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Daoist immortal of the jade tradition
nodes.significantEvent: one of the Twelve Golden Immortals of Kunlun Mountain in the Fengshen Yanyi, master of Yang Jian (Erlang Shen)
nodes.symbolism: jade purity as the goal of Daoist cultivation, the master who teaches the half-divine hero
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wise old man who trains the hero of consciousness

nodes.name: King Di Xin of Shang
nodes.domain: tyranny, the fall of the Shang, debauchery, the Mandate of Heaven lost
nodes.object: wine pool, meat forest, Cannon Burning punishment device
nodes.characterTrait: tyrannical, debauched, cruel, intelligent but corrupted
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: last king of the Shang Dynasty, physically powerful and intelligent but corrupted by his consort Daji
nodes.significantEvent: created the Wine Pool and Meat Forest for orgies, invented the Paolao (cannon burning) torture, his tyranny caused Heaven to withdraw its Mandate and support King Wu of Zhous rebellion, committed suicide by burning himself in his palace
nodes.symbolism: the archetypal tyrant whose debauchery causes the fall of a dynasty, the Mandate of Heaven withdrawn from the unworthy, the last ruler destroyed by his own excess
nodes.neumannArchetype: the negative father archetype, the patriarchal ruler corrupted by the shadow anima (Daji) whose excess triggers the cosmic transfer of power
nodes.birthCircumstances: last ruler of the Shang Dynasty (r. c. 1075-1046 BCE)

nodes.name: Zhang Guifang
nodes.domain: war, the Shang Dynasty, loyalty to the doomed
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Shang Dynasty general in the Fengshen Yanyi
nodes.significantEvent: served the doomed Shang Dynasty against the rising Zhou, fought and died for King Zhou despite the cosmic inevitability of the Shangs fall
nodes.symbolism: the loyal general of the doomed dynasty, service to the old order even unto death
nodes.neumannArchetype: the loyal masculine servant of the dying patriarchal order

nodes.name: Zhao Qi
nodes.domain: ghosts, the supernatural, haunting
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a supernatural ghost figure in Chinese folklore
nodes.significantEvent: associated with ghost stories and supernatural encounters in Chinese folk tradition
nodes.symbolism: the supernatural presence that reminds mortals of the other world, the ghost as the unresolved dead
nodes.neumannArchetype: the unresolved shadow that haunts consciousness

nodes.name: Zheng Lun
nodes.domain: gate protection, the supernatural, nasal power
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: guardian deity who emits beams from his nostrils, one of a pair of supernatural gate guardians in the Fengshen Yanyi
nodes.significantEvent: paired with Heng Ha Er Jiang (the two generals Heng and Ha), guards gates and temple entrances, one snorts and the other blows to create devastating supernatural attacks
nodes.symbolism: the paired gate guardians whose breath weapons protect sacred spaces, the power of inhalation and exhalation as cosmic forces
nodes.neumannArchetype: the threshold guardian whose breath (spirit/pneuma) is a weapon of consciousness

nodes.name: Igai
nodes.domain: mourning, the afterlife, grief, the netherworld
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: deity associated with mourning and funerary rites
nodes.significantEvent: one of the beings encountered in the afterlife, associated with the grief and mourning that accompanies death
nodes.symbolism: the divine embodiment of mourning, grief as a sacred process of transition
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow of grief in the passage through the unconscious

nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the consort or companion of Sol (the sun goddess)
nodes.significantEvent: associated with Sol (the sun), his name may relate to gleaming or radiance
nodes.symbolism: the companion of the sun as the radiance associated with solar light, the masculine complement to the feminine sun
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine companion of the solar feminine, the radiance-consciousness that accompanies the sun

nodes.domain: the morning, the dawn, the underworld hours, stellar navigation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: deity associated with the dawn and the navigation of the underworld hours
nodes.significantEvent: one of the deities who assisted the solar barque in its journey through the underworld hours of the night

nodes.domain: fertility, earth, creation, death, regeneration

nodes.symbolism: the undifferentiated feminine containing both life and death, the womb and the tomb as one
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother archetype itself, preceding differentiation into Good Mother and Terrible Mother

nodes.domain: Orphic cosmogony, the firstborn, creation

nodes.symbolism: the first creative impulse of the cosmos, the light-bearer who emerges from the cosmic egg, the god swallowed and reborn
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child as the first light of cosmic consciousness emerging from the uroboric egg
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from the Cosmic Egg in Orphic cosmogony

nodes.name: Rhesus
nodes.domain: war, Thrace, horses, the Trojan alliance, night raids
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Thracian king with magnificent white horses and golden armor
nodes.significantEvent: came to Troy with his magnificent white horses, an oracle said Troy could never fall if his horses drank from the Xanthus river and ate Trojan grass, Odysseus and Diomedes killed him in a night raid before the horses could drink
nodes.symbolism: the savior who arrives too late, destiny prevented by a single night, the horses that could have saved Troy but never reached the river
nodes.neumannArchetype: the solar hero (white horses, golden armor) whose light is extinguished by the shadow warriors (night raid) before his saving potential can be realized
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of the river god Strymon and one of the Muses, king of Thrace

nodes.name: Sarpedon I
nodes.domain: war, honor, Lycia, divine lineage, the afterlife
nodes.characterTrait: noble, brave, honorable, favored by Zeus
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the tallest and most handsome of the Trojan allies
nodes.significantEvent: led the Lycian contingent at Troy, killed Patroclus close friend Tlepolemus, later killed by Patroclus, Zeus wept tears of blood for him and had Sleep and Death carry his body back to Lycia for proper burial
nodes.symbolism: the son of Zeus who cannot be saved even by his divine father, the limits of divine power against fate, the honored warrior returned home by supernatural means
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine son whose father (Zeus) cannot save him from fate, the hero whose death reveals the limits of even the sky fathers power
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Zeus and Laodamia (or Europa), king of Lycia, grandson of Bellerophon

nodes.name: Talthybius
nodes.domain: heralds, diplomacy, sacred messages, the Trojan War
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: venerable herald, respected by both sides

nodes.symbolism: the sacredness of the herald, the inviolable messenger who moves between warring factions, the divine protection of honest communication
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine mediator whose sacred function transcends the conflict between opposing forces
nodes.birthCircumstances: herald of Agamemnon and the Greek army at Troy
nodes.deathCircumstances: In Hecuba, Talthybius brings an order from Agamemnon to Hecuba, telling her to bury her daughter, Polyxena, who was sacrificed to Achilles.

nodes.name: The Dying God
nodes.domain: death, resurrection, vegetation, sacrifice, renewal
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: young beautiful male, often torn apart or hung upon a tree
nodes.significantEvent: dies and is reborn cyclically, identified across Osiris, Attis, Adonis, Tammuz, Baldur, and Dionysus
nodes.symbolism: death as prerequisite for renewal, the vegetation cycle as divine drama, sacrifice as cosmic necessity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the son-lover of the Great Mother who must die to be reborn, the hero in his sacrificial aspect

nodes.name: Ersa
nodes.domain: dew, the morning dew, freshness
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: gentle maiden embodying the morning dew
nodes.significantEvent: the morning dew personified, nourishing the earth each dawn with gentle moisture
nodes.symbolism: the renewal that comes each morning, the gentle moisture that sustains life between night and day, tears of the dawn
nodes.neumannArchetype: the gentle feminine that mediates between the night (unconscious) and day (consciousness) through the gift of moisture
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Zeus and Selene (Moon), or daughter of Eos (Dawn)

nodes.neumannArchetype: the solar warrior aspect of the Great Father, the martial masculine consciousness that burns with the suns destructive power

nodes.domain: the morning star, Venus at dawn, heralding the day
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: radiant youth carrying a torch, the morning star personified

nodes.symbolism: the star that announces the coming day, hope preceding fulfillment, the light before the light, the herald of solar consciousness
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine herald of consciousness, the animus who precedes the full light of solar awareness
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Eos (Dawn) and Cephalus, or of Atlas, brother of Hesperus

nodes.name: Ptah
nodes.domain: creation, craftsmanship, metalworking, architecture, speech
nodes.object: was-scepter combining with djed and ankh (the unique Ptah-scepter, signifying stability, life, and power); ptah-cap (his distinctive tight skullcap); mummy-wrappings
nodes.characterTrait: creative, craftsman, articulate, world-building, silent power
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Anthropomorphic mummified man wearing a tight skullcap and a straight false beard; holding the unique was-djed-ankh scepter; standing on a Ma'at-pedestal.
nodes.significantEvent: In the Memphite cosmogony (preserved in the Shabaka Stone, 25th Dynasty though probably much older), Ptah creates the cosmos through thought and speech: 'the heart conceived, the tongue spoke' — a remarkably proto-philosophical theology. All other gods are aspects of Ptah's creative thought. In Memphis, paired with Sekhmet (consort) and Nefertem (son) as the Memphite triad.
nodes.symbolism: creation through thought and speech (logos), the divine craftsman who shapes reality, the power of the spoken word to create, the union of conception and articulation as the creative act
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father as the divine logos, the masculine creative principle that shapes the world through thought and speech rather than physical generation
nodes.birthCircumstances: Self-engendered, primordial; identified with the primordial mound itself in some interpretations.
nodes.domain_source: Pyramid Texts; the Memphite Theology (Shabaka Stone, Cairo Museum) — the central source for the Memphite cosmogony; standard Egyptian iconography

nodes.name: Theban Triad
nodes.domain: Thebes, divine family, cosmic governance, the Karnak temple
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the divine family of Thebes consisting of Amun (father), Mut (mother), and Khonsu (son)
nodes.significantEvent: the most powerful divine family in New Kingdom Egypt, worshipped together at the Karnak temple complex, the model for divine family worship throughout Egypt
nodes.symbolism: the divine family as the template of cosmic order, father-mother-son as the trinitarian structure of divinity, the Karnak complex as the earthly home of the supreme divine family
nodes.neumannArchetype: the archetypal divine family: Great Father (Amun), Great Mother (Mut), and Divine Child (Khonsu)

nodes.symbolism: the lioness of war at the southern temple, the fierce feminine protector of the sacred precinct
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible Great Mother in her lioness-warrior form at the southern sanctuary

nodes.name: Ame-no-Koyane
nodes.domain: prayer, ritual, the Nakatomi clan, divine words, liturgy
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: heavenly kami of prayer and ritual, ancestor of the Nakatomi priestly clan (later the Fujiwara)
nodes.significantEvent: recited the powerful norito (ritual prayers) outside Amaterasus cave, his descendants became the Nakatomi clan who served as ritualists at court, which evolved into the powerful Fujiwara clan that dominated Japanese politics for centuries
nodes.symbolism: the power of ritual prayer to draw forth the divine, the priestly function as the most politically powerful role, the norito as the words that move the gods, the prayer that restores the sun
nodes.neumannArchetype: the priestly masculine whose words (logos) draw the Great Mother (Amaterasu) from the unconscious (cave), the ritual-consciousness that reconnects heaven and earth
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the heavenly kami who participated in luring Amaterasu from her cave

nodes.neumannArchetype: the chthonic monster of the oceanic unconscious, the tentacled shadow of the deep that pulls consciousness down into the abyss

nodes.physicalCharacteristics: mysterious visitors from the otherworld who bring blessings, not a specific deity but a category of spiritual beings

nodes.significantEvent: one of the secondary shrine deities associated with mountain worship and Shugendo practices, served as an attendant spirit in syncretic mountain cult traditions
nodes.symbolism: the child deity as the youthful attendant of the mountain, the subordinate divine figure who serves the greater kami, youth as a quality of the sacred mountain spirit
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child of the mountain, the youthful consciousness that serves the greater mountain deity

nodes.domain: feminine shrine deities, consorts of major kami, the divine feminine of shrines
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the generic term for the female kami enshrined alongside the primary male deity at a shrine
nodes.significantEvent: many major shrines have a himegami (princess kami) enshrined alongside the primary deity, representing the feminine complement to the masculine kami
nodes.symbolism: the feminine divine presence that accompanies every major masculine shrine kami, the princess as the necessary feminine complement to the masculine divine
nodes.neumannArchetype: the anima of the shrine, the feminine that must accompany every masculine kami to complete the divine pair
nodes.birthCircumstances: The fifth deity, Ame-no-Oshikumone, was added much later and is said to be the divine child of Ame no koyane and Himegami.

nodes.neumannArchetype: the dual hero representing the tension between mortal and immortal nature

nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother in her harvest aspect, the generous yielding of the earth

nodes.object: fishing spear, harpoon, nets, bird-catching tools

nodes.symbolism: the left hand as the hand of the hunter and fisher, the invention of tools as a divine gift, fishing and hunting on water as sacred activities requiring divine patronage
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine of the hunt and fishery, the tool-making consciousness of aquatic subsistence

nodes.name: Heibai Wuchang
nodes.domain: death, the underworld, judgment, escort of souls
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: two tall underworld officials, one dressed in white (Bai Wuchang) with a tall hat and protruding tongue, one in black (Hei Wuchang) with a dark face, they escort souls to the underworld
nodes.significantEvent: escort the souls of the dead to the courts of Diyu (hell) for judgment, appear at the time of death to take the departing soul, their tragic origin story exemplifies loyal friendship
nodes.symbolism: death as an impartial escort, the black and white pair as yin and yang of mortality, loyal friendship honored even in the bureaucracy of death
nodes.neumannArchetype: the doubled death figure as the threshold guardians of the underworld, the black/white pair as the duality that greets consciousness at death
nodes.birthCircumstances: originally two loyal friends named Xie Bi An (White) and Fan Wujiu (Black) who died due to their faithful friendship and were appointed as underworld escorts

nodes.name: Mountain God
nodes.domain: mountains, hunting, the wild, mountain passes, mountain danger
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the generic mountain deity (yama no kami) who rules the mountains and their wild inhabitants
nodes.significantEvent: the mountain god who must be appeased by hunters, woodcutters, and travelers, offerings are made before entering the mountains, the mountain kami descends to the rice paddies in spring as the ta-no-kami (rice paddy god) and returns to the mountain in autumn
nodes.symbolism: the mountain as the dwelling of the wild divine, the seasonal descent to the paddies as the divine cycle of mountain and field, the mountain god who becomes the field god as the unity of the wild and the cultivated
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father/Mother of the wild mountain who seasonally descends to the cultivated field, the movement between the wilderness of the unconscious and the cultivated consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: Successive generations of the Son of Heaven Zen carry out sacrifices to heaven and earth, and also to the gods of the mountains.

nodes.name: The Culture Hero
nodes.domain: civilization, fire, agriculture, law, technology
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: divine or semi-divine figure who transgresses divine boundaries for human benefit
nodes.significantEvent: steals fire or sacred knowledge from the gods and gives it to humanity, often punished for this theft, identified across Prometheus, Maui, Anansi, Raven
nodes.symbolism: the advancement of civilization through divine transgression, suffering as the price of knowledge
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hero who separates from the Great Mother and brings consciousness to humanity

nodes.name: Shikigami
nodes.domain: familiar spirits, onmyodo, sorcery, divination, servants
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: invisible spirits summoned and controlled by onmyoji (practitioners of onmyodo), used as familiars and servants
nodes.significantEvent: shikigami were summoned by famous onmyoji like Abe no Seimei to perform tasks, spy on people, guard areas, and do the sorcerers bidding, they could take various forms and were invisible to ordinary people
nodes.symbolism: the summoned spirit as the sorcerers tool, the invisible familiar as the extension of the masters will, the paper talisman as the vessel for the spiritual servant, control over spirits as the essence of Japanese sorcery
nodes.neumannArchetype: the spirit-servants of the magician, the controlled aspects of the unconscious summoned by the disciplined ego-consciousness of the sorcerer

nodes.domain: caution, discretion, piety
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: spirit of discretion and cautious piety
nodes.significantEvent: personification of the cautious reverence that prevents transgression against the gods
nodes.symbolism: the virtue of knowing ones limits before the divine, caution born of reverence
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine consciousness of appropriate limitation before the numinous

nodes.domain: wandering, the planets, celestial movement
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the five wandering stars (planets) personified
nodes.significantEvent: the five visible planets (Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn) personified as wandering divine beings moving against the fixed stars
nodes.symbolism: the divine wanderers who move through the heavens on their own paths, celestial freedom against the fixed order, the planets as gods in motion
nodes.neumannArchetype: the individual lights of consciousness moving independently through the greater cosmic order
nodes.birthCircumstances: children of Eos (Dawn) and Astraeus (Stars)

nodes.name: Heidi
nodes.domain: sky, the north, water, winter, darkness
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Black Emperor or Dark Emperor, ruler of the northern sky
nodes.significantEvent: presides over winter and the northern direction, associated with the water element and the color black in Chinese five-element cosmology
nodes.symbolism: the dark and cold as a cosmic principle, the north as the direction of death and winter, water in its frozen and dangerous aspect
nodes.neumannArchetype: the dark father of the northern unconscious, the winter consciousness where yang retreats into the depths
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the Wufang Shangdi (Five Forms of the Highest Deity), rules the north and winter

nodes.name: Geb
nodes.domain: earth, fertility, vegetation, the underworld, kingship
nodes.object: ankh; was-scepter; the earth itself (his body)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Anthropomorphic man lying beneath Nut (his sister-wife the sky), often green-skinned to indicate vegetation, sometimes with vegetation growing from his body. In iconography, depicted reclining as the foundation of the cosmos.
nodes.significantEvent: Son of Shu and Tefnut; cosmic-incestuous spouse of his sister Nut; father (by Nut) of Osiris, Isis, Set, and Nephthys. After his union with Nut, Shu (their father) separated them on Atum's command — Geb pressed down as the earth, Nut lifted up as the sky. Geb's laughter is earthquakes; his earth-body sustains all life and contains the dead.
nodes.symbolism: the earth as the male principle (reversed from many other mythologies), the supine body as the landscape, the green skin as fertile earth, the goose as the primordial cackle of creation, the throne as resting on the earth
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father as the earth itself, the masculine principle that is the ground of all being, the body upon which the drama of consciousness is enacted
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Shu and Tefnut.

nodes.name: Suijin
nodes.domain: water, rivers, wells, rain, irrigation, water spirits
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the kami of water in all its forms, the divine presence in rivers, wells, springs, and rain
nodes.significantEvent: Suijin is the general term for water kami worshipped throughout Japan at rivers, wells, and springs, essential for rice cultivation and daily life, water was considered the purest element and the dwelling of divinity
nodes.symbolism: water as the most sacred element, the river as the flowing divine, the well as the deep source of life, irrigation as the channeling of divine water for human sustenance
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of water, the feminine fluidity that gives life to all cultivation and consciousness

nodes.name: Zuijin
nodes.domain: shrine guardians, the gate, protection, warriors, shrine entrance
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: armored warrior figures that guard the entrances of Shinto shrines, depicted as fierce warriors in ancient armor
nodes.significantEvent: statues of zuijin (gate-guardians) are placed at the entrances of many Shinto shrines to protect the sacred space from evil spirits, they are the divine warriors who defend the threshold between the profane and sacred
nodes.symbolism: the armored guardian at the gate between worlds, the divine warrior who protects the sacred threshold, the armed figure that defends the shrine from spiritual pollution
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine guardians of the threshold between the conscious (profane) world and the unconscious (sacred) space of the shrine

nodes.name: Itztlacoliuhqui
nodes.domain: obsidian, frost, cold, justice, punishment, blindness, the curved obsidian knife
nodes.characterTrait: cold, punishing, blinding, just, obsidian-sharp, frost-wielding
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Curved Obsidian Blade, depicted blindfolded with obsidian-bladed instruments, associated with frost and cold
nodes.significantEvent: represents the cold and frost that destroys crops, also associated with blind justice and punishment, an aspect of Tezcatlipoca connected to coldness and the obsidian blade, his blindfold represents the blindness of justice
nodes.symbolism: the curved obsidian as the cold blade of justice, frost as the punishment of the earth, blindness as the impartiality of divine judgment, the freezing of the earth as cosmic punishment
nodes.neumannArchetype: the blind justice-consciousness of the cold, the masculine of the obsidian blade that punishes without seeing

nodes.domain: speed, the messenger, Huitzilopochtlis lieutenant, warfare, running
nodes.characterTrait: fast, swift, messenger, lieutenant, running, warlike
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Swift Runner, the swift messenger and lieutenant of Huitzilopochtli
nodes.significantEvent: served as the running messenger and deputy of the war god Huitzilopochtli, led the warriors in ritual races and carried the god's standard in battle
nodes.symbolism: the swift runner as the earthly deputy of the sun, speed as a divine quality of warfare, the lieutenant who carries the war gods authority on earth
nodes.neumannArchetype: the messenger-son who carries the authority of the solar war-father, the swift masculine of earthly warfare

nodes.name: Wakumusubi
nodes.domain: young growth, sprouting, agricultural beginnings, new life
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: kami of young plant growth and sprouting, the divine spirit of new agricultural life
nodes.significantEvent: represents the young growth of plants, the first sprouting of seeds, born from the death of the fire god as the renewal of life from destruction
nodes.symbolism: the young sprout as new life from the ashes of fire, the beginning of growth as a divine event, the spring sprouting as the resurrection of the vegetative spirit
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child of renewed growth, the young vegetation-consciousness that springs from the death of the destructive element
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from the slain body of Kagutsuchi, the fire god

nodes.domain: sky, thunder, sovereignty, law, cosmic order
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: bearded ruler enthroned in the sky, wielding thunder
nodes.significantEvent: appears across Indo-European traditions as Zeus, Jupiter, Dyaus Pitar, Tyr, establishing cosmic and social order
nodes.symbolism: divine sovereignty over the cosmos, the separation of heaven and earth, law as divine mandate
nodes.neumannArchetype: the archetypal Father, the masculine principle separated from the Great Mother

nodes.name: Eunostus
nodes.domain: lawful conduct, orderly behavior
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: spirit of orderly and lawful conduct
nodes.significantEvent: personification of proper behavior within the bounds of law and custom
nodes.symbolism: the inner disposition toward lawful action, order as a quality of character not merely external compliance
nodes.neumannArchetype: the ordered aspect of consciousness, the internalization of cosmic law

nodes.name: Podalirius
nodes.domain: healing, medicine, the Trojan War, Asclepian tradition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: physician warrior, son of Asclepius
nodes.significantEvent: served as physician to the Greeks at Troy, specialized in internal medicine while his brother Machaon was a surgeon, after the war established healing centers
nodes.symbolism: the medical tradition descended from the divine healer, internal medicine as a divine art, the healer-warrior who saves rather than destroys
nodes.neumannArchetype: the son of the Great Healer who carries the internal medicine tradition, the masculine that preserves life within the context of war
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Asclepius and Epione, brother of Machaon

nodes.domain: feminine divine power, the collective feminine divine, women deities
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the feminine divine aspect or collective of feminine divine powers
nodes.significantEvent: represents the collective feminine divine power in Aztec religion, the concept of the divine feminine as a unified force across multiple goddesses
nodes.symbolism: the collective feminine divine as a unified power, the divine womanhood that pervades multiple goddesses, the feminine as a collective cosmic force
nodes.neumannArchetype: the collective Great Mother principle, the unified feminine consciousness that manifests through multiple goddess forms

nodes.name: Heng and Ha
nodes.domain: protection, Buddhism, temple guardianship, breath
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: two fierce temple guardians, one with mouth open (exhaling Ha) and one with mouth closed (inhaling Heng), muscular and intimidating
nodes.significantEvent: guard the gates of Buddhist temples, one exhales a deadly yellow gas and the other inhales souls, together they represent the complete cycle of breath and the defense of sacred space
nodes.symbolism: the in-breath and out-breath as the fundamental rhythm of existence, the open and closed mouth as the duality of expression and silence, the defense of the sacred through complementary forces
nodes.neumannArchetype: the paired threshold guardians whose complementary breaths represent the masculine defense of sacred consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: Buddhist guardian figures derived from Indian vajra-wielders (dvarapalas)

nodes.name: Household deity
nodes.domain: household protection, domestic religion, the family, ancestors, the hearth
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the collective household deities including Lares, Penates, Genius, and Vesta, worshipped at the household shrine
nodes.significantEvent: the complex of household deities who protected every Roman home, worshipped daily at the lararium, the most personal and continuous form of Roman religious practice
nodes.symbolism: the household as a sacred space with its own divine protectors, domestic religion as the foundation of Roman piety, the daily offering as the maintenance of divine protection
nodes.neumannArchetype: the collective protective spirits of the domestic space, the divine guardians of the personal center of consciousness
