nodes.name: Succoth-benoth
nodes.domain: A deity or cult-object made by the Babylonian deportees in Samaria, per 2 Kings 17:30. Etymology disputed: possibly a Hebrew folk-etymology of Sarpanitu (Marduk's consort), possibly a reference to a Babylonian booth-ritual, possibly an actual deity-name unknown elsewhere.
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a deity associated with Babylonian worship, mentioned in the Hebrew Bible as a foreign god
nodes.significantEvent: mentioned in 2 Kings 17:30 as a deity worshipped by the Babylonians settled in Samaria, associated with fertility cults, exact nature debated by scholars
nodes.symbolism: the foreign god worshipped by the Babylonian colonists, the mysterious deity of the imported religion
nodes.neumannArchetype: the foreign numinous imported by the colonists, the alien divine consciousness brought to the conquered land
nodes.domain_source: 2 Kings 17:30 (the only canonical attestation). NOTE: the Hebrew sukkōt-bənōt literally reads 'booths of daughters'; existence as a Babylonian deity is contested.
nodes.characterTrait_source: 2 Kings 17:30 (the only canonical primary attestation; the descriptors 'Babylonian, syncretic, fertility-associated' are interpretive based on the disputed Sarpanitu-etymology and the contested Babylonian booth-rite tradition)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: 2 Kings 17:30 (no physical description in the primary source; the field is descriptive of the entry's contested status)
nodes.significantEvent_source: 2 Kings 17:30
nodes.eventTypes_source: 2 Kings 17:24-41 (the larger Deuteronomistic narrative context — punishment of the northern kingdom and its replacement population)

nodes.name: Shu
nodes.domain: air, light, dryness, separation, order
nodes.object: ostrich-feather (his symbol, also the symbol of Ma'at); ankh; was-scepter
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Anthropomorphic, wearing the ostrich-feather on his head; often depicted holding up Nut (the sky) with arms raised, separating her from Geb (the earth lying beneath).
nodes.significantEvent: With his sister-consort Tefnut, the first generation engendered by Atum (by his spitting, sneezing, or autoerotic act). Father of Geb and Nut. After their cosmic-incest union, Shu inserts himself between Geb and Nut at Atum/Ra's command, lifting Nut (sky) up and pressing Geb (earth) down — eternally separating heaven and earth.
nodes.symbolism: the breath of life and the space between heaven and earth, the act of separation as the creation of order from chaos, the air as the medium of consciousness, the ostrich feather as lightness and truth
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine principle of separation and differentiation, the consciousness that creates space between the parents (earth and sky) allowing the world to exist
nodes.birthCircumstances: Emerged from Atum (by spitting, sneezing, or autoerotic act); first emergence in the Heliopolitan cosmogony along with his twin-sister Tefnut.

nodes.significantEvent_source: Heliopolitan cosmogony; Coffin Texts spell 76 (the Shu-and-Tefnut emergence narrative)
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Pyramid Texts §1248; Heliopolitan cosmogony
nodes.birthTypes_source: Pyramid Texts §1248

nodes.name: Fides
nodes.domain: faithfulness, loyalty, trust, oaths, honor
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: veiled woman holding grain and fruit, personification of good faith and trust
nodes.significantEvent: one of the oldest Roman deities, her temple on the Capitoline Hill was where the Senate stored treaties, oaths sworn by Fides were the most sacred and binding in Roman law
nodes.symbolism: good faith as the foundation of Roman civilization, the veiled goddess as the hidden trust that underlies all agreements, the treaties in her temple as oaths made divine
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine principle of trust and fidelity, the anima as the guarantor of all binding agreements between men

nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman holding a cornucopia and caduceus, personification of good fortune and happiness
nodes.significantEvent: her temple in the Campus Martius was built by Lucullus after his victories, represented the state of divine favor and success, appeared on coins promising prosperity
nodes.symbolism: happiness as a divine gift, good fortune as the feminine blessing on worthy endeavors, the cornucopia of success
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine as the bestower of fortune and happiness, the anima of success

nodes.name: The Earth Mother
nodes.domain: earth, agriculture, childbirth, nourishment, the dead
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: maternal figure associated with the fertile earth, sometimes depicted pregnant or nursing
nodes.significantEvent: appears across traditions as Gaia, Terra, Pachamama, Nerthus, Prithvi, receiving the dead and bringing forth the living
nodes.symbolism: the earth as living maternal body, the cycle of sowing and harvest as birth and death, the ground that receives and regenerates
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Good Mother aspect of the Great Mother, the nourishing earth

nodes.name: Euphorbus
nodes.domain: the Trojan War, reincarnation, Pythagorean philosophy
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the most beautiful of the Trojan warriors
nodes.significantEvent: killed Patroclus alongside Hector but was then slain by Menelaus, Pythagoras later claimed to be the reincarnation of Euphorbus and recognized his shield in the temple of Hera at Argos
nodes.symbolism: the beautiful warrior whose death connects to the philosophical doctrine of reincarnation, the soul that transmigrates across the ages
nodes.neumannArchetype: the beautiful masculine slain in battle whose soul endures through reincarnation, the bridge between the heroic and philosophical ages
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Panthous, a Trojan elder
nodes.deathCircumstances: In the Iliad Euphorbus wounded Patroclus before the Achaean hero was killed by Hector, and was then killed by Menelaus in the fight for Patroclus' body.

nodes.symbolism: retribution as an inescapable cosmic law, punishment as the consequence built into the fabric of the universe
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible feminine of cosmic retribution, punishment as the Great Mothers enforcement of blood-law
nodes.birthCircumstances: sometimes identified with or alongside the Erinyes

nodes.name: Holy Mother the Original Lord
nodes.domain: creation, primordial mother, Daoism, origin
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: supreme maternal deity of certain Daoist traditions
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped as the supreme mother of all existence in some Daoist sects, the feminine origin of the cosmos before the Three Pure Ones
nodes.symbolism: the feminine origin that precedes even the highest male deities, the original mother of the cosmos, the Dao in its maternal aspect
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the absolute origin, the feminine that precedes and generates all subsequent cosmic order

nodes.name: Qu Yuan
nodes.domain: poetry, patriotism, sacrifice, the Dragon Boat Festival, exile
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: aristocratic poet-statesman in flowing robes, standing at the rivers edge
nodes.significantEvent: exiled for his political views, when the Chu capital fell to Qin he drowned himself in the Miluo River on the fifth day of the fifth month, locals raced boats to try to save him and threw rice into the river to keep fish from eating his body, originating the Dragon Boat Festival (Duanwu Jie)
nodes.symbolism: the poet-patriot who dies with his country, suicide as the ultimate act of political protest, the Dragon Boat Festival as the annual commemoration of righteous despair, poetry as the vehicle of patriotic soul
nodes.neumannArchetype: the sacrificial culture hero who returns to the Great Mother (river) when the patriarchal order (Chu) is destroyed, the poets descent into the waters of the unconscious
nodes.birthCircumstances: nobleman and minister of the state of Chu during the Warring States period (c. 340-278 BCE)

nodes.name: Qetesh
nodes.domain: love, sexuality, fertility, the Near East, sacred prostitution
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: nude woman standing on a lion, holding serpents and lotus flowers, a Near Eastern goddess in the Egyptian pantheon
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped in Egypt as a goddess of sacred sexuality and pleasure, associated with both Hathor and Astarte, her image appears on numerous stelae showing her nude standing on a lion
nodes.symbolism: the nude goddess on the lion as the feminine mastery of animal power, sacred sexuality as a divine gift, the lotus and serpent as symbols of fertility and regeneration
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the mistress of sacred sexuality, the feminine that masters the animal instinct (lion) through the power of desire
nodes.birthCircumstances: Semitic goddess of sacred sexuality and fertility adopted into the Egyptian pantheon during the New Kingdom

nodes.name: Egeria
nodes.domain: fountains, prophecy, childbirth, divine counsel, nymphs
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: nymph or goddess of a sacred spring, depicted as a beautiful water spirit in a woodland grove
nodes.significantEvent: advised King Numa on the establishment of Romes religious institutions, met him secretly at night in her sacred grove, associated with the foundation of Roman religion through her divine counsel, her spring was sacred to Diana at Nemi
nodes.symbolism: the sacred spring as the source of divine wisdom, the nymphs nocturnal counsel as the unconscious advising the conscious ruler, the grove as the liminal space where divine and human meet
nodes.neumannArchetype: the anima as the divine counselor, the feminine wisdom from the spring (unconscious) that guides the patriarchal ruler in establishing sacred order
nodes.birthCircumstances: nymph of a sacred spring near Aricia, counselor to the legendary King Numa Pompilius

nodes.name: Mater Matuta
nodes.domain: dawn, the morning, childbirth, harbors, the sea, maternal care
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess of the dawn and of mothers, worshipped at the harbor town of Satricum
nodes.significantEvent: her great festival Matralia on June 11 was celebrated exclusively by free-born women in their first marriage, during which they prayed for the children of their sisters rather than their own, a unique ritual inversion
nodes.symbolism: the dawn as the daily rebirth presided over by the mother goddess, the Matralia prayer for sisters children as the communal maternal instinct, the harbor as the safe maternal enclosure from the sea
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of the dawn, the feminine that brings consciousness into the light of each new day, the maternal who extends care beyond her own children
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient Italic goddess of the dawn, identified with the Greek Eos and Leucothea

nodes.name: Pomona
nodes.domain: fruit, orchards, cultivation, grafting, autumn
nodes.characterTrait: cultivating, fruit-bearing, autumnal, patient, nurturing of gardens
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful goddess holding a pruning knife and fruit, the divine gardener of orchards
nodes.significantEvent: her sacred grove the Pomonal was on the road to Ostia, tended by her own priest (the flamen Pomonalis), the story of her wooing by Vertumnus (who changed shapes to win her love) is one of the most charming Roman myths
nodes.symbolism: the pruning knife as the cultivation of nature through careful cutting, the apple as the perfected fruit of patient cultivation, the orchard as the feminine garden of cultivated nature
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of the cultivated garden, the feminine that transforms wild nature into fruitful abundance through patient cultivation
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient Roman goddess of fruit trees and orchards, one of the few purely Roman deities with no Greek equivalent

nodes.name: Genius
nodes.domain: personal spirit, creativity, fertility, the individual soul, guiding force
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: depicted as a young man with a cornucopia making a libation, or as a serpent, the personal divine spirit of each individual
nodes.significantEvent: every Roman man had his own Genius that represented his creative and generative power, the Genius of the paterfamilias was worshipped by the household, the Genius of the emperor (Genius Augusti) became a major state cult
nodes.symbolism: the individual divine spark within each person, the serpent as the indwelling divine power, the creative spirit that makes each person unique, the birthday as the festival of ones personal Genius
nodes.neumannArchetype: the individuated masculine consciousness, the personal divine principle within each man that represents his unique creative potential
nodes.birthCircumstances: the divine spirit born with each Roman man at birth (women had a Juno)

nodes.name: Di Penates
nodes.domain: the household, the pantry, family protection, the hearth, ancestors
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: small divine figures kept in the household shrine (lararium), guardian spirits of the pantry and household stores
nodes.significantEvent: the Di Penates were the most intimate household gods, kept in the lararium alongside the Lares, offered food from every meal, the Penates of the Roman state were kept in the Temple of Vesta and represented the divine protection of Rome itself
nodes.symbolism: the divine protection of the household pantry as the most intimate form of religion, the food offering as the sharing of sustenance with the divine, the lararium as the domestic temple, the state Penates as the scaled-up household religion
nodes.neumannArchetype: the protective patriarchal spirits of the domestic center, the divine guardians of the nourishing interior of consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient Roman household deities associated with the inner sanctum of the home

nodes.name: Konohanachiru-hime
nodes.domain: falling blossoms, autumn, the scattering of flowers, death, transience
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the princess of scattering blossoms, the sister of Konohanasakuya-hime who represents the falling and death of flowers
nodes.significantEvent: while her sister represents the blooming of cherry blossoms, Konohanachiru-hime represents their falling and scattering, completing the cycle of bloom and decay
nodes.symbolism: the falling petal as the completion of beauty, autumn as the season of the scattering princess, the cycle of bloom and fall as the complete feminine of the flower, death as the necessary complement to beauty
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother in her autumnal aspect, the feminine of death and scattering that completes the cycle begun by the blooming sister
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the mountain god Ohoyamatsumi, sister of Konohanasakuya-hime

nodes.physicalCharacteristics: ancient phallic deity associated with stone pillars and fertility, worshipped in the Suwa region

nodes.symbolism: the phallic stone as the marker of sacred boundaries, the ancient fertility worship predating organized Shinto, the stone pillar as the masculine principle of territorial division
nodes.neumannArchetype: the phallic masculine of the boundary stone, the ancient patriarchal consciousness expressed through the erect stone marker

nodes.name: Indigitamenta
nodes.domain: invocations, lists of gods, ritual precision, religious law
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: sacred books listing the names and functions of all Roman gods, used by priests to ensure correct invocation
nodes.significantEvent: the official priestly books that listed every Roman deity by name and function, ensuring that each god was invoked correctly and with the proper ritual formula, the foundation of Roman religious precision
nodes.symbolism: religion as precise cataloguing and correct invocation, the divine as requiring exact naming, the books of names as the technology of Roman religious power, precision as piety
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine ordering consciousness applied to the divine, the patriarchal cataloguing of all numinous powers through naming

nodes.domain: death, mortality, the end of life, inevitability
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: personification of death, depicted as a dark figure or skeletal presence
nodes.significantEvent: personification of death in Roman religion, the inevitable end that comes for all mortals and even some gods, accepted as a natural part of the cosmic order
nodes.symbolism: death as a divine personification rather than a mere event, the inevitability of mortality as a cosmic law, death as a masculine figure (Mors) in Roman tradition
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow of mortality, the masculine principle of finality that terminates temporal consciousness

nodes.domain: new gods, imported deities, divine novelty
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: collective term for newly introduced gods in Roman religion, as opposed to the ancient native deities

nodes.symbolism: religious openness to new divine powers, the absorption of foreign gods as a feature of Roman imperialism, the distinction between old and new divine orders
nodes.neumannArchetype: the new masculine divine imported from abroad, the foreign numinous integrated into the patriarchal order

nodes.domain: shepherds, flocks, pasture, fertility, rural life
nodes.characterTrait: pastoral, fertile, nurturing of flocks, rural, spring-associated
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: pastoral deity associated with shepherds and their flocks, depicted in a pastoral setting
nodes.significantEvent: the Parilia festival on April 21 (also Romes traditional founding date) was a purification ceremony for flocks with bonfires that shepherds leaped through, one of the most ancient and beloved Roman rural festivals
nodes.symbolism: the pastoral life as sacred, the purification of flocks through fire, the founding of Rome coinciding with the shepherds festival, the rural origins of civilization
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother/Father of the pastoral life, the divine guardian of the flocks that represent the instinctual life of the community

nodes.domain: doors, hinges, thresholds, protection of doorways
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess of door hinges and the threshold, guardian of the domestic entrance

nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine guardian of the threshold, the Great Mother who controls the gate between the safe interior of consciousness and the dangerous exterior

nodes.domain: springs, prophecy, poetry, inspiration, water
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: nymphs of a sacred spring, the Roman equivalent of the Greek Muses, associated with prophecy and poetry

nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of inspiration, the feminine waters of the unconscious from which creative consciousness flows
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient Italian water nymphs associated with a sacred spring near the Porta Capena in Rome

nodes.name: Caca
nodes.domain: fire, the hearth, female virtue, Hercules, the Aventine
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a divine woman associated with the sacred fire and the founding myths of Rome
nodes.significantEvent: associated with the discovery of fire and the Aventine Hill, sometimes identified as the sister of Cacus whom Hercules defeated, she betrayed her brother to Hercules and was rewarded with a cult
nodes.symbolism: the feminine who allies with the hero against the monster (her brother), fire as the feminine gift to civilization, the betrayal of the chthonic in favor of the heroic
nodes.neumannArchetype: the anima who betrays the shadow (Cacus) and allies with the hero (Hercules), the feminine that sides with consciousness against the unconscious monster
nodes.birthCircumstances: In ancient Roman religion and myth, Caca or Cacia is the giantess sister of Cacus, the son of Vulcan who stole cattle from Hercules during the course of his western labors.

nodes.name: Dea Tacita
nodes.domain: silence, the dead, ghosts, curses, the mute goddess
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the silent goddess, a muted nymph whose tongue was cut out, associated with the dead and curses
nodes.significantEvent: associated with Ovids story of the nymph Lara whose tongue was cut out by Jupiter for revealing his secrets, she became the mother of the Lares by Mercury, her festival involved placing fish offerings on the threshold to silence evil spirits
nodes.symbolism: enforced silence as the punishment for revealing divine secrets, the muted feminine as the mother of the household spirits, the fish offering as food for the silent spirits, silence as the language of the dead
nodes.neumannArchetype: the silenced anima whose enforced muteness makes her the mother of the guardian spirits, the feminine voice suppressed by the patriarchal order that becomes the voice of the dead

nodes.name: Cura
nodes.domain: anxiety, worry, care, the human condition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: personification of care, anxiety, and worry, the divine being who shaped humanity from clay
nodes.significantEvent: in the myth preserved by Hyginus, Cura (Care) first shaped human beings from clay, Jupiter gave them spirit and Earth gave them body, Saturn decreed that Cura would possess humans throughout their lives, making anxiety the defining condition of human existence
nodes.symbolism: anxiety as the fundamental condition of being human, care as both worry and attentiveness, the clay of the body shaped by the hands of divine anxiety, the human condition as essentially anxious
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine principle of existential care that shapes and possesses consciousness throughout life, the anxiety that is inseparable from being human

nodes.name: Discordia
nodes.domain: strife, discord, conflict, the golden apple
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: personification of discord and strife, identified with the Greek Eris
nodes.significantEvent: threw the golden apple inscribed To the Fairest among the goddesses at the wedding of Peleus and Thetis, sparking the Judgment of Paris and ultimately the Trojan War
nodes.symbolism: the golden apple as the instrument of discord, the uninvited guest who destroys the feast, strife as the feminine force that sets the masculine world to war through beauty and jealousy
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow anima whose discord sets the patriarchal order to war, the destructive feminine that exploits vanity
nodes.birthCircumstances: She was the daughter of Nox (Night) and Erebus.

nodes.significantEvent: a figure connected to the establishment of divine authority in the Ise region, linked to the martial extension of the solar lineage
nodes.symbolism: the warrior prince as the martial extension of solar divine authority, Ise as the sacred territory of the sun goddess
nodes.neumannArchetype: the solar warrior-son who extends the authority of the Great Solar Mother into the terrestrial domain

nodes.name: Moriya-no-Kami
nodes.domain: Suwa, the conquered deity, the indigenous god, Moriya
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: ancient indigenous deity of the Suwa region, predating the arrival of the heavenly kami
nodes.significantEvent: the indigenous god of Suwa who was conquered by Takeminakata when the latter was driven from Izumo, represents the older layer of native worship that was subjugated by the incoming mythology but continued to be honored at Suwa Shrine
nodes.symbolism: the conquered indigenous god as the older layer of the sacred, the defeated local deity who continues to be honored, the tension between the incoming heavenly mythology and the older earth-bound worship
nodes.neumannArchetype: the chthonic Great Father of the indigenous earth, the older masculine consciousness conquered by the newer heavenly order but never fully suppressed

nodes.name: Ninigi-no-Mikoto
nodes.domain: the heavenly descent, the founding of the earthly dynasty, rice, the Three Sacred Treasures
nodes.object: the Three Sacred Treasures (mirror, sword, jewel), rice
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: grandson of Amaterasu, the divine figure who descended from heaven to earth to establish divine rule
nodes.significantEvent: descended from the High Plain of Heaven to Cape Himuka in Kyushu (the Tenson Korin or Heavenly Descent), bringing the Three Sacred Treasures and rice cultivation, married Konohanasakuya-hime and rejected Iwanaga-hime, establishing the imperial line but also human mortality
nodes.symbolism: the heavenly descent as the founding act of divine kingship, the Three Sacred Treasures as the regalia of legitimate rule, rice as the gift of heaven to earth, the choice of beauty over endurance as the origin of human mortality
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine prince who descends from the Great Solar Mother to establish patriarchal rule on earth, the masculine consciousness that brings heavenly order to the earthly realm
nodes.birthCircumstances: grandson of Amaterasu and son of Oshihomimi
nodes.domain_source: Kojiki, scroll I (the central Tenson Kōrin narrative); Nihon Shoki
nodes.object_source: Kojiki — Yata-no-Kagami (mirror), Yasakani-no-Magatama (jewel), Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi (sword) — the Three Sacred Treasures granted by Amaterasu for the descent
nodes.characterTrait_source: Kojiki — heavenly descendant, the founder of the earthly imperial dynasty
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Kojiki; iconography of the descent (the 'heavenly descendant' kōrin imagery)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Kojiki — grandson of Amaterasu (son of Oshihomimi); chosen to descend from Takamagahara (the High Plain of Heaven) to rule the earthly land; descended at Mount Takachiho in Kyūshū with the Three Sacred Treasures and a retinue of kami; met by Sarutahiko at the eight crossroads; married Konohanasakuya-hime; great-grandfather of Emperor Jimmu
nodes.eventTypes_source: Kojiki — Tenson Kōrin (the heavenly descent), the founding of the earthly imperial line
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Kojiki — son of Oshihomimi and Takuhadachiji-hime; grandson of Amaterasu
nodes.birthTypes_source: Kojiki

nodes.name: Ōyamatsumi
nodes.domain: mountains, the wilderness, hunting, marriage, the mountain father
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Great Mountain Deity, father of Konohanasakuya-hime and Iwanaga-hime, ruler of all mountains
nodes.significantEvent: offered both his daughters to Ninigi as brides, but when Ninigi rejected the ugly Iwanaga-hime and only took the beautiful Konohanasakuya-hime, he cursed human life to be as brief as cherry blossoms rather than as enduring as rock
nodes.symbolism: the mountain father whose daughters represent beauty and endurance, the curse of the mountain upon humanity for choosing beauty over longevity, mountains as the paternal principle of the landscape
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father of mountains whose two daughters represent the feminine choice between transient beauty and eternal endurance
nodes.birthCircumstances: born during the creation of the land by Izanagi and Izanami

nodes.name: Postverta
nodes.domain: seeing the past, hindsight, childbirth, prophecy
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: aspect of the goddess Carmenta who sees the past, one of the two Carmentae
nodes.significantEvent: together with Antevorta she completes the prophetic vision: Postverta sees the past while Antevorta sees the future, invoked during childbirth to know the childs ancestry and karmic inheritance
nodes.symbolism: hindsight as a divine faculty, the ability to see whence one comes as essential to knowing where one goes, the past as equally prophetic as the future
nodes.neumannArchetype: the backward-looking prophetic feminine, the anima that preserves and reads the past

nodes.name: Annona
nodes.domain: grain supply, food distribution, imperial provision, public welfare
nodes.object: grain measure, modius, cornucopia, ships prow
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman holding a grain measure (modius) and cornucopia, sometimes with a ships prow representing grain imports
nodes.significantEvent: personification of the grain supply and public food distribution in Rome, the most critical concern of the Roman state, failure to maintain Annona caused riots and overthrew emperors
nodes.symbolism: the grain supply as the foundation of political stability, food distribution as a divine feminine function, the ships prow as the importation of grain from Egypt and Africa, the modius as the measured portion
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of public nourishment, the feminine that feeds the masses and whose absence brings collapse

nodes.name: Iwasaku and Nesaku
nodes.domain: rock-splitting, creation, stone, the generation of deities from Kagutsuchis body
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: paired deities born from the blood and body of Kagutsuchi when Izanagi slew him, associated with the splitting and generation of rocks
nodes.significantEvent: when Izanagi killed Kagutsuchi with his sword, many deities sprang from the blood and body, Iwasaku and Nesaku represent the splitting and shaping of rock, the generation of stone deities from the death of fire
nodes.symbolism: the splitting of rock as a generative divine act, stone born from the death of fire, the creation of solid matter from the destruction of the volatile element
nodes.neumannArchetype: the generative pair born from the death of fire, the stone-consciousness that emerges when the volatile is destroyed
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from the blood or body of the slain fire god Kagutsuchi

nodes.name: Susanoo-no-Mikoto
nodes.domain: storms, the sea, serpents, heroism, Izumo, wildness, poetry
nodes.characterTrait: wild, impetuous, heroic, storm-associated, poetic, exile-enduring
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: powerful storm god, brother of Amaterasu, wild and impetuous deity who embodies both destruction and heroism
nodes.significantEvent: was banished from heaven for his outrages against Amaterasu (which caused her to hide in the cave), descended to Izumo Province where he slew the eight-headed serpent Yamata-no-Orochi, found the divine sword Kusanagi in its tail, married Kushinadahime, composed what is considered the first Japanese poem
nodes.symbolism: the wild storm that destroys but also cleanses, the impetuous brother who is both the cause of darkness and the slayer of the dragon, the outcast who becomes the hero, the first poet, the storm as the creative-destructive force of nature
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hero who is banished from the heavenly order and must slay the dragon of the unconscious (Orochi) in exile, the masculine that causes the withdrawal of the Great Mother (Amaterasu) but then redeems itself through the heroic act in the underworld
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from the nose of Izanagi during the purification after his visit to Yomi
nodes.domain_source: Kojiki, scroll I (his birth from Izanagi's nose, exile from heaven, slaying of Yamata-no-Orochi); Nihon Shoki
nodes.object_source: Kojiki — Totsuka-no-Tsurugi (his ten-grasp sword); Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi (the sword recovered from the tail of Yamata-no-Orochi, given to Amaterasu, now one of the Three Sacred Treasures)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Kojiki — his unruliness, weeping for his dead mother Izanami, violence in heaven (filling Amaterasu's irrigation ditches, defecating in her ritual hall, flaying a piebald horse and throwing it into her weaving-hall)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Kojiki — bearded warrior-figure with long unbound hair; the storm-kami iconography
nodes.significantEvent_source: Kojiki — born from Izanagi's nose; exiled from heaven after his violence against Amaterasu caused her cave-withdrawal; descended to Izumo and slew the eight-headed serpent Yamata-no-Orochi to rescue Kushinada-hime, whom he married; the sword Kusanagi was found in the serpent's tail
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Kojiki — born from Izanagi's nose during his post-Yomi purification
nodes.birthTypes_source: Kojiki

nodes.name: Ōkuninushi
nodes.domain: the land, nation-building, medicine, magic, marriage, Izumo
nodes.characterTrait: compassionate, wise, medicine-knowing, building, politically skilled, benevolent
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Great Land Master, ruler of the province of Izumo and the unseen world
nodes.significantEvent: rescued the White Rabbit of Inaba, endured trials set by Susanoo in the underworld, built the land of Japan with Sukunabikona, eventually ceded the land to the heavenly kami (the kuni-yuzuri or yielding of the land), given sovereignty over the unseen spiritual world in exchange
nodes.symbolism: the Great Land Master who builds the world but must surrender it to heaven, the earthly ruler who is given the invisible world, the compassion shown to the white rabbit as the nature of the benevolent king, medicine as the gift of the earthly ruler
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father of the earthly realm who builds the world but must surrender visible sovereignty to the heavenly order, retaining rule over the invisible (unconscious) realm
nodes.birthCircumstances: descendant of Susanoo, grew to become the ruler of the earthly realm
nodes.domain_source: Kojiki, scrolls I-II (the central source for the Izumo cycle); Nihon Shoki; the Izumo Fudoki
nodes.object_source: Kojiki — the bow and arrows Susanoo gave him; the koto (lute) Susanoo gave him
nodes.characterTrait_source: Kojiki — clever, persistent, suffering (tormented by his eighty brothers), kind (saving the hare of Inaba), erotically prolific (multiple wives)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Kojiki; Izumo iconography
nodes.significantEvent_source: Kojiki — son of Susanoo (or his descendant); tormented by his eighty brothers; saved the white hare of Inaba; passed Susanoo's three trials (snake-room, centipede-room, fire-arrow); eloped with Susanoo's daughter Suseribime; became 'great-land-master' of Izumo; eventually agreed to give up the earthly kingdom to Amaterasu's grandson Ninigi (the kuni-yuzuri 'transfer of the land')
nodes.eventTypes_source: Kojiki — kuni-yuzuri (transfer of the land), divine marriages, brother-tormented hero, hare-rescue
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Kojiki — descendant of Susanoo; complex genealogy
nodes.birthTypes_source: Kojiki

nodes.name: Shinatsuhiko
nodes.domain: wind, gales, air, the male wind deity
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: ancient male wind deity, the masculine kami of the wind
nodes.significantEvent: an ancient wind deity predating the more well-known Fujin, born from the divine breath of Izanagi, represents the masculine aspect of wind
nodes.symbolism: the divine breath as the origin of wind, the masculine wind as the active air, the breath of the creator-father as the source of the atmosphere
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine of the breath-wind, the air-consciousness born from the creative exhalation of the Great Father
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from the breath of Izanagi

nodes.name: Shikome
nodes.domain: the underworld (Yomi), pursuit, ugliness, the hags of death
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: ugly women of the underworld (Yomi) sent by Izanami to pursue Izanagi when he fled from her decaying form
nodes.significantEvent: when Izanagi broke his promise and looked at Izanamis rotting body in Yomi, then fled, she sent the shikome (ugly women of Yomi) to pursue him, he escaped by throwing objects behind him that transformed into obstacles
nodes.symbolism: the ugly pursuing women as the terrifying agents of the death-mother, the pursuit from the underworld as the chase of death after the living, the thrown objects becoming barriers as the magical defense against the underworld
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible feminine agents of the death-mother, the shadow-animas sent by the Great Mother of death to recapture the fleeing masculine consciousness

nodes.name: Nunakawahime
nodes.domain: jade, love, marriage, Okuninushis consort, Echigo
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful jade princess of Echigo (Niigata), consort of Okuninushi
nodes.significantEvent: Okuninushi traveled to Echigo to court Nunakawahime, they exchanged famous courtship poems, she became one of his consorts
nodes.symbolism: jade as the stone of divine beauty and love, the courtship poems as the sacred exchange of love between deities, the jade princess as the feminine of precious stone
nodes.neumannArchetype: the anima as the jade princess, the precious feminine that the hero must court through the exchange of poetic words
nodes.birthCircumstances: princess of the Echigo region, famous for its jade

nodes.domain: grain, rice, food, harvest, the spirit of grain
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the spirit of grain and food, particularly associated with rice
nodes.significantEvent: the grain spirit closely identified with the kami Inari, represents the sacred essence of rice and grain, the divine spirit within the harvest
nodes.symbolism: the grain spirit as the soul of rice, the divine essence within the staple food, the sacred nature of the harvest as the dwelling of a specific kami
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine grain-spirit, the Great Mother as the soul within the food that sustains consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: child of Susanoo or born from the food deities

nodes.domain: activity, energy, industriousness, getting things done
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: personification of energy and industriousness, the divine force that motivates action
nodes.significantEvent: invoked by Romans seeking the energy and motivation to accomplish tasks, the divine spur to action and industriousness
nodes.symbolism: energy and industriousness as divine feminine gifts, the motivation to act as coming from the divine, activity as a sacred quality
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine principle of active energy, the anima that motivates the masculine to purposeful action

nodes.name: Bubona
nodes.domain: horses, donkeys, mules, livestock, stables, protection of draft animals
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess who protected horses, donkeys, mules, and oxen in their stables
nodes.significantEvent: protected draft animals and livestock in their stables, invoked by farmers and teamsters to keep their working animals healthy and safe
nodes.symbolism: the divine care for working animals as the most practical form of rural religion, the stable as a sacred space under feminine protection
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of working animals, the feminine that protects the beasts of labor

nodes.name: Diana Nemorensis
nodes.domain: the hunt, the sacred grove, kingship, ritual murder, Nemi
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Diana in her specific aspect as the goddess of the sacred grove at Nemi, the Lady of the Wood
nodes.significantEvent: the most famous and mysterious of Dianas cults, where the Rex Nemorensis (King of the Wood) held his office by slaying his predecessor and could only be challenged by a runaway slave who broke a golden bough, the starting point of Sir James George Frazers The Golden Bough
nodes.symbolism: the sacred grove as the feminine space where masculine kingship is won through ritual violence, the golden bough as the key to the underworld, the runaway slave as the challenger of established order, the most famous example of ritual regicide in antiquity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of the sacred grove who grants sovereignty to the masculine through ritual combat, the feminine in whose space masculine power is won and lost through violence

nodes.name: Decima
nodes.domain: fate, measurement, the middle portion, the lifespan, destiny
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: one of the three Roman Fates (Parcae), who measures the thread of life
nodes.significantEvent: the Roman equivalent of Lachesis, Decima measured the thread of each persons life determining its length, the middle sister between Nona (the spinner) and Morta (the cutter)
nodes.symbolism: the measurement of the lifespan as a divine feminine act, the middle sister as the determiner of proportion, the thread of life as the fundamental metaphor of fate
nodes.neumannArchetype: the middle aspect of the Great Mother of fate, the feminine that measures the length of each consciousness

nodes.name: Nona
nodes.domain: fate, spinning, the beginning of life, birth, destiny
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: one of the three Roman Fates (Parcae), who spins the thread of life
nodes.significantEvent: the Roman equivalent of Clotho, Nona spun the thread of each persons life, her name derives from the ninth month of pregnancy (nona), linking her to the beginning of life
nodes.symbolism: the spinning of the thread of fate at birth, the ninth month as the moment of fates beginning, the spindle as the instrument that creates the thread of individual destiny
nodes.neumannArchetype: the first aspect of the Great Mother of fate, the feminine that spins the thread of each new consciousness into being

nodes.name: Juventas
nodes.domain: youth, vigor, coming of age, military service, rejuvenation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: young woman personifying youth and vitality, identified with the Greek Hebe
nodes.significantEvent: young men offered a coin to her temple when they first put on the toga virilis (the toga of manhood), marking their transition from boyhood to citizenship and military eligibility
nodes.symbolism: the divine feminine of youthful vigor, the coming-of-age as a sacred transition blessed by the goddess of youth, the coin offering as the price of entering adulthood
nodes.neumannArchetype: the anima of youth, the feminine that blesses the transition from the divine childs state to the adult masculine
nodes.birthCircumstances: parents: Jupiter and Juno

nodes.name: Juturna
nodes.domain: springs, fountains, healing waters, virginity, prophecy
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: nymph or goddess of a sacred spring, associated with healing and oracular waters
nodes.significantEvent: her sacred spring in the Roman Forum (Lacus Juturnae) was where the Dioscuri (Castor and Pollux) watered their horses after the Battle of Lake Regillus, her waters were considered healing and sacred
nodes.symbolism: the sacred spring as the place where the divine touches the earthly, healing waters as the gift of the nymph, the Forum spring as the center of civic sacrality
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of healing waters, the feminine spring at the center of civic consciousness

nodes.name: Hersilia
nodes.domain: protection, the Sabine women, peace, reconciliation, marriage
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Sabine woman who became the wife of Romulus, later deified as a goddess
nodes.significantEvent: led the Sabine women in interposing themselves between their Roman husbands and their Sabine fathers during the war following the abduction, creating peace between the two peoples, deified after death as the goddess Hora Quirini
nodes.symbolism: the feminine as the peacemaker between warring masculine groups, the abducted bride who becomes the reconciler, the woman who stands between armies to create peace
nodes.neumannArchetype: the anima who reconciles the opposing masculine forces through the power of the marriage bond and maternal love
nodes.birthCircumstances: originally a Sabine woman abducted by the Romans in the Rape of the Sabines

nodes.name: Levana
nodes.domain: lifting newborns, fatherhood, recognition of children, birth
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess who presided over the moment when the father lifted his newborn from the ground, acknowledging it as his own
nodes.significantEvent: invoked at the critical moment after birth when the Roman father lifted his child from the ground (a ritual called tollere liberos), acknowledging the child as legitimate and accepting paternal responsibility
nodes.symbolism: the lifting from the ground as the act of paternal recognition, the feminine goddess who presides over the masculine act of acceptance, the ground as the state of non-recognition from which the child is raised
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine who mediates the patriarchal act of recognition, the goddess of the threshold between birth and acceptance into the fathers lineage

nodes.name: Liberalitas
nodes.domain: generosity, imperial largesse, gift-giving, distribution
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: woman scattering coins or holding a cornucopia and tessera (distribution token), personification of generosity
nodes.significantEvent: appeared on imperial coins representing the emperors generosity in distributing money, food, and gifts to the people and soldiers, the congiarium and donativum as imperial largesse
nodes.symbolism: imperial generosity as a divine feminine quality, the distribution of wealth as a sacred act, the tessera as the token of divine largesse
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of imperial generosity, the feminine that distributes the patriarchal abundance to the people

nodes.name: Liberty
nodes.domain: freedom, political liberty, the pileus, modern symbolism
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the concept and personification of political liberty, depicted as a woman with liberty cap and broken chains
nodes.significantEvent: the Roman concept of Libertas that evolved into the modern concept of political liberty, influenced the French Revolution and the American founding, the Statue of Liberty derives from this Roman personification
nodes.symbolism: political freedom as a divine inheritance from Rome, the liberty cap as the universal symbol of emancipation, the broken chains of tyranny, the evolution from Roman goddess to modern democratic ideal
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine principle of political liberation, the anima of democratic consciousness inherited from Rome

nodes.name: Gallia
nodes.domain: Gaul, conquest, Roman provinces, national personification
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: personification of Gaul as a Roman province, typically depicted as a woman in Celtic attire or as a defeated warrior
nodes.significantEvent: appeared on Roman coins and monuments representing the conquered province of Gaul, often shown subdued or mourning, later became the basis for the French national personification Marianne
nodes.symbolism: the conquered province as a subdued feminine figure, the romanization of the Celtic world, the provincial identity as a feminine body under Roman control
nodes.neumannArchetype: the conquered feminine of the foreign territory, the vanquished Great Mother of the Celtic lands
nodes.birthCircumstances: The only evidence of her name to date is an altar set up at Vindolanda by its auxiliary garrison of the 4th cohort of Gauls, stationed there from the early 3rd century onwards.

nodes.domain: Africa, conquest, Roman provinces, wild animals, grain, exotic wealth
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: personification of Roman Africa wearing an elephant-scalp headdress, surrounded by exotic animals and grain

nodes.symbolism: Africa as the exotic feminine source of wealth and sustenance for Rome, the elephant headdress as the crown of the conquered continent, the grain supply as the maternal nourishment from across the sea

nodes.name: Britannia
nodes.domain: Britain, the Roman province, conquest, the northern frontier
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: personification of Roman Britain depicted as a seated woman with shield and trident, on rocks by the sea
nodes.significantEvent: appeared on Roman coins from Hadrian onward, personifying the island province at the edge of the known world, later became the national personification of Great Britain
nodes.symbolism: the island at the worlds edge as a seated maritime feminine figure, the shield and trident as the defense of the northern seas, the provincial personification that outlived the empire to become a national symbol
nodes.neumannArchetype: the insular Great Mother at the worlds edge, the maritime feminine of the northern frontier

nodes.name: Agdistis
nodes.domain: creation, ambiguity, self-castration, gender fluidity, Phrygia, Cybele
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: hermaphroditic deity associated with the cult of Cybele, depicted with both male and female characteristics
nodes.significantEvent: in the myth the gods feared Agdistis power and castrated the deity, from the blood an almond tree grew whose fruit impregnated Nana who bore Attis, establishing the cycle of castration and fertility central to the Cybele cult
nodes.symbolism: gender ambiguity as a primordial divine state, the castration that generates new life, the fear of the gods before the power of the undifferentiated, the almond as the fruit of self-mutilation that produces the beloved (Attis)
nodes.neumannArchetype: the uroboric primordial being that must be castrated for differentiated consciousness to emerge, the terrible hermaphroditic Great Parent whose power must be reduced
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from the earth or from a stone in Phrygian myth, an ambiguous primordial being

nodes.name: Invidia
nodes.domain: envy, jealousy, malice, the evil eye
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: emaciated woman eating her own heart, surrounded by serpents, the personification of destructive envy

nodes.symbolism: envy as self-consumption, the gnawing heart of jealousy that destroys from within, the serpents of malice that accompany the envious soul, the dark cave of the envious mind
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow anima of envy, the feminine that consumes itself through jealousy of others

nodes.name: Lucina
nodes.domain: childbirth, light, bringing to light, the first breath
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: aspect of Juno (Juno Lucina) who presided over childbirth and brought children into the light of day
nodes.significantEvent: the most important divine figure in Roman childbirth, mothers called upon Juno Lucina at the moment of delivery, her temple on the Esquiline was where offerings were made for successful births, knots had to be untied in her presence to ensure easy delivery
nodes.symbolism: birth as bringing into the light, the untying of knots as the removal of obstacles to birth, the torch as the light that welcomes the newborn into the world, the first breath as the gift of the light-bringing goddess
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of birth who brings consciousness into the light of the world, the feminine that illuminates the newborn awareness

nodes.name: Moneta
nodes.domain: money, coins, minting, warning, memory, the mint
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: aspect of Juno (Juno Moneta) associated with the Roman mint, depicted with coin-making implements

nodes.symbolism: the divine feminine as the source of money, the mint as a temple, the warning geese as divine vigilance, the etymology of money from the goddess name
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the source of economic value, the feminine that produces the symbolic tokens of exchange (money)
nodes.birthCircumstances: She is mentioned in a fragment of Livius Andronicus' Latin Odyssey: Nam diva Monetas filia docuit ("since the divine daughter of Moneta has taught.

nodes.domain: volcanic gases, sulfur, malaria, disease prevention, purification
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess of noxious vapors and sulfurous gases, both feared and propitiated

nodes.symbolism: the noxious vapor as a divine power that must be appeased, the volcano as the source of both danger and purification, sulfur as both poison and cleanser
nodes.neumannArchetype: the chthonic Great Mother of volcanic emissions, the feminine of the earths dangerous depths
nodes.birthCircumstances: For instance, the 5th-century author Servius the Grammarian claims that any "foul scent is thought to properly belong to Mefitis," who he claims was "born from sulfur water.

nodes.name: Maia
nodes.domain: growth, spring, the earth, May, motherhood, warmth
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: ancient goddess of growth and spring warmth, associated with the month of May
nodes.significantEvent: the month of May was named after her, offerings were made to her on May 1 by the flamen Volcanalis (priest of Vulcan), associated with the warmth that makes plants grow
nodes.symbolism: the month of May as the month of growth and the Great Mother, spring warmth as a divine feminine gift, the growth of vegetation as the feminine principle of nature
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of spring growth, the feminine warmth that makes consciousness blossom
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient Italic goddess, later identified with the Greek nymph Maia (mother of Hermes)
nodes.deathCircumstances: Annually, a pregnant sow was sacrificed to the goddess by one of Vulcan's flamens, a sacrifice Macrobius claimed was suitable for an earth goddess.

nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible Great Mother of infant death, the feminine of the threshold where birth becomes death

nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of the city, the feminine fortune that protects and sustains the urban center of civilization

nodes.characterTrait: radiant, sovereign, life-giving, dignified, commanding, merciful
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: radiant sun goddess, the supreme deity of the Shinto pantheon, too brilliant to look upon directly
nodes.significantEvent: withdrew into the cave Ama-no-Iwato after being offended by her brother Susanoo, plunging the world into darkness, lured out by the comic dance of Ame-no-Uzume and the mirror, sent her grandson Ninigi to rule the earth with the Three Sacred Treasures, ancestress of the Japanese imperial line
nodes.symbolism: the sun as the supreme divine feminine, the mirror as self-recognition and truth, the cave as the withdrawal of consciousness, the Three Sacred Treasures as the legitimacy of divine rule, rice cultivation as the gift of the sun goddess
nodes.neumannArchetype: the supreme Great Mother as the sun herself, the solar feminine whose withdrawal into the cave represents the descent of consciousness into the unconscious, and whose return brings light and order back to the world
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from the left eye of Izanagi as he purified himself after visiting the land of the dead (Yomi)
nodes.domain_source: Kojiki, scroll I (her birth from Izanagi's left eye); the Amano-Iwato narrative; the descent of Ninigi; the Ise Grand Shrine traditions; Nihon Shoki
nodes.object_source: Kojiki — the Yata-no-Kagami (mirror), Magatama-no-Tama (jewel), Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi (sword) constitute the Three Sacred Treasures of imperial regalia, traced to Amaterasu
nodes.significantEvent_source: Kojiki (the Amano-Iwato cave-of-heaven episode, the descent of Ninigi, the granting of the Three Sacred Treasures); Nihon Shoki
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Kojiki — born from Izanagi's left eye during his purification after Yomi
nodes.characterTrait_source: Kojiki (her grief at Susanoo's violence, withdrawal to the cave); Nihon Shoki
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Kojiki; Nihon Shoki; standard iconography (the sun goddess, sometimes depicted with the mirror)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Kojiki

nodes.name: Izanagi-no-Mikoto
nodes.domain: creation, purification, the masculine principle, sky, the living
nodes.object: naginata (jeweled spear of heaven), purification water
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: male creator deity, progenitor of the Japanese islands and many kami
nodes.significantEvent: together with Izanami stirred the primordial ocean with the Spear of Heaven to create the first island (Onogoro), fathered the Japanese islands and numerous kami, after Izanamis death descended to Yomi to retrieve her but fled in horror at her decayed form, performed the first purification ritual (misogi) creating Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi, and Susanoo
nodes.symbolism: the spear stirring the ocean as the masculine creative act, the descent to Yomi as the masculine encounter with death, the purification as the masculine response to pollution, creation through the union and separation of the masculine and feminine principles
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father who creates through union with the Great Mother but must separate from her after encountering death, the masculine that generates the supreme kami through purification after contact with the underworld
nodes.birthCircumstances: appeared at the beginning of creation as one of the first individual deities
nodes.domain_source: Kojiki, scroll I (the central source for the creation-and-Yomi narrative); Nihon Shoki; Engishiki
nodes.object_source: Kojiki — Ame-no-Nuboko (heavenly jeweled spear); Totsuka-no-Tsurugi (sword used to kill Kagutsuchi)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Kojiki (his role in creation, descent to Yomi, purification)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Kojiki; standard iconographic depictions of the male creator-kami
nodes.significantEvent_source: Kojiki — together with Izanami stirred the cosmic ocean with Ame-no-Nuboko to create the islands of Japan; fathered numerous kami; descended to Yomi to recover Izanami; fled when he saw her decayed form; performed purifying ablutions in the Tachibana river from which Amaterasu (left eye), Tsukuyomi (right eye), and Susanoo (nose) were born
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Kojiki — the seventh generation of primordial kami
nodes.birthTypes_source: Kojiki

nodes.name: Izanami-no-Mikoto
nodes.domain: creation, death, the underworld (Yomi), the feminine principle, earth
nodes.characterTrait: creative, dying, decaying, wrathful in death, maternal
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: female creator deity who became the goddess of death, described as rotting and maggot-ridden in Yomi
nodes.significantEvent: together with Izanagi created the Japanese islands and numerous kami, died giving birth to the fire god Kagutsuchi, descended to Yomi (the land of the dead) where she rotted and became a terrifying death goddess, when Izanagi fled she vowed to kill 1,000 people daily while he vowed to give life to 1,500
nodes.symbolism: the feminine creator who becomes the death goddess through the act of giving birth, the passage from life-giver to death-dealer, the rotting body in Yomi as the reality of death that the masculine cannot face, the daily exchange of death and birth between the divorced cosmic parents
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother in her complete cycle from creator to destroyer, the feminine that gives birth and then becomes death itself, the terrible mother in Yomi whose decomposing body is the reality from which masculine consciousness flees
nodes.birthCircumstances: appeared at the beginning of creation as the feminine counterpart of Izanagi
nodes.domain_source: Kojiki, scroll I; Nihon Shoki
nodes.object_source: Kojiki — Ame-no-Nuboko (shared with Izanagi); the peaches of Yomi (which Izanagi threw to escape her pursuing Shikome)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Kojiki — her role in creation, death by Kagutsuchi-burning, transformation into Yomi-queen
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Kojiki — depicted as the female creator; in the Yomi episode, her decayed corpse-form is described in detail (maggot-ridden, with the eight thunder-gods emerging from her body)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Kojiki — co-created the islands of Japan with Izanagi; died giving birth to Kagutsuchi (the fire-kami who burned her); became queen of Yomi; cursed Izanagi to kill 1,000 humans daily; Izanagi countered with 1,500 daily births — establishing the cosmic birth-death balance
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Kojiki — the seventh generation of primordial kami
nodes.birthTypes_source: Kojiki
nodes.deathTypes_source: Kojiki — burned to death by giving birth to Kagutsuchi
nodes.deathCircumstances_source: Kojiki — death from Kagutsuchi's fire during childbirth; descent to Yomi as its queen

nodes.name: Kami
nodes.domain: divine spirits, nature, sacred power, all phenomena
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the fundamental concept of divine or sacred beings in Shinto, not a single deity but the term for all divine spirits, which number in the millions
nodes.significantEvent: the concept of yaoyorozu no kami (eight million kami) expresses the Shinto belief that divinity pervades all natural phenomena, from great deities to the spirit in each tree, rock, river, and mountain
nodes.symbolism: divinity as pervading all nature rather than transcending it, the sacred as immanent in every phenomenon, the eight million as a number of infinite divine presence, the unity of the natural and the divine
nodes.neumannArchetype: the collective numinous that pervades all of nature, the divine as immanent in every aspect of the world rather than transcendent above it
nodes.birthCircumstances: kami exist throughout all of nature and the cosmos, present since creation

nodes.name: Ame-no-Uzume
nodes.domain: dawn, merriment, dance, revelry, the arts, fertility
nodes.characterTrait: merry, bold, erotic, comic, shamanic, dancing
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful goddess of dawn and merriment, known for her ecstatic and ribald dancing
nodes.significantEvent: performed a lewd and comic dance on an overturned tub outside Amaterasus cave, exposing her body and making the assembled gods roar with laughter, the laughter and light from the mirror lured Amaterasu out of her cave and restored light to the world
nodes.symbolism: the erotic comic dance as the force that restores the light, laughter as the power that overcomes divine withdrawal, the exposed body as the bold assertion of life against the darkness, the feminine that uses sexuality and humor to save the world
nodes.neumannArchetype: the anima as the sacred dancer whose erotic comedy draws the Great Mother (Amaterasu) out of the unconscious (cave), the feminine that uses the body and laughter to restore solar consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the heavenly kami, the divine entertainer
nodes.domain_source: Kojiki, scroll I (the central Amano-Iwato narrative); Nihon Shoki
nodes.object_source: Kojiki — the bamboo grass, the upturned wooden tub on which she danced, the sasaki-tree branches
nodes.characterTrait_source: Kojiki — bold, ecstatic-dancing, mirth-evoking, sexually-frank (her dance is described as exposing herself)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Kojiki; iconography of the dancing kami
nodes.significantEvent_source: Kojiki — danced ecstatically and bawdily on an upturned wooden tub outside the Amano-Iwato cave, exposing herself; the assembled kami roared with laughter; Amaterasu, curious, peeked out; the strong-armed kami grabbed her and the sun was restored. Later wedded Sarutahiko at the crossroads encounter during Ninigi's descent
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Kojiki — heavenly kami
nodes.birthTypes_source: Kojiki

nodes.name: Kagutsuchi
nodes.domain: fire, volcanoes, destruction, smithing, death
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the fire god, born as a blazing infant whose flames consumed his mother
nodes.significantEvent: his birth killed Izanami, triggering Izanagis grief and rage, Izanagi beheaded him with his sword and from Kagutsuchis blood and body sprang numerous other kami, his death created an entire generation of gods
nodes.symbolism: fire as the element whose birth kills the mother, the creative-destructive paradox of flame, the slain fire god whose blood and body generate new deities, the first death as caused by the birth of fire, fire as both the creator and destroyer of civilization
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible divine child whose birth kills the Great Mother, the fire of consciousness that destroys the primordial feminine, the masculine element that must be slain by the father to generate the differentiated world
nodes.birthCircumstances: born to Izanami, his birth-fire burned and killed her, causing the first death in the world
nodes.domain_source: Kojiki, scroll I; Nihon Shoki
nodes.object_source: Kojiki — his own fiery body (the means of his mother Izanami's death)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Kojiki — fire-kami; cause of his mother's death
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Kojiki — fire-deity
nodes.significantEvent_source: Kojiki — born from Izanami, burned her to death in childbirth; Izanagi in grief beheaded him with the sword Ame-no-Ohabari; from his blood and dismembered body sprang many further kami (the mountain kami, valley kami, sword-making kami)
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Kojiki — son of Izanagi and Izanami; cause of her death
nodes.birthTypes_source: Kojiki
nodes.deathTypes_source: Kojiki — beheaded by Izanagi with Ame-no-Ohabari
nodes.deathCircumstances_source: Kojiki — beheaded by Izanagi; further kami emerged from his blood and body

nodes.name: Chalchiuhtlatonal
nodes.domain: jade, water, divination, the calendar, precious green
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Jade of the Sun or Jade Radiance, associated with jade, water, and the calendar
nodes.significantEvent: a calendrical deity associated with the tonalpohualli (the 260-day ritual calendar), connected to divination and the precious jade stone
nodes.symbolism: jade as solidified water and the most precious substance, the calendar as the jade-like structure of time, divination through the sacred calendar as reading the jade of fate
nodes.neumannArchetype: the crystallized consciousness of the calendar, the jade-like order of sacred time

nodes.name: Hachiman
nodes.domain: war, archery, fishing, agriculture, divine protection, the imperial family
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: syncretic war god combining Shinto and Buddhist elements, the divine protector of Japan
nodes.significantEvent: one of the most widely worshipped kami in Japan with approximately 25,000 shrines, patron of the samurai class, his cult at Usa Hachiman-gu was one of the most powerful in Japan, the Minamoto clan made him their clan deity
nodes.symbolism: the deified emperor as the divine protector of the nation, the dove as the messenger of the war god (unusually peaceful for a war deity), the syncretic union of Shinto and Buddhist warrior traditions
nodes.neumannArchetype: the deified Great Father of war, the historical patriarch (Emperor Ojin) elevated to the status of the divine protector of national consciousness
nodes.domain_source: Engishiki; Usa Jingū and Iwashimizu Hachimangū traditions; the Hachiman shrine network (~25,000 shrines, second most-numerous after Inari)
nodes.object_source: Hachiman iconography — bow and arrows; the white dove as messenger
nodes.characterTrait_source: Standard Hachiman tradition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Hachiman iconography — war-kami; sometimes depicted as the deified Emperor Ōjin (15th legendary emperor); sometimes as a Buddhist bodhisattva (Hachiman Daibosatsu)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Hachiman is identified with the deified Emperor Ōjin (legendary 15th emperor, son of Empress Jingū). Patron of warriors and the Minamoto clan; the Iwashimizu Hachimangū at Kyoto became one of the most important war-shrines in medieval Japan

nodes.name: Benzaiten
nodes.domain: water, music, eloquence, wealth, knowledge, Buddhism
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful woman playing a biwa (Japanese lute), often depicted on a dragon or surrounded by water, one of the Seven Lucky Gods (Shichifukujin)
nodes.significantEvent: one of the Seven Lucky Gods and the only female among them, worshipped at Enoshima shrine and many others, patroness of musicians, writers, and artists, associated with rivers, lakes, and the sea
nodes.symbolism: the biwa as the instrument of divine eloquence, water as the element of flowing creativity, the serpent as the chthonic power of water-wisdom, the only feminine among the Seven Lucky Gods as the essential feminine dimension of prosperity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of creative waters, the feminine of eloquence and music whose flowing consciousness nourishes all artistic and intellectual endeavor
nodes.birthCircumstances: identified with the Hindu-Buddhist goddess Saraswati, adopted into Japanese religion

nodes.name: Konohanasakuya-hime
nodes.domain: cherry blossoms, Mount Fuji, volcanoes, beauty, transience, childbirth
nodes.object: cherry blossoms, the summit of Mount Fuji
nodes.characterTrait: beautiful, transient, volcanic, blooming, protective of birth
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: supremely beautiful goddess, the personification of cherry blossom beauty and the explosive power of volcanoes
nodes.significantEvent: Ninigi chose to marry her instead of her ugly sister Iwanaga-hime (Rock-Long Princess), which is why humans have beautiful but short lives rather than long and enduring ones, she is the goddess of Mount Fuji and all Japanese volcanoes
nodes.symbolism: the cherry blossom as the supreme symbol of transient beauty, Mount Fuji as the beautiful volcano, the choice of beauty over longevity as the human condition, the flower that blooms brilliantly and falls quickly as the model of human life
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother in her beautiful but transient aspect, the feminine of blooming beauty whose choice over the enduring sister determines the brevity and beauty of human consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the mountain god Ohoyamatsumi, wife of Ninigi (grandson of Amaterasu)
nodes.domain_source: Kojiki, scroll I; Nihon Shoki; Mount Fuji shrine traditions (especially Fujisan Hongū Sengen Taisha)
nodes.object_source: Kojiki — cherry blossoms (her name 木花咲耶姫 = 'tree-flower-blooming-princess'); Mount Fuji (the volcano she presides over)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Kojiki — beautiful, brief-lived (like the cherry blossom), proud, demonstrating fidelity by giving birth in a burning hut
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Kojiki — beautiful young woman; Mount Fuji iconography
nodes.significantEvent_source: Kojiki — daughter of Ōyamatsumi (mountain-kami); chosen by Ninigi as bride, rejecting her elder sister Iwanaga-hime ('long-rock'), which led Ōyamatsumi to curse Ninigi's descendants with mortality (had he accepted Iwanaga his line would have endured like rock; choosing Konohanasakuya, life would be brief like blossoms); proved her fidelity by giving birth to Hoderi, Hosuseri, and Hoori in a burning hut
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Kojiki — daughter of Ōyamatsumi
nodes.birthTypes_source: Kojiki

nodes.name: Fūjin
nodes.domain: wind, storms, air, the sky
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: fearsome deity carrying a large bag from which he releases the winds, often depicted with wild hair blown by gales, terrifying visage
nodes.significantEvent: carries a bag of winds on his shoulders and releases them to create storms and breezes, paired with Raijin (thunder god) as one of the great elemental kami, depicted on the famous Wind and Thunder screens at Kennin-ji temple
nodes.symbolism: the bag of winds as the contained power of the atmosphere, the wild-haired storm god as the untamed air, wind as both destructive and life-giving, the paired wind-thunder deities as the complementary forces of the storm
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine of the uncontrolled atmosphere, the wild wind-consciousness that cannot be tamed
nodes.birthCircumstances: born during the creation of the world, the kami of wind

nodes.name: Kitsune
nodes.domain: foxes, shapeshifting, trickery, guardianship, Inari, magic
nodes.characterTrait: cunning, shapeshifting, loyal, magical, trickster, intelligent
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: supernatural fox spirit that can take human form, often depicted as a white fox, grows additional tails with age and power (up to nine)
nodes.significantEvent: kitsune can be benevolent guardians or malicious tricksters, they serve as messengers of Inari at shrines throughout Japan, a nine-tailed kitsune is the most powerful, they can seduce humans by taking the form of beautiful women
nodes.symbolism: the fox as the shapeshifter between animal and human, the nine tails as the accumulation of supernatural power, the white fox as the divine messenger, the fox-woman as the supernatural seductress, the boundary between the wild and the civilized
nodes.neumannArchetype: the trickster-anima in animal form, the shapeshifting feminine that crosses the boundary between nature and human consciousness, the fox as the cunning aspect of the unconscious
nodes.birthCircumstances: fox spirits who serve the kami Inari, or independent supernatural beings

nodes.name: Nibhaz
nodes.domain: A deity of the Avvites (resettled in Samaria, 8th c. BCE). Possibly canine-formed in late rabbinic gloss.
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a deity worshipped by the Avvites, possibly associated with dogs or barking
nodes.significantEvent: mentioned in 2 Kings 17:31 as a deity worshipped by the Avvites settled in Samaria, sometimes depicted as a dog-headed figure
nodes.symbolism: the barking god as the canine divine, the mysterious deity of the displaced Avvite people
nodes.neumannArchetype: the animal-god of the foreign settlers, the canine consciousness of the displaced people
nodes.domain_source: 2 Kings 17:31 (the only canonical attestation: 'the Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak'); Babylonian Talmud b. Sanhedrin 63b (folk-etymology dog-form, possibly from Hebrew nbḥ 'to bark'). NOTE: name does not appear in any extant Mesopotamian or Aramaic primary source; existence as a real cult figure is contested.
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: b. Sanhedrin 63b
nodes.animals_source: b. Sanhedrin 63b (folk-etymology dog-form)
nodes.characterTrait_source: 2 Kings 17:31; b. Sanhedrin 63b (the late rabbinic gloss giving canine-form)
nodes.significantEvent_source: 2 Kings 17:31 (the only canonical primary attestation)

nodes.name: Amatsukami
nodes.domain: the heavenly kami, the high plain of heaven, celestial order
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the collective kami of heaven (Takama-ga-hara), the celestial deities as opposed to the earthly kami (Kunitsukami)
nodes.significantEvent: the celestial kami who dwell in the High Plain of Heaven, they sent Ninigi to earth to establish divine rule, they represent the cosmic order and heavenly authority
nodes.symbolism: the heavenly realm as the source of divine authority, the celestial kami as the upper cosmic order, the High Plain of Heaven as the divine counterpart to the earthly realm
nodes.neumannArchetype: the collective patriarchal consciousness of heaven, the celestial masculine order from which earthly authority descends

nodes.name: Kotoamatsukami
nodes.domain: the primordial heavenly kami, the first five, cosmic beginnings
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the five primordial heavenly kami who appeared at the very beginning of creation, all hitorigami (solitary deities) who immediately hid
nodes.significantEvent: the five kami who appeared at the beginning of creation: Ame-no-Minakanushi, Takamimusubi, Kamimusubi, Umashiashikabihikoji, and Ame-no-Tokotachi, they all immediately concealed themselves after appearing
nodes.symbolism: the five primordial cosmic principles that precede all creation, the immediate concealment as the mystery of the divine origin, the solitary nature of the first beings as the pre-relational state of existence
nodes.neumannArchetype: the five primordial consciousnesses that emerge from the void and immediately return to concealment, the first differentiations of awareness from the undifferentiated
nodes.birthCircumstances: the first five kami to come into being in the universe, preceding all other creation
nodes.deathCircumstances: Kamimusubi is also said to have transformed the grains produced by the food goddess Ōgetsuhime (Ukemochi no kami) after she was slain by Susanoo.

nodes.name: Hitorigami
nodes.domain: solitary creation, primordial kami, self-generation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the solitary kami (hitorigami) who appeared alone without a partner and immediately hid
nodes.significantEvent: the hitorigami are the primordial kami who came into being without sexual pairing, they represent the initial stage of creation before the masculine-feminine pairing of Izanagi and Izanami
nodes.symbolism: the solitary god as the pre-gendered state of divine existence, the hiding as the mystery of the self-generated, creation without partnership as the most primordial form of divine manifestation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the uroboric consciousness before the differentiation into masculine and feminine, the self-creating divine that precedes the hieros gamos
nodes.birthCircumstances: Most are said to have been created from the "male essence" and, as such, are male in gender.

nodes.name: Iwanaga-hime
nodes.domain: rock, endurance, longevity, ugliness, immortality rejected
nodes.characterTrait: enduring, rocky, ugly, immortal, rejected, eternal
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Rock-Long Princess, daughter of the mountain god Ohoyamatsumi, the ugly sister of Konohanasakuya-hime
nodes.significantEvent: offered together with her beautiful sister to Ninigi as brides, but Ninigi rejected her because of her ugliness and only married the beautiful Konohanasakuya-hime, the mountain god cursed humans to have short lives like cherry blossoms instead of long lives like rock because of Ninigis rejection
nodes.symbolism: the rock princess as the endurance rejected in favor of beauty, the choice of transient beauty over eternal ugliness as the defining human choice, the curse of short human life as the consequence of rejecting endurance
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible Great Mother of endurance rejected by the hero who prefers the beautiful transient feminine, the stone-mother whose rejection determines human mortality
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the mountain god, sister of Konohanasakuya-hime (Blossom Princess)

nodes.name: Hoderi
nodes.domain: sea, fishing, the Hyuga cycle, jealousy, the elder brother
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the elder brother, known as Sea-Wisdom (Hoderi), son of Ninigi and Konohanasakuya-hime
nodes.significantEvent: exchanged his fishhook for his younger brother Hooris bow, but when Hoori lost the fishhook Hoderi demanded it back, Hoori descended to the sea palace to retrieve it and returned with power over the tides, eventually subjugating Hoderi, ancestor of the Hayato people
nodes.symbolism: the elder brother subjugated by the younger as the mythic pattern of succession, the lost fishhook as the catalyst for the descent to the sea palace, the sea as the realm from which power is retrieved
nodes.neumannArchetype: the elder shadow-brother who is overcome by the younger hero, the masculine who loses sovereignty to his junior through the heros descent to the deep
nodes.birthCircumstances: elder son of Ninigi and Konohanasakuya-hime, born in fire
nodes.domain_source: Kojiki, scroll II (the Yamasachi-Umisachi narrative); Nihon Shoki
nodes.object_source: Kojiki — his fishhook
nodes.characterTrait_source: Kojiki — elder brother, jealous, the sea-fisherman who would not forgive Hoori's loss of the fishhook
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Kojiki
nodes.significantEvent_source: Kojiki — exchanged his fishhook with Hoori (the bow); when Hoori lost it, demanded its return; received it eventually with Watatsumi's tide-jewels working against him; subjugated by Hoori; became the ancestor of the Hayato people (the subjugated southern peoples)
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Kojiki — son of Ninigi and Konohanasakuya-hime
nodes.birthTypes_source: Kojiki

nodes.name: Ajisukitakahikone-no-Kami
nodes.domain: thunder, agriculture, the storm, Izumo
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: powerful thunder deity associated with Izumo Province
nodes.significantEvent: associated with thunder and agricultural fertility, attended the funeral of Amenowakahiko and was mistaken for the dead god, kicked the funeral hut away in anger
nodes.symbolism: thunder as the voice of the kami of storms, the agricultural power of lightning, the fierce divinity of the Izumo region
nodes.neumannArchetype: the son of the Great Father (Okuninushi) who wields thunder, the masculine of elemental storm power
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Okuninushi, the great land deity of Izumo
