nodes.domain: swords, the killing of Kagutsuchi, fire-cutting, the heavenly blade
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a divine sword used by Izanagi to behead the fire god Kagutsuchi
nodes.significantEvent: the sword Izanagi used to behead his son Kagutsuchi in grief and rage after the fire gods birth killed Izanami, from the blood and body of Kagutsuchi sprang numerous new kami
nodes.symbolism: the sword that kills the son to avenge the mother, the blade as the instrument of paternal wrath, the divine weapon that generates new deities through destruction
nodes.neumannArchetype: the patriarchal weapon that slays the terrible son (fire) to avenge the Great Mother, the cutting instrument that differentiates through violence

nodes.domain: the sun, ancestry, the Owari and Mononobe clans, heaven
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: heavenly kami associated with the sun, sometimes identified as a son or aspect of Amaterasu
nodes.significantEvent: descended from heaven and became the ancestor of several powerful Japanese clans, his mythology connects the imperial solar line to the warrior and administrative clans
nodes.symbolism: the solar descent that founds noble lineages, the extension of heavenly authority through multiple bloodlines
nodes.neumannArchetype: the solar son who descends to establish earthly lineages, the masculine heir of the Great Solar Mother
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Amaterasu in some lineages, ancestor of the Owari and Mononobe clans

nodes.physicalCharacteristics: powerful warrior kami, wielder of divine swords
nodes.significantEvent: sent by the heavenly kami together with Takemikazuchi to subjugate the earthly kami and pacify the land before Ninigis descent, a divine warrior who cleared the path for heavenly rule on earth
nodes.symbolism: the divine sword as the instrument of heavenly authority, the warrior-kami who clears the path for divine rule, the martial aspect of celestial sovereignty
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine warrior of heaven who defeats the earthly powers to establish the dominion of celestial consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: a kami born from the blood of Kagutsuchi or from divine weapons

nodes.symbolism: the mountain as the guardian against fire, the syncretic fusion of Shinto and Buddhist fire-prevention, the mountain ascetic tradition as the path to mastering elemental forces
nodes.neumannArchetype: the mountain father who masters fire, the ascetic masculine consciousness that controls the destructive element through discipline

nodes.name: Kodama
nodes.domain: trees, forests, tree spirits, nature, echoes
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: tree spirits that dwell within old trees, invisible to most but audible as echoes or rustling sounds in ancient forests
nodes.significantEvent: kodama are the spirits inhabiting old trees, particularly ancient forests, felling a tree with a kodama was considered dangerous and could bring a curse, the echo heard in forests was believed to be the voice of the kodama
nodes.symbolism: the tree as a vessel for divine spirit, the echo as the voice of the tree-soul, the ancient forest as the dwelling of countless spiritual presences, the sacred prohibition against felling old trees
nodes.neumannArchetype: the numinous of the forest, the tree-consciousness that speaks through echoes, the vegetative unconscious that inhabits the ancient growth

nodes.domain: the Hyuga descent, Ninigis brothers, warfare, sacrifice
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: eldest brother in the group sent to establish divine rule on earth
nodes.significantEvent: died in battle during the descent and conquest of the earthly realm, his death was one of the sacrifices necessary for the establishment of divine rule on earth
nodes.symbolism: the elder brother who falls so that the younger may establish the kingdom, the sacrifice necessary for the founding of divine rule, the warrior who dies in the process of cosmic conquest
nodes.neumannArchetype: the elder brother-shadow who is sacrificed so that the hero (younger brother) may succeed, the masculine that dies for the establishment of royal consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: elder brother of Jinmu and other princes

nodes.name: Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto
nodes.domain: the moon, night, food taboo, the calendar, the tides
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the moon god, counterpart to Amaterasu (sun) and Susanoo (storm)
nodes.significantEvent: killed the food goddess Ukemochi for the manner in which she produced food (from her body), Amaterasu was so disgusted by this act that she refused to ever face Tsukuyomi again, which is why the sun and moon are never seen together in the sky
nodes.symbolism: the moon as the cold killer who cannot tolerate the earthy origins of food, the separation of sun and moon as the consequence of violence against the food goddess, the night as the domain of the violent and isolated
nodes.neumannArchetype: the lunar masculine who kills the food-mother, the cold consciousness of the night that separates itself from the solar feminine through violence
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from the right eye of Izanagi during the purification after visiting Yomi
nodes.domain_source: Kojiki, scroll I; Nihon Shoki (which preserves the more developed Tsukuyomi-Ukemochi narrative)
nodes.object_source: Kojiki — no specific objects; iconography minimal
nodes.characterTrait_source: Nihon Shoki — slew Ukemochi for her food-from-the-body production, prompting Amaterasu's anger and the day-night separation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Kojiki; Nihon Shoki — sparse iconographic tradition compared to Amaterasu and Susanoo
nodes.significantEvent_source: Nihon Shoki — Amaterasu sent Tsukuyomi to attend Ukemochi's feast; Tsukuyomi, disgusted by her producing food from her body (mouth, nose, anus), killed her; Amaterasu was so angered that she refused ever to face him again, establishing the eternal separation of day and night
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Kojiki — born from Izanagi's right eye during his post-Yomi purification
nodes.birthTypes_source: Kojiki

nodes.name: Raijin
nodes.domain: thunder, lightning, rain, storms, drums
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: fearsome thunder god, depicted with a ring of drums which he beats to create thunder, often shown with a terrifying face
nodes.significantEvent: the thunder kami paired with Fujin (wind god), together they represent the elemental forces of the storm, famously depicted on the Wind and Thunder screens at Kennin-ji temple
nodes.symbolism: the drums as the instruments of thunder, the ring of drums as the circular nature of the storm, the thunder as the voice of the divine wrath, the paired wind-thunder deities as the complementary forces of the tempest
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine of thunder who beats the cosmic drums, the elemental consciousness that speaks through the storm
nodes.domain_source: Standard Shintō tradition; Kojiki (the eight thunder-kami who emerged from Izanami's decaying body in Yomi); Nihon Shoki
nodes.object_source: Raijin iconography — circle of drums (the source of thunder) around his back; mallet to strike them
nodes.characterTrait_source: Standard Raijin tradition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Raijin iconography — fierce demonic appearance with horns, claws, and a circle of taiko drums surrounding him; often depicted as Fūjin's counterpart in temple guardian-statue pairs (e.g., the Fūjin-Raijin paintings of Tawaraya Sōtatsu, 17th c.)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Standard Shintō tradition; Kojiki
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Kojiki — one of the eight thunder-kami from Izanami's body
nodes.birthTypes_source: Kojiki

nodes.name: Ryūjin
nodes.domain: the sea, dragons, the underwater palace, tides, weather
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Dragon King of the Sea, ruler of the underwater palace Ryugu-jo, a great dragon or dragon-shaped being
nodes.significantEvent: rules the sea from his underwater palace Ryugu-jo where Hoori descended to retrieve the lost fishhook, father of Toyotama-hime (who married Hoori), controls the tides with the tide jewels
nodes.symbolism: the dragon as the lord of the oceanic depths, the underwater palace as the treasure-house of the sea, the tide jewels as mastery over the waters, the marriage alliance between land and sea
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father of the oceanic unconscious, the dragon-consciousness of the depths who guards the treasure (tide jewels) that the hero must retrieve

nodes.name: Sarutahiko Ōkami
nodes.domain: crossroads, guidance, earthly kami, the phallus, travel, martial arts
nodes.characterTrait: guiding, earthly, phallic, large-nosed, martial, territorial
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a towering earthly kami with a very long nose and red face, standing at the crossroads between heaven and earth
nodes.significantEvent: the chief of the earthly kami (kunitsukami) who greeted Ninigi at the crossroads when the heavenly grandson descended to earth, guided the heavenly procession to its destination, married Ame-no-Uzume
nodes.symbolism: the crossroads guide as the earthly kami who meets heaven, the long nose as a phallic symbol, the red face as the mark of power, the marriage of the earthly guide and the heavenly dancer as the union of earth and heaven
nodes.neumannArchetype: the phallic Great Father of the earthly crossroads, the masculine earth-consciousness that guides the descending heavenly order to its proper place
nodes.birthCircumstances: In the Nihon Shoki, he is the one who meets Ninigi-no-Mikoto, the grandson of Amaterasu, the Sun goddess, when he descends from Takama-ga-hara.
nodes.domain_source: Kojiki, scroll I; Nihon Shoki; the Sarutahiko Jinja traditions
nodes.object_source: Kojiki — described in distinctive physical terms but no specific iconographic objects
nodes.characterTrait_source: Kojiki — guide of Ninigi at the heavenly descent; tall, fierce-eyed, glowing earthly-kami
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Kojiki — described as immensely tall (seven shaku, two saka), with a long nose, glowing eyes like the eight-handed mirror; in later iconography depicted as a tengu-like figure with long nose and red face
nodes.significantEvent_source: Kojiki — encountered Ninigi at the eight crossroads of heaven during the Tenson Kōrin; identified himself as Sarutahiko, the chief earthly-kami of the crossroads; guided Ninigi to the earthly land; later wedded by Ame-no-Uzume
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Kojiki — earthly kami, no specific birth-narrative
nodes.birthTypes_source: Kojiki

nodes.name: Oshihomimi
nodes.domain: the heavenly ear, sovereignty, the first heir, Amaterasus son
nodes.characterTrait: sovereign, ear-associated, heavenly, first-born heir, regal
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: son of Amaterasu and heir to the heavenly sovereignty
nodes.significantEvent: was chosen to descend from heaven to rule the earth but declined, instead sending his son Ninigi to make the heavenly descent in his place
nodes.symbolism: the heir who declines to descend, the first-born who delegates to his son, the heavenly sovereignty that passes through generations before touching earth
nodes.neumannArchetype: the reluctant heir who passes the heroic task of descent to the next generation, the masculine that delegates the confrontation with the earthly to the divine grandchild
nodes.birthCircumstances: born to Amaterasu, the first heir of the sun goddess

nodes.name: Tengu
nodes.domain: mountains, martial arts, long noses, forests, supernatural warriors, Shugendo
nodes.animals: eagle, serpent, snake, hawk, fish, dog, bear, monkey, dragon
nodes.characterTrait: fierce, ascetic, martial, long-nosed, forest-dwelling, supernatural
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: supernatural mountain beings with long noses and red faces, wearing the garb of mountain ascetics (yamabushi), sometimes depicted with wings
nodes.significantEvent: tengu are the supernatural guardians and terrors of the mountains, they can be both benevolent teachers of martial arts and malevolent tricksters, the great tengu Sojobo taught the legendary warrior Minamoto no Yoshitsune swordsmanship on Mount Kurama
nodes.symbolism: the long nose as the mark of supernatural pride, the mountain as the training ground of the supernatural warrior, the tengu as the dangerous teacher who instructs through trial, the boundary between helpful guide and destructive trickster
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow-father of the mountain who teaches the hero through terrifying trials, the masculine of the wild mountain that must be encountered for the warrior to gain mastery

nodes.domain: Mount Kurama, tengu king, martial arts, supernatural mastery, swordsmanship
nodes.characterTrait: supreme, masterful, ancient, martial, wise, supernatural
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the king of the tengu, an immensely old and powerful supernatural being who dwells on Mount Kurama near Kyoto
nodes.significantEvent: the most powerful tengu in Japan who taught the legendary young warrior Minamoto no Yoshitsune the art of swordsmanship and strategy on Mount Kurama, the supreme master of martial arts among the supernatural beings
nodes.symbolism: the king of the mountain supernaturals as the ultimate martial teacher, Mount Kurama as the training ground of legendary warriors, the supernatural mastery that can only be gained from the most powerful and dangerous teacher
nodes.neumannArchetype: the supreme wise old man of the mountain, the terrifying masculine teacher whose instruction transforms the young hero into the greatest warrior

nodes.name: Toyotama-hime
nodes.domain: the sea, the sea palace, childbirth, dragons, transformation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Luminous Jewel Princess, daughter of the Dragon King Ryujin, a beautiful woman who can take dragon or sea-creature form
nodes.significantEvent: married Hoori (Fireshade) at the sea palace, when she came to land to give birth she told him not to watch, he looked and saw her in her true form (a dragon or wani), shamed, she returned to the sea forever, but sent her sister Tamayori-hime to raise the child
nodes.symbolism: the sea princess who gives birth in her true form, the prohibition against watching the birth as the taboo of seeing the divine in its true shape, the shame of being seen in animal form as the barrier between the sea and land worlds
nodes.neumannArchetype: the anima from the oceanic unconscious who must give birth in her true (dragon) form, the feminine of the deep whose secret nature cannot be witnessed by the masculine
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the Dragon King Ryujin (Watatsumi) of the sea palace

nodes.name: Ugayafukiaezu
nodes.domain: the imperial lineage, the thatched roof, Jimmu, the connection between sea and land
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the son of Hoori and Toyotama-hime whose birth-hut was left with an unfinished thatched roof
nodes.significantEvent: raised by his aunt Tamayori-hime (whom he later married), father of Emperor Jimmu, the legendary first Emperor of Japan, the bridge figure between the mythological age and the historical imperial line
nodes.symbolism: the unfinished roof as the incomplete threshold between the divine and the human, the marriage with his aunt as the endogamous preservation of the divine lineage, the bridge between myth and history
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child whose unfinished birth-hut represents the incomplete transition from mythological to historical consciousness, the liminal figure between the age of kami and the age of emperors
nodes.birthCircumstances: born in a thatched birth-hut on the seashore before the roof was finished, hence his name (meaning Thatch-Meeting-Incompletely)

nodes.name: Tenjin
nodes.domain: scholarship, poetry, calligraphy, learning, thunder, examinations
nodes.characterTrait: scholarly, poetic, wise, calligraphic, justice-seeking, examination-blessing
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the deified spirit of Sugawara no Michizane, patron of scholarship and learning
nodes.significantEvent: after his death in exile, terrible plagues, lightning strikes, and disasters struck Kyoto, which were attributed to his angry spirit, to appease him he was deified as Tenjin and enshrined at Kitano Tenmangu, he became the patron of scholarship and is visited by millions of students before examinations
nodes.symbolism: the unjustly exiled scholar whose angry spirit becomes the god of learning, the ox as his sacred animal, plum blossoms as his symbol, the transformation of a vengeful ghost into a benevolent patron of education
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow-father whose wrath is transformed into benevolent wisdom, the angry patriarch whose vindication transforms him into the patron of intellectual consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: Sugawara no Michizane was a brilliant 9th-century scholar and statesman who was unjustly exiled
nodes.deathCircumstances: He died in exile in 903.

nodes.name: Takenouchi no Sukune
nodes.domain: loyalty, longevity, statecraft, the legendary minister, the imperial court
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a legendary minister said to have served multiple emperors over an impossibly long lifespan
nodes.significantEvent: said to have served five emperors spanning 244 years, a legendary figure of extreme loyalty and longevity in service to the imperial court, deified as a kami of loyalty and state service
nodes.symbolism: the impossibly long service as the ideal of perpetual loyalty, the minister who transcends human lifespan through devotion, longevity as the reward for perfect service to the throne
nodes.neumannArchetype: the eternal wise counselor who serves the patriarchal sovereignty, the masculine of perpetual loyalty to the ruling consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: Takenouchi no Sukune was supposedly the son of Princess Kagehime, and is said to be grandson to .

nodes.name: Bragi
nodes.domain: poetry, eloquence, wisdom, song, the skaldic art
nodes.object: his harp (in some iconographic readings); his tongue (on which runes are cut, per Sigrdrífumál 16); the mead of poetry (which is associated with him as patron of skalds)
nodes.characterTrait: poetic, eloquent, wise, well-spoken, the patron of skalds
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Bearded and long-bearded ('the long-bearded one' is one of his epithets, possibly a reflex of the historical skald Bragi Boddason 'the Old', 9th c., whose name may have been theologized into the divine Bragi). Wisest of the Æsir in the use of words.
nodes.significantEvent: Patron of poetry and the skaldic art. In Skáldskaparmál 1, instructs Ægir on the origin of poetic diction. In Lokasenna, attempts to silence Loki when he enters the banquet; Loki insults him for cowardice (Lokasenna 11-15). The historical 9th-century skald Bragi Boddason is sometimes thought to have been deified or to have given his name to the divine Bragi — the chronological-theological relationship is unsettled.
nodes.symbolism: poetry as a divine gift from the god of eloquence, the skaldic art as sacred, the harp as the instrument of divine speech, the connection between poetry and the afterlife
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine of the creative word, the logos-consciousness that celebrates the deeds of heroes through poetic speech
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Odin in some traditions; husband of Iðunn.
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 26; Skáldskaparmál (opening — Bragi as host); Lokasenna 8-16 (Bragi's confrontation with Loki at Ægir's feast); Grímnismál 44
nodes.object_source: Skáldskaparmál (the gift of runes on his tongue from Odin)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Gylfaginning 26; Lokasenna 8-16; Skáldskaparmál
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Gylfaginning 26 ('renowned for wisdom and most of all for eloquence and command of language; he is exceedingly skilled in poetry; from him poetry is called bragr; long-bearded')
nodes.significantEvent_source: Skáldskaparmál (the opening dialogue with Ægir); Lokasenna 8-16
nodes.birthTypes_source: Snorri
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Snorri's tradition; Skáldskaparmál

nodes.name: Toyouke-hime
nodes.domain: food, grain, clothing, sericulture, agriculture, industry, the outer shrine of Ise
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the food and grain goddess, enshrined at the outer shrine (Geku) of the Grand Shrine of Ise
nodes.significantEvent: enshrined at the Geku (outer shrine) of Ise alongside Amaterasu at the Naiku (inner shrine), she provides the sacred food offerings to Amaterasu, representing the material sustenance that supports the divine
nodes.symbolism: the food goddess who serves the sun goddess as the material supports the divine, the outer shrine as the provider of nourishment to the inner shrine, agriculture and industry as sacred service to the divine order
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of food and sustenance who provides material nourishment to the solar consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: In the Kojiki, Toyouke-hime is noted as the daughter of Wakumusubi and granddaughter of Izanami.

nodes.name: Toshigami
nodes.domain: the New Year, harvest, ancestral spirits, the turning of the year, grain spirits
nodes.characterTrait: seasonal, New Year-associated, harvest-bringing, ancestral, cyclical
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the kami of the New Year and the incoming harvest, the deity who visits at the turning of the year
nodes.significantEvent: Toshigami visits households during the New Year period, arriving through the kadomatsu (pine decorations) and shimenawa (sacred ropes), the mochi (rice cakes) offered at New Year are the food of this deity, representing the grain spirit of the new year
nodes.symbolism: the New Year as the arrival of the divine, the kadomatsu as the landing place of the visiting kami, the mochi as the food of the year-god, the annual renewal as a divine visitation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the cyclic deity of renewal, the divine visitor who brings the new consciousness with each annual cycle
nodes.birthCircumstances: According to the Kojiki, Toshigami was the son of Susanoo and Kamuo Ichihime and the older brother of Ukanomitama.

nodes.domain: birthplace, the guardian kami of ones birth territory, ancestral land protection
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the guardian kami of the land where one was born, the divine protector of ones natal territory
nodes.significantEvent: every person has an ubusunagami, the kami of the place where they were born, this kami protects them throughout life regardless of where they move, the first shrine visit (miyamairi) introduces the newborn to their ubusunagami
nodes.symbolism: birth as creating an eternal bond with the local kami, the natal territory as the sacred ground of ones origin, the lifelong protection from the birthplace deity regardless of migration
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother/Father of the birthplace, the natal consciousness that protects throughout life

nodes.name: Ta-no-Kami
nodes.domain: rice paddies, agriculture, harvest, fertility, the field kami
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the kami of the rice paddy, the divine presence in the cultivated field
nodes.significantEvent: Ta-no-Kami descends from the mountains in spring to dwell in the rice paddies and ensure a good harvest, then returns to the mountains in autumn as Yama-no-Kami, this seasonal movement between mountain and field is one of the most fundamental patterns in Japanese folk religion
nodes.symbolism: the seasonal movement between mountain and field as the divine rhythm of agriculture, the rice paddy as the sacred space of cultivation, the harvest as the fruit of divine presence in the field
nodes.neumannArchetype: the seasonal Great Mother/Father who descends from the unconscious (mountain) to dwell in the cultivated consciousness (field) and returns after the harvest

nodes.name: Tamayori-hime
nodes.domain: child-rearing, the sea, the imperial lineage, substitute motherhood
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: younger sister of Toyotama-hime, a beautiful woman connected to the sea realm
nodes.significantEvent: sent by her sister Toyotama-hime to raise the child Ugayafukiaezu after Toyotama-hime returned to the sea in shame, later married Ugayafukiaezu and became the mother of Emperor Jimmu, the first legendary Emperor
nodes.symbolism: the substitute mother who raises the child of the sea princess, the aunt who becomes the wife, the endogamous marriage that preserves the divine sea-lineage, the bridge between the sea world and the imperial line
nodes.neumannArchetype: the substitute Great Mother who raises the divine child when the original mother returns to the unconscious (sea), the nurturing feminine that connects the oceanic and terrestrial lineages
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the Dragon King Ryujin, younger sister of Toyotama-hime

nodes.domain: Suwa, wrestling, thunder, submission, the earthly kami
nodes.object: snake, dragon, iron hook, sword, mirror, arrow
nodes.animals: serpent, snake, horse, deer, hawk, vulture, boar, rabbit, rooster, dragon
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a powerful warrior kami, son of Okuninushi, associated with strength and wrestling
nodes.significantEvent: challenged Takemikazuchi to a wrestling match for control of the land, was defeated and fled to Suwa in Nagano where he was trapped, his struggle at Suwa became the basis for the sumo wrestling tradition, the last earthly kami to resist the heavenly cession
nodes.symbolism: the wrestling match for sovereignty as the physical contest between earth and heaven, defeat and exile to Suwa as the final submission of the earthly to the heavenly, the origin of sumo as a divine wrestling match for cosmic authority
nodes.neumannArchetype: the last earthly masculine to resist the heavenly patriarchal order, the son of the Great Land Father who loses the cosmic wrestling match to the celestial warrior
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Okuninushi, the Great Land Master

nodes.name: Sukunabikona
nodes.domain: medicine, brewing, hot springs, insects, the small god, nation-building
nodes.characterTrait: tiny, wise, medicine-knowing, brewing, helpful, diminutive
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: an incredibly small deity, so tiny he arrived riding on a wave in a pod (or boat made from a bean pod)
nodes.significantEvent: arrived from across the sea in a tiny boat and helped Okuninushi build and civilize the land, taught the arts of medicine and brewing sake, then departed by being flung from a bent stalk of millet into the sky
nodes.symbolism: the tiny god who arrives from the unknown sea with the gifts of civilization, the small as the carrier of great knowledge, medicine and brewing as the twin gifts of the miniature divine, departure by catapult as the mysterious return of the visiting god
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child/wise old man paradox, the tiny masculine consciousness that brings the gifts of civilization from across the sea of the unconscious
nodes.birthCircumstances: When Kuebiko saw the dwarf, he said "That is Sukuna son of Kami-Musubi.

nodes.domain: food, agriculture, the production of food from the body, sacrifice
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the food goddess who produced food from her own body
nodes.significantEvent: produced food from various orifices and parts of her body to feed the gods, when Tsukuyomi (the moon god) saw how she produced the food he was disgusted and killed her, from her dead body grew rice, wheat, millet, beans, and silkworms

nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother whose sacrificed body becomes the earth and its crops, the dismembered feminine whose death produces the sustenance of civilization
nodes.birthCircumstances: Ōgetsu-hime/Ukemochi is married to , the son of Toshigami through his wife in the Kojiki, making Hayamato her great-grandnephew through her brother Ōyamatsumi.

nodes.name: Yamato Takeru
nodes.domain: heroism, warfare, sacrifice, the imperial family, tragic heroism
nodes.characterTrait: heroic, tragic, shape-shifting, brave, doomed, valorous
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a legendary prince and warrior, perhaps the greatest hero of Japanese mythology
nodes.significantEvent: sent by his father on perilous missions, disguised himself as a woman to assassinate the Kumaso chieftains, used the sword Kusanagi to escape a fire trap in the wilderness, died on his final campaign and his spirit became a white bird that flew away
nodes.symbolism: the tragic hero who serves the father but is never truly accepted, the disguise as a woman as the heros use of the feminine, the white bird as the soul freed from the doomed body, the sword Kusanagi as the divine protection that eventually fails
nodes.neumannArchetype: the tragic hero who serves the patriarchal order but is consumed by it, the masculine consciousness that uses the feminine (disguise) to accomplish the heroic task but is ultimately destroyed
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Emperor Keiko, a prince of the imperial house
nodes.deathCircumstances: He was born circa 72 and died in 114.
nodes.domain_source: Kojiki, scroll II (the central Yamato Takeru narrative); Nihon Shoki
nodes.object_source: Kojiki — Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi (the grass-cutting sword, given by his aunt Yamatohime-no-mikoto from Ise; the sword from the Yamata-no-Orochi tail)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Kojiki — heroic, tragic, fiercely-warrior, sacrificed by his father's distrust
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Kojiki — warrior-prince; in some scenes disguised as a woman to enter the Kumaso brothers' feast
nodes.significantEvent_source: Kojiki — son of Emperor Keikō; named originally Ōusu (when as a boy he tore his brother apart); sent by his suspicious father to subdue distant lands (Kumaso in the south, Emishi in the east); disguised himself as a maiden to kill the Kumaso brothers (who renamed him Yamato Takeru); used Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi to cut grass and start a counter-fire when trapped in a burning field; eventually died from cursed-mountain-deity disease, transforming into a white bird at death

nodes.deathCircumstances_source: Kojiki — killed by the curse of the mountain-kami; transformed into a white bird at death; the white bird flew back toward Yamato

nodes.name: Baldr
nodes.domain: light, beauty, purity, innocence, death, dreams
nodes.object: his hall Breiðablik ('Wide-shining'); his ship Hringhorni (the great ship which is his funeral-pyre, 'the largest of all ships'); a ring (which Odin lays on his pyre, Draupnir or another)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: The fairest of the Æsir; so bright that light shines from him (Gylfaginning 22). The plant baldursbrá (the chamomile, 'Baldr's brow') is named for the brightness of his brow.
nodes.significantEvent: Baldr begins to dream of his death (Baldrs draumar; Gylfaginning 49). Odin rides to the underworld to consult a vǫlva. Frigg makes all things in nature swear not to harm him — but neglects the mistletoe as too young. The Æsir make sport of throwing weapons at the now-invulnerable Baldr; Loki, in disguise, learns of the omitted mistletoe, fashions it into a dart, and gives it to the blind Hǫðr to throw. Baldr is killed. The Æsir make a great funeral pyre on the ship Hringhorni; the giantess Hyrrokkin pushes it out to sea. Hermóðr rides Sleipnir to Hel to seek Baldr's release; Hel agrees if all things weep for him. All do — except the giantess Þǫkk (Loki in disguise), who refuses, and so Baldr remains in Hel until after Ragnarok. After Ragnarok, Baldr returns from Hel with his brother Hǫðr to inhabit the renewed world (Vǫluspá 62; Gylfaginning 53).
nodes.symbolism: the beautiful god whose death begins the end of the world, innocence destroyed by trickery, the one thing overlooked (mistletoe) as the fatal weakness, the death that cannot be undone as the beginning of cosmic destruction
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child of light whose death initiates the dissolution of the cosmic order, the pure consciousness destroyed by the shadow (Loki)
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Odin and Frigg.
nodes.deathCircumstances: Killed by his blind brother Hǫðr, who is given a mistletoe-dart by the disguised Loki; Hǫðr throws and Baldr falls dead. His funeral on the ship Hringhorni is the great mourning of the Æsir. Hermóðr rides to Hel to ransom him, but Loki (as the giantess Þǫkk) refuses to weep, and Baldr remains in Hel. After Ragnarok, he returns from Hel with his brother Hǫðr to dwell in the renewed world.
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 22, 49 (the death of Baldr); Vǫluspá 31-33; Baldrs Draumar (the prophetic-dreams poem); Vegtamskviða; Skáldskaparmál; Saxo Grammaticus, Gesta Danorum 3 (the very different Saxo version)

nodes.name: Thor
nodes.domain: thunder, lightning, strength, protection, storms, agriculture, consecration
nodes.object: Mjǫllnir (his hammer, forged by Sindri/Eitri and Brokk); Megingjǫrð (his belt of strength, doubles his might); Járngreipr (his iron gloves, used to wield the hammer); his goat-drawn chariot (drawn by Tanngrisnir 'Tooth-gnasher' and Tanngnjóstr 'Tooth-grinder'); Bilskírnir (his hall, the largest in Asgard with 540 rooms)
nodes.characterTrait: mighty, hot-tempered, voracious (Þrymskviða 24-26, his bridal feast), straightforward, loyal-to-Æsir, monster-slaying, the friend of farmers and free men
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Red-bearded, mighty in stature, with eyes of fire (Þrymskviða 27, where Thrym fears the bride's fierce eyes — actually disguised Thor). Wields Mjǫllnir, wears Megingjǫrð and Járngreipr. The standard Bronze Age Thor amulet (the 'Þórs hamarr' miniature pendants from Viking-Age Scandinavia, e.g., Skåne) shows the inverted-T hammer.
nodes.significantEvent: Many adventures: kills Hrungnir in single combat (Skáldskaparmál 17); fishes for Jǫrmungandr with Hymir, hooking the Midgard Serpent (Hymiskviða; Gylfaginning 48); journeys to Útgarða-Loki with Loki and Þjálfi (Gylfaginning 44-47, the famous trickery of the giant-king); recovers stolen Mjǫllnir from Þrymr by going disguised as Freyja in bridal garb (Þrymskviða); kills the giant Geirrøðr (Skáldskaparmál 18). At Ragnarok, kills Jǫrmungandr but takes nine paces and dies of the serpent's venom (Vǫluspá 56-57; Gylfaginning 51).
nodes.symbolism: the hammer as the weapon of consecration and destruction, thunder as the voice of divine protection, the goats that can be eaten and resurrected as the cycle of agricultural renewal, the red beard as the fire of righteous anger, nine steps as the number of death
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father of protection and strength, the masculine warrior-consciousness that defends the ordered world against the forces of chaos
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Odin and Jǫrð (the earth-goddess) per Skáldskaparmál 14; sometimes Fjǫrgyn is given as the mother (a name for Jǫrð).
nodes.deathCircumstances: Slays Jörmungandr (the Midgard Serpent) at Ragnarök but falls dead after nine steps from the serpent's venom (Vǫluspá 56).
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 21, 44-46; Skáldskaparmál 4-25 (the Hrungnir, Geirröd, and other Thor-adventures); Þrymskviða; Hárbarðsljóð; Hymiskviða; Vǫluspá 56 (his Ragnarök fate)

nodes.name: Freyja
nodes.domain: love, beauty, fertility, war, death, gold, seidr (magic), the slain
nodes.object: Brísingamen (necklace), falcon-feather cloak, boar (Hildisvíni), chariot drawn by cats
nodes.characterTrait: beautiful, passionate, magical, fierce, weeping, desiring, generous
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the most beautiful of the goddesses, wears the Brisingamen necklace, rides a chariot drawn by two cats, possesses a falcon-feather cloak
nodes.significantEvent: receives half of the battle-slain in her hall Sessrumnir (the other half go to Odin in Valhalla), wept golden tears for her lost husband Odr, taught seidr magic to Odin, obtained the Brisingamen necklace from four dwarves
nodes.symbolism: the golden tears as grief transformed into beauty, half the slain as the feminine share of death, the falcon cloak as the ability to travel between worlds, the Brisingamen as the magical adornment of the divine feminine, seidr as the feminine magic that even the Allfather sought to learn
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of love, death, and magic, the supreme feminine whose domain encompasses both desire and the battlefield dead
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Njord, sister of Freyr, a Vanir goddess who came to the Aesir after the Aesir-Vanir war

The Sǫrla þáttr 'four-dwarves' acquisition is late (14th c. Flateyjarbók).

nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 24 ('the most renowned of the goddesses, fairest of all'); Skáldskaparmál 20 (Brísingamen); Þrymskviða 13 (her wrath shaking the halls)

nodes.name: Freyr
nodes.domain: fertility, kingship, sunshine, rain, harvest, peace, prosperity
nodes.object: Skíðblaðnir (the magnificent ship made by the sons of Ívaldi, foldable to fit in a pouch yet large enough to hold all the Æsir); Gullinbursti / Slíðrugtanni (the golden boar made by Sindri and Brokk, that pulls his chariot and lights up the dark with its golden bristles); his magical sword (which fights of itself against the giants — given away when he sent Skírnir to woo Gerðr, hence his fatal weaponlessness at Ragnarok); a horse named Blóðughófi ('Blood-hoof')
nodes.characterTrait: generous, peaceable, fertile, lovesick (in Skírnismál), tragic-in-Ragnarok
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Beardless and youthful (in some euhemerized sources); fertility-god par excellence. Adam of Bremen describes the third statue at the Uppsala temple as 'Fricco, with a huge phallus' (cum ingenti priapo) — corroborating Freyr's fertility-iconographic role.
nodes.significantEvent: The major narrative: while sitting on Hliðskjálf (Odin's high seat), Freyr looks into all the worlds and sees the giant-maiden Gerðr in Jǫtunheim; falls desperately in love. Sends his servant Skírnir with his sword and his horse Blóðughófi to win her. Skírnir threatens Gerðr with terrible curses (Skírnismál 25-36) and finally wins her consent to meet Freyr after nine nights at Barri. Freyr's gift of his sword to Skírnir leaves him weaponless — at Ragnarok, this is fatal: he must fight the fire-giant Surtr unarmed, and is killed (Vǫluspá 53; Gylfaginning 49).
nodes.symbolism: the gift of the sword for love as the sacrifice of defense for desire, the boar as the golden beast of the harvest, the ship Skidbladnir as the vessel of abundance, the lord of the Vanir as the divine king of fertility
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father of fertility and peace, the masculine of the harvest who sacrifices his weapon (defensive consciousness) for the love of the feminine (Gerd)
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Njǫrðr and his sister-wife (the unnamed Vanic mother).
nodes.deathCircumstances: Falls to Surtr at Ragnarök, weaponless because he gave his sword to Skírnir to win Gerðr (Vǫluspá 53; Gylfaginning 51).
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 24; Skáldskaparmál 7, 17; Skírnismál (the wooing of Gerðr); Lokasenna 35-36; Vǫluspá 53; Adam of Bremen (the Uppsala statue with phallus); Ynglinga saga 10-12
nodes.object_source: Skírnismál; Skáldskaparmál 35 (Skíðblaðnir and Gullinbursti, dwarven gifts); Gylfaginning 24, 37
nodes.characterTrait_source: Skírnismál (his lovesick longing); Gylfaginning 24, 37 (his beloved-king status among Vanir and giants); Lokasenna 35 (Njǫrðr's defense of Freyr's good fame)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Adam of Bremen, Descriptio Insularum Aquilonis (the Uppsala statue with great phallus); Gylfaginning 24; standard iconography (golden-haired fertile-king type)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Skírnismál (his longing for Gerðr, sending of Skírnir to woo her, surrender of his sword); Vǫluspá 53; Gylfaginning 51 (his Ragnarök death without his sword)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Lokasenna 36
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Lokasenna 36

nodes.name: Heimdall
nodes.domain: watchfulness, the rainbow bridge (Bifrost), hearing, sight, the horn Gjallarhorn, Ragnarok
nodes.object: Gjallarhorn (the loud horn, hidden under Yggdrasil's root, blown to summon the gods at Ragnarok); his sword Hǫfuð (literally 'Head', possibly a pun on his having killed Loki who was a 'head' as in chief)
nodes.animals: ram (his epithet `Hallinskíði` 'leaning-stick', which Snorri says means ram in poetic diction)
nodes.characterTrait: watchful, far-seeing, far-hearing (he hears wool growing on sheep and grass on the earth), faithful guardian, ultimately Loki's slayer-and-slain
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: White-shining (`hvítastr ása`, 'whitest of the Æsir'), with golden teeth (epithet `gullintanni` 'gold-toothed'). His abode is Himinbjǫrg ('Heaven's-cliff') at the rainbow-bridge Bifrǫst. He needs less sleep than a bird, sees by night and day at a distance of a hundred leagues, and hears wool growing on sheep and grass growing on the earth.
nodes.significantEvent: Watcher at Bifrǫst against the giants. Holds the Gjallarhorn under Yggdrasil's root, ready to sound it at Ragnarok. As Ríg, walks among men and fathers the three social classes (thrall, freeman, lord), per Rígsþula. At Ragnarok, blows the Gjallarhorn to summon the gods to battle (Vǫluspá 46), then meets Loki on the field; they are mutual slayers (Gylfaginning 51).
nodes.symbolism: the rainbow bridge as the threshold between worlds, the horn that signals the end as the alarm of cosmic destruction, the nine mothers as the waves of the sea, the watchman at the border of order and chaos
nodes.neumannArchetype: the watchman-consciousness at the threshold, the masculine awareness that guards the border between the ordered world and the chaotic beyond
familyRoles: father (as Ríg) of the three social classes
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of nine mothers (the nine sisters by the sea) per Heimdallargaldr cited in Skáldskaparmál 8 and Hyndluljóð 35.
nodes.deathCircumstances: Falls in mutual slaughter with Loki at Ragnarök (Vǫluspá 51; Gylfaginning 51).
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 27; Skáldskaparmál 8, 16; Vǫluspá 1, 27, 46; Þrymskviða 14; Rígsþula (Heimdall as Rígr, ancestor of the social orders); Húsdrápa (skaldic)
nodes.object_source: Gylfaginning 27 (Gjallarhorn, his great horn, and Gulltoppr, his golden-maned horse, and Himinbjǫrg, his hall at the heaven's edge by Bifrǫst)
nodes.animals_source: Skáldskaparmál 8 (the epithet); the symbolic embodiment is debated — could be either embodiment-emblem or simply a poetic kenning
nodes.characterTrait_source: Gylfaginning 27 (sees a hundred leagues by day or night; hears the grass grow and wool sprout on sheep; sleeps less than a bird)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Gylfaginning 27; Skáldskaparmál
nodes.significantEvent_source: Rígsþula (his fathering of the social orders as Rígr); Þrymskviða 14 (his counsel to retrieve Mjǫllnir); Vǫluspá 46 (his sounding of the horn at Ragnarök); Gylfaginning 51 (mutual slaughter with Loki)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Skáldskaparmál 8; Hyndluljóð 35
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Skáldskaparmál 8 (citing the lost Heimdallargaldr); Hyndluljóð 35

nodes.name: Njörðr
nodes.domain: the sea, wind, wealth, fishing, sailing, harbors
nodes.object: Nóatún ('Ship-enclosure'), his hall by the sea-shore; his ship-paraphernalia (sails, anchors)
nodes.characterTrait: kindly, prosperity-bringing, sea-faring, lover of harbors and ships, unhappy in mountain-dwelling (the failed Skaði-marriage)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Vanir god, possibly older in iconographic type (compare Tacitus's Germania 40, Nerthus). His feet are the most beautiful: when Skaði must choose her husband by his feet alone (his face being hidden), she chooses Njǫrðr's feet thinking they must be Baldr's (Skáldskaparmál 33).
nodes.significantEvent: Vanir hostage to the Æsir after the Æsir-Vanir war (along with his children Freyr and Freyja). His sister-wife (in Vanir custom of brother-sister marriage) bore Freyr and Freyja with him in Vanaheim; the Æsir's prohibition on incest meant they did not continue this marriage in Asgard. Marries the giantess Skaði after the gods give her compensation for Þjazi's death; she chooses him by his feet, expecting Baldr; the marriage fails because she loves the mountains and he loves the sea (Skáldskaparmál 33).
nodes.symbolism: the failed marriage between sea and mountain as the incompatibility of different elemental natures, the wealth of the sea as the foundation of maritime prosperity, the Vanir as the older fertility religion
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father of the sea and wealth, the masculine of the ocean whose nature is incompatible with the mountain-feminine (Skadi)
familyRoles: god of the sea, wind, and wealth
nodes.birthCircumstances: Vanir god; one of the three Vanir hostages exchanged at the end of the Aesir-Vanir war (Njǫrðr, Freyr, Freyja).
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 23; Skáldskaparmál 7; Vafþrúðnismál 38-39; Lokasenna 33-36; Ynglinga saga 4-9; Adam of Bremen
nodes.object_source: Gylfaginning 23 (Nóatún, his hall by the sea); standard iconography
nodes.characterTrait_source: Gylfaginning 23; Skáldskaparmál; Lokasenna 35-36
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Gylfaginning 23; standard iconography of bearded sea-prosperity god
nodes.significantEvent_source: Gylfaginning 23 (the marriage to Skaði — she chose her husband by his feet, expecting Baldr, getting Njǫrðr; they could not agree on residence and parted); Vafþrúðnismál 38-39 (his Vanir-hostage status after the Aesir-Vanir war)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Vanir-hostage tradition; Ynglinga saga 4

nodes.name: Ullr
nodes.domain: archery, skiing, hunting, winter, oaths, single combat, glory
nodes.object: bow, skis, shield (which he can use as a boat); his ring (oath-binding)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Tall, archer-warrior in fur garments; depicted on skis or skates in Norse art.
nodes.significantEvent: Son of Sif by an unknown father (i.e., before her marriage to Thor); stepson of Thor (Skáldskaparmál 14). In Saxo's Gesta Danorum 3.4-3.5, when Odin is exiled for ten years for an unspeakable deed, Ollerus (Ullr) rules in his stead, using bone-runes to skim across the sea.
nodes.symbolism: the bow and skis as the instruments of winter survival, yew as the wood of both the bow and the rune of death, winter hunting as the sacred pursuit of the cold season
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine of winter hunting, the consciousness of survival in the cold season through skill and discipline
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Sif by an unknown father (before her marriage to Thor); stepson of Thor.
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 31; Grímnismál 5 (his hall Ýdalir); Atlakviða 30 (oath sworn 'by Ullr's ring'); Saxo Grammaticus, Gesta Danorum 3.4-3.5 (the Ollerus narrative — Ullr ruling in Odin's stead during his exile)
nodes.object_source: Snorri Gylfaginning 31 (bow and skis); Atlakviða 30 (oath-ring); Snorri (the shield as boat — 'Ullr's askr' as a kenning for shield)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Gylfaginning 31
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Gylfaginning 31; standard iconography of skiing-archer god
nodes.significantEvent_source: Skáldskaparmál 14; Gylfaginning 31; Saxo 3.4-3.5

nodes.name: Víðarr
nodes.domain: silence, vengeance, the forest, strength, Ragnarok, survival
nodes.object: his thick magic shoe (made of all the leather scraps people ever cut off when making shoes — used to hold Fenrir's lower jaw open while Vidar pulls upward to tear the wolf apart)
nodes.characterTrait: silent, strong, vengeful, post-Ragnarok-surviving — `inn þǫgli áss` 'the silent god'
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Tall, mighty in strength, second only to Thor among the Æsir. Wears the great shoe described above. Lives in Víði ('the wide land'), a land grown over with shrubs and tall grass.
nodes.significantEvent: At Ragnarok, after Fenrir has swallowed Odin, Vidar leaps forward, plants his great shoe on the wolf's lower jaw, grasps the upper jaw, and tears Fenrir's jaws apart, killing him. Survives Ragnarok and inhabits the renewed world (Vafþrúðnismál 51).
nodes.symbolism: the thick shoe as the instrument of vengeance accumulated over time, silence as the preparation for the ultimate act, the vengeance of the son for the devoured father, survival through silence and patience
nodes.neumannArchetype: the silent son who avenges the patriarchal father, the patient masculine consciousness that endures until the moment of action and survives the cosmic destruction
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Odin and the giantess Gríðr.
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 29, 51; Vǫluspá 55; Vafþrúðnismál 53; Lokasenna 10 (Odin asks Vídar to make place for Loki)
nodes.object_source: Gylfaginning 51; Vǫluspá 55 (the great shoe, made of the scraps of leather that men cut off for the toes and heels of their shoes — the cosmological resource collected over generations)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Gylfaginning 29 ('the silent god' — almost as strong as Thor)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Gylfaginning 29
nodes.significantEvent_source: Vǫluspá 55; Vafþrúðnismál 53; Gylfaginning 51 (avenges Odin at Ragnarök by stepping on Fenrir's lower jaw with his great shoe and tearing the wolf's mouth apart)

nodes.name: Forseti
nodes.domain: justice, peace, reconciliation, law, mediation, judgment
nodes.object: Glitnir ('Glittering'), his hall — built of gold and silver, where he sits to settle all disputes
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Sits in his hall Glitnir, settling disputes — 'all who come to him with disputes go away reconciled' (Gylfaginning 32). The hall has pillars of red gold and a roof of silver.
nodes.significantEvent: The judge of the Æsir; god of justice and reconciliation.
nodes.symbolism: the golden throne as the seat of impartial justice, Glitnir as the hall of brilliant judgment, reconciliation as the highest legal art, the son of the light-god as the inheritor of fairness
nodes.neumannArchetype: the judicial consciousness that resolves conflict through reason and fairness, the son of the light-god who embodies the impartial judgment of civilization
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Baldr and Nanna.
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 32; Grímnismál 15 (the only major Eddic mentions); Frisian saint-Foseti tradition (Vita S. Liudgeri)
nodes.object_source: Grímnismál 15 (his hall Glitnir, with gold pillars and silver roof)

nodes.name: Höðr
nodes.domain: darkness, blindness, winter, the unwitting killer
nodes.object: the mistletoe-shaft Loki gave him (his weapon of unwitting killing)
nodes.characterTrait: blind, unwitting, instrument-of-Loki, victim of Váli's vengeance, post-Ragnarok-restored
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Blind (Gylfaginning 49: 'mighty in strength but blind'). His blindness makes him the unwitting tool of Loki's plot.
nodes.significantEvent: Standing apart at the gathering where the gods sport with weapons against the invulnerable Baldr because he is blind. Loki, in disguise, gives him a mistletoe-dart and guides his hand; Hǫðr throws and Baldr falls dead. The very next day, Váli (Odin's son born for vengeance, only one day old) kills Hǫðr in retribution (Vǫluspá 33; Baldrs draumar 11). After Ragnarok, Hǫðr returns from Hel with Baldr to inhabit the renewed world (Vǫluspá 62).
nodes.symbolism: the blind brother who kills the bright one, the unwitting instrument of the trickster, darkness destroying light without understanding, the innocence of the murderer who does not know what he does
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow-twin of the light-god, the dark unconscious masculine that destroys the bright consciousness without awareness, manipulated by the trickster
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Odin and Frigg; brother of Baldr.
nodes.deathCircumstances: Slain by Váli (Odin's son begotten specifically for vengeance, who at one day old slew Hǫðr) per Baldrs Draumar 11 and Vǫluspá 32-33.
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 22 (his blindness), 49 (the killing of Baldr); Vǫluspá 32-33; Baldrs Draumar; Saxo Grammaticus, Gesta Danorum 3 (the very different Saxo version where Hotherus is a heroic mortal)
nodes.object_source: Gylfaginning 49 (the mistletoe-dart given him by Loki)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Gylfaginning 22, 49; Vǫluspá 32-33
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Gylfaginning 22 ('blind, mighty enough; the gods would prefer that one need not name him, for the work of his hands shall long be held in memory among gods and men')
nodes.significantEvent_source: Gylfaginning 49 (the killing of Baldr); Vǫluspá 32-33; Baldrs Draumar; Vǫluspá 62 (his post-Ragnarök reconciliation with Baldr)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Gylfaginning 22
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Gylfaginning 22; Vǫluspá

nodes.name: Mímir
nodes.domain: wisdom, knowledge, memory, counsel, the severed head, wells
nodes.object: Mímisbrunnr (his well of wisdom, beneath the second root of Yggdrasil); his severed head (preserved by Odin with herbs and incantations to keep it speaking)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: In some sources, complete; in Heimskringla's Ynglinga saga 4, beheaded by the Vanir during the hostage exchange — Odin recovers the head, embalms it with herbs, and chants incantations over it so that it speaks to him forever.
nodes.significantEvent: Guardian of Mímisbrunnr, the well of wisdom beneath the second root of Yggdrasil — Odin pledged one eye in exchange for a draught (Vǫluspá 28-29). In Heimskringla's Ynglinga saga 4, sent with Hœnir as Æsir-hostage to the Vanir during the post-war exchange; the Vanir, finding Hœnir useless without Mímir's counsel, beheaded Mímir and sent his head back to Odin, who preserved it. Odin consults the head before Ragnarok (Vǫluspá 46; Gylfaginning 51 — 'Odin rides to Mímisbrunnr and takes counsel of Mímir for himself and his folk').
nodes.symbolism: the severed head as wisdom that survives death, the well as the source of hidden knowledge, the eye sacrificed for wisdom as the price of deep knowing, the speaking head as the oracle of the preserved past
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wise old man reduced to his essential function (the head), consciousness as pure intellect separated from the body, the patriarchal wisdom that survives even decapitation
nodes.birthCircumstances: Mímir's origins are not clearly narrated; sometimes described as a Jǫtunn, sometimes as one of the original divine beings.
nodes.deathCircumstances: Beheaded by the Vanir during the hostage-exchange that ended the Aesir-Vanir war (Ynglinga saga 4); Odin preserves the head with herbs and incantations to continue receiving counsel.
nodes.domain_source: Vǫluspá 28-29 (Mímir's well); Sigrdrífumál 14; Snorri, Gylfaginning 15; Ynglinga saga 4 (his beheading by the Vanir; Odin preserves the head); Skáldskaparmál; Heimskringla
nodes.object_source: Vǫluspá 28-29 (the well of wisdom beneath Yggdrasil); Ynglinga saga 4 (the severed head, preserved with herbs and chants by Odin)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Vǫluspá; Ynglinga saga 4 (giving counsel and bringing news from many worlds)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Ynglinga saga 4 (the severed head — Odin's continuing counselor)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Vǫluspá 28-29 (Odin's eye in the well, his daily payment for wisdom); Ynglinga saga 4 (the Aesir-Vanir hostage exchange; Mímir beheaded by the Vanir; Odin preserves the head with herbs); Vǫluspá 46 (Odin speaks with Mímir's head before Ragnarök)
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Ynglinga saga 4 (Vanir-hostage); Snorri
nodes.birthTypes_source: Snorri

nodes.name: Hermóðr
nodes.domain: bravery, the underworld journey, rescue attempts, divine messengers
nodes.object: Sleipnir (Odin's eight-legged horse, which Hermóðr borrows for the ride to Hel)
nodes.characterTrait: brave, swift, faithful — undertakes the perilous Hel-journey
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Riding-skill emphasized; 'swift' (`hvati`) and 'bold' (`prúði`) as epithets.
nodes.significantEvent: When Baldr dies, Hermóðr volunteers to ride to Hel and ransom him. Borrows Sleipnir, rides nine nights down the Helvegr through deep dark valleys, crosses the bridge Gjallarbrú (the gold-thatched bridge over the river Gjǫll, guarded by the maiden Móðguðr), leaps Sleipnir over the gates of Hel, and finds Baldr in Hel's hall. Hel agrees to release Baldr if all things weep for him. Hermóðr returns to Asgard with the message and with the ring Draupnir (which Baldr sends back to Odin) and the linen-cloak Nanna sends to Frigg.
nodes.symbolism: the journey to the underworld as the attempt to undo death, the ride on the eight-legged horse as the shamanic descent, the one who refuses to weep as the obstacle to resurrection, the failed rescue as the irreversibility of cosmic fate
nodes.neumannArchetype: the heroic son who descends to the underworld to rescue the dead brother, the masculine consciousness that attempts to reverse the work of death but fails against the tricksters final deception
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Odin and Frigg in Snorri's account.
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 49 (the Hel-ride to recover Baldr); Hyndluljóð 2; Húsdrápa (skaldic)
nodes.object_source: Gylfaginning 49 (Odin's horse Sleipnir, borrowed for the journey)

nodes.name: Hœnir
nodes.domain: silence, mystery, the Vanir hostage, creation (gave spirit to humans)
nodes.characterTrait: silent, indecisive (Ynglinga saga makes him a poor decision-maker without Mímir's counsel), giver-of-spirit
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Tall and handsome (per Snorri); a god of mysterious function. In Vǫluspá 18 he gives óðr (spirit / breath / inspiration) to the first humans.
nodes.significantEvent: With Odin and Lóðurr, creates the first humans Askr and Embla from driftwood (Vǫluspá 17-18). Goes with Mímir as Aesir hostages to the Vanir at the end of the Aesir-Vanir war (Ynglinga saga 4); his indecisiveness without Mímir's counsel causes the Vanir to behead Mímir.
nodes.symbolism: the gift of spirit to humanity, the silent god who gives the animating breath, mystery and silence as divine qualities, the hostage who is incomplete without his wise companion (Mimir)
nodes.neumannArchetype: the spirit-giver who bestows the animating consciousness on the first humans, the mysterious masculine whose gift is the breath of awareness
nodes.domain_source: Vǫluspá 17-18 (the creation of humans with Odin and Lóðurr); Ynglinga saga 4 (Hœnir as Vanir hostage); Reginsmál prose introduction

nodes.name: Móði and Magni
nodes.domain: strength, wrath, Ragnarok survival, inheritance, Thors legacy
nodes.object: Mjǫllnir (which they will inherit after Thor's death at Ragnarök, per Vafþrúðnismál 51)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Strong sons of Thor; Magni already a powerful child in Skáldskaparmál 17, where at three years old he lifts the dead Hrungnir's leg off the prone Thor.
nodes.significantEvent: In Skáldskaparmál 17, Magni at three nights old (or three winters) lifts Hrungnir's leg off the unconscious Thor — Thor remarks that his son is exceptionally strong. After Ragnarök, the two brothers inherit Mjǫllnir and Thor's possessions, surviving into the new world (Vafþrúðnismál 51; Gylfaginning 53).
nodes.symbolism: the sons who inherit the fathers weapon after the cosmic destruction, strength and wrath as the qualities that survive Ragnarok, the hammer passed to the next generation as the continuation of protective power
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine sons who inherit the patriarchal weapon (Mjolnir) after the cosmic father dies, the continuation of protective consciousness beyond the destruction of the old world
nodes.birthCircumstances: Sons of Thor; Magni is by the giantess Járnsaxa (Skáldskaparmál 17); Móði's mother is unspecified (probably Sif).

nodes.characterTrait: creator-brothers; in some traditions briefly rule and take Frigg while Odin is in exile
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Sons of Borr and Bestla; brothers of Odin. Not described in detail individually.
nodes.significantEvent: With Odin, slay Ymir and from his body shape the cosmos: flesh becomes earth, blood becomes sea, bones become mountains, teeth becomes rocks, skull becomes heaven, brain becomes clouds, hair becomes trees, eyelashes become Midgard (Gylfaginning 8). With Odin, also walk the seashore and find the driftwood pieces from which they make Askr and Embla (in the Snorri version, where Vili and Vé take the roles given to Hœnir and Lóðurr in Vǫluspá).
nodes.symbolism: the three brothers as the creative trinity, the killing of the primordial giant as the necessary destruction of the undifferentiated to create the differentiated world, the body of Ymir as the raw material of creation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the patriarchal trinity that slays the primordial uroboric being (Ymir) and creates the ordered world from its dismembered body
nodes.birthCircumstances: Sons of Borr and the giantess Bestla.
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 6-8; Ynglinga saga 3; Lokasenna 26 (the cryptic reference to Frigg lying with Odin's brothers)

nodes.name: Váli
nodes.domain: vengeance, Baldr, growth, Ragnarok survival
nodes.characterTrait: vengeance-formed, swift-growing, fierce-from-birth — born for the single purpose of avenging Baldr
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Grows to manhood in a single night — 'one night old' when he kills Hǫðr; refuses to comb his hair or wash until the deed is done (Vǫluspá 33; Baldrs draumar 11).
nodes.significantEvent: Born to Odin and the giantess Rind specifically to avenge Baldr's death. Kills Hǫðr the day after his birth, refusing to wash or comb his hair until the deed is done. Survives Ragnarok and inhabits the renewed world.
nodes.symbolism: the one-day growth as the urgency of vengeance, the son born for a single purpose as the divine instrument of retribution, vengeance as requiring a being specifically created for the task
nodes.neumannArchetype: the avenging son created by the father for the sole purpose of retribution, the masculine consciousness that grows instantly to fulfill the patriarchal demand for justice
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Odin and the giantess Rindr; born specifically to avenge Baldr.
nodes.domain_source: Vǫluspá 32-33; Baldrs Draumar 11; Snorri, Gylfaginning 30, 49
nodes.characterTrait_source: Vǫluspá 32-33; Baldrs Draumar 11
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Vǫluspá 33 (does not wash his hands nor comb his hair until he has placed Baldr's slayer on the pyre)

nodes.name: Fáfnir
nodes.domain: greed, dragons, treasure, transformation, cursed gold
nodes.object: the cursed treasure of Andvari, the ring Andvaranaut
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a dwarf who transformed into a dragon to guard his cursed treasure hoard
nodes.significantEvent: killed his father Hreidmar to take the cursed gold of Andvari, transformed into a dragon to guard the treasure, was eventually slain by the hero Sigurd on the advice of his brother Regin, Sigurd tasted Fafnirs blood and gained the ability to understand bird speech
nodes.symbolism: the transformation into a dragon as the ultimate expression of greed, the cursed gold that destroys all who possess it, the dragon-slaying hero as the liberator of hoarded wealth, the blood of the dragon as the source of hidden knowledge
nodes.neumannArchetype: the human transformed into the dragon of greed, the consciousness that becomes the very monster it sought to exploit, the hoard-guardian that must be slain by the hero
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of the dwarf Hreidmar, brother of Regin and Otr
nodes.deathCircumstances: Slain by Sigurðr at the ford-pit on Gnitaheiðr. Sigurðr digs a pit, waits in it as Fáfnir crawls over to drink, and stabs the dragon from below.
nodes.domain_source: Reginsmál; Fáfnismál; Vǫlsunga saga 13-19; Skáldskaparmál 39
nodes.object_source: Skáldskaparmál 39 (the cursed Andvari-hoard, including the ring Andvaranautr); Reginsmál (the cursed gold)
nodes.animals_source: Fáfnir is transformed into a dragon — symbolic embodiment via transformation

nodes.name: Ægir
nodes.domain: the sea, brewing, feasts, waves, storms, hospitality
nodes.object: great cauldron (the one Thor and Týr fetch from Hymir in Hymiskviða, mile-deep); his hall on Hlésey; the brewing-vat
nodes.characterTrait: hospitable to the Aesir, mighty in brewing, dwelling under the sea
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Sea-giant (Jǫtunn) of immense age; husband of Rán; father of the nine wave-maidens (the daughters of Ægir and Rán: Himinglæva, Dúfa, Blóðughadda, Hefring, Uðr, Hrǫnn, Bylgja, Dröfn, Kólga). Sometimes considered an alter-ego or peer of Njǫrðr in sea-dominion.
nodes.significantEvent: Hosts the gods at his hall for the famous feast that occasions Loki's flyting (Lokasenna). Hymiskviða describes Thor and Týr fetching the great cauldron from Hymir specifically so that Ægir can brew enough ale for the gods.
nodes.symbolism: the sea as a host who gives feasts, the great cauldron as the vessel of divine hospitality, the nine wave-daughters as the children of the ocean, the giant who serves the gods as the sea that provides for civilization
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father of the sea who hosts the gods, the oceanic masculine whose hospitality nourishes the divine order
nodes.birthCircumstances: Sea-giant of primordial age; in some genealogies, brother of Logi (fire) and Kári (wind).
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 1, 25; Skáldskaparmál (opening — Ægir's feast); Lokasenna prose (the feast at Ægir's hall); Hymiskviða (the cauldron-quest is for Ægir's brewing)

nodes.name: Borr
nodes.domain: ancestry, the divine lineage, fatherhood
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: father of Odin, an early divine ancestor
nodes.significantEvent: married the giantess Bestla and fathered Odin, Vili, and Ve, the three gods who would slay Ymir and create the world
nodes.symbolism: the divine father as the bridge between the first being (Buri) and the creator gods (Odin and brothers), the marriage of god and giantess as the union necessary for the birth of the world-creators
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father who bridges the primordial (Buri) and the creative patriarchal order (Odin)
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Buri (the first being licked from the ice by the cosmic cow Audhumla), father of Odin by the giantess Bestla

nodes.name: Nidhogg
nodes.domain: the underworld, corpses, the world tree, destruction
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a great dragon or serpent that dwells beneath the world tree Yggdrasil
nodes.significantEvent: continuously gnaws at the roots of Yggdrasil from beneath, feeds on the corpses of the dead, exchanges insults with the eagle at the top of the tree via the squirrel Ratatosk, represents the constant threat to the cosmic order from below
nodes.symbolism: the gnawing at the world trees roots as the constant undermining of cosmic order, the corpse-eater beneath the tree as death at the foundation of life, the insult exchange between dragon and eagle as the eternal conflict between the depths and the heights
nodes.neumannArchetype: the chthonic dragon that gnaws at the roots of the cosmic tree, the destructive unconscious that constantly undermines the world-axis of consciousness
nodes.domain_source: Vǫluspá 39, 66; Grímnismál 32, 35; Snorri, Gylfaginning 15-16
nodes.object_source: (gnaws at Yggdrasil's root and corpses)
nodes.animals_source: Nidhogg IS the serpent/dragon — embodiment

nodes.name: Lóðurr
nodes.domain: creation, giving warmth and blood to humans, the divine trinity of creation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Not described visually. The name's etymology and identity are contested in scholarship — some equate Lóðurr with Loki (the names are phonetically related), others with Vé (one of Odin's brothers), others as a separate figure.
nodes.significantEvent: With Odin and Hœnir, creates the first humans Askr and Embla from driftwood (Vǫluspá 17-18). Lóðurr's contribution: lá (warmth/blood) and litir góðir (good color/complexion).
nodes.symbolism: the gift of blood and warmth to humanity, the fire of life that animates the human form, the third member of the creative trinity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the warmth-giving masculine of the creative trinity, the consciousness that provides the vital heat of life
nodes.domain_source: Vǫluspá 18 (the only Eddic mention by this name — in the human-creation triad with Odin and Hœnir)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Vǫluspá 18 ('Lóðurr gave them lá ok litu góða' — warmth/blood and good color)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Vǫluspá 18; scholarly debate
nodes.significantEvent_source: Vǫluspá 17-18

nodes.name: Máni
nodes.domain: the moon, night travel, time-keeping, the lunar cycle
nodes.object: his moon-chariot; the children Bil and Hjúki whom he takes up from the well
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the personification of the moon, drives the moons chariot across the sky
nodes.significantEvent: drives the moon chariot across the sky, perpetually chased by the wolf Hati who will finally catch and devour the moon at Ragnarok
nodes.symbolism: the moon as a being chased by a wolf through the sky, the lunar cycle as a cosmic chase, the devouring of the moon at Ragnarok as the end of time, the moon-brother and sun-sister as the gendered luminaries
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine of the moon chased by the shadow-wolf, the lunar consciousness perpetually fleeing from the devouring darkness
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Mundilfari, brother of Sol (the sun)
nodes.deathCircumstances: Devoured by the wolf Hati at Ragnarök.

nodes.domain: day, light, the morning, dawn
nodes.object: his chariot drawn by the horse Skinfaxi ('Shining-Mane'), whose mane illuminates the sky
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the personification of Day, rides the horse Skinfaxi whose shining mane illuminates the world
nodes.significantEvent: rides the horse Skinfaxi across the sky each day, the light from the horses mane illuminates the world below
nodes.symbolism: the son of dawn and night as the product of their union, the shining-maned horse as the light that proceeds from the dawn, day as a rider crossing the sky
nodes.neumannArchetype: the solar son who rides light across the sky, the masculine consciousness of daylight born from the union of dawn and night
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Dellingr (Dawn) and Nott (Night)

nodes.domain: the undead, graves, haunting, restless dead, burial mounds
nodes.object: grave-mound treasure (which the draugr guards); their own swollen, blackened corpses
nodes.characterTrait: undead, restless, guarding, terrifying, strong, corpse-like
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: an undead creature that dwells in burial mounds, immensely strong, often swollen and dark in color, sometimes able to change size
nodes.significantEvent: draugar are the restless dead who guard their burial mounds and the treasure within, they can kill intruders with supernatural strength, some draugar leave their mounds to haunt the living, they can be defeated by wrestling them back into their graves
nodes.symbolism: the restless dead who cannot let go of their possessions, the burial mound as the threshold between the living and the dead, the undead warrior as the refusal to surrender to death, greed beyond the grave
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow that refuses death, the ego-consciousness that clings to its possessions even beyond the grave, the terrible father of the burial mound

nodes.domain: fate, guardian spirits, family lineage, death omens, animal doubles
nodes.animals: the animal form specific to each person
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a personal guardian spirit or alter ego, often taking animal form, that accompanies a person throughout life
nodes.significantEvent: the fylgja follows a person from birth to death, appearing in dreams as an animal whose nature reflects the persons character, seeing ones own fylgja while awake is an omen of death
nodes.symbolism: the animal double as the instinctual nature of the self, the guardian that follows through life, the death omen of seeing ones own spirit, the animal form as the reflection of character
nodes.neumannArchetype: the anima/animus as the personal guardian spirit, the animal-soul that accompanies consciousness and whose revelation means the approach of death

nodes.symbolism: luck as a transferable personal power, fortune as an inherited quality, the leaders luck as a communal resource, the lending of luck as the sharing of divine favor
nodes.neumannArchetype: the mana or numinous power that accompanies the successful ego, the accumulated fortune of consciousness that can be shared or inherited

nodes.symbolism: the guardian at the threshold of consciousness, the protective spirit perceptible at the boundary of sleep, the watcher that warns of approaching danger
nodes.neumannArchetype: the guardian of the threshold between conscious and unconscious, the protective presence at the border of awareness

nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the monstrous beings bound by the gods until Ragnarok, primarily Fenrir and Loki

nodes.symbolism: the binding of chaos as the temporary containment of destruction, the fetters that will eventually break as the inevitability of cosmic dissolution, the bound monster as the restrained but indestructible threat
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow bound beneath consciousness, the chaotic unconscious that is temporarily restrained but will eventually break free and overwhelm the ego

nodes.physicalCharacteristics: large, ugly, often stone-like creatures that dwell in mountains and wilderness, turn to stone in sunlight

nodes.neumannArchetype: the chthonic serpent-shadow that guards the treasure of the unconscious at the boundary of consciousness

nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a water spirit that inhabits rivers and lakes, can take the form of a beautiful person, a horse, or other shapes

nodes.symbolism: the water spirit as the danger of the depths, the beautiful lure of drowning, the shapeshifter of freshwater as the deceptive surface of the deep, music as the sound that draws victims to the water
nodes.neumannArchetype: the anima of the water that lures consciousness into the depths of the unconscious, the beautiful but deadly feminine of the freshwater

nodes.name: Lyngbakr
nodes.domain: the sea, enormous sea creatures, whales, the deep ocean
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a vast whale or sea creature with heather growing on its back, often confused with a small island
nodes.significantEvent: similar to the hafgufa, the lyngbakr (heather-back) is a whale-like creature so enormous that heather grows on its back, making it appear to be a small island
nodes.symbolism: the heather-backed whale as the living island, the sea creature disguised by vegetation, the depth of the ocean that mimics the surface of the land
nodes.neumannArchetype: the chthonic sea-mother whose back is mistaken for solid earth, the unconscious depth disguised by the familiar vegetation of consciousness

nodes.name: Selkolla
nodes.domain: demonic women, hauntings, decapitation, the supernatural threat
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a demonic woman, sometimes headless, who haunts and terrorizes people
nodes.significantEvent: Selkolla was a demonic female entity from Icelandic folklore who terrorized a district until she was defeated by a priest, she is associated with hauntings and supernatural menace
nodes.symbolism: the headless woman as the feminine threat without reason, the demonic haunting as the destructive anima, the priest who defeats her as the triumph of the sacred over the demonic
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible anima in her destructive aspect, the headless feminine shadow that terrorizes consciousness until exorcised by the sacred masculine

nodes.name: Germanic dragon
nodes.domain: treasure, fire-breathing, flying, the cosmic threat, hoarding
nodes.characterTrait: hoarding, fire-breathing, flying, treasure-guarding, destructive, ancient
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a great winged, fire-breathing serpent that guards treasure hoards, the supreme monster of Germanic tradition
nodes.significantEvent: the Germanic dragon is the archetypal treasure-hoarding monster, from Fafnir to the dragon of Beowulf, they guard vast hoards and devastate the land with fire, the hero must slay the dragon to liberate the treasure
nodes.symbolism: the dragon as the supreme monster of greed and hoarded wealth, fire-breathing as the destructive power of the treasure-guardian, the heros dragon-slaying as the liberation of blocked wealth and the ultimate test of courage
nodes.neumannArchetype: the uroboric monster that must be slain by the hero, the dragon-mother/father that guards the treasure of consciousness and must be overcome for individuation

nodes.name: Óðr
nodes.domain: frenzy, ecstasy, passion, wandering, Freyjas lost husband
nodes.characterTrait: frenzied, ecstatic, passionate, wandering, lost, desired
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the lost husband of Freyja, associated with frenzy and ecstatic states
nodes.significantEvent: Freyjas husband who wandered away and was lost, causing her to search for him weeping golden tears, sometimes identified with Odin, his name is related to the word for frenzy, madness, and poetic inspiration
nodes.symbolism: the lost beloved as the object of the golden tears, frenzy as the divine masculine of ecstatic states, the wandering husband as the masculine that cannot be held, the search and weeping as the feminine response to the loss of the ecstatic
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wandering animus lost to the Great Mother (Freyja), the ecstatic masculine consciousness that departs and cannot be recovered

nodes.name: Huītzilōpōchtli
nodes.domain: war, the sun, sacrifice, hummingbirds, the south, the Aztec state
nodes.characterTrait: fierce, warlike, demanding, solar, sacrificial, patriotic
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Left-Handed Hummingbird, depicted as a warrior with hummingbird feathers on his left leg, blue-painted skin, and wielding the fire serpent Xiuhcoatl
nodes.significantEvent: immediately after birth he slew his sister Coyolxauhqui and the four hundred southern stars (Centzon Huitznahua) who had attacked his mother, this battle reenacted daily as the sun defeating the moon and stars at dawn, the patron deity of Tenochtitlan and the Aztec empire, demanded human sacrifice to sustain the sun
nodes.symbolism: the hummingbird as the reborn warrior soul, the daily solar battle against the moon and stars, human sacrifice as the fuel for the sun, the warrior god who is born fighting, the left hand as the south (the direction of the sun at zenith)
nodes.neumannArchetype: the solar hero who is born from the Great Mother already armed and immediately slays the lunar-stellar siblings, the masculine sun-consciousness that must be fed with sacrificial blood to continue its battle against the darkness
nodes.birthCircumstances: born fully armed from his mother Coatlicue on Mount Coatepec after she was impregnated by a ball of feathers
nodes.deathCircumstances: When performed, typically multiple victims were sacrificed per day at any one of the numerous temples.
