nodes.name: Tláloc
nodes.domain: rain, water, agriculture, mountains, caves, lightning, fertility, the dead
nodes.object: jade, water vessels, lightning bolts, rubber balls
nodes.characterTrait: nurturing, wrathful, rain-giving, lightning-hurling, mountain-dwelling, demanding
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goggle-eyed rain god with fangs, depicted with jade ornaments and wielding lightning bolts, blue-green skin
nodes.significantEvent: rules Tlalocan (the paradise of those who die by water or lightning), presides over the third sun which was destroyed by rain of fire, demands child sacrifice to ensure rain, the mountains are his storehouses of water
nodes.symbolism: the goggle eyes as the storm-seeing gaze, jade as solidified water, the mountains as water containers, child sacrifice for rain as the terrible price of agricultural fertility, the cave as the womb of rain
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible Great Father of rain who demands child sacrifice, the masculine of the life-giving waters whose generosity requires the most terrible offering
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the oldest and most important Mesoamerican deities, predating the Aztec civilization

nodes.name: Mictlāntēcutli
nodes.domain: death, the underworld (Mictlan), bones, the dead, the lowest level
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a skeletal god with a skull face, blood-splattered bones, and owl feather headdress, lord of Mictlan (the nine-layered underworld)
nodes.significantEvent: rules Mictlan with his wife Mictecacihuatl, the dead must journey through nine layers of the underworld over four years to reach him, Quetzalcoatl descended to Mictlan to steal the bones of the previous humanity to create the current human race
nodes.symbolism: the nine layers of the underworld as the stages of dissolution, the skull face as the ultimate reality beneath all flesh, the bones as the seed of rebirth (Quetzalcoatl used them to create new humans), death as a four-year journey
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible Great Father of death and dissolution, the skeleton-consciousness of the lowest level who guards the bones from which new humanity can be created
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the primordial deities created by the dual god Ometeotl

nodes.name: Tonacatecuhtli
nodes.domain: sustenance, creation, the lord of our flesh, fertility, the first couple
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Lord of Our Sustenance, the masculine aspect of the supreme dual creator deity
nodes.significantEvent: with Tonacacihuatl created the four Tezcatlipocas and set them to create the world, the ultimate source of all sustenance and creation
nodes.symbolism: the lord of the flesh as the masculine source of all nourishment, the primordial father as the provider of sustenance, creation as the act of providing food for all beings
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father of sustenance, the patriarchal source of nourishment at the apex of the cosmos
nodes.domain_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — Tonacatecuhtli ('Lord of Sustenance') as the masculine aspect of the supreme creator-duality, dwelling in the thirteenth heaven Omeyocan; Sahagún Book 6.7
nodes.object_source: Codex Borgia 9-13 (the Tonalamatl panels) — the cosmic axis
nodes.characterTrait_source: Florentine Codex 6.7
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Codex Borgia 9 — ancient bearded creator with consort Tonacacihuatl, often appearing in the central panel of the Tonalamatl divinatory calendar
nodes.significantEvent_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — paired with Tonacacihuatl in Omeyocan ('Place of Duality'), the thirteenth and highest heaven; together they engendered the four cosmic-direction Tezcatlipoca-aspects (Black/Tezcatlipoca, Red/Xipe Totec, Blue/Huitzilopochtli, White/Quetzalcoatl). The supreme creator-pair, also called Ometeotl in their unified aspect.
nodes.birthTypes_source: Florentine Codex 6.7

nodes.name: Tezcatlipoca
nodes.domain: kingship, night, creation
nodes.object: jaguar, arrow, spear, mirror, shield, smoking knife, obsidian knife
nodes.characterTrait: dark, powerful, capricious, sorcerous, all-seeing, shape-shifting, unpredictable
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Smoking Mirror, depicted with an obsidian mirror replacing his foot (lost to the earth monster Cipactli), black-striped face, jaguar associations
nodes.significantEvent: the great rival of Quetzalcoatl, tricked and corrupted Quetzalcoatl causing his exile from Tula, transforms into a jaguar, creates and destroys one of the five suns (world ages), the lord of the night who sees all through his obsidian mirror
nodes.symbolism: the obsidian mirror as the dark instrument of self-knowledge, the jaguar as the night predator, the smoking mirror as the clouded truth, the trickster rival who corrupts the feathered serpent, the dark twin of the creator
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow of the creator, the dark masculine of the night who confronts the solar hero with his own reflection, the negative father whose obsidian mirror reveals the shadow-self
nodes.domain_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — Tezcatlipoca ('Smoking Mirror') as the supreme cosmic-deity in the older Toltec-Aztec tradition; Sahagún Book 1.3; the great Toxcatl festival
nodes.object_source: Florentine Codex; Codex Borgia — obsidian mirror (smoking mirror); macuahuitl (obsidian-bladed sword); shield; the four-direction-color pattern
nodes.animals_source: Tezcatlipoca's sacred animals: jaguar (his nahual or animal-form, ocelot); coyote
nodes.characterTrait_source: Florentine Codex 1.3, 3.1 — Tezcatlipoca as 'Night-Wind', 'Possessor of the Sky', omnipresent, capricious, both giver and taker
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Codex Borgia and Magliabechiano — depicted with black-and-yellow face stripes, obsidian mirror replacing missing foot (lost to Tlaltecuhtli); the four directional aspects: Black (north), Red/Xipe Totec (east), Blue/Huitzilopochtli (south), White/Quetzalcoatl (west)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — the Five Suns narrative (Leyenda de los Soles): Tezcatlipoca was the first sun; Quetzalcoatl knocked him from the sky with a great stone, ending the first age; he became the jaguar that devoured the first humans. Repeated cosmic conflict with Quetzalcoatl. Tricked Quetzalcoatl into drunkenness causing his exile (Toltec Tula narrative). Lost his foot to Tlaltecuhtli during the creation of the earth.

nodes.name: Xiuhtecuhtli
nodes.domain: fire, time, the calendar, turquoise, the year, the hearth, rulership
nodes.object: turquoise crown, fire serpent (Xiuhcoatl), incense bag
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Turquoise Lord, the old fire god with a turquoise crown and fire-serpent associations
nodes.significantEvent: lord of fire and time, patron of the New Fire Ceremony held every 52 years when the Aztec calendar cycle completed, the fire that burns at the center of the home and the center of the universe
nodes.symbolism: turquoise as the color of fire and time, the 52-year fire ceremony as the renewal of cosmic time, the hearth fire as the center of the domestic and cosmic orders, the old fire god as the most ancient deity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the ancient Great Father of fire and time, the oldest masculine consciousness whose flame is the center of all order
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the oldest Mesoamerican deities, identified with Huehueteotl (the Old God)
nodes.deathCircumstances: Xiuhtecuhtli was embodied in the teotecuilli, the sacrificial brazier into which sacrificial victims were cast during the New Fire ceremony.

nodes.name: Tōnatiuh
nodes.domain: the sun, the fifth sun, the current world age, movement, sacrifice
nodes.object: the solar disk, eagle headdress, sacrificial knife
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the sun god of the fifth and current world age, often depicted at the center of the Sun Stone (Calendar Stone) with his tongue as a sacrificial knife
nodes.significantEvent: the current sun (Nahui Ollin, Four Movement) who demands human sacrifice to continue his journey across the sky, without the blood of human hearts the sun will stop moving and the world will end in earthquakes
nodes.symbolism: the sun that demands sacrifice to continue moving as the Aztec justification for ritual killing, the tongue as a sacrificial knife as the suns hunger for blood, the fifth sun as the current and possibly final world age, the eagle as the solar bird
nodes.neumannArchetype: the demanding solar father who requires the sacrifice of human consciousness (hearts) to maintain his existence, the terrible sun-god whose need consumes the very beings who worship him

nodes.name: Xochipilli
nodes.domain: flowers, music, dance, love, beauty, games, fertility, homosexuality, art
nodes.characterTrait: beautiful, artistic, musical, ecstatic, flower-associated, dancing, playful
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Prince of Flowers, a beautiful young god adorned with flowers, depicted with butterfly associations and floral body paint
nodes.significantEvent: patron of art, dance, music, and homosexuality, associated with hallucinogenic mushrooms and ecstatic states, twin brother of Xochiquetzal, his festivals involved music, dance, and the consumption of psychoactive plants
nodes.symbolism: the flower as the symbol of beauty and transience, mushrooms as the door to divine ecstasy, the butterfly as the transformed soul, dance and music as the highest forms of divine worship, beauty as a masculine divine principle
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child of beauty and ecstasy, the masculine of the flower-consciousness that experiences the divine through art, dance, and altered states
nodes.birthCircumstances: associated with the solar and flower realms, the divine patron of beauty and art
nodes.domain_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — Xochipilli ('Flower Prince') as god of flowers, music, dance, art, hallucinogenic plants, male homosexual love; Sahagún Book 1.14; the famous Xochipilli sculpture (Tlalmanalco, c. 1450, now Museo Nacional)
nodes.object_source: Codex Borgia — flower-staff; flute or rattle; flowered garments
nodes.animals_source: Xochipilli's sacred animals: butterflies; flowers in general
nodes.characterTrait_source: Florentine Codex 1.14
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: The famous Xochipilli sculpture — seated cross-legged young man in a tunic of flowers; his body and pedestal carved with images of hallucinogenic plants (mushrooms, morning glory, tobacco, sinicuichi); face in ecstatic-trance expression
nodes.significantEvent_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — patron of poets, painters, and dancers; especially associated with hallucinogenic plant-use (the famous Xochipilli sculpture is sometimes called 'the Prince of Flowers' or 'the God of Ecstasy' in modern ethnobotanical analysis).

nodes.name: Centeōtl
nodes.domain: corn, maize, agriculture, sustenance, the young corn god
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the young corn god, depicted with yellow body paint and a headdress of corn ears and feathers
nodes.significantEvent: the god of maize and sustenance, represents the corn plant at all stages of growth, honored at the harvest festivals, the most important food deity in Aztec religion since corn was the staple of life
nodes.symbolism: corn as the divine body that sustains humanity, the young corn god as the eternal renewal of the staple crop, the seasonal cycle of planting and harvest as the life and death of the corn deity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child of the corn, the vegetation god whose annual death and rebirth represents the cycle of agricultural consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Tlazolteotl (earth mother) and Piltzintecuhtli

nodes.name: Ehecatl
nodes.domain: wind, breath, the morning star, creation, Quetzalcoatl
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the wind god, an aspect of Quetzalcoatl, depicted wearing a buccal (duck-bill) wind mask through which he blows the wind
nodes.significantEvent: an aspect of Quetzalcoatl as the god of wind, swept the roads clean before the rain god Tlaloc, his temples were cylindrical (to reduce wind resistance), his breath gave life to the sun and set it in motion
nodes.symbolism: the wind as the breath of the feathered serpent, the cylindrical temple as the form that lets wind pass, the sweeping clean before the rain as the preparation for fertility, breath as the force that moves the sun
nodes.neumannArchetype: the breath-consciousness of the feathered serpent, the invisible wind-masculine that animates the sun and prepares the world for rain

nodes.name: Tlāhuizcalpantēcuhtli
nodes.domain: Venus as morning star, dawn, warfare, sacrifice, the east
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Dawn Lord, the god of the morning star Venus, depicted with a star-marked face and dart-throwing weapons
nodes.significantEvent: when Quetzalcoatl sacrificed himself on the funeral pyre, he became Tlahuizcalpantecuhtli (Venus as the morning star), he shot darts of light at the new sun but was struck back and transformed, his rays were feared as dangerous at dawn
nodes.symbolism: the morning star as a warrior who attacks the sun at dawn, Venus as the dangerous light between night and day, the transformation of the feathered serpent into the attacking star, dawn as a moment of cosmic warfare
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hero (Quetzalcoatl) transformed into the attacking morning star, the masculine consciousness that challenges the sun at the threshold of day
nodes.birthCircumstances: an aspect or transformation of Quetzalcoatl/Xolotl in stellar form
nodes.deathCircumstances: Once he started burning, his ashes were lifted and various beautiful birds were sacrificed until Quetzalcoatl's spirit leaves his heart as a star and becomes a part of the sky.

nodes.name: Tecciztecatl
nodes.domain: the moon, conch shells, pride, cowardice, the failed first attempt
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Conch Shell Lord, associated with the moon, depicted with conch shell ornaments
nodes.significantEvent: was supposed to throw himself into the cosmic fire first to become the sun but hesitated out of fear, the humble Nanahuatzin jumped first and became the sun, Tecciztecatl then jumped in shame and became the dimmer moon, the gods threw a rabbit at his face to dim his brightness further
nodes.symbolism: the proud god who becomes the moon through hesitation and cowardice, the rabbit thrown at the moon as the mark of his failure, the conch shell as the spiral of descent from the intended sun to the lesser moon, pride leading to a lesser destiny
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow of the solar hero, the masculine who fails the test of sacrifice and becomes the lesser light, the cowardly consciousness that is dimmed by the rabbit of shame
nodes.birthCircumstances: He was a son of Tlaloc and Chalchiuhtlicue.
nodes.deathCircumstances: The first three suns perished by wind storms, jaguars and fiery rain respectively.

nodes.name: Ixtlilton
nodes.domain: medicine, healing, disease, feasting, children, the black-faced one
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Little Black One, depicted with black face paint, a god of medicine and healing
nodes.significantEvent: a healing deity who cured diseases and protected children, associated with feasting and entertainment, his temple contained a jar of healing black liquid, those who drank from it were cured
nodes.symbolism: the black face as the mask of the healer, the healing liquid as the medicine of the dark deity, the protection of children as the tenderness of the black-faced god, healing as coming from the dark
nodes.neumannArchetype: the dark healer, the shadow-father whose blackness contains the medicine that heals, the wisdom of healing found in the darkness

nodes.name: Centzonhuītznāhua
nodes.domain: stars, the south, the four hundred southern stars, Huitzilopochtli
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Four Hundred Southerners, gods of the southern stars
nodes.significantEvent: attacked their mother Coatlicue when she became pregnant with Huitzilopochtli, were defeated and slain by the newborn war god, became the stars of the southern sky
nodes.symbolism: the four hundred stars as the brothers defeated by the sun, the southern sky as the battlefield of the solar birth, the stellar siblings slain at dawn as the stars that vanish when the sun rises
nodes.neumannArchetype: the stellar brothers defeated by the solar hero, the collective unconscious overwhelmed by the rising sun-consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: sons of Coatlicue, brothers (and enemies) of Huitzilopochtli

nodes.name: Centzonmīmixcōa
nodes.domain: stars, the north, the four hundred cloud serpents, hunting
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Four Hundred Mimixcoa, gods of the northern stars associated with hunting
nodes.significantEvent: created as star warriors but failed to perform their duties of warfare and sacrifice, were punished and sacrificed, their sacrifice became the model for human sacrifice in Aztec religion
nodes.symbolism: the four hundred star-warriors who failed and were sacrificed as the divine model for human sacrifice, the northern stars as the punished warriors, failure in sacrifice leading to becoming the sacrifice
nodes.neumannArchetype: the stellar warriors who fail the patriarchal demand for sacrifice and become the sacrificed themselves, the unconscious punished for failing to serve consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: created by the gods as star-beings

nodes.name: Tlaltecuhtli
nodes.domain: the earth, the earth monster, creation, the surface of the earth, devouring
nodes.object: skulls, claws, mouths covering the body
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Earth Lord/Lady, depicted as a monstrous crouching figure covered in mouths, eyes, and claws at every joint, the earth as a living devouring surface
nodes.significantEvent: the gods Quetzalcoatl and Tezcatlipoca tore the earth monster in half to create the earth (upper half) and sky (lower half), but she constantly demands blood and hearts to be fed, the earthquakes are her movements of hunger
nodes.symbolism: the earth as a living hungry monster that must be fed, the surface we walk on as the skin of the devouring, the mouths at every joint as the earths insatiable appetite, creation through the violent dismemberment of the feminine earth-body
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible Great Mother as the devouring earth, the feminine body torn apart by the masculine gods to create the world, whose hunger is never satisfied
nodes.domain_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — Tlaltecuhtli ('Earth Lord') as the earth-monster from whose torn body the earth was made; Histoyre du Mechique (16th c. fragmentary source); Codex Chimalpopoca; the famous Tlaltecuhtli monolith from the Templo Mayor (rediscovered 2006)
nodes.object_source: Templo Mayor monolith iconography — claws at all four corners; great teeth-mouths at every joint
nodes.animals_source: Tlaltecuhtli's form: monstrous toad-or-crocodile-or-composite
nodes.characterTrait_source: Histoyre du Mechique; Templo Mayor iconography
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Templo Mayor monolith — clawed creature with teeth-mouths at every joint; female; in pose of childbirth (with the rain emerging); colored red and yellow
nodes.significantEvent_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — Tezcatlipoca and Quetzalcoatl found Tlaltecuhtli walking on the primordial waters; transformed into great serpents and tore her body in two, one half becoming the earth, the other the sky; Tezcatlipoca lost his foot in the process (replaced by obsidian mirror). From her hair grew trees, flowers, and herbs; her eyes wells and small caves; her mouth rivers and great caves; her shoulders mountains. She demanded human hearts in compensation for her dismemberment — establishing the cosmic-debt of human sacrifice.
nodes.birthTypes_source: Histoyre du Mechique

nodes.name: Xipe Totec
nodes.domain: spring, renewal, agriculture, flayed skin, goldsmiths, the east, regeneration
nodes.object: flayed human skin, golden attire, shield, rattle staff
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Our Lord the Flayed One, depicted wearing a suit of flayed human skin, golden body paint, associated with spring renewal
nodes.significantEvent: his worship involved the ritual wearing of flayed human skins (Tlacaxipehualiztli festival) which symbolized the earth putting on new vegetation in spring, the old skin represented the dead surface of winter, the new growth beneath represented spring
nodes.symbolism: the flayed skin as the old earth shedding its surface for spring renewal, the human skin worn as a suit as the earth putting on new vegetation, the golden god beneath the dead skin as the new growth, the most disturbing ritual as the most profound agricultural metaphor
nodes.neumannArchetype: the vegetation god whose flaying represents the earth shedding its dead surface for renewal, the masculine that puts on the skin of the sacrificed to embody the Great Mothers renewal
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the four sons of Ometeotl, associated with the east and red Tezcatlipoca
nodes.domain_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — Xipe Totec ('Our Lord, the Flayed One') as god of agricultural renewal, vegetation, springtime; Sahagún Book 1.2; the Tlacaxipehualiztli festival ('Flaying of Men') for him in March
nodes.object_source: Codex Borgia — flayed-skin garment (the central iconography — Xipe wears the skin of a flayed sacrificial victim, signifying death-renewal); rattle-staff (chicahuaztli)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Florentine Codex 1.2; the Tlacaxipehualiztli ritual texts
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Codex Borgia — depicted wearing the flayed skin of a sacrificed victim, the skin appearing as a loose-fitting suit with hands hanging at his wrists; yellow-painted body underneath; red-and-white striped face
nodes.significantEvent_source: Florentine Codex (Bernardino de Sahagún, *Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España*, 1545-1590); Codex Borgia, Borbonicus, Magliabechiano, Telleriano-Remensis; Codex Chimalpopoca (*Leyenda de los Soles*); Diego Durán, *Historia de las Indias de Nueva España*; Crónica Mexicáyotl (Tezozomoc) — Tlacaxipehualiztli festival: captives sacrificed by gladiatorial combat or arrow-shooting; their skins flayed and worn by priests for 20 days. The seasonal logic: as maize-grain sheds its husk to grow, so the new agricultural season requires the old skin's death-renewal. One of the four directional Tezcatlipocas (Red Tezcatlipoca, east).
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Florentine Codex — one of the four directional Tezcatlipocas, sons of Ometeotl
nodes.birthTypes_source: Florentine Codex

nodes.name: Piltzintecuhtli
nodes.domain: the young sun, princes, children, hallucinogenic plants, the rising sun
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Young Prince Lord, a solar deity associated with the young and rising sun
nodes.significantEvent: represents the sun as a young prince, associated with hallucinogenic plants and altered states, the patron of young nobles and princes
nodes.symbolism: the young sun as the princely rising solar force, hallucinogenic plants as the doorway to the young suns realm, youth as the quality of the rising sun, the prince as the solar heir
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child of the sun, the youthful solar consciousness in its ascending phase
nodes.birthCircumstances: a youthful solar deity, connected to Tonatiuh as the sun in its youthful phase
nodes.deathCircumstances: He was considered the father of Centeōtl, a deity who was sacrificed in order to bring forth plants.

nodes.domain: omnipresence, the supreme being, the lord of the near and the nigh, the unknowable
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Lord of the Near and the Nigh, a title for the supreme deity expressing divine omnipresence and intimacy
nodes.significantEvent: a title or concept for the supreme Aztec deity who is simultaneously near (intimate) and nigh (imminent), expressing the paradox of a transcendent god who is also intimately present in all things
nodes.symbolism: the near and the nigh as the paradox of divine omnipresence, the supreme being who is both transcendent and intimate, the philosophical expression of the divine as simultaneously far and close
nodes.neumannArchetype: the supreme consciousness that is both transcendent (far) and immanent (near), the paradox of the divine that is everywhere and nowhere

nodes.domain: disease, plague, sorcery, the jade turkey, Tezcatlipoca
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Jade Turkey, an aspect of Tezcatlipoca in turkey form, associated with disease and pestilence
nodes.significantEvent: a manifestation of Tezcatlipoca as a jade or jeweled turkey, associated with plague and disease, could bring pestilence upon those who offended him
nodes.symbolism: the jeweled turkey as the beautiful carrier of disease, the gorgeous bird that brings plague, the divine beauty that conceals pestilence, Tezcatlipocas power to send sickness through his animal form
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow of Tezcatlipoca in animal form, the beautiful unconscious (turkey) that carries the disease of the shadow

nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Radiant Star, associated with the Milky Way and the male creative stellar principle

nodes.neumannArchetype: the stellar masculine of creation, the star-consciousness that generates alongside the feminine stellar principle

nodes.name: Cipactonal
nodes.domain: the calendar, divination, the day, creation, the first man, astrology
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the first man and inventor of the tonalpohualli (260-day ritual calendar), a figure of great wisdom
nodes.significantEvent: with his wife Oxomoco created the sacred 260-day calendar (tonalpohualli) which governed all Aztec ritual and divination, the Adam-figure of Aztec mythology who also discovered medicine and agriculture
nodes.symbolism: the first man as the inventor of sacred time, the calendar as the map of fate, divination as reading the structure of time, the first couple as the founders of civilization through the calendar
nodes.neumannArchetype: the first patriarchal consciousness that structures time into the sacred calendar, the masculine that imposes order on the chaos of undifferentiated days
nodes.birthCircumstances: They bore a son named Piltzin-tecuhtli, who married a maiden, daughter of Xochiquetzal.

nodes.name: Cintēteo
nodes.domain: corn, maize deities, agriculture, the corn gods collectively
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Corn Gods, the collective maize deities who preside over all aspects of corn cultivation
nodes.significantEvent: the group of corn deities who govern all stages of maize growth, harvesting, and preparation, collectively ensuring the staple crop of Aztec civilization
nodes.symbolism: the collective corn spirits as the multiple divine aspects of the staple food, maize as requiring many divine guardians for its cultivation, the divine committee of sustenance
nodes.neumannArchetype: the collective vegetation gods of the staple crop, the multiple consciousnesses required to govern the growth of the food of civilization

nodes.name: Yacatecuhtli
nodes.domain: merchants, trade, roads, travelers, wealth, commerce
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Pointed Nose Lord, patron deity of merchants (pochteca), depicted with a pointed nose and travelers staff, carrying a merchant bundle
nodes.significantEvent: patron of the pochteca (long-distance merchants) who traveled dangerous routes carrying trade goods, merchants prayed to him for safe passage and successful trade, the cacao bean as the currency of divine commerce
nodes.symbolism: the pointed nose as the merchants ability to sniff out profitable trades, the staff as the merchants weapon and walking stick, the merchant bundle as the carried wealth, trade roads as sacred paths under divine protection
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father of trade and commerce, the masculine consciousness of the merchant road and the exchange of goods

nodes.name: Xocotl
nodes.domain: fire, fruit, the fire ceremony, the harvest of fire
nodes.object: fire, fruit (associated with the Xocotl Huetzi festival)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: associated with fire and fruit, connected to the Xocotl Huetzi (the Great Feast of the Dead/Falling of the Fruit) festival
nodes.significantEvent: associated with the Xocotl Huetzi festival in which a pole was raised with an effigy and fruit at the top, warriors competed to climb it, connected to fire ceremonies and the harvest
nodes.symbolism: the fruit at the top of the pole as the prize of the warrior-climber, fire and fruit as the harvest of divine energy, the climbing contest as the ritual competition for sacred prizes
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine of the fire-harvest, the consciousness that climbs toward the fruit of divine energy

nodes.domain: grass, agriculture, minor vegetation, the grass lord
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Grass Lord, a minor vegetation deity associated with dried grass and agricultural residue
nodes.significantEvent: a minor deity associated with dried grass and agricultural vegetation, part of the extensive Aztec pantheon of specialized agricultural deities
nodes.symbolism: dried grass as the humble remnant of the harvest, the minor vegetation deity as the divine attention to even the least aspect of agriculture
nodes.neumannArchetype: the humble vegetation consciousness of the dried grass, the smallest unit of agricultural divinity

nodes.name: Tlalocayotl
nodes.domain: rain spirits, the Tlaloque, rain helpers, mountain spirits
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the rain spirits associated with Tlaloc, the small mountain and rain deities who serve the great rain god
nodes.significantEvent: the collective rain spirits who serve Tlaloc, dwelling on mountains and pouring rain from their water jars, responsible for specific types of rain and storms
nodes.symbolism: the mountain spirits as the local servants of the rain god, the water jar as the container of rain, the mountains as the storehouses of water, the collective rain-servers as the distributed system of divine precipitation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the collective rain-servants of the Great Father of rain, the distributed consciousnesses of precipitation

nodes.name: Tlacotzontli
nodes.domain: hair, tonsure, priestly dedication, sacrifice, the hair lord
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Hair Lord, associated with ritual tonsure and the cutting of hair in priestly and sacrificial contexts
nodes.significantEvent: associated with the ritual cutting of hair in sacrificial and priestly dedication, hair as a sacred substance in Aztec religion
nodes.symbolism: hair as a sacred substance containing life force, the ritual cutting of hair as dedication to the divine, the tonsure as the mark of priestly service
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine of the sacred hair, the consciousness of ritual dedication through the cutting of the bodys most visible growth

nodes.name: Hindu deities
nodes.domain: the collective divine beings of Hinduism, the cosmic order, dharma
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the collective concept of the Hindu divine beings encompassing all deities from the supreme Brahman to local village gods
nodes.significantEvent: the Hindu deities represent one of the largest and most complex pantheons in world religion, organized in triads (Trimurti), families, avatars, and local manifestations
nodes.symbolism: the unity in multiplicity of the Hindu divine, the one supreme reality manifesting as countless deities, the cosmic order (dharma) as the organizing principle of the divine
nodes.neumannArchetype: the collective numinous of the Hindu cosmos, the infinite manifestations of the divine consciousness
nodes.domain_source: Hindu tradition — Vedas, Itihāsas, Purāṇas, Āgamas, Tantras

nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Category entry
nodes.significantEvent_source: Collective Hindu pantheon spans Vedic devas, Purāṇic Trimūrti and consorts, avatars, regional and folk deities, eternal Brahman

nodes.name: Ardhanarishvara
nodes.domain: androgyny, the union of Shiva and Parvati, divine gender unity, cosmic balance
nodes.object: trident (right/Śiva side), lotus (left/Pārvatī side); Śiva-side carries trident-drum-axe; Pārvatī-side carries lotus and mirror
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Lord Who Is Half Woman, depicted as half Shiva (male right side) and half Parvati (female left side), with one breast, half a mustache, and split attire
nodes.significantEvent: represents the inseparable unity of the masculine and feminine principles in Hindu cosmology, demonstrates that the supreme god contains both genders within one body
nodes.symbolism: the half-and-half body as the visual proof that masculine and feminine are one, the split form as the cosmic balance, the androgynous deity as the resolution of all gender duality
nodes.neumannArchetype: the uroboric unity of masculine and feminine in one body, the divine androgyne that precedes and transcends gender differentiation
nodes.birthCircumstances: Cosmic-iconic moment of complete union; not a separately-born being but a form taken by Śiva-Pārvatī to demonstrate inseparability.
nodes.object_source: Standard Ardhanārīśvara iconography (Elephanta Caves, c. 5th-8th c.); Purāṇic tradition
nodes.domain_source: Skanda Purāṇa, Maheśvara-khaṇḍa; Liṅga Purāṇa 5; Śiva Purāṇa, Pārvatī-khaṇḍa; Ardhanārīśvara-stotra (Śaṅkara)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Śaiva iconographic-theological tradition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard iconography — right side male Śiva (matted hair, third eye, ash-color, tiger-skin, trident), left side female Pārvatī (smooth hair, ornaments, sari, lotus, breast on left only)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Śiva Purāṇa, Pārvatī-khaṇḍa; Sage Bhṛgu narrative
nodes.birthTypes_source: Purāṇic tradition
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Śiva Purāṇa

nodes.name: Adityas
nodes.domain: solar deities, cosmic law, the celestial group, Vedic gods, the sun in its aspects
nodes.object: the solar disc in various aspects
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the group of solar deities, typically twelve in number, each representing the sun in a different month
nodes.significantEvent: the twelve Adityas represent the sun in each of the twelve months, they uphold cosmic order (rita) and are the guardians of law and truth, Vishnu is sometimes counted among them as the supreme Aditya
nodes.symbolism: the twelve solar aspects as the suns monthly faces, cosmic law upheld by the solar deities, the celestial group as the guardians of truth, the twelve as the complete cycle of the solar year
nodes.neumannArchetype: the twelve-fold solar masculine of cosmic law, the patriarchal sun-consciousness that upholds the world order through its monthly manifestations
nodes.birthCircumstances: sons of the goddess Aditi and the sage Kashyapa
nodes.domain_source: Rig Veda 1.89, 2.27, 8.18; Bṛhad-Āraṇyaka Upaniṣad; Mahābhārata, Ādi Parvan 65

nodes.name: Ap
nodes.domain: water, the cosmic waters, purification, the primal element, the water deities
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the deified cosmic waters, one of the Vedic elements, represented as divine feminine beings
nodes.significantEvent: the Ap or Apas are the deified waters of Vedic religion, considered among the most sacred and purifying of all elements, all rivers and bodies of water are manifestations of this divine principle
nodes.symbolism: water as the primal divine element, purification through water as the fundamental spiritual act, the cosmic waters as the feminine source of all life
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the cosmic waters, the feminine element that purifies and gives life to all consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: Agni, the god of fire, has a close association with water and is often referred to as Apām Napāt "offspring of the waters".

nodes.name: Damayanti
nodes.domain: love, beauty, devotion, fidelity, the ideal wife, the Nala and Damayanti story
nodes.characterTrait: beautiful, devoted, faithful, patient, wise, virtuous
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a princess of extraordinary beauty, the ideal of feminine devotion and fidelity
nodes.significantEvent: chose King Nala as her husband in a svayamvara (bride-choice) even though the gods themselves competed for her, remained faithful to him through his years of exile and gambling addiction, her story in the Mahabharata is one of the great love stories of Hindu mythology
nodes.symbolism: the faithful wife who chooses the human over the divine, devotion that endures through suffering and exile, the ideal of feminine constancy, the svayamvara as the free choice of love
nodes.neumannArchetype: the anima who chooses the human masculine over the divine, the faithful feminine consciousness that endures through the heros downfall
nodes.birthCircumstances: princess of the Vidarbha kingdom

nodes.symbolism: the river as the flowing divine feminine, purification through sacred water, the descent of the celestial river to earth as the gift of the gods to humanity, the confluence of rivers as the meeting of divine streams
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the flowing river, the feminine consciousness that purifies and nourishes civilization through its perpetual flow

nodes.symbolism: the Celtic divine as deeply connected to nature, the otherworld, the seasons, and the tribal order, the druids as the priestly guardians of divine knowledge
