nodes.name: The Dagda
nodes.domain: fertility, abundance, knowledge, magic, the cauldron, the club, the harp, fatherhood
nodes.object: the cauldron of plenty (Undry), the club (kills and resurrects), the harp (controls seasons)
nodes.characterTrait: generous, powerful, crude, mighty, knowledgeable, fatherly, enormous-appetited
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Good God, an enormous powerful figure with a huge appetite, carries a vast club so heavy it must be dragged on wheels, depicted as a powerful but crude father figure
nodes.significantEvent: king of the Tuatha De Danann, possesses three treasures: the cauldron that never empties, the club that kills with one end and resurrects with the other, and the harp that controls the seasons, mated with the Morrigan at Samhain to ensure victory over the Fomorians
nodes.symbolism: the cauldron of plenty as the unlimited source of nourishment, the dual club as the power over life and death, the harp of seasons as mastery of cosmic time, the enormous appetite as the hunger of the all-father
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father of the Celtic world, the crude but powerful masculine consciousness that controls sustenance (cauldron), life and death (club), and cosmic time (harp)
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the Tuatha De Danann, a leader among the Irish gods

nodes.name: Danu
nodes.domain: motherhood, water, the Tuatha De Danann, the mother goddess, rivers, the earth
nodes.characterTrait: maternal, watery, earth-associated, tribe-mothering, fertile, nurturing
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the great mother goddess of the Tuatha De Danann (the People of the Goddess Danu), associated with rivers and the earth
nodes.significantEvent: the mother of the Tuatha De Danann, the divine race that ruled Ireland before the coming of the Milesians, her name may be connected to the Danube river, she represents the primordial maternal principle of Celtic religion
nodes.symbolism: the mother goddess whose name defines her children (the Tuatha De Danann), rivers as the flowing body of the divine mother, the earth as the maternal body from which the divine race springs
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of the Celtic divine race, the feminine earth-and-water consciousness from which the gods themselves are born
nodes.birthCircumstances: the primordial mother goddess of the Irish pantheon

nodes.name: Lugh
nodes.domain: light, craftsmanship, war, kingship, many skills, the harvest, the sun
nodes.characterTrait: many-skilled, luminous, young, kingly, masterful, triumphant
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Shining One, the many-skilled god (Samildanach), young, handsome, and radiant
nodes.significantEvent: arrived at the court of Nuada and proved he was master of every skill, killed his grandfather Balor of the Evil Eye with a sling-stone through his deadly eye at the Second Battle of Mag Tuired, became king of the Tuatha De Danann, the harvest festival Lughnasadh is named after him
nodes.symbolism: the many-skilled one as the complete human, the young god who kills his own grandfather as the overthrow of the old destructive order, the sling-stone through the evil eye as the precision that defeats malice, the harvest festival as the gods gift of abundance
nodes.neumannArchetype: the solar hero who slays the terrible grandfather (Balor), the young luminous consciousness that overcomes the destructive eye of the devouring old king
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Cian and Ethniu, grandson of Balor of the Evil Eye

nodes.name: Nuada
nodes.domain: kingship, war, justice, sovereignty, the silver hand
nodes.object: the Sword of Light (Claíomh Solais), silver prosthetic arm
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the king of the Tuatha De Danann who lost his hand in battle and had it replaced with a silver prosthetic
nodes.significantEvent: lost his right hand fighting Sreng at the First Battle of Mag Tuired, was forced to abdicate because a blemished king could not rule, the physician god Dian Cecht made him a silver hand (hence Nuada Airgetlam, Nuada of the Silver Hand), later restored to the kingship
nodes.symbolism: the lost hand as the price of sovereignty, the silver replacement as the artificial wholeness of the wounded king, the blemished king who cannot rule as the Celtic requirement for perfection in the ruler
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wounded king who loses his creative hand and must be healed or replaced, the patriarchal sovereignty that requires physical wholeness
nodes.birthCircumstances: first king of the Tuatha De Danann

nodes.name: Brigid
nodes.domain: poetry, healing, smithcraft, fire, spring, Imbolc, the hearth
nodes.characterTrait: creative, healing, fiery, triple-aspected, poetic, spring-bringing
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a triple goddess of poetry, healing, and smithcraft, later syncretized with Saint Brigid of Kildare
nodes.significantEvent: a triple goddess presiding over poetry, healing, and smithcraft, her sacred fire at Kildare was tended for centuries, later syncretized with the Christian Saint Brigid, her festival Imbolc marks the beginning of spring
nodes.symbolism: the triple goddess as the three creative arts (poetry, healing, smithcraft), the sacred fire as the flame of inspiration and craft, the spring festival as the return of the creative fire, the seamless transition from goddess to saint
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of the three creative fires, the feminine of inspiration (poetry), restoration (healing), and transformation (smithcraft)
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the Dagda

nodes.name: Cernunnos
nodes.domain: animals, forests, fertility, wealth, the underworld, stags, serpents
nodes.characterTrait: antlered, forest-dwelling, wealthy, fertile, lord-of-animals, mysterious
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Horned One, depicted with stag antlers, seated cross-legged, holding a torc and a ram-horned serpent, surrounded by animals
nodes.significantEvent: known primarily from the Gundestrup Cauldron and Pillar of the Boatmen in Paris, worshipped across Celtic Gaul, the lord of animals and the wild, associated with wealth and fertility, his antlers connect him to the forest and the stag
nodes.symbolism: the antlers as the crown of the forest king, the cross-legged posture as meditation or dominion over the earth, the ram-horned serpent as the chthonic power, the torc as wealth and sovereignty, the lord of animals as the master of the wild
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father of the wild, the antlered masculine consciousness that sits between the civilized and the animal, master of the instinctual world

nodes.name: Manannán mac Lir
nodes.domain: the sea, the otherworld, weather, mists, trade, magic, the Isle of Man
nodes.object: the crane-skin bag, the ship that sails itself, the cloak of mists
nodes.characterTrait: sea-ruling, misty, otherworldly, magical, shape-shifting, trickster
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the god of the sea and the otherworld, a powerful magician associated with mists, weather, and the sea
nodes.significantEvent: rules the otherworldly island realm of Tir na nOg and the sea around Ireland, possesses magical items including the crane-skin bag of treasures and the ship that steers itself, associated with the Isle of Man (named after him)
nodes.symbolism: the misty sea as the boundary of the otherworld, the self-steering ship as the divine vessel, the crane-skin bag as the container of magical treasures, the sea god as the ruler of the liminal space between worlds
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father of the oceanic otherworld, the masculine consciousness that rules the liminal sea between the known world and the mysterious beyond
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Lir, the sea god

nodes.name: Badb
nodes.domain: war, death, crows, the battlefield, prophecy, the Morrigan
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the war goddess in crow form, one of the three aspects of the Morrigan, associated with the fury and carnage of battle
nodes.significantEvent: appears over battlefields in the form of a crow or raven, her shrieking drives warriors to frenzy or terror, she washes the armor of those about to die at the ford
nodes.symbolism: the crow over the battlefield as the feminine face of war death, the shriek as the voice of battle-frenzy, the washing at the ford as the omen of death, the triple war goddess as the three aspects of combat violence
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible Great Mother of the battlefield, the feminine of death that appears as the carrion bird over the slain
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the three sisters of the Morrigan (with Macha and Nemain), daughter of Ernmas

nodes.name: Macha
nodes.domain: war, sovereignty, horses, fertility, death, battle frenzy, the Morrigan
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: war goddess and sovereignty goddess, one of the three aspects of the Morrigan, associated with horses and kingship
nodes.significantEvent: cursed the men of Ulster with labor pains when they forced her to race while pregnant (the Curse of Macha), their weakness at the time of Ulsters greatest need is the consequence, gave her name to Emain Macha (Navan Fort)
nodes.symbolism: the pregnant goddess forced to race as the violation of the divine feminine, the curse upon the warriors as the consequence of disrespecting the goddess, sovereignty as a feminine divine quality that punishes those who abuse it
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of sovereignty and horses, the feminine whose violation leads to the weakness of the patriarchal warriors
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the three sisters of the Morrigan (with Badb and Nemain), daughter of Ernmas

nodes.name: Nemain
nodes.domain: war, frenzy, panic, the Morrigan, battle madness, confusion
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the war goddess of battle frenzy and panic, one of the three aspects of the Morrigan
nodes.significantEvent: induces panic, frenzy, and confusion among enemy warriors on the battlefield, her name means frenzy or battle fury, her shriek alone could kill warriors or drive them mad with terror
nodes.symbolism: battle frenzy as a divine feminine gift or curse, the shriek that kills as the weaponized voice, panic as the feminine weapon on the battlefield, the madness of war as a goddess
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible feminine of battle madness, the Great Mother in her aspect of the frenzy that dissolves rational consciousness on the battlefield
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the three sisters of the Morrigan (with Badb and Macha), daughter of Ernmas

nodes.name: Aengus
nodes.domain: love, youth, poetry, dreams, beauty, music, the Otherworld
nodes.characterTrait: youthful, beautiful, poetic, dreaming, loving, musical
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Young Son, the god of love, youth, and poetic inspiration, eternally young and beautiful
nodes.significantEvent: fell in love with a woman he saw in a dream and searched all Ireland for her, known as Oengus of the Brugh (Newgrange), his four bright birds are his kisses made visible, wooed and won the swan-maiden Caer Ibormeith
nodes.symbolism: the dream of the beloved as the origin of the quest for love, the four birds as visible kisses, the eternal youth of love, Newgrange as the dwelling of the young god of love
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child of love, the eternally youthful masculine consciousness that seeks the anima through dreams
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of the Dagda and Boann

nodes.name: Balor
nodes.domain: destruction, the evil eye, the Fomorians, giants, tyranny, darkness
nodes.object: the Evil Eye (one eye that kills all it sees when opened)
nodes.characterTrait: tyrannical, destructive, giant, evil-eyed, oppressive, powerful
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the king of the Fomorians, a giant with one enormous eye that kills everything it looks upon, so heavy it takes four men to lift the eyelid
nodes.significantEvent: prophesied to be killed by his own grandson, tried to prevent this by imprisoning his daughter Ethniu, but she bore Lugh who fulfilled the prophecy by killing Balor with a sling-stone through the Evil Eye at the Second Battle of Mag Tuired
nodes.symbolism: the Evil Eye as the gaze of destruction that kills all it sees, the prophecy of the grandsons vengeance as the inevitable overthrow of tyranny, the sling-stone through the eye as the precise strike that defeats overwhelming evil, the old tyrant killed by the young hero
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible Great Father who must be slain by his own grandson (the hero), the devouring eye of the patriarchal tyrant overcome by the young solar consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: king of the Fomorians, the destructive giant race

nodes.name: Ernmas
nodes.domain: motherhood, the Tuatha De Danann, the mother of the triple war goddesses
nodes.characterTrait: maternal, divine-mothering, ancestral, Tuatha De Danann
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: mother of the three war goddesses (Badb, Macha, and Nemain/the Morrigan)
nodes.significantEvent: mother of the triple war goddesses Badb, Macha, and Nemain (the Morrigan), her mothering of the war goddesses connects warfare to the maternal divine
nodes.symbolism: the mother of the war goddesses as the feminine source of battle-fury, the maternal origin of the triple death-goddess
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother who gives birth to the triple terrible feminine of war, the maternal origin of the death-dealing anima
nodes.birthCircumstances: a mother goddess of the Tuatha De Danann

nodes.name: Bres
nodes.domain: kingship, tyranny, the Fomorians, half-breeds, agriculture, oppression
nodes.characterTrait: tyrannical, stingy, beautiful, oppressive, half-Fomorian, miserly
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Beautiful, a handsome but tyrannical king, half Tuatha De Danann and half Fomorian
nodes.significantEvent: became king of the Tuatha De Danann when Nuada lost his hand, but ruled as a tyrant and forced the gods to do menial labor, his miserliness and oppression led to the first satire ever composed in Ireland (by Cairbre the poet), eventually deposed and the Tuatha De Danann restored
nodes.symbolism: the beautiful tyrant as the deceptive appearance of oppression, the half-breed king as the compromise that leads to tyranny, the first satire as the power of the poetic word against unjust rule
nodes.neumannArchetype: the false king whose beauty conceals tyranny, the shadow-ruler who oppresses the divine order until overthrown by the legitimate sovereign
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Elatha (a Fomorian king) and Eri (of the Tuatha De Danann)

nodes.name: Cú Chulainn
nodes.domain: heroism, war, the Hound of Culann, Ulster, martial arts, rage, sacrifice
nodes.object: the Gae Bolga (barbed spear), chariot, sword
nodes.animals: hound, horse (Liath Macha and Dub Sainglend)
nodes.characterTrait: heroic, rage-prone, youthful, loyal, doomed, warp-spasming, semi-divine
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Hound of Culann, the greatest warrior of the Ulster Cycle, undergoes a terrifying warp spasm (riastrad) in battle where his body contorts monstrously
nodes.significantEvent: killed the smith Culanns guard dog as a child and took its place as guardian (hence Cu Chulainn), single-handedly defended Ulster against the armies of Connacht during the Tain Bo Cuailnge while the Ulster warriors lay under Machas curse, killed his own son Connla unknowingly, died standing up tied to a stone
nodes.symbolism: the warp spasm as the berserker transformation that makes the hero monstrous, the hound as the guardian nature, killing ones own son as the tragedy of the warrior, dying standing up as the refusal to surrender even in death
nodes.neumannArchetype: the supreme hero whose battle-fury transforms him into a monster, the masculine warrior-consciousness that becomes the very thing it fights through the excess of its own rage
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of the god Lugh and Deichtine, originally named Setanta

nodes.name: El
nodes.domain: creation, fatherhood, kingship of the divine council, ageless wisdom, decree-giving, the source of the Two Rivers, the mountain Lel
nodes.object: throne, divine staff, the seat of the divine council; his tent at the source of the Two Rivers (Mount Lel)
nodes.characterTrait: aged, white-bearded, kindly (his epithet `dpʾid` 'compassionate'), wise, council-presiding, sometimes ineffectual, occasionally drunken (KTU 1.114), occasionally lustful (KTU 1.23)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Aged, white-bearded patriarch (`ʾab šnm` 'father of years'); enthroned in his tent at the source of the Two Rivers; bull-horned in iconography. The El stele from Ugarit (the seated bearded god, RS 8.295 / Aleppo Museum) is the canonical image.
nodes.significantEvent: Heads the divine assembly (`pḫr ʾilm`). Grants kingship to Yam in the Baal Cycle's opening (KTU 1.1-1.2), but ultimately approves Baal's palace after Athirat's intercession (KTU 1.4 IV-V). Mates with two human women in the Goodly-Gods liturgy, fathering Shahar and Shalim (KTU 1.23). Becomes drunk at his banquet in the marzeah text (KTU 1.114). Promises Kirta a wife and royal dynasty after Kirta's wife and family die (KTU 1.14).
nodes.symbolism: the bull as the supreme patriarchal symbol of strength and fertility, the mountain at the source of rivers as the cosmic center, the divine council as the assembly of the gods, the aged father who rules through wisdom rather than force
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father of the Canaanite cosmos, the aged patriarchal consciousness who rules through compassion and wisdom from the cosmic mountain
nodes.domain_source: KTU 1.4 IV 41-end (El's tent at the source of the Two Rivers); KTU 1.6 I (El laments Baal's death and chooses Athtar as successor); KTU 1.14 I-VI (Kirta Epic — El's promise to Kirta); KTU 1.23 line 52 (El's mating with two women); KTU 1.114 (El's drunkenness at his marzeah); KTU 1.47 = 1.118 (Ugarit pantheon list — El at the head)
nodes.object_source: KTU 1.2 I 21-22 (his throne); KTU 1.4 IV 21-26 (his tent at the convergence of the two oceans); KTU 1.6 I 32-38 (the Mountain Lel)
nodes.animals_source: His standard epithet is `ṯr ʾil` 'Bull El' — symbolic embodiment, not companion-mount. KTU 1.4 IV 39, 1.6 IV 26 et al.
nodes.characterTrait_source: KTU 1.4 II-V (his patient council-presiding); KTU 1.6 I (lamenting Baal); KTU 1.14 (compassion to Kirta); KTU 1.23 (sexual potency); KTU 1.114 (drunkenness)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: KTU 1.2 III 5 (`ʾab šnm`); the El stele (RS 8.295); standard Ugaritic-Canaanite iconography of the seated bearded high god
nodes.significantEvent_source: KTU 1.1-1.6 (Baal Cycle); KTU 1.14-1.16 (Kirta Epic); KTU 1.17-1.19 (Aqhat Epic); KTU 1.23 (Goodly Gods); KTU 1.114 (El's drunkenness)

nodes.name: Baal
nodes.domain: storms, rain, thunder, fertility, kingship, battle, the cycle of life and death, Mount Saphon
nodes.object: thunderbolt, mace (Yagrushu and Ayyamur), spear, cedar palace
nodes.characterTrait: warlike, storm-commanding, fertile, kingly, dying-and-rising, wrathful
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Storm God, depicted as a young vigorous warrior wielding a thunderbolt and mace, wearing a horned helmet
nodes.significantEvent: defeated the sea god Yam to establish his kingship, built a palace on Mount Saphon, was swallowed by the death god Mot and descended to the underworld, later revived to resume his struggle with death, the eternal cycle of his death and resurrection reflects the seasons
nodes.symbolism: the storm as the life-giving masculine power, the thunderbolt as the weapon of fertility, the death and resurrection as the seasonal cycle, the battle with Yam (sea) and Mot (death) as the eternal struggle between order and chaos
nodes.neumannArchetype: the dying and rising young god who battles the forces of chaos (sea) and death, the masculine consciousness that must descend into the underworld and return to maintain the cosmic order
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of El and Asherah (or son of Dagon in some traditions)
nodes.deathCircumstances: Swallowed by the death-god Mot (KTU 1.5 vi 8-25). Body recovered, mourned, and buried on Mount Saphon by his sister Anat, who then kills Mot in revenge. El dreams that Baal lives; the heavens rain oil and the wadis run with honey, signalling his return.
nodes.domain_source: KTU 1.4 v 6-9, vii 25-37 (storms, rain); KTU 1.6 iii 4-7 (fertility cycle); KTU 1.2 iv 32-34 (kingship); KTU 1.3 iii 28-31 (Saphon — cosmic mountain seat); KTU 1.5 vi - 1.6 vi (death-and-resurrection cycle)
nodes.object_source: KTU 1.4 vii 28-37 (lightning); KTU 1.2 iv 11-25 (the two clubs Yagrushu 'Driver' and Ayyamur 'All-Driver' forged by Kothar-wa-Khasis); Baal-au-foudre stele from Ras Shamra (spear, c. 14th c. BCE); KTU 1.4 v 18 - vi 9 (cedar palace on Saphon)
nodes.animals_source: The bull is canonical for Baal-Hadad. KTU 1.5 v 17-22 (Baal mates with a heifer, debated reading); his epithet aliyn 'mighty' parallels bull-iconography across NW Semitic. Iconography: the seated-bull representations. NOTE: 'Lion' removed — primarily Anat's animal (KTU 1.3 ii); Baal's lion association is weaker.
nodes.deathCircumstances_source: KTU 1.5 vi 8-25 (death); KTU 1.6 ii 26-37 (Anat's recovery and burial); KTU 1.6 iii 1-9 (El's dream of resurrection)
nodes.significantEvent_source: KTU 1.2 iv 7-32 (defeat of Yam); KTU 1.4 v 18 - vi 35 (palace on Saphon); KTU 1.5 ii 6-20, vi 8-25 (death by Mot); KTU 1.6 ii 26 - vi 34 (revival and continued struggle)
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: KTU 1.5 vi 24, 1.6 vi 56-58 (bn dgn, son of Dagan); KTU 1.4 iv 47 (El called father in some passages — see edge-tension note)
nodes.characterTrait_source: KTU 1.4 V-VII (Baal's pride upon receiving palace); KTU 1.5 (Baal's bravado and demise); KTU 1.6 V-VI (Baal's combat with Mot)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: The Baal stele from Ugarit (Louvre AO 15775, 14th c. BCE) — young vigorous warrior wielding mace and spear, horned crown; KTU 1.4 V (Baal's palace iconography)
nodes.eventTypes_source: KTU 1.1-1.6 (the Baal Cycle): cosmic battle, palace-building, descent to underworld, death-and-resurrection
nodes.birthTypes_source: KTU 1.5 VI (Baal as son of Dagan); KTU 1.4 V-VII; standard Ugaritic theology
nodes.deathTypes_source: KTU 1.5 VI 8-25 (Baal swallowed by Mot); KTU 1.6 (Baal's recovery)

nodes.name: Anat
nodes.domain: war, the hunt, fertility, virgin-warrior status (her epithet `btlt ʿnt`), violent passion, devotion to Baal, the marshes
nodes.object: bow (which she desires from Aqhat in KTU 1.17-1.18); spear, sword, mace; her wings (she flies between heaven and the marshes); the chariot she rides
nodes.animals: heifer (her form when she mates with Baal in KTU 1.10-1.11)
nodes.characterTrait: violent, blood-soaked, passionate, devoted to Baal, virginal-yet-sexual (her epithet `btlt` 'maiden'), implacable, vengeful (Aqhat Epic), grieving (Baal Cycle)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Young warrior goddess; armed; winged in some iconography; depicted with weapons. The Anat figurines from Ugarit show a frontal-facing armed female with horned crown.
nodes.significantEvent: In the Baal Cycle: Anat massacres Baal's enemies (KTU 1.3 II — wading in blood); intercedes for Baal's palace (KTU 1.3 IV-V); upon Baal's death, finds, mourns, and buries his body (KTU 1.5 VI - 1.6 I); confronts and slays Mot (KTU 1.6 II — splitting him with a sword, winnowing him with a sieve, grinding him with a mill, scattering his remnants for the birds). In the Aqhat Epic: covets Aqhat's bow, offers him gold and immortality in exchange; rebuffed, contrives his death through Yatpan; weeps over his death and joins his sister Pughat in seeking justice.
nodes.symbolism: the virgin warrior goddess who wades in blood as the paradox of sexuality and violence, the defeat of death through agricultural processing (grinding like grain), the devoted sister who rescues the dead brother, the feminine of both love and slaughter
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible Great Mother as the virgin warrior, the feminine that destroys death itself through the violence of agricultural processing, the anima that is simultaneously virginal and drenched in blood
nodes.birthCircumstances: Daughter of El. Sister-consort of Baal. Standard Ugaritic theology.
nodes.domain_source: KTU 1.3 II (Anat's massacre — wading in blood); KTU 1.3 III-IV (Anat's hunt); KTU 1.5 VI - 1.6 II (Anat's mourning and slaying of Mot); KTU 1.18-1.19 (the Aqhat Epic — Anat covets Aqhat's bow and contrives his death); pantheon list KTU 1.47 / 1.118
nodes.object_source: KTU 1.17 VI 16-50 (her offer to Aqhat for the bow); KTU 1.3 II 5-16 (her weapons in the massacre); KTU 1.13 (her flight)
nodes.animals_source: KTU 1.10-1.11 (the so-called 'Baal-Anat Cycle' — Anat in heifer-form mates with Baal; the resulting calf-bull is born). Symbolic embodiment via shapeshifting.
nodes.characterTrait_source: KTU 1.3 II (the massacre — 'her liver swelled with laughter, her heart filled with joy, Anat's liver with triumph as she waded knee-deep in soldiers' blood'); KTU 1.5 VI 11-25 (mourning Baal); KTU 1.6 II 30-37 (slaying Mot); KTU 1.18-1.19 (vengeance against Aqhat)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Ugaritic iconography (Anat figurines and reliefs); KTU 1.3 II (her blood-spattered post-battle washing — implies physical embodiment of warrior-goddess type); standard Late Bronze Age iconography
nodes.significantEvent_source: KTU 1.3 II-V (Baal Cycle, Anat's massacre and intercession); KTU 1.5 VI - 1.6 II (mourning Baal, killing Mot); KTU 1.17-1.19 (Aqhat Epic)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Standard Ugaritic theology — daughter of El
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: KTU 1.3, 1.6 passim; pantheon list KTU 1.47 / 1.118

nodes.name: Kothar-wa-Khasis
nodes.domain: craftsmanship, magic-incantation, the forging of divine weapons, building, music — his name means 'Skilful-and-Wise' or 'Adroit-and-Perceptive'
nodes.object: his forge and bellows; his crafting tools; the magical weapons he forges (Yagrushu and Ayyamur for Baal); the palace materials (cedar, gold, lapis); the bow he forges for Aqhat
nodes.characterTrait: skilful, adroit, magical, generative, residing far away (his abodes Memphis/Hekupta and Caphtor/Crete — the West and the South)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Craftsman-god in standard divine garb; iconographic depictions are sparse. Resides at Memphis (Egypt) and Caphtor (Crete) — reflecting Late Bronze Age cultural debt to Egyptian and Aegean craft traditions.
nodes.significantEvent: Forges Baal's twin maces (Yagrushu 'Driver' and Ayyamur 'Chaser') with which Baal defeats Yam (KTU 1.2 IV 11-26). Builds Baal's palace on Mount Saphon, debating with Baal whether to install a window (KTU 1.4 V-VII). Forges the magnificent bow that Aqhat receives — which Anat then covets, leading to Aqhat's death (KTU 1.17 V).
nodes.symbolism: the divine craftsman as the maker of both weapons and palaces, the magical maces as the instruments of cosmic order, the builder-god as the one who gives form to divine power
nodes.neumannArchetype: the patriarchal craftsman-consciousness that gives form and weapon to the divine order, the masculine of skilled creation
nodes.domain_source: KTU 1.1 III 1-25 (his summoning); KTU 1.2 IV 7-32 (forging Yagrushu and Ayyamur for Baal); KTU 1.4 V-VII (building Baal's palace); KTU 1.17 V (forging Aqhat's bow); KTU 1.100 (his role in the snakebite incantation)
nodes.object_source: KTU 1.2 IV (Baal's weapons); KTU 1.4 V-VII (the palace); KTU 1.17 V (Aqhat's bow); KTU 1.4 I 23-40 (his forge)
nodes.characterTrait_source: KTU 1.1 III 17-21 ('his throne is at Hekupta — Memphis — the place of his crafting; his abode at Crete — Caphtor — the throne where he sits'); KTU 1.4 V
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: KTU 1.1 III 17-21 (his abodes)
nodes.significantEvent_source: KTU 1.2 IV; 1.4 V-VII; 1.17 V

nodes.name: Dagon
nodes.domain: grain, agriculture, fatherhood of Baal — Akkadian/Eblaite Dagan, Ugaritic Dagan, Philistine Dagon
nodes.characterTrait: ancient, agriculture-associated, paternal in relation to Baal
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: In the Hebrew Bible (1 Samuel 5:4), the Philistine Dagon-statue at Ashdod has hands and head broken off when fallen before the Ark — implying a humanoid form. The popular 'fish-tailed' interpretation (medieval Jewish commentators reading Hebrew *dāg* 'fish') is etymologically unsupported — the name relates to grain (*dagan*) not fish.
nodes.significantEvent: Father of Baal in Ugaritic theology (KTU 1.5 VI 23-24, 1.6 VI 51, repeatedly). Major god in the Eblaite pantheon (Dagan of Tuttul). In the Hebrew Bible, the Philistine god whose statue falls before the Ark (1 Samuel 5) and at whose temple Samson dies (Judges 16:23-30).
nodes.symbolism: grain as the divine body of the earth-god, the deep as the source of agricultural fertility, the ancient grain deity as the oldest layer of Canaanite worship
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father of grain, the ancient masculine of agricultural fertility from the deep earth
nodes.domain_source: KTU 1.5 VI 23-24 (Baal as 'son of Dagan' explicit); pantheon list KTU 1.47 / 1.118; the Eblaite god-list (Dagan as a major early-second-millennium figure); 1 Samuel 5:1-7 (Philistine Dagon at Ashdod); Judges 16:23 (Philistine Dagon at Gaza)
nodes.characterTrait_source: KTU 1.5 VI 23-24; Eblaite god-list; 1 Samuel 5
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: 1 Samuel 5:4 (the broken statue); Wyatt 2002, Religious Texts from Ugarit; the Ugaritic root dgn = grain, not fish
nodes.significantEvent_source: KTU 1.5 VI 23-24, 1.6 VI 51; Eblaite god-list; 1 Samuel 5; Judges 16

nodes.name: Shapash
nodes.domain: the sun, illumination, the divine messenger between heaven and the underworld, justice — `nrt ʾilm špš` 'the luminary of the gods, Shapash'
nodes.object: her chariot or solar disc; she 'rises' and 'sets' across the cosmos and traverses the underworld at night (cf. Mesopotamian Shamash)
nodes.characterTrait: all-seeing, mediating, oracular, traveler-protector, illuminating, just
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Solar goddess; not depicted iconographically in detailed Ugaritic art (the sun is typically a winged disc emblem). Her name means 'sun' (śapšu/špš).
nodes.significantEvent: In the Baal Cycle, she searches for the missing Baal (KTU 1.6 I 8-18); witnesses the descent of Anat with Baal's body to Mount Saphon for burial; mediates between Mot and Baal in the final confrontation, warning Mot that El no longer supports him (KTU 1.6 VI 22-29). In KTU 1.100, the anti-snake-bite incantation, she travels among the gods on the petitioner's behalf.
nodes.symbolism: the feminine sun as the all-seeing witness, the nightly journey through the underworld as the suns dark passage, the lamp of the gods as the illumination of truth, justice as the product of the all-seeing solar eye
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother as the sun, the feminine solar consciousness that sees all and reveals truth through her all-illuminating light
nodes.birthCircumstances: Daughter of El.
nodes.domain_source: KTU 1.6 I 8-18 (Shapash searches for Baal); KTU 1.6 VI (her oracle to Mot warning him to yield); KTU 1.100 (the anti-snake-bite incantation, where Shapash mediates among the gods); pantheon list KTU 1.47 / 1.118
nodes.object_source: KTU 1.6 (her movements); standard Late Bronze Age solar iconography
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard West-Semitic solar iconography; Ugaritic onomastic evidence
nodes.birthTypes_source: Standard Ugaritic theology — daughter of El
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Pantheon list KTU 1.47 / 1.118

nodes.name: Resheph
nodes.domain: plague, war, fire, the burning arrow, the divine messenger of death, military ferocity — `ršp` 'flame, plague-arrow'
nodes.object: bow and arrows (his plague-shafts); shield; sometimes mace and lightning
nodes.characterTrait: warlike, plague-bringing, fierce, swift, cognate of Mesopotamian Nergal
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Armed warrior god; horned crown often surmounted by a gazelle; raised arm wielding mace or arrow; standing pose. Late Bronze Age Egyptian-Ugaritic iconography is the canonical type (Megiddo, Ras Shamra, and Egyptian New Kingdom stelae).
nodes.significantEvent: In Kirta Epic (KTU 1.14 I 18-21), Resheph kills a fifth of Kirta's family in a plague. In Ugaritic and Egyptian New Kingdom contexts, invoked as a warrior-god. Cognate of Mesopotamian Nergal (in the Akkadian Ugarit god-list explicit). In Hebrew Bible, the plague-personification accompanying YHWH (Habakkuk 3:5) — though demoted to common-noun status in many other passages.
nodes.symbolism: plague as a divine weapon, the god who sends and cures disease, lightning as the bolt of divine wrath, the warrior-pestilence connection as the dual destruction of war and disease
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible Great Father of plague and war, the masculine consciousness that destroys through both weapons and disease
nodes.domain_source: KTU 1.14 I 18-21 (Resheph kills a fifth of Kirta's family in plague); KTU 1.78 (astronomical text linking Resheph to Mars); pantheon list KTU 1.47 / 1.118; the Akkadian Ugaritic god-list links Resheph with Nergal; Habakkuk 3:5 (Resheph as YHWH's plague-attendant); Deuteronomy 32:24 (Resheph as 'fiery shafts'); the Egyptian New Kingdom adoption of Resheph as a war-god (Ramesside period)
nodes.object_source: Egyptian New Kingdom Resheph stelae (the standard armed-warrior pose); Habakkuk 3:5
nodes.animals_source: Resheph's standard Egyptian-period iconography includes a gazelle on his horned crown — symbolic embodiment-emblem (reproductively-symbolic counter to his death-aspect)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Habakkuk 3:5; Egyptian Resheph stelae; Ugaritic Akkadian god-list (Resheph = Nergal)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Late Bronze Age Resheph stelae (Egyptian and Levantine); the Megiddo Resheph
nodes.significantEvent_source: KTU 1.14 I 18-21; KTU 1.78; Akkadian Ugarit god-list; Habakkuk 3:5

nodes.name: Moloch
nodes.domain: contested. The Hebrew Bible references *mōlek* / *mlk* in contexts of child-sacrifice (especially Leviticus 18:21, 20:2-5; 2 Kings 23:10; Jeremiah 32:35). The contested question is whether Moloch is (a) the proper name of a deity (the standard older interpretation, supporting the existence of a child-sacrifice cult to a god named Moloch), or (b) the name of a sacrificial offering — *mōlek* / *molk* as a Punic technical term for 'offering' attested at Carthage in the Punic *molk* inscriptions (Eissfeldt 1935). Heider 1985 and Day 1989 argue against Eissfeldt; the issue remains unsettled.
nodes.characterTrait: contested as a deity; if a deity, child-sacrifice-receiving, fearsome, royal-titled (the name *mlk* = 'king')
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Diodorus Siculus 20.14 describes a bronze image of Cronos (Carthaginian Baal-Hammon) at Carthage with downward-sloping hands into which children were placed and tipped into a fire below — this image has been popularly conflated with Moloch but is properly Baal-Hammon. No clear Moloch-iconography exists from primary sources.
nodes.significantEvent: Hebrew Bible polemic associates Moloch-worship with child-sacrifice in the Hinnom Valley (the Topheth of Jeremiah 7:31-32, 19:6, 32:35). Josiah's reform reportedly defiles the Topheth (2 Kings 23:10). The Punic-Carthaginian molk-sacrifice inscriptions document a real child-sacrifice rite at Carthage (Eissfeldt's reading).
nodes.symbolism: the burning of children as the most terrible form of sacrifice, the Valley of Hinnom as the earthly hell, the bronze arms as the inhuman embrace of the devouring god, Gehenna as the origin of the concept of hell
nodes.neumannArchetype: the most terrible Great Father who devours his own children through fire, the patriarchal consciousness of sacrifice taken to its absolute extreme
nodes.domain_source: Leviticus 18:21, 20:2-5; 2 Kings 23:10; Jeremiah 32:35; 1 Kings 11:7 (Solomon and 'Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites' — possible scribal confusion with Moloch); Punic *molk* inscriptions from Carthage; Eissfeldt 1935 *Molk als Opferbegriff*; Heider 1985 *The Cult of Molek*; Day 1989 *Molech: A God of Human Sacrifice in the Old Testament*
nodes.characterTrait_source: Hebrew Bible polemic against Moloch-worship; Heider 1985; Day 1989
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Diodorus Siculus 20.14 (the Carthage image, properly of Baal-Hammon, popularly attributed to Moloch in later tradition)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Jeremiah 7:31-32, 19:6, 32:35; 2 Kings 23:10; Carthage Tophet excavations (Stager & Wolff 1984); Punic molk-inscriptions

nodes.name: Horon
nodes.domain: cursing, healing-from-snakebite, the underworld (in some texts), exorcism, magical incantation
nodes.object: incantation-formulae; the snake (which he both controls and counters)
nodes.characterTrait: chthonic, cursing, healing, dual (both sender and curer of plague/snakebite)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Not described in detail. In KTU 1.100, he resides in `mṣrm` (Egypt) — possibly reflecting his association with Memphis or with Egyptian Horus-syncretism; the etymology of his name is debated (possibly 'pit/hole', referring to his chthonic abode).
nodes.significantEvent: In KTU 1.100, the anti-snake-bite incantation 'The Mare's Recipe', Shapash travels among the gods seeking a cure; only Horon (resident in `mṣrm`) provides effective help. In KTU 1.16 VI 54-58, Kirta invokes Horon and Athtart to curse his son Yassib. In KTU 1.82, Horon is invoked in an exorcism.
nodes.symbolism: the divine curse as a supernatural weapon, malevolence as a divine domain, the dark magic of the underworld as a realm of divine power
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow-father of the curse, the dark masculine consciousness of malediction and destructive magic
nodes.domain_source: KTU 1.16 VI 54-58 (Kirta curses his son Yassib using Horon and Athtart); KTU 1.100 (Horon among the gods petitioned for snakebite cure); KTU 1.82 (incantation invoking Horon); KAI 27 (Arslan Tash incantation tablet, possibly invoking Horon — debated)
nodes.object_source: KTU 1.100 (the anti-snake-bite incantation in which Horon plays a key role); KTU 1.82
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: KTU 1.100; the etymological note follows Wyatt 2002 *Religious Texts from Ugarit*

nodes.name: Attar
nodes.domain: Venus (the morning star), aborted kingship, irrigation, dawning, masculine counterpart of Astarte (Athtart)
nodes.object: throne of Baal (which he attempts to fill but fails — his feet do not reach the footstool, his head not the headrest)
nodes.characterTrait: ambitious, inadequate, descended, complaining; in his South Arabian aspect, a major active deity
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Young god; his stature is too small to fill Baal's throne (KTU 1.6 I 56-65). Specific physical description otherwise sparse in primary sources.
nodes.significantEvent: When Baal is killed by Mot, Athirat nominates her son Athtar to take Baal's throne. Athtar mounts the throne but his feet do not reach the footstool and his head not the headrest; he descends and rules instead in the underworld / over the earth (KTU 1.6 I 39-65). In an earlier passage (KTU 1.2 III), he had already complained to El that he was unfairly passed over.
nodes.symbolism: the planet Venus as a masculine deity, the attempt to fill the absent kings throne as overreach, the small god on the large throne as the inadequacy of the pretender, the desert irrigation as the masculine gift of water to dry land
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow who attempts to usurp the throne of the absent hero, the inadequate masculine consciousness that cannot fill the place of the true king
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Athirat and El.
nodes.domain_source: KTU 1.6 I 39-65 (Athtar's failed succession to Baal's throne); KTU 1.2 III 12-25 (Athtar's earlier failed claim); pantheon list KTU 1.47 / 1.118; South Arabian inscriptions (where Attar/ʿAthtar is a major god)
nodes.object_source: KTU 1.6 I 56-65 (the famous failure-to-fit description)
nodes.characterTrait_source: KTU 1.6 I 39-65 (his pathetic failure); South Arabian inscriptional context (where Attar is a major active god)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Son of Athirat (and El) per KTU 1.6 I

nodes.name: Anunnaki
nodes.domain: The collective of major Mesopotamian gods. In Sumerian usage often the gods of the upper world; in later Akkadian usage often the netherworld gods (especially the Anunnaki of the netherworld in Inanna's Descent and Ishtar's Descent).
nodes.characterTrait: NOTE: do not entangle this entry with the modern Sitchinian 'ancient astronaut' pseudoscience reading of Anunnaki — that is a 1970s extra-textual elaboration with no primary-source basis.
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the great gods of Sumerian and Akkadian religion, the collective divine council that determines fate
nodes.significantEvent: Sit as the Seven Judges of the Netherworld in Inanna's Descent. In Atrahasis and Enuma Elish, distinguished from the Igigi (younger gods). Etymology: 'offspring of An'.
nodes.symbolism: the divine council as the collective determination of fate, the gods who sit in judgment over the dead, the creation of humanity as a labor-saving device for the gods
nodes.neumannArchetype: the collective patriarchal consciousness that judges and determines fate, the council of the divine fathers who create humanity as servants
nodes.birthCircumstances: The Anunnaki were believed to be the offspring of An and the earth goddess Ki.
nodes.domain_source: ETCSL 1.4.1 lines 167-180 (the Anunna as netherworld judges); Ishtar's Descent (Akkadian); Atrahasis I 1-10; Enuma Elish VI 39-44 (Anunnaki distributed by Marduk to their stations)
nodes.significantEvent_source: ETCSL 1.4.1 lines 167-180; Atrahasis I 1-10; Enuma Elish VI 39-44
nodes.object_source: ETCSL 1.4.1 lines 167-180 (the seven Anunna and their judgement)
nodes.animals_source: Mesopotamian iconography of the divine council; the Anunnaki are not specifically associated with single embodiment animals — the entry's 'ox, dragon' likely reflects collective theriomorphic associations attested in some primordial traditions
nodes.characterTrait_source: ETCSL 1.4.1 lines 167-180; Atrahasis I 1-10; Enuma Elish VI 39-44 (their function as judges and council)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: ETCSL 1.4.1 lines 167-180; Enuma Elish VI 39-44; standard collective council descriptions
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Etymology of An-unna-ki ('those born of An on/of the earth'); standard Sumerian theogonic tradition
nodes.birthTypes_source: Standard Sumerian theogonic tradition (offspring of An and Ki)

nodes.name: Apkallu
nodes.domain: wisdom, civilization, the antediluvian foundation of culture, fish-man-hybrid form, magical incantation
nodes.characterTrait: wise, fish-garmented, seven-fold, civilizing, sage, purifying
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Seven Sages, depicted as figures wearing fish garments or as hybrid fish-men, carrying purification vessels
nodes.significantEvent: Emerged from the Apsû in antediluvian times — seven sages, the first being Oannes/Uan/Adapa. Taught humans writing, agriculture, building, divination, kingship. Were withdrawn back to Apsû by Marduk in the Erra Epic.
nodes.symbolism: the seven sages as the divine gift of civilization, the fish garment as the wisdom of the deep waters, the purification vessel as the cleansing power of divine knowledge, seven as the number of complete wisdom
nodes.neumannArchetype: the seven wise old men sent by the water-father to bring consciousness and civilization to the pre-flood humanity
nodes.domain_source: Berossus, Babyloniaca fr. 1 (preserved in Eusebius via Polyhistor) — Oannes/Adapa as the first sage; Bīt mēseri incantation series; Erra Epic I 162-163 (Marduk sends the Seven Sages back to Apsû)
nodes.object_source: Standard apkallu iconography from Neo-Assyrian palace reliefs (Nimrud, Khorsabad)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Berossus, Babyloniaca fr. 1; Bīt mēseri I-II; Erra Epic I 162-163
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Neo-Assyrian palace reliefs (Nimrud, Khorsabad); apotropaic figurines from foundation deposits
nodes.characterTrait_source: Berossus fr. 1; Bīt mēseri
nodes.animals_source: Berossus fr. 1 (Oannes as fish-man); Bīt mēseri; Neo-Assyrian apkallu reliefs (Nimrud, Khorsabad) where the fish-cape is the canonical iconographic identifier

nodes.name: Ancestors of Enlil
nodes.domain: Enlil, ancestry, the divine lineage, Sumerian theology
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the ancestral deities who precede Enlil in the divine genealogy
nodes.significantEvent: the divine ancestors of the god Enlil, representing the theological genealogy that traces the supreme god back to primordial origins
nodes.symbolism: the divine genealogy as the legitimation of supreme godhood, the ancestors who precede the chief god as the theological foundation of sovereignty
nodes.neumannArchetype: the patriarchal ancestors who precede the supreme consciousness, the genealogical chain of divine authority
nodes.animals_source: Some Sumerian theogonic traditions (the 'En-ki/Nin-ki' couples, etc.) include vulture or bird associations among Enlil's primordial ancestors; this is a tentative attestation
nodes.domain_source: An-Anum god-list and other Sumerian theogonic traditions list a series of antediluvian primordial pairs as Enlil's ancestors (Enmesarra-Ninmesarra, Enki-Ninki, Enlul-Ninlul, etc.)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Sumerian theogonic tradition (the primordial Enki-Ninki couples, etc., as Enlil's antediluvian ancestors); An-Anum god-list
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Sumerian theogonic tradition; An-Anum god-list (these primordial pairs are listed but not iconographically described)
nodes.significantEvent_source: An-Anum god-list; Sumerian theogonic tradition listing primordial pairs as Enlil's ancestors

nodes.name: Igigi
nodes.domain: The younger generation of gods. In Atrahasis, the labouring gods who rebel against Enlil before humans are created to take their place. In later Akkadian usage, often the gods of heaven (in contrast to the Anunnaki, then taken as gods of underworld).
nodes.object: picks, baskets, mattocks (the implements of their cosmic labour)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the younger sky gods who serve the Anunnaki, associated with heaven
nodes.significantEvent: Bear the cosmic labour of digging the Tigris and Euphrates and the irrigation canals. Rebel against Enlil after long ages. At Enki's intervention, Mami creates humanity to take over their labour.
nodes.symbolism: the rebellion of the younger gods as the divine origin of human labor, the creation of humanity as the solution to divine exhaustion, the divine strike as the catalyst for human creation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the younger divine consciousness that rebels against the labor imposed by the patriarchal elders, leading to the creation of human consciousness as a replacement
nodes.domain_source: Atrahasis I 1-50 (the rebellion); Enuma Elish VI 27-29; Codex Hammurabi prologue
nodes.significantEvent_source: Atrahasis I 1-50, 156-191
nodes.object_source: Atrahasis I 1-50
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Atrahasis I (where they appear collectively)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Atrahasis I 1-191

nodes.name: Šulak
nodes.domain: latrines, lurking, surprise attack, illness contracted in privies
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: lion-shaped lurker; appears in privies
nodes.significantEvent: a demon that haunts lavatories and can afflict people with disease, one of the many specific demons of Mesopotamian religion associated with particular places and ailments
nodes.symbolism: the lavatory demon as the spirit of impurity, the specific location of demonic habitation, the ancient recognition that places of waste are sources of disease
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow of the place of elimination, the chthonic consciousness of bodily waste and disease
nodes.domain_source: Babylonian Diagnostic Handbook SA.GIG (the lurker of the latrine, mukīl rēš lemutti); Babylonian Talmud b. Berakhot 62a (the demon bar-šulah described in Aramaic, lion-form, of latrines)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Babylonian incantation iconography; b. Berakhot 62a
nodes.significantEvent_source: SA.GIG (Diagnostic Handbook) tablet 27 [tablet number from memory, not verified]; b. Berakhot 62a
nodes.characterTrait_source: b. Berakhot 62a; SA.GIG
nodes.animals_source: b. Berakhot 62a (lion-form); SA.GIG; Babylonian incantation iconography

nodes.name: Nibiru
nodes.domain: A celestial designation in Mesopotamian astronomy: the 'crossing-place' (Akkadian nēberu), associated with Marduk in his astral aspect; the planet Jupiter in some contexts.
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: A celestial point or the planet Jupiter, depending on the source. NOT a 'planet' in the modern Sitchinian pseudoscientific sense — Zecharia Sitchin's 1976 'Planet X / Planet Nibiru' theory is a 20th-century extra-textual elaboration with no primary-source basis. The primary Mesopotamian sources use nēberu as an astronomical/astrological term.
nodes.significantEvent: A celestial point/body designated nēberu in Mesopotamian astronomy; not a deity-figure with narrative events. Modern Sitchinian elaborations (1976) are extra-textual.
nodes.symbolism: the celestial crossing point as the cosmic ford, the planet Jupiter as the marker of the crossing, the astronomical observation as a divine navigation point
nodes.neumannArchetype: the cosmic crossing point of celestial consciousness, the masculine ford where the heavenly rivers intersect
nodes.domain_source: Enuma Elish V 6 ('nēberu shall hold the crossings of heaven'); Enuma Elish VII 124-130 (Marduk-Nēberu among the fifty names); MUL.APIN astronomical compendium
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Enuma Elish V 6, VII 124-130; MUL.APIN
nodes.significantEvent_source: Enuma Elish V 6, VII 124-130; MUL.APIN
nodes.object_source: Enuma Elish V 6, VII 124-130; MUL.APIN astronomical compendium (where Jupiter / Marduk's celestial body is identified with nēberu)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Enuma Elish V 6 ('nēberu shall hold the crossings of heaven'); MUL.APIN — the etymology nēberu = 'crossing-place / ford'

nodes.name: Shuqamuna and Shumaliya
nodes.domain: Kassite royal cult, divine protection of kings, the bird-cult (Shumaliya), warrior protection (Shuqamuna), the divine couple of the Kassite dynasty
nodes.object: Kassite royal cult emblems — the standard kudurru-icons of the Kassite dynasty
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a paired Kassite deity, associated with horses and warfare
nodes.significantEvent: paired Kassite deities associated with horses and warfare, brought to Babylon by the Kassite dynasty, representing the equestrian martial tradition of the Kassite people
nodes.symbolism: the paired gods as the divine duality of the warrior horseman, the horse as the sacred animal of the Kassite warrior class
nodes.neumannArchetype: the paired masculine of the horse-warrior, the twin martial consciousness of the Kassite equestrian tradition
familyRoles: divine couple of the Kassite dynasty
nodes.domain_source: Kassite-period kudurru inscriptions (Brinkman 1976); Kassite-Babylonian hymns; Reallexikon der Assyriologie entries (Krebernik)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Kassite kudurru-inscription corpus
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Kassite kudurru iconography
nodes.characterTrait_source: Kassite kudurru-inscription corpus
nodes.animals_source: Kassite-period kudurru iconography (the horse-emblem appears on royal kudurrus)
nodes.object_source: Kassite-period kudurru iconography

nodes.name: Acintya
nodes.domain: supreme god, monotheism, Balinese Hinduism, the formless, the empty
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Supreme God of Balinese Hinduism, the formless and inconceivable absolute, the one god behind all manifestations
nodes.significantEvent: Acintya is the supreme deity of Balinese Hinduism, considered the formless absolute from which all other gods emanate, associated with the concept of emptiness (sunya) blending Hindu and Buddhist ideas
nodes.symbolism: the formless supreme as the source of all forms, the inconceivable god who transcends all representation, the Balinese synthesis of Hindu and Buddhist supreme concepts
nodes.neumannArchetype: the uroboric absolute that precedes all differentiation, the supreme consciousness beyond form and name

nodes.name: Barong
nodes.domain: protection, good, the lion, the dance, the eternal struggle with evil
nodes.object: mirrors, gilded ornaments, beard of human hair
nodes.characterTrait: protective, good, lion-formed, dancing, combative, guardian
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a lion-like protective spirit, the king of good spirits, depicted as a colorful and elaborate lion figure in Balinese dance-drama
nodes.significantEvent: the eternal opponent of Rangda (the queen of evil spirits) in the Barong dance, their battle never resolves as neither good nor evil can fully triumph, representing the Balinese concept of cosmic balance (rwa bhineda)
nodes.symbolism: the lion-spirit as the champion of good, the eternal dance-battle with evil as the Balinese concept of balance, the elaborate mask as the face of protective divinity, the unresolved battle as the perpetual cosmic equilibrium
nodes.neumannArchetype: the protective Great Father in animal form, the masculine guardian consciousness that eternally battles the terrible feminine (Rangda) without resolution

nodes.name: Bedawang Nala
nodes.domain: the cosmic turtle, the foundation of the world, the underworld, earthquakes
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the World Turtle, a colossal turtle upon whose back the world rests
nodes.significantEvent: the giant turtle Bedawang Nala supports the entire world on its back, when it moves earthquakes occur, it dwells in the cosmic ocean beneath the world
nodes.symbolism: the cosmic turtle as the foundation of all existence, earthquakes as the movements of the world-bearer, the ocean beneath the world as the watery abyss, the patient burden-bearer of all creation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the chthonic Great Mother as the world-bearing turtle, the patient feminine consciousness upon which all existence rests

nodes.name: Dewi Sri
nodes.domain: rice, agriculture, fertility, prosperity, the rice goddess
nodes.characterTrait: nurturing, rice-giving, prosperous, fertile, gentle, agricultural
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the goddess of rice and fertility, depicted as a beautiful woman associated with rice paddies and golden abundance
nodes.significantEvent: the most important agricultural goddess in Balinese Hinduism, worshipped at every stage of rice cultivation, offerings are made to her before planting, during growth, and at harvest, rice is treated as her sacred body
nodes.symbolism: rice as the body of the goddess, the rice paddy as the sacred field of feminine fertility, the harvest as the gathering of the divine body, the golden rice as the golden goddess
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of rice, the feminine whose body is the staple food, the agricultural goddess whose cultivation is the worship of the feminine earth
nodes.deathCircumstances: Sacrificed; plants grew from her body

nodes.name: Leyak
nodes.domain: witchcraft, evil spirits, shapeshifting, black magic, the night
nodes.characterTrait: evil, shapeshifting, nocturnal, cannibalistic, witch-like, terrifying
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: malevolent witches who can transform into various animals and monsters at night, practitioners of black magic
nodes.significantEvent: leyak are practitioners of black magic who can detach their heads and entrails from their bodies at night to fly around seeking victims, they are the most feared supernatural beings in Balinese folk religion
nodes.symbolism: the detached flying head as the separation of the witch from the human body, the nocturnal transformation as the dark side of consciousness, the leyak as the ultimate fear of the hidden evil within the community
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible shadow-feminine of the night, the dismembered anima that flies through the darkness seeking to devour

nodes.name: Naga Basuki
nodes.domain: serpents, the underworld, water, protection, the cosmic serpent
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Great Naga of the underworld, a divine serpent associated with water, the earth, and cosmic protection
nodes.significantEvent: Naga Basuki dwells beneath the world and is associated with the cosmic waters and the underworld, worshipped in Balinese Hindu tradition as a protective serpent deity
nodes.symbolism: the cosmic serpent of the underworld as the chthonic guardian, the naga as the water spirit of the deep earth, the serpent as the link between the underworld and the surface
nodes.neumannArchetype: the chthonic serpent-consciousness of the underworld, the uroboric naga that guards the depths beneath consciousness

nodes.name: Mara
nodes.domain: temptation, illusion, desire, death, the enemy of enlightenment
nodes.object: bow and arrows of desire, armies of demons
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Evil One, the lord of desire and death who tempts and obstructs those seeking enlightenment
nodes.significantEvent: attempted to prevent Siddhartha Gautama from achieving enlightenment under the Bodhi Tree by sending his armies of demons and his beautiful daughters to tempt and distract, the Buddha touched the earth as witness and defeated Mara
nodes.symbolism: the armies of desire as the obstacles to enlightenment, the daughters of Mara as the temptations of sensual pleasure, the earth-touching gesture as the defeat of illusion through grounding in reality, desire and death as the two faces of the same obstacle
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow of the enlightened consciousness, the ego-desire that attempts to prevent the dissolution of the self into nirvana, the lord of illusion whose defeat is the achievement of awakening

nodes.name: Avalokiteshvara
nodes.domain: compassion, mercy, the bodhisattva ideal, universal salvation, the Lotus Sutra
nodes.object: lotus, vase of nectar, rosary, willow branch
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Bodhisattva of Compassion, depicted with multiple arms and eyes (the thousand-armed form), embodying infinite compassion, manifests in many forms including female (Guanyin/Kannon)
nodes.significantEvent: the bodhisattva who heard the cries of all sentient beings and vowed not to enter nirvana until all beings are saved, the most widely worshipped bodhisattva in Mahayana Buddhism, manifests as Guanyin in Chinese tradition and Kannon in Japanese
nodes.symbolism: the thousand arms as the infinite reach of compassion, the multiple eyes as the all-seeing awareness of suffering, the lotus as purity arising from the mud of the world, the vow to save all beings as the supreme expression of compassion
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother/Father of compassion, the consciousness that refuses personal liberation in order to save all other consciousnesses from suffering

nodes.name: Manjushri
nodes.domain: wisdom, learning, transcendent insight, the sword of wisdom, scriptures
nodes.characterTrait: wise, youthful, sharp-minded, transcendent, scholarly, princely
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Bodhisattva of Wisdom, depicted as a youthful prince wielding a flaming sword in one hand and holding the Prajnaparamita scripture on a lotus in the other
nodes.significantEvent: embodies the transcendent wisdom (prajna) that cuts through all ignorance and illusion, his flaming sword severs the bonds of delusion, widely worshipped in Mahayana Buddhism as the patron of scholars and students
nodes.symbolism: the flaming sword as the sharp intellect that cuts through delusion, the scripture on the lotus as wisdom arising from the world, the youthful appearance as the eternal freshness of true insight, the prince of wisdom as the royal nature of the intellect
nodes.neumannArchetype: the eternal divine youth of wisdom, the masculine consciousness of transcendent insight that cuts through all illusion with the sword of discrimination

nodes.name: Furrina
nodes.domain: darkness, wells, springs, mystery, robbery, theft
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: mysterious goddess of springs and wells, associated with darkness and obscurity
nodes.significantEvent: had a sacred grove on the Janiculum Hill where her annual festival was celebrated, one of the most obscure Roman deities, her rites were mysterious and ancient, associated with robbers and thieves who operated near her grove
nodes.symbolism: the dark feminine of springs and wells, the mysterious underground waters, the grove as the haunt of both the divine and the criminal, obscurity as a divine quality
nodes.neumannArchetype: the dark Great Mother of underground waters, the obscure feminine of the chthonic depths

nodes.name: Vajrapani
nodes.domain: power, protection, wrathful compassion, the vajra, spiritual strength
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Bodhisattva of Power, depicted as a fierce warrior wielding the vajra (diamond thunderbolt), dark-skinned and muscular
nodes.significantEvent: embodies the power and strength of all the Buddhas, represents the fierce compassion that destroys obstacles to enlightenment, protector of the dharma who subdues evil with wrathful force
nodes.symbolism: the vajra as the indestructible weapon of spiritual power, the fierce face as wrathful compassion that destroys evil for the good of all beings, the dark skin as the power of the depths, the thunderbolt as the sudden destruction of ignorance
nodes.neumannArchetype: the wrathful Great Father of spiritual power, the fierce masculine consciousness that protects the dharma through the application of destructive force against evil

nodes.name: Yama
nodes.domain: death, judgment, the underworld, the wheel of life, karma, the afterlife
nodes.object: the Wheel of Life (bhavachakra), mirror of karma, scales
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Lord of Death and Judge of the Dead, depicted holding the Wheel of Life in his mouth or hands, often with a terrifying face
nodes.significantEvent: judges the dead according to their karma, holds the Wheel of Life showing the six realms of rebirth, the mirror of karma reflects the deceased persons deeds, the first being to die who became the lord of the dead
nodes.symbolism: the Wheel of Life in the mouth of death as the cycle of rebirth driven by desire, the mirror of karma as the reflection of accumulated deeds, the judgment of the dead as the karmic sorting of consciousness, the first to die as the ruler of the realm of death
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father of death and karmic judgment, the masculine consciousness of mortality that holds the wheel of samsara in its jaws

nodes.name: Amitabha
nodes.domain: infinite light, the Pure Land, the western paradise, compassion, salvation through faith
nodes.characterTrait: infinite-light, compassionate, saving, Pure Land-ruling, peaceful, infinite
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Buddha of Infinite Light and Infinite Life, depicted in deep red or golden color, seated in meditation
nodes.significantEvent: rules the Pure Land (Sukhavati) in the western direction, made 48 vows to save all beings who call upon his name, the central figure of Pure Land Buddhism, the most popular form of Buddhism in East Asia
nodes.symbolism: the infinite light as the boundless compassion that illuminates all darkness, the Pure Land as the paradise achievable through faith, the 48 vows as the comprehensive promise of universal salvation, the western direction as the land of the setting sun transformed into paradise
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Father of infinite light and compassion, the masculine consciousness of boundless illumination that transforms the western land of death (setting sun) into paradise

nodes.name: The Monad
nodes.domain: the supreme being, the one, the source of all, the unknowable, divine fullness
nodes.characterTrait: supreme, unknowable, singular, source-of-all, transcendent, perfect
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the One, the supreme and unknowable source of all existence in Gnostic theology, beyond all description and comprehension
nodes.significantEvent: the Monad is the ultimate source from which all divine emanations (aeons) proceed, too perfect and transcendent to be known directly, the material world is the result of a catastrophic fall far from the Monads perfection
nodes.symbolism: the One as the source beyond all duality, the unknowable god as the perfection from which all imperfection falls, the transcendent source that can only be approached through gnosis (direct knowledge), the fullness (pleroma) as the totality of divine emanation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial uroboric unity from which all consciousness emanates, the undifferentiated absolute before any differentiation occurs

nodes.name: Barbelo
nodes.domain: the first emanation, the divine feminine, the womb of the aeons, forethought
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the First Thought of the supreme god, the divine feminine emanation from the Monad, the womb from which the aeons are born
nodes.significantEvent: the first emanation from the Monad, Barbelo is the divine feminine thought or forethought who gives birth to the aeons and the divine fullness (pleroma), she represents the supreme feminine principle in Gnostic theology
nodes.symbolism: the first thought as the feminine origin of all divine emanation, the womb of the aeons as the divine feminine creativity, forethought as the feminine foresight that initiates the chain of being
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial Great Mother of divine emanation, the first feminine consciousness that emerges from the undifferentiated Monad

nodes.name: Abraxas
nodes.domain: the cosmic ruler, mystical words, the 365 emanations, the Basilidean system, gems
nodes.object: talismanic gems (Abraxas stones), the rooster-headed serpent-legged figure
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: depicted on talismanic gems as a figure with a rooster head, human body, and serpent legs, carrying a whip and shield
nodes.significantEvent: in the Basilidean Gnostic system, Abraxas (or Abrasax) is the supreme being whose name has the numerical value 365 (representing the 365 heavens or the days of the year), he encompasses all opposing forces in one being
nodes.symbolism: the numerical value 365 as the totality of the cosmic year, the rooster head as the solar announcer of dawn, the serpent legs as the chthonic foundation, the combination of opposing symbols in one being as the unity of all cosmic forces, the talismanic gem as the magical condensation of cosmic power
nodes.neumannArchetype: the cosmic totality figure who unites all opposites (solar rooster and chthonic serpent) in one being, the uroboric consciousness of the complete cosmic year

nodes.name: Norea
nodes.domain: resistance, feminine wisdom, the flood, Seth, the Gnostic feminine hero
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a wise and powerful feminine figure in Gnostic mythology, associated with resistance against the Demiurge
nodes.significantEvent: in Gnostic texts Norea is a powerful feminine figure who resists the archons (rulers of the material world), she survived the flood by burning the first ark and was protected by divine powers, she received gnosis (saving knowledge) from the aeons
nodes.symbolism: the feminine resistance against the false patriarchal creator, the burning of the ark as the refusal to submit to the Demiurges plan, the woman who receives gnosis as the feminine wisdom that sees through the material illusion
nodes.neumannArchetype: the heroic anima who resists the false patriarchal order (the Demiurge), the feminine consciousness that sees through illusion and receives true knowledge
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Eve and Adam in Gnostic tradition

nodes.name: Agdistis
nodes.domain: hermaphroditism, wild nature, castration, Cybele, primordial gender, Phrygia
nodes.characterTrait: hermaphroditic, wild, castrated, primordial, gender-fluid, Phrygian
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a hermaphroditic primordial deity of great power, combining both male and female characteristics
nodes.significantEvent: the gods feared the power of the hermaphroditic Agdistis and castrated the deity, from the blood an almond tree grew whose fruit impregnated the nymph Nana who bore Attis, establishing the cycle of castration and rebirth central to the cult of Cybele
nodes.symbolism: the hermaphroditic being as the primordial state before gender differentiation, the castration as the forced division of the undifferentiated, the almond as the fruit of the wound, the birth of Attis from the wound as new life from mutilation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the uroboric hermaphrodite that must be castrated (differentiated) for the ordered gendered world to exist, the primordial being whose mutilation generates the cycle of death and rebirth
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from the earth or from a rock, a primordial self-generated being
nodes.deathCircumstances: Castrated by the gods; survived

nodes.name: Sabazios
nodes.domain: ecstatic worship, horses, beer, snakes, liberation, Thrace and Phrygia
nodes.characterTrait: ecstatic, nocturnal, horse-riding, beer-drinking, liberating, orgiastic
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a Phrygian and Thracian god of ecstatic worship, depicted on horseback or with serpents, associated with nocturnal rites
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped through ecstatic nocturnal rites involving snake-handling, beer or wine consumption, and frenzied dancing, later syncretized with Dionysus in Greece and adopted into Roman religion as a mystery cult
nodes.symbolism: the nocturnal ecstasy as the divine liberation from ordinary consciousness, the serpent as the instrument of the rite, beer and wine as the drinks of divine frenzy, the horse as the vehicle of the ecstatic deity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine of ecstatic dissolution, the orgiastic consciousness that breaks through ordinary awareness through the frenzy of nocturnal rites
nodes.birthCircumstances: a Phrygian-Thracian deity later identified with Dionysus and Jupiter

nodes.name: Men
nodes.domain: the moon, Phrygia, agriculture, the underworld, fate, the crescent
nodes.object: crescent moon, pine cone, cap (Phrygian cap)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a Phrygian moon god depicted wearing a crescent moon on his shoulders and a Phrygian cap, holding a pine cone
nodes.significantEvent: widely worshipped in Phrygia as a moon god associated with agriculture and the underworld, his cult spread throughout Anatolia, the crescent moon was his primary symbol
nodes.symbolism: the crescent moon as the symbol of the lunar masculine, the Phrygian cap as the mark of the Anatolian divine, the pine cone as the symbol of fertility and the connection to Attis and Cybele, the moon as the governor of agricultural time
nodes.neumannArchetype: the lunar masculine of Anatolia, the moon-father who governs agricultural cycles and the fate of the underworld

nodes.name: Kek
nodes.domain: darkness, obscurity, the primordial night, chaos
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: frog-headed man representing primordial darkness, paired with the serpent-headed Kauket
nodes.significantEvent: together with the other members of the Ogdoad (Nun/Naunet, Amun/Amunet, Heh/Hauhet) created the conditions for the emergence of light and the sun from the primordial darkness
nodes.symbolism: darkness as a primordial creative force, not the absence of light but its precondition, the necessary obscurity from which creation emerges, the Ogdoad as the eight forces of pre-creation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial darkness from which consciousness (light) must emerge, the uroboric night that precedes the dawn of awareness
nodes.birthCircumstances: one of the eight primordial deities of the Ogdoad of Hermopolis, personification of darkness

nodes.name: Nun
nodes.domain: primordial waters, chaos, the abyss, pre-creation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: man with a frog head, or as the dark boundless primordial ocean itself, depicted as wavy lines of water
nodes.significantEvent: the primordial ocean from which the first god (Atum) emerged on the primordial mound, contains the potential of all creation within his formless waters, persists at the edges of the created world threatening to return
nodes.symbolism: the formless potential before creation, the infinite dark waters of non-existence, the ocean of chaos that both precedes and surrounds the ordered world, the pre-conscious state from which awareness emerges
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial uroboros, the undifferentiated pre-conscious state from which the ego (Atum/Ra) must emerge, the oceanic unconscious that precedes all differentiation
nodes.birthCircumstances: existed before creation, the infinite dark waters from which all emerged

nodes.name: Sia
nodes.domain: perception, insight, divine knowledge, cognition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: personification of the concept of perception and divine knowledge, depicted as a man
nodes.significantEvent: sailed in the solar barque with Ra, representing the perceptive faculty of the creator god, through Sia Ra perceived what needed to be created and through Hu he spoke it into being
nodes.symbolism: perception as a divine faculty, the suns ability to see and know all things, the cognitive aspect of creation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the perceptive aspect of the Great Father, the masculine consciousness as the faculty of divine knowing
nodes.birthCircumstances: companion of Hu (divine utterance), together they represent the full creative power of the sun god

nodes.name: Koptos colossi
nodes.domain: fertility, Min, the ancient world, Coptos, colossal statues
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: three colossal statues of the god Min found at Coptos, among the oldest monumental stone sculptures in Egyptian history
nodes.significantEvent: these massive limestone sculptures from the predynastic period (c. 3300 BCE) are among the oldest known large-scale stone sculptures in Egypt, they represent Min in his ithyphallic form and show the antiquity of his cult
nodes.symbolism: the earliest monumental expression of the divine masculine in stone, the antiquity of the fertility cult in Egyptian civilization, the colossal as the expression of divine power
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial phallic Great Father in his most ancient stone form, the masculine principle petrified in the oldest monumental sculpture

nodes.name: Jörmungandr
nodes.domain: the world ocean, cosmic boundaries, Ragnarok, poison, serpents
nodes.characterTrait: enormous, encircling, venomous, cosmic, boundary-forming, world-ending
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the World Serpent (Midgard Serpent) so large it encircles the entire world and grasps its own tail
nodes.significantEvent: thrown into the ocean by Odin where it grew so large it encircled Midgard and grasped its own tail, Thor tried to catch it while fishing, at Ragnarok it will rise from the ocean and Thor will kill it but die from its venom
nodes.symbolism: the serpent that encircles the world as the boundary of the knowable, the self-devouring tail as the uroboros of cosmic time, the venom as the poison of the boundary, the final battle between thunder and serpent as the climax of the cosmic drama
nodes.neumannArchetype: the uroboric serpent that encircles consciousness, the primordial chaos-beast that must be slain at the cost of the heros life
nodes.birthCircumstances: offspring of Loki and the giantess Angrboda, thrown into the ocean by Odin
nodes.deathCircumstances: Slain by Thor at Ragnarök; Thor falls dead from the serpent's venom after nine steps.
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 34, 47-48, 51; Vǫluspá 50, 56; Hymiskviða 21-25 (Thor fishes for the serpent)
nodes.object_source: (the serpent is the object — encircles Midgard)
nodes.animals_source: Symbolic — Jörmungandr IS the world-serpent; embodiment-monster, not just an animal-mount
nodes.significantEvent_source: Gylfaginning 34, 47-48, 51; Vǫluspá 50, 56; Hymiskviða

nodes.name: Rekhyt
nodes.domain: the people, the commoners, loyalty, worship, the lapwing
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the lapwing bird (rekhyt) with human arms raised in worship, representing the common people of Egypt
nodes.significantEvent: depicted in temples and on palace walls as the common people in a posture of worship before the pharaoh and the gods, the rekhyt hieroglyph came to represent all the common subjects of Egypt in an attitude of adoration
nodes.symbolism: the common people as worshippers, the lapwing as the bird of the masses, the transformation of a conquered people into loyal subjects, collective worship as the posture of the community before the divine
nodes.neumannArchetype: the collective human consciousness in its posture of submission before the Great Father (pharaoh/gods), the ego in worship before the Self

nodes.name: Hu
nodes.domain: creative speech, authority, the divine word, command
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: personification of the creative utterance of the creator god, depicted as a man
nodes.significantEvent: sailed in the solar barque with Ra, representing the spoken command through which the creator brought the world into existence, the power behind all divine decrees and creative acts
nodes.symbolism: the word as the instrument of creation, divine speech that brings things into being, the logos of Egyptian theology, command as creation
nodes.neumannArchetype: the logos aspect of the Great Father, the masculine creative principle expressed as the commanding word
nodes.birthCircumstances: companion of Sia (divine perception), together they are the creative faculties of Ra

nodes.name: Kamimusubi
nodes.domain: creation, divine production, musubi (creative power), the primordial feminine
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: one of the three primordial creation kami, represents the feminine aspect of divine creative power (musubi)
nodes.significantEvent: one of the three Zoka Sanshin (Three Gods of Creation) who appeared at the very beginning, represents the feminine productive power (musubi) that creates and nurtures all things, ancestor of the Izumo lineage
nodes.symbolism: the feminine creative power at the origin of the cosmos, musubi as the divine productive force that generates all life, the feminine aspect of the creative trinity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial Great Mother of creation, the feminine musubi (creative binding force) that generates the world alongside the masculine creative principles
nodes.birthCircumstances: the third kami to appear at the beginning of creation, a hitorigami
nodes.domain_source: Kojiki, scroll I; Nihon Shoki
nodes.object_source: Kojiki — abstract creative-musubi power
nodes.characterTrait_source: Kojiki — third of the Kotoamatsukami; female-aspect of cosmic generative power
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Kojiki — abstract; female; hitorigami
nodes.significantEvent_source: Kojiki — third of the first five Kotoamatsukami; the female cosmic-creative principle, paired with Takamimusubi as the masculine; embodies musubi (the generative-binding power that produces all beings)
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Kojiki — self-arising; hitorigami
nodes.birthTypes_source: Kojiki

nodes.name: Fecunditas
nodes.domain: fertility, cattle, livestock, rural prosperity
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess of fertility and the prosperity of livestock
nodes.significantEvent: ensured the fertility and health of livestock, worshipped by farmers and herders for the prosperity of their animals
nodes.symbolism: the divine blessing on livestock as the foundation of rural wealth, animal fertility as a sacred concern, the prosperity of the herd as a divine gift
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother of animal fertility, the feminine that nurtures and multiplies the herds
