nodes.name: Shinigami
nodes.domain: death, the underworld, soul collection, Japanese death deities
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: gods or spirits of death that invite humans toward death, often appearing when someone is near death
nodes.significantEvent: shinigami are relatively late additions to Japanese mythology, influenced by Buddhist and Chinese concepts, they appear to those near death and guide or lure them toward dying
nodes.symbolism: death as a divine invitation, the shinigami as the face of mortality, the death spirit that appears at the threshold, the inevitable divine summons
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow of consciousness that appears at the threshold of death, the terrible masculine of the death drive

nodes.name: Febris
nodes.domain: fever, disease, healing from fever, the swamp
nodes.characterTrait: fever-associated, disease-related, both causing and curing, ambiguous
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goddess of fever, invoked both to cause and to cure fevers
nodes.significantEvent: had three temples in Rome, she could both send and remove fevers, offerings were made to appease her and persuade her to depart from the sick, she represented the malaria that plagued Romes swampy environs
nodes.symbolism: disease as a divine power that must be propitiated rather than fought, the ambiguity of the fever goddess who both sends and cures, the swamp as the source of both disease and divine power
nodes.neumannArchetype: the ambiguous Great Mother of disease, the feminine that both afflicts and heals, the chthonic power of the swamp

nodes.name: Ame-no-Minakanushi
nodes.domain: the center of heaven, the cosmos, the beginning, the supreme kami
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the first kami to appear in the universe, the Lord of the August Center of Heaven, a hitorigami (solitary deity) who immediately hid
nodes.significantEvent: appeared at the very beginning of creation in the High Plain of Heaven (Takama-ga-hara) and then immediately concealed himself, the supreme cosmic deity who is the center of all existence but remains hidden, the first of the Kotoamatsukami (the five primordial heavenly kami)
nodes.symbolism: the center of heaven as the cosmic origin point, the supreme kami who hides as the ultimate divine mystery, the beginning that precedes all other beginnings, the center that is invisible
nodes.neumannArchetype: the primordial Great Father of the cosmic center, the supreme patriarchal consciousness that immediately hides, the origin point from which all subsequent consciousness emerges
nodes.birthCircumstances: the very first kami to come into existence when the universe began
nodes.domain_source: Kojiki, scroll I; Nihon Shoki — the first of the Kotoamatsukami
nodes.object_source: Kojiki — abstract primordial cosmic axis
nodes.characterTrait_source: Kojiki — first cosmic kami; hitorigami (solitary, sexless)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Kojiki — abstract; sometimes anthropomorphized in later tradition
nodes.significantEvent_source: Kojiki — the first kami to come into existence at Takamagahara; followed by Takamimusubi and Kamimusubi to form the first three Kotoamatsukami; remained 'hidden' from the world's affairs
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Kojiki — self-arising at the beginning of the cosmos

nodes.name: Loki
nodes.domain: trickery, fire, shape-shifting, chaos, wit, betrayal, Ragnarok
nodes.object: his shoes that allow him to run on air and water; his ability (or self-cast spell) of shape-shifting itself
nodes.characterTrait: cunning, mocking, treacherous, witty, shape-shifting, both helpful and harmful to the Æsir, ultimately the betrayer at Baldr's death and the released enemy at Ragnarok
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Of striking appearance (Snorri describes him as 'fair and beautiful in face'); shape-shifts at will into mare (mating with the giant's horse Svaðilfari to bear Sleipnir, Gylfaginning 42), salmon (when fleeing the gods after Baldr's death, Gylfaginning 50), fly (in the Brokk-Sindri wager, Skáldskaparmál 35), falcon-form (using Freyja's borrowed cloak, Þrymskviða 5; Skáldskaparmál 18, the Iðunn-rescue), seal (when he and Heimdall fight over the Brísingamen).
nodes.significantEvent: Many. Bears Sleipnir from his mare-form mating with Svaðilfari (Gylfaginning 42). Steals and recovers the Brísingamen from Heimdall. Wagers with Brokk and Sindri the dwarves and loses, having his lips sewn shut by Brokk (Skáldskaparmál 35). Causes Iðunn's abduction by Þjazi and her recovery (Skáldskaparmál 18). Insults all the gods at Ægir's banquet (Lokasenna). Engineers Baldr's death by guiding Hǫðr's mistletoe-shaft, then prevents his return from Hel by refusing to weep (the giantess Þǫkk, Gylfaginning 49). Bound by the Æsir under a venom-dripping serpent, Sigyn his wife holding a bowl to catch the venom (Gylfaginning 50; Vǫluspá 35). At Ragnarok, breaks free, captains Naglfar (the ship of dead men's nails), and meets Heimdall in mutual slaying (Vǫluspá 51-52; Gylfaginning 51).
nodes.symbolism: the trickster who is both necessary and destructive, the shapeshifter who crosses all boundaries, the father of monsters as the progenitor of cosmic threats, the blood-brother who becomes the ultimate betrayer, chaos as both creative and ultimately destructive
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow of the divine order, the trickster-consciousness that generates both the useful and the monstrous, the chaos that the patriarchal order adopts but cannot control
familyRoles: father of Fenrir, Jǫrmungandr, Hel (with Angrboða)
husband of Sigyn (with sons Narfi and Váli)
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of the giant Fárbauti and Laufey (also called Nál); brother of Helblindi and Býleistr per Snorri.
nodes.deathCircumstances: Bound after the death of Baldr (Gylfaginning 50) to three stones with the entrails of his son Vali (transformed into a wolf to slay his brother Narfi); a serpent drips venom over his face, with his wife Sigyn holding a bowl to catch it. Breaks free at Ragnarök and falls in mutual slaughter with Heimdallr (Vǫluspá 51-56; Gylfaginning 51).
nodes.domain_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 33-34, 49-51 (his binding); Skáldskaparmál (his theft of Idun's apples, the recovery of Mjǫllnir, the cutting of Sif's hair, the making of the gifts of the gods); Lokasenna (the flyting); Vǫluspá; Þrymskviða; Þrymskviða; Reginsmál prose; Snorri's Skáldskaparmál 33 (the origin of his children with Angrboða)
nodes.object_source: Skáldskaparmál 35 (the wager with the dwarves); Gylfaginning 49-51 (the binding-bonds made of Vali's-transformed-son's entrails)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Lokasenna; Skáldskaparmál passim; Gylfaginning 33
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Snorri, Gylfaginning 33 ('fair and handsome of appearance, but evil in disposition'); standard iconography

nodes.birthTypes_source: Gylfaginning 33
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Skáldskaparmál 16; Gylfaginning 33

nodes.name: Marmennill
nodes.domain: the sea, merfolk, prophecy, storm warning, maritime encounters
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a merman figure of Norse mythology, half human and half fish
nodes.significantEvent: marmennill are sea-folk who can be caught by fishermen, if treated well they may prophesy about coming storms or future events, they dwell in the deep ocean and rarely interact with humans
nodes.symbolism: the merman as the prophetic voice of the sea, the captured sea-being who reveals the future, the exchange between fisherman and sea-spirit as the bargain for oceanic knowledge
nodes.neumannArchetype: the masculine of the oceanic depths who provides prophetic knowledge when captured by consciousness

nodes.name: Ōmeteōtl
nodes.domain: duality, creation, the supreme being, male-female unity, the origin of all
nodes.characterTrait: dual, supreme, creative, male-female, originating, transcendent
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Dual God, simultaneously male (Ometecuhtli) and female (Omecihuatl), the supreme creator dwelling in the highest heaven (Omeyocan)
nodes.significantEvent: the supreme dual deity who created all the other gods, dwells in Omeyocan (the Place of Duality) at the thirteenth and highest level of heaven, too remote to be worshipped directly, generated the four Tezcatlipocas who create and destroy the world ages
nodes.symbolism: the dual nature of divinity as simultaneously male and female, the supreme being too transcendent for direct worship, the Place of Duality as the highest heaven, the generation of the four world-creators from the original unity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the uroboric unity of masculine and feminine before differentiation, the primordial androgynous consciousness from which all polarities emerge
nodes.birthCircumstances: self-existing, the first cause, the ultimate origin of all existence

nodes.name: Xolotl
nodes.domain: lightning, Venus as evening star, deformity, twins, the underworld, dogs, monsters
nodes.characterTrait: deformed, monstrous, dog-headed, lightning-bringing, twin, underworld-journeying
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the monstrous twin of Quetzalcoatl, depicted with backwards feet, wrinkled skin, and empty eye sockets, often associated with the Xoloitzcuintli dog
nodes.significantEvent: accompanied the dead through the underworld as a guide dog, represents Venus as the evening star (while Quetzalcoatl is the morning star), refused to sacrifice himself at the creation of the fifth sun and tried to flee death, his tears of fear carved the valleys in his eye sockets
nodes.symbolism: the monstrous twin as the dark double of the creator, the dog as the guide of the dead, the evening star as the twin of the morning star, deformity as the price of fearing death, the tears that carve the face as the mark of cowardice before sacrifice
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow-twin of the hero (Quetzalcoatl), the deformed masculine who fears the sacrifice that consciousness demands, the guide through the underworld who is himself marked by the refusal to die
nodes.birthCircumstances: twin brother of Quetzalcoatl, born as a deformed or monstrous version of the feathered serpent

nodes.domain: mountains, caves, echoes, jaguars, earthquakes, the earth interior
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Heart of the Mountain, depicted as a spotted jaguar in a cave, the jaguar that dwells inside the earth
nodes.significantEvent: represents the echoes in caves and mountains as the voice of the earth-jaguar, associated with earthquakes as the movements of the mountain heart, the jaguar that prowls inside the living earth
nodes.symbolism: the jaguar inside the mountain as the living heart of the earth, echoes as the voice of the mountain-jaguar, the cave as the mouth of the earth, earthquakes as the heartbeat of the mountain spirit
nodes.neumannArchetype: the chthonic masculine-jaguar that dwells within the Great Mother (the mountain), the animal consciousness of the earth interior
nodes.birthCircumstances: an aspect of Tezcatlipoca associated with the interior of the earth and mountains

nodes.name: Nanāhuātzin
nodes.domain: humility, sacrifice, disease, the sun, self-immolation, transformation
nodes.characterTrait: humble, diseased, brave, self-sacrificing, transforming, courageous
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: a humble, pimpled, diseased god covered in sores and blisters
nodes.significantEvent: at the creation of the fifth sun, the gods needed one of them to throw himself into the cosmic fire to become the sun, the proud Tecciztecatl hesitated but the humble diseased Nanahuatzin bravely threw himself into the flames and became the sun (Tonatiuh)
nodes.symbolism: the diseased humble god who becomes the sun as the triumph of courage over pride, self-sacrifice into fire as the ultimate creative act, disease and poverty as no barrier to divine destiny, the most lowly becoming the most exalted through sacrifice
nodes.neumannArchetype: the humble divine child who through self-sacrifice into the fire becomes the supreme solar consciousness, the lowest becoming the highest through the total surrender of self
nodes.birthCircumstances: " According to a translation of the Histoyre du Mechique, Nanāhuātzin is the son of Ītzpāpālōtl and Cozcamiauh or Tonantzin, but was adopted by Piltzintecuhtli and Xōchiquetzal.

nodes.name: Mrtyu
nodes.domain: death, the personification of death, mortality, the inevitable end
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the personification of death in Hinduism, distinct from Yama (the god of death), Mrtyu is death itself as an abstract principle
nodes.significantEvent: the personification of death as a cosmic principle, Mrtyu represents the inevitable mortality that even the gods cannot fully escape, the abstract concept of dying as a divine force
nodes.symbolism: death as an impersonal cosmic force, the inevitability of mortality as a divine principle, Mrtyu as the ultimate fate that underlies all existence
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow of consciousness itself, death as the absolute boundary of ego-awareness
nodes.domain_source: Atharva Veda; Kaṭha Upaniṣad (Mṛtyu/Yama and Naciketas); Bhagavad Gītā 11.32
nodes.object_source: Vedic-Purāṇic tradition
nodes.characterTrait_source: Kaṭha Upaniṣad; Mahābhārata
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Purāṇic tradition; often identified with Yama or Kāla
nodes.significantEvent_source: Kaṭha Upaniṣad; Bhagavad Gītā 11.32
nodes.birthTypes_source: Vedic tradition

nodes.name: Mot
nodes.domain: death, sterility, the underworld, the parched earth, devouring
nodes.object: his vast jaw (one lip touches the earth, the other the heavens — KTU 1.5 II 2-3); the city Hmry of his realm; the throne of his sovereignty in the underworld
nodes.characterTrait: ravenous, devouring, implacable, sovereign over the dead, ultimately defeated, briefly returns
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Vast, cosmic in scale (his jaw spans heaven and earth); voracious; in iconography (rare) sometimes serpentine or skeletal.
nodes.significantEvent: Demands tribute from Baal (KTU 1.4 VII - 1.5 I). Swallows Baal into his vast gullet, leading to Baal's death and the desiccation of the earth (KTU 1.5 VI 8-25). Confronted by Anat, who slays him in a sequence of agricultural-and-cooking transformations: she splits him with a sword, winnows him with a sieve, parches him with fire, grinds him with a mill, scatters his remnants in the field for the birds (KTU 1.6 II 30-37). Returns and confronts Baal in single combat seven years later; the gods intervene (KTU 1.6 V-VI). Finally tamed but not extinguished — the seasonal-mortality cycle continues.
nodes.symbolism: the insatiable mouth of death reaching from earth to heaven, the seasonal drought as the reign of Mot, the treatment of Mot like grain (cutting, winnowing, grinding) as the agricultural defeat of death, deaths inevitable return because death cannot die
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible Great Father of death and the underworld, the devouring masculine that swallows the young god (Baal) and must be defeated but can never be permanently destroyed
nodes.birthCircumstances: Beloved son of El (`mt ydd ʾil ġzr`).
nodes.deathCircumstances: Slain by Anat in a sequence of agricultural transformations: she splits him with a sword, winnows him with a sieve, parches him with fire, grinds him with a mill, scatters his remnants for the birds (KTU 1.6 II 30-37). Despite this, he returns seven years later to challenge Baal again (KTU 1.6 V-VI), reflecting the cyclical nature of death-and-life.
nodes.domain_source: KTU 1.4 VII 47 - 1.6 VI (the entire latter half of the Baal Cycle); KTU 1.5 II 1-6 ('the beloved of El, the hero, the lord of the dust'); KTU 1.23 (Mot mentioned in the prologue of the Goodly Gods)
nodes.object_source: KTU 1.5 II 2-6 (the cosmic jaws); KTU 1.4 VIII 7-12 (his city Hmry)
nodes.characterTrait_source: KTU 1.5 I-II (his demand for tribute); 1.5 VI (his swallowing of Baal); 1.6 II (his defeat by Anat); 1.6 V-VI (his return and final fight with Baal)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: KTU 1.5 II 2-6
nodes.significantEvent_source: KTU 1.4 VII - 1.6 VI
nodes.birthTypes_source: Mot is 'beloved son of El' in KTU 1.4-1.5
nodes.deathTypes_source: KTU 1.6 II 30-37 (his initial agricultural slaying by Anat); KTU 1.6 VI (his eventual return)

nodes.name: Yam
nodes.domain: the sea, primordial chaos, judgeship of the river (his epithets `ym` 'sea' and `nhr` 'river'), the cosmic ocean adversary of Baal
nodes.object: his throne (granted by El at the start of the Baal Cycle); his messengers (sent to demand Baal's submission, KTU 1.2 I)
nodes.animals: serpent, dragon (his form/embodiment as the cosmic-sea adversary)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Cosmic sea personified; in narrative, anthropomorphized as a sovereign-king with messengers and throne; in his draconic aspect, serpent-or-dragon-formed.
nodes.significantEvent: At the start of the Baal Cycle, El elevates Yam and grants him kingship (KTU 1.1 IV 14-32). Yam sends messengers to the divine assembly demanding Baal's submission as his slave (KTU 1.2 I). Baal accepts the challenge; with weapons forged by Kothar-wa-Khasis (Yagrushu and Ayyamur, the 'Driver' and 'Chaser'), Baal defeats Yam in single combat (KTU 1.2 IV). Yam is dismembered or scattered; Athtart restrains Baal from boasting too much.
nodes.symbolism: the chaotic sea as the primordial threat to cosmic order, the sea serpent as the monster of the deep, the defeat of Yam by the storm god as the triumph of order over chaos, the seven-headed serpent as the multiplied terror of the deep
nodes.neumannArchetype: the uroboric chaos-dragon of the sea, the primordial unconscious that must be slain by the heroic storm-consciousness for the ordered world to exist
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of El (sometimes called 'beloved of El'); rival of Baal for divine kingship.
nodes.deathCircumstances: Defeated by Baal in single combat with the magical maces Yagrushu ('Driver') and Ayyamur ('Chaser'), forged by Kothar-wa-Khasis. After being struck, Yam is shattered; Athtart restrains Baal from total annihilation.
nodes.domain_source: KTU 1.1-1.2 (the Baal-Yam combat); his epithets `zbl ym` 'Prince Sea' and `ṯpṭ nhr` 'Judge River' appear repeatedly
nodes.object_source: KTU 1.1 IV 14-32 (El grants Yam kingship and his throne); KTU 1.2 I 11-19 (Yam's messengers)
nodes.animals_source: KTU 1.3 III 38-44 (Anat's boast lists Yam-Tannin and the seven-headed serpent — Lotan — among defeated cosmic-sea adversaries; `tnn` and `bṯn` are draconic embodiments of the cosmic sea)
nodes.characterTrait_source: KTU 1.2 I-IV — his demand for Baal's submission, his combat with Baal, his defeat
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: KTU 1.2 (anthropomorphic king); KTU 1.3 III 38-44 (draconic aspect)
nodes.significantEvent_source: KTU 1.1 IV - 1.2 IV
nodes.birthTypes_source: Yam as son of El (`bn ʾil` in some passages); cf. pantheon list KTU 1.47 / 1.118
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: KTU 1.1 IV (El's initial favor for Yam); pantheon list KTU 1.47 / 1.118

nodes.name: Batara Kala
nodes.domain: time, destruction, the underworld, darkness, the devourer, Shiva
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the god of the underworld and the devourer, son of Shiva (Batara Guru) and Uma (Dewi Durga) in their wrathful forms
nodes.significantEvent: Batara Kala rules the dark underworld and devours those who transgress cosmic law, associated with eclipses (he swallows the sun and moon), children born at inauspicious times must be purified to avoid his influence
nodes.symbolism: the devouring god of time and the underworld, the eclipse as the swallowing of celestial light, the purification ritual as the escape from the devourers grasp, time as the ultimate destroyer
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible Great Father of time and the underworld, the devouring masculine consciousness of chronological destruction
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from the wrathful aspects of Shiva and Uma in Balinese mythology

nodes.name: Yaldabaoth
nodes.domain: the demiurge, the false god, the creator of the material world, ignorance, the lion-headed serpent
nodes.characterTrait: ignorant, tyrannical, jealous, false-godlike, demiurgic, material-world-creating
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: the Demiurge, often depicted as a lion-headed serpent or a blind and ignorant god, the false creator of the material world
nodes.significantEvent: the ignorant creator god who fashioned the material world as a flawed and imprisoning copy of the divine realm, declares himself the only god out of ignorance, identified by Gnostics with the God of the Old Testament, humanity contains a spark of the true divine trapped in his material creation
nodes.symbolism: the lion-headed serpent as the bestial creator, the blindness as the ignorance of the false god, the material world as a prison created by a flawed deity, the declaration I am the only god as the supreme ignorance, the trapped divine spark as the human tragedy
nodes.neumannArchetype: the terrible demiurgic father who creates the prison of the material world out of ignorance, the false patriarchal consciousness that imprisons the divine spark within matter
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from Sophia (Wisdom) through a mistake or act of pride, without a male counterpart

nodes.name: Proserpina
nodes.domain: the underworld, spring, grain, death, renewal
nodes.characterTrait: dual-natured, spring-like, underworld queen, innocent yet powerful
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful maiden carrying a torch and grain or flowers, or as the stern queen of the underworld, the goddess of two worlds
nodes.significantEvent: abducted by Pluto to the underworld, her mother Ceres caused all vegetation to die in grief, Zeus mediated a compromise where she spends half the year underground and half above, her annual return causes spring
nodes.symbolism: the pomegranate as the food of the dead that binds one to the underworld, the maiden abducted as the transition from innocence to queen of death, the seasonal cycle as the journey between worlds, death and renewal as inseparable
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Kore (maiden) who becomes the Queen of the Dead, the Great Mothers daughter who must descend to the underworld to complete the cycle of consciousness
nodes.domain_source: Ovid, Metamorphoses 5.346-571; Fasti 4.417-620; Cicero, In Verrem 4.106-109; Claudian, De Raptu Proserpinae (4th c. CE — the most extensive Roman narrative)
nodes.object_source: Proserpina iconography — pomegranate; sheaf of grain; torch; the underworld throne
nodes.characterTrait_source: Ovid; Claudian
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Identical to Persephone — youthful goddess; later enthroned as underworld queen
nodes.significantEvent_source: Roman tradition — identified with Greek Persephone; the abduction (raptus) by Pluto from the Sicilian field at Enna; her annual return brings spring (an explicit Roman seasonal-myth); Ovid Met. 5 and Claudian's De Raptu Proserpinae are the major Roman narratives. The Aventine Triad's Libera was sometimes identified with Proserpina
nodes.birthTypes_source: Standard interpretatio

nodes.name: Osiris myth
nodes.domain: death, resurrection, kingship, agriculture, the afterlife, judgment
nodes.object: crook, flail, atef crown, djed pillar
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: mummiform man with green or black skin wearing the white atef crown with ostrich feathers, holding crook and flail, lord of the underworld
nodes.significantEvent: murdered by his brother Set who dismembered his body and scattered the pieces throughout Egypt, reassembled by Isis who conceived Horus from his restored body, became lord of the underworld and judge of the dead, his annual death and resurrection symbolized the Nile flood and agricultural cycle
nodes.symbolism: death and resurrection as the eternal cycle, the green skin as vegetation reborn, the mummified body as the promise of eternal life, the just ruler who judges the dead, the grain that dies and is reborn
nodes.neumannArchetype: the dying and resurrecting god, the Great Father of the underworld whose death and reassembly by the Great Mother (Isis) creates the possibility of eternal life for all humanity
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Geb (earth) and Nut (sky), brother and husband of Isis, brother of Set, Nephthys, and sometimes Horus the Elder

nodes.name: Mannus
nodes.domain: ancestry, tribal origin, kingship
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: divine ancestor, first man of Germanic tradition
nodes.significantEvent: son of Tuisto, fathered the three tribal ancestors of the Ingaevones, Herminones, and Istaevones
nodes.symbolism: divine ancestry of the Germanic peoples, tripartite tribal division
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine ancestor figure establishing human civilization
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of earth-born Tuisto

nodes.name: Baduhenna
nodes.domain: war, battle, sacred groves
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: war goddess associated with a sacred grove
nodes.significantEvent: nine hundred Roman soldiers were slaughtered in her sacred grove during the Frisian revolt of 28 CE according to Tacitus
nodes.symbolism: divine feminine fury in battle, the sacred grove as site of divine violence
nodes.neumannArchetype: Terrible Mother in her warrior aspect

nodes.name: The Alcis
nodes.domain: divine twins, youth, sacred rites
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: twin young men worshipped without images in a sacred grove, priests dressed in feminine attire
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped by the Naharvali tribe in a sacred grove with a priest in womens clothing, identified by Tacitus with Castor and Pollux
nodes.symbolism: divine twinship, sacred androgyny in ritual, the Indo-European Divine Twins archetype
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Divine Twins representing duality within unity

nodes.name: Hariasa
nodes.domain: war, fury
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: war goddess known only from a single Roman-era inscription
nodes.significantEvent: attested by a votive inscription found near Cologne, dedicated by Frisian soldiers serving in the Roman army
nodes.symbolism: Germanic feminine war fury, divine patronage of warriors abroad
nodes.neumannArchetype: Terrible Mother in her battle-fury aspect

nodes.name: Pan
nodes.domain: nature, shepherds, wilderness, fertility, music, panic
nodes.characterTrait: lustful, musical, playful, terrifying, wild, rustic
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: goat legs, horned, pointed ears, shaggy-haired, bearded, human torso
nodes.significantEvent: pursued the nymph Syrinx who was transformed into reeds from which he made his pipes, caused panic among the Persians at Marathon, shouted that Great Pan is dead during the reign of Tiberius
nodes.symbolism: untamed nature, the wild instinct, the panic terror of encountering the divine in wilderness, the animality within humanity
nodes.neumannArchetype: the nature god representing the instinctual layer of the psyche, the goat-god of animal vitality and creative wildness
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Hermes and a daughter of Dryops, or of Hermes and Penelope

nodes.name: Chiyou
nodes.domain: war, metal-working, weapons, agriculture, rebellion
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: bronze-headed with iron forehead, bull horns, four eyes, six-armed, human body with hooves, hair like swords and spears
nodes.significantEvent: invented metal weapons and waged war against the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi) at the Battle of Zhuolu, created a great fog but was defeated when Huangdi invented the south-pointing compass, beheaded and his blood stained the maple trees red
nodes.symbolism: the rebel innovator who challenges the established cosmic order, metal-working as both advancement and destruction, the defeated adversary who remains honored as an ancestor, the fog of chaos dispersed by the compass of order
nodes.neumannArchetype: the shadow warrior who challenges the established patriarchal consciousness (Yellow Emperor), the Promethean rebel whose innovations (metal weapons) serve destruction, the dark twin of the culture hero
nodes.birthCircumstances: leader of the Jiuli (Nine Li) tribe, legendary ancestor of the Hmong and Miao peoples

nodes.name: Despoina
nodes.domain: mysteries, the underworld, nature, the Arcadian cult
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: bull, human
nodes.significantEvent: worshipped in secret mysteries at Lycosura in Arcadia, her true name could not be spoken by the uninitiated, her cult statue was made by Damophon
nodes.symbolism: the hidden name of the divine feminine, the mysteries that must not be spoken, the daughter born from the union of earth and sea
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hidden aspect of the Great Mother whose true identity is itself the mystery, the forbidden name of the feminine divine
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Demeter and Poseidon, conceived when Poseidon ravished Demeter in horse form, sister of the horse Arion

nodes.name: Lares Familiares
nodes.domain: hearth
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: youthful male figures in dancing pose holding drinking horns and pateras, housed in the household shrine (lararium)
nodes.significantEvent: the Lares Familiares were the guardian spirits of each Roman household, worshipped daily at the lararium, garlanded on family occasions, carried along when the family moved, every significant family event included offerings to them
nodes.symbolism: the dancing youthful spirits as the vitality of the ancestral lineage, the lararium as the miniature temple of family religion, the daily offering as the continuous relationship between living and ancestral
nodes.neumannArchetype: the ancestral masculine spirits who protect the continuity of family consciousness across generations
nodes.birthCircumstances: ancient Roman spirits of the household and crossroads, possibly deified ancestors

nodes.name: Hou Ji
nodes.domain: agriculture, fertility
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Lord of Millet, the divine ancestor of the Zhou Dynasty
nodes.significantEvent: taught the people to cultivate millet and other grains, established agriculture as the foundation of Chinese civilization, worshipped as the god of agriculture and ancestor of the Zhou royal house
nodes.symbolism: the divine origin of agriculture, the abandoned child who brings the gift of grain, the ancestral hero whose gift feeds all subsequent civilization
nodes.neumannArchetype: the divine child abandoned and protected by the Great Mother (nature), who grows to become the culture hero of agriculture
nodes.birthCircumstances: born when his mother Jiang Yuan stepped in the footprint of Shangdi (the Supreme Deity), abandoned as an infant but miraculously protected by animals

nodes.name: Amun
nodes.object: double-plumed crown (his distinctive iconography); ankh; was-scepter; the ram-headed sphinx (criosphinx); the goose (his other sacred form)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Anthropomorphic king wearing the distinctive double-plumed crown; blue-skinned (the color of the primordial waters); sometimes ram-headed (the criosphinx form); the goose is his other sacred form.
nodes.significantEvent: Originally one of the Hermopolitan Ogdoad (paired with Amunet as 'hidden' principles). Rose to prominence as the Theban dynastic god (11th Dynasty onward), eventually becoming the supreme imperial god of New Kingdom Egypt under the title Amun-Ra. Combines the hidden/primordial Amun-aspect with the visible/solar Ra-aspect. Briefly suppressed by Akhenaten's Aten-cult (14th c. BCE), restored under Tutankhamun. The Theban triad: Amun (father), Mut (mother), Khonsu (son).
nodes.symbolism: the hidden god whose power pervades all creation, the union of the hidden and the visible (Amun-Ra), the double plume as the duality of Upper and Lower Egypt, the ram as creative fertility
nodes.neumannArchetype: the supreme Great Father who is hidden and transcendent, the invisible masculine principle that generates all visible creation
familyRoles: Theban triad father (with Mut and Khonsu)
supreme imperial god of New Kingdom Egypt
nodes.birthCircumstances: In Hermopolitan cosmogony, one of the eight primordial beings (with Amunet) representing the 'hidden' principle before creation.
nodes.domain_source: Pyramid Texts (early references); the Theban-Karnak inscriptions (his major cult-center, 18th Dynasty onward); the Hymns to Amun (Leiden Hymn, Cairo Hymn, etc.); the Amduat
nodes.object_source: Standard Amun iconography; Karnak inscriptions
nodes.characterTrait_source: Hymns to Amun; Karnak inscriptions
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard iconography
nodes.significantEvent_source: Karnak inscriptions; Hymns to Amun; Amarna-period sources
nodes.birthTypes_source: Hermopolitan cosmogony
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Hermopolitan cosmogony

nodes.name: Vesta
nodes.domain: earth, fire, home, hearth
nodes.characterTrait: virginal, devoted, flame-keeping, domestic, sacred, serene
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: veiled woman in modest robes, often depicted standing near the sacred flame, the most austere of the Roman goddesses
nodes.significantEvent: her sacred flame in the Temple of Vesta in the Roman Forum was tended by the Vestal Virgins who served for 30 years, if the flame went out it was considered a terrible omen for Rome, the Vestals had extraordinary privileges and influence
nodes.symbolism: the eternal flame as the life of the state, the hearth as the center of both home and civilization, virginity as the dedication of the feminine entirely to the sacred, the fire that must never go out
nodes.neumannArchetype: the Great Mother reduced to her most essential symbol: the flame of consciousness that must be perpetually maintained, the virginal feminine devoted entirely to keeping awareness alive
birthTypes: identified with Hestia; swallowed by Saturn
familyRoles: first-born of Saturn and Ops; first-swallowed
virgin goddess (her vow guarded by the Vestal Virgins on earth)
indigenous Roman as Latin Vesta predating the Hestia-interpretatio
nodes.domain_source: Ovid, Fasti 6 (the central source — Vestalia June 9); Cicero, De Natura Deorum 2.67; Plutarch, Numa 9-13; Dionysius of Halicarnassus 2.64-70 (Vestal Virgin institution); Livy 1.20 (Numa's institution)
nodes.object_source: Vesta iconography — sacred fire (the ever-burning hearth); donkey (her sacrificial animal); fascinum (apotropaic phallus)
nodes.animals_source: Vesta's sacred animals: donkey (which brayed and woke her when Priapus tried to assault her — the etiology of the Vestalia donkey-decoration); the sacred fire itself
nodes.characterTrait_source: Ovid, Fasti 6; the Vestal Virgin tradition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Vesta iconography — minimally depicted (her sacred fire being her primary 'image'); when depicted, modest veiled matron
nodes.significantEvent_source: Roman tradition — identified with Greek Hestia; central to Roman state-religion (the Vestal Virgins maintained her eternal flame on the Forum; if it went out, it was state-emergency); six Vestals chosen at age 6-10, served for 30 years, vowed virginity (broken vow punished by live burial); the Vestal Virgins were the only women who could own property without male oversight; Vestalia festival June 9
nodes.birthTypes_source: Roman interpretation

nodes.name: Inari Ōkami
nodes.domain: war, crafts, fertility, agriculture, grain supply
nodes.object: rice sheaves, fox statues, torii gates
nodes.characterTrait: fertile, prosperous, shape-shifting, generous, commercial, agricultural
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: kami of rice and prosperity, can appear as male, female, or androgynous, often associated with white foxes who serve as messengers
nodes.significantEvent: one of the most widely worshipped kami in Japan with over 30,000 Inari shrines (identified by their red torii gates and fox statues), patron of rice cultivation, commerce, industry, and worldly success, the foxes (kitsune) serve as divine messengers
nodes.symbolism: the red torii gates as the threshold of abundance, the fox as the cunning messenger of prosperity, rice as the foundation of Japanese civilization, the most democratic of kami worshipped by farmers, merchants, and industrialists alike
nodes.neumannArchetype: the androgynous Great Mother/Father of abundance, the divine principle of prosperity that transcends gender and social class, the numinous of worldly success
nodes.domain_source: Engishiki (10th c.); Fushimi Inari-taisha traditions (founded 711 CE, the central Inari shrine); Konjaku Monogatari-shū
nodes.object_source: Inari iconography — rice sheaves; the white-fox (Kitsune) messengers; the cinnabar-red torii gates (Fushimi Inari has ~10,000 torii)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Standard Inari tradition; Fushimi Inari-taisha
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Inari iconography — variable: sometimes depicted as an old man with white beard, sometimes as a young woman, sometimes androgynous; the fox is the constant messenger-companion
nodes.significantEvent_source: Inari is associated with rice, agriculture, fertility, and prosperity. By the medieval period, Inari became the most widely worshipped kami in Japan, with over 30,000 Inari shrines (about a third of all Shintō shrines). The Fushimi Inari-taisha at Kyoto is the head shrine.

nodes.name: Three Pure Ones
nodes.domain: creation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: three supreme Daoist deities seated together: Yuanshi Tianzun (Celestial Worthy of Primordial Beginning), Lingbao Tianzun (Celestial Worthy of Numinous Treasure), Daode Tianzun (Celestial Worthy of the Way and Virtue)
nodes.significantEvent: represent the Dao in three aspects: the origin (Yuanshi), the preservation (Lingbao), and the ethical manifestation (Daode/Laozi), rule the three highest heavens
nodes.symbolism: the Dao expressing itself in three supreme aspects, the trinity of origin, preservation, and ethical manifestation, the highest mystery of Daoist theology
nodes.neumannArchetype: the triple expression of the ultimate masculine principle, the Dao differentiated into three aspects of cosmic consciousness: the origin, the treasury, and the ethical expression
nodes.birthCircumstances: the three emanations of the Dao itself, the highest beings in the Daoist pantheon

nodes.name: Eos
nodes.domain: dawn, renewal, each new day
nodes.object: chariot, rose, tiara, pitcher of dew
nodes.characterTrait: beautiful, amorous, eternally renewing, cursed with insatiable desire for mortals
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: rosy-fingered, saffron-robed, winged, driving a chariot
nodes.significantEvent: cursed by Aphrodite with insatiable desire for mortal men after Eos slept with Ares, abducted Tithonus and asked Zeus for his immortality but forgot to ask for eternal youth so he withered into a cicada
nodes.symbolism: the eternal renewal of each new day, the tragedy of immortality without youth, the dawn as the threshold between darkness and light
nodes.neumannArchetype: the feminine dawn archetype, the seductive goddess whose desire for mortal men represents the pull of consciousness from the unconscious
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the Titans Hyperion and Theia, sister of Helios and Selene

nodes.name: Helios
nodes.domain: sun, sight, oaths, cattle
nodes.object: sun chariot, golden cup, aureole, crown of rays
nodes.animals: horse, rooster, wolf, cattle, serpent, bull, lion, stag, dog, bear, cock, crane, cow, dragon
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: radiant, beardless or bearded, crowned with rays of light, driving a golden chariot across the sky
nodes.significantEvent: drives the sun chariot daily across the sky from east to west, told Demeter what happened to Persephone, his son Phaethon lost control of the chariot and nearly burned the earth
nodes.symbolism: the all-seeing eye of heaven, the regularity of cosmic order, the danger of mortal presumption in wielding divine power
nodes.neumannArchetype: the solar consciousness that illuminates all things, the all-seeing witness of the cosmos
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of the Titans Hyperion and Theia, brother of Selene and Eos

nodes.name: Apollo
nodes.domain: sun, prophecy, music, order, art
nodes.animals: swan, raven, dolphin, wolf, mouse, python
nodes.characterTrait: rational, orderly, beautiful, truthful, sometimes cruel, far-striking
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beardless, eternally youthful, radiant, golden hair
nodes.significantEvent: Opposition to Dionysus at Delphi; Pythian Apollo
nodes.symbolism: rational consciousness, the light of truth and order, the tension between civilization and ecstatic experience, prophecy as divine knowledge
nodes.neumannArchetype: the solar hero representing the triumph of consciousness over the unconscious, opposed to and reconciled with Dionysus at Delphi
familyRoles: god of Delphi, Delos, Didyma, Klaros oracles
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Zeus and the Titaness Leto, twin brother of Artemis, born on the island of Delos
nodes.domain_source: Homer, Iliad (especially Book 1 — the plague on the Achaeans); Homeric Hymn to Apollo (Delian and Pythian); Hesiod, Theogony 918-920; Apollodorus 1.4; the Delphic, Delian, and Didyma oracular cults
nodes.object_source: Apollo iconography — lyre (κιθάρα, the gift of Hermes); bow and arrows (with which he caused plague in Iliad 1); laurel-crown (after the Daphne pursuit); tripod (Delphic oracular seat); kithara
nodes.animals_source: Apollo's sacred animals: dolphin (the form he took to lead Cretan sailors to Delphi — origin of 'Pythian'/Δελφοί); raven (originally white, blackened when bringing news of Coronis's infidelity); wolf (Apollo Lukeios); deer; swan
nodes.characterTrait_source: Homer; Hesiod; the Apolline cult; the Plutarchan tradition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard Apollo iconography — youthful unbearded perfect male (the κοῦρος ideal); long hair; often nude or in himation; bearing lyre or bow
nodes.significantEvent_source: Homeric Hymn to Apollo — Leto, persecuted by Hera, gave birth to Apollo and Artemis on Delos (the only place that received her); Apollo's first deed was slaying the Python at Delphi, establishing his oracular seat; the pursuit of Daphne who became the laurel; plagued the Achaeans with his arrows in Iliad 1; killed the Cyclopes after Asclepius's death; his beloveds included Hyacinthus (accidentally killed by discus) and Cyparissus
nodes.eventTypes_source: Homer; Homeric Hymn to Apollo; Apollodorus
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Homeric Hymn to Apollo 14-126 — born on Delos after Leto, persecuted by Hera, was refused by every other land
nodes.birthTypes_source: Homeric Hymn to Apollo

nodes.name: DionysusBacchus
nodes.domain: wine, ecstasy, mystery religion, fertility, death and rebirth, orphic mysteries
nodes.object: thyrsus, grapevine, ivy crown, mirror, kantharos, mask
nodes.animals: bull, panther, tiger, lion, goat, snake, leopard, fox, serpent, horse, deer, dolphin, pig, dog, bear, cow, donkey, centaur, cerberus
nodes.characterTrait: ecstatic, wild, liberating, maddening, twice-born, dismembered and reborn
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: bull-horned, sometimes serpentine, youthful or bearded, crowned with ivy
nodes.significantEvent: as Zagreus was dismembered by the Titans who were then struck by Zeus thunderbolt, humanity arose from their ashes containing both Titanic and Dionysiac elements
nodes.symbolism: the divine spark within mortal flesh, dismemberment and reassembly as the mystery of death and rebirth, the Orphic doctrine of the souls divine origin and bodily imprisonment
nodes.neumannArchetype: the dying and rising god of the mystery tradition, the son-lover of the Great Mother who is dismembered and reborn, representing the transformation of consciousness
nodes.birthCircumstances: in Orphic tradition son of Zeus and Persephone as Zagreus, torn apart by Titans and reborn through Zeus thigh, the twice-born god

nodes.name: Scylla
nodes.domain: sea, death, the strait, monstrosity
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: multiple heads, monstrous, dog-headed, serpent's tail
nodes.significantEvent: devoured six of Odysseus sailors as his ship passed through the strait between her and Charybdis, no hero could defeat her
nodes.symbolism: the inescapable peril that must be endured, the devouring feminine from which there is no escape, the monstrous transformation of beauty
nodes.neumannArchetype: the devouring female figure at the negative pole of the Great Mother, alluring and death-dealing, whose mother is connected to the underworld
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Phorcys and Hecate or Crataiis, or transformed from a beautiful nymph by Circe

nodes.name: Artemis
nodes.domain: hunt, wilderness, moon, childbirth, virginity, wild animals
nodes.object: bow, arrow, quiver, hunting spear, crescent moon
nodes.characterTrait: virginal, fierce, independent, protective of the wild, punishing
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: tall, athletic, youthful huntress in short tunic, many-breasted in Ephesian form
nodes.significantEvent: protects her virginity fiercely, transforms Actaeon into a stag for seeing her bathe, demands sacrifice of Iphigenia at Aulis, punishes Niobe for boasting
nodes.symbolism: the untamed feminine, wilderness as sacred space, virginity as autonomous power rather than passivity, the Great Goddess in her aspect as Lady of the Beasts
nodes.neumannArchetype: the virginal Great Goddess encompassing all poles, the non-Greek Artemis is broader than the classical virginal version, includes Hecate-Artemis cult
familyRoles: patroness of childbirth, hunting, wild animals, the moon
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Zeus and Leto, twin sister of Apollo, born on the island of Delos where she assisted her mothers delivery of Apollo
nodes.domain_source: Homer, Iliad; Homeric Hymn 27; Hesiod, Theogony 918-920; Apollodorus 1.4; the Ephesian Artemis cult; the Brauronian Artemis cult; Callimachus, Hymn to Artemis
nodes.object_source: Artemis iconography — bow and arrows; quiver; lunar crescent (in her late-classical lunar-syncretic aspect); torch; the polos crown of the Ephesian Artemis
nodes.animals_source: Artemis's sacred animals: deer (the central — she rides a deer-chariot, was given golden-antlered deer; the Ceryneian Hind); bear (the Brauronian arkteia ritual); hunting-dog; quail (Ortygia, her Delos-birth-island)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Homer; Homeric Hymn 27; Callimachus; the Aktaion narrative; the Hippolytus narrative
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard Artemis iconography — youthful huntress in short chiton, with bow and quiver; the Ephesian Artemis with her many-breasted/many-egged polos (a different syncretic tradition)
nodes.significantEvent_source: Homeric Hymn to Artemis — twin of Apollo, born on Delos to Leto; assisted at her brother's birth (hence patroness of childbirth despite virginity); the Aktaion narrative (Apollodorus 3.4.4) — Actaeon saw her bathing, was transformed into a stag and torn apart by his own hounds; the Hippolytus narrative — Hippolytus's devotion to her caused his death by Aphrodite's revenge; the Calydonian boar hunt; the slaying of Orion (variously narrated)
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Homeric Hymn to Apollo — born on Delos before Apollo (some traditions); twin
nodes.birthTypes_source: Homeric Hymn

nodes.name: Sphinx
nodes.domain: death, riddles, protection, wisdom through terror
nodes.characterTrait: enigmatic, deadly, self-destroying when defeated, guardian
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: lion body, human head, eagle wings, sometimes serpents tail
nodes.significantEvent: sat outside Thebes posing a riddle to all who passed and devouring those who failed, killed herself when Oedipus answered correctly
nodes.symbolism: the enigma of human identity (What walks on four legs, two legs, three legs?), the monstrous guardian who tests consciousness, the riddle as threshold between ignorance and knowledge
nodes.neumannArchetype: the guardian figure at the threshold of consciousness, the veiled sphinx with penetrating eyes who tests the hero, connected to the motherhood-death duality
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of Typhon and Echidna, or of Orthos and the Chimera

nodes.name: Hapi
nodes.domain: the Nile, flood, fertility, abundance, water, androgyny
nodes.object: papyrus, lotus, offering table laden with food
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: man with a large belly and pendulous breasts representing abundance, wearing aquatic plants on his head, blue or green skinned
nodes.significantEvent: the annual inundation of the Nile was the central event of Egyptian life, Hapis arrival brought the fertile silt that made agriculture possible, without him Egypt would be desert, his androgynous appearance symbolized the union of male and female fertility
nodes.symbolism: the flood as divine abundance, the androgynous body as the union of all fertility, the Nile as the life-blood of Egypt, the generous belly as the overflowing bounty of the waters
nodes.neumannArchetype: the androgynous fertility principle that transcends the division of masculine and feminine, the waters that bring the Great Mothers fertility through the Great Fathers inundation
nodes.birthCircumstances: personification of the annual Nile flood that brought fertility to Egypt
nodes.deathCircumstances: Egyptian historian Al-Maqrizi (1364–1442) claimed in his "El Khutat El Maqrizia" ("The Maqrizian Plans") that virgins were sacrificed annually as "brides of the Nile" ("Arous El Nil").

nodes.name: Yue Lao
nodes.domain: love, marriage, matchmaking, the moon, destiny
nodes.object: red thread of fate, marriage book
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: elderly smiling man under the moon, carrying a book of marriages and a bag of red threads
nodes.significantEvent: ties an invisible red thread between the ankles of those destined to be married, his marriage book contains the names of all future couples, once the thread is tied nothing can prevent the union
nodes.symbolism: love as predestined fate tied by the red thread, the moon as the illumination of romantic destiny, the old man as the patient divine force that connects souls across time and distance
nodes.neumannArchetype: the positive senex who weaves the connections between masculine and feminine consciousness, the wise old man whose red thread binds the animus and anima in their fated union
nodes.birthCircumstances: the Old Man of the Moon, the divine matchmaker

nodes.name: Circe
nodes.domain: magic, transformation, herbalism, nature, enchantment
nodes.characterTrait: enchanting, powerful, dangerous, knowledgeable, seductive, ultimately helpful
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: beautiful goddess with braided hair, singing at her loom, surrounded by enchanted beasts
nodes.significantEvent: transforms Odysseus men into swine, is overcome by Odysseus with Hermes help, becomes his lover and advisor, directs him to the underworld to consult Tiresias
nodes.symbolism: the enchantress who transforms men into beasts, the feminine power that can either bestialize or enlighten, the Lady of the Beasts in the Odyssey
nodes.neumannArchetype: personalized form of primordial enchantment, the Aphrodite-like figure always subject to defeat by the conscious hero, the Lady of the Beasts who transforms the unworthy
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughter of the sun god Helios and the Oceanid Perse, sister of King Aeetes of Colchis, aunt of Medea

nodes.name: Siren
nodes.domain: death, enchantment, the sea, music, temptation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: winged, part bird
nodes.significantEvent: lured sailors to their deaths with their irresistible singing, Odysseus survived by having himself bound to the mast while his crew plugged their ears, the Argonauts survived through Orpheus outsinging them
nodes.symbolism: the deadly allure of forbidden knowledge, enchantment as the dissolution of the conscious will, the sea as the unconscious that draws consciousness to its destruction
nodes.neumannArchetype: attributes of the Archetypal Feminine as siren, the enchantment that dissolves masculine consciousness, the death enchantment of the negative feminine pole
nodes.birthCircumstances: daughters of the river god Achelous and one of the Muses, or of Phorcys

nodes.name: Menelaus
nodes.domain: kingship, the Trojan War, marital honor, Sparta
nodes.characterTrait: wronged, devoted, brave but secondary to his brother, persistent
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: red hair in some traditions, strong warrior though not the equal of Achilles or Ajax
nodes.significantEvent: husband of Helen whose abduction by Paris caused the Trojan War, defeated Paris in single combat but Paris was saved by Aphrodite, reunited with Helen after the fall of Troy
nodes.symbolism: the wronged husband whose personal grievance launches a civilization-defining war, honor that demands the destruction of a city, the man who gets his wife back but at what cost
nodes.neumannArchetype: the patriarchal masculine whose possession of the anima (Helen) is challenged by the erotic masculine (Paris), requiring the entire hero-world to restore the patriarchal order
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of Atreus and Aerope, brother of Agamemnon, king of Sparta

nodes.name: Achilles
nodes.domain: war, heroism, honor, mortality
nodes.animals: snake, horse, dog, bear, phoenix, centaur
nodes.characterTrait: wrathful, proud, brave, loyal, honorable, swift
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: swift-footed, handsome, golden hair warrior
nodes.significantEvent: withdraws from battle over dishonor from Agamemnon, returns after Patroclus is killed by Hector, slays Hector and drags his body around Troy, killed by Paris with an arrow to his heel
nodes.symbolism: the tension between glory and mortality, the cost of wrath, the hero whose invulnerability has a fatal flaw
nodes.neumannArchetype: the hero in his wrathful and mortal aspect, the son who must die young to achieve eternal glory
nodes.birthCircumstances: The central character in Homer's Iliad, he was the son of the Nereid Thetis and Peleus, king of Phthia and famous Argonaut.

nodes.name: Athena
nodes.domain: wisdom, warfare, crafts, strategy, weaving, civilization
nodes.characterTrait: wise, strategic, virginal, fierce, just, patron of heroes
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: tall, armored maiden, helmeted, grey-eyed, often bearing the aegis with the Gorgon head
nodes.significantEvent: sprang fully-armed from the head of Zeus; contested with Poseidon for Athens and won by gifting the olive tree; aided Perseus, Heracles and Odysseus; turned Arachne into a spider
nodes.symbolism: the wise virgin, civilizing intellect, the union of intuition and reason, transformation of warlike force into ordered civilization
nodes.neumannArchetype: Spiritual transformation of the Feminine — the wise virgin daughter who emerges from the patriarchal head, representing the sublimation of the Great Mother into Sophia/wisdom
familyRoles: virgin-goddess (one of the three Παρθένοι — Athena, Artemis, Hestia)
nodes.birthCircumstances: born from the head of Zeus after he swallowed her pregnant mother Metis
nodes.object_source: Athena iconography — aegis (with the gorgoneion); helmet; spear; shield; owl as companion-bird; olive tree (her gift to Athens defeating Poseidon's salt-spring)
nodes.animals_source: Athena's sacred animals: owl (γλαύξ — her companion and emblem, hence the 'owls to Athens' proverb); snake (in the Athena Parthenos tradition); horse (which she invented the bridle for)
nodes.domain_source: Homer, Iliad passim and Odyssey (especially her patronage of Odysseus); Hesiod, Theogony 886-900 (birth from Zeus's head); Homeric Hymn 28; Apollodorus 1.3.6; the Athenian Acropolis traditions (Erechtheion, Parthenon)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Hesiod, Theogony
nodes.significantEvent_source: Hesiod, Theogony 886-900 — born fully-armored from Zeus's forehead after Zeus swallowed her pregnant mother Metis (fearing a prophesied son who would overthrow him); Hephaestus split Zeus's head with an axe to allow her emergence; the contest with Poseidon for Athens (Apollodorus 3.14.1) — Athena's olive defeated Poseidon's salt-spring; patroness of Odysseus through the Odyssey; armed Diomedes in the Iliad; aided Heracles in his labors
nodes.characterTrait_source: Homer; Hesiod; the Panathenaic cult; the wisdom-and-craft tradition
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard Athena iconography — armored maiden, helmeted, bearing spear and aegis-shield with gorgoneion; cf. Pheidias's Athena Parthenos (5th c. BCE)
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Hesiod, Theogony 886-900 — born from Zeus's head

nodes.name: Narcissus
nodes.domain: self-love, beauty, vanity, transformation
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: extraordinarily beautiful youth, slender, with curling hair
nodes.significantEvent: fell in love with his own reflection in a pool and wasted away unable to leave it; transformed into the narcissus flower; rejected the love of the nymph Echo
nodes.symbolism: the danger of self-absorption, the soul trapped by its own image, the unconscious fascination with the ego that prevents true relationship
nodes.neumannArchetype: Negative anima fixation — the youth caught in his own reflection, unable to project the anima onto another and therefore unable to develop; the ego trapped by its mirror-image
nodes.birthCircumstances: son of the river god Cephissus and the nymph Liriope; prophecy at birth said he would live long only if he never recognized himself
nodes.deathCircumstances: wasted away beside the pool gazing at his own reflection; transformed into a flower at death

nodes.name: Mary
nodes.domain: motherhood of Jesus, Theotokos ('God-bearer', defined at Council of Ephesus 431), virginity, intercession (in Catholic and Orthodox tradition), the Magnificat (Luke 1:46-55), the most prominent woman in Christian devotion; in Islam, the only woman named in the Quran and one of its most honored figures (Maryam, mother of ʿĪsā)
nodes.object: the cup of the Annunciation (in Annunciation iconography); the lily; the spindle (in Protoevangelium and apocryphal traditions, she was weaving when Gabriel came); the rosary (later Catholic devotion); blue mantle (standard Marian iconography)
nodes.characterTrait: virginal, obedient ('Be it unto me according to your word', Luke 1:38), prophetic (Magnificat), pondering (Luke 2:19, 2:51), maternal, sorrowful (the seven sorrows of Mary in Catholic devotion), interceding (the wedding at Cana), present at Pentecost (Acts 1:14)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Young Galilean Jewish woman of Nazareth, betrothed to Joseph at the time of the Annunciation. Christian iconography depicts her in blue mantle and white veil, often youthful or as Mater Dolorosa beneath the cross. The Quran honors her: 'Allah chose you and purified you and chose you above the women of all nations' (Surah 3:42). She is a virgin who conceives by the Spirit (Christian) or by Allah's word (Islamic).
nodes.significantEvent: Annunciation by Gabriel (Luke 1:26-38; Quran 3:45-47, 19:17-21). Visitation to Elizabeth and the Magnificat (Luke 1:39-56). Birth of Jesus in Bethlehem (Luke 2:1-7; Matthew 1-2; Quran 19:22-26 — birthing under a palm tree). Presentation in the Temple (Luke 2:22-38). Flight to Egypt (Matthew 2:13-15). Finding Jesus in the Temple at age 12 (Luke 2:41-52). Wedding at Cana (John 2:1-12). Standing at the foot of the cross (John 19:25-27). Present with the disciples at Pentecost (Acts 1:14). In later Christian tradition: Dormition / Assumption (Catholic dogma since 1950).
nodes.symbolism: Stella Maris paralleling Isis and Tara; Pieta as mother of death; Christian continuation of Great Mother; spinner of fate; upper and lower feminine principles; Holy Ghost connection
nodes.neumannArchetype: Christian continuation of Great Mother archetype. Stella Maris paralleling Isis and Tara. Upper and lower feminine principles kindled through Mary.
nodes.birthCircumstances: Daughter of Joachim and Anne (Christian tradition, principally from the Protoevangelium of James); in Quran, daughter of ʿImrān, dedicated to Allah's service in the temple by her mother (Surah 3:35-37). The Catholic dogma of the Immaculate Conception (1854) holds that she was preserved from original sin from the moment of her conception.
nodes.deathCircumstances: Not narrated in the New Testament. Eastern Orthodox tradition: she dies (the Dormition, koimēsis); Catholic dogma (Munificentissimus Deus, 1950): she is 'assumed body and soul into heavenly glory' at the end of her earthly life, leaving open whether she died first. Islamic tradition is silent about her death.
nodes.domain_source: Matthew 1-2; Luke 1-2; John 2:1-12, 19:25-27; Acts 1:14; Quran 3:33-47, 19:1-40, 21:91, 66:12 (Maryam, daughter of ʿImrān); Protoevangelium of James (2nd c. CE, the major non-canonical source for her childhood); Council of Ephesus 431 (Theotokos); Catholic Marian dogmas (Immaculate Conception 1854, Assumption 1950)
nodes.object_source: Standard Marian iconography in Western and Eastern Christian art; Protoevangelium of James 11 (the spindle)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Luke 1:26-38; Quran 3:42-47, 19:16-22; Christian iconographic tradition
nodes.significantEvent_source: Matthew 1-2; Luke 1-2; John 2, 19; Acts 1; Quran 3, 19; Munificentissimus Deus 1950 (Assumption dogma)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Catholic dogma of Immaculate Conception (Ineffabilis Deus 1854); Protoevangelium of James 4-5 (Anne and Joachim's miraculous conception of Mary in old age)
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Protoevangelium of James 4-5; Quran 3:33-37; Ineffabilis Deus 1854
nodes.deathTypes_source: The NT does not narrate Mary's death. Eastern Orthodox tradition: the Dormition (her death and bodily assumption to heaven). Catholic dogma: the Assumption (defined 1950, leaves open whether she died first).
nodes.deathCircumstances_source: Eastern Orthodox liturgical tradition (the feast of the Dormition, 15 August); Munificentissimus Deus 1950

nodes.name: Janus
nodes.domain: beginnings, transitions, gates and doorways, time, war and peace, first invocation in prayer, the new year
nodes.domain_source: Ovid, Fasti 1.63-294 (the central source — interview with Janus); Virgil, Aeneid 7.180; Macrobius, Saturnalia 1.7-9; Cicero, De Natura Deorum 2.67; Livy 1.19 (Numa's establishment of the Temple of Janus); the Argei procession
nodes.object_source: Standard Janus iconography — key (he is janitor caeli); rod or staff; double-faced
nodes.characterTrait_source: Ovid; Macrobius; Cicero
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: two-faced (bifrons), bearded, sometimes shown with four faces (quadrifrons), holding key and staff
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard iconography — bifrons (two-faced), looking simultaneously forward and back; one face usually bearded, the other beardless (in some traditions); on Republican coinage, often shown with two identical bearded heads facing opposite directions
nodes.significantEvent: Instituted as object of cult by Numa Pompilius. The gates of his temple in the Forum Romanum were opened in time of war and closed in peace, an event so rare Augustus boasted in his Res Gestae of having achieved it three times. He is named first in every Roman prayer. He receives Saturn in Latium in the euhemeristic tradition (Macrobius). He gives extended instruction to Ovid in the Fasti book 1.
nodes.significantEvent_source: Ovid, Fasti 1.63-294 — Janus as god of beginnings, doorways, transitions, and the start of every action; opened and closed the gates of war (the Temple of Janus's doors stood open in wartime, closed in peace — closed only thrice in Roman Republic history before Augustus); presided over every threshold; opened the year (January = Ianuarius)
nodes.birthTypes_source: Macrobius, Saturnalia 1.9
familyRoles: indigenous Italic god (predates the Greek interpretatio)
nodes.familyRoles_source: husband (of Camise / Iuturna in some traditions); father (of Tiberinus in late tradition — Servius ad Aen. 8.330)
nodes.birthCircumstances: Indigenous Italic god of beginnings; in some Roman accounts ruled Latium with Saturn after the latter's flight from Olympus; presided over the Golden Age
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Ovid, Fasti 1.235-254; Macrobius, Saturnalia 1.7

nodes.name: Apsu
nodes.domain: primordial freshwater, the sweet-water abyss, the begetter of the first gods
nodes.domain_source: Enuma Elish I 1-78
nodes.significantEvent: The primordial freshwater. With Tiamat, the first divine pair; their commingling waters give rise to the first gods (Lahmu, Lahamu, Anshar, Kishar, Anu, Ea). When the noise of the younger gods disturbs his sleep, plots their destruction with his vizier Mummu. Is forestalled and slain by Ea, who casts his binding-spell of sleep upon him; Ea then builds his dwelling on Apsu's remains.
nodes.significantEvent_source: Enuma Elish I 1-78
nodes.birthCircumstances: Primordial; existed before the heavens were named.
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Enuma Elish I 1-2
nodes.deathCircumstances: Slain in his sleep by Ea, who pours sleep upon him with an incantation, takes his crown and aura, and binds him.
nodes.characterTrait: initially patient with the younger gods, then sleep-disturbed, plotting destruction; slow-witted relative to Ea
nodes.characterTrait_source: Enuma Elish I 21-72
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: The freshwater abyss personified; not described anthropomorphically in detail. His 'crown' and 'aura' (mēlammu) are taken by Ea after his death.
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Enuma Elish I 67-72
nodes.birthTypes_source: Enuma Elish I 1-4

nodes.name: Lahmu
nodes.domain: primordial god (the "hairy one" / mud), early generation; later associated with apkallu-figures
nodes.domain_source: Enuma Elish I 9-12
nodes.significantEvent: First-generation god, born of Apsu and Tiamat. Spouse of Lahamu. Parent of Anshar.
nodes.significantEvent_source: Enuma Elish I 9-12
nodes.characterTrait_source: Enuma Elish I 9-12
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: In Akkadian iconography, Lahmu is depicted as a curly-haired bearded male with six locks. Originally a personification of muddy water/silt.
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Akkadian iconography; Wiggermann 1992 'Mesopotamian Protective Spirits' on the Lahmu type
nodes.birthCircumstances: Born of Apsu and Tiamat; among the first generation of named gods.
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Enuma Elish I 9-12
nodes.birthTypes_source: Enuma Elish I 9-12

nodes.name: Lahamu
nodes.domain: primordial goddess, mate of Lahmu
nodes.domain_source: Enuma Elish I 9-12
nodes.significantEvent: First-generation goddess, born of Apsu and Tiamat. Spouse of Lahmu. Parent of Kishar.
nodes.characterTrait_source: Enuma Elish I 9-12
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Female counterpart of Lahmu; not typically depicted iconographically as distinct.
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Enuma Elish I 9-12
nodes.birthCircumstances: Born of Apsu and Tiamat; among the first generation of named gods.
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Enuma Elish I 9-12

nodes.name: Anshar
nodes.domain: the upper firmament/whole-sky; second-generation primordial; later identified with Aššur in Assyrian recension
nodes.domain_source: Enuma Elish I 11-15; in Neo-Assyrian recensions of Enuma Elish, Anshar = Aššur
nodes.significantEvent: Second-generation primordial god, born of Lahmu and Lahamu. Spouse of Kishar. Father of Anu. In tablet III sends his vizier Kakka to Lahmu and Lahamu to summon the gods.
nodes.significantEvent_source: Enuma Elish I 11-15, III
nodes.characterTrait: primordial, paternal, council-leader; in Tablet III, sends his vizier Kakka to summon the gods
nodes.characterTrait_source: Enuma Elish I 11-15, III
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Personification of the upper firmament; in Neo-Assyrian recensions, identified with the state god Aššur.
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Enuma Elish I 11-15; Neo-Assyrian theological substitution Anshar=Aššur
nodes.birthCircumstances: Born of Lahmu and Lahamu.
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Enuma Elish I 11-15

nodes.name: Kishar
nodes.domain: the lower firmament/whole-earth; second-generation primordial
nodes.domain_source: Enuma Elish I 11-15
nodes.significantEvent: Second-generation primordial goddess, born of Lahmu and Lahamu. Spouse of Anshar. Mother of Anu.
nodes.characterTrait_source: Enuma Elish I 11-15
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Personification of the lower firmament/whole-earth; female counterpart of Anshar.
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Enuma Elish I 11-15
nodes.birthCircumstances: Born of Lahmu and Lahamu.
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Enuma Elish I 11-15
nodes.significantEvent_source: Enuma Elish I 11-15
nodes.birthTypes_source: Enuma Elish I 11-15

nodes.name: Mummu
nodes.domain: vizier of Apsu; embodied wisdom-counsel, mist
nodes.domain_source: Enuma Elish I 30-72
nodes.significantEvent: Vizier of Apsu. Counsels Apsu to destroy the younger gods (against Tiamat's wish). When Ea slays Apsu, Mummu is captured, bound, and led by a nose-rope; his crown and aura are taken by Ea.
nodes.significantEvent_source: Enuma Elish I 30-72
nodes.characterTrait: advising, scheming, vizier-like; counsels Apsu to destroy the younger gods
nodes.characterTrait_source: Enuma Elish I 30-72
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Vizier figure; led by a nose-rope after his capture by Ea (Enuma Elish I 71-72).
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Enuma Elish I 71-72

nodes.name: Kingu
nodes.domain: champion of Tiamat; bearer of the Tablets of Destiny; sacrificial source of human blood
nodes.domain_source: Enuma Elish I 147-162; IV 119-122; VI 29-32
nodes.significantEvent: Tiamat's second consort after Apsu's death; given the Tablets of Destiny and command of her army. Defeated and bound by Marduk. Slain in tablet VI; from his blood, Ea (or Marduk) creates humanity.
nodes.significantEvent_source: Enuma Elish I 147-162 (elevation); IV 119-122 (defeat and Tablets of Destiny taken); VI 29-32 (sacrifice for humans)
nodes.deathCircumstances: Bound by Marduk after his army's defeat; later sacrificed, his arteries cut by Ea, his blood used to create humanity.
nodes.object: Tablets of Destiny (given by Tiamat in EE I 156-162)
nodes.object_source: Enuma Elish I 147-162
nodes.characterTrait: champion, weak in actual combat, sacrificed
nodes.characterTrait_source: Enuma Elish I 147-162; IV 119-122; VI 29-32
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Tiamat's elevated consort and champion; bound by Marduk in Tablet IV; sacrificed in Tablet VI.
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Enuma Elish IV-VI
nodes.birthCircumstances: Among the gods born within Tiamat's company; specific parentage not clarified in EE.
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Enuma Elish I (he is among 'the gods her sons' before his elevation)

nodes.name: Anu
nodes.domain: sky, kingship of heaven, the supreme high god of the An-Anum lists, fate-determining authority, the constellations
nodes.domain_source: Enuma Elish I 14-21; standard An-Anum god-list (Litke 1998); Codex Hammurabi prologue (col. I); Atrahasis passim
nodes.object: horned crown, the Tablets of Destiny (in some traditions)
nodes.object_source: Standard royal-divine iconography; Anu's horned cap is the supreme divine emblem in Mesopotamian art
nodes.significantEvent: Son of Anshar and Kishar, equal to his fathers. Begets Ea/Nudimmud in his image. In Enuma Elish, fashions and gives the four winds to Marduk (IV 41-46) but is unable himself to confront Tiamat. Standard head of the supreme triad (Anu, Enlil, Ea). Father of many gods; standard father-figure invoked across the tradition.
nodes.significantEvent_source: Enuma Elish I 14-21, IV 41-46; Atrahasis; Codex Hammurabi; Anu hymns
nodes.characterTrait: supreme, paternal, decree-giving, sometimes ineffectual in action (Enuma Elish III — Anu confronts Tiamat but turns back)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Enuma Elish III; Atrahasis I; standard pantheon-prologue formulae (e.g. Codex Hammurabi prologue col. I)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Aged sky-god; horned crown is his and the supreme divine emblem in Mesopotamian art (the multi-tiered horned cap).
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Standard Mesopotamian iconography (the horned crown is Anu's and is the highest divine insignia); Akkadian seals; the An-Anum god-list
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Anshar and Kishar; equal to his fathers (Enuma Elish I 14-16).
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Enuma Elish I 14-16
nodes.eventTypes_source: Enuma Elish I, III, IV; Atrahasis; Codex Hammurabi prologue
nodes.birthTypes_source: Enuma Elish I 14-16

nodes.name: Enlil
nodes.domain: wind, storm, the executive sovereignty of the gods, the calendar, kingship-conferral, the Tablet of Destinies
nodes.domain_source: Enlil and Ninlil (ETCSL 1.2.1); Atrahasis (Lambert-Millard 1969) — Enlil is the council-leader who decrees the flood; Codex Hammurabi prologue; Sumerian Enlil hymns (ETCSL 4.05.1)
nodes.object: staff of office, Tablet of Destinies (in some traditions, before given to Marduk)
nodes.object_source: Sumerian Enlil hymn corpus; the Tablet of Destinies is canonically Enlil's in early traditions
nodes.significantEvent: Executive head of the Sumerian and early-Babylonian pantheon. Father of Nanna, Nergal, Ninazu, and Enbilulu (by Ninlil). In the Enlil and Ninlil myth, follows the young Ninlil who has bathed in the canal, lying with her three more times in different netherworld disguises; she bears him Nanna and three netherworld gods. In Atrahasis, decrees the flood to silence noisy humanity; is circumvented by Enki who warns Atrahasis. In Anzu, his Tablet of Destinies is stolen by the bird Anzu; Ninurta (his son) recovers it.
nodes.significantEvent_source: Enlil and Ninlil (ETCSL 1.2.1); Atrahasis II-III; Anzu (SAACT 3); Sumerian Enlil hymns
nodes.characterTrait: executive, decree-giving, sometimes harsh (decrees the Flood in Atrahasis), sometimes lustful (Enlil and Ninlil)
nodes.characterTrait_source: Atrahasis II-III; Enlil and Ninlil (ETCSL 1.2.1)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Bearded sovereign god; horned crown; standard royal-divine iconography. His emblem is the divine number 50 in numerical god-lists.
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Sumerian Enlil hymns (ETCSL 4.05.1); Ur III iconography
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Anu in standard An-Anum theology; in some recensions an early-generation god of equal seniority to Anu.
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Standard An-Anum theology; cf. Enuma Elish (which omits Enlil from the primordial line, focusing on Anu→Ea→Marduk)
nodes.eventTypes_source: Enlil and Ninlil (ETCSL 1.2.1); Atrahasis II-III; Anzu
nodes.birthTypes_source: Standard An-Anum theology

nodes.name: Ninlil
nodes.domain: grain, destiny, queen of the gods (as Enlil's consort), the womb-conduit of major gods
nodes.domain_source: Enlil and Ninlil (ETCSL 1.2.1)
nodes.significantEvent: In the Enlil and Ninlil myth (ETCSL 1.2.1), is approached by young Enlil at the canal in spite of her mother's warning; is condemned by the divine assembly for the union; bears Nanna, then in successive disguises bears three netherworld substitutes (Nergal-Meslamtaea, Ninazu, Enbilulu).
nodes.significantEvent_source: Enlil and Ninlil (ETCSL 1.2.1)
nodes.object_source: Sumerian Ninlil hymns; standard Sumerian grain-goddess iconography
nodes.characterTrait: initially compliant young goddess, then defiant (in Enlil and Ninlil), then queenly mother
nodes.characterTrait_source: Enlil and Ninlil (ETCSL 1.2.1)
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Young goddess of grain; standard Sumerian goddess iconography.
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Sumerian Ninlil hymns; Ur III iconography
nodes.birthCircumstances: Daughter of Nidaba/Nisaba (grain goddess) and Haya in standard genealogies.
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Sumerian-Akkadian god-lists; Asher-Greve & Westenholz 2013
nodes.birthTypes_source: Sumerian-Akkadian god-lists

nodes.name: Enki
nodes.domain: freshwater (Apsû), wisdom, magic and incantation, craft, cunning, intercession for humanity, the seven me
nodes.domain_source: Enuma Elish I 17-78 (slays Apsu, becomes lord of the freshwater); Atrahasis I-III (warns Atrahasis); Inanna and Enki (ETCSL 1.3.1) — guardian of the me; Enki and the World Order (ETCSL 1.1.3); Enki and Ninhursag (ETCSL 1.1.1)
nodes.object: the seven me (cosmic offices); the gushing waters; the boat of magur; standard freshwater-stream iconography from his shoulders
nodes.object_source: Inanna and Enki (ETCSL 1.3.1); standard Enki-Ea iconography
nodes.animals_source: Standard Enki-Ea iconography (the suḫurmāšu hybrid is his emblem-creature)
nodes.significantEvent: Son of Anu (Sumerian tradition) or of Anshar/Kishar (Enuma Elish I 17). Slays Apsu and establishes his dwelling on his remains. Father of Marduk by Damkina. Father of Asalluhi. Outwits Tiamat's plan only as far as he himself can; passes the championship to Marduk. In Atrahasis warns the flood-hero in defiance of Enlil's decree. In Inanna and Enki, gives away the me when drunk in Eridu; tries unsuccessfully to recover them. In Enki and Ninhursag, fathers a series of plant-children with Ninhursag; eats the eight plants that grow; is struck with eight illnesses; is healed by Ninhursag with eight healing-deity offspring (one per illness, one per body-part, including Ninti from his rib).
nodes.significantEvent_source: Enuma Elish I-VI; Atrahasis I-III; Inanna and Enki (ETCSL 1.3.1); Enki and Ninhursag (ETCSL 1.1.1); Enki and the World Order (ETCSL 1.1.3); Enki hymns (ETCSL 4.27)
nodes.characterTrait: wise, cunning, intercessory, generative, sometimes drunk, technocratic
nodes.characterTrait_source: Inanna and Enki; Enki and Ninhursag; Atrahasis
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Wise bearded god; depicted with streams of water (containing fish) flowing from his shoulders or from the vessel he holds. Often shown with the suḫurmāšu (goat-fish hybrid) at his feet. The Adda Seal (BM 89115, Akkadian period) is the canonical iconographic source.
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Adda Seal (BM 89115); standard Akkadian-period and later iconography; Enki and the World Order (ETCSL 1.1.3)
nodes.birthCircumstances: Son of Anu (Sumerian theology) — Enuma Elish I 17 says Anu begets Nudimmud (=Ea) in his image.
nodes.birthCircumstances_source: Enuma Elish I 17; Sumerian Enki hymns (ETCSL 4.27)
nodes.eventTypes_source: Enuma Elish I-VI; Atrahasis I-III; ETCSL 1.1.1, 1.1.3, 1.3.1; Enki hymns
nodes.birthTypes_source: Enuma Elish I 17

nodes.name: Damkina
nodes.domain: consort of Ea, mother of Marduk, queen of Eridu
nodes.domain_source: Enuma Elish I 78-83
nodes.significantEvent: Wife of Ea. Mother of Marduk, born in pure Apsû.
nodes.significantEvent_source: Enuma Elish I 78-83
nodes.characterTrait_source: Enuma Elish I 78-83
nodes.physicalCharacteristics: Consort of Ea; standard goddess iconography. Not described in detail in narrative.
nodes.physicalCharacteristics_source: Enuma Elish I 78-83 (her brief appearance as Marduk's mother)

nodes.name: Ninhursag
nodes.domain: mountain mother goddess, midwifery, wild fauna, womb-creator, the foothills (ḫursag); often equated with Ki, Mami, Aruru, Belet-ili, Nintur
nodes.domain_source: Enki and Ninhursag (ETCSL 1.1.1); Atrahasis I (parallel mother-figure to Mami); Sumerian god-lists; ORACC AMGG entry
nodes.significantEvent: Great mother-goddess of the Sumerian pantheon. In Enki and Ninhursag, her partnership with Enki produces a series of plant-deity children, then heals him after he eats the forbidden plants (the Ninti episode). Co-creator of humanity in some traditions. Equivalent or partially-overlapping with Aruru, Mami, Belet-ili. Sometimes spouse of Enlil (and mother of Ninurta), sometimes spouse of Enki.
nodes.significantEvent_source: Enki and Ninhursag (ETCSL 1.1.1); Atrahasis I; Sumerian-Akkadian god-lists
nodes.object: reed-marsh setting; agricultural produce; the sacred mound (ḫursag, mountain)
nodes.object_source: Enki and Ninhursag (ETCSL 1.1.1); standard Sumerian mother-goddess iconography
nodes.characterTrait: generative, occasionally angered (curses Enki for eating her plants in Enki and Ninhursag), then compassionate (heals him with the eight healing-deity births)
